criteria.text: Taking the raw address of a list element inside #Unsafe (`*list[0]`) either compiles to a pointer into the list's storage or is refused with a registered error; on dev 0ccdff27ea it was an internal compiler error ("raw address of a temporary"), which violates I2. Every place-expression form under `*` (list, array, field, nested index, view) is probed at O0, O1 and O2 and lands as a case (found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation).

D-AUTOPIN1=A is built for the choice kinds sema records today. Each automatic choice is sound by default: storage form, web placement (the JS or Wasm web partition, FnBody.web_bucket, with its recorded reason), collection, copies and inlining. `jet inspect choices` and editor hovers show each choice with its reason; a marker or effect denial locks it; a later change that breaks a lock fails the build naming the fact that changed. Proof: a golden per choice kind and a UI snapshot for a broken lock.

D-RAWPTR2=A is built: `?mem.Ptr<T>` (null is None), `p.offset(n)`, `p.byte_offset(n)`, `p.cast<U>()`, `mem.alloc_raw(size:, align:)`, `mem.free_raw(^p)`, `mem.window(p, len)`, `mem.copy` and `mem.fill`, all inside #Unsafe and keeping the pointer's origin; dev-mode and hardened builds still check range, liveness and alignment. Proof: a golden on O0, O1 and O2 and a UI snapshot for a use outside #Unsafe.

D-STACKBOUND1=A is built: `jet inspect memory` prints the worst-case stack and heap per entry point from backend frame sizes and the call graph. `!Mem.Stack(above: N)` enforces a stack limit and `!Mem.Alloc(above: N)` the total heap any call path may allocate; recursion needs `#MaxDepth(n)`, and dynamic calls need a sealed target set. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter InspectMemoryReport` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter stack_bound_`, one snapshot per refusal.

Found 2026-11-09 (G6Lead, probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Lead/ballots/probes/cycle/s19 and s20): a strong edge hidden in a closure is accepted and leaks. A feed owns a Close stream and a listener closure captures the feed strongly; E0221 accepts it, the program prints "end" and never "closed 7". Cause: SharedCycles.jet treats a `.Lambda` as a fresh value and skips places of function type. Safe code that forms such a cycle is refused by sema (or freed, if the type opts into collection), on O0, O1, O2 and web; a case proves the refusal, the weak-capture form (s22) still runs and closes, and a UI snapshot shows the diagnostic. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter SharedCycles/closure_strong_edge_` (refusal and the weak-capture s22 form) on O0, O1, O2 and web, and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter closure_strong_edge_cycle`.

Found 2026-11-09 (TlsLead): `mem.address_of(shared[0])` on a mutable Shared list fails in lowering with "ir.build unlowered: write place StaticCall of Shared<[Int]>". Sema either accepts the program and it lowers and runs the same on O0, O1, O2 and web, or refuses it with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot; a case proves it.

A raw-pointer fault (R0801 and the other raw-access stops) is reported at the line and column of the faulting access, not at the enclosing #Unsafe gate, and its report prints the range detail (the valid range and the attempted offset) its row declares. A case shows both at O0, O1, O2 and under --profile=hardened. (Found by G10Safe-1 in seed probes q68/q69 for #3645 c8 S2/S3; Main.) Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Unsafe/raw_fault_points_at_access` on O0, O1, O2 and `--profile=hardened`.

D-AUTOPIN1=A is built for browser-or-server placement and update notifications, which split from c7 on 2026-11-13. Sema records no browser-or-server placement fact and no update-notification choice yet; both need the web runtime contract (D-WEB-RUNTIME-API1, #6445). Each becomes a recorded choice with a reason, is shown by `jet inspect choices` and hovers, can be locked, and a broken lock is refused. Proof: a golden per kind and a UI snapshot for a broken lock.

cards.title: jet check is too slow for a large single unit: 9.2k Jetpack lines take 329 s (NixEval 5.5k = 195 s alone)
cards.body: Measured by the Jetpack port (#3590) with target/debug/jet (built 2026-09-26), each under a cgroup cap. jet check src/jetpack.jet on the assembled Jetpack unit: NixEval area only (5,539 lines) 195 s, 680 MB peak; Foundation+PackageModel only (3,663 lines) 79 s; both together (9.2k lines, master 31b1e0bf3) 329 s, 800 MB peak, 0 errors, 199 lints. Receipts: ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-bootstrap/lead-c3e0b738ad/check.receipt and 5efbbecdee/check.receipt. The port targets ~120k lines in one unit (mirroring Compiler/Bootstrap); at this rate a single check would take far longer than an hour, which blocks the per-slice proof loop and later the build-time performance cell. Note the binary is a debug build; release timings are unmeasured. Needs: profile where check time goes on this unit (the unit is available by re-running Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh) and a root fix.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jet check` on a large single unit roughly linear in source size, and stop it running out of memory. Today it blocks three things: the Jetpack per-slice proof loop (#3590), stage zero of self-hosting (#218 criterion 12), and later the build-time performance cell.

## Current state
Measured with the debug `target/debug/jet` (built 2026-09-26), under a cgroup cap. Release timings are unmeasured.

| Unit | Lines | Wall | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jetpack NixEval only | 5,539 | 195 s | 680 MB |
| Foundation + PackageModel | 3,663 | 79 s | — |
| Both (master 31b1e0bf3) | 9.2k | 329 s | 800 MB (0 errors, 199 lints) |
| Compiler front slice (70 files, 2.93 MB) | — | 39 min single-core, OOM-killed | 8 GB, no verdict |
| EnvModel unit (185 sources) | — | exceeds the 6 GB cap in ~8 s | — |

- The lexer slice (94 KB) takes 25 s. Receipts: `~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-bootstrap/lead-c3e0b738ad/check.receipt` and `5efbbecdee/check.receipt`.
- Root-cause lead (`~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/jet-packages-study.md` §3): cost follows content, not size. The NixEval prefix timings are:
  - Text (225 lines): 0.5 s.
  - Adding API types and NixJson (825 lines): 37.4 s.
  - Adding the Lexer and Parser (1,588 lines): 69.6 s.
  - Adding `Jetpack/NixEval/Source/Evaluator/Values.jet` (260 lines of recursive `NixEvalValue`/`NixEvalNative`/`NixEvalThunk` enums and impls): 180.2 s, i.e. +110.6 s.
  - Adding 1,796 lines of evaluator methods: only +15.9 s.
- Splitting into files or packages does not help: a 5-line app over NixEval takes 207.6 s on the first run and 209.7 s on an unchanged rerun.
- Receipts are never reused under systemd-run. The environment identity at `Source/ReceiptStore.rs:3566-3573` ignores the Nix temp variables but not `INVOCATION_ID`.
- The bootstrap assembles one compiler unit on purpose (`Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list`), and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet` carries the whole module graph into checking.

## Changes
1. Profile first. Run `perf record` (or the sema phase timers) with a release `jet check` on `Jetpack/NixEval` and on a synthetic recursive-enum fixture. Name the pass whose cost grows with the recursive type graph times its use sites; likely suspects are drop/copy/derive/structural-recursion or type-identity walks without memoization.
2. Fix it at the root in the shipped checker (`crates/jet-sema`, the bootstrap checker used for stage zero). Memoize per type identity, or compute the fixpoint once per SCC. Then make the same fix in `Compiler/JetSema` so the self-hosted checker never inherits the algorithm.
3. Add `INVOCATION_ID` to the receipt environment-ignore list (`ReceiptStore.rs:3571`) as an immediate fix. #2517 later deletes ReceiptStore and replaces it with per-module memoization.
4. Add the scaling regression `recursive_enum_check_scales_linearly` in `tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs`. Checking N and 4N use sites of a three-way recursive enum must take at most 5x the time, with a fixed memory ceiling.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases cli_compiler_speed/recursive_enum_check_scales_linearly`: passes.
- Measurement with a release build: `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area NixEval` finishes in under 20 s (today 195 s on a debug build) and stays under 1 GB peak. The receipt is recorded.
- `bash ~/.cache/jet-luna/slice-scaling.sh target/release/jet after lexer parser front`: the front slice finishes under the 6 GB cap with a verdict.
- An unchanged rerun under systemd-run replays the receipt.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the root cause is in the checker. The Rust bootstrap checker and Compiler/JetSema get the same fix in one build.

## Dependencies
None. This card unblocks #3590 and #218 stage zero.

Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: absorbed #3951, #2533; their criteria are carried here as [#n] rows.
Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: absorbed #3951, #2533; their criteria are carried here verbatim as [#n] rows.
Retargeted to the Jet compiler under the Rust freeze, 2026-10-01 (owner): the Rust compiler only gets stage-zero blockers, deletions and C-ABI runtime exports.

2026-09-30 data: Foundation area (73 sources incl. Compiler front end, ~25 claims) jet check: 1204 s timeout at 5.0G peak (not memory-bound); rerun at 5400 s pending. PackageModel unit jet run (108k lines): >3500 s, ~3.9G. Memory is no longer the limit; time is. Blocks all Jetpack stabilization.
Phase 0b plan build-out (2026-09-29, Opus 5.5): plan rewritten for the self-hosted direction with a runnable proof and batch key batch-jetc-sema.

2026-09-28 21:30: jet check on the EnvModel unit (185 Jetpack+Compiler front-end sources, ~113 test claims) exceeds the 6G per-check cap within ~8 s (journal: scope oom-kill, 6G peak); same for StoreCorePort earlier. Contained by the cgroup cap; machine unaffected. Full type checks of any area that includes the Compiler front end are infeasible under the current OOM policy until check memory drops; build-out continues on --syntax only.

Phase 0 triage 2026-09-28 (jetpack1a, Opus 5.5): E_BUILD. jet check on the assembled Jetpack unit is super-linear: 9.2k lines take 329 s, dominated by recursive-enum Values.jet (+110 s). This blocks the Jetpack per-slice loop and stage zero of self-hosting (the Rust checker is OOM on the Compiler front slice). Receipts are also never reused under systemd-run because INVOCATION_ID enters the environment identity. Evidence: Card log: JetPackagesStudy prefix timings (Values.jet +110.6 s); Source/ReceiptStore.rs:3568-3573 (env-identity ignore list lacks INVOCATION_ID); Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list + Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet (single-unit assembly)

Scale data point (JetCompilerRunPath): Rust jet check of the Jet compiler front slice (70 files, 2.93 MB) ran 39 min single-core and was OOM-killed at 8 GB without a verdict; a 94 KB lexer slice takes 25 s. This blocks stage zero of self-hosting (#218 criterion 12), not only Jetpack.

Triage 2026-09-28 (Luna 5.6 high legwork, Pip reviewed): RETARGET_JET. This is a compiler-loop performance defect, not Jetpack implementation policy: the Jet bootstrap intentionally assembles one compiler unit (sources.list:1-4) and its Driver carries the complete module graph into checking (Identity.jet:109-147). The measured regression is reported and still actionable, but release performance is unverified (bugs-4.json:64-80). Evidence: The card reports 329 seconds for a 9.2k-line assembled check and 195 seconds for the 5.5k-line NixEval slice at ~/.cache/jet-luna/triage/bugs-4.json:64-80; release timing is unverified. ; Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list:1-4 defines one unqualified Compiler unit and says the list is the only assembly order. ; Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:1-2 identifies the Jet front-end as parse, check, lower, and assemble. Jet target: Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet, Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet, Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list.

Also: check results are never reused between runs under systemd-run because the receipt environment identity includes INVOCATION_ID (ReceiptStore.rs:3568-3573 already ignores Nix temp variables for the same reason), and receipts are not stored for ../ path deps.

Root-cause lead from JetPackagesStudy (report ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/jet-packages-study.md section 3): check cost follows content, not size. NixEval prefix timings: Text 225 lines 0.5 s; +API types/NixJson 825 lines 37.4 s; +Lexer/Parser 1,588 lines 69.6 s; +Values.jet (260 lines: recursive NixEvalValue/NixEvalNative/NixEvalThunk enums and impls) 1,848 lines 180.2 s (+110.6 s); +1,796 lines of evaluator methods 196.1 s (+15.9 s). Splitting into files or packages does not help: a dependency is re-checked in full every time and nothing is reused between runs (5-line app over NixEval: 207.6 s first run, 209.7 s unchanged rerun). Suspect a whole-unit pass that scales with the recursive enum/type graph times use sites. A PhaseTiming profile is the next step.

criteria.text: A profile names the super-linear pass in the Jet checker (Compiler/JetSema) on the recursive NixEval enums, and a check of a fixture with 4N use sites takes at most 5x the N-site time with bounded memory.
A release `JET=jet jet Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet --area NixEval` finishes in under 20 s and 1 GB peak (from 195 s and 680 MB on a debug build). Proof: the committed receipt of that run.

The 30-variant named-payload `#Comparable` enum program (Examples/features/types/enum_many_variants) builds on every level within the compile-speed budget, with generated code size linear in variant count and derived equality, compare, Debug and cleanup bodies no longer exploding. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CompileBudget/enum_many_variants` with 12- and 30-variant rows.

Each kept generated-code compile-cost lever (derive trimming, explicit types, backend-specific trimming) has a before-and-after backend time on the corpus, a keep-or-drop decision and a passing level differential. Proof: a committed receipt per lever.

A `jet check` of a small program returns within 1 s of its result being known, even on a contended disk, and its receipt stays durable: the receipt write costs one barrier per check (objects first, then one fsync of the directory and index), or the write is handed off with the next command waiting on it. Today 0.35 s of compile is followed by 49-84 s of fsync under lane load.

cards.title: Compile-time surfaces leave prefix @ so @ can mean a live link
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-09-28: use `@` for checked live links (D-MEMREF1) and migrate completely away from `@` for compile time. The owner asked for a full suite of questions, including alternatives such as dunder names.

Inventory of current `@` uses (Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md, Examples):
1. Compile-time values and blocks: `@name :: expr`, `@ { }`, `#Static @LIMIT`. D-PREP-SURFACE2 already moves these to `prep { }` plus ordinary names; #3505 and #3520 own that cutover.
2. Compile-time branch and loop: `@if`, `@loop`, and declaration templates (S57, D-STRUCT-ONCE1).
3. Metadata roots: `@TYPE`, `@FUNCTION`, `@METHOD`, `@CLOSURE`, `@PROGRAM`, `@PACKAGE`, `@SOURCE`, `@VALUE`, `@TYPES`, and `@PHASE` (D-META-REFLECT2, D-PREP-SURFACE2).
4. Fact members: `T.@layout`, `@name`, `@fields`, `@range`, `@dimension`, `@measure`, `@exactness`, `value.@origin`, and `f.@effects`, plus the overlapping `T.reflect()` (D-LAYOUT-FACTS1, D-FACT-READ1, D-TRACK-ORIGIN1).
5. Build facts: `@build.os`, `profile`, `package.name`/`version`, `settings.*`, and `stamp.*` (D-ONCE-AT1, D-CONF-MODULE1).
6. Const generic binder: `<@N: Int>` (D-CONSTGEN1, #3505).
7. Fences: `@[ … ]@` (D-EACH1, D-FENCE-GLYPH1, D-FENCE-RANGE1).
8. Compile-time function marker: `@fn` (D-FOUND-LITERAL1).
9. Non-compile-time uses: infix package refs `target@provider#version`, `host@root`, and the command home files `@run.jet`, `@build.jet`, `@dev.jet`, and `@test.jet` (D-JPK-REF1, D-JPK-OSHOST1, card #1866). D-ONCE-AT1 also reserved an infix 'at a machine' form.

The ballots here pick the family and each item's spelling. After ratification, one coherent cutover migrates the parser, sema, formatter, grammars, diagnostics, examples, and spec together (greenfield rule). It sequences with #3505/#3520 and the self-hosting port (#218).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Take every compile-time meaning off prefix `@`, so that in code `@` means only a D-MEMREF1 checked live link. Do it in one cutover of parser, sema, formatter, grammars, teaching diagnostics, examples and spec.

## Current state
- Ratified and landed: D-PREP-SURFACE2, D-PREP-BRANCH1, D-PREP-FN1 (`prep { }`, `prep if/loop/fn`), D-FENCE2 (`<: … :>`), D-CONSTGEN2 and D-AT-INFIX1. The Jet parser teaches E0388 for the retired `@if/@loop/@fn/@ { }` (`Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Statements.jet:374-392`).
- Still open with recommended option A: D-COMPILER-NS1 (the family: plain word `prep` plus a `compiler.` namespace), D-META-ROOT3 (`compiler.type/function/method/closure/program/package_info/source/value/types/phase`, marked facts become record fields, `T.reflect()` retires, `reflect.of(value)` stays), D-BUILD-FACT2 (build facts) and D-NAME-SPLICE1 (computed declaration names and declaration metadata).
- Remaining prefix-`@` code paths in the Jet parser: `@name ::` comptime constants (`Parser/Entry.jet:148-150`, `Parser/Items.jet:994-998`), `@` marker metadata (`Parser/Declarations/Markers.jet:54-58`), and the `@`-headed prep recovery arms (`Statements.jet:233-236, 399, 431`; `Declarations/Markers.jet:150`). Metadata roots (`@TYPE` …), fact members (`T.@layout` …) and `@build.*` still exist as described in the card inventory.
- Non-compile-time infix uses (`target@provider#version`, `host@root`, `@run.jet` home files) are out of scope and keep their meaning.

## Changes (written for option A on all four ballots)
1. After ratification, record the complete old-to-new mapping in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs`, `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` and the Jet syntax registry under `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry`.
2. `Compiler/JetLexer` and `Compiler/JetParser`: parse `compiler.` roots as ordinary calls, marked facts as fields, build facts per D-BUILD-FACT2 and computed names per D-NAME-SPLICE1. Retired `@` forms are not Jet syntax and get no teaching diagnostic; E0388's teaching is removed under #4148 c4. Prefix `@place` parses as a D-MEMREF1 link.
3. `Compiler/JetSema`: resolve the `compiler.` namespace through the prelude (`#NoPrelude` opts out) and route it to the existing metadata path (#3520).
4. Mirror the parser in `crates/jet-parser` so the bootstrap still parses the corpus. Migrate the formatter, `jet devtools grammars`, `Examples/`, `Core/`, `Docs/` and UI snapshots in the same commit.

## Proof
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/at_compile_time_retired.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `cargo test --test selfhost_parser` passes.
- Jet slice check: `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` reports no diagnostic in `Compiler/JetLexer` or `Compiler/JetParser` (map through `~/.cache/jet-luna/compiler-bootstrap/compiler.map.json`).
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=comptime cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=reflection cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` both pass with identical AOT and `jet run` output.
- `jet devtools grammars` regenerates with no remaining `@` compile-time rule.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-front`: a lexer/parser surface cutover plus the Rust parser mirror.

cards.body:
Owner 2026-09-28: the standard library must be written in Jet under Core/; port whatever the Rust Prelude files still own. Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/prelude-core-gap.json (Opus 5.5 study, file:line citations). Move every semantic item (validation, defaults, formats, protocol logic, limits, error meaning) into the named Core/*.jet home; keep only policy-free provider leaves in Rust (raw syscalls, socket I/O, vetted TLS/SQLite/Parquet/Wasmtime engines). Migrate every route (AOT emit, JIT, interpreter, web where applicable) to call the one Jet meaning (I9) and delete the duplicated Rust policy in the same cutover. Proof needs a compiler build that embeds the edited Core sources, so this is blocked by #3663 (master does not compile) and #3591.

Files: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs.
Homes: Core/http/{client,http,h1,h2,hpack,cookie}.jet. Resolve the retry divergence (Jet retries PUT/DELETE, Rust only safe methods) to one documented rule. Delete dead client-handle builder code and JetHTTPAmbientDeadline::push if no caller remains.

cards.plan:
**Goal.** The HTTP client's meaning moves into Core:
- HTTP/1.1 framing, HTTP/2 framing and HPACK
- cookies with public-suffix rules
- redirects, proxies, pool/per-origin limits, DNS TTL, phase timeouts
- header/form/multipart encoding and retries

It lives in `Core/http/{client,http,h1,h2,hpack,cookie}.jet`. Rust keeps socket I/O, TLS (rustls) and gzip inflate leaves only.

**Current state.**
- `Core/http/` has `client.jet` (518 lines), `http.jet` (1227) and `server.jet` (91). There is no `h1`/`h2`/`hpack`/`cookie.jet`.
- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs` (5534 lines) holds the policy. The card body lists 18 semantic items with line ranges, which this plan keeps:
  - ambient deadline :18-67, limit constants :68-78, pool :104-276
  - client builders :283-700, cookies/PSL :704-1118
  - H2 :1180-1660/:3915-4224, DNS cache :1746-1785, PEM :1842-1941
  - timeouts :2088-2166, send parts :2167-2530, forbidden headers :2531-2588
  - form/multipart :2589-2644/:5413-5534, redirects :2645-3020, proxy :3021-3078
  - H1 write :3180-3511, head parse :3774-3914, body framing :4225-4562, HPACK :5003-5412
- Retry divergence: `Core/http/client.jet:232` `retryable_method` retries GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE/PUT/DELETE, while Rust retries safe methods only.
- `Core/http/http.jet` already has `valid_header_name`/`has_ctl` (:1043/:1051), `form_encode`/`query_encode` (:716-769) and `parse_response`/`content_length` (:474/:870).
- #3663 was fixed in 6fc6f3862.

**Changes (one sub-module per patch).**
1. `h1.jet` (new): request encoding, upload body writing, the streaming head reader, and `BodyFraming` (content-length/chunked/close) readers over a byte-stream leaf.
2. `hpack.jet` (new): static table, integer/string/Huffman codec and the decoder dynamic table. `h2.jet` (new): frame read/write, connection settings/flow control and the response body reader.
3. `cookie.jet` (new): `CookieJar`, date parse, domain/path match, and the PSL `registrable_domain` over a generated constant table (F2).
4. `client.jet`:
   - pool/origin limits, the DNS TTL cache and phase timeouts
   - redirect follow with body-replay rules, and proxy/no_proxy selection
   - reconcile the limit constants with the existing `C_MAX_*`
5. `http.jet`: the forbidden-request-header list and multipart encoding.
6. Retry rule, kept as the one documented rule: RFC 9110 idempotent methods (current Jet `retryable_method`), and only when the body is replayable and no response bytes arrived. The Rust safe-only branch is deleted. Document it in the `client.jet` doc comment.
7. PEM helpers move to `Core/net/tls.jet`, shared with #3666.
8. Delete the ported Rust, the dead client-handle builders and `JetHTTPAmbientDeadline::push` if uncalled, plus the Jet-owned `core.http` dispatcher rows. Regenerate the tables.

**Proof.**
- The commands in add_criteria.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases http/` and `cargo test --test http_dependency_audit`: pass.
- A perf cell is required only if the matched networking battery covers the client. Rerun it and keep the Rust route on any loss.

**Batch.** `batch-core-net`: Core http/net source and its Rust Prelude twin, needing one build and the net retest.

**Dependencies.** None open. It shares the PEM parser with #3666, and whichever lands first owns `Core/net/tls.jet` PEM.

(1) Status lines with an empty or doubled-space reason are accepted and the reason never decides success; today all are rejected (http.jet:569-611).
(2) No silent defaults: case-sensitive methods; typed results for content_length, version, method and reason, so "Content-Length: 1x" fails; header setters refuse invalid names visibly (http.jet:225, 244, 828).
(3) Distinct HTTPError kinds for request-line faults, plus one documented error-to-status table.
(4) The h1 step returns NeedMore, Done or Error with consumed counts; zero progress stops with a typed error instead of spinning (live hang at 3 bytes per read); truncation differs from a clean close; leftover bytes start the next message (keep-alive); chunked framing with trailers is decoded in Jet.
(5) A bounded pump compacts and grows to the head limit, then refuses with a typed 431/413. The same carry-the-partial-line rule should give Core a streaming lines() over any reader; Core in Jet has only whole-file read_lines (Core/files/files.jet:932).
(6) One rule for repeated header fields; case-insensitive lookup allocates nothing.
(7) The server serializer sends Date; the MIME table moves to Core and gains mp4, webm, mp3 and pdf.
(8) Every fixture gives identical results fed 1, 2, 3, 7 or all bytes per read, built by a framing-aware test helper (D-TESTKIT1).
(9) A golden streaming proxy relays chunked bodies, and a handler can stream a response body (no source-facing streaming response exists today).

cards.title: Project jobs run the same on every tier: `jet <job>` and `jet jobs` dispatch, typed arguments, `after:` order, validation, freshness and inspection
cards.body:
Destination: a #Job declared once runs by name (`jet <job>`, `jet jobs <job>`, `jet run -- <job>`) with typed scalar parameters from argv, its `after:` predecessors in order, validation before any effect, declared input/output freshness, and one process and job identity model for inspection and lifecycle events, with byte-identical output from a built binary and from `jet jobs`.

cards.title: Sync engine: query, mutation and action kinds, app.live, one owning module, and the bootstrap and local-only design
cards.body:
Owner note (2026-09-28): "I want a jet-native tool that functions like convexdb as an excellent, world class sync engine" (linked video https://youtu.be/pRf8_40EDtM is Tom Delalande's Linear case study, not a Convex video).

Harvest (mine-for-jet report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28):
- Linear (video 4:12-8:26): the client downloads the workspace once, then every read and write is local; one observable state re-renders views; the engine turns local changes into transactions and streams remote changes over a socket, so local and remote changes look identical; the server accepts or rejects each transaction and the client rolls back on reject; large workspaces forced lazy loading and a partial bootstrap; engineers can switch sync off to prototype locally; there is no plug-and-play engine, and it takes several full-time engineers to maintain.
- Convex (https://docs.convex.dev/functions/runtimes): queries and mutations must be deterministic (seeded Math.random, Date.now frozen per call) so the system can retry and re-run them; non-deterministic work such as fetch lives only in actions.

Jet already ratified most of the mechanism: D-LIVEQUERY1 (footprint-tracked live queries over -[DB.Read]> functions, #Transact write-set invalidation, pushes to Signal<T>), D-EFFDBREAD1, D-SYNC1 (CRDT values over the live channel), D-DBPOLICY1 (row policies below app code), D-DX-QUERY1 (optimistic mutation with rollback), D-DX-SERVERFN1 (typed calls derived from App actions), D-QUERY-LIVE1 (incremental maintenance). Jet's advantage Convex cannot copy: effect rows can prove at compile time that a query only reads, that a mutation is replay-safe, and that only actions touch the network; the same Jet validation code runs on client and server (I9).

Current state is far from that: the shipped example does not compile, Core/app is string-keyed, and app/web duplicate the surface (#3700, #3701).
cards.plan:
**Goal**
A Jet-native local-first sync engine at Convex/Linear grade (owner note 2026-09-28: "a jet-native tool that functions like convexdb as an excellent, world class sync engine"). It covers client cache and partial bootstrap, local reads and writes as transactions, server accept or reject with rollback, socket fan-out, an offline queue and a local-only mode. Query, mutation and action are compiler-checked effect classes.

**Current state**
- Ratified mechanism: D-LIVEQUERY1 (footprint-tracked live queries over `-[DB.Read]>`, `#Transact` invalidation, `Signal<T>` push), D-EFFDBREAD1, D-SYNC1 (CRDT values), D-DBPOLICY1, D-DX-QUERY1 (optimistic mutation plus rollback), D-DX-SERVERFN1 and D-QUERY-LIVE1.
- Code: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Database.jet:31-41 tags `query`/`query_one`/`live` as `DB.Read` and `execute` as `DB.Write`. Effect checks are in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet. Core/sync/sync.jet exists. Core/app is string-keyed, and the D-LIVEQUERY1 example does not compile (#3700). app and core.web duplicate the surface (#3701).

cards.title: Diagnostic readability sweep: rewrite every active diagnostic in plain words (Opus 5.5 workers)
cards.body:
Destination: every active diagnostic reads in plain words, enforced so it cannot regress:
- What names the learner's specific problem, using the names in their code.
- Why gives the reason in one or two plain sentences.
- Fix gives a concrete edit or command.
- No internal vocabulary: decision IDs, constant names, 'unit', byte offsets, stage names. That material lives in `jet explain CODE --verbose` and `--json`.

Why it matters: owner-directed P0 (2026-09-28, learnability report F17). A census of 813 active rows found 218 with a placeholder Why, 297 whose What repeats the internal meaning, and 287 with decision IDs in user-facing text. The research basis is Becker et al. 2019, Barik et al. 2018 and Ko et al. 2004.

The authority is the diagnostic registry; Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet is generated from it.

Related cards (2026-11-15 split): stop locations and traces #6915, error values in handlers #6916, progress output #6917, user-visible text case #6734, IOError #6881, ComputeError #6624.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Owner-directed P0 (2026-09-28, learnability report F17). Every active diagnostic reads in plain words:
- **What** names the learner's specific problem, using the names in their code.
- **Why** gives the reason in one or two plain sentences, with no placeholder.
- **Fix** gives a concrete edit or command.
- No internal vocabulary: decision IDs, constant names, "unit", "source bytes", byte offsets, key=value dumps, stage names. That material moves to `jet explain CODE --verbose` and `--json`.

The rubric is enforced so the sweep cannot regress.

## Current state
- The authority is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`. `Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs:9-10` generates `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet` from it.
- The 2026-09-28 census found 813 active rows: 218 with the placeholder Why "The registered <stage> rule applies here" (for example `Diagnostics.jet:7-8`, E0001/E0002), 297 whose What repeats Meaning, and 287 with decision IDs in human text.
- E0114 (probe p08) still says "its final statement produces no value … statements and semicolon-terminated expressions yield unit" (`tests/ui/missing_return.stderr`, `tests/ui/total_guard_missing_value.stderr`). It is produced only in Rust (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration.rs:969`, `CheckerCore/blocks.rs:199`); JetSema has no E0114.
- `tests/diagnostics_format.rs` already checks row completeness and sentence case (`:13-75`), but not placeholder text or decision IDs.
- Rows owned by other open P0 cards are sequenced first: #3715 (E0121), #3718 (authority errors) and #3719 (unclosed delimiter).

## Changes
1. **Docs.** Write the rubric into `Docs/spec/diagnostics.md`.
2. **Validator.** Add `every_active_diagnostic_reads_in_plain_words` to `tests/diagnostics_format.rs`, and apply the same checks in `generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs` so generation fails on a violation.
3. **Rewrite.** Rewrite the rows in `Diagnostics.jet` using disjoint code-range lanes run by `opus-worker` (Claude Opus 5.5), with one integration owner. Update the dynamic message builders in `crates/jet-parser` and `crates/jet-sema` that fill those rows, then regenerate `DiagnosticRows.jet`.
4. **E0114.** Add E0114 to JetSema (the final-statement check in the block/return analysis) and have it name the uncovered path's condition. Mirror the path-naming in `crates/jet-sema/.../blocks.rs` for the shipped binary.
5. **Snapshots.** Re-bless every affected UI snapshot one fixture at a time (`JET_UI_FILTER=<f> UPDATE_EXPECT=<f>`, with `UPDATE_EXPECT_REASON`). The orchestrator reviews each change as text.
6. **Probes.** Re-run the report's Appendix A probes on a fresh build. A probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test diagnostics_format`: all tests pass, including the new rubric test, which is the census. Log its counts on the card.
- `cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` and `cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots lint_snapshots`: pass after reviewed re-blessing.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/missing_return.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.
- Every lane returns `Tools/agent/lane-check.sh` `CHECK OK`, and the lanes are listed on the card.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: diagnostic registry text and sema message builders, proven by the UI/format suites in one retest pass.

## Dependencies
#3715, #3718 and #3719 (all P0, ready) own overlapping rows and land first.

cards.title: Last use moves everywhere; kept parameters inferred; x.move() and x.copy() are the exact pins
cards.body: D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (ratified; owner comment: 'Compiler chooses if unmarked, programmer can manually put sigils where desired for exact. full control'). Parent #3741. Evidence: probe p34/p35 — storing a read parameter deep-copies even at the caller's last use (~20% slower builder).
cards.plan:
1. Last use of a name moves in every position (bindings, fields, args, collection elements, captures) with no mark.
2. Infer per parameter whether the body keeps it (stores/returns/sends); keeping params lower by value; callers at last use move.
3. Exported functions: formatter writes `&&T` on kept params (D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A) (pin; body edit cannot silently change API).
4. Written `x.move()` / `x.copy()` are exact pins (D-COPY-MOVE-SPELL1=A, D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A): `x.move()` must move (error if x used after), `x.copy()` always copies now. Unmarked = compiler choice.
5. Hover/jet doc show inferred keep; `jet audit copies` lists every remaining copy.
6. Paired perf cell: builder via kept param vs inline vs Rust.

Zero unjustified copies (owner order 2026-11-14). Every .copy() in Compiler, Core, Jetpack and Tools is either removed (moved at its last use, borrowed, the owner restructured, or a name made an interned id) or carries a justification row in the copy ledger. A row names the copy site and a paired two-program measurement on the reference machine showing that the copy makes that path faster, in wall time or peak memory, than the copy-free spelling. A copy that is neutral or slower is not justified. Tests/Guards/copy_ratchet.jet fails on any copy without a justified row, and the count of unjustified copies is 0. Baseline 2026-11-14: 6,686 explicit copies in 637 Compiler files, none justified. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter copy_ratchet` reports 0 unjustified copies.

Implicit copies count too. The compiler reports every deep copy it inserts without a written .copy() as a site list, from jet check --trace or a lint, and the same zero-unjustified rule and guard apply to it. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Copies/implicit_copy_site_list`, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter copy_ratchet` counts implicit copies.

No copy ceiling ever rises. No SUB, rebase or lander fix-up raises a ledger ceiling or adds a row without a justification; the guard and the lander refuse it. Main raised SerdeItems.jet to 50 in the stack127 fix-ups on 2026-11-14; that rise is undone. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter copy_ratchet` refuses a raised ceiling or an unjustified row (a negative-control case), and the SerdeItems.jet ceiling is back below 50.

Removing copies never makes Jet slower. Each copy-removal batch shows the cold self-compile wall time and peak memory, measured on the batch compiler, at or below the batch before it. Proof: each copy-removal batch receipt lists cold self-compile wall time and peak memory, each at or below the batch before it.

One copy meaning: `.copy()` forks every component whose type has a fork meaning (Clock, or any type with __fork), recursively, whatever holds it (list, option, struct, tuple, map, enum payload or a nesting of these), by one type-driven walk; today only list and option are covered. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter copy_forks_` with one case per holder kind on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Failure model: three-state outcomes, failure ceilings, visible failure points, dbg and hop trails
cards.body:
Destination: Jet's ratified failure law is built end to end. `T? E!` matches as three states (.Val, .None, .Err; D-OUTCOME-SHAPE1=A, done here). Failures pass up by themselves and None never does. A written failure contract is an optional ceiling and failure sets follow the effect law (D-FAIL-PUBSIG1=A, D-FAIL-EFFECT1=A). Readers see failure points through tools, and teams may require marks (D-FAIL-VISIBLE1=A). A function names its own error cases (D-ERR-CASES1=A, D-FAIL-INFER-UNION1=A). `dbg` works in pure code (D-DBG1=A). `err.as<T>()` recovers a typed failure (D-ERR-TRAIT1=A).

Why it matters: failures are the most common control flow in real programs; each gap here is a place where a beginner writes a conversion by hand or an expert cannot see where a failure leaves.

Spec: Docs/spec/spec.md failure sections; probes: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3838/.

Owned elsewhere: the editor's faint `?` inlay hint (#4917), publish's failure-set version rule (#6860).
cards.plan:
1. Patterns on `T? E!` accept `.Val(x)`, `.None`, `.Err(e)` directly; exhaustiveness over the three.
2. Nested `.Ok(...)` form: greenfield cutover — migrate all sources; the old form gets no teaching diagnostic or jet fix (owner order).
3. Failures keep automatic pass-up; None never leaves a function unless written (`?` on the optional) or `.or_err("why")`.
4. `??` resolves either state.
5. Optional internal single-tag layout only with a paired perf cell.

cards.title: Elegance audit fixes: diagnostic registry and keyword table consistency
cards.body:
Folds five small findings from Docs/audits/elegance-audit-2026-09-30.md into one session-sized card. Each member card's body holds its evidence and exact sites; the member cards are closed into this one.

Members (closed into this card): #3988, #3990, #3992, #4017, #4018. Read each member's body and log for repros, sites and evidence. Board prep 2026-10-01 (plan by TowerPrep, applied by TowerCloser); estimate 1.5 sessions.

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):
D-SURFACE-BUDGET1=A
Derive active counts from canonical syntax/marker/fact/CLI rows; only owner decision raises language-surface ceilings; retirement lowers counts; keyword list regenerated rather than copied; ballot reports before/after; public Core functions reported by module/trend, NEVER hard-gated; guard mutation and generation fixtures prove these distinctions.
Paths: Tools/agent surface counting/guard and ballot before-after report; Jet syntax registry/keyword list; Prelude/{Markers,Facts}.jet; Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CLICommands.jet; public Core function inventory trends
Registry/spec/UI/goldens: Legacy crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs LEXICAL_LEDGER and Syntax/package_files.rs JET_KEYWORD_LIST are reference; Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Syntax.jet keyword list currently stale (pub/tag/policy/marker names/None). Canonical Jet registry projection, ceiling rows carry approved decision IDs, D-SURFACE-BUDGET1=A. No second hand-maintained table.; Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md ceiling decision rows; keyword reference/editor grammar generation; AGENTS I7/counted surface guard; dated owner-feedback proposal records final report-only Core count; No new user diagnostic mandated; guard fixture failures for unauthorized +1 surface count and keyword drift; generated CLI/editor registry snapshots; Count before/after keyword/sigil/built-in marker/fact/CLI addition/retirement; adding public Core fn changes report only and never fails gate; regenerate actual keyword list and editor consumers
Timing: TOOLS/JET REGISTRY PORT NOW; preserve one canonical registry through handover, derive real active counts. Minimal registry port seam may be mirrored only if needed for port consumers under #29 and tracked dies-at-cutover. #28 Sol author/Opus review.
Open prerequisite/conflict: Posted old proposal gated library functions: ratified revision explicitly removes that restriction. Historic 43/49/61 counts stale after marker/pub/Learn retirements: derive actual counts, do not pin old numbers. alias retained under B; no alias keyword decrement.

cards.title: Principle: a value can owe a transition (one debt concept for must-use, single-use, and tasks)
cards.body:
Elegance principle hunt, 2026-10-01. Jet checks several kinds of value debt with separate rules, words, and escapes: `#MustUse` (E0419, discard `.drop("reason")`), `#SingleUse` (E0140-E0143, discard `consume(x)` inside `#Unsafe("reason")`), and a bound task that owes a join (L1101, discharge `.join()` or `.detach()`). Ratified D-CONC-UNIT1=A already moved tasks onto the single-use obligation checker. Typestate and taint already share one flow store, `Facts

` (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/FlowFacts.rs:1-80`). `GateKind` already has `DutyDrop` and `StateTransition` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs:671-672`). Users cannot declare a debt for their own types. Closed-book prediction test: 6 hit, 0 near, 0 miss. Owner choice: ballot D-OWES1.

cards.title: One lane type: width-parameterized and scalable SIMD vectors
cards.body:
Owner request: start from what hardware can do and turn it into high-level constructs, keeping both a bottom-up and a top-down path. Mojo defines every scalar and vector as one library type `SIMD[dtype, width]` (`Int = Scalar[DType.int]`, Modular commit 99e3a880 `std/simd.mojo:115-240,443-468`).

Today Jet has a closed family of named lanes (D-SIMD3=B: F32x4, F32x8, F64x2, F64x4, I32x4, I32x8, I64x2, I64x4, U8x16, U8x32; Examples/features/lowlevel/simd_wide.jet). A width cannot be a parameter, so generic code over "the widest native width" cannot be written, and vector-length-agnostic hardware (Arm SVE, RISC-V V) has no spelling. Const generics (D-CONSTGEN1=A, #3505) make a parameterized lane type possible.

Ballot D-LANES1 decides the lane surface.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-LANES1. Implementation waits on #3505 const generics; then define the lane type in Core over compiler intrinsics, migrate the named family in one cutover, and add SVE/RVV lowering where the target supports it.

cards.title: Use newer CPU instructions in one binary: multiversioned functions and typed intrinsics
cards.body:
Owner request: leverage what hardware can do now (bottom-up), give experts direct access to machine instructions, and stay forward-facing for new hardware.

Today D-FFI-ASM-CPU1=B builds for the target baseline and needs explicit CPU flags for newer instructions; a shipped binary cannot use AVX-512 when present and fall back otherwise. Experts can reach instructions only through audited `#FFI(asm)`; the compiler-only `__core_intrinsic` namespace (D-CORE-CALL1) is closed to users. Prior art: Rust `#[target_feature]` + `is_x86_feature_detected!` + `core::arch`; GCC `target_clones`; Google Highway dynamic dispatch; Mojo `CompilationTarget` queries and `comptime if`; Odin `@(enable_target_feature=...)` and `base:intrinsics` (265 procedures).

Ballot D-CPU-DISPATCH1 decides how code opts into newer instructions.
cards.plan: D-CPU-DISPATCH1=A is ratified. Add the chosen target-feature function form, a per-process feature probe in the Prelude, safe typed intrinsics in Core for the chosen ISAs, and dispatch on every tier.

cards.title: Co-editing one program from text and Canvas (EYG shared-tree lesson)
cards.body:
Owner request: EYG sends the AST over the wire, which could let a text editor and a visual blueprint editor edit the same program at once; Mojo has no traditional AST and parses straight to MLIR. Take the best of both: a lighter compiler and blueprint-style editing.

EYG's IR is a closed node list encoded as DAG-JSON with content-addressed references; text is one optional parser (commit 75f09475, `packages/gleam_ir/src/eyg/ir/tree.gleam:15-44`, `spec/README.md:44-92`). Mojo's parser emits the MLIR `lit` dialect (MojoCompilerWalkthrough.md:136-138). Jet parses text to an AST without lossless trivia (formatter re-emits canonical syntax), Canvas edits go through source transactions (D-CANVAS-RAD1=A), and no stable node identity crosses the LSP boundary.

Ballot D-PROGRAM-FORM1 decides the shared program form.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-PROGRAM-FORM1. If A wins: on a stale Canvas revision, resolve the edit's anchors in the newest revision, replay, format, re-check, publish atomically; report anchor conflicts. The self-hosted front-end shape (Mojo's no-AST lesson) stays an internal implementation choice.

cards.title: C header import depth: read real headers with a full C front end
cards.body:
Owner request: use Zig's cross-compatibility as a wedge: import C headers directly, act as a drop-in C/C++ compiler, build foreign projects in Jetpack, and export C ABI libraries.

Today `jet cc`/`jet c++` exist and use the pinned Jetpack toolchain (`crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1333-1349`); `#Export(c)` exists (Examples/features/packages/library_loadable); foreign builds are on #1347; cross toolchains on #758/#1058/#1060. The weak link is header import: `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CBind.rs:1-12` is a focused std-only parser that maps scalars, strings, pointers, slices, and layout records, and skips the rest. Zig's `@cImport`/`translate-c` reads real headers through a full C front end, including macros, unions, bitfields, function pointers, and variadics; Zig probe Z6 cross-compiled C to Windows and AArch64-musl from one host.

Ballot D-CIMPORT1 decides the header engine.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-CIMPORT1. Then extend the binder, run it against a corpus (zlib, sqlite3, libcurl, SDL3) for every supported target, and report unmapped declarations with registered diagnostics.

Live probe: a wrong fn C.strlen declaration passes V's checker and fails only as raw TinyCC output on generated src.c ('too many arguments to function'). Jet's checked binder + overlay is the beat vector; real-header import here is what makes it true. Related probe card #5037; C source translation ballot D-CSRC-IMPORT1 on #5034. cards.title: Portable sandboxed app format: what Jet ships to run anywhere (Docker/Nix/WebAssembly replacement)
cards.body:
Owner direction (2026-10-01): Jet should be portable and better than WebAssembly, and replace Docker and Nix. EYG ships a checked program and lets the host supply effects.

Jet today: native binaries (trusted code), OCI images projected from environments (D-ENV-IMAGE1=A), wasm32-wasip2 (D-WASISRV1=A, #1914), sandbox components (--target=sandbox), Wasmtime plugins (D-PLUGIN1=A, D-DEP-WASM1=A), Hangar store and build-step sandbox (D-JPK-SANDBOX2=D). Output.Bundle is the closed catch-all kind for distributables (D-ECO-OUTPUT-KINDS1=A). The portable-platform proposal (JPM/1, JPH/1) is unratified with no prior card.

Ballot D-PORTABLE1 decides the portable app form of Bundle.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-PORTABLE1. Then specify the .jetapp layout, host selection, confinement reporting (confined/verified/TRUSTED), and grant storage; paired cell against an OCI container and plain wasmtime on startup, size, and throughput.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work (non-Linux OS, AArch64 or other targets) is frozen for now. CardClose-1's ready sweep listed this card's remaining blocker as cross-platform.

Folded #4762 "Extensible hardware requirements with trusted scan, target facts and pre-entry admission" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of parent #4195 (Portable sandboxed app format: what Jet ships to); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: D-HOST-CAPS1=A Proposes Core Hardware, HardwareKind, HardwareRequirement, HardwareProbe and ScanContext as specified in the explainer. Hardware contains main memory, storage and typed device entries. Target gains hardware; every Output gains target, requires and uses. Package-defined kinds use pure type-owned satisfies/coarse methods; scan probes are separately trust-granted. $build.hardware shares D-CONF's typed fact plane and merge law; $build.cpu remains the CPU entry. Host observations, grants and kind/probe package identities determine launch admission/cache identity, never a producer's asserted facts. Free amounts are checked before each GPU job. Implementation areas: Core hardware typ

Independent witness (Blow, cKyrT8OVbDo 00:00-09:40): untrusted plugins should share structured data without serialize/parse, get write permission only to chosen memory without a separate process, and a plugin that crashes inside shared lock-free code after incrementing a counter leaves the host unrecoverable; containers exist because the OS stopped reliably rerunning programs; wanted: one portable, sandboxed, backend-neutral instruction format. Today D-PLUGIN1=A / D-DEP-WASM1=A accept copied boundary values as a loss; the portable proposal (Docs/proposals/jetpack/portable-platform-specification.md H-ISP-002, L-11a, CV-15; unratified) already specifies sealed zero-copy and trap termination, which this corroborates. Research lead for C2 measurement (not verified): in-process hardware write isolation (x86 protection keys, Arm permission overlays) for verified guests, with known limits (few keys, no speculative-read protection). Local IPC culture serializes to JSON even on one machine (CK-07): include a large structured value crossing the boundary in the C2 measurement against wasm and OCI.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.title: Authority law: thirteen roots in one table, the word authority, transitive Panic and memory denials, one policy ladder, and contain/harden
cards.body:
Destination: the authority model is one closed table of thirteen roots with FFI language leaves (D-AUTHORITY-ROOTS1=A), read by every checker with no private copy; no surface says capability for permissions (D-AUTHORITY-WORD1=A); Panic and memory denials are enforced transitively and take arguments (D-NOPANIC1=A, D-AUTHORITY-MEM2=A); one policy surface names every audited escape (D-ONCE-GATE1=A); and the package keys `contain` and `harden` work as ratified.

Why: an authority promise that one checker reads differently from another, or that an unknown call can discharge, is not a promise.

Source: the P04 ratified-contract scope (Main's ruling 2026-11-13: the proofs are tests/cases rows, not the proposed tests/ratified suite), with #1566, #1894 and #2846. Sandbox items went to #6930, tags to #6931, crypto to #6925, native sandbox enforcement to #6697 and netrc to #6632.

cards.title: Close package roots, typed configuration and environment ownership
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Reserved Package source-file law; Jet root noun for the complete checked graph; runtime: package field for runtime PATH deps; First-class cargo build field: Recipe.cargo(lock:); What should changing a JetOS machine feel like?; Should packages and JetOS live in one project?; How much must plain jet check prove?; Build/config: one plane of typed facts; Facts in text, actions in the function; One meaning for the word profile; What jet split does with inline Package facts; formatter: passthrough for non-.jet files; jet split/fold law (Fold-only); Public typed package model for Jet tools; Build file versions without lost locks or rewritten evidence; Package policy and exception source surface

**Decision IDs:** D-ECO-FILEROOT1, D-ECO-ROOTNAME2, D-ECO11, D-ECO2, D-ECO-JETOS2, D-ECO1, D-CHECKSCOPE1, D-CONF-PLANE1, D-CONF-SPLIT1, D-CONF-WORD1, D-ECO-SPLITPOLICY1, D-ECO12, D-ECO13, D-PACKAGE-MODEL1, D-BUILDCOMPAT1, D-JPK-POLICYSURFACE1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-BUILDCOMPAT1:** Use version in a clear scope, preserve originals, and automatically read supported older data without changing its meaning. Version-1 locks from older Jet releases remain readable.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Jet has registered unsupported lock-version diagnostics and refuses unknown required marker meanings (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:11310-11312). Complete original-evidence preservation, linked readable views and automatic older-version translation in Rust and Jet were not established.
- **D-CHECKSCOPE1:** Resolve the owning project and every declared runnable output; Validate imports, reachable Core closure, canonical TIR, and every applicable execution-tier lowering; Preserve isolated single-file checks.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust project check explicitly sets inspect-only execute:false/no authority grant (crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:3477-3481); tests/project_check.rs is the consumer suite. Jet CLI exposes file check (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Host.jet:47-61; Front.jet:502), not an established all-runnable-output/workspace check.
- **D-CONF-PLANE1:** Adopt the model; Configuration is the program's knowledge about itself: every build fact (identity, machine, profile, settings, policy) is a typed value on one registered plane, with one contribution law and one audit command; The ratified role-typed Package shape becomes the only manifest vocabulary; the legacy flat parser is deleted. build.os, which already works this way, becomes the plane's first row; Later D-CONF ballots (fact reads, settings, contribution law) land on this substrate.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust folded fact vocabulary is registered (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:36-37). Jet has folded snapshots (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet:462-464), but loader explicitly lacks declared manifest settings (Expressions/FactReads.jet:640-643); complete typed single fact plane/cutover missing.
- **D-CONF-SPLIT1:** Manifest text is the complete index of what is configurable: every fact is declared there with its type and default. fn build performs actions — probes, steps, generated code — and may contribute a value to a declared fact; Every computed contribution is recorded in .jet/lock and named by jet explain. fn build can never mint an undeclared fact; The pushback the owner asked for is honest: a flat facts-in-text-only rule fails, because a probed toolchain or a find() member list is only knowable by computation; The law keeps those as computed contributions instead of banning them.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust pipeline records contributions/generated modules in .jet/lock (Source/CmdCompile.rs:3682-3686). Jet loader still declares no manifest settings (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/FactReads.jet:640-643), so text-declared facts plus checked computed contributions are not complete.
- **D-CONF-WORD1:** release, debug, and ci keep the word, matching --profile and its ratified sugar --release; The board identity is a machine description; before its unbuilt surface ships, it is renamed into the machine vocabulary and selected beside triples with --target; Environment profiles become presets (amends D-ENV-PROFILE1's field and flag spelling). Package/user profiles are already generation snapshots and take the generation word (amends D-JPK-PROFILE1's wording only). Each rename is an amendment named here; none changes behavior.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust machine axis is selected by target (Source/main.rs:2879-2882); Jet CLI registers separate env/preset selectors (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Commands.jet:961-964). Jet environment command is unavailable (Front.jet:491-506); full profile/generation manifest vocabulary cutover not established.
- **D-ECO-FILEROOT1:** package.jet is the sole reserved source filename, for the root Config contribution. Other source files may contribute named typed Config values; legacy project/workspace/env source-role filenames do not remain independent reserved authorities.
  - **Gap witness:** CONTRADICTED — Rust Syntax/jetpack_config.rs:404 has package.jet, but :412 still defines workspace.jet and Source/CmdCompile.rs:2056-2057 loads env.jet as an active environment root; ModuleEval/mod.rs:1772 reads repository env.jet. Jet module tooling likewise retains role contributions. Sole-reserved-file cutover is not complete.
- **D-ECO-JETOS2:** A System is another typed project value. Jet builds a complete generation, shows its changes, proves it is ready, switches once, and keeps the previous generation.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust JetOS commands/plan/store/generation/proof owners exist; ModuleEval/PackageOutput.rs:4-5 lowers System/Fleet from outputs. A complete checked-build/diff/readiness/atomic-switch/retained-rollback machine generation acceptance remains open; Compiler/ only prepares semantics.
- **D-ECO-ROOTNAME2:** Jetspace names the whole checked graph of sources, environments, outputs, systems and fleets. Package names the graph’s package nodes, not the complete root graph.
  - **Gap witness:** CONTRADICTED — The checked root remains called Package in Rust Package/mod.rs:3-5 and Manifest.rs:555, with PackageOutputPlan.graph_identity at ModuleEval/PackageOutput.rs:47-49. No Jetspace public type/diagnostic surface was found in Rust Package or Jet PackageModel searches.
- **D-ECO-SPLITPOLICY1:** Split creates the closed Config needed to move inline facts and records a reversible ledger.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production split seam exists at Source/main.rs:3667-3671; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-ECO1:** One checked Jetspace graph connects package sources, environments, outputs, services, images, systems and fleets; a machine can point to the package it runs. Final names/file law are D-ECO-ROOTNAME2 and D-ECO-FILEROOT1.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Package/Config/output/System/Fleet graph owners exist, but complete checked Jetspace identity/names and one source-to-machine proof graph are not established; the root still uses Package (Package/mod.rs:3-5). Jet port package engine is outside compiler and in progress.
- **D-ECO11:** runtime is the package field for external tools required on PATH at runtime, separate from build dependencies. Output wrappers consume that same typed list.
  - **Gap witness:** CONTRADICTED — Rust crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Manifest.rs:536-541 now parses runtime as core/alloc/hosted, not a list of PATH dependencies; no later ratified decision was found reversing this specific chosen field meaning. Jet PackageModel consumes the same changed schema.
- **D-ECO12:** formatter names an external formatter for non-Jet files. jet fmt formats .jet natively and delegates other languages to the named tool, so one command formats the whole tree, matching the flake's formatter attribute.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production fmt seam exists at Source/main.rs:3604-3607; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-ECO13:** Split moves whole modules plus attached comments into the conventional file, computed fields verbatim; A STABILITY test pins byte-identical round-trip; If a top-level binding is shared across the split boundary, split refuses with E13xx naming both referents and the fix; Reversibility is guaranteed for whole modules.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production split seam exists at Source/main.rs:3667-3671; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-ECO2:** build takes a typed recipe. Recipe.cargo(lock:) maps buildRustPackage and cargoLock.lockFile in one line.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Recipe.cargo is registered at Rust Syntax/package_files.rs:648, but inspected ModuleEval/Eval.rs:2400-2439 parses copy/prebuilt/build recipes and not cargo. No complete lock-driven Recipe.cargo consumer was established; finite Recipe.build is a different ratified feature.
- **D-JPK-POLICYSURFACE1:** All package policy — sources, licenses, advisories, maturity, hooks, cache roles, exceptions — lives in the one ratified `policy:` namespace of the workspace manifest beside `policy.trust`, `policy.providers`, and `policy.replacements` (D-JPK-GRANTSCHEMA1, D-JPK-PROVIDERAUTH1, D-JPK-REPLACEPOLICY1); no second config file and no inline dependency markers. Absent policy means the ratified safe defaults; effective policy is the auditable intersection of the source request/max with stronger org/host policy, which may refuse or narrow but never weaken, and source exceptions cannot override stronger policy.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Source/Publish/Policy.rs:1-5 implements manifest-side package policy/source mapping receipts. Jetpack Foundation/Source/Syntax.jet:531-534 declares the shared policy namespace. Complete expiring exception drafts, org/host intersection, inspect receipts and all policy families were not established in both ecosystem implementations.
- **D-PACKAGE-MODEL1:** Add one immutable typed package model to the existing compile-time-only core.compiler seam. Reuse jet-pkg-model and jet-env-model.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust exposes compile-time compiler package values (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:520-523), and Jet CompilerServices has the ordinary compiler-value seam (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/CompilerServices.jet:251-265). Full immutable package/lock/resolved-profile data, shared package/env-model reuse and runtime rejection consumer proof were not established.


Effective-scope corrections:


All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

Active contract: Complete the ratified ruling. Ecosystem entries are typed values in package.jet; role declarations like module env.dev respell as those values.

Gap evidence (static source witness, not a passing test): Rust EnvFile.rs:183-199 still reads ENV_FILE and parses legacy pkg.source calls; jet-env-model/ModuleEval/Source.rs:554-555,834-835 still uses env.jet and teaches module env.<name>. Jetpack EnvModel/ModuleEval/EnvPlanBuilder.jet:213,348-349 retains the matching ENV_FILE root and role-module teaching path. The ruling requires typed package values, not a second role-module/role-file interpretation; parser aliases unrelated to this ruling are not evidence.

1. Rust freeze: do not change Source/, crates/ Rust implementations or add Rust tests. Implement in the Jet compiler, Jet-hosted tooling and owning Jet packages. Core/, Docs/ and canonical Prelude/*.jet are shared inputs to the frozen reference: coordinate owner timing before editing them. Regenerate generated Compiler registries; never hand-edit DiagnosticRows.jet, CoreCallRows.jet or CoreSources.jet. Historical Rust file:line witnesses diagnose the gap; they do not authorize a Rust repair.
2. Implement only the missing consumer boundary identified by each cited gap witness, preserving working behavior; reuse the owning source, checker, registry and provider seam rather than introduce a parallel mechanism.
3. [D-BUILDCOMPAT1] Use version in a clear scope, preserve originals, and automatically read supported older data without changing its meaning. Version-1 locks from older Jet releases remain readable. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Jet has registered unsupported lock-version diagnostics and refuses unknown required marker meanings (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:11310-11312). Complete original-evidence preservation, linked readable views and automatic older-version translation in Rust and Jet were not established.
4. [D-CHECKSCOPE1] Resolve the owning project and every declared runnable output; Validate imports, reachable Core closure, canonical TIR, and every applicable execution-tier lowering; Preserve isolated single-file checks. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust project check explicitly sets inspect-only execute:false/no authority grant (crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:3477-3481); tests/project_check.rs is the consumer suite. Jet CLI exposes file check (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Host.jet:47-61; Front.jet:502), not an established all-runnable-output/workspace check.
5. [D-CONF-PLANE1] Adopt the model; Configuration is the program's knowledge about itself: every build fact (identity, machine, profile, settings, policy) is a typed value on one registered plane, with one contribution law and one audit command; The ratified role-typed Package shape becomes the only manifest vocabulary; the legacy flat parser is deleted. build.os, which already works this way, becomes the plane's first row; Later D-CONF ballots (fact reads, settings, contribution law) land on this substrate. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust folded fact vocabulary is registered (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:36-37). Jet has folded snapshots (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet:462-464), but loader explicitly lacks declared manifest settings (Expressions/FactReads.jet:640-643); complete typed single fact plane/cutover missing.
6. [D-CONF-SPLIT1] Manifest text is the complete index of what is configurable: every fact is declared there with its type and default. fn build performs actions — probes, steps, generated code — and may contribute a value to a declared fact; Every computed contribution is recorded in .jet/lock and named by jet explain. fn build can never mint an undeclared fact; The pushback the owner asked for is honest: a flat facts-in-text-only rule fails, because a probed toolchain or a find() member list is only knowable by computation; The law keeps those as computed contributions instead of banning them. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust pipeline records contributions/generated modules in .jet/lock (Source/CmdCompile.rs:3682-3686). Jet loader still declares no manifest settings (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/FactReads.jet:640-643), so text-declared facts plus checked computed contributions are not complete.
7. [D-CONF-WORD1] release, debug, and ci keep the word, matching --profile and its ratified sugar --release; The board identity is a machine description; before its unbuilt surface ships, it is renamed into the machine vocabulary and selected beside triples with --target; Environment profiles become presets (amends D-ENV-PROFILE1's field and flag spelling). Package/user profiles are already generation snapshots and take the generation word (amends D-JPK-PROFILE1's wording only). Each rename is an amendment named here; none changes behavior. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust machine axis is selected by target (Source/main.rs:2879-2882); Jet CLI registers separate env/preset selectors (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Commands.jet:961-964). Jet environment command is unavailable (Front.jet:491-506); full profile/generation manifest vocabulary cutover not established.
8. [D-ECO-FILEROOT1] package.jet is the sole reserved source filename, for the root Config contribution. Other source files may contribute named typed Config values; legacy project/workspace/env source-role filenames do not remain independent reserved authorities. Owning evidence: CONTRADICTED — Rust Syntax/jetpack_config.rs:404 has package.jet, but :412 still defines workspace.jet and Source/CmdCompile.rs:2056-2057 loads env.jet as an active environment root; ModuleEval/mod.rs:1772 reads repository env.jet. Jet module tooling likewise retains role contributions. Sole-reserved-file cutover is not complete.
9. [D-ECO-JETOS2] A System is another typed project value. Jet builds a complete generation, shows its changes, proves it is ready, switches once, and keeps the previous generation. Owning evidence: PARTIAL — Rust JetOS commands/plan/store/generation/proof owners exist; ModuleEval/PackageOutput.rs:4-5 lowers System/Fleet from outputs. A complete checked-build/diff/readiness/atomic-switch/retained-rollback machine generation acceptance remains open; Compiler/ only prepares semantics.

Owning evidence: CONTRADICTED — The checked root remains called Package in Rust Package/mod.rs:3-5 and Manifest.rs:555, with PackageOutputPlan.graph_identity at ModuleEval/PackageOutput.rs:47-49. No Jetspace public type/diagnostic surface was found in Rust Package or Jet PackageModel searches.
11. [D-ECO-SPLITPOLICY1] Split creates the closed Config needed to move inline facts and records a reversible ledger. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust: production split seam exists at Source/main.rs:3667-3671; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.

Final names/file law are D-ECO-ROOTNAME2 and D-ECO-FILEROOT1. Owning evidence: PARTIAL — Rust Package/Config/output/System/Fleet graph owners exist, but complete checked Jetspace identity/names and one source-to-machine proof graph are not established; the root still uses Package (Package/mod.rs:3-5). Jet port package engine is outside compiler and in progress.
13. [D-ECO11] runtime is the package field for external tools required on PATH at runtime, separate from build dependencies. Output wrappers consume that same typed list. Owning evidence: CONTRADICTED — Rust crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Manifest.rs:536-541 now parses runtime as core/alloc/hosted, not a list of PATH dependencies; no later ratified decision was found reversing this specific chosen field meaning. Jet PackageModel consumes the same changed schema.
14. [D-ECO12] formatter names an external formatter for non-Jet files. jet fmt formats .jet natively and delegates other languages to the named tool, so one command formats the whole tree, matching the flake's formatter attribute. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust: production fmt seam exists at Source/main.rs:3604-3607; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
15. [D-ECO13] Split moves whole modules plus attached comments into the conventional file, computed fields verbatim; A STABILITY test pins byte-identical round-trip; If a top-level binding is shared across the split boundary, split refuses with E13xx naming both referents and the fix; Reversibility is guaranteed for whole modules. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust: production split seam exists at Source/main.rs:3667-3671; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
16. [D-ECO2] build takes a typed recipe. Recipe.cargo(lock:) maps buildRustPackage and cargoLock.lockFile in one line. Owning evidence: PARTIAL — Recipe.cargo is registered at Rust Syntax/package_files.rs:648, but inspected ModuleEval/Eval.rs:2400-2439 parses copy/prebuilt/build recipes and not cargo. No complete lock-driven Recipe.cargo consumer was established; finite Recipe.build is a different ratified feature.
17. [D-JPK-POLICYSURFACE1] All package policy — sources, licenses, advisories, maturity, hooks, cache roles, exceptions — lives in the one ratified `policy:` namespace of the workspace manifest beside `policy.trust`, `policy.providers`, and `policy.replacements` (D-JPK-GRANTSCHEMA1, D-JPK-PROVIDERAUTH1, D-JPK-REPLACEPOLICY1); no second config file and no inline dependency markers. Absent policy means the ratified safe defaults; effective policy is the auditable intersection of the source request/max with stronger org/host policy, which may refuse or narrow but never weaken, and source exceptions cannot override stronger policy. Owning evidence: PARTIAL — Rust Source/Publish/Policy.rs:1-5 implements manifest-side package policy/source mapping receipts. Jetpack Foundation/Source/Syntax.jet:531-534 declares the shared policy namespace. Complete expiring exception drafts, org/host intersection, inspect receipts and all policy families were not established in both ecosystem implementations.
18. [D-PACKAGE-MODEL1] Add one immutable typed package model to the existing compile-time-only core.compiler seam. Reuse jet-pkg-model and jet-env-model. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust exposes compile-time compiler package values (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:520-523), and Jet CompilerServices has the ordinary compiler-value seam (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/CompilerServices.jet:251-265). Full immutable package/lock/resolved-profile data, shared package/env-model reuse and runtime rejection consumer proof were not established.
19. Migrate every affected public caller, example, test and existing doc/changelog section in the same clean cutover. Coordinate overlapping scopes; P23 owns module names, P03 non-Effect enums, #3986 Effect, P12 marker generation, P19 diagnostic templates and P27 fact-query lifetime separation.
20. D-EXEC1 staging: finish stage zero and semantic/output parity on current engines first; unify the compiled runtime and shared low-level ABI/drop representation next; build Jet O0/O1 x86-64 then aarch64, require whole-example-corpus parity and O0 live function replacement, and only then retire Cranelift/MIREval/--interpret in one cutover. Frozen engine-specific work stays frozen until its step lands. Before retirement retain applicable current-engine proof; after retirement retarget durable tests to O0/O1/O2/web. No early engine deletion or declaration that a surviving old engine is itself a violation.
21. Deliver the named Jet-side tests/goldens and real consumer receipts in criteria. Main runs verification once on the integrated snapshot; performance/process requirements require their real receipts, not fabricated code.

Package outputs are validated (E1321), and a package can name several executable entries (ruling B). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E1321` and `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter manifest_named_executables`.

Suitable small examples, scaffolds, dogfood and benchmarks use one authored source with an inline `package {}` header and explicit authority, with no duplicated metadata, while real multi-file apps stay multi-file with a recorded reason. D-ENV-FILES1=A: one managed file graph with safe shorthand and exact sync policy. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter d_env_files1_contract` passes, a Jet #Test that drives the ratified contract through the production path with a reviewed golden.

D-ENV-FLAKEGRAPH1=A: one flake-class graph for Jet environments. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter d_env_flakegraph1_contract` passes, a Jet #Test that drives the ratified contract through the production path with a reviewed golden.

Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter d_env_flakeparts1_contract` passes, a Jet #Test that drives the ratified contract through the production path with a reviewed golden.
