criteria.text: D-LINK-SIBLING1=A eligibility: a link field of type @T or [@T] has the sibling fields of type T or [T] as candidates (a String field also qualifies for @String, and a type-parameter field counts); one candidate infers the tie, two or more require `#Within(field)` (an error naming both otherwise), none means untied; a construction in the module that stores links from outside the tied field is an error naming the constructor, while an empty list and untied records follow the ordinary stored-link rules. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/link_sibling_tie_` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter link_sibling_`.

A tied record's source field stays frozen while any link taken from it is alive, including links kept past an escape or a move-apart, and a copy of the record shares the frozen source without retargeting its links. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/link_sibling_frozen_source_` on O0, O1 and O2, with a UI snapshot for the write refused while frozen.

Only a tied, frozen sibling list is exempt from D-LINK-ITEM1, and a tied record may derive Encode but a derived Decode is refused with a registered error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/link_sibling_item_exemption` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter link_sibling_decode_refused`.
The tie is published as a fact like inferred link sources, and hover and `jet inspect` show which field a link field is tied to.

cards.title: Pinned shared Jet globals and isolated Core state providers
cards.body:
D-CORE-GLOBAL-STATE1=A
Proposed compiler law: sema admits a shared initializer for #Persist, checks T under existing Shared crossing rules, and records stable binding identity and type/layout facts. The new branch requires a `name: value` declaration (not `:=`) so the module handle cannot be reassigned, moved out, or transiently absent.

The initializer must be a closed, non-suspending, infallible state-construction expression: literal data and checked pure construction, no task/world capture, external effects, or access to other lazy globals. Cyclic global initialization is rejected, not allowed to hang. The example creates only an empty typed map inside Storage. Allocation remains subject to existing allocation behavior; no new retry policy is introduced.

All execution modes implement identical once-only publication. State is inaccessible until initialization finishes. Ordinary statements use the existing Shared lock/cleanup law, not scalar persist take/set. Transactions and guards remain unchanged; this ballot adds no new atomicity mechanism. A failed or cancelled ordinary update releases locks under existing Shared rules; this ballot does not promise rollback outside #Transact.

Reload never runs the initializer again for a retained cell. Layout/migration checks complete at the existing reload boundary before new code uses old storage. The process default and each test-world provider are implemented in Jet. Vetted #Unsafe FFI/syscalls may supply host synchronization, but no Rust implementation is retained.

Implementation areas: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet E0622 admission, stable Global binding facts; Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Lower/Statics.jet once/Shared global path; Jet runtime once+lock/reload/world provider; Core/math/random.jet, Core/sys/sys.jet env overlay, Core/testing/testing.jet fault switches, Core/auth/auth.jet and Core/web/storage*.jet; no scalar take/set gap
Spec/registry: Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md Persist writable/global/reload amendments, D-CONC-SHARE1 ordinary shared expr and migration precedence; core-library RNG/env/fault/auth/storage scope; CLOSURE 3.11 and existing leaf removal rows; Legacy Syntax.rs #Persist/KW_SHARED reference; Jet Persist registration/init constraints cite D-CORE-GLOBAL-STATE1=A; shared keyword remains D-CONC-SHARE1; NO new marker; DiagnosticRows E0622 and new cycle/initializer/handle refusal registered
Diagnostics/UI: Equivalent unmarked mutable table rejected; immutable handle assignment/move; cyclic/effectful/suspending/world-capture initializer refusal; initializer-only retained-cell reload report; fresh identity and layout restart/migration reports
Examples/goldens: Contended first access exactly once/no partial publication; indexed Shared map update #4751 mandatory; counter atomic statement; two-key Transact invariant + cancellation/panic guard release; compatible body/init reload retains; rename fresh/process restart empty; parallel worlds/children local-session separation; browser scope unchanged
Timing: JET PORT NOW; minimal Persist/Shared/global admission seam essential for existing Core state rows may be mirrored under #29 with dies-at-cutover ledger. Broader unrelated feature work remains frozen. Runtime policy, once/lock/world/reload implementations are Jet-owned; scalar Alloc root does not prove shared-cell semantics. CURRENT #29/#31: a MINIMAL seam necessary to port an existing Core row/runtime layer/test harness may also change the Rust half, registered as dies at cutover; all actual layer policy/carriers must still be ported to Jet. This exception does not permit duplicating new features. #28 Sol authors, Opus reviews. cards.title: Toolchain-private Core seams for Jetpack (D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A) (held-directory process, held link)
cards.body: Decided: D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A (ratified 2026-11-01), a toolchain-private module, as c1 states. The ballot text below is history. Jetpack (the Jet package manager) needs two capabilities that exist only as raw Core kernels: run a child process with a held Directory as its cwd (#4895: kernel core.process.__with_directory_raw, CoreSystem2 d13edcfff) and the held link (compiler_link_held). Today they're reached through reserved __ names that the parser now rejects (E0067), so the Jet CLI's assembled source doesn't parse. Renaming them to legal names (files.compiler_process_directory, compiler_link_held) makes them ORDINARY PUBLIC Core functions: CoreReview5-2-2 traced Sema core_call 2607-2653: there is NO caller-privacy fence; the only gate (compiler_api_allowed, CompilerServices.jet:98-111) is a compile-time-only gate for core.compiler, not privacy; #Unsafe and names don't restrict callers. Visibility law today (D-VIS-MODULE1): public by default, priv only on modules and fields. Options (same program: Jetpack's TreeHash runs git with a held directory): A) Make them public, documented Core functions (e.g. process.spawn_in(spec, dir: Directory)). Beginner: one more safe capability (held handle, no path races). Expert: same. Cost: permanent public API to maintain. B) Add ONE toolchain-private visibility: a module-level marker so a Core module is importable only by the compiler and Jetpack (checked by sema, registered in Syntax.rs with a decision ID). Beginner: never sees it. Expert: can't call it. Cost: a new visibility mechanism (I8 allows it with this ratification). C) Jetpack calls the raw runtime route directly (#Import / ABI binding of the existing route symbol) with no Core wrapper. Beginner: unaffected. Cost: Jetpack carries unsafe ABI glue; violates the one-mechanism preference for Core access. Main recommends B if more toolchain-only seams are expected (they are: link, process dir, build receipts), else A for process.spawn_in only. Blocks: CLIParity1 / CLIParity2 composition (goal 4).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): body, title reworded; the text waited on an owner answer that ratified decisions already give, or on a choice within ratified scope; it is recorded as decided (Main's operational authority) and nothing waits.

Main 2026-11-01: D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A is ratified; this card now tracks building it. Criteria 1-4 come from CardClose-1's plan (CardClose-63), and criterion 5 keeps seam 5 (build-receipt producer) here because no other card holds it. Seam 3 (pass a held lock to a child) stays on #5089 criterion 6. CardClose-1 is building criteria 1-2.
Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Fourth case (NativeLead24-2 ruling on CLIParity2's retained-root lock): the Jet RuntimeLock must own an AdvisoryLock taken through the existing Core Directory.lock (same root inode, EX|NB flock on the held '.'); acquire / probe / marker / journal all from the same held root authority; nested identity from FileID, not path. A child process lease must INHERIT that same locked open file description (no reopen / re-flock / raw Int cast), but Core/process has no typed AdvisoryLock attachment / inheritance today. That's a Core/process seam needed by Jetpack only: public option (A) = a documented ProcessSpec capability to inherit a held AdvisoryLock; toolchain-private option (B) = the same seam behind the toolchain-private visibility. Same decision as the other three cases.

Third case (CopyPareto1, #4884 native List.sort_by): the compiler's sort_by intrinsic should lower to ONE private Core kernel (Core/collections, ordinary generic Jet function) so every tier shares the meaning (I9). Same-module private generic calls are fine today, but an EXTERNAL compiler intrinsic -> PRIVATE Core kernel call is not authorized by the current permission model (Sema Calls/Core.jet:160 / resolver 172 use public export / privacy); it must keep the registered declaration SymbolID / module owner / generics -> MIRCallee.User and still deny direct user calls to the private kernel. Options as in the ballot: A) make the kernel a public documented Core function; B) the toolchain-private visibility would also let compiler-lowered intrinsics target private Core kernels; C) n/a here (no raw route). Main's recommendation (B) now covers three cases: Jetpack seams, the compiler's build-receipt producer, and compiler intrinsics -> private Core kernels.

Additional case (CLIParity3, producer 0af618774): the compiler's own build-receipt producer needs Core/build internals that are module-private today: Core/build/keys.jet:280 (priv factory), session 127 / 147 (priv state / session, finished plan storage and target output readers). The pre-existing Driver BuildQueries already reaches the priv Core build session as a whole gateway, but that predates any ruling and isn't an authorized seam. So the ballot's question covers compiler -> Core-private access as well as Jetpack -> Core-private access; option B (one toolchain-private visibility) would cover both uniformly.

CoreReview5-2-2 confirmed there's no existing fence to reuse: compiler_api_allowed is granted only to the selected build entry (Rust BodyCheck 4232-45 / state 9902225: bundle.entry only), ordinary TreeHash / Git helpers don't qualify, and user comptime bypasses the gate anyway (6336 2680 / 2722); semantically core.build is a read-only graph / receipt query surface (6336 2712-49, D-BUILDQUERY1), not a mutable FS / Exec ProcessSpec carrier. So the ballot's options stand as written.

criteria.text: Mechanism (D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A, ratified 2026-11-01). `priv(toolchain) module` parses only in a toolchain package, meaning one whose source root lies inside the Jet distribution root that supplied Core (Core, Compiler/*, Jetpack/*); package names play no part. In any other package it is E0414, whose registry text becomes "only `priv(package)` exists outside the toolchain". A `use` or qualified path into a toolchain-private module from a non-toolchain package is E0605 ("`core.files.toolchain` is private to the Jet toolchain"). LSP completion and the generated reference never list such a module. Proof: new UI snapshots Tests/UI/priv_toolchain_in_user_package.{jet,stderr} (E0414) and Tests/UI/core_files_toolchain_user_use.{jet,stderr} (E0605). The ballot probe (a user `run()` calling the held-folder seam, today `jet check` clean) becomes E0605. A JetLSP completion test shows `core.files.` does not offer `toolchain`.

Seams 1 and 2 have their home. Core/Files gains `priv(toolchain) module toolchain` with `run_in(spec: ProcessSpec, folder: Directory) -[FS, Exec, Env]> ProcessSpec IOError!` and `link_into(source: FileReader, folder: Directory, name: String) -[FS.Write]> Bool IOError!`. Both are typed and have no `#Unsafe` marker. `files.compiler_with_process_directory` and `files.compiler_link_held` are deleted, along with their registry rows (Prelude/Core.jet, CoreSourceOwned, CoreCallRows, StructureRegistry, RawHostKeys test). Jetpack/Foundation/Source/TreeHash.jet calls `held.run_in` / `held.link_into` with no `#Unsafe` block. Proof: the Core/Files held-directory tests pass on run_in; the Jetpack Foundation TreeHash tests pass; `grep -r 'compiler_with_process_directory\|compiler_link_held'` over Core/Compiler/Jetpack/tests returns 0 rows.

Compiler-generated calls pass. A call the compiler lowers into a toolchain-private module is admitted, while the same name written in user source is E0605. Proof via seam 4: user `list.sort_by(f)` lowers to the Core collections sort kernel, now moved into a `priv(toolchain) module`. Examples golden collections sort rows pass on o0/o1/o2, and Tests/UI/sort_kernel_user_call.{jet,stderr} shows E0605.

Registry/spec/chain. Syntax-decisions S18 gains the `priv(toolchain)` line (Spellings ledger regenerated, `lexical-ledger.mjs --check` clean). spec.md visibility section and the E0414/E0605/E0609 rows name `priv(toolchain)`, and the diagnostic pages for those codes are regenerated. Chain FIXED_POINT; suites lose no row.

Seam 5 under D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A: the compiler's build-receipt producer reads Core/build's session and key state (keys factory, session plan, target storage) through a `priv(toolchain)` reader instead of module-private access; the receipt is unchanged and a user `use` of the reader is E0605. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CoreSeams/build_receipt_reader` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0605_toolchain_reader`.

D-EMBED-TOOLCHAIN1=A table cutover, part 2: the five Core-declaration tables (CoreSourceOwned, EnumRows, StructureRows, the EnumPayload tail, CoreCallRows) are computed at build time from toolchain: reads, their copies and generator modes are deleted, and the declaration parser lives in one package. Walked and data-named reads use computed embed_file and find paths (D-EMBED-WALK1=A). The comptime cost of CoreCallRows (896 KB) against the generator run is recorded in the card log. Proof: the five generated files are absent from `git ls-files Compiler` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter comptime_embed_` passes. (was #6151 c53)

cards.title: Build D-PRIVATE-NATIVE-CARRIER1: HTTP Body holds a private native stream in a priv field, and the HTTP Body cutover lands on it
cards.body: Owner decision needed (new mechanism / public API). The ratified HTTP law (D-HTTPDEPTH1=A; Core + runtime joint ruling) wants ONE public source-owned Body capability facade over a PRIVATE opaque lazy native transport (the existing Arc<Mutex<JetHTTPBody>> kernel). NativeLead24-2 confirmed no mechanism for that exists today: opaque_methods only registers Source impl signatures on PUBLIC known native carriers; the old browser facade (BrowserServer { private native: BrowserTestServer? }) used an already-public carrier and the current line removed it; JetForeignHandle is public and needs a real C library / typedef / close metadata. Missing: a PRIVATE checked native identity with scope, default-constructor rejection, ownership / lifecycle and physical mapping on every tier (I9). Stand-ins (empty record, private RawInt, host RuntimeValue, public alias) are rejected. Blocks GoldenPareto1's Body cutover (6 HTTP goldens). Options (same program: req.body.text() on an incoming request): A) Make the transport a PUBLIC documented native carrier type (e.g. core.http.BodyTransport), not user-constructible, used as Body's field. Beginner: one more type name visible in docs / errors, never needed. Expert: can name the type; no new mechanism. B) Add ONE general private native-carrier mechanism: a Core module can declare a native kernel type private to that module (sema rejects naming / constructing it outside; ownership / drop / clone rules from its native metadata; mapped identically on all tiers). Beginner: never sees it. Expert: clean facades. Cost: a new mechanism (I8, needs this ratification), reusable for other facades. C) Drop the facade: Body IS the native carrier directly (public, as today's incoming body), with the outgoing Empty / Text / Bytes constructors as functions returning it. Beginner: one type. Cost: re-opens the Core + runtime ruling. Main recommends B if more Core facades over native kernels are expected (likely: streams, sockets), else A. Related but distinct: #4896 (which modules may IMPORT toolchain-private Core seams).

log.text: PROGRESS ONLY, sema part only: E0605 for omitted priv fields in literals and priv-module type paths, with 3 new ui tests; the Http Body cutover stays parked (IrTypes-45) Landed in wave 28 as dev bb770de593 (IrTypes-45).
Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-PRIVATE-NATIVE-CARRIER1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Joint Core + Native conclusion (CoreReview5-2-2): a Source facade privately holding a PUBLIC opaque seed handle DOES exist (encoding/stream JSONPush 870-877: private output: FileWriter; JSONWriter 201 output: JSONPush; constructor factory 1327; FileWriter known in core_types 303 with opaque constructability). That pattern supports option A directly (public, non-constructible native carrier held privately by the facade). What does NOT exist is a PRIVATE internal native kernel identity with constructor privacy + lifecycle / clone / drop carrier metadata (option B). Type.Named is a sufficient representation either way; no new Opaque IR kind is needed. Main's updated recommendation: A, following the JSONPush / FileWriter precedent, unless the owner wants B as a general mechanism for future facades.

criteria.text: D-PRIVATE-NATIVE-CARRIER1=A is built: core.http declares its native stream type in a `priv module`, and `Body` is a struct holding it in a `priv` field; Bodies come only from responses, requests, `body_text`, `body_bytes` and `body_empty`.
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev since 43873ce5e6: Core/Http/Http.jet declares `priv body_carrier: module { BodyStream }` and `Body: struct { priv stream: body_carrier.BodyStream }`; Bodies come from requests, responses and the body_* / Body.* constructors. criteria.text: Naming the stream type or building a `Body` (or a `Directory` or `FileWriter`) by hand from user code is E0605, with UI snapshots; the HTTP Body cutover lands on the new carrier and the http goldens pass on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev since 43873ce5e6 (with 4c64794ac9 streaming bodies on it). `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter` http_body_carrier_is_private, http_body_literal_is_private, directory_literal_is_private and forged_file_writer_literal: each PASS (E0605); `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Network/HTTP/`: 51 PASS, 0 FAIL over O0/O1/O2, on the gate-p136 batch jet.

cards.title: One option table drives both CLI flags and declarative build config (owner rule: no CLI-only or config-only options)
cards.body: Owner rule 2026-10-09 (OWNER-DIRECTIVES #51): every CLI flag/option must also be writable declaratively in the build configuration (package.jet Build profiles / fn build), and vice versa, from ONE option definition (I8). Audit 2026-10-09: $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Main/CLI-CONFIG-PARITY.md. Today there are four independent surfaces: Jet CLI registry rows (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CLICommands.jet), frozen Rust command and flag tables (crates/jet-foundation CLICommands.rs, crates/jet-cli CLI.rs), the Rust host argv/profile handling (Source/main.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs), and the declarative package/build model (crates/jet-pkg-model Package/Blocks.rs, jet-foundation Syntax/package_files.rs, comptime BuildContext). check-command-table.mjs compares only Jet vs Rust CLI rows. Work (Jet side only; the Rust is frozen): one Jet option table whose rows carry both the CLI spelling and the build-config field, consumed by the Jet CLI parser and the Jet package/build model; a --check that fails on any CLI-only or config-only option; migrate every existing option and list the current gaps from the audit. Priority after Rust out of the compiler (owner #48).

criteria.text: `jet --help | wc -l` prints at most 50: the common commands, one line each (419 lines on 2026-10-28).
`jet help <command>` prints only that command's flags, and `jet help --all` prints the full table, all from the one option table.
No help summary line wraps mid-word at 80 columns.

D-JET-HOME1=A is carried out as one verified cutover that keeps keys, trust and retention records. After any jet command on a clean home directory, only ~/.config/jet/ and ~/.cache/jet/ exist (honouring XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME), and ~/.jet and ~/.local/share/jet are never created. The same work sits on frozen #4573.

No two registry flags share a meaning: of each pair the Jet CLI accepts today (--route/--path, --cook/--cook-mode, --force-clean/--clean in Compiler/JetCLI/Source/CLI/Commands.jet), one spelling is kept, and a removed spelling gets the ordinary unknown-flag error with its normal suggestion. Which spelling of each pair is kept is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Help, completion and CLI snapshots are regenerated, and in-repo callers use the kept spellings. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsSurface/` passes, and git grep finds no removed spelling outside tests that pin its rejection.

Build profile names have one home, the stock-profile table beside JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (census F29). Inspect.jet and Front.jet derive from it (Inspect.jet also knew `hardened` and `ci`; Front.jet did not), and a gate guard fails on any copy that differs.
Every flag of check, build, run, test and dev has a build-config key, and every build-config key has a flag, both generated from the one option table beside JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (owner rule 2026-10-09).

CLI flag ownership derives from the compiler's command declarations, while application command schemas and output-envelope contracts stay distinct. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter cli_flags_from_command_declarations`. (was #3186 c6)

Args decoding outside the entry, checked builder plans and the flag, env and default merge use the one Args projection, and an invalid present value is reported. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter args_projection_`. (was #3236 c30)

`jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/ArgsReference` passes, and a Jet test validates the man, ReST, Markdown and YAML output with real consumers (man, a ReST parser, a CommonMark renderer and an independent YAML reader), reporting a missing consumer as SKIP-HOST. Proof: those two commands. (was #3242 c31)

Nested, inherited and repeated flags, aliases, grouping, cardinality, double-dash, dynamic completion, hooks and lifecycle errors have conformance goldens. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/Conformance`. (was #3242 c36)

Run, build, dev and test overrides and argument forwarding keep the launcher's and the application's namespaces apart, and an absent override behaves as stock. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsCommands/override_namespaces`. (was #3242 c37)

Builders still support runtime-defined schemas through the same Core parser, with no second semantic parser and no compiler-CLI DSL migration. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/RuntimeSchemaBuilder`. (was #3242 c38)

Equivalent #CLI and builder grammars produce identical values, help, errors and completion on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/MarkerBuilderPair`. (was #3242 c40)

A plain `jet test Compiler/JetCLI/Tests/FrontDoor.jet` (no JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY, no Tests/.jet/build/IDENTITY, no extra runtime dir) passes every test: the tests that compile fixtures get the identity and runtime pack of the jet under test from the jet running them, never from a train-only environment variable or a build-tree file. On seed-t23 (dev 9755703c76), 18-20 FrontDoor tests fail only on E0003 'native host omitted its compiler identity' or 'no runtime pack': 10 semver/public-API tests, 3 receipt tests, jobs_metadata, the exported run library feed, inspect_build (2), inspect_output, try and fix_recheck_rolls_back (G6Meta, 2026-11-11). Proof: that plain command reports 0 failed on the train compiler. (was #3242 c43)

Each reference format carries the parse/help fixture's names, defaults, inherited options, visibility and examples, omits hidden and secret options, and escapes punctuation, fences, multiline text, descendant anchors and adversarial input correctly. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/ArgsReference` and the consumer test's fixture comparison. (was #3242 c46)

The generators are deterministic and contained: two runs with explicit headers and date are byte-identical, output over the size cap and malformed metadata return a structured error (never an exit or panic), and the generator runs no target code and writes no file outside its output. Proof: `jet test Core --filter args_reference_hygiene`. (was #3242 c47)

`jet build` names the binary from package.jet, prints its path and size on one line, and keeps profiles apart: `jet new hello && cd hello && jet build` prints one line. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIBuild/names_binary_prints_path_and_size`. (was #6418 c25)

Header binding has one canonical spelling, `jet inspect bind <header>`, as Docs/Spec/cli.md specifies, and bind no longer sets also_canonical_top_level in CLICommands.jet. Proof: `git grep -n also_canonical_top_level -- Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CLICommands.jet` shows no bind row, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Bind/` passes. (was #6418 c144)
Every ratified flag spelling in CLICommands.jet parses: no ratified spelling gets the unknown-flag E2102. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter cli_ratified_flags_parse`. (was #6418 c147)

Every help line resolves to a live command and every dispatcher command appears in help, because help is generated from the dispatcher table. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsSurface/group_help_and_man_inventory_every_nested_description`. (was #6418 c148)

cards.title: Report ALL errors by default: promote keep-going diagnostics from compiler-internal JET_KEEP_GOING to the default user behavior
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-09: the compiler must not stop at the first error; by default it reports ALL errors so a user or agent can fix them in one pass. Today (dev 2026-10-09): within a phase the Jet compiler already collects many diagnostics, but between phases it stops once errors exist (e.g. JetDriver Pipeline.jet:2220 'if jet_driver_has_errors(diagnostics) && !keep_going -> return None', BodyComptime.jet:221). A full all-phases mode exists only as the compiler-internal JET_KEEP_GOING=1 env var (Compiler/Bootstrap/Host/Entry.jet:10-128; JetDriverKeepGoing in JetDriver Identity.jet:524; sema keep-going traps CheckProgram.jet:2243+; comptime drops failed items; the optimizer traps rejected functions and reruns; the emitter keeps every failure), documented as never shipped. Work (Jet side only): make all-phases collection the default for check/build/run/test, with failed items replaced by typed traps so later phases still run without cascade noise (dedupe and suppress errors caused by an already-reported failure); no artifact is produced when any error exists; one canonical option to stop at the first error, available both as a CLI flag and as a build-config setting (owner rule #51: CLI and declarative config never diverge); registered diagnostics/snapshots for the summary line; docs. Keep the internal skip list (JET_KEEP_GOING_SKIP) as a compiler-developer tool only if still needed.

JetSemIndex Docs/Collect, Contracts, Doctests and Graph plus 36 JetLSP files import private core.files.runtime.kernel_path_components and use doc_os_path.OsPath, display_span, file_stem_span and from_encoded, none of which exist in Core. cards.title: Build swap and replace out of a borrowed place (D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A, D-WRITE-TAKE1=A)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-09 while fixing Core: Core CSV (streaming rows, ~791 self.fields) and crypto (~99 hash.pending.bytes) want to move a value out of a field below a read/write borrow and immediately reinitialize it. The current rules make that E0201 by design (spec.md:1077-1082, 1e1825f4e); there is no general take/replace/swap API (only Cell.replace, spec 1313-1316). Interim: crypto restructured to consume at finish; CSV uses a restructure or an explicit .copy() then reset (an extra allocation per row). Decided: D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A and D-WRITE-TAKE1=A (ratified) add the canonical take and replace; this card builds them.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): body reworded; the text waited on an owner answer that ratified decisions already give, or on a choice within ratified scope; it is recorded as decided (Main's operational authority) and nothing waits.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A and D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A (no call-site marks; `&&` marks a take).
Moved from ready to planning: an idea with no acceptance criteria can't be implemented or closed. It needs criteria first (CardClose-1 ready sweep, 2026-11-01).

D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A is ratified, so this card moves from ballot to build. Also: Docs/audits memory-model-2026-10-05.md:167 still names the older 'old :: ^x; x = new' route; the build must match the ratified form.

Related (2026-10-09): Core/crypto/jetc.jet needs to turn an owned Secret into an X25519SecretKey; there is no audited owner-transfer (only the copying expert.secret_bytes). Interim: build the key from the audited copy and let the Secret close and zeroize itself. Owner decision: add an audited expert transfer, e.g. expert.x25519_secret_from_secret(^Secret) plus a secret length accessor, with the take/replace question above.

Interim taken 2026-10-09: Core CSVReader row handoff now copies the fields and resets the borrowed storage (61a4cfa1c), an extra allocation per row; crypto SHA-256 finalizes the pending buffer in place instead (d0989d126, no copy). Revisit CSV if a canonical take/replace API is ratified.

criteria.text: Core CSV row handoff and the crypto pending bytes use replace instead of the interim copy-then-reset, with no extra allocation per row. Proof: git grep finds no copy-then-reset in Core/Csv and Core/Crypto, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CSV/` passes.

D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A, extended by D-WRITE-TAKE1=A (ratified 2026-11-04): core.mem has `swap<T>` and `replace<T>` (`-[!Panic]>`), named by the prelude with no import, a user-defined swap or replace still wins, and List and Map gain swap. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/TakeReplace` on O0, O1 and O2.

Sema tracks each moved-out gap in a borrowed place (E0121): an exit, or a call that can stop, inside a gap is E0201, and its fix offers swap or replace. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0201_moved_out_gap` with the fix shown in the snapshot.

The generated code moves the value back into the place on every stop path inside a gap, so no place is left empty after a failure. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/TakeReplaceGapRestore` on O0, O1 and O2.

criteria.text: In a fresh `jet new` project with no `jetpack` binary on PATH, `jet add ../geometry` (path) and `jet add git+<url>#<rev>` (git) write the dependency to package.jet and the lock, and `jet build` resolves it.
`jet fetch` and `jet update` work for path and git dependencies; a second run leaves the lock bytes unchanged.

A missing or silent package engine is reported as missing or broken with the fix; E1227 "disagree" appears only when both sides answer with different protocol versions. UI snapshots cover all three cases.
Package commands run only the engine shipped beside the running `jet` (toolchain root); a fake `jetpack` placed earlier on PATH is never executed (test).

criteria.text: Each accepted option is set from a package.jet profile, from fn build and from the CLI through one definition, with an executable example and golden output.

cards.title: One build plan produces several configurations of the same program
cards.body:
## Outcome

`fn build` can register one program in several configurations in a single plan: debug, release, web, or a cross target. Each configuration has its own profile and target, and all are built by one `jet build` with separate outputs.

## Evidence

- In Jai, every `compiler_create_workspace` call carries its own `Build_Options` (The Way to Jai @19cb4b7 `examples/30/30.1_workspaces.jai`, `30.13_dynamic_libraries.jai`).
- Blow's "build all" builds a debug workspace and a release workspace in parallel (`OHZwYYW9koI` 00:03:01, 2015-10-15). Tsoding's game build produces release, debug and WebAssembly outputs on every build (`kjF_YuLsPqo` 00:05:13, 2022).
- In Jet, `BuildTarget` has a toolchain handle but no profile (`crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/targets.rs:129-143`). The profile is chosen once per invocation (`--profile`/`--release`, D-BUILD-DEFAULT1). Two configurations of one program need two invocations.

## Ballot

The public `BuildContext` API shape, on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15): a profile and target argument on each registered target, or a named configuration set applied to a target. Builds on #4913's one option table and D-BUILDCTX-FLAGS1 defaults.

One review: Round3Review.

criteria.text: One `fn build` registers the same program in at least two configurations with different profiles and targets, and one `jet build` writes both artifacts to distinct output paths.

Each configuration's receipt names its profile and target, and changing one configuration's settings leaves the other configurations' outputs byte-identical. Proof: a cases row under `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_multi_config` builds twice with one setting changed and compares the output digests.
An executable example of the multi-configuration plan has golden output on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Host facts for prep and build-time code
cards.body:
## Outcome

Prep code and build-time code can tell the machine they run on (the host) from the machine the program is built for (the target). When an evaluated Core call has per-OS behaviour, the rule for which OS it uses is written down and tested.

## Evidence

- Jai hit this problem. A `#run` inside a module with per-OS implementations must use the host version, not the target version (Blow `jjCfAg_gtDw` 00:43:50, April 2023). By September 2024 Jai had added an extra hidden "host imports" workspace for compile-time code (`LPdMNsL5MgI` 00:03:21).
- Jet exposes only target facts: `$build.os` (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/OSTarget.rs:13-15`). No host fact root exists (searched `$host`, `host.os` and `HOST_OS` over `crates/jet-foundation/src`, `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source`, `syntax-decisions.md` and `metaprogramming.md`: no hits). Toolchain handles record host and target triples (D-BUILDTOOLCHAIN1), but prep code cannot read them.

## Owner gate

Adding a fact root or a `BuildContext` member is new registered surface (I7). The owner also decides what a prep-time call with per-OS behaviour does when cross-compiling (I9 keeps one meaning).

criteria.text: A prep block and a build action can each read the host OS and architecture separately from the target facts ($build), through one registered surface tied to a decision ID.
A cross-compiling example shows the host and target facts differing, and the rule for per-OS Core calls during preparation is stated and tested.
Host facts read during preparation are part of the cache key.

Registered host facts sit beside $build for prep and build-time code, and a per-OS Core call made during prep follows the host; proved by a golden example that cross-compiles and prints both host and target facts.

A project or package policy can reject host facts: any read of them then fails the build with a registered diagnostic (what/why/fix and a UI snapshot) naming the reading line, so a hermetic build can be enforced; every host-fact read is recorded in the build record for audit.

(was #6126) An owner ballot on the surface is ratified: how fn build sets a settings value per target, and the names of the target hardware facts (word size, pointer size, cache-line size, CPU features).

(was #6126) fn build sets a declared setting to different values for two targets; each target's artifact reads its own value through `$build.settings.<key>`, and the value folds at build time. Golden output on every tier.

(was #6126) Code reads target hardware facts (word size, pointer size, cache-line size, CPU feature set) at build time; they follow the selected target, not the host, proved by a cross-target build whose facts differ from the host's.
(was #6126) Setting an undeclared key, or a value of the wrong type, for a target gives a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot.
(was #5008) A breakpoint inside a prep block, a prep fn recipe, a marker body or fn build pauses during jet build, with locals, call stack and the step count shown.
(was #5008) The evaluator's behaviour, step budget and results are the same with or without the debugger attached (I9); a focused test proves it.

cards.title: Compiler event parity: import, program-wide generation, placeholders, link and artifact stages, per-invocation hooks
cards.body:
## Outcome

A package can replace the link step of one executable target with a declared, cached build action. That action receives the compiler's object files and libraries and produces the artifact. A package can also run checked steps on the written artifact, such as signing or embedding an icon or manifest, with failures reported as Jet diagnostics.

## Evidence

- Jai: setting `use_custom_link_command` makes the compiler stop at the `READY_FOR_CUSTOM_LINK_COMMAND` phase. `Message_Phase.compiler_generated_object_files` lists the objects, and the metaprogram links them itself, then calls `compiler_custom_link_command_is_complete(w)` (focus-editor `first.jai` @c6b3ead lines 75, 153-155, 357-391).
- `PRE_WRITE_EXECUTABLE` lets a metaprogram replace the executable (Blow `AdoShhhnsQA` 00:03:53, 2018). `POST_WRITE_EXECUTABLE` reports the linker exit code (The Way to Jai @19cb4b7 `examples/30/30.5_compiler_intercept.jai:46-53`). Focus sets the icon and manifest after a successful link.
- Jet links internally (`Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Image/ELF.jet:30`) or through rustc. D-HOOK-STAGES1 makes `compiler.emitted(Artifact)` read-only, with findings only. `b.action` (D-BUILDACTION1) can add steps over declared outputs, but it cannot take over an executable target's link.

## Ballot

Amending D-HOOK-STAGES1 or D-BUILDACTION1 to allow a typed link step (c1, c2) is public API; it is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Linker-argument options belong to #5005.

log.text: c1c decision (Main, within D-LINK-STEP1=A): BuildAction is the plain description struct core.build.BuildAction{name, run, inputs, outputs, allow} that the free build.action(...) makes and a link hook returns (the ratified spelling). The build-session handle that b.run/b.action return is renamed BuildStep in one cutover, and b.action builds the same description and registers it (one mechanism). D-BUILDACTION1 names no handle type. The hook runs at compile time through the tool-stage #run mechanism, and the driver runs the returned action in the hermetic executor.

c1 ballot needed (D-LINK-DEFAULT1, to post): how LinkInputs.default is spelled as a BuildAction when Jet links in process. Every BuildAction today is an argv the hermetic executor runs (ActionKind only classifies identity; b.jet() names the running compiler as a tool). Options: (A) a public 'jet link <objects> <libraries> -o <out>' verb that b.jet() steps run; (B) a builtin action kind the executor runs as Jet's StaticLink, with no argv; (C) an internal linker binary shipped beside jet. Meanwhile c1c is built with hooks returning their own argv actions, and default means Jet's own link. Slices: c1a option rows, c1c hook action through the executor (cases custom_link_step, ui custom_link_step_fails), c1d per-output options and policy forbid, c2 post_link/before_write.

cards.title: Jai parity: Jet does everything Jai does, safe by default with expert opt-outs
cards.body:
## Outcome

Owner direction (2026-10-16): Jet must be as or more powerful and flexible than Jai. Every Jai feature or idea gets an explicit Jet counterpart. Safety and auditability stay the default, and experts can turn the guardrails off. The Jai author's regrets are designed out. Every owner choice is balloted.

## Evidence

The 1:1 audit is `Docs/audits/jai-parity-2026-10-16.md`. Each Jai feature row names its Jet counterpart, its state (shipped, groundwork, ratified, open ballot, gap or refused) and the decision or card that closes it. Sources and the Jai reconstruction are in `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-10-15-jai.md`.

## Children

One child card per ballot, plus the existing build cards #5005, #5006, #5009 and #5010. This card closes when every audit row is shipped with an executable witness, or carries a ratified refusal the owner chose. The durable form of the audit is the executable coverage manifest that #3520 criterion 10 requires; this card adds the Jai rows to it.

cards.title: Expert opt-out model: how experts turn off Jet's guardrails to reach Jai-level power
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-EXPERT1 picks the one opt-out mechanism every Jai-parity power uses. Jai has no guardrails; Jet keeps them as defaults. Today each power has its own switch (`metaprogramming: unrestricted`, `#Impure` plus `--gate impure=allow`, `#StepLimit`), and some powers have none (full host access while compiling, build-wide check relaxation, string code, duck-typed generics). Audit rows: A05-A07, A20, E12-E17, B03, B06, B16.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.

Proof: a UI snapshot per opt-out shows the refusal without it, and a golden shows the power with it.

A dependency using one without the root grant is refused.

cards.title: Context parity with Jai: readable context, typed keys, scratch storage, assertion handler
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-CONTEXT1. Jai passes an implicit context (allocator, logger, temporary storage, assertion handler, stack trace, print style, thread index; #add_context, push_context). Jet has the D-CTX1 `#Context(...) { }` block for allocator, logger and deadline. The earlier context-extension card #3502 is frozen by the owner pending what context adds; the owner's 2026-10-16 direction (every Jai feature) supersedes that freeze for this decision. Audit rows: F01-F13, E24, E34.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.
cards.plan: Owner 2026-10-29: moved up; no longer sequenced after the speed goal. 1) #5030 done (C1). 2) Context reads (allocator, logger, deadline, scratch, on_assert, print, thread, trace) plus the Context read effect in sema (C2). 3) #ContextKey typed keys and task-owned context inherited by spawned tasks (C3). 4) Scratch storage and the assertion/print/trace hooks (C4). 5) Correct the spec overstatement #5892 (C5). Any exact spelling D-JAI-CONTEXT1 leaves open goes to an owner ballot before step 2. Proof per step: executable example with goldens on O0/O1/O2, UI snapshots for new diagnostics, one shared runtime meaning (I9).

log.text: 2026-11-15 TowerKeeper-1: c10, c11, c12, c16 and c20 met with G3Core commits and passing cases on dev a652c3674b (gate-p141). Still failing there: the context/context_allocator_* cases, context_scratch_block_rewinds_and_moves_what_leaves (ICE) and Examples/Memory/Allocation/ContextAllocator (served by the allocator: false), so c2 (allocator field), c4, c21 and c22 stay open.

c2 allocator field: no ballot needed (Main, 2026-11-12). Ratified D-CONTEXT1 types the field as `allocator: mem.Allocator`, and D-ALLOC-TRAIT1=A makes mem.Allocator a trait whose calls go through one trait-value slot with no box. So context.allocator reads as a borrowed mem.Allocator trait value. Arena, Bump, Pool and Fixed implement the trait, and #Context(allocator:) accepts any implementer, user allocators included, in place of the hard-coded four-name list. G12Docs-4 builds it as G3Core-c2-ctxalloc on G3Core-c2-ctxreads.

Main 2026-11-12 (c2): context.scratch reads as a borrow of the task arena, which is a mem.Arena view. Dropping it frees nothing, escaping it is E0631 and use after reset is a located stop, as D-JAI-CONTEXT1/D-CONTEXT1 state; no new type. context.allocator has no ratified value form for the current allocator: mem.Allocator is a trait, and only mem.Heap, mem.System and mem.Counting are named as package.jet allocators. That one field goes to ballot D-CONTEXT-ALLOCATOR1 (Main drafting). G12Docs-4 builds c2 for the other seven fields with goldens at O0/O1/O2.

G3Core-ctx8-r2 (c5) cut the spec status notes. Unbuilt parts it names: allocator routing in #Context blocks (new criterion c21) and context.allocator, .scratch and .print reads (already c2, c8 and c10).

Unlanded work, recorded 2026-11-12 (dead-lane sweep, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/REPORT.md). The G3Ctx lane has no agent. Only G3Ctx-1 (1e1fff240f) and G3Ctx-15 (a32aeb5757) are on dev. Unlanded and staged in Main/inbox: G3Ctx-2 (c3), G3Ctx-3 (c2), G3Ctx-4 (c8), G3Ctx-7 (c6), G3Ctx-8 (c5), G3Ctx-17/17b (c4 partial). G3Ctx-18 (c4 with #6314 c3) is only work in progress, saved as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/G3Ctx-t9.patch, with its draft message at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/g3ctx18.msg. The source tree is kept at lanes/G3Ctx/t4 (t7 is its worktree). All of it predates D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1=F (ratified 2026-11-12), so each SUB is re-checked against F and its review conditions (c16-c20) and rebased on dev before landing. Owner: G12Docs-4 (G3), after #5971.

Adversarial review of F, G12Docs-66 (Docs/audits/context-implicit-input-review-2026-11-12.md): F holds only on conditions, namely the local-value fold, module values, the #Memo key, the C-callback clause and the pure wording, each now a criterion on this card. c14 (a passing review) stays open until the spec closes those gaps and a second review passes. Decided within scope: locals that reach context stay run-time code, and module values that reach context keep E0643. The C-callback clause needs an owner ballot.

D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1 ratified F on 2026-11-12: context is an implicit input to every function, as in Jai. c2 and c13 now state F's build, and the new last criterion is F's cross-family review, which goes first.

Conflict found 2026-11-11 (G8Scope-3 sweep): c2's slice 1e1fff240f added `Context` as a 13th effect root (Compiler/Prelude Effect enum, generated EffectRoots.jet). Ratified D-EFFTYPE-KERNEL1 lists 12 roots. An effect root is user-visible language surface, so this goes to an owner ballot: ratify Context as a 13th root, or carry context reads under an existing root or a sub-effect. Until it is ratified, c2 cannot close. The ballot is drafted by G8Scope-3 and reviewed by sol-reviewer.
Correction to the previous log: the new criteria are c8 (the hooks) and c9 (the paired perf cell), not c7 and c8.

Owner asked 2026-11-10 ~21:20 where the Jai/Odin-style implicit context stands. Main probe 2026-11-10 on the t17a compiler (dev c2cecce162): `#Context(allocator: …)` blocks run, but `context.allocator` and `context.scratch` give E0107 (no `context` name), `#Context(frame_index: 3)` gives E0761 (only allocator, logger and deadline exist), and `#ContextKey` is not recognized (E0357 casing on the constant). The design is ratified (D-JAI-CONTEXT1=A 2026-10-17, D-CONTEXT1=A 2026-10-29, D-ALLOC-SITE1=A on #6314), but the card had no goal, so no agent picked it up after 2026-10-29. It is now under G3 (Core library completeness); c4 was rewritten to D-CONTEXT1's contract, and c7 (hooks) and c8 (the paired perf cell) were added.

D-CONTEXT1 is added and ready. It folds and replaces D-CONTEXT-NAME1, KEYS1, ALLOC1, FIELDS1 and SCRATCH1, which are deleted (originals in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots/backup38/). It passed Main's adversarial pass after revision 2 (older-container growth, exits, deep-move cost, the contiguous-reservation address test, the expert way out). Once ratified, amend D-JAI-CONTEXT1 SCRATCH/HANDLER/KEYS and D-CTX1 as its detail lists.

NixTmp-ctx0 landed as 36825b7a15. Runtime context is now a task-owned record (TCB@48 points to the current record, per-thread root at @448, task state @200), inherited at spawn, and #Context deadline writes in place with LIFO restore. New golden Examples/features/concurrency/context_task_inherit.jet passes O0/O1/O2 (s1 and s2), and a mutant without inheritance fails it on all tiers. Chain s2==s3. C3 is half done (inheritance; keys wait on D-CONTEXT-KEYS1). C1 is still open (no allocator or logger routing).

Context ballots on Tower: D-CONTEXT-NAME1, KEYS1, ALLOC1 (full) and FIELDS1, SCRATCH1 (short). Drafted by NixTmp (ALLOC1 by Ballots-4). Adversarial reader for NixTmp files: Ballots-4; for ALLOC1: Main. Short-ballot review recorded here because validate rejects reviewPasses on short ballots. FIELDS1: on_assert scope widening carded, re-entrancy rule, per-tier trace rule. SCRATCH1: strawman mark-stack replaced by a self-restoring Close mark (Odin TEMP_GUARD), example fixed, losses carded.
Owner 2026-10-29 (direct): context moved up ahead of the speed-goal sequencing. Assigned to NixTmp (freed by parking #5962).

Folded #5030 "#Context(allocator:) and #Context(logger:) are checked but have no runtime effect" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: #Context runtime effect is a step of context parity #5025 (D-CTX1)). Body: ## Problem D-CTX1 ratified `#Context(allocator: a) { ... }` to swap the allocator for a block (and `logger:` for logging). The parser and sema accept both fields (`crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs:1241-1295`; `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:3752-3781`), but lowering reads only the `deadline` field (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/tir_to_mir_stmt.rs:686-693`). The allocator and logger values are lowered and discarded, so `Examples/features/effects/smart_context.jet` does not swap the allocator at runtime, and that example has no golden output. Sema's `context_allocator_active` flag only feeds lint L0506 (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs:4
Owner 2026-10-26: make sure context parity gets done; decision is ratified, so tracked here as a sequenced implementation plan rather than a new ballot. Removed stale needs-owner.
Board burndown 2026-10-22: ratified D-JAI-CONTEXT1 already decides context parity; implementation remains.

criteria.text: (was #5030) #Context(allocator:) and #Context(logger:) are checked but have no runtime effect: Examples/features/effects/smart_context.jet match their goldens on o0 (jet run) and o1 (jet build), or the error becomes the intended
criteria.evidence: Examples/features/effects/smart_context.jet matches its golden on o0 and o1 at dev f2898ba8d5 (base $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/base/f2898ba8d5, 2026-11-02). o0: the wave-35 base golden run (tier run) lists effects/smart_context as passed. o1: TESTKIT_ARGS="--tier o1 --filter Examples/features/effects/smart_context" jet test Tools/testkit "suite golden" gives 1 passed, 0 failed. No known-failing row.

criteria.text: Code reads typed context fields (context.allocator, .logger, .deadline, .scratch, .on_stop, .print, .thread, .trace) as an implicit input to every function, under D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1=F: a read adds nothing to an effect row and needs no grant, a pure -[]> function may read context, and goldens on O0/O1/O2 through the one shared runtime prove it. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Context/ReadFields` on O0, O1 and O2.

#ContextKey typed keys: packages declare keys, #Context(name: v) sets them for a region, context.get(name) reads them, and spawned tasks inherit the task-owned context; goldens and UI snapshots. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Context/TypedKeys` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Context/typed_keys`.

D-CONTEXT1=A scratch blocks: `#Context(allocator: context.scratch) { … }` (or any mem.Arena) sends every allocation in the block, including in libraries, to the task's scratch arena (one contiguous reservation per task, pages committed on touch). Block exit rewinds to the entry mark, and nested blocks are nested marks. `&arena.reset()` inside the block is E0204. A value that leaves the block (a store into older data, return, a task hand-off or an escaping closure) first moves into the destination's own allocator, found by the one subtract-and-compare address test, and an older container grows from its owner's allocator. No reset call and no mark are user-visible, and dropping a scratch value frees nothing. Goldens on O0, O1 and O2 through the one shared runtime, plus UI snapshots for E0204. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Context/ScratchBlock` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0204`.

`context.trace` reads an owned list of SourceLocation records (D-JAI-SITE1), innermost first, from the same frame source as panic and fault reports, and prints the same text on every supported target; golden on o0, o1 and o2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Context/Trace` on O0, O1 and O2.

The context hooks take effect: context.on_stop (D-CONTEXT1=A: `on_stop: fn(debug.Stop)`, the handler a failed assert or panic reaches), context.print and context.thread are readable, on_stop and print are settable through #Context, and a replaced stop handler runs on a failed assert. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/Context` (ContextOnStop, ContextPrintStyle, ContextPureReads) on O0, O1 and O2; all 24 rows pass on dev a652c3674b with gate-p141.

The escape cost the D-CONTEXT1 claim rests on is measured: a paired two-program perf cell (scratch block against plain allocation) for a frame-style workload (and a second program that uses scratch differently) shows the address test costs nothing measurable outside scratch blocks and that scratch beats the plain form inside them, recorded in the canonical manifest (AGENTS.md, Performance gate). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry context-scratch` and its manifest row.

D-PRINTSTYLE1=A is built (owner ratified 2026-11-11): term.PrintStyle has simple typed default fields (int_base, int_min_digits and the rest the ballot lists), installed through the approved Context, `#Context(print: term.PrintStyle{int_base: .Hex, int_min_digits: 4}) { … }`, and applied by Core/Text/Fmt.jet's radix and decimal formatting. The ballot program prints 00ff; [0001, 0002, 0003]; x = 255. Owner: the G3 lane. Proof: an example golden on O0, O1 and O2 printing the ballot's intended output, a UI snapshot for every diagnostic the form adds, and every in-repo use migrated in the same batch (greenfield, no old spelling kept).

cards.title: Mutable globals initialized while compiling (Jai #no_reset)
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-COMPTIME1 (short ballot). Jai keeps globals changed at compile time in the binary (`#no_reset`) and copies compile-time heap data into static storage. Jet's E0622 (D-MODULE-VALUE1) requires mutable module globals to start from a literal. Audit rows: A10, A11, A12.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).
Board burndown 2026-10-22: ratified D-JAI-COMPTIME1 already decides mutable globals computed while compiling; implementation remains.

criteria.text: The syntax this card adds has its Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax row, its Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md entry and regenerated editor grammars in the same change (comptime-initialized mutable globals, D-JAI-COMPTIME1=A). Proof: after `jet self devtools grammars`, `git status --short Tools/editors` is empty, and `jet test tests/guards --filter grammar` and `jet test tests/guards --filter syntax_reconciliation` pass.
criteria.evidence: G6Meta-4 on dev 3685eb41cb, gate-p27 jet (2026-11-13). Data/Syntax Spellings.jet LEXICAL_LEDGER has the row "name := value — mutable module global… starts from any storable value its initializer computes while building", and Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:441 has the full D-JAI-COMPTIME1=A entry. jet self devtools grammars regenerated the sections, and diff -rq of Tools/editors against an untouched copy is empty. jet test tests/guards --filter grammar gives 13/0, and --filter syntax_reconciliation gives 15/0, now selecting tests since filterstem (batch 19, c01ff2ad91). Logs: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Meta/grj.sx_{gram,gg,sr}.out. c5 and c6 (the storable values and static layout) stay open.

criteria.text: A module global written `name := <value>` starts from any storable value computed while compiling, including `[U8]`, `[T]`, maps and structs holding them, with no startup copy (D-JAI-COMPTIME1=A). E0622 is retired for these. `spec.md:255-259` is updated, and a golden mutates a module-global `[U8]` at O0/O2. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (ratified, not built; compiler 0ccdff27ea).
criteria.evidence: dev bda8175585: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter tests/run/Comptime/MutableGlobalStarts on batch compiler gate-p131 (dev 8d83659ef3): 6 PASS, 0 FAIL (MutableGlobalStartsFromComputedValue and MutableGlobalStartsFromAnyStorableValue at o0/o1/o2)

criteria.text: A module global written `name := <value>` whose computed value holds exact Ints beyond a machine word, or a map keyed by a nominal type, is laid out as static data while compiling, with no first-use build or startup copy (D-JAI-COMPTIME1=A, "no startup copy"). The first-use build (atomic ready word plus compare-exchange) is left only for values that hold runtime handles, which cannot exist while compiling. A golden mutates each kind at O0/O1/O2, and an IR or object test shows no first-use helper for them. (Gap found in G6Meta-5029c5-r2, Main.)
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev since bced5762a5 (with ce550d258a, G6Meta-5029f1): a mutable module global holding a 2^70 Int, an enum-keyed map, struct-keyed maps and wide Int keys is laid out as static data, and only a Shared cell keeps a first-use start helper. `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter module_storage/module_globals_start_laid_out_unless_they_hold_a_handle` on the gate-p136 batch jet: PASS 1, FAIL 0. The case mutates each global at -O0/-O1/-O2 and in the -O2 AOT build, and `jet inspect decisions -O1` counts 0 `storage.start` calls and 0 ready-word loads in the laid-out reader.

cards.title: C source import: translate C into editable safe Jet, keep the rest behind the checked binder (c2v lesson)
cards.body: Source: mine-for-jet V report (Docs/research, 2026-10-16). V's c2v translates whole C and C++ projects to V through Clang's JSON AST (vlang/c2v README:1-86; DOOM and Doom 3 demos) and is V's main on-ramp for C codebases. Jet has no C source importer: Docs/spec/reference/migration-tier-map.md:28 keeps C binder-only by D-ADOPT-TIER1=A. The owner wants C compatibility as an on-ramp for new users (2026-10-16). V's model has two defects Jet must not copy: translated files relax the language rules (@[translated]: globals, pointer writes without unsafe, C scalar conversions; doc/docs.md:10990-11014), and vlang/doom still links the C platform layer and has broken sound (doom README:5-9). Jet already ratified one Clang declaration extractor for C and C++ (D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1=A, D-CIMPORT1=A, #4174), so a body importer can extend the same extraction instead of adding a parser. D-CSRC-IMPORT1=A (ratified) settles whether Jet translates C source into editable Jet, and so the C row of the tier map.
cards.plan: 1. Owner ratifies D-CSRC-IMPORT1. 2. If A: extend the shared Clang extractor from declarations to function bodies; translate each function into safe Jet when every construct maps (pointers to views/indices, arrays to fixed lists, unions to enums when tagged); leave the function in C behind the generated binder otherwise, with JT0101 naming the construct, span and reason. 3. Differential oracle per translated function against the original C (D-MIGRATE-SRC1). 4. Corpus: zlib, sqlite3 subset, Chocolate Doom src/doom; report translated/left-in-C counts per file.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): body reworded; the text waited on an owner answer that ratified decisions already give, or on a choice within ratified scope; it is recorded as decided (Main's operational authority) and nothing waits.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-CSRC-IMPORT1 ratified by the owner.

criteria.text: `jet import c` on a corpus (zlib, a sqlite3 subset, Chocolate Doom src/doom) writes byte-stable editable Jet (D-CSRC-IMPORT1=A); every untranslated function is called through the checked binder and carries a JT0101 note with span and reason.
Every translated function passes a differential fixture against its C original on O0, O1 and O2, and no generated code contains `#Unsafe`.

cards.title: Jet Doom: a separate GPL-2.0 project, written in Jet, proved by demo sync and benchmarked against C, V, Go, C#, Rust and Zig ports
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-16 (chat, mine-for-jet V session): 'the jet doom port would go in a separate project so that the license doesnt conflict. jet stays MIT but jet doom would be whatever license is needed. i also want as much as possible to be jet not leaning on c ffi/interop for most of it.' Doom's source is GPL-2.0 (id Software release; Chocolate Doom, doomgeneric, gore are GPL-2.0), so the port lives in its own repository under GPL-2.0; nothing GPL enters the Jet repository. Evidence: vlang/doom is a c2v translation of Chocolate Doom's src/doom only, linked against Chocolate Doom's C platform objects and SDL; its README lists inlined #define constants and broken sound effects; last push 2024-07 (vlang/doom build_whole_project.sh:10-36, README.md:1-9). Peers with source (gh metadata 2026-10-16): Chocolate Doom (C, reference accuracy), doomgeneric (C, portable), AndreRenaud/gore (Go), sinshu/managed-doom (C#), Henrique194/iron-doom (Rust), lumi2021/zigDOOM (Zig), vlang/doom (V). Feasibility: game logic (~45k C lines in Chocolate Doom src/doom plus the shared engine files) is fixed-point integer code, tables and a software renderer, all expressible in safe Jet with fixed-width wrapping arithmetic and fixed lists; the only OS edge is the Core platform layer (#5035). The C source importer (#5034, ballot D-CSRC-IMPORT1) can seed the port but is not required. Assets: Freedoom IWADs (BSD-3) can be shipped with tests; shareware doom1.wad only as an unmodified download.
cards.plan: 1. Create the separate GPL-2.0 repository (owner creates or approves the remote); vendor nothing from Jet except as a Jet package dependency. 2. Port order: WAD/zone/tables, fixed-point math and tic loop, playsim, software renderer, menus/HUD, sound mixer and OPL/MIDI synthesis in Jet, platform via #5035. 3. Correctness oracle: demo playback must stay in sync tic for tic with Chocolate Doom; compare per-tic game-state hashes and -statdump output on DEMO1-4 of doom1.wad and Freedoom demos. 4. Benchmark cell: -timedemo with rendering on and -nodraw, at 320x200 and 1280x800, single-thread, reporting fps, ms/frame p50/p99, peak RSS, binary size and clean build time; peers built from pinned commits with their release flags; record in the measurement manifest; strict gate (Jet/peer < 1.00, Rust <= 1.05). 5. Report FFI line count: target zero foreign calls outside Core.

cards.title: Compiler session protocol: jet.session.v1 NDJSON, `--listen=-` on check/build/test/run/dev, `--serve` owners and attach
cards.body:
## Outcome
One session protocol for every external client, per the ballots ratified 2026-10-17. D-SESSION-WIRE1=A: newline-delimited JSON `jet.session.v1`, UTF-8, one message per line. Reports are the D-REPORT-MACHINE1 object unchanged, build events come from the `compiler.Event` registry (D-COMPILER-EVENT1=A), the first line is `hello` with the toolchain identity, a mismatch refuses the attach (the CLI runs fresh and explains under --verbose; Jetpack reports E1227), lines are capped at 1 MiB, and artifacts never cross the wire. D-SESSION-ENTRY1=C: `--listen=-` on `jet check|build|test|run|dev` serves the protocol on stdio, with no hidden verb. D-SESSION-OWNER1=A: `jet dev --serve` and `jet self lsp --serve` may own the workspace endpoint. The first owner holds the lock in `.jet/session` and the other attaches as a client. This amends D-BUILD-SESSION1 (`dev --serve` only), and D-JPK-NODAEMON1 holds because both are foreground processes.

This card also carries the real work of #2529 (D-BUILD-SESSION1). That card is `done` without code: there is no `--serve`, `--session`, socket or tests/cli_dev_session.rs at 161cf85cc (finding F1).

## Plan
1. T2 codec: CompilerService.jet's tagged-value/CtValue codecs become the session JSON codec; `foundation_parse_protocol_json` stays the reader; the narrow diagnostic codec is deleted and the D-REPORT-MACHINE1 writer used.
2. `--listen=-` flag row in CLICommands.jet next to --threads/--trace; Front.jet parsing for the five verbs; session loop over the S1 session; per-verb `update` per the ratified D-SESSION-UPDATE1 table.
3. `--serve` on `jet dev` and `jet self lsp`: endpoint security as ratified (0700 per-user dir, symlinks rejected, peer credentials, nonce from .jet/session, one owner per workspace by lock); `--session=auto|off|required` attach on build/run/test; `invoke` envelope; Ctrl-C cancels the client's request.
4. Docs/spec/reference/cli.md section for --listen and --serve; help snapshots regenerated in the same commit.

Identity set: Compiler/ only, so this lands after a0_004.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: every criterion has a proof; c1 drops warnings (D-NO-WARNINGS1=A).

criteria.text: An attached `jet build` equals a fresh build for every corpus program across success, error and ICE: the binary SHA-256 is identical, and stdout, stderr and `--json` lines are identical except for observation fields (timestamps, durations, RSS).

`jet check|build|test|run|dev --listen=-` each answer hello, update, cancel and exit on stdio, with the ratified per-verb meaning of `update`. A malformed line gets a report line and the session continues, and `--listen=<addr>` other than `-` is refused with a UI snapshot.
A toolchain-identity mismatch on `hello` refuses the attach, and the CLI runs fresh and says why only under --verbose. A line of 1 MiB plus 1 byte is refused with a report.

With `jet self lsp --serve` running, `jet build` attaches (no second compiler process), and a later `jet dev --serve` attaches as a client. Closing the owner leaves no endpoint, and the next `jet build --verbose` prints the fresh-process note.
A foreign client (another user, a wrong nonce or a symlinked endpoint) is refused, and an edit made while no session ran is picked up by the next attached build.
The adoption receipt, comparing fresh-process and attached overhead on the #2859 corpus, is recorded. Proof: a committed measurement under Docs/Audits with both timings and the commands.

D-JETPACK-SERVICE1=A: Jetpack reaches the compiler through one `jet check --listen=-` session, and `jet __jetpack` is deleted. The EnvModel and ProjectEntry service tests pass with exactly one `jet` child per Jetpack command. Proof: `jet test Jetpack/EnvModel` and `jet test Jetpack/ProjectEntry`, and `git grep -n __jetpack -- Compiler Jetpack` prints nothing.

cards.title: jet build Compiler/ --trace just works: native multi-package builds, build-entry resolution, self-contained install
cards.body:
## Owner intent (2026-10-18 14:20)
From the repo root, `jet build Compiler/` (optionally with `--trace`) builds the compiler using the `jet` on PATH. It needs no .mjs assembler, no --runtime-dir, no env vars and no prlimit. The NixOS `jet` points at the latest approved or released compiler.

## Owner rulings (this session; recorded as ratified)
- **`--trace`** prints the live phase trace to stdout/stderr. Each phase prints as it ends (wall, CPU s, cores busy, memory), with a summary at the end.
- **`--trace=<file>`** writes the trace to `<file>` as Chrome trace events, readable in Perfetto.
- **`Compiler/` becomes a package root.** Add `Compiler/package.jet` as a workspace whose members are the compiler packages.
- **`jet build <dir>` runs the package's BUILD entry,** `fn build(...) -> ... { ... }` (the build script), not `run.jet`, which is the executable entry point.
  - The Compiler workspace's build entry builds the `jet` CLI executable from Compiler/JetCli.
  - Research the existing build-entry convention first and follow it: Project.jet already recognizes `@build.jet`, and `build.jet` is a project marker in ReceiptIdentity.jet.
  - Anything not yet ratified goes on a ballot.

## Gaps measured 2026-10-18 with the round-D compiler (dev bc5e44948)
1. **Multi-package builds with path deps.** `jet build Compiler/JetCli/run.jet` reads every dependency package (after 4 stray hard links were broken), then fails module resolution:
   - E0610 "No module named `jet_sema`/`jet_driver`/`jet_foundation` in scope";
   - E0603 "the imported dependency module is not present in its authorized package root";
   - 3,474 stderr lines in total.

   Port package-graph module resolution (transitive path deps) to the Jet driver. Then retire the Tools/agent/native-compiler.mjs assembly for the self-build (greenfield cutover: one mechanism).
2. **`jet build <directory>`.** The Jet CLI refuses it ("not part of the Jet-hosted CLI yet", Front.jet:583 jet_cli_not_ported). Port the resolution from directory to package.jet or workspace to build entry.
3. **Stack.** The compiler needs a 1 GiB stack (prlimit or ulimit). Run the compiler's main on a large stack inside the runtime or CLI.
4. **Toolchain root and identity** come from env vars (JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY). Default both from the install layout (the binary's directory); inside a Jet checkout, use that checkout. The interim launcher does this today.
5. **C toolchain** for the native link and foreign C. Today it comes from Tools/agent/jet-env (nix develop; ~3-4 s per command). The NixOS package should provide cc/ld directly.
6. **`--trace` and `--trace=<file>`** as above. Today only the JET_TRACE_FILE env var exists.
7. **The `jet` on PATH was the Rust implementation.** ~/nixos/modules/apps/dev/jetlang.nix execs the newest cargo target, and the cargo targets were removed in the 2026-10-18 cleanup.

## Interim (in place 2026-10-18 14:15)
- `~/.local/share/jet-seeds/current` points to `round-d/`, which holds `jet`, `jet-runtime/`, `toolchain/` (an export of bc5e44948), `IDENTITY` and `SOURCE`.
- The launcher `~/.local/share/jet-seeds/bin/jet` supplies the stack, the toolchain and identity defaults, and jet-env.
- It is linked as `$JET_STATE_ROOT/targets/approved/release/jet`, which the existing NixOS wrapper scans, so `jet` on PATH runs the approved compiler without a rebuild.
- Approving a new compiler means repointing `current`.
- Follow-up: change jetlang.nix to exec the launcher directly (one nixos-rebuild) and drop the cargo scan.

## Acceptance
- In a clean checkout, `jet build Compiler/` builds a jet CLI identical to chain s2 for the same SHA.
- `jet build Compiler/ --trace` shows the live phases.
- It works with only the approved `jet` on PATH.
- Collect-all diagnostics.
- Examples and UI snapshots cover the new CLI behaviour (I4/I5).

- **Types:** BuildContext → Build, TestSuite → Test, a new Dev context. BenchSuite and the bench command are removed (benchmarks are measurement tests).
- **Build:** `fn build(b: Build)` returns nothing. The driver takes the plan from the Build session after the call (BuildQueries.jet currently demands a returned BuildPlan, E3502). `b.plan()` stays only as an introspection query for graph/receipt_diff.
