B2 package-graph findings (2026-10-20, from checking each Compiler/<Pkg> as a real package with the b2 install). Fixed and committed: loader namespace fallback cascade; missing package deps (jet_cli→jet_optimizer/jet_sema, jet_sema→jet_lexer, compiler_bootstrap→its host imports); Tests/ dirs are own <pkg>_tests packages (≈190 test programs with fn run had joined the namespaces); self-imports removed; Data/ registries are own data packages; codegen nominal scope across namespace member files and across package imports (SIGILL 'fallback value disagrees with its joined type'); sema imports resolve through namespace members (E0611/E0107 on jet_lexer TOKEN_*). Remaining structural work: the assembled compiler is ONE namespace that inlines 100 Jetpack files (Foundation 5, PackageModel 65, Store 6, Trust 3, EnvModel 21) and Jetpack's own unit inlines 94 Compiler files. As real packages these form cycles: (1) jet_foundation ↔ Jetpack/Foundation (compiler used authority_holds/authority_parse_right; Jetpack/Foundation TreeHash uses mir_sha256_*) — broken by moving Authority.jet (self-contained, 402 lines) into jet_foundation Policy/; (2) Jetpack/PackageModel and EnvModel use jet_foundation/jet_lexer/jet_parser (AST, CtValue, lex, parse_lexed, record codec, sha256) while jet_cli/jet_driver/jet_semindex/jet_devserver use PackageModel/EnvModel/Store/Trust; EnvModel calls jet_cli's in-process comptime_evaluate. Plan: Jetpack model groups become packages that depend on jet_foundation/jet_lexer/jet_parser (downward only); jet_driver/jet_cli depend on them; EnvModel's comptime_evaluate becomes an injected callback (the jet_cli implementation passed in), removing the EnvModel→jet_cli edge. Then jet build Compiler/JetCli.

Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (in session), Dev context surface: jet dev is the rapid-prototyping loop (web server to view/test a web app; hot reload for games/engines). fn dev(d: Dev) configures it with d.watch(path) (extra watched files/dirs), d.serve(port) (dev web server with browser live reload), d.reload(.Restart | .Hot). Stock defaults: watching on and hot reload (.Hot), so scripts rerun live and web apps rerun or hot reload. Owner quote: 'i guess all three is fine, the default should probably be hot reload and watching so even scripts can rerun live, then web apps can be rerun/hot reloaded without issue'. Implementation note: in-process code swap (.Hot) is engine work tracked separately; until it lands the loop restarts and says so.

B1 landed on dev (33f199a4a, c824a74d2, 727bd9080, 97db9a33a, f3e31ad82, 69d368600, faaca1841). fn build(b: Build) returns nothing, b.default(target); Test context; fn run() serves apps (D-ENTRY-RUN1). Stock jet dev (build, run, watch, rebuild on change, errors wait for the next change) and jet test for packages/dirs ported to the Jet CLI; fn test(t: Test) runs before the stock harness. Native test harness now links on the Jet toolchain (TestHarness.jet replaces the Rust-only jet_rt_test_unit/spawn/join and fs/eprint symbols). Runtime defects found and fixed: rt_text_ascii rewrote shared strings in place (process worker lowercased static env literals, so reused ProcessSpecs lost variables); ProcessSpec env/env_remove ordering; test setup print trapped; test report hidden by capture policy; tests from other package member files not collected. Probes on faaca1841 (s2 1:51.70): package tests 2/2, fn test override, sibling-file tests, failing test exits 1 with the report, jet dev rerun on edit and recovery after a syntax error, spec reuse keeps env. Open: fn dev(d: Dev) context not built (needs the same compile-time evaluator host path as fn build; moves with B2); failing-test report prints the stop twice and no per-test fail line. Release chain b1-m running.

Correction to the D-ENTRY-CTX1 ratification comment: `fn run(r: Run)` there is Main's extrapolation, not the owner's words. The owner named Build, Dev and Test. Whether `fn run` also takes a Run context (replacing D-ENTRY-VALUE1's `fn run() -> App`) is open and goes to the owner.

D-ENTRY-CTX1 ratified (A, amended): `fn build(b: Build)`, `fn dev(d: Dev)`, `fn test(t: Test)`, with no return types. Each entry configures the context it receives, and the command uses that context implicitly. There is no bench command or Bench context; benchmarks are measurement-style tests within `jet test`. The cutover retires BuildContext/BuildPlan returns, TestSuite and BenchSuite, migrates every in-repo caller and example, and revisits D-CONF-ENTRY1/D-CMD-OVERRIDE1 wording. The Compiler workspace fn build is the first user.

criteria.text: From the repository root, `jet build Compiler/` with the `jet` on PATH builds the compiler with no .mjs assembler, no --runtime-dir, no environment variables and no prlimit. Proof: from a clean checkout, `jet build Compiler/` exits 0 with a scrubbed environment (`env -i PATH=$PATH HOME=$HOME`), and the built jet passes `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLICommands/`.

`--trace` prints each phase as it ends (wall, CPU s, cores busy, memory) with a summary; `--trace=<file>` writes Chrome trace events Perfetto reads. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLICommands/build_trace_phases` and `--filter cli_commands/build_trace_file_is_chrome_trace`.

cards.title: Compiler architecture review follow-ups: generator gate, gated tool packages, one helper home, one layout owner
cards.body:
Destination: the findings of the 2026-10-22 architecture review (Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md) that no other card owns are closed: generators have one freshness gate, every tool package is gated or deleted, Core and the runtime share one internal helper home, layout has one owner, every import is declared, and IR Lint keeps the Core arity rows true.

Why it matters: drift between copies is silent; each of these is a place where a fix in one copy does not reach the others (Pillar 5, Docs/spec/philosophy.md: one home per rule).

The pipeline itself is ratified as D-ARCH-IR1=A (one non-SSA slot IR between the AST and machine code) and is built: JetIR is the only IR, and IR Lint types every op (db30a75783).

Owned elsewhere: the route tables (#6151, #6615 c8), keep-going's second control flow (#4914), the sandbox target and the committed guest wasm (#6366).

log.text: Closed as merged: every open criterion moved to the card that owns its work, each tagged (was #5073 cN): #6952 (1), #6568 (1), #6880 (1), #6203 (1), #4723 (1), #6851 (1).

Rebuilt: legacy one-line items restated from the 2026-10-22 architecture review with dev counts and proofs; c3, c11, c14-c16 met; c1 merged into #6615 c8; c7 moved to #4914 c11; c9, c10 moved to #6366 c42, #6366 c43.
Owner 2026-11-09 asked for static typing on the remaining untyped IR ops; #6065 and #6114 are done and archived, so the follow-up criteria live here. Built by SUB OwnerDesk-1.

Single-source census F21 (Docs/audits/2026-11-05-single-source-census.md): Generators whose output no gate checks. Already owned by #5073 c2, #6168, #4896 c4; this is the drift evidence those criteria must clear. One hand-written home: The generator registry (F7). Fix: add `--check`; run every generator in s5. Drift check: s5. Drifted on 2026-11-05: Not checked (that needs the generators run) Effort S.

Single-source census F20 (Docs/audits/2026-11-05-single-source-census.md): Each runtime generator written twice. Already owned by #5073 c2; this is the drift evidence those criteria must clear. One hand-written home: One generator; the literals move into the Prelude rows (F3, F16). Fix: delete one twin (the Jet one, if the cutover goes that way). Drift check: Gate the survivor's `--check` in s5. Drifted on 2026-11-05: Not compared table by table; the generated headers agree Effort M.

Single-source census F7 (Docs/audits/2026-11-05-single-source-census.md): Which generators exist and which files are generated. Already owned by #5073 c2; this is the drift evidence those criteria must clear. One hand-written home: One generator registry (each tool, its outputs, its `--check`). Fix: gen: s5, batch-land and prescreen read the registry. Drift check: The registry's own check: every file with a "Generated by" header has a registry row, and every row has a gate. Drifted on 2026-11-05: Yes. `batch-land.sh:75` tests `git ls-files --error-unmatch Tools/agent/RuntimeGenerators` (the `.jet` is missing), so the fallback list always runs. That list (trap, lifecycle, stop-exports, host-errors, scheduler, services, test, observe, compiler-needed-text) lacks host-carriers, fault-report, unicode-tables and core-tables. s5 checks host-carriers but not observe-messages or compiler-needed-text. GEN and GENX (CoreSources, CoreCallRows, … Effort S.
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 3 criteria from archived #4131, #4535, #4540: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

Folded #5120 "capabilities feature example needs a prebuilt guest wasm" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Examples/features capabilities example cannot run without a prebuilt guest wasm module once the sandbox route is retired (s12). Provide the guest artifact through the build or mark the example as requiring it.

Folded #5119 "Manifest `targets: [sandbox]` outlives sandbox execution" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: s12 retired sandbox execution and E1258/E1259, but package manifests still accept `targets: [sandbox]`. The owner removed --target=sandbox, so remove `sandbox` from the manifest target schema, its docs and every in-repo manifest in one cutover (greenfield, no alias).

Folded #5116 "Remove dangling imports and undeclared dependencies" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). jet_comptime, jet_loader, jet_fixer and jetpack_provider are imported but do not exist; JetCli/Commands/package.jet:4-6 declares only jet_cli but imports 5 more packages. First check whether nested packages inherit their parent dependencies.

Folded #5114 "Keep-going: one failure-capture path per phase" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). JET_KEEP_GOING creates separate control flow and thread schedules in sema, comptime, lowering, optimization and emit. Use the task join with a typed trap everywhere; normal mode stops after the reporting phase. Removes the untested second path.

Folded #5113 "Single layout owner after cutover A" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). Layout is computed in sema TargetLayoutEngine, LIR lower_repr_layout and JetIR ir_struct_size/ir_enum_box_size. After A, JetIR type rows are the only layout and reflection reads them. Done when one function computes size and alignment.

Folded #5112 "Shared internal module for Core and runtime helpers" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). ascii_lower has 13 copies, hex helpers 8+, UTF-8 validators 6, JSON escaping 4 with different escape sets, checked arithmetic 5. One importable internal home plus a same-name census; no public API change.

Folded #5108 "Gate or delete packages outside the build" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). JetDevserver has 1633 check errors and JetDebug 184; Console, LSP Hover and EditActions import packages that do not exist; JetRuntime's 3322 expected errors hide regressions and need a runtime-mode check. Done when every package has a zero-error baseline or is gone. Deleting tool packages is an owner ballot.

Folded #5107 "Unicode tables as static data" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). 68,117 lines (48% of JetRuntime Source) are binary searches unrolled into nested ifs. Emit read-only data arrays and one shared lookup; add static read-only data to the IR if missing. Done when the runtime pack builds faster and the Unicode tests pass.

Folded #5106 "Generator registry with a lander freshness gate" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). 27 generators, about 8 without --check, Node and Jet copies side by side, and #5099 (RuntimeGenerators E2105 at every landing). One implementation per generator, all with --check, run as a lander gate. Done when the lander verifies every generated file at each landing.

Folded #5105 "One route registry" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5073 (Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR ->); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source: Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md (evidence at dev 45bca333d). Routes are listed in RuntimeRoutes.jet (16k lines, sorted by hand), JetEval Routes, JetIR BuildRoutes, the IR machine and CoreCallRows. Derive one registry with a generated index from #Export(c) and Core declarations. Done when adding a route edits one place.

Destination: One IR, one route registry, one layout owner.
Notes: Batch ARCH of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: per-card criteria; self-compile FIXED_POINT and goldens unchanged. Order: #5105 #5106 #5108 #5201 #5107 #5112 #5113 #5114 #5116 #5119 #5120.

Fog: no criteria yet on #5073 #5105 #5106 #5107 #5108 #5112 #5113 #5114 #5116 #5119 #5120 #5201 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).

cards.body:
# Script ergonomics ballots (final; for Main to file on Tower)

One entry per proposed new API or syntax. Each names the exact spelling, the semantics, a
before/after taken from the four idiomatic tool rewrites
(`$JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/ScriptErgonomics/idiomatic/{TestShards,WebBundleCheck,LexerKeywordRows,Lifecycle}.jet`),
and the saving counted with `count.sh` (program lines / whitespace tokens: no blanks, comments,
`#Test` blocks or `package {}`). A saving marked [INFERENCE] is read off the before/after text,
not measured on a rewritten file.
Not ballots (bug fixes, no new surface). Landed: `pad_start`/`pad_end` link, `remove_prefix`/`remove_suffix`
methods (efbc29643), web baseline (17537755c). Patch ready, not landed (see lane report): the prelude
rows below and the collecting-loop propagation fix.
- readable prelude names `eprint`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `file_exists`, `keep`, `Clock`,
  `Instant`, `Date`, `Duration` resolve without `use` (Spec.md:305-317, D-CORE-PRELUDE1/2);
  `Date.today()` reaches `LocalDate` statics; `files.read`/`read_file` take `String | Path`
  like `write`; `.or_err(...)`/`keep(...)` no longer ICE (core.prelude loads);
- integer selectors of every width (`{i64:Hex(8)}`) and `Pad`/`PadLeft` of any displayable value
  (`{n:PadLeft(2, "0")}`), as codegen already lowered them;
- `"x".pad_start(n, f)` / `pad_end` link (they share the `rjust`/`ljust` runtime routes);
- `s.remove_prefix(p)` / `s.remove_suffix(p)` are methods (String.jet already had the bodies);
- `Int.parse` (any fallible call) inside a collecting loop propagates like the statement form
  (former draft B9).

---

## B1 — List concatenation with `+`
- Spelling: `a + b` where `a: [T]`, `b: [T]` → new `[T]`; operands unchanged (read, not moved).
- Semantics: eager copy of `a` then `b`. `View<T>` operands are E0108 (write `.copy()`); maps and
  sets keep their own operators (none). No new token: `+` widens its operand set, which is
  language surface, so it needs ratification.
- Beginner path: `all: header + rows`. Expert path: `xs.extend(ys)` (in place, no copy).
- Alternatives: (a) `xs.concat(ys)` method only; (b) status quo
  `out := xs.copy(); loop y in ys -> out.push(y)`.
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:62): `text: "{HEADER.join("\n")}\n{(loop row in rows -> "{row}\n").join("")}"`
  After: `text: "{(HEADER + rows).join("\n")}\n"`.
- Before (LexerKeywordRows, 2 sites): `values := m.get(k) ?? [String]{}` / `values.push(v)` /
  `m[k] = values` — After: `m[k] = (m.get(k) ?? [String]{}) + [v]`.
- Saving: −4 lines in LexerKeywordRows, −0 lines/−9 tokens in Lifecycle [INFERENCE].
- Trade-off: `+` hides an O(n) copy; the L0501 copy-in-loop lint covers the hot case.

## B2 — Compound update of a list slot (`xs[i] += n`)
- Spelling: `xs[i] op= v` for `xs: [T]` (mutable binding), `i: Int`, every compound operator that
  exists for `T`.
- Semantics: one bounds check, then read-modify-write of the slot; an out-of-range index stops
  before any write, so no partial update exists. Maps keep E0164 (a missing key has no value
  to update); maps get no sugar in this ballot.
- Today: E0164 "Compound assignment can't target an indexed slot".
- Before (TestShards.jet:44): `loads[lightest] = loads[lightest] + row.weight`
  After: `loads[lightest] += row.weight`.
- Saving: 0 lines, −2 tokens per site.
- Alternative: keep E0164 (explicit total update).

## B3 — `String.find` / `rfind` return a character index as `Int?`
- Spelling (changed signature, same names): `s.find(needle) -> Int?`, `s.rfind(needle) -> Int?`.
- Semantics: the character (Unicode scalar) index of the first/last match, `None` when absent, so
  it composes with `slice`, `len` and `regex.Match.start/end`, which already count characters.
  Byte search stays available as `s.bytes().index_of_seq(n.bytes())`.
- Today: `find` returns a UTF-8 byte offset (Core/Text/String.jet:83) and `-1` when absent;
  `"héllo // c".slice(0, "héllo // c".find("//"))` prints `héllo /` (probe r1.jet).
- Before (LexerKeywordRows literal port): `at: line.find("//")` +
  `code: if at < 0 -> line else -> byte_slice(line, 0, at)` plus a `byte_slice` helper.
  After: `code: line.slice(0, line.find("//") ?? line.len())`.
- Saving: the byte-helper family in every text port (PortReview counted 103 lines across ports;
  −1 line per site [INFERENCE]).
- Changes a ratified API: one cutover migrating every caller.
- Alternatives: (a) keep bytes, add `slice_bytes(a, b)`; (b) only document `split_once`.

## B4 — Ambient `write(text)` (stdout without a newline)
- Spelling: `write(text: String)` in the readable prelude, beside `print`/`eprint`.
- Semantics: writes `text` to stdout unchanged (no newline), same `IO` effect and flush rules
  as `print`; `#NoPrelude` hides it like `print`.
- Today: `print` always appends `\n`; raw text needs `out := term.stdout()` +
  `out.write(text).drop("...")`; `term.stdout().write(t)` is E0111 (a plain call cannot change a temporary).
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:64-66): `else if args[0] == "--print" {` / `out := term.stdout()` /
  `out.write(text).drop("lifecycle text")` / `}` — After: `else if args[0] == "--print" -> write(text)`.
- Saving: −3 lines in Lifecycle, and its `use core.term` line once B4 lands (−1).
- Alternatives: `print(text, end: "")` (labelled argument on an existing builtin); allow `&` on a
  temporary handle for one call.

## B5 — Script entry without `fn run()` (top-level statements)
- Spelling: a loose file (or `#!` script) with no `fn run` may contain statements at top level.
- Semantics: those statements, in order, are the body of an implicit fallible `fn run()`;
  `fn`, `struct`, constants and `use` stay items; a file that has `fn run` and top-level
  statements is an error. Authority and package rules are unchanged.
- Today: "Ordinary files execute only their explicit `fn run` body" (Examples/features/script_mode).
- Before: `fn run() {` … `}` (2 lines + one indent level). After: the body alone.
- Saving: −2 lines per script (TestShards, WebBundleCheck, Lifecycle, LexerKeywordRows: −8).
- Trade-off: two entry shapes (I8), mitigated because the implicit form desugars to exactly
  `fn run()`. Coordinate with lane ScriptMode (`#!`, `-A`).

## B6 — `fail(message, code)` for expected failures
- Spelling: `fail(message: String, code: Int{1}) -> Never` in the readable prelude.
- Semantics: writes `message` and a newline to stderr, runs scope guards, exits with `code`.
  Unlike `panic` (program bugs, E3001 frame) it prints no frame.
- Before (all four rewrites): `fn fail(message: String) -> Never {` / `term.eprint(message)` /
  `process.exit(1)` / `}` (TestShards names it `usage` with code 64).
- After: `fail("...")` / `fail("...", 64)` at the call sites; no helper.
- Saving: −4 lines per script (−16 over the four), and `use core.process` where only `exit`
  used it.
- Alternative: `#Error struct` + `return Err(...)` from `run()` (exists; prints a framed report).

## B7 — Named regex groups on `Match`
- Spelling: `m.named(name: String) -> String?` on `core.regex.Match`.
- Semantics: the text of the named group `(?<name>…)` in this match; `None` when the group did
  not participate or the name is not in the pattern (the pattern is known: a `Regex{…}` literal
  makes an unknown name a compile error).
- Today: groups are positional (`m.groups[2]`); named groups parse but have no accessor on the
  source engine path.
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:45-49): `kind: m.groups[0]`, `name: m.groups[2]`,
  `m.groups[3].trim()`. After: `m.named("kind") ?? ""`, `m.named("name") ?? ""`, …
- Saving: 0 lines; removes index bookkeeping (readability only).

## B8 — `files.is_executable(path)`
- Spelling: `files.is_executable(path: String | Path) -[FS]> Bool` in `core.files`.
- Semantics: true when `path` names a regular file the current process may execute; `false` for
  a failed probe, like `is_file`.
- Before (WebBundleCheck.jet:39): `if (process.cmd(["test", "-x", "{root}/{JET_ENV}"]).run() ?? fail(...)).code != 0 -> fail(...)`
  After: `if !files.is_executable("{root}/{JET_ENV}") -> fail(...)`.
- Saving: 0 lines, −8 tokens, and no `Exec` authority for the probe.

## B9 — `Path.script_dir()`
- Spelling: `Path.script_dir() -> Path` (static on the prelude `Path`).
- Semantics: the directory of the entry source file of the running program (the file `jet run`
  was given), canonicalized; for a built binary, the directory recorded at build time.
- Today every ported tool assumes cwd = repository root; the originals computed it from
  `import.meta.url` / `BASH_SOURCE`.
- Before: `root: files.cwd()` (wrong when run from elsewhere).
  After: `root: Path.script_dir().join("../..")`.
- Saving: 0 lines; fixes a behavior difference from the originals.
- Trade-off: one more ambient read of the entry path; must be defined for `jet build` output.

## B10 — Lint: constant `re.compile("…")` should be a `Regex{…}` literal
- Spelling: new lint code (next free L-code) "this pattern is a constant; write `Regex{…}`",
  with an auto-fix that rewrites the call and un-escapes backslashes.
- Semantics: fires on `re.compile(<string literal>)` / `compile_with(<literal>, flags)` with no
  interpolation; the literal is compile-checked and needs no `?? panic`.
- Evidence: the four ports re-implemented 873 lines of scanners (PortReview) and no port used a
  `Regex{}` literal; rewrites with literals were 0.7–1.1× the originals.
- Saving: per site, −1 `?? panic(...)` and doubled backslashes.

cards.title: Jet-native raylib: a 1:1 raylib API written in idiomatic Jet that works out of the box
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-21: replace the dlopen-of-libraylib path with Jet-native raylib, API 1:1 with raylib, written in idiomatic Jet, working with no installed C library. Everything above the OS graphics boundary is Jet: windowing, input, rlgl, shapes, textures, text, models, audio mixing. Constraint to decide (owner): the GPU driver (libGL/libvulkan, libX11/Wayland) must be loaded from the user system at run time; the Jet runtime is fully static musl with no dynamic loader. Options: (a) graphical programs build as dynamically linked executables, (b) the runtime gains a minimal loader for driver libraries. Today the native tier implements raylib only on the no-library path (headless), from RouteRuntimeA2. Related: text shaping (HarfBuzz) is the same question - a Jet-native shaper (OpenType GSUB/GPOS) vs the fallback 1:1 glyph shaper.

cards.title: Build D-LINK-MODEL1=A: each linked part has its own linkage, shown by jet inspect
cards.body:
## Situation
Jet native programs are fully static Linux executables today: the runtime pack carries a private musl libc (used only for pthread, getaddrinfo DNS, and libm math) and no dynamic loader. The code already marks musl as interim (Compiler/JetRuntime/imports.list:10 "musl until glibc dynamic linking"; Thread.jet: "interim pthread imports die when musl leaves the pack"; raw clone/futex already written). D-JPK-VARIANT1=D ratified `runtime/libc` and `linkage` as native variant axes with context-derived defaults, but no decision says which default applies when.

The owner wants Jet-native raylib (#5086) that works out of the box. The GPU is only reachable through the vendor driver the user's OS ships (Linux: libGL/libEGL/libvulkan + libX11/libwayland-client, built against glibc; macOS: Metal/libSystem; Windows: d3d/opengl32/kernel32). Those must be loaded from the user's system at run time by the platform's own loader. A static musl process cannot load a glibc-built driver (the driver expects glibc's loader, TLS and allocator).

Other languages: C, C++, Rust, Jai link the platform libc dynamically by default (Jai: `#system_library "d3d11"`, OS loader, no custom loader). Go and Zig build fully static binaries with no libc for pure programs and switch to dynamic platform-libc linking when a program needs system libraries (cgo / linkSystemLibrary). macOS and Windows effectively require dynamic system libraries for every program.

## Same program under each option
```jet
// tool.jet (CLI)        // game.jet
fn run() {               fn run() {
    print("hi")              window := game.open(800, 600, "demo")
}                            ...
                         }
```

### A. Static by default, dynamic when the program needs OS libraries (recommended)
- tool.jet -> one static file, no libc (musl removed: Jet's own threads/DNS/math), runs on any Linux of the same architecture.
- game.jet -> dynamically linked against the platform libc (glibc on Linux), GPU/window drivers loaded by the OS loader. The compiler decides from what the program reaches (graphics/windowing Core APIs, `#Import(c)` of a system library); no annotation needed.
- Expert path: `jet build --linkage=static|dynamic` (the D-JPK-VARIANT1 axis) to force either; forcing static on a program that needs drivers is a diagnostic.
- macOS/Windows: always dynamic against system libraries (the platforms require it); static only on Linux.
- Trade-offs: two link modes to maintain and test (I9 parity runs both). Dynamic Linux builds inherit glibc version skew: build against an old-enough glibc baseline (as Go/Rust release builds do) so binaries run on older distros.
- Edge cases: a static program that later adds graphics silently becomes dynamic (shown in `jet build` output and `jet inspect`); plugin hosts (#5087) stay static (the WASM interpreter needs no OS library).

### B. Always dynamic (C/Rust/Jai model)
- Both programs link the platform libc dynamically. One mode, simplest mental model, drivers always reachable.
- Trade-offs: no "copy one file to any Linux box" for CLI tools and servers (glibc skew; containers need a libc); slightly slower start; musl still leaves.

### C. Always static, with a Jet-written loader for driver libraries
- Listed for completeness, not recommended: vendor GPU drivers (Mesa, NVIDIA) are glibc-built and depend on glibc loader internals and TLS; a custom loader in a non-glibc process would have to reimplement glibc's ABI. Impractical and fragile.

### D. Keep today's model (static musl, no graphics without dlopen)
- Raylib stays headless-only natively; contradicts the owner direction in #5086.

## Related owner directions (2026-10-21)
- HarfBuzz is removed: core.font shapes with Jet's own shaper only (correct for Latin/Cyrillic/Greek; complex scripts wrong until a Jet-native OpenType GSUB/GPOS shaper exists - Rust's rustybuzz and Go's go-text are pure-language precedents).
- musl leaves the runtime in every option (Jet-owned threads, DNS resolver, math).

log.text: Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-LINK-MODEL1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Owner amendment (2026-10-21): linkage is decided PER LINKED ITEM, not only per program, and is controllable in the package's fn build settings. Each linked item (Jet runtime and libc, a system library such as libGL or libX11, a bundled C library, a foreign closure) carries its own linkage (static or dynamic); option A's rule supplies each item's default (pure Jet and bundled C sources static; OS driver and system libraries dynamic, which makes the executable dynamically linked against the platform libc). The build function can override linkage per item (and the CLI flag --linkage stays the whole-program expert override). A request that cannot work (static linkage for a system driver library, static libc on macOS/Windows) is a diagnostic. To ballot before implementation: the exact build-settings spelling, the per-item defaults table, and how jet inspect reports the resulting linkage per item.

Owner selected option A (2026-10-21): static by default, dynamic when needed. CLI tools, servers and scripts build as one static file with no libc (musl leaves the runtime: Jet-owned threads via raw clone/futex, DNS resolver, math). Programs that reach graphics/windowing Core APIs or import a system C library build dynamically linked against the platform libc (glibc on Linux, with an old-enough baseline for portability) so OS drivers load through the platform loader; macOS/Windows always link system libraries dynamically. Expert override: jet build --linkage=static|dynamic (the D-JPK-VARIANT1 linkage axis); forcing static on a program that needs drivers is a diagnostic. Also owner directions: HarfBuzz removed (core.font shapes with Jet's own shaper; a Jet-native OpenType shaper is the later path), Jet-native raylib (#5086), WASM-interpreter plugins after D-ARCH-IR1 (#5087).

criteria.text: D-LINK-MODEL1=A: each linked part has its own linkage (pure Jet and bundled C static; OS drivers and system libraries dynamic), `fn build` can change any part, and `jet inspect` lists each part with its linkage and source.
The declared native package and module closure feeds linker inputs and missing-library errors, including the canonical z package key for -lz, proven by link execution on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Implement the ratified Core APIs the Jetpack port needs (process fds/exec, byte I/O, seek, net inheritance, pinned HTTP, json limits, streaming archives)
cards.body:
Found by lane CliFoundation porting the Rust Jetpack fetch/add/remove/update/init/split/fold closure (Store, Provider, Nix, Publication, Environment). Each item is used by the Rust reference and has no Jet Core equivalent; each is new public Core API (owner ratification).
1. ProcessSpec: pass an open FileReader/Directory/RuntimeLock fd to the child at a fixed descriptor slot (Rust clears CLOEXEC; CacheLease, NixProjection); exec-replace the current process (Rust CommandExt::exec; ShellEnv).
2. Process byte I/O: ProcessStdin.write_all([U8]); byte reads on ProcessStdoutStream (today only write(String) and lines()). CacheEndpoints, LeaseSnapshot. (Also needed by script ports: invalid UTF-8 child output.)
3. FileReader.seek.
4. core.net: socket-activation listeners and unix peer credentials (Store Broker).
5. HTTP fetch pinned to a pre-resolved, public-checked address set (Rust jet_net::get_stream_pinned + resolve_public_addresses; Publication already calls a nonexistent core.http.client.jet_http_build_resolve) and streaming Body reads.
6. json.parse with caller limits (Nix index needs 256 MiB / depth 16; Core caps at 16 MiB).
7. core.archive streaming tar and zstd readers (RegistryFetch, NixClosureAdmission).

Body: Found by RustTests (2026-10-23): Examples golden io/archive_hostile line 15 expects Unsupported for the zstd declared output bomb; Core (both before and after ArchiveNamesLinear) gives Malformed. Decide which is right from the archive error contract, then fix Core or the golden, on every tier.

Folded #5083 "Core has no way to hand a held file lock to a child process (RuntimeLock.keep_open_for never compiled)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5089 (Implement the ratified Core APIs the Jetpack port); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Jetpack/Foundation/Source/ProjectLock.jet RuntimeLock.keep_open_for called spec.keep_open(^self.owner), but ProcessSpec has no keep_open (nor any file-descriptor inheritance other than with_directory for held directories) in Core or its history; the method never compiled (the Jetpack assembled unit has been broken since before a0_007). It was ported from Rust acquire_lease_lock + set_inheritable: the launched process tree inherits the lease lock so the kernel lock stays held until the last descendant exits. Its only caller is Jetpack/Environment/Source/Shell/ShellEnv.jet:113 (cache lease handed to a shell). B2 (2026-10-20) made Jetpack/Foundation a real package (jetpack_foundation), so the m

Folded #4687 "jet store: fresh-store open is idempotent under concurrent runs" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5089 (Implement the ratified Core APIs the Jetpack port); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Concurrent jet runs that open a fresh store must not fail. ensure_dir checks before creating, so the loser fails with AlreadyExists. Body: Found 2026-10-24 by O0Image-3 during the U7 port (#4589); detail in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/O0Image/u7/CORE-GAPS.md. Jetpack calls six Core APIs that never existed in Core: (1) HTTPDestinations/Client.destinations, the SSRF pin for registry fetches (SECURITY: currently unenforced); (2) ProcessSpec.keep_open(handle, at:) plus RuntimeLock.keep_open_for, to pass fds to a child (8 sites); (3) ProcessSpec.replace_process (exec); (4) net.inherited_listeners and unix_peer, for broker socket activation and peer-uid authz; (5) files.delete_at_reboot (Windows); (6) streaming gzip.reader, archive.tar_reader and TarKind. Interim handling (Main ruling): (2)/(4) fail closed with a typed 'not supported yet' error; (3) is emulated as spawn+wait+exit status; (5) is dropped; (6) uses in-memory bounded gzip plus a strict local ustar parser with a malicious-tar case; (1) is removed and listed as a security gap. Each of these is new public Core API, so each needs an owner ballot with exact syntax before it's built. Acceptance: ballots ratified, the Core APIs implemented with goldens, and Jetpack's interim code replaced. Log 2026-10-25 agent: Gap 12 (U7 CLI): there is no runtime-path wasm component load with a digest pin and Limits (fuel/memory/tables/timeout). The Jetpack compiler-extension and build-plugin hosts fail closed; this is owned by #5487 (own wasm engine). Log 2026-10-24 agent: More gaps from U7 Services, approved as Jetpack-local interim measures (Main 2026-10-24); each needs a Core ballot item. (9a) Process start identity: read /proc/<pid>/stat locally, parsing from the last ')' (field 22), and emit the same 'linux-proc-start:<starttime>' token as Rust; other hosts fail closed. (9b) process.find(identity) plus kill/terminate: alive means the identity matches and the state is not Z; the signal goes through the existing group kill path, with the identity rechecked first. (9c) Child stdout/stderr to log files: Core ProcessStreamMode has no File mode, so the unix path wraps argv in an sh exec redirect that keeps the pid and process-group leader. (9d) The Windows guardian Job Object needs Core containment, so it fails closed. Log 2026-10-24 agent: Two more gaps from the U7 Engine port (O0Image-3): (7) no client redirect/proxy policy in Core HTTP; Jetpack follows redirects by hand per hop after the allowlist and refuses relative Locations other than root/scheme-relative. (8) no Directory dup; RemoteCheckout reopens by path and fails closed unless the inode matches. Both need owner-ballot API before Core grows them.

Board burndown 2026-10-22: Not a ballot: every item is already ratified: D-CORE-PROCINHERIT1, D-CORE-PROCREPLACE1, D-CORE-PROCBYTES1, D-FSOPS1 (seek), D-CORE-NETINHERIT1, D-CORE-NETPEER1, D-CORE-HTTPDEST1, D-CORE-HTTPBODYLIMIT1, D-CORE-JSONLIMIT1, D-CORE-TARSTREAM1, D-CORE-ZSTDSOURCE1, D-CORE-CODECSTREAM1. Open point for the owner: this card spells the fd slot as an Int (pass_to(spec, at: Int)) while D-CORE-PROCINHERIT1 says no raw number appears in safe code; implement the decision spelling.

Core lane spelling (CorePort5) for item 1 fd passing, Directory: directory.pass_to(spec: ProcessSpec, at: Int) -[FS, Exec, Env]> ProcessSpec IOError!. Mirrors the Rust CacheLease handle passing (CLOEXEC cleared on a held handle): the held directory is duplicated into the ProcessSpec at descriptor slot at (3 or more), so renaming or closing it here afterwards never changes what the child sees; a slot the spec already passes, or a stdio slot, is IOError.InvalidInput. Shares one implementation with the compiler store bridge (compiler_with_process_directory). Golden io/process_pass_directory: the child reads marker.txt through /proc/self/fd/9 after the directory was closed and renamed; reused slot 9 and slot 2 give InvalidInput.

Core lane spelling (CorePort4) for item 7 zstd: zstd.decompress(data) now decodes every RFC 8878 frame form (compressed blocks, Huffman literals, FSE sequences, repeat offsets and tables, skippable and concatenated frames, windowed frames; dictionaries Unsupported; 64 MiB whole-buffer budget). Streaming: zstd.decoder() -> ZstdDecoder with feed(&self, bytes), read(&self, limit) -> [U8] ZstdFileError! (at most limit bytes; [] when more input is needed or all frames are done), finish(self) ZstdFileError! (Malformed on a truncated frame); zstd.reader(^file: FileReader) -> ZstdReader with read(&self, limit) -[FS.Read]> [U8] ZstdFileError! ([] at end of file). Byte-source design: push decoder (feed/read) for any source, plus an owning FileReader puller; no trait. Window limit 2^27 like the reference decoder default. Golden io/compress_zstd_stream; queued 1792605634-CorePort4.

Core lane spellings (CorePort3): (1) files.stat(path, links: LinkPolicy?{None}) -> Stat IOError!: default describes a final link itself, .Follow describes its target (std::fs::metadata, target nlink), .Refuse is IOError.InvalidInput on a final link; golden io/files_stat_links. (2) json.parse_with_limits(text, limits: EncodingLimits) -> Dyn EncodingError!: caller max_item_bytes and max_depth, mirrors patch_with_limits; golden serde/json_parse_limits. (3) FileReader.seek(position: Int) IOError!: absolute SeekFrom::Start, drops read-ahead; golden io/files_reader_seek. (4) ProcessStdin.write_all(bytes: [U8]) IOError! and ProcessStdoutStream/ProcessStderrStream.read(max: Int) -> [U8] IOError! (empty at EOF, mirrors FileReader.read); native golden pending the ProcessChild.stdout O0 field lowering. Bootstrap note: Core source cannot call new host rows until the next seed (seed E1004), so new native APIs are compiler handle methods or live in new Core modules outside the compiler closure.

Owner approved the batch in principle (2026-10-21): the Core lane designs each of the 7 capabilities to mirror the Rust capability with idiomatic Jet spelling, proves each with goldens, and records each as a ratified decision on this card; the owner may veto any spelling after the fact.

cards.title: Web target on JetIR: a new IR to JS/Wasm backend (A4)
cards.body: The Jet compiler has no live web path: no Jet CLI route constructs JetDriverCompileTarget.Web; web builds today run only through the Rust driver (crates/jet-driver MIRWeb emitter) and Bootstrap/Host/Native.rs, emitting MIR to JS (JetCodegen Emit/Web, 167 functions over 7 files) and MIR to Rust source to rustc for the Wasm bucket. JetIR/JetBackend have no JS or Wasm emitter. A6 S4b deletes Emit/Web with the MIR pipeline, and R7a deletes the Rust driver, so the 113 --target web cases stop running until this lands. cards.title: Secure, current and reproducible systems in the AI-attack era (JetOS and Jetpack)
cards.body:
Owner discussion 2026-10-23: Jet aims to replace Nix. Nix buys reproducibility by pinning, while current security advice (AI shortens patch-to-exploit from weeks to hours) is "update everything fast". These goals conflict less than they seem: a declarative system can make updates atomic, reversible and verifiable, so it should be the easiest system to keep current. This umbrella collects the directions to discuss and plan later; nothing here is scheduled now.

Directions (child cards):
1. Need fewer updates: memory safety (I1) removes the largest CVE class; per-program authority limits blast radius.
2. Make updating cheap and safe: a security lane separate from feature pins, atomic generations, health checks, automatic rollback, exact advisory matching, optional targeted patching (grafts).
3. Make updates trustworthy: capability diffs on update, independent-builder reproducibility checks, signed trust root and transparency log (#2199), hermetic builds with no install scripts (#4760), bootstrappability from a small seed (#4154).
4. Declarative plus imperative: imperative changes write back to the declaration, giving an audit trail, drift detection and attested generations.
5. AI agents as users: capability-limited agent sessions by default.

Choices for ballots (Q1 and Q3 are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15); Q2 is settled by D-AUTH-DEFAULT1=A, #5459):
Q1. Should JetOS apply security fixes automatically by default, or only when the declaration opts in?
Q2. Should a dependency update that widens authority (new network, file write, #Unsafe) be blocked until approved, or only flagged?
Q3. Is temporarily breaking bit-reproducibility for patch speed (grafts) acceptable if recorded and reconciled, or should reproducibility be absolute with a faster build farm instead?

Related existing cards: #2199 trust root, #3033 release updates without breaking the app, #3418 inferred effects and policy, #4154 bootstrap resilience, #4195 portable sandboxed app format, #4268 authority and sandbox boundaries, #4760 build hooks in the sandbox, #5070 package effects block.

cards.title: JetOS security update lane: fixes apply within a window, separate from feature pins, with automatic rollback
cards.body: A declaration pins features, but security fixes flow on their own lane and apply within a declared window. Each update builds a new generation, switches atomically, runs health checks (boot, services, declared probes) and rolls back automatically on failure. People skip updates because they fear breakage; this removes the fear. Owner question Q1 on the parent (automatic by default or opt-in). Related: #3033.

cards.title: Supply-chain security: exact advisory matching, targeted grafts, capability diff on update, verified reproducibility and a declarative audit trail
cards.body: Jetpack and JetOS know every input a system is built from (lock and closure). Match security advisories against that exact graph, down to the version and build options, so "am I affected?" is an exact query instead of a guess, and the security lane knows exactly what to update. Covers both packages and whole JetOS generations.

log.text: Board cleanup: one stream; #5458, #5459, #5460 and #5462 merged here, every criterion tagged (was #N cK).

criteria.text: jetpack answers "is this package affected by advisory X?" from the exact lock and closure, down to version and build options (JetOS generations stay out of scope while JetOS is frozen). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Advisory/exact_match_affected_and_unaffected` on a fixture graph with one affected and one unaffected path.

Whether grafts are allowed is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15); if they are, a graft is recorded in the declaration, applied without rebuilding dependents, and reconciled by the next full build. Proof: `tower decision show <id>` ratified, then `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Graft/recorded_applied_reconciled`. (was #5458 c1)

Updating a dependency whose new version adds an effect (for example Net.Connect) or a `#Unsafe` block reports each widened effect with the dependency function that needs it, at update time and on the next run (D-AUTH-DEFAULT1=A); `--locked` refuses the update with a registered error, and a written authority row is a ceiling. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter CapabilityDiff/widened_effect_on_update` against a fixture registry. (was #5459 c1)

Two independent builds of each published package from the same inputs are bit-identical, checked by the release gate, and each build attestation is appended to a transparency log anchored at the trust root, so a silently re-published package is detected. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Reproducibility/republish_detected`. (was #5460 c1)

An imperative change to a package writes back into its declaration, and drift from the last good state is reported (system-root and boot attestation wait while JetOS is frozen). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter AuditTrail/imperative_change_written_back`. (was #5462 c1)

The final generated security report and its canonical evidence are committed, and the report lists exactly the 134 original candidate IDs, each with one final disposition. Proof: the committed report under Docs/Audits/security-final-<date>/, with a count of 134 unique IDs and 134 dispositions. (was #1387 c4)

The security-scan procedure is a committed Jet tool under Tools/ (the deleted scripts/agent/security-scan.mjs is not restored, by the greenfield rule), and its finalize step at the integration HEAD exits 0 with zero unresolved reportable findings, zero deferred items and zero open questions, and publishes Docs/Audits/security-final-<date>/. Proof: the tool's finalize run on a clean checkout, recorded in the report's gate section. (was #1387 c6)

Each release ships a compliance bundle: an SBOM, SLSA provenance and an air-gap install runbook, generated by the release gate. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter release_compliance_bundle` and the bundle files in the release receipt. (was #2199 c25)

cards.title: Targeted security patching (grafts) without a full rebuild, recorded and reconciled in the declaration
cards.body: To ship a fix for a widely used library fast, replace it in existing outputs without rebuilding every dependent (Guix calls these grafts). Trade-off: the result is no longer bit-identical to a from-scratch build. Proposal: the graft is recorded in the declaration and the next full build reconciles it. Whether grafts are allowed at all (Q3 on the parent) is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

cards.title: Capability diff on dependency update: widened effects or #Unsafe are reported with the call path, and --locked refuses them
cards.body: Jet tracks authority and effects in the type system, so an update can be diffed by what it is allowed to do, not only by its text. "This update now wants network access" or "this update adds an #Unsafe block" is shown at update time. Defends against maintainer takeovers (xz style), typosquatting and AI-generated or hallucinated packages. Q2 on the parent (block or flag) is settled by D-AUTH-DEFAULT1=A: an update reports each widening, and --locked refuses it (c1). Related: #3418, #5070.

cards.title: Verified reproducibility: independent builders must agree bit-for-bit, published to a transparency log
cards.body: If independent builders produce identical outputs from the same inputs, a tampered binary is detectable. The compiler chain already enforces this for itself (stage 2 == stage 3, 1 thread == 12 threads); extend it to every published package and JetOS generation, and record build attestations in an append-only transparency log anchored at the trust root (#2199), so silent re-publishing is visible.

cards.title: Per-program authority on JetOS, and capability-limited AI agent sessions by default
cards.body: Every JetOS program and service declares its authorities (files, network, devices, spawn) and is refused anything else, so a compromised component (for example an image parser) has nowhere to go. Software run by AI agents gets a capability-limited sandbox by default, and widening it is an explicit, logged grant, which limits prompt-injection damage. Related: #4195, #4268.

cards.title: Declarative system audit trail: imperative changes write back, drift detection, read-only root, attested generations
cards.body: The planned imperative mode writes every change back into the declaration. That gives an audit trail of what changed and who changed it, drift detection against the last good state, and one-command recovery. Add a read-only system root and boot-time attestation that the running generation matches its declaration hash, so a persistent compromise must defeat the OS on every boot.

cards.title: Compile speed: 30M lines per second, with per-phase lines/s budgets
cards.body: Owner asked 2026-10-23 for the theoretical maximum compiler speed. Self-compile input: Compiler+Core non-test = 1,263 files, 576k lines, 38.9 MB; output ~55-63 MB. Today about 30 s wall / ~120-150 CPU-s (about 90,000 cycles per token). Reference per-core targets (Carbon toolchain goals): lex+parse 10M lines/s, semantic analysis 1M lines/s; direct x64 emission (no LLVM) can plausibly match about 1M lines/s at O0. Applied: about 1.2 s single-core, about 80-100 ms on 16 cores with near-linear sema/codegen scaling, plus output write/fault cost. Physical floor (memory bandwidth plus a few hundred cycles per token end to end) is tens of ms on 16 cores. Levers: data-oriented compiler data (index-based SoA IR, arenas, no per-node RC or atomics), interned symbols (no string_compare), hashed maps, parallel sema/codegen per function, SIMD lexing, direct emission without a link step, huge pages for output. Work: add per-phase lines/s to the trace report; set phase budgets; card each gap.
cards.plan:
Owner-ordered speed program (owner 2026-11-12). This plan is the one ordered home for compile speed, run speed and the related size work. Work runs in this order. A step starts when its predecessor's criteria land, except where a track is marked parallel. Every step's proof is in its criteria.

Step 0. Measure and guard (prerequisite, small).
- #5479 c1: a throughput cell for a million-line corpus.
- #5479 c5: the train speed gate (+10% fails).
- #5479 c2: per-phase lines/s budgets that add up to 30M.

Step 1. Cut the work. This is the top priority now: 1a, then 1b.
- 1a, #6328 c22: checked Core and Prelude ship precompiled inside the jet binary. The owner ruled this part of the toolchain, not a compile cache (2026-11-08, restated 2026-11-12: option B of the exec-tiers comparison). Owner: G11Speed-4. It follows Docs/proposals/precompiled-libraries-2026-11-05.md section 8 and uses the RecordCodec format (auto-derived Encode/CBOR, no hand-written codec). Slices, each its own SUB:
  S1. check Core and Prelude alone as one closed graph; `jet devtools core-record --check` reports counts; a Core read of a per-program fact is refused.
  S2. a census in Docs/audits of every sema and IR read of Core AST or registration state while handling user code; it fixes what the record holds.
  S3. the jet.core/v1 writer and reader (header with compiler identity, target and Core digest; modules; decl and registration rows; comptime values; checked bodies; the AST S2 names). A round-trip test; two builds give identical bytes.
  S4. a core-record step in Compiler/build.jet, embedded in the jet binary, with no file I/O per compile.
  S5. the cutover: the loader and sema seed every <corelib>/ module from the record, lazily per item. The Core parse and the demand-driven Core body check go in the same change, with no flag and no fallback path. The D-CORE-LAYERS1 impl-reach rule (1b S1) stays, and is applied to the record's impl rows.
  S6. comptime and IR read Core constants and bodies from the record.
  S7. Core machine code at O0, O1 and O2 is built with jet and linked by reach.
  S8. proof: goldens, ui and cases byte-identical before and after; PortBars and #6759 c9 timings before and after; strace -c of hello.
  Known risk, measured in S1: near-name suggestions and errors in Core code no program reaches can differ.
- 1b, #6759 c10 (moved from #6281 c162): D-CORE-LAYERS1=A. Owner: G11Speed-4, after 1a (slice plan written by G6Meta-4). Slices, each its own SUB:
  S1. the reach rule: a Core trait impl is a lazy row, reached only when its type and its trait are both reached (compiler-implied traits such as Display, Equatable and Comparable count as reached). It is written as one function over impl rows (type module, trait module) that CoreReach calls today and the 1a S5 record loader calls after the cutover. Proof: the c03 probe (core.time zoned+now: 33 units, 113 MB, 0.55 s on seed-b13, pulled in through ZonedDateTime's impl Decode) before and after, plus decode and display cases.
  S2. the layer table in Core/package.jet, and a registered sema error for an upward core.<area> name under `jet check Core`, with a ui snapshot.
  S3-S5. Core moves that remove the 67 upward references in 12 pairs (census at 4bb64588): encoding to files 27, crypto to files 20, data to db 6, net to http 3, data to files/sys 2+2, encoding to archive 2, and one each of crypto to tasks, encoding to db, meta to compiler, rt to time and sync to text. Git and Target get layer rows. `jet check Core` is clean.
  S6. the proof SUB with traces.
- 1c, #6759 c1, c5, c2, c4 and c9: one comptime child per compile, and load, finalize and memory proportional to the code reached. Then #6759 c8 and c3, and #6527 c10: the PortBars speed bar for cold tool twins.

Step 2. Use the machine.
- #5479 c6: modules stream through the pipeline, comptime runs in parallel, at least 24 of 32 threads busy.
- #6328 c23: small programs compile on the calling thread.

Step 3. Data-oriented core.
- #5479 c7: interned u32 ids, flat columns, per-phase arenas.
- #5910: self-compile under 1 GB, with no per-node heap allocation or RC.

Step 4. Fused per-function pipeline and a direct executable image writer (#5479 c8).

Step 5. Front-end primitives and budgets.
- #5910 c6: a SIMD lexer at 1 ns/byte or less.
- Every phase within its #5479 c2 budget, each overrun with a named root.

Staffing (owner 2026-11-12 evening: "do steps 0-5 right now with 1-2 agents"; G6, which ranks above this program, keeps G6Meta-4): steps 0-5 run now with one agent, G11Speed-4. Order: step 0, 1a, 1b (G6Meta-4 handed over its S1-S6 slice plan and the 67-reference census), 1c, then steps 2, 3, 4 and 5. When a probe wait blocks one item, the agent writes the next independent slice.

Step 6. The compiler compiled well (#5479 c9). Not now: it starts only once the language is mostly stable.

Owner direction 2026-10-23: every improvement that takes the compiler to 30M lines/s must also be applied to codegen, so all code Jet generates is as fast as physically possible without taking control from experts. Rule for the throughput work: each slice is tagged GENERAL (a runtime, codegen or Core mechanism any Jet program gets automatically) or COMPILER-ONLY (a data-structure choice inside the compiler). Prefer GENERAL: implement it once in codegen/runtime/Core and let the compiler benefit as an ordinary Jet program (I8 one mechanism). Examples: non-atomic RC unless shared (#5475), frozen immortal constants (mapfreeze), no reclamation at process end (#5478), escape-proven bump/arena placement (Goose lesson), small-Int fast paths, tag compare (#5473), Shared/queue primitives without futex waits on hot paths, the work-stealing task scheduler, hashed Map instead of binary search (#5474), COW uniqueness at every place (#5480). COMPILER-ONLY wins (interned ids, SoA AST/IR) are each followed by a ticket asking how codegen or Core can give user programs the same (for example Columns<T>/SoA layout, an interned Symbol type, or arenas via escape analysis). Experts keep control via the existing explicit surfaces (layout attributes, #Region, #Unsafe, explicit allocators); defaults stay safe.

criteria.text: End metric: `jet build` of the corpus runs at 30M lines per second or faster, with output identical to the slower build. Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Guards walk the tree once. A Tests/Guards run builds one shared file index of the tree in process (each path with its kind and size, and contents read on demand and held only for that run), walked once and handed to every guard. None of the 43 guards that walk the tree walks it itself. Acceptance: the guards pass unchanged, a source scan proves no guard calls a directory walk, and the 4-shard Tests/Guards run takes under 30 s cold on a dev export, down from about 75–90 s, measured before and after. Owner: Lander2, after the Land.jet census SUB. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards` passes, `jet test Tests/Guards --filter guard_no_dir_walk` passes, and a committed before-and-after timing of the 4-shard run.

Plan step 0, stop the bleeding: every train records its compiler build's CPU-s and per-phase seconds against the previous seed and fails past +10% (the train speed gate). The 2026-11-11 regression (sema.bodies 5.0 -> 52.1 s, comptime.precheck 0.3 -> 19.2 s between a0.0.43 and seed-t22) is bisected to its commits and fixed at the root, and the #6527 slide from a0_021 (53.6K lines/s, 54 CPU-s) is undone. Gate: at least 55K lines/s and at most 60 µs of CPU per line. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens).
criteria.evidence: dev bb39234060: Throughput.jet --batch judges each batch build against the previous batch's build on CPU, traced CPU and each process's phase CPU, failing past +10%. jet test Tools/perf/compile-throughput/Throughput.jet: 11 passed; --batch gate-p132c to p134 PASS and p134 to p136 PASS (traced CPU -49.7%, par 3.6 to 4.1). The lander's batch build now runs it after every build.

criteria.text: Plan step 1, use the machine: average parallelism goes from about 5 to at least 24 of 32 threads. Modules stream through the pipeline as soon as their dependencies are checked (no phase-wide barriers), comptime runs in parallel, work queues are wait-free, and the allocator keeps per-thread arenas so threads take no global lock. 32 threads beat 16. Gate: at least 400K lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 2, data-oriented core: every compiler name, symbol, type and function is an interned u32 id (no String keys in maps). AST, types and IR are flat struct-of-arrays columns, compiler data lives in per-phase arenas freed in bulk, and compiler data carries no reference counts. Peak RSS falls under 1 GB (#5910). Gate: at most 5 µs of CPU per line and at least 5M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 3, fused per-function pipeline: each function goes parse -> check -> lower -> select -> encode while its data is still in cache, with no whole-program intermediate copy, and a direct executable image writer replaces the object-then-link path. Gate: at most 1.5 µs of CPU per line and at least 20M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 4, the compiler compiled well. Starts only once the language is mostly stable (the major syntax, semantics and Core churn is done), so tuning isn't wiped out by later cutovers: Jet's own release code generation (register allocation, inlining, bounds-check hoisting, SIMD selection) and a SIMD lexer at 1 GB/s or more close the gap to hand-written machine code on the compiler's five hottest loops, each with an asm-parity ceiling cell (Tools/Perf/AsmParity). Every gain is general, applies to all generated code (owner, 2026-10-23), and is proven on a second program. Gate: at most 1 µs of CPU per line and at least 30M lines/s end to end, which is c3. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median). and `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` for the hot-loop cells.

Duplicated generic instances are measured as a percentage of backend time on phase-1 units; only above 15% does each instance get exactly one deterministic placement, and if the trigger is conclusively unmet the criterion closes with the measurement. Proof: a committed backend-time receipt with the duplicate share.

The speed gate decides each phase from the median of 3 or more runs, inside a measured noise band, and times the candidate compiler, not the seed. Found on p138: the same binary spreads 10% on ir.x64, a single run flagged noise as +26.7% ir.x64 and +31.3% ir.object, and gate-p138's main compile ran the p136 seed. Proof: two gate runs on one unchanged binary give no phase verdict, and the gate log names the candidate jet it timed.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P1+P2 load: Core reach sources are parsed once, on the parse threads. Today: `CoreReach jet_driver_reach_parse_sources` runs serially on the lead twice, once from `reach_parse_held` and once from `core_restore_bodies`. That is 205 of load_reach's 635 lead samples, about 0.4 s. Measured on the p189 trace: the load span takes 1116 ms, and only 509 ms of it is the threaded file batches. Done when: the batch trace's load lead drops by ≥300 ms, with byte-identical output.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P3 register: registration's serial passes become visible to the gate. Today: the `register` span (845 ms in p189, process CPU 4.8× its wall in tp170) has no child spans. The 240 lead samples of `sema_registration_prepare_graph` spread over about 30 serial sub-passes. The largest are qualified-name canonicalize (18), units mentions scan (15) and marker modules (12+7). Done when: each pass over 20 ms is a trace span, and the gate's register row names the largest one.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P4 comptime: the land splice's owners run on threads. Today: `LocalSplice sema_local_splice_owners` is serial on the lead: 260 lead samples, about 0.5 s. Measured on the p189 trace: `comptime.land.splice` takes 603 ms (sema.local_values 288 + 161, compare 113). Done when: the splice's owner pass is partitioned per module on CompilerThreads, and the splice span drops by ≥250 ms with identical output.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P4 sema.check: Core bodies are decoded off the lead. Today: `CoreBodies sema_core_body_load` → `sema_core_body_decode` runs serially inside `sema_check_registration_top_level`: 222 lead samples, about 0.45 s. The sema.check span is 325 ms in p189, and the rest of the decode lands in comptime. Done when: the decode runs on threads, or beside load, and the lead samples drop by ≥150.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P5a+P5b sema.bodies: direct calls stop resolving their callee by key text. Today: `Direct sema_call_direct_checked_from_target` and `sema_call_check_direct_target_owned` take 315 of the 1743 lead body-stream samples. String clone, hash and eq are the top three self symbols of the whole build (2.0%, 1.7% and 1.4% of all cycles). The bodies span is 2386 ms in p189, at 8.8× CPU. Done when: the callee is held as its symbol id, and the body stream's CPU drops by ≥10%.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P5c sema.effects: the graph is read in place on threads, and each function's node is looked up once. Today: `compiler_transfer_rows` fill/take moves every module and node twice, serially (about 35 ms). Three serial per-function key lookups (collect 8, stack 9 and stamp 12 ms) and resolve_edges (23 ms) run on the lead. The sema.effects span is 664 ms in p189. Speed-3 has SUB effects-threads-read-in-place for this.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P5c sema.effects: `sema_effect_node_index` stops looking nodes up by key text. Today: the effect graph keys nodes by function-key strings (`NameRows node_by_key`). Solve (26 ms), resolve_type_params (19 ms) and node_key_table (12 ms) each look keys up serially. Done when: nodes are indexed by symbol id, and the sema.effects lead drops by ≥50 ms.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P5d sema.failure: candidates and union rows are built on threads. The span is 148 ms in p189. Candidate collection (about 38 ms) and union rows (about 30 ms) were serial. Speed-3 has SUB sema-failure-on-threads for this, in cycle p192.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P6 other finalize: Core demand reads and keys run on threads. Today: `sema_core_demand_named` reads, keys and resolves symbol keys on the lead: 55 + 36 + 34 + 6 lead samples. Measured on the p189 trace: `sema.core_demand.name` takes 149 ms and `sema.core_demand` takes 458 + 70 ms. Done when: the named demand runs per module on threads, and `sema.core_demand.name` drops to ≤50 ms.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P7 lower: driver lowering becomes visible to the gate. Today: the `lower` span (186 ms in p189; 0.19 s wall, 0.96 s CPU in tp170 O0) has no child spans. Done when: its serial passes over 20 ms are trace spans, so a root can be named.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P8 ir.build: the IR merge stops running serially on the lead. Today: `BuildMerge ir_merge` takes 232 lead samples, about 0.46 s. `ir_merge_new`/`group`, `ir_merge_scan` and `key_rows` are serial; only `rewrite_parts` is threaded. The ir.build span is 2195 ms in p189. Done when: the scan and key rows run per wave on threads, and the merge lead samples drop by ≥100.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P9 ir.opt + ir.lint: lint's static rows are built once, off the lead. Today: `Lint ir_lint_context` → `ir_lint_static_rows` takes 37 lead samples (about 75 ms). The p189 trace has ir.lint at 90 ms and O0 at 135 + 717 ms. Done when: the rows are built beside opt or on threads, and the ir.lint span is ≤20 ms.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P10 ir.x64: the reached-only scan and release stop running serially. Today: `X64Module ir_x64_reached_only` (32 lead samples) and `ir_x64_release_fill`/`run` run on the lead around the threaded selection. The selection itself is 4351 worker samples. The ir.x64 span is 1050 ms in p189. Done when: the reached-only scan is partitioned and the release goes aside, so the lead drops by ≥60 ms.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P11 ir.object: object layout copies stop. Today: `Object x64_object_lay` (141 lead samples, of which 25 are `jet_rt_mem_move`) and `x64_object_file` (72 lead samples, of which 36 are `mem_move`) copy section bytes serially. The ir.object span is 636 ms in p189. Done when: the sections are written in place, with no whole-section moves, and the lead samples drop by ≥60.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P14 native.link: link sections are written on threads. Today: `StaticLink link_write_sections` takes 64 of the link's 143 lead samples, and `link_collect` takes 34. Both are serial. The native.link span is 409 ms in p189. Done when: the sections are written per piece on CompilerThreads, and native.link drops by ≥100 ms.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P15 residual: build.plan stops compiling build.jet through the full driver. Today: `BuildQueries jet_driver_query_build_plan` takes 502 lead samples: `lowering_inputs_selection` 281 and a whole `load_reach` 189. The build.plan span is 550 ms in p189. Done when: the plan loads only build.jet's own closure, and build.plan is ≤150 ms.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): P15 residual: the compile's target state is dropped aside. Today: `cli.target.drop` takes 1.05 s wall at 1.03 s CPU (tp170 O0), serially at exit. Speed-3 has SUB target-drop-aside for this.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): outside: build steps hash their inputs once, on tasks. Today: `Cache build_snapshot_declared_inputs` takes 221 lead samples, 153 of them sha256. `action_output_lock_rows` takes 178 lead samples, all of them sha256. Together that is about 0.8 s of serial input hashing. Speed-3 has SUBs step-inputs-on-tasks and runtime-pack-digests-on-tasks for this.

Phase root (c2 budget overrun, measured on the p189 gate trace, tp170 and the rec187 perf profile): outside: the runtime step's Core check runs on more threads. Today: the `runtime` step is 9.55 s of the 30.2 s p189 build, and it sits on the critical path after native.link. Inside it, `runtime.core` takes 6.6 s with `sema.finalize` at 2.7 s (`sema.bodies` 1.2 s) and an `ir.opt` span of 1.27 s. Done when: the largest serial share of `runtime.core`'s ir.opt is partitioned on CompilerThreads, and the runtime step drops by ≥1 s.

Root F (proved by G11Speed's bisect, 2026-11-11, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/report-bisect.md): 9afa7da76b (#6206 c22 CheckedText Hole/build) dropped the Distinct-only guard of sema_expression_checked_text_target, so every typed literal and Type.method() call walked every impl with string-cloning name lookups (77.9% of samples on seed-t22). It was amplified by 8c02016476, af8d3e09d0 and 8eaf6f17cc. Fixed by G11Speed-1, which indexes CheckedText impl rows once at registration (same rows, same order). Acceptance: the c1 cell's default-mode CPU-s on the t22 tree is at most 1.10x a0.0.43's per corpus line; comptime.precheck and sema.bodies wall are each at most 1.10x a0.0.43's; and perf shows sema_expression_checked_text_target under 1% of samples. Measured on the fix (n=1, basic): 749 to 164 CPU-s, 6.7K to 14.8K lines/s. Proof: the per-phase receipt of the c1 self-compile cell (`JET_TRACE_FILE` of `jet build Compiler` on the reserved slot, with perf where named). (was #6527 c4)

Root C: 42d3bedfe8 and d17bb32500 (2026-11-08) made `jet build Compiler` build the whole toolchain (runtime pack, IDENTITY) and regenerate the Prelude copies and keyword spans, about 23 s of untraced build steps per build (wall 36 to 74 s with CPU flat). Acceptance: every untraced step of the c1 cell is traced phase by phase and takes at most 2 s of wall, or becomes part of the traced compile. Proof: the per-phase receipt of the c1 self-compile cell (`JET_TRACE_FILE` of `jet build Compiler` on the reserved slot, with perf where named). (was #6527 c5)

Root B: bb770de593 (2026-11-01, the default level also versions small loops, runs the SSA round trip and the reductions) took ir.opt from 1.2 to 8.9 s wall. Acceptance: ir.opt at the default level costs at most a0_021's per-line cost (1.18 s wall over 646K lines) times 1.10 on the c1 cell, or each pass over that bound has its own named root. Architectural only (owner order 2026-11-11: no small tuning during language churn): the fix is pass scheduling or structure, not per-pass tweaks. Proof: the per-phase receipt of the c1 self-compile cell (`JET_TRACE_FILE` of `jet build Compiler` on the reserved slot, with perf where named). (was #6527 c6)

Root A: the a0_021 to a0_022 jump (2026-10-28 to 10-30, 54 to 89 CPU-s, compiler side +21% across trees) is attributed by the c1 cell's per-phase CPU on the a0_022 tree, both compilers, to named commits, and each named root is fixed or carded here. Proof: the per-phase receipt of the c1 self-compile cell (`JET_TRACE_FILE` of `jet build Compiler` on the reserved slot, with perf where named). (was #6527 c7)

Checking a root never needs gigabytes. With seed-b6 at d97d742871 and MemoryMax=6G, `jet check` was OOM-killed on 8 roots: Compiler/JetBackend/Tests, Compiler/JetCLI, Compiler/JetCLI/Commands, Compiler/JetCLI/Commands/Tests, Compiler/JetCLI/Tests, its GateProjection.fixture and RustForeign.fixture, and Compiler/JetDriver/Tests. Other scopes peaked at 6.0-6.8 GB. A collect-all census records the peak RSS of `jet check` for every in-repo root, and each phase's memory owner (parse, register, comptime, sema, IR) is named from a profile of the worst root. Every root's peak is then at most 3 GB, with no caching or reuse. Proof: a committed collect-all census of `jet check` peak RSS for every in-repo root, every row at or under 3 GB. (was #6527 c11)

The budget checker (Tools/Perf/Budget/Check) attributes all-thread CPU to each phase: the per-phase CPU rows sum to the build's measured process CPU within 5%, with no double counting of concurrent phases and no loss of worker-task CPU. Proof: run it on a self-compile trace and compare the row sum with the receipt's CPU-s.

Owner ruling 2026-11-05, compile model: no incremental compilation. jet run, jet dev and jet test link Core and the runtime as precompiled toolchain pieces built once with the compiler; only the user's program is compiled, fresh each time. jet build compiles from the entry points outward and includes only reached code: unreached Core code is never compiled, so it adds no bytes. Main's notes: the precompiled piece must carry Core's checked interface (not only machine code), because re-checking Core per program is c55's cost; generic Core bodies ship as IR and are specialized per program; it ships with the toolchain and is identified by compiler identity, so it is not a cache; I9 is kept because both paths compile the same Core source, and tier goldens compare them; reachability keeps methods of types used as trait objects, runtime roots, and everything in jet dev (hot reload).

criteria.text: Runtime deadlock (found by TestSpeedLead 2026-11-05): with more running tasks than about (cores+8)/2, nested joins hang. Every thread waits in futex_wait on a task that never gets a worker, because the scheduler adds at most 8 workers to cover blocked waits (Compiler/JetRuntime Scheduler.jet:1097). Reproduced by a testkit pool whose entries each join a child and its resident watcher task, on the AOT and run tiers; JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=256 avoids it. Met when a join on a child that hasn't started yet runs that child on the joining thread (or an equivalent that never deadlocks), a cases fixture nests joins inside a task group whose limit is at least the core count and finishes on O0, O1 and O2, and the testkit's default pool no longer needs its workaround.
