Decision (Main): JetDevserver clears its registration errors for c6. The swap paths that use the #6625-gated HotSwapDecision and StateRetentionFact types (NativeSwap, NativeSwap02, WebModuleSwap) keep their modules but drop those uses and return the same explicit not-available refusal as the remaining 501 routes until #6625 lands; then they are restored against the real types. Root of the 854 dependency errors in a keep-going check of JetDevserver: under JET_KEEP_GOING a registration error leaves graph.complete false, and sema_copy_nominal_has_impl (JetSema Ownership/Copy.jet) then answers known: false for every nominal program-wide, so dependency packages that check clean alone report UseAfterMove and comptime closure errors. A checker fix (graph-wide facts stay known for modules without registration errors) is assigned to G5DevX-2.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-13): JetDevserver imports about 67 names that no package declares (the devtools protocol, the old semindex query API, driver entry points, env-model and repl types). The port takes path (b): the protocol types live in jet_devserver, their only user; semantic queries use the existing SemIndex/SemRef/SemDef API; check, format and render call the current driver entries, adding a minimal public entry in the package that owns the job only where none exists; no duplicated types (I8). Features no #5931 criterion needs are dropped and listed. About 12 wrong import paths move to jet_foundation. G5DevX-2 owns it, in hour-sized SUBs.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-13), child signal dispositions: Core process spawn keeps POSIX exec semantics. Ignored signals are inherited and caught handlers reset to default (HostSpawn.jet jet_rt_process_spawn_child; SIGPIPE is reset, as in Rust std). This matches Rust std, Go and Python, and is what nohup and shells rely on. Resetting every signal (POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGDEF) was rejected because it would break deliberate SIG_IGN inheritance. core-library.md documents it, and a caller that needs an interruptible child resets or subscribes before spawning (Tools/canvas-test/Run.jet, G5DevX-canvas5b). Root of the canvas_cli_lifecycle TIMEOUT: the background-job shells in the test harness ignore SIGINT.
Owner ruling 2026-11-09: do NOT delete JetDevserver; finish the port. Not next: the goal order is G1, then G4, then G8, then G6.

cards.title: Scripting measured against every peer: the ScriptBench gate, the run phases and the peer audit
cards.body:
Owner ruling, 2026-10-28. This replaces the old rule where a `#!` first line silently granted every permission.

In plain words: a Jet script gets no extra powers just by having a `#!` line. The first time it needs one (reading files, the network, and so on), Jet asks you in the terminal, once. Your answer is remembered for that exact script. If you already wrote `-A` (allow all), Jet does not ask. Printing, arguments, stdin, time, randomness and exit are always free.

Behavior:
1. A `#!` launch line no longer grants anything implicitly (today `jet_cli_source_invocation` in Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Authority.jet sets `all = true` for any `#!/` file).
2. `-A` (or `--allow=...`) written on the launch line, e.g. `#!/usr/bin/env -S jet -A`, applies as if typed. `./script` and `jet run script.jet` behave the same. `-A` on the command line works as today.
3. Ask once: when the run needs a permission it was not given and stdin/stderr are a terminal, Jet asks before the program starts. Sema already knows the required effects, so one prompt lists every missing permission and its resource, for example "read files under ./data" or "connect to the network". It offers allow once, always allow this script, and no. "Always" is remembered against the script's content hash in the project's single top-level `.jet/` (or the user cache for loose scripts). If the content changes, Jet asks again.
4. With -A present, Jet never asks. Outside a terminal (CI, pipes), Jet never asks either: it fails with the exact-grant error (5).
5. Exact-grant errors name the smallest grant (e.g. `--allow=FS.Read:./data`) and also say that `-A` grants every effect. `jet fix` writes the chosen grant onto the launch line (scripts) or into package.jet (packages).
6. Free basics: stdout/stderr printing, args, stdin, env-free time reads, randomness and exit never need a grant.
7. `--verbose` under -A prints one line listing the effects the run actually used, so users learn what to narrow.

One meaning on every tier (I9): the prompt and grants live in the shared CLI authority path, not per backend.

cards.title: Install Jet with one tested command: release tarball, installer script and a Nix flake package
cards.body:

cards.title: New GPU and accelerator support arrives as a library: a public device-provider interface
cards.body:
Jet should run fast on any chip, including chips that do not exist yet. Today each GPU family Jet knows (CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU) is wired into Core, so supporting a new accelerator means changing Jet itself. Mojo shows the better model: a hardware vendor ships a library that teaches the language a new device. This card makes Jet work that way.

Owner direction 2026-10-28: replaces the audit's "restore AI/ML / re-scope #3955" proposal. The shape is ballot D-ACCEL-LIB1, hosted here.

Builds on ratified decisions: D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A (CPU chip instructions are Core library entries, #4565), D-HOST-CAPS1=A (packages add hardware kinds, #4195), D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A, D-COMPUTE1=D and D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1=D (Core owns the compute contract with a CPU reference). Related: #3026, #3028, #4731, #4762, #3955.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work is frozen for now. Remaining criteria need CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, Android and iOS device providers.

Merged #3028 "GPU provider matrix and actual cross-target dispatch" into this card (GPU and accelerator providers as a library); its 14 open item(s) are carried as "(was #3028)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T25: KernelIR + DeviceProvider proposal (D-KERNELIR1 and its epic card) folded here by owner direction; no separate ballot or card. Four layers, no MLIR: typed device facts (D-HOST-CAPS1) replace the string devices in Core/Compute/Solve.jet:83-84; #Kernel stays the restricted subset with a CPU reference (D-COMPUTE-KERNEL-SURFACE1=B); a provider implements caps, lower, load, launch, alloc and copy over a public, versioned kernel IR; Core.Compute tensors, autodiff and tiles target that interface. First providers are mined from the Rust-era backends #1144-#1146. Shader stages (#3027) use the same interface.

criteria.text: D-ACCEL-LIB1 is ratified.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json decisions: D-ACCEL-LIB1 (cardId = #5964) status=ratified outcome=A ratifiedAt=2026-10-28

criteria.text: A package outside Core adds a test accelerator (a provider that runs kernels on the CPU through the provider interface) with no compiler or Core change; device selection finds it from the package's hardware description and runs the CPU-reference conformance suite against it.
The existing CUDA, Vulkan, Metal and WebGPU providers use the same public interface; no provider uses a private path.
A provider that fails the conformance suite is refused at selection with a named failure and is never used silently.

core.compute selects a device by a typed `Device` value built from the hardware description; the string device names in Core/Compute/Solve.jet are gone, and an unknown device kind is a compile error with a registered UI snapshot.

Providers lower from one public, versioned kernel IR (a subset of the compiler IR; no MLIR dependency); `jet inspect` prints a kernel's IR and its version, and a provider that declares an unsupported IR version is refused at selection with a named error (test).

The CUDA, Metal and Vulkan/WebGPU providers are ported from the Rust-era backends of #1144-#1146 (code mined, not re-authored) and pass the CPU-reference conformance suite where the device exists; without the device, selection reports unavailable and never falls back silently.

(was #3028) The existing provider family runs authored compute and graphics across all required Linux/Windows/macOS/browser/Android/iOS routes without adding HIP or a second public API merely for vendor coverage.

(was #3028) Supported NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple and Android mobile GPU routes have actual device execution/readback or presentation evidence. Every required platform has a successful supported route; hardware absence does not count as completion.

(was #3028) CUDA is correctly compute-only; Vulkan, Metal and browser WebGPU carry the matching graphics routes. Receipts identify the actual provider/device/program/profile rather than a generic GPU label.

(was #3028) All adapters consume the same checked program, resource and numeric facts. F32Strict/Reproducible compute and the graphics contract agree with their references across applicable execution tiers.

(was #3028) Loader/capability absence, unsupported precision/format, device loss, queue/allocation failure and invalid lifetime produce bounded typed failures. No implicit CPU/headless replacement or fabricated success occurs.
(was #3028) Existing Tensor .Auto, provider-issued unsafe contracts, system-loader trust, backend lifetimes and I6 dependency boundaries remain intact.

(was #3028) The canonical matrix records exact applicability, source/binary/device identity and focused results. Unsupported but required cells remain open; later broad campaign proof does not replace this card's complete matrix.

(was #3028) [#3207] A 16-op chain on resident F32 input reports exactly one allocation, upload and readback (compute_residency test). There is no hidden f64 roundtrip. Kernel-only and end-to-end timing are reported separately.
(was #3028) [#3208] Examples/features/web/compute_errors.jet (wrong rank, out of bounds, bad reshape, matmul mismatch) gives identical output on native and browser. There is no second JS checker.
(was #3028) [#3209] W3: compute writes an RGBA resource that graphics consumes on one identified device, with every copy disclosed.
(was #3028) [#3210] The matched W0–W6 GPU matrix runs with compiler, device, driver, policy and cache recorded, separating kernel-only and end-to-end timing.
(was #3028) [#3211] Golden tooling/compute_ml_handoff: W4 dtype, shape, stride, device and owner, plus custom-op/autodiff composition, with every copy disclosed (D-DATA-BRIDGE1).
(was #3028) [#3222] An authored kernel traces from source, proof and cache identity to the provider program (`compute_parity -- kernel_trace_`), with typed source and device failures.
(was #3028) [#3220] Selecting a non-CPU device without its component returns the D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A actionable missing-component result (golden). Each named dependency goes to its own ballot.

cards.title: Workspace roots: check, test, fmt, doc and build act on members; status and parts list them
cards.body:
A workspace is one folder holding several packages. Today `jet check`, `jet test`, `jet build` and `jet doc` at the workspace root refuse with "ambiguous" and exit 2, `jet status` shows a phantom `target run.jet`, and a failing dependency hides its own errors. This card makes the root useful. What root commands act on is ballot D-WORKSPACE-CMD1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-04, mono_probe.sh / notes/mono_probe.log).

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-WORKSPACE-CMD1=A: at the root of a three-member workspace, `jet check`, `jet test`, `jet doc` and `jet build` act on every member, `-p <member>` narrows them, and `jet run` still asks which program to start.
`jet status` at a workspace root lists members and their entries (no phantom `target run.jet`), and `jet project parts` lists the members.
E0626 for a failing dependency prints that dependency's own diagnostics inline.
criteria.evidence: jet check of a package importing a failing dependency prints that dependency's own errors inline (E0113 at shapes/shapes.jet:2:5), then its E0626 (tests/ui/dependency_package_errors PASS, ui-liveui-n21ui.txt); a failing workspace member's errors print once (workspace_check_covers_every_member_without_picking_an_entry asserts count = 1, PASS); jet run of net/backend_battery prints the underlying E2104 (service.tree #4957 at Batteries/backend/backend.jet:271:21) before E0626

criteria.text: `jet doc` writes to `<project>/.jet/doc/` and prints that path, and never writes docs/ in the source tree. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetDoc/writes_under_state_dir`. (was #3421 c11)

`jet doc --out <dir>` never overwrites a file that lacks the generated-file header: with a hand-written docs/index.md, `jet doc --out docs` exits non-zero with a registered error naming docs/index.md and leaves the file unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetDoc/out_refuses_hand_written_file`. (was #3421 c12)

cards.title: Lockfile: committed, machine-independent, and outside the disposable `.jet/` folder
cards.body:
A lock file pins the exact dependency versions so every machine builds the same thing. Today the lock lives in `.jet/lock`, which `jet new` tells git to ignore, and it stores a build timestamp, so it would churn on every commit. This card makes the lock reproducible and places it where ballot D-LOCKFILE1 (hosted here) decides.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-02, LAY-06): generated .gitignore = `.jet/build/ .jet/lock .jet/cache/` (Host.jet:1478); `[build.stamp]` in the lock. Related: D-LOCK1 (spec), D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B, #3421.

log.text: #6563 c1 precut audit re-added 2 criteria from archived #2218: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: `jet new` writes the lock where D-LOCKFILE1=A puts it, plus the .gitignore it specifies. Proof: a jet new case (`jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_new`).
The lock holds no per-machine state: building the same project on two machines gives byte-identical locks, and build stamps live under `.jet/build/`.
The spec lists every `.jet/` subpath and whether it is disposable, and files meant to be committed live outside `.jet/`.
A lock change prints a changelog-shaped diff with version moves, added and removed counts and the net size change, and `jetpack lock diff` shows the same on demand.

A channel dependency update writes the exact lock and a build then uses it offline, a channel build with no lock is E1271, and `jetpack outdated` lists channel refs with newer releases. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackEngine/channel_update_writes_exact_lock_and_build_uses_it_offline` and `--filter jetpack_engine/channel_build_without_lock_is_e1271`.

A clean prepared environment runs a script with its recorded dependency and source hashes, missing or changed material is an error with no registry fallback, and lifting the script into a package keeps its dependency identity.

cards.title: Tables for data analysis: a dataframe type over Arrow column batches
cards.body:
Destination: Core ships a lazy table type over the shared Arrow column batches (D-DATA-FRAME1=A, ratified 2026-10-28: dataframe in Core): read a CSV into a frame, filter, group, join, sort and select by column name with compile-time column and unit checks, through the shared compute operations, and show and plot frames in `jet notebook` with no package install.

Why it matters: data analysts expect a dataframe; Jet has none.

Decisions: D-DATA-FRAME1=A, D-COMPUTE1=D (frames integrate through the compute operation family), D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1, D-DATA-READER1 (scan into column batches).

Evidence: audit 2026-10-28, DOMAIN gaps.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: D-DATA-FRAME1=A ratified (dataframe in Core); plot criteria restated.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json: D-DATA-FRAME1 status=ratified outcome=A ratifiedAt=2026-10-28 (card #5968)

criteria.text: Reading a CSV into a frame and running filter, group-by with a sum, join, sort and select by column name works and matches Polars on the same file (golden). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Data/frame_ops` against the Polars golden.

Frame operations run through the shared compute operations; no second kernel path. Proof: `git grep -n -E "fn (filter|group|join)" -- Core/Data/Frame` shows every operation calling the shared compute module.
In a frame built from `csv.decode<Row>`, a misspelled column name or a column type mismatch is a compile error; the paired Polars and pandas programs fail only at run time (test pairs).
Columns can carry units: adding a `Meters` column to a `Seconds` column is a compile error (test).
`jet notebook` shows a frame as a table and draws `frame.plot(x, y)` with no package install (test).
A typed plot plan checks marks, channels, scales, axes, legends, facets and layers in Jet source.
Text and SVG projections share the one plot plan and materialize deterministically; finite values render exactly and signed zero is normalized.
The inspector derives selections, values, schema and transformation facts from the same typed plot and table source.
(was #2449 c4) DataTable on O0, O1 and O2 delegates to the shared DataPlot semantic implementation, proven by executable and golden tests on every applicable tier.

cards.title: One manifest per project: fold env.jet and workspace.jet into package.jet sections
cards.body:
A manifest is the file that describes a project. Jet projects can carry package.jet, env.jet and workspace.jet, and a user must learn which setting goes where. Removing the legacy pkg.jet is already decided (D-JPK-LEGACY1=A, #5075). Whether the remaining files become sections of package.jet is ballot D-MANIFEST-ONE1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-05). Related: D-CONF-NAME1 (members live in package.jet).

log.text: Test finding (DeclTypes-3, w22-wave cases, q/sg/cases-w22-wave.txt): 3 env_hook cases FAIL with 'capture prefix line missing': export_changed_definition, export_failed_reload and export_unchanged_directory. A 'module env.dev {prompt}' counts as a typed env (EnvironmentHash.jet:115, environment_names > 0), so an untrusted non-tty export prints 'env.jet here is not trusted' and emits no JETPACK_ENV_HASH line. Whether a prompt-only env needs trust is a trust-law question for this manifest card, not a small fix. The other 16 env_hook rows pass once a jetpack binary is present.

Merged #5980 "Map: Package model: workspaces, lockfile, one manifest, environments" into this card (one manifest per project and the package model); its 1 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5980)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

D-MANIFEST-ONE1: FutureAudit 2026-10-28 (FUTURE.md "Votes on audit ballots", T22): a `commands:` section of the one manifest also answers the Make and just task-runner pains (Make.5); no separate task-runner ballot.

criteria.text: D-MANIFEST-ONE1 is ratified.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json: D-MANIFEST-ONE1 status=ratified outcome=A ratifiedAt=2026-10-30 (card #5969)

criteria.text: D-MANIFEST-ONE1=A: a project with environments and workspace members has only package.jet at its root, env.jet and workspace.jet are no longer read, and every in-repo project is migrated in one cutover. Proof: `git ls-files '*env.jet' '*workspace.jet'` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Manifest/one_file_members_environments`.
Package dependencies imply a prepared environment (D-DEPS-ENV1=A): each battery example compiles after `jet env --prep` with no env.jet.

Every remaining per-package or cwd-relative `.jet/` writer (build/deps, lock unless a ratified package-scoped lock, cache/api, cache/schema, codemods, game-*, jobs, state/jobs.db) writes to the one workspace root, and shared cache goes under ~/.cache. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter project_state_dir_single`. (was #3421 c7)

After build, test and run inside each member of a three-member workspace, exactly one `.jet` directory exists, at the workspace root. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ProjectRoot/workspace_has_one_state_dir` (counts with `find . -name .jet -type d`). (was #3421 c9)

One function returns the project state directory (the workspace root, else the package root), and no other code joins a `.jet` path by hand. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter project_state_dir_single` over Compiler/, Core/ and Jetpack/. (was #3421 c10)

Tracked fixture inputs that lived under nested `.jet` directories are migrated with their consumers, so no tracked file sits under a nested `.jet` and no canonical source silently disappears. Proof: `git ls-files '*/.jet/*'` lists only files under the workspace root `.jet`, and the consumers' cases pass. (was #3421 c14)

cards.title: Map: Wrong-meaning bugs: values, patterns, comparisons and checked arithmetic
cards.body:
Destination: Each listed program computes the documented value on every tier.
Notes: Batch B04 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: cd <worktree> && JET=$JET Tools/agent/jet-env jet test Tools/testkit "suite cases" with one regression case per card (o0,o1,o2 agree). Order: #3838 #4909 #4679 #4726 #4906 #4929 #5020 #5940 #5941 #4156 #4721 #4745 #4976 #4977 #5037.
Decisions so far: D-PAT-NAMED-NEST1 (ratified=A) on #3838
Fog: no criteria yet on #5940 #5941 #4929 #4679 #5020 #4976 #4977 #4745 #4721 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

log.text: I1 defect found 2026-11-15 03:23: tests/cases/closures/escaping_lambda_owns_the_file_reader_it_reads_on_every_tier.case hangs (TIMEOUT 600 s, 0.9 s cpu) on p154 through p159. strace of jet run -O0 shows openat(lines.txt)=4, then close(4) at once, then a FUTEX_WAIT forever on the main thread before the first print: the FileReader moved into the escaping lambda is dropped when line_reader ends, and the lambda then locks freed memory. Owner GoalsB-5-2 (top priority): a capture by move clears the local's drop; a drop-counter case without I/O proves it on every tier.

Closed (Map card): the G3Core lanes landed nearly every item on dev; each is now met with its commit and a passing case on dev 168e1e9e92. c10's two remaining Jetpack workaround sites went to #6661 (#6661 c6); the streamed chars() gate from c18 went to #3262 (#3262 c33).

c34 decisions (Main, 2026-11-13, for G3Core-2): (1) D-FIXED-WRAP1 A (ratified 2026-11-04) outranks the older D-POLICY-FILE1. The block marker is #Overflow(.Stop|.Wrapping|.Saturating), which replaces #Policy(arithmetic: .Checked|.Wrapping|.Saturating), and arithmetic is no longer a #Policy setting; placement rules are unchanged. The Data/Syntax row and syntax-decisions.md change in the same SUB. (2) Seed gate: part A (the integer from_* and receiver methods retired, about 3,150 callers rewritten) is seed-safe and lands now. Step (a) makes the compiler accept #Overflow and lands now. Step (b) moves every site and deletes the #Policy(arithmetic:) parser; it needs a seed that knows #Overflow and lands right after the next admit. The gap between (a) and (b) is the bootstrap seam only, as with the @T cutover in #4500. (3) Float-to-integer conversions (from_float, from_f32, from_decimal, from_fraction) are not part of D-FIXED-WRAP1; #6313 owns them.

c4 ruling (Main, 2026-11-13): the canonical typed comparison (equal_unordered, used by core.testing.compare and the history supplier) compares two Dyn.Number lexemes by exact decimal value, with arbitrary precision and never through binary64: "1.0" equals "1.00", "1e2" equals "100.0", "-0.0" equals "0.0", and "1e400" equals "10e399". Int, Float and Number stay distinct variants. Dyn == stays exact. Spelling preservation (encoding-decisions, JSON numbers) governs rendering only. Found by G12Docs-4 on b14, where these pairs compared unequal.

c29 decision (Main, 2026-11-13): the plugin wire budget is PG_MAX_WIRE = 1 MiB per string argument and result. It is declared beside PG_FUEL, PG_MAX_PAGES (256 pages, 16 MiB), PG_MAX_TABLE and PG_MAX_FRAMES in PluginHost.jet and enforced the same way (pg_failure, Budget(.Wire), PG_LIMIT_WIRE), so it adds no second mechanism. 1 MiB is 1/16 of the memory budget, so an over-budget result is still in bounds and only the wire budget refuses it. Neither the criterion nor spec.md named a number; spec.md now records this one (SUB G3Core-c29-wire).

c25/c27: ballot D-COMPONENT-TUPLE1 posted (author G12Docs-4; non-author adversarial review ReviewComponentTuple, Claude Opus, which respelled A from _0/_1 to part0/part1 after probes showed _0 fails E0357 and breaks D-NAME-SIGIL1, and rebuilt D on the #Import overlay model). Recommendation A (part0, part1). c25b needs four edits if A is ratified.

c8 reproduces on seed-b13 (D-SCRIPT-HELPERS1 authoring, 2026-11-12, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots/probes/D-SCRIPT-HELPERS1): a closure that writes a captured := local loses the write when passed as a callback, so each(...) leaves the value at 0 (p13, q09). A task that calls such a closure compiles and loses the write (q12), while writing the name directly in the task is refused with E1101 (q11), so the same write is refused in one spelling and silently dropped in the other. Closures also copy values they only read (q16, q18), against spec.md 'shared read access' (Docs/spec/spec.md:1167-1181). Rerun: sh run.sh p13.jet q09.jet q11.jet q12.jet q16.jet q18.jet in that directory.

c2 items 1-4 are proved by G3Core-t1b (7dfa3007a5, PASS 1 each); item 5 (files.map(p).path ICE) is still open with G12Docs-4. c10 items b and c pass as fallback_break_keeps_later_locals_in_scope_on_every_tier and equality_with_a_constant_payload_compares_on_every_tier.

G3Core-t1 (tests only, direct land) map from G12Docs-4. c2, the #4721 CliSeams1 items: 1 resource_returned_from_a_temporary_result_match_stays_open_on_every_tier; 2 advisory_lock_closes_through_a_moved_value_on_every_tier; 3 borrowed_file_writer_writes_through_a_fallible_function_on_every_tier; 4 optional_success_result_fallback_agrees_across_execution_tiers. Item 5 (MappedFile path field) still fails on seed-b13: files.map(p).path is an ICE, "ir.build unlowered: field of core.files.MappedFile", at O0/O1/O2, so c2 stays open until G12Docs-4 lands that fix. c3: the bare_none case covers a bare None returned from a T? E! function. `?? None` refused on T? E! is the spec rule (spec.md:1408-1412, ?? yields the innermost payload and its right side must be that payload), not this bug. c35 is covered by the recursion-stop case.

c38 shares its root with #6281 c41: a flat 1024-arm match is refused with E1403 (nests 257 levels) because arm chains reach sema as nested Expr.If. One iterative else-chain walk in sema, lowering and IR closes both.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-DECL-COLON1=A (`name: value`, no `::`); I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

The 10 Core sites stay plain T{x}. Each narrows a value that is masked or built to fit, so the new E3010 stop never fires and their meaning is unchanged. The census found no compiler sites. Destination: Collections and codecs are linear-time, one-meaning and typed (DataTree/Dyn, #Codable).
Notes: Batch C04 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: cd <worktree> && JET=$JET Tools/agent/jet-env jet test Core (collections, json, encoding, data suites) plus serde/* goldens. Order: #3236 #3280 #4295 #4306 #4472 #4602 #4626 #4667 #4884 #3271 #3272 #4412 #4499 #4520 #4682 #4739 #4757 #4781 #4789 #4828 #4886 #4611.
Decisions so far: D-LIST-RETAIN1 (ratified=A) on #4412; D-KEY-TRAITS1 (ratified=A) on #4499; D-ORDER-BY1 (ratified=A) on #4499; D-MAPLIT-DUP1 (ratified=A) on #4626; D-JSON-READER1 (open) on #4739; D-DATATREE-RULES1 (ratified=A) on #4602; D-BINARY-CANONICAL1 (ratified=A) on #4472; D-ONE-CODECS1 (ratified=A) on #3236
Fog: no criteria yet on #4667 #4682 #4884 #4886 #4499 #4739 #4611 #4602 #4781 #4789 #4828 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

Deadline triage, 2026-11-10: #5976 is G3, not a 15:00 goal. TlsLead moved to G1/G4 work after c111 (TlsLead-58). c110 (the wss server transport: option A, the runtime WsConn over a checked Jet closure transport, was proposed) and c80-c82 (the zero-arg cycle replay design) are deferred.

c11 ruling (Main, within the ratified D-ONCE-VERB1=A): List replace is the by-value swap that the ratified ballot shows (names.replace("Bob", "Rob"), "List: swap first equal value"). xs.replace(old, new) -> Bool swaps the first equal element in place and reports whether it found one. The index form replace(index, value) duplicates indexed assignment xs[i] = v (I8), so it is removed and its callers migrate in one cutover. The stdlib-api-laws.md table row, which says swap at an index, is corrected to match the decision. TlsLead-2 is building it.

c13 is parked. My earlier in-scope ruling is withdrawn. The ratified D-ENV-MUTATE1 ships the fallible set as an edition-gated correction and keeps set () on existing editions (release-policy.md:123-124), and the cases env_overlay/old_edition_invalid_set_{uses_exact_runtime_error,names_its_call_site} pin that. c13 can be done only in a new edition, which is an owner gate.

c42: the internal part is done. TlsLead-38 landed in ecf04d985a, and tcp_reads_reuse_one_buffer_and_return_only_the_bytes_read PASSes: one reused buffer per stream, and a list the caller holds stays unchanged. The public read-into surface waits on D-NET-READINTO1, so c42 stays open.

c91 is not met: the Set type's methods (len, has, clear, shuffle, max, from, to_list...) still lower to runtime builtins (Compiler/JetIR/Source/RouteBuiltin.jet:52-212 jet_set_* and HashSet::clear; BuildSets.jet:520+), not the Jet set implementation. The core.collections.set module itself has no dispatcher row. c90 has a SUB in train 3 (Main-5976c90: the core_set_foundations cases gain O1 and O2 steps).

c54-c58 probe (seed a0_042, dev e4096a0f3b, Examples/Systems/Terminal/Progress.jet). The golden passes on o0, o1 and o2 but pins only stdout. With stderr not a TTY, progress writes nothing at all (empty stderr at O0, O1 and O2), which breaks c56's 'non-TTY output emits one line per update'. On a pty it redraws one line per pull, e.g. '\rwork 33% 1/3', then 2/3 and 3/3, plus step 1/3..3/3 and break 1/3. So c54 and c55 hold on a TTY, but no committed test sees the progress text. Next: make non-TTY emit one line per update, then pin both modes in a case (a pty step and a piped step) on O0, O1 and O2.

Examples concept-area cutover (2c3e68a70b) moved paths this card's criteria cite. Read each cited path as its new home: c81: Examples/features/collections/lazy_cycle.jet -> Examples/Collections/LazyCycle.jet [new path does not exist yet: the criterion still has to create it]; c81: Examples/features/expected/collections/lazy_cycle.out -> Examples/Collections/LazyCycle.out [new path does not exist yet: the criterion still has to create it]; c87: Examples/features/collections/destructive_iter.jet -> Examples/Collections/DestructiveIter.jet [new path does not exist yet: the criterion still has to create it]; c87: Examples/features/expected/collections/destructive_iter.out -> Examples/Collections/DestructiveIter.out [new path does not exist yet: the criterion still has to create it].

Folded #4886 "List.replace does not have the ratified D-ONCE-VERB1 swap meaning (it clones to a new list)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CopyPareto1. Ratified D-ONCE-VERB1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7049): 'replace keeps only the List swap meaning'. Today List.replace is a pure clone-to-new-list in both the registry and the Rust Prelude (~Prelude:3041), not the in-place swap that returns the old value. Fix both tiers to the ratified meaning (in-place replace returning the old element) and migrate every caller in one cutover; regression on both tiers. Check the exact ratified signature first (Tower card for D-ONCE-VERB1).

Folded #4884 "List.sort_by must be O(n log n) on the JetIR route" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CopyPareto1 (goal 10), confirmed by NativeReview2 / NativeLead24-2: native O0 List.sort_by computes insertion positions over an index permutation (O(n^2)) and then allocates a replacement element buffer once (Lower/Combinators.jet:523-698/713); it may have replaced an older O(n log n) canonical index-merge. Every native program sorting a large list pays quadratic time. Main-admitted fix: make the canonical List.sort_by kernel a stable O(n log n) sort by reusing the existing canonical stable index-merge + swap-cycle (no second sort implementation), same stability / comparator semantics on every tier; regression with a large list + a stability case + a timing bound. Order: CopyPareto1

Folded #4828 "core.data.sketch: native shared-clone (Arc<Mutex>) violates ratified D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (sketches are plain values)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: I9 divergence, pre-existing. core.data.sketch {cms, hll, reservoir, tdigest}: the Core source new factories build ordinary value records (a clone copies), while the native seed Sketch.rs uses Arc<Mutex> with SHARED clone semantics (a clone aliases the same sketch), and no source types{} registration exists, so the shipped behavior is the native sharing. Runtime keeps native carriers preserving it for now. Owner decision (ballot D-SKETCH-CLONE1, later): which clone semantics the public sketch types have, and whether the source factories are dead or must change. Raised by CoreReview4.

Folded #4789 "data/plot row_type names differ by tier (I9): Rust type_name vs Jet row names vs none" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: The data/plot row_type naming differs by execution tier: native uses Rust std::any::type_name::<T>() (fully qualified Rust paths), comptime builds checked Jet row names, and the interpreter has no generic type-name marshal at all. The plot factory and the data Rows constructor stay native (uncredited) until a single per-tier type-name contract exists; other plot/data rows port normally (CoreReview4).

Folded #4781 "Lenient untyped JSON decode is declared pure but reads the wall clock and writes to stderr" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: D-JSON3's lenient untyped decode ships with no effects, yet the seed reads SystemTime::now (JSONDataTree.rs:159) and writes an audit line to stderr (eprintln). The Core port (JsonStreams7) keeps today's effect row and ledgers the hidden Time/IO as a truthfulness gap. Fixing it like the JobQueue A' ruling (add the effects; migrate callers) changes public effects, so it needs an owner decision.

Folded #4739 "json.JSONReader / jsonl.JSONLReader: one public type name, two next() signatures (DataEvent for text, DataEvent? for files)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CorelibX3 (2026-10-07) while porting the JSON/JSONL streams to Jet. Core.jet's text reader JSONReader(text).next returns DataEvent, while the native file-handle JSONReader.next returns DataEvent?; explicit parameters typed json.JSONReader mean the file handle. One public name has two shapes, so no single Jet class can express it, and users can't tell from the name which next() they get (I8: one mechanism). The port keeps today's behavior: the file-handle reader stays a native nominal boundary (dispatch only; all parse, limit, state and error policy in Jet), recorded in leaves.d. Needed: check the ratified streams/data decisions for the reader contract. Then either make both readers

Folded #4682 "core.collections Counter/OrderedMap/Chain and heap helpers copy on every operation (quadratic)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source read at dev 595e0dca3: every Counter inc and OrderedMap map_set is an O(n) scan plus a full copy, so counting n words is O(n^2); heap helpers copy the list on each push and are Int-only. Back them with the built-in [K:V] map or retire them for [K:V] methods; heap helpers take &[Int] and sift in place; add a 10^5-insert scale budget row.

Folded #4667 "json.parse is about 460 times slower than V8 on a 2.4 MB document" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven: 30,000 records, 2,366,671 bytes; default jet run parse about 12.3 s wall versus Node JSON.parse 26.5 ms (json_probe.jet, node_json.js). Fix: byte-level parser without per-character String/DataTree churn, or a native provider; add a JSON throughput budget (for example 50 MB/s on this shape) to the performance gate. Related: csv.to_string and JSONWriter grow a String by self-interpolation in a loop (csv.jet:77-80, json.jet:208-212), a quadratic copy; collect and join once.

Folded #4611 "Owner ballot candidate: json.parse_with_limits / parse_allow_duplicates_with_limits (custom depth/size limits on parse, mirroring patch_with_limits)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root idea step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found 2026-10-05 by PortIntegrate: the port's Jet sources (seed shared by port/tools and port/compiler) called core.encoding.json.parse_with_limits and parse_allow_duplicates_with_limits, which exist only as unregistered functions in Core/encoding/json.jet (not in Prelude/Core.jet exports, CoreModuleExports, CoreCallRows, docs or conformance). Main ruled: callers use parse()/parse_allow_duplicates() (defaults depth 256, 16 MiB items) and the unregistered functions are removed; if a real caller needs custom limits, ballot the API (precedent: patch_with_limits).

Folded #4602 "One DataTree: owner rulings on duplicate keys, exact numbers, strict typed text and bytes" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 1 criteria, 1 ratified decisions). Body: Owner rulings 2026-10-05 (from Idiom-Runtime3's comparison $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Idiom-Runtime3/DATATREE-DIFF.md of the ported runtime carrier vs the compiler built-in DataTree; I8: one DataTree, the built-in). (1) Duplicate object keys are a parse error; the explicit parse_allow_duplicates option keeps the later value. (2) Numbers keep their exact text: a Number variant holds the original lexeme (1.50 re-renders as 1.50; 1e400 and integers beyond Int are kept exactly); reading as Int/Float checks range at that point. (3) Decoding is strict: JSON "42" into an Int field is an error. (4) CBOR (and other binary) byte strings decode to a Bytes variant. Reconcile Docs/spec/reference/core-libra

Folded #4412 "Core List: keep only some items, in place (D-LIST-RETAIN1)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 2 criteria, 1 ratified decisions). Body: Add an in-place stable retain to Core List, as ratified in D-LIST-RETAIN1. Ports of Vec::retain must not allocate a new list. No new ballot is needed. Acceptance: retain keeps order, removes in place, and a golden checks no reallocation on the performance cell. Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired): Found 2026-10-03 by the tools port (TOOLS-N10 notebook trust store, ToolsLead-1). Core and Foundation lists have push/pop/remove/reverse/update_first but no in-place stable retain (filter by predicate keeping order), truncate or swap. Ports of Rust Vec::retain must drain by ownership into a new vector (linear, on

criteria.text: (was #4412) Core List: keep only some items, in place (D-LIST-RETAIN1): [#4513] D-ARRAY-INIT1=A: [T#N].filled(value) and [T#N].from_fn(make) write direct slots, with copy-law refusal and exact partial-initialization cleanup on every backend.

Jet bounds are traits (<T: Comparable>); syntax-decisions.md mentions closed type-list bindings for generic modules (amendment to D-GENMOD-VALUE1, around line 9118). Question: does Jet already express 'T is one of these concrete types' for generic functions with one mechanism? If not, record the gap with a two-program example; any new spelling is an owner ballot (Syntax.rs,

Body: The tooling/sync_crdt example asserts a row policy check (allows(policy, user, row_owner)) and prints the policy (`RowPolicy(table=tickets, expr=owner == user)`). Per D-DBPOLICY1 the row rule belongs to core.db, but the registered core.db API has only policy and policy_audit; the check and display leaves exist only as core.sync rows (Prelude jet_db_policy_allows/show). Golden stem parked until the owner ballot on where these functions live is ratified. Found by GoldenW2b/GoldenFix13, 2026-10-07.

Body: raylib.jet declares 15 functions, none a line or text measure, so the iprof overlay port from DaJWWePhRsM cannot be written. color(300, -5, 1, 255) silently clamps (raylib.jet:34-36,108-112). raylib.key_down("SPCE") checks clean and returns false (probe g_key.jet); gamepad buttons, axes and sprite names have the same shape (raylib.jet:76-94). Texture and sound loaders return Never! and play_sound returns Bool (raylib.jet:96-106), breaking stdlib law 2. Fix: draw_line, measure_text, U8 colour fields plus color_normalized, Key/PadButton/PadAxis/SpriteId enums and key_pressed under D-GAME-INPUT1, !IOError/!AudioError loaders.

cards.title: Close always runs exactly once: fields drop in order, and a Close during unwinding or cancellation follows the spec
cards.body:
Destination: every Close and #MustFinish value is released exactly once on every exit. Fields drop in the order D-FIELD-DROP-ORDER1=A sets, a second panic during unwinding stops the process as the spec says, and a cancel never cuts a running Close short.

Why: a Close that is skipped, runs twice or is cut short leaks a resource or corrupts its protocol (a file, a lock, a connection, a flush or a commit).

Source: map #5989 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation. Its move and copy criteria went to #6923, purity check skipping to #3039, and region release to #6924. The known-failing row for the cancel case names this card.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

Map split 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. This card keeps Close and drop order (c5, c17, c18). Moves and copies (c1, c2, c3, c4, c7, c10, c12, c13, c20) went to #6923, c14 to #3039 (PURESKIP), and c16 to #6924.
Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: respelled for D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A (x.move() replaces ^x).

Merged #5041 "No implicit copies: native codegen and compiler source copy only where the source explicitly asks (.copy()), every copy justified" into this card (drop glue and moves: moves never copy, no implicit copies); its 5 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5041)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Folded #5906 "A Close temporary passed to a borrowed parameter is never closed: sink(S { id: 5 }) skips close" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Repro (fc382a23cd discovery jet, jet run): struct S { id: Int }, impl S.Close { fn close(^self) { print("close {self.id}") } }, fn sink(x: S) { print("sink") }, fn run() { sink(S { id: 5 }); print("end") } prints 'sink', 'end' and never 'close 5'. The same happens with a generic fn sink<T>(x: T). With fn sink<T>(x: ^T) and sink(^S { id: 5 }) it prints close 5. So a temporary with a Close impl bound to a read parameter is never closed after the call (a secret would not be scrubbed, a handle not released). Files: $JET_RUN_ROOT/Main/cv/g92b.jet, g92.jet. Acceptance: the temporary closes exactly once after the call on run and build; a golden example in Examples/features/memory proves it.

Folded #5821 "A task closure keeps its captured arguments alive after the body moves them out" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by RustOut's Sglue slice (2026-10-23): with `task f(x)`, the closure environment keeps x alive for the task's whole life, so moving x out inside the body (or dropping it) frees nothing. In the compiler, ir_merge_runs(parts[at]) shared each IR part with its task, the merge rewrite then copy-on-write copied the functions (+0.24 GB at ir.build) and ir.opt copied them again (+0.55 GB); the x64 'free on a task' never freed anything before link. Workaround in the slice: pass tasks only keys and counts. Fix: a moved or last-use capture must transfer ownership out of the task environment (or the env must release a capture at its last use), same meaning on every tier (I9). Proof: an example whe

Folded #5581 "golden: `_x ::` tuple of guards never dropped; omitted fields of a partial destructure never dropp" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: - Root: no-match (output differs from golden, no diagnostic) - Triage: CARD IR ownership (mine, gB if time): `_x ::` tuple of guards never dropped; omitted fields of a partial destructure never dropped/closed - Raised at: - - Examples: memory/destructure_drop_order (Examples/features/memory/destructure_drop_order.jet) Found by the 2026-10-23 base34ad golden census (O0Load roots table).

Folded #5517 "Owned destructure skips drop output" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by the Rust test port (RustTests, 2026-10-23). The ported testkit case is known-failing until this lands. First error: jet run omits the after first/after second drop lines Cases: tests/cases/tir_patterns_and_fields/owned_destructure_preserves_observable_drop_order_on_every_tier.case Rust behavior it replaces: owned destructure drops fields in the observable order Acceptance: the case(s) pass on the current seed with the same meaning on every applicable tier; drop the known-failing row in the same patch.

Folded #5927 "Lint: sort()/min/max/<=> on a named tuple whose written field order differs from its label order" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Named tuples order by label (alphabetical) order, not written order; this is specified and intended. The compiler's own ir_first_rows sorted (at, key, row) expecting key-first, which was an O(N^2) and last-wins bug, fixed in #5911 2a. Proposal: a warning when sort/sort_desc/min/max/<=>/Map-key ordering applies to a named tuple whose written order differs from its label order, saying which order it uses and to use sort_by. This is a new diagnostic and needs owner approval (product behavior). Found by RustOut-4 2026-10-24; one other site, BuildMerge.jet:239, is correct.

Folded #5463 "Lint cost sites: rebuild TCostReport from JetIR" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: JetCodegen Codegen/CostReport.jet filled JetDriverCompileResult.cost_report while MIR was lowered (capture_cost_report). S4b-a stopped every compile mode after checking and S4b-b deleted JetCodegen. No pass fills the report now: jet_driver_cost_query (JetDriver CostQueries.jet) returns an empty TCostReport, and `jet lint` cost diagnostics (JetCli Lint.jet jet_cli_cost_diagnostics) carry only the sema L2510 rows. Port: record the cost sites (allocation, copy, dynamic dispatch) while JetIR is built and fill TCostReport there. Acceptance: the cost-lint tests and goldens that the MIR path covered pass on JetIR.

Folded #4686 "Lints: a field-less struct of static functions should be a module; a constructor must return its owner type" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: b02_static_only.jet checks clean with no warning; b01_surprising_ctor.jet: struct Payment { fn new(kind: String) -> Stripe } and Payment.new("card").id prints 1 with only an unused-parameter warning. Add a lint suggesting module X { ... }, and reject or lint a static new/over/from_* whose success type is not the owner (allow T? and T E!), enforcing D-API-CTOR1.

Folded #4671 "Lint: a Float binding seeded with infinity but only assigned Int values" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven: best := -math.infinity() then best = d over [5, 3] prints 5.0 with no diagnostic (APICompPython u17); the faithful Python port silently changes the result type. Suggest xs.max() ?? fallback. Corrects claim v3-P2:PYB-37.

Folded #4669 "Unconditional-recursion lint over call-graph cycles" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven gap: ping(n) -> pong(n+1), pong(n) -> ping(n+1) passes check with no problems (q19_mutual_recursion). Add a warning when every path through a function reaches a call back into its own call-graph cycle with no exit, as rustc's unconditional_recursion does, using the semindex call graph. Never blocks.

Folded #4629 "Constant ranges that can never run: one advisory lint and one written stride law (S19/S22)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 4 criteria, 1 ratified decisions). Body: Split from the NC-DIAG draft by the fresh review (2026-10-05) and extended with the v3-P2 delta. NEW small card completing existing law. S22 (inclusive `a..b`) and D-RANGE-EXCL1=C (half-open empty when a >= b) are ratified; S19 states a dynamic nonpositive stride raises E0123. The law never states what a constant inclusive range with start above end, or a constant stride whose sign contradicts the bounds, does; observed behavior is zero iterations. This card documents that behavior (no semantic change) and adds an advisory lint under D-LINTPOLICY1=A, visible per D-LINT-VISIBILITY2=A. Joins the lint family owned by #2141/#3919. No existing card (searched 'reversed range|empty range|descending

criteria.text: A source loop over a constant range that can never run (`10..1`, `1..10, -1`) is a tidy error with a registered code and UI snapshot: jet check and jet build list it and exit non-zero, and jet run runs without printing it. The stride law is written in the spec (S19/S22).

cards.title: Scripts may read the file you name on the command line, and use a private temp folder, without a prompt
cards.body:
When you type `./wc.jet notes.txt`, you have already said which file the script may read. This card lets that act count as the permission: a `#CLI` field of type `Path` grants reading exactly the path you passed, and a private per-run temp folder (`files.temp_dir`) needs no prompt. Everything else still asks once, as owner ruling #5949 says. Ballot D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1, hosted here, decides; this card builds the winner.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T11 items 2 and 3 (the powerbox model: a file picker grants the file the user picked). Writes are not designated; they keep the #5949 prompt.

Related: #5949, D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A (#3705), spec.md "Command registry and typed inputs" (`Path` is a supported #CLI scalar), core-library.md `temp_dir`.

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: `./wc.jet notes.txt`, where wc.jet takes a #CLI struct with a `Path` field, reads notes.txt with no prompt and no flag, while reading any other file still prompts. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/cli_path_designates_read` (a pty case).

The grant covers exactly the passed path after resolving `..` and symlinks, and only for reading: writing the passed path still prompts. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/cli_path_designation_exact_`, one case for the resolution and one for the write.
A script that calls `files.temp_dir(prefix)` gets a fresh directory under a per-run root with no prompt, and the root is removed at exit, also after a failure.
`jet run --verbose -A` and the prompt list designated paths as granted by argument, and the spec and the #5949 basics list are updated in the same change.

D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A: a manifest-less script shows one default-yes confirmation naming each authority and call site before any effect; there is no prompt when authority is fully declared, and EOF or unknown input never grants. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ScriptConfirm/` covering accept, refuse and non-TTY.

cards.title: Run-time checks for #Unsafe code and foreign edges: the hardened profile (D-MEM-HARDEN1=A) and every aliasing and undefined-behavior class, like Rust's Miri
cards.body:
Rust has Miri: a slow interpreter that catches memory mistakes the type checker missed, such as reading past a buffer inside unsafe code. Jet should have the same safety net. This card adds an opt-in checking run at O0 that tracks extra state for every value and stops with a named error on any aliasing, bounds, release, race or uninitialised-read mistake, including inside `#Unsafe` blocks and at foreign edges.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T06 ("new card for the O0 checking mode if #4726 does not cover it"; #4726 lists results, not a checker).

Related: #4309 (static IR ownership verifier, a compile-time check; this is its run-time partner), #4620 (memory model), #4726 (defined-behavior ledger), D-MEM-HARDEN1=A (shipping run-time checks for unsafe islands and foreign edges).

cards.title: `jet test` tries many task orders: seeded schedules over the replay recorder find races and deadlocks
cards.body:
A concurrency bug often appears only in one rare order of task steps, so a test passes a thousand times and fails in production. Rust needs extra tools (loom, shuttle) to search those orders. Jet already records task message and lock order for exact replay (D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A, built in the Rust era as #4252). This card lets `jet test` run a concurrent test under many seeded orders and print the seed of a failure, so it replays exactly.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T07 and T21. The Rust-era replay recorder is a capability row on the not-built census card and must be ported first.

Related: #3239 (task outcomes), #4637 (fair turns), #5468 (stop edges in tasks).

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A is spelled out across c2, c3, c4 and c8, and c1 merged into c8.
Moved from G1 to G15 (testing toolkit) by owner order 2026-11-06: G1 keeps only hand-off and durability.

c1 spelling is an owner gate: TestProfiles drafts D-TEST-SCHEDULES1 (#Test marker argument vs jet test flag vs body call); Main posts it after an adversarial pass. The seeded single-worker scheduler / replay recorder port (D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A) proceeds ungated

criteria.text: A concurrent `#Test` can ask for schedule exploration with a run count (spelling recorded in Docs/spec); `jet test` runs it under that many seeded task orders and reports the result per seed.
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6012 c8: the run-count spelling and its recording in the spec are the D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A spelling criterion

criteria.text: Under `reruns:`, each rerun picks a different task order at the pause points (task start or join, lock, channel send or receive, shared read or write, yield). A test with fewer possible orders than its count runs each order once, depth-first, and says `all N orders`, and reruns run in parallel on virtual time. A planted lost-update race and a planted lock-order deadlock each fail within the default count. The report prints the rerun, its order number, each step with its source line and the replay command, and a deadlock or suspected livelock names who holds what and who waits.
`jet test FILE "name" --seed=<n>` replays exactly the printed order through the replay recorder, reproducing the same failure three times in a row.

The `reruns:` spelling lands with its Data/Syntax registry row, a syntax-decisions.md log entry, editor grammars regenerated by `jet self devtools grammars` and re-blessed snapshots, and the deadlock text in spec.md (lines 2872-2888 on 2026-11-06) is updated.

D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A spelling: `#Test("…", reruns: N)` takes a whole number N of at least 1, and a value below 1 is a registered compile error with a UI snapshot. `reruns:` in a TestProfile, `t.reruns(n)` in fn test and `--reruns=<n>` set it for a run, in that order, and change only tests that ask for reruns. A property test with `reruns:` is a compile error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter test_reruns_` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TestSchedules/reruns_settings_order`.

D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A on the self-hosted toolchain: task message and lock order is recorded in .jetproof-replay at the scheduler, channel, lock and join boundaries, and a two-task race recorded under `jet run` replays identically under `jet run` and a built binary.

`jet run --record` is built, and the prim-receipts-G2 probe that found the defect passes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Prove/run_recorded_alias_time_receipt_replays_without_execution`. (was #6418 c115)

cards.title: Registry publish policy: short-lived identities instead of stored tokens, and a runnable example per public function
cards.body:
Two rules decide what it takes to publish a package. First, how the publisher proves who they are: in 2025 a worm spread through npm by stealing long-lived publish tokens, and trusted publishing replaces them with a short-lived identity from the CI job. Second, what a package must contain: pages with only type signatures leave users guessing, so each public function could be required to ship a tested example. Ballots D-TRUSTPUB1 and D-REGISTRY-EXAMPLE1, hosted here, decide; this card builds the winners.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T15 and T20. Already ratified and not reopened: the transparency log, TUF metadata and transactional publish (D-JPK-REGISTRY1=D), signing (D-PKGSIGN1), the trust root (#2199).

Publishing runs every doc example, and the package page shows example coverage and the reasoned exemption count; coverage is shown, not forced (D-REGISTRY-EXAMPLE1=A).

cards.title: Remote builds and shared cache work with existing build farms
cards.body:
Big teams speed up builds by running steps on a shared farm of machines and sharing a cache of results. Jet has ratified who may use a remote builder and how it is bound (D-JPK-REMOTE1=D: `build.remote` grants, `jet remote bind`), but not the wire protocol. Ballot D-REAPI1, hosted here, decides between the open protocol existing farms speak and a Jet-only one.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T22.

log.text: #6563 c1 precut audit re-added 9 criteria from archived #693, #1043, #3087: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-REAPI1 is ratified; the criteria below follow option A and are re-cut in the same change if another option wins.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json: D-REAPI1 status=ratified outcome=A ratifiedAt=2026-10-29 (card #6026); criteria follow option A as written

criteria.text: With a remote builder bound by `jet remote bind`, `jet build` runs actions on a stock Remote Execution API server and its cache through the farm adapter (D-REAPI1=A), and outputs are byte-identical to a local build. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter RemoteBuild/reapi_adapter_byte_identical` against a containerised server.
Remote use still needs the D-JPK-REMOTE1=D grants: a project can neither force remote execution nor name an endpoint.
Local and remote action identity, inputs, outputs, worker platform, sandbox, signatures, provenance, cache publication and the consumed build result mean the same.

Corrupt or mismatched entries, malicious workers, lost connections, cancellation, timeout, replay, partial upload and sandbox failure never become local truth or publish partial outputs. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter RemoteBuild/hostile_remote_`, one case per failure.

The remote scheduler picks a builder by capability and fails over in order, an ineligible builder falls back locally when allowed, and remote execution identity binds the complete action request (the Rust tests remote_scheduler_selects_capabilities_then_fails_over_in_order, remote_ineligible_builder_honors_local_fallback and remote_execution_identity_binds_the_complete_action_request).

cards.title: Infrastructure as typed Jet: a first-party package where the plan is a value tests can check
cards.body:
Teams describe servers, databases and networks in tools like Terraform, then apply that description to a cloud. Those tools have their own languages, keep secrets in a state file, and make plans hard to test. A first-party Jet package could describe infrastructure in typed Jet, with the plan as a value that tests assert on and apply running only under Net and Secret authority. Ballot D-INFRA1, hosted here, decides whether to build it and whether to reuse Terraform/OpenTofu providers.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T24. Sequenced after the HTTP client and server (audit card 3: #3665, #4957), hence `later`. Fleet and OS deployment are epoch e9 and out of scope.

criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json: D-INFRA1 status=ratified outcome=A ratifiedAt=2026-10-28 (card #6027); not B, so no freeze

criteria.text: An `infra` package plans a two-resource deployment against a fake provider (D-INFRA1=A); the plan is a value a `#Test` asserts on, and apply runs only with Net and Secret grants.
Infrastructure state is stored as a content-addressed lock, and a `Secret` value never appears in state or plan output.

cards.title: Write a typed Jet config out as JSON, YAML or TOML for other tools
cards.body:
Many tools read settings from JSON, YAML or TOML files. Jet lets a project write configuration as typed Jet and can already export a JSON Schema from a type (D-CORE-JSON-SCHEMA1=A). Hand-copying the values into those files repeats them, and the copies drift. Ballot D-CONFIG-EXPORT1, hosted here, decides whether a command writes a checked Jet config value out in those formats. It is not hosted on #4275, whose ratified scope forbids new ballots.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T23.

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json decision D-CONFIG-EXPORT1: status=ratified outcome=A (export command) ratifiedAt=2026-10-28

criteria.text: The export command writes a named config value from a fixture as JSON, YAML and TOML (D-CONFIG-EXPORT1=A), and each output decodes back into the same typed value. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ConfigExport/round_trip_`, one case per format.
With the schema option, the export command writes the JSON Schema for the value's type from the same codec metadata, and a value that fails its type is never exported.

cards.title: Complete the marker API as a metaprogramming rung: every target, typed reflection, one shared API with derives and fn build, library diagnostics, expand/test tooling
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: markers are a rung on the metaprogramming ladder and need a solid, comprehensive API for building and using them; fix the gaps.

Findings (MarkerScout, dev be55563b38, read-only):
(1) User marker bodies expand only on structs, top-level functions and text blocks (Compiler/JetSema Registration/UserTemplates.jet:417-458). Enums, variants, methods, fields, modules and packages are not wired, although built-in markers reach them.
(2) Reflection lacks module and package info and markers on enum variants. Marker arguments come back as untyped MarkerInfo{name, args} (Comptime/Reflection.jet:340), not as the marker's declared typed parameters.
(3) Marker bodies, derives and fn build do not share one reflection and emit API.
(4) There is no way for a library or user marker to register its own diagnostic codes with what/why/fix text (I4).
(5) There is no expand or inspect view or test helper for marker output; jet emit is unwired (#6038).
(6) Wrapping or around behaviour (decorator-like) is absent by design (D-METADEPTH1/2, D-PROCMACRO1), which is a ballot question.
(7) The Data/Syntax Markers.jet name list (25) duplicates part of the Prelude registry (81).
The ladder is: comptime expression, comptime fn, marker, derive, fn build. They share the same reflection and emit API, differing only in scope (philosophy pillar 4).

A ballot is being drafted; B2 stays parked until the vote. All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.title: Packages ladder: loose files grow into a package with `jet init`, workspaces serve every command, and the effects and gate rungs are decided
cards.body:
Destination: climbing from loose files to a package to a workspace needs no rewrite (philosophy pillar 4, Ladders, Not Cliffs). `jet init` grows loose files into a package, writing package.jet and rewriting path imports with every edit shown (D-LOOSE-GROW1=A); a workspace serves check, test and run at its root (D-WORKSPACE-CMD1=A); the workspace inheritance, effects block and audited-gate rungs follow owner rulings that are not yet ballots.

Source: Docs/audits/ladder-audit-2026-10-28.md findings L-01, L-03, L-04, L-05 and L-13 (merged cards #6042, #6043, #6044, #6051). The audit's drafted ballots D-WORKSPACE-INHERIT1, D-ABILITIES-BLOCK1 and D-ORG-POLICY1 are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). E0982 must be registered again with its emitter when `jet init` lands (2026-11-12 log).

cards.title: Mutation testing and coverage-guided fuzzing for jet test
cards.body: Split from #6035 by owner answer 2026-10-28 (Q4: own card). The best-in-class evaluation (Audit/drafts4/BEST-IN-CLASS.md) lists mutation testing (peers: cargo-mutants, Stryker, PIT) and coverage-guided fuzzing (peers: libFuzzer/cargo-fuzz, Go native fuzzing, AFL++) as axes where Jet's test system has nothing. Both should climb the same test ladder and use the one settings table, without a second mechanism. Ratified fuzz rows that the CLI refuses today (Front.jet:1023-1027) are built under #6035 S3; this card covers coverage guidance and mutation.
