criteria.text: An owner ballot fixes the surface for mutation testing and coverage-guided fuzzing on the test ladder.
criteria.evidence: D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30: both on by default; mutate: changed|all|off with stock changed; grade: generated is coverage-guided with a corpus under testdata/fuzz/<test>/.

criteria.text: Mutation testing and fuzzing each run on an example package with golden output, and their results are rows in the `jet test` report.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1=A mutation: `mutate` is a row of the one test settings table (`changed` by default, plus `all` and `off`). By default only functions whose IR changed are mutated. All mutants share one build (mutant schemata), each runs only the tests that reach it (last killer first), and the kill matrix is cached in the #6035 store.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1=A equivalent mutants: a mutant equal to the original after canonical-IR folding is dropped unrun. An effect-free survivor is proved equivalent by the solver, or reported with an input that tells it apart (fuzzing is the fallback), and an effectful survivor is reported as unchecked. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter mutate_survivor_outcomes`, one row per outcome.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1=A fuzzing: `grade: generated` steers generation by branch coverage and keeps new-branch inputs and shrunk failures under the corpus directory (testdata/fuzz/<test>/ by default), and later runs replay them as ordinary rows.

A reviewed must-kill catalog names one exact mutation and the layer expected to reject it for every critical silent-data seam class. Proof: the catalog is committed under Docs/testing, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter must_kill_catalog` runs every entry.
The mutation score and survivor list come from the catalog and immutable result bundles, and a manual exemption, hidden skip or stale target commit fails the run.

A coverage-guided fuzz run of a parameterized #Test finds a planted crash in a parser fixture within its time budget and saves the crashing input as a regression case that later plain `jet test` runs replay.

Optional independent-condition coverage evidence uses witness pairs. Branch reports keep their meaning, short-circuiting is unchanged, and bitmask coverage never claims independent bits. Source versus object scope and the build and target identity are recorded, and release gates do not change.

jet test runs with a named profile, --set values and coverage compile and execute their assertions with no ICE in the generated status and history JSON parser, which uses the canonical Foundation JSON contract.

cards.title: Memory checks accept every safe program: no over-strict rejections
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: if a program is memory safe, Jet must accept it. Checks must be neither over-strict nor under-strict; only `#Unsafe` blocks opt out.

Known over-strict case: E0221 rejects a type that could form a strong loop at its declaration. It rejects a plain linked list (`next: Shared<Node>?`) and a tree with weak parent links and strong `kids` (probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/ballots2/probe/family2.jet). A strong loop can only close when a strong field of an existing shared value is written with a value that reaches it. Building by construction (prepend, a new child) never loops.

Scope: every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic.

log.text: Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: respelled for D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A and D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A; the soundness rule is unchanged.

Merged #6200 "Over-safety audit: every hard error protects soundness, every restriction names its expert way out, and no sealed floors" into this card (memory and safety checks accept every safe program); its 3 open item(s) are carried as "(was #6200)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Landed 6e013d30c9 (SmallGoals5-g7): immediately called lambda no longer reports E0217; UI row local_cell_guard_immediately_called_lambda_reads PASS. Partial; remaining items unchanged (E0204 nested call, E0212 payload window, E0219/E0220 blocked by #5677, linear-guard Fn lambda E0121).

2026-10-29 Main: landed 3a2f6b469d (SmallGoals5-g5): a non-escaping lambda may read a Cell guard (E0217 only for escaping lambdas). UI test _5 is rewritten to an escaping lambda, and a new test proves the non-escaping capture checks clean. C3 and C4 stay partial; the remaining items are in land/SmallGoals5-g5-cards.tsv.

criteria.text: A census of every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic lists, for each, safe programs it rejects today (probe files with expected output) and unsafe programs it must keep rejecting. Proof: the census is committed under Docs/Audits, and each probe is a case: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter MemoryCensus/`.

E0221 fires only where a strong loop can actually close (a write of a strong field of an existing shared value whose new value can reach it), never at a type declaration; a strong linked list built by prepend and a weak-parent tree with strong kids compile and run on O0 and O1.
criteria.evidence: Landed cb59b8f072 (E0221 at the write site). On dev cb59b8f072 base jet: tests/ui/shared_weak_parent_tree.jet prints 'Ada has 2 kids' rc 0 under jet run, --optimize=none, --optimize=basic and the built binary; golden Examples/features/memory/shared_graph_building.jet (prepend list + weak-parent tree) PASS o0/o1/o2.

criteria.text: Every other over-strict rejection in the census is fixed in sema, or carded with a ballot if the fix needs new syntax; every unsafe probe still fails with its diagnostic. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter MemoryCensus/` passes, with every safe probe accepted and every unsafe probe refused with its code.

Each active error row in Compiler/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet carries a safety class (soundness: refusing it prevents a memory, type, aliasing or resource fault; or opinion: the program would run safely) and a one-line reason. A Jet tool generates a dated audit under Docs/Research from those fields, and its `--check` fails when an error row lacks a class. It may land in slices by code range. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter diagnostic_safety_class` passes with every active error row classified.

Every sealed floor (a soundness refusal that neither #Unsafe nor another ratified expert opt-in can lift) is listed with its code, its sema location (file:line) and the expert path to the same program, or "none" with the reason, in the audit c5 generates. Proof: the generated audit's sealed-floor section, reproduced by the c5 tool's `--check`.

Soundness U1 (Prep 2026-11-04, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3836/s64.jet): an escaping lambda that captures a list window of a local that dies owns a materialized copy, so the probe prints 2000|true| on O0, O1 and O2 instead of reading freed memory. The fix is in IR: ir_lambda honors sema's materialized and cloned captures. Sema keeps accepting the program. A case pins it on every tier.
criteria.evidence: dev 7567ee4508 (G10Safe-lambda-owned-window, g10-fold2 cmds 39-44, all rc 0, on that fold jet): ir_lambda honors sema materialized and cloned captures. Case view_copy_semantics/an_escaping_lambda_owns_the_window_it_captures pins the probe on every tier, and the whole view_copy_semantics/, closures/ and core_and_closures/ filters plus CodegenCeiling --check pass.

criteria.text: Wrong result L1 (Prep 2026-11-04, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3836/s36x.jet): writes inside a loop in a non-escaping lambda reach the captured variable, so the probe prints 3|6|3 on O0, O1 and O2 instead of 3|3|0. A case pins it on every tier.
criteria.evidence: dev c7d8c0291b (G10Safe-lambda-loop-write, g10-fold2 cmds 50-53, on that fold jet): case closures/a_lambda_write_inside_a_loop_or_branch_reaches_the_captured_variable gives PASS 1 (O0, O1 and O2). The whole closures/ filter gives PASS 40, FAIL 0, KNOWN-FAILING 2 (the existing #5454 rows). The ui effects/iterable_loop_charges_its_cursor_effects gives PASS 1, and the Ownership/Checks.jet check is rc 0.

criteria.text: (S1, I1 soundness) A refill write 'self.r = next(self.r)' (next takes &&) on a &self receiver, where next can stop (panic), never closes the moved value twice. Today both the callee frame and the caller's owner close it: probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/bal2/p/stop_refill.jet prints 'close a' twice before E3001 on -O0 and -O1 (refill-move path, Checking.jet:583-584). Rule: while a write place is empty, nothing that can stop may consume the moved value; sema rejects it or the place is refilled before any stop. The probe becomes a Tests/Cases case that closes once on O0/O1/O2, and the 8 repo sites of 'x.f = g(x.f)' (g takes &&) (CheckProgram.jet:5580/5581/6385/6529/7346, Host.jet:2553, Review.jet:282, Loops.jet:177) check clean or are migrated. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/stop_refill_closes_once` on O0, O1 and O2, and `jet check` over Compiler passes at the 8 sites.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-TASK-WINDOW1 A: a task in a `task.group` may capture a read view or a write window into storage whose owner outlives the group. The capture is a loan held until the group's join. Two live tasks holding overlapping windows, where either writes, are refused with the group-loan diagnostic E1101 (ConcurrentCaptureNotOwned), the one code the existing group-loan rule uses. So is any use of the owner inside the group. The element type must be sendable, and IR holds the window by address (BuildExpr.jet:6297-6300). Proof: prep/c6066/bal/task_a.jet prints 6 on O0, O1 and O2; today it is E0631 at 9:17 and 9:27 (Lambdas.jet:2171-2184). prep/c6066/bal2/task_overlap.jet (both tasks write window `a`) and task_owner.jet (`print(v[0])` inside the group) are refused, each with a UI snapshot. All three become tests/cases cases.
criteria.evidence: Built in e9bb4a3dbe (a group task may capture a window into an outer owner as a loan held to the join). on batch compiler p155 (dev 49836bd978), 2026-11-15 01:48: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter concurrency_boundaries/a_group_task_can_write_through_a_window_into_an_outer_owner PASS 1 (split O0/O1/O2 and ranges O0/O2 print 6, read O0/O2 prints 10 and 1; overlap refused with E1101 ConcurrentCaptureNotOwned at overlap.jet:6:21; an owner read in the group refused at owner.jet:6:16); --profile ui --filter taskgroup_window_ PASS 2 (taskgroup_window_lent_to_two_writing_tasks, taskgroup_window_owner_read_inside_group). The prep probes became these cases.

criteria.text: Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-MAPSLOT-WINDOW1 A: `&map[key]` at a `ViewMut<V>` destination is a one-value window over the entry's value, read as `w[0]`. IR builds the header from the entry's value address with length 1, as ir_list_window does. A missing key stops exactly as `map[key]` does. Adding or removing entries while the window lives is refused by the existing loan check (today that is E0220 at slot_grow.jet 8:5). Proof: prep/c6066/bal/slot_a.jet prints 1 on O0, O1 and O2; today it is E0108 at 2:5. prep/c6066/bal2/slot_grow.jet is refused at 8:5, with a UI snapshot. prep/c6066/bal2/slot_missing.jet stops with `the map has no entry for key "z"` on every tier. All three become cases.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-INDEX-COMPOUND1 A: `xs[i] op= v` and `map[key] op= v` mean the long form, with one lookup. - E0164 is retired: Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:157 becomes a retired row, and the Statements.jet:5835 refusal is removed. The Dyn-path refusal at Statements.jet:5961, which shares the code, moves to its own registered code with the same text. - Proof: prep/c6066/bal/idx_a.jet prints 2 then 2 on O0, O1 and O2. - prep/c6066/bal2/idx_missing.jet stops with E3001 `the map has no entry for key "z"`. idx_range.jet stops with E3010 `the list has 2 items, so position 5 doesn't exist`. Both match their long forms, idx_long_missing.jet and idx_long_range.jet. - tests/ui/compound_index_target becomes a run case. - The E0164 text is amended in spec.md:1449-1452, syntax-decisions.md:264-265 (S17) and architecture.md:834-835. - The comments at Statements.jet:6158 and :6221 are corrected, and so is the fixture comment at tests/cases/l0503_behavior/…/prefer_compound_assign.jet:20. L0503 itself does not change.
criteria.evidence: aaa6331fc0 release candidate kit (chain s2 98d89707fb97975a): tests/ui/compound_index_target.jet PASS. This row is the proof the precut audit named for this criterion.

criteria.text: Definite initialization accepts a fixed array `[T#N]{ uninit }` that a counted loop fully writes before any read; today it reports E0420. The census covers each fill shape (counted loop, while with index, fill call) and each lands as a case. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (dev 0ccdff27ea). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DefiniteInit/fixed_array_loop_fill_`, one case per fill shape.

Found 2026-11-09 (G6Lead, probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Lead/ballots/probes/cycle2/a5 and s14b): writing through a Shared field of a pool element, `scene[id].material.color = c`, is refused with E0302, and an inline closure in a Shared field write or push reports E0118 naming the internal `__jet_shared_value`. D-SHARED-CYCLE2=A is built. The one ownership checker accepts a Shared tree whose links are made through helper functions once its complete alias and call summaries prove the links safe, as in the ballot program (make_child, then root.kids.push(child.copy())), which prints 1 on O0, O1 and O2. cards.title: Upgrades need no hand edits: every breaking change ships a `jet fix` rewrite, and last release's code builds on the new one
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D28). `jet --version` on commit 8fbf094 prints "release readiness: not-ready" and "1.0 compatibility policy: future-1.0 (planned; not active)". Go 1 (compat promise plus `go fix`) and Perl 5 are best in class: old code keeps running. Python 2 to 3 took twelve years because most changes needed hand edits.

Design that beats them. Jet keeps greenfield freedom (AGENTS.md) but makes every break mechanical: a change that makes accepted source fail `jet check` must register a `jet fix` rewrite in the same change. CI proves it on the previous release's Examples/ and on a fixed corpus of scripts. Go fix covers a subset of changes; Jet's rule covers all of them, so users never hand-edit to upgrade. No card owns this: #5071 removes editions and retired forms but does not gate migrations. Map: #5982.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Owner 2026-11-06: not scheduled before v1 release preparation. c6 moved to #3720 (D-TEACH-RECONCILE1=A and the greenfield order remove retired-spelling paths now); c7 and c8 moved to #5950. For Main: tests/cases/onboarding_recovery/entry_recovery_covers_missing_ambiguous_legacy_and_stale_layouts expects jet run to migrate main.jet to run.jet, which the greenfield order (2026-11-06) forbids; drop its legacy arm and repoint its known-failing row to #5950.
Examples concept-area cutover (2c3e68a70b) moved paths this card's criteria cite. Read each cited path as its new home: c1: Examples/features -> Examples.

Owner 2026-11-06: until v1 release preparation no retired spelling, API or library path gets a teaching error, snapshot or jet fix rewrite; this card is where migration support is established during v1 release preparation. Not scheduled before then.
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 5 criteria from archived #266, #679, #1727: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

criteria.text: A blocking release guard checks out the previous release's Examples/ and a fixed corpus of 200 scripts (the ScriptBench programs plus Examples), runs `jet fix --all` and then `jet check` with the new toolchain, and fails on any error.
A change that makes previously accepted source fail `jet check` without registering a `jet fix` rewrite fails the guard (a planted-break test).

`jet fix` applies every rewrite added since the toolchain in the lock, or since `--since <version>`, and prints one line per rewrite kind with a count (D-LANG-MIGRATE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_fix_since_lock` and the UI snapshot `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter jet_fix_since_summary`.
Across every release since the guard turned blocking, moving the corpus forward needs 0 hand edits, logged on this card per release. Proof: the per-release log entries citing the guard's receipt.
The `1.0 compatibility policy` line of `jet --version` reads from Docs/Spec/release-policy.md, and the policy names the release in which the guard became blocking.

(was #1727 c1) jet fix produces the same plan value jet codemod does and records an undo log [precut audit: failing on 9c7ddf1359: C:cli_runtime/jet_fix_apply_writes_replay_log_and_undo_restores_source FAIL snapshot mismatch: tests/cases/cli_runtime/printfamily.fixed.out]
criteria.evidence: 34290833a9 release candidate kit (chain s2 613ff4f17287d935): tests/cases/cli_runtime/jet_fix_apply_writes_replay_log_and_undo_restores_source.case PASS. This row is the proof the precut audit named for this criterion.

criteria.text: Every breaking language change lands with one codemod plan in Compiler/Migrations, named by toolchain version, with an old-spelling fixture the suite replays (D-LANG-MIGRATE1=A).

When a check fails in a project whose lock names an older toolchain, it adds one line naming that toolchain and the count of pending rewrites, never a spelling; the old spelling keeps the generic error (D-LANG-MIGRATE1=A).

cards.title: Port the Python bridge and the PyPI/npm providers to the self-hosted toolchain: `use py.X` in a loose script, each foreign package fenced by its grant
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D06, ecosystem size). Python has 600k+ PyPI packages and JavaScript 3M+ npm packages; Jet's own registry has no public content, so Jet loses on reach by count. The ratified design already answers this. D-FFI-PY1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4166): `use py.X` talks to a supervised sidecar CPython with a typed message boundary and the `-[FFI.Py]>` effect; `py@embed` is the opt-in in-process mode. D-JPK-EXTPROV1=A (:4185): PyPI, npm and SwiftPM are first-class providers, fetched, hash-pinned and offline after the first fetch. D-DATA-BRIDGE1=A (:5964) reserves the `py.*` and `r.*` roots. Both were built in the Rust era (#180, #937 done) and never ported: probe on commit 8fbf094, `jet run -A b/pyuse.jet` with `use python.numpy as np` gives E0603 "The imported module is not present in the package source snapshot". No open card owns the port (#5984 is a map with no criteria).

Why this beats every peer rather than tying. Reach becomes a superset: PyPI plus npm plus Jet packages, where Python reaches only PyPI and Node only npm. Safety is better than at home: a PyPI package runs in a sidecar whose OS access is fenced by the script's grants, so a package that reads ~/.ssh is refused unless FS.Read for that path was granted. pip, uv and npm run package code with the user's full authority. Mojo also imports Python modules but runs them in-process with no fence.

Scope: the self-hosted `py.*` binder (sidecar default, `py@embed` opt-in), the PyPI and npm providers in the resolver behind #4833's fetch path, typed stubs from `.pyi` files where present, and the authority wiring. The R bridge (D-FFI-R1) follows the same sidecar path and is out of scope here.

criteria.text: A loose script with `use py.numpy as np` and `print(np.mean([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))` prints 2.0 under `jet run`: the first run fetches and hash-pins numpy from PyPI, and the second works with the network disabled (today E0603).

Reach census: at least 90 of the 100 most-downloaded PyPI packages import and pass a one-call smoke test through `use py.X` on Linux x86-64, with the script and table checked in and each failure listed with its reason. Proof: the checked-in census table and the committed receipt of its script's run.

A fixture PyPI package that opens ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 at import is refused with an authority error naming FS.Read and the path unless that grant was given, while the same package under `pip install` and `python3 -c 'import fixture'` reads the file (paired test).
The #5949 first-run prompt lists `FFI.Py` and the Python package names when a script first uses `py.*`, and a dependency update that adds a Python package asks again (#5459 rules).

With `py@embed`, 100k calls of a small pure Python function take less than 1.5x the same calls inside CPython, and with the sidecar default the median round trip is under 20 microseconds. Proof: a committed benchmark receipt per release.
A manifest dependency in the D-JPK-EXTPROV1 form (`leftpad: npm@"1.3.0"`) fetches, pins and is called through its typed first-party stub package, and the second run works offline.

The first run of a loose script with one dependency, on a cold cache, is faster than `uv run` of the PEP 723 equivalent and `deno run` with one `jsr:` import of similar size (median of 5, Jet/peer < 1.00). Proof: the committed hyperfine receipt. (was #5949 c23)

cards.title: Benchmark Jet's build and package system against Nix, and beat it
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: Jet's build and package system must be lightning fast, substantially faster than Nix, more powerful, and easier to use, audit and reason about. Nix is a required peer for the build, package and configuration cells.

Compare like with like: the same project or package set built hermetically by both, on the same machine, cold and warm. Nix evaluation and store operations count, and so do Jet's check, store and cache.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed card: G11 by the owner's 2026-11-09 ruling (speed and size are G11).

KitSpeed first receipt 2026-10-28 (5 samples, interleaved; Jet/Nix medians with the SemanticIndex O(n²) fix): eval 0.77, noop 20.4, incremental 4.87, cold_cache 5.21, scratch 3.88 — all lose. Causes: 73% build-plan query (whole-package Interpreter check, eager ProgramInfo, third Doc-mode recheck); no build stamp or artifact cache (JET_CACHE_DIR unread); Core rechecked per process (~150 ms). Fix plan: build stamp, plan cache + per-module interface/object caches, CAS under JET_CACHE_DIR, build-program closure scoping + one shared check + lazy ProgramInfo, persisted Core interface. Receipt: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/land/kitspeed-nix-peer-receipt.txt

criteria.text: The canonical performance manifest lists Nix as a required peer with paired cells: config evaluation (`nix eval` against `jet check` of the build program), no-op rebuild, one-file incremental rebuild, cold build from a populated cache or substituter, and a from-scratch hermetic build of the same medium project; each cell has a harness and committed receipts. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs` passes with the Nix rows.

Every Nix cell meets the gate (Jet/Nix below 1.00), and the evaluation, no-op and incremental cells reach Jet/Nix of at most 0.25; losses stay on cards with their cause. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry nix-build` shows no loss.

A side-by-side note shows the same project in Nix and in Jet: lines and concepts a reader needs, how each declares and audits inputs and effects, and reproducibility (bit-identical output on two machines or two clean stores). Proof: `git ls-files 'Docs/**/nix-vs-jet*'` names the committed note.

cards.title: `Set` is a sorted array with a memmove per insert
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R3 (cells: w13 wall/CPU). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `Set` is a sorted array (`Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildSets.jet:1-7`). Each insert shifts the tail with memmove (`ir_set_insert_body`, `:65-95`, memmove `:77-88`). Building a set of 2 M lines is O(n²) moves.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_mem_move` 80.0 %, `jet_rt_string_compare` 5.8 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 18,666 ms vs PHP 733.1 ms, Python 1,363.8 ms.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

W13 root (CardClose-1, perf on a 200k-line subset, base s1 release): jet_ir_set_insert → jet_rt_mem_move is 88.5% self, string_compare 4.0%. Set<String> is a sorted array (Compiler/JetIR BuildSets.jet:65-95, ir_set_insert_body). Each new key is binary-searched, then the tail is memmoved, so n distinct keys cost O(n^2) shifting: 200k keys take 3.5 s, 2M lines 87 s. Fix: a hashed Set index like BuildMaps' hash/capacity, or insert-then-sort for bulk adds.

ScriptBench w13 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w13-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 86.9 s wall, 79.1 s CPU, 220 MB RSS. Wall ratios: 249x python, 78.6x ruby (the closest), 241x php. jet run 56.5 s; that run may have overlapped other jobs, so it is not yet evidence of an inversion. The root is not profiled yet.

cards.title: JSON decodes through a `Dyn` tree and refuses typed input over 16 MiB
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R4 (cells: w06 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: JSON parses to a `Dyn` tree first, then decodes the tree to the typed records in a second pass (`Core/Encoding/Json.jet:93`). Typed `json.decode<T>(text)` refuses input over 16 MiB (`Json.jet:81`, `:718`), so a 44 MB file must take the two-pass path. Every node is allocated and freed.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_alloc_8` 12.5 %, `jet_rt_free_8` 10.4 %, `jet_rt_alloc` 6.2 %, `jet_rt_dyn_to_native` 4.2 %, `jet_rt_dyn_from_native` 3.7 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 9,785 ms and 1,950,092 KB peak vs Bun (TS) 395.8 ms / 289,728 KB, Python 1,502 ms / 403,264 KB.

log.text: Safety finding (Main, 2026-11-12): on seed-b13 a one-key Dyn write on a non-Object value crashes with SIGSEGV instead of a program stop (I1). G11Speed-dk1 makes it an exit-70 stop and covers it in case encoding_parity/dyn_object_key_write_reads_only_the_keys, as well as making the write native (c3); held behind probe g11-c3dyn.

HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

G1Lead b7ff715849 fixes the a0_039 gate regression from option D (c1dd8c7b26). A migration block now loads core.encoding, and E0105 never names a generated __ helper. G1Lead proof on a dev-built compiler: golden Examples/Data/Migrations/run.jet PASS on O0, O1 and O2; ui migration_change_via_ok PASS; ui marker_module_ambiguous PASS on its original snapshot; all 12 ui migration* and 6 marker_module* rows PASS; golden CryptoMigration, DecodeMigration and DBMigrationProof PASS on O0 to O2; cases filter migration 6 PASS and 3 known, decode 30 PASS and 8 known. Main re-cuts a0_039 at this commit.

G1Lead landed option D as dev c1dd8c7b26: typed json.decode<T> reads the document in place through one generated reader per type; decode(tree) is the same body over the tree source. Worker verify: check/build/selfcheck rows 0; filters encoding_parity 27, json 91, codable 13, serde 4, decode 29, corelib_parts_encoding_streams 4, all PASS. General-mechanism proof on a second program (package index, 50k+100k packages, identical output): 1648-1719 ms / 444 MiB vs 2922-3268 ms / 1.20 GiB. w06: 1633-1822 ms / 505 MB vs 3593-4058 ms / 1.46 GB. Main runs the c1/c2 peer measurements with the next seed.

Owner correction 2026-11-08 (to Main), superseding the process in the previous entry: NO ballot. The owner ratifies D directly: engineer away the downsides (hand-written impl migration, Flatten/untagged without a second semantics, error-order parity with the tree path, public Decode change size, code size and compile time), then build D. A design pass that removes each downside comes first inside the build; no owner gate before building.

Owner direction 2026-11-08 (to Main): option D. The generated Decode body reads an abstract format-neutral reader interface; Dyn is one reader and a JSON byte cursor another, so there is one copy of the decode rules (SerdeItems) and every format streams with no intermediate tree. The downsides must be engineered away before presentation: the migration of hand-written Decode impls (adapter or one cutover), Flatten and untagged enums (buffering or lookahead without a second semantics), the size of the public Decode change, the beginner surface, and error-order parity with the tree path. Process: a ballot draft with exact surface and same-program alternatives, then an adversarial design review in Docs/audits (serde Deserializer/visitor and Swift Decoder as the strongest existing designs, with measured probes), then a redesign until it holds, then owner ratification, then build. Options A/B/C are superseded.

Main 2026-11-08 06:10 c1 is owner-gated. Every #Codable decode is a Sema-generated body over `tree: Dyn` (Registration/SerdeItems.jet: field lookup, defaults, presence/E2410, DenyUnknownFields, validate, Flatten, migration, tagged/untagged enums). JetIR ir_dyn_decode only dispatches to it, so a one-pass decode needs a second, generated, per-type decoder over a byte cursor. Options (G1Lead scoping): (A) a hidden codec slot on the Prelude Decode trait, `__decode_json(cursor)`, whose default materializes the subtree and calls decode. SerdeItems emits the streaming body beside decode with shared helpers, and Flatten, untagged, migration and hand-written impls use the fallback, unchanged. This changes a public trait shape (Prelude Traits.jet, the OwnedTraitRows ratchet), so it needs a ballot and an adversarial review. Recommended. (B) a compiler-generated free function per type over a Core-private cursor. It needs a privacy exemption for generated items in Sema/Calls/Core.jet, which is frozen, so the freeze must be lifted. (C) JetIR synthesizes the readers from type rows plus TSerdeAttribute, duplicating the SerdeItems semantics in IR. That is a second mechanism (I8), the largest and riskiest; not advised. Any option must keep per-field errors in declaration order, and a syntax or duplicate-key error anywhere must replace the field errors, as the tree path does. Separately in scope now: dropping the 16 MiB typed-decode refusal (typed decode over 16 MiB then works through the tree path). That is not the root fix.

Main 2026-11-08 00:00: PortsLead-2 found c1 needs a streaming Decode path. The Prelude trait is decode(tree: Dyn) and SerdeItems derives it, so every typed decode builds the Dyn tree first. Meeting c1 needs a language-level change to the Decode trait and its derive, not a library fix. It needs a design (and a ballot if it changes the public trait) before code. Deferred out of the overnight G4 push.

W06 root (CardClose-1): json.parse_with_limits (Core/Encoding/Json.jet:93 → parse_value/object/array, 392-672) builds the whole 40 MB document as a Dyn tree: one allocation per value and key, plus a positions map per object. Person.decode then walks it again (dyn_to_native, string_clone). Typed json.decode<T> refuses input over 16 MiB, which forces this path. Fix: a typed streaming decode from bytes straight to the target type, with no Dyn tree.

Correction (CardClose-1, perf stat -r 3, sbench/w06-evsym.txt): there is no O0-vs-full inversion. --release 4.06 s, 18.0G cycles; --optimize=none 4.06 s, 17.5G; jet run 5.22 s, a third of it compile. The earlier jet-bin 5961 ms was load noise. Root: per-value allocation and the Dyn round-trip. jet_rt_alloc_8, free_8, alloc, dyn_from_native, string_drop and free make up about half of all cycles, all in the runtime pack, which --optimize does not touch.

ScriptBench w06 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w06-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 5961 ms wall, 5640 ms CPU, 1.26 GB RSS. The closest peer is python (4.09x wall, 3.93x RSS); bun is 46.6x wall and 9.0x RSS. jet run (4468 ms) beats the optimized binary, the same inversion seen on w05.

criteria.text: `json.decode<T>(text)` parses straight into typed records with no `Dyn` tree and accepts input over 16 MiB, so the 44 MB w06 file allocates no per-node Dyn value.

ScriptBench workload w06, measured with the manifest method (hyperfine -N, interleaved, same machine), beats every measured peer on warm wall, CPU and peak RSS (Jet/peer below 1.00) with the built release binary; the jet run time (compile included) is shown beside it and gated under G11 (#6953); same output on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet Tools/Perf/Scriptbench/Bench.jet --data DIR --out DIR --only w06` receipt.

Setting a key on a Dyn object costs the same whatever the object already holds: `out[key] = v` does no native-to-handle round trip over the object's existing contents. Found by G4Ports-1 (2026-11-12, performance-surface twin): 30 small keys set after a 110-row array take 390 ms per 20 objects, against 12 ms when set before it (32x). Proof: a paired two-program cell (keys set before and after a large member) whose times are equal within noise, plus a second program that builds a large JSON report with interleaved keys, on O0/O1/O2.
criteria.evidence: 00583d1d94: landed G11Speed-dk1c: one-key Dyn write writes the native Object in place; structural O0/O1/O2 case under a 60 s step timeout passes on the lander's proof lines (jet test Compiler --profile cases <case>), paired before/after receipt in the SUB msg

criteria.text: core.json tree_depth (Core/Json/Json.jet, the `value.keys()` plus `value[key]` walk) is linear in the document size, so json.patch on a large document is not quadratic. Proof: a case timing tree_depth and patch on a document and on one 4x larger, where time grows at most about 4x, on O0/O1/O2.
criteria.evidence: 233209f518: landed G11Speed-jd1c: tree_depth walks object entries once (json.patch 2,000 vs 8,000 members was 439 vs 7,095 ms on seed-b13); structural O0/O1/O2 case patching a 200,000-member object under a 60 s step timeout passes on the lander's proof lines

cards.title: CSV builds fields byte by byte, re-validates UTF-8 per field and materializes every row
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R5 (cells: w05 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: CSV pushes each byte into a `[U8]` (`Core/Encoding/Csv.jet:341-441`), then makes each field with `String.from_bytes(field.copy())`, which validates UTF-8 again per field (`:382`, `:390`). All rows are materialized before the caller sees one, so peak memory grows with the file.

Evidence: perf: `core_encoding_csv_parse_rows_with` 12.7 %, `jet_rt_free_8` 10.3 %, `unit_numeric_int_parse` 7.5 %, `jet_rt_alloc_8` 6.8 %, `unit_text_bytes_utf8_error` 5.4 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 1,976 ms and 719,540 KB peak vs LuaJIT 498.8 ms / 2,768 KB, Python 2,136 ms / 11,848 KB.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.
w05 streamed with csv.reader: 204.4G -> 33.9G instructions:u (6.0x), 26.6 s -> 5.2 s, RSS 151 MB (csv.rows: 850 MB); same totals Landed in wave 32 as dev f251c88891 (Codegen-1-55).

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL every cell; jet-bin 1057 ms / 879 MB, closest peer php 1.08/1.07. Root: csv.rows materializes [CSVRow] (Csv.jet:62/400); perf self: numeric_trim_start 18.9%, parse_rows_with 18.9%, int_parse 12.5%, sentry enter/leave 6.6%.

Codegen-1 root analysis on dev bb770de593 (w05, 1M rows, instructions:u / ms / RSS):
- csv.rows as written: 9.35G / 1323 ms / 850 MB, because every row is materialized.
- Streaming csv.reader + next(): 204G / 26.5 s / 149 MB. encoding.__read_byte runs once per byte, at about 7000 instructions per byte.
- With an unlanded Core fix (CSVReader reads buffer_bytes chunks via __read_into, charges the budget once per buffer, and has a bulk path for unquoted bytes): 33.9G / 5.2 s / 151 MB.
- Remaining cost: per-field stream.charge/reserve and the AllocationBudget guard edits.
- The fix is parked in Codegen-1's lane (w28 Core). It is not lane-checked yet.

cards.title: Waiting for a child process polls in 1–10 ms slices (~10 ms per spawn)
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R6 (cells: w07 wall). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: Waiting for a child polls. The collector waits in 1 ms slices (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/ProcessExecutionCollect.jet:190`); the waiter yields in 10 ms scheduler waits (`:225-229`, comment: "polling remains the seed's 10ms scheduler wait"). About 10 ms per child; w07 runs 100 children.

Evidence: Timed: jet-bin warm 1,057.9 ms (≈ 10.6 ms per child) vs Bun 129.3 ms, Python 141.2 ms. CPU is much closer (jet-bin 216 ms vs Bun 132 ms), so most of the wall time is waiting.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.
Owner cut the agent count to 2. MechD-3 stopped. Unlanded: its c2 (w07) work and inline-run drafts in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MechD (patch-g5 landed as c639365c56). c2 is not started.

c1 follow-up (MechD-3): on the CardClose-54 base c66f96253f, strace -f -c over 1000 run() calls shows 1000 poll calls, one per run, each returning on pipe HUP or pidfd readiness, and 0 nanosleep or clock_nanosleep. The 1-10 ms sleep slices are gone.

c2 remeasured on 2ba0d540c4 (base jet, ScriptBench copy $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb/scriptbench with imports migrated to 'use X :: core.X'; bun is 1.3.13 because 1.4.4 is no longer substitutable; receipt $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/w07w11.json). w07 FAILS, so c2 stays open. jet-bin 110.8 ms wall, 5920 KiB; jet-run 116.3 ms, 9684 KiB. Losses: php wall 1.09 / cpu 1.14 (php 101.6 ms); perl cpu 1.01 and rss 1.00; rss vs lua 1.35, luajit 1.34, bash 1.16. jet-run also loses to python cpu 1.01, bun wall 1.02, perl wall 1.01, php wall 1.14, and rss vs perl, lua, luajit and bash. Roots: per-spawn cost (about 1.1 ms vs php's 1.0 ms) and a 5.9 MiB resident floor against 4.4-5.1 MiB for lua and bash.

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 (BENCH.md, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL. jet-bin 192.9 ms loses wall/cpu to php 1.30/1.33, perl 1.12/1.10, python 1.11/1.11. Root: run_spec starts a collector thread (192 MiB stack, clone/join), 3 pipe2 pairs capturing unread stdio, /dev/null, 23 extra parent syscalls per child; peers inherit stdio.

ScriptBench w07 on dev 1620f05362 + tools (wave-27 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 12:35): still FAIL c2. jet-bin 191.1 ms wall / 187.4 ms cpu / 4140 KiB for 100 children; loses to php 146.3 ms (1.31x) and perl 175.4 ms (1.09x); jet-run also loses on rss to perl and lua. The 1-10 ms poll is gone (c1); the remaining ~0.45 ms per child is spawn-path CPU (the child already uses clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK)). Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w07w10.log

Landed on dev at undefined in CardClose-54 (patch row: criterion/count 1): Root removed (tsc s1, runtime pack 827b3c1660d49fda = dev 69a987b5a6 + d4f3932172): the waiter's park slot is woken by the collector when it sets done, and the idle collector sleeps on the child's pidfd instead of 1-10 ms slices. Probe: 1,000 sequential run_spec(cmd(["true"])) take 11165 -> 3815 ms under strace, and timed park waits ending on the timeout fall from 1291 to 261 (re-parks; 0 lost wakes). ScriptBench w07 jet-bin 1037.6 -> 133.9 ms wall (7.7x), jet-run 1052.7 -> 128.6 ms; O0/O1/O2 print children ok=100.

Correction (CardClose-1): process_execution_env_remove (ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:26) is about a third of the jet process's own samples, or 17.4% of all samples, not 38%. No other jet function is above 4%.

W07 root after CardClose-54, on 69a987b5a6 + CardClose-54 (CardClose-1; confirm on the wave-24 HEAD). Each spawn builds the child environment twice: once to prepare (Compiler/JetRuntime ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:240) and once for the receipt identity, only to read PATH (ProcessExecutionReceipt.jet:250). Each build copies the inherited environment through process_execution_env_set (ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:45), which removes by key linearly for each var. With 169 vars that is about 14k string_eq per build, plus 4 allocations per var: 38% of user samples. The inherited keys are already unique, so the fix is to move-push them and read PATH directly. Pinned to one CPU, jet equals python (0.23 s); php and bun remain ahead. Handoff: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/HANDOFF-scriptbench.md.

cards.title: `para_map` runs one worker per 64 items and ignores `limit:`
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R8 (cells: w11 wall). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `para_map` splits work into fixed 64-item ranges (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Parallel.jet:24-26`, `:90`) and starts at most one worker per range (`:94`). w11 has 100 URLs, so only 2 workers run, each doing up to 64 blocking GETs in a row, whatever `limit:` says.

Evidence: Timed: jet-bin warm 1,356.9 ms vs Bun 222.5 ms, Python 312.5 ms; 64 × 20 ms server delay = 1.28 s.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c6 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c8 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c9 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c10 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q19): A. Public Core gets core.tasks.cpu_ns() -> Int (CPU time used by the current task) and core.tasks.current_task() returns a real task id; the compiler trace uses that public surface rather than a private route.

SchedLead commit 1/7 landed as afe2acc8c8: tasks run on fibers that park instead of blocking their worker thread; closed InlineAsm rails X64_FIBER_SWITCH and X64_GS_BASE_WRITE, gated by IRProgram.asm_rails. Its receipt: precommit rc=0, VERIFY OK, LaneCheck CHECK OK; focused task/cancel/generator/para/deadline/sleep cases and the concurrency goldens equal to baseline. #6403 r08: the quick task finishes in 98.7 us (base 2.9 s). 100000 cancel/timer/wake race rounds all accounted on every tier (base hangs). No leak over 3 x 10000 cancelled parked tasks. About 5.7 KB per parked task. w11 still loses to bun on wall (105.95 vs 94.66 ms); the root is the para_map limit cap at the core count, which is commit 2. Open: the ~32k live-fiber cap (vm.max_map_count) must degrade or diagnose, never crash; a 100k-task case is requested. #6403 c4 names a function that was removed; it gets reworded to the offload stats at c6.

Owner decision 2026-11-08 (to Main): build the async-I/O scheduler redesign now, no ballot. Tasks are multiplexed on few threads, with the epoll wait run on the waiting thread (the D-PARA-LIMIT1 path) instead of an OS thread per in-flight wait plus a poller-thread hop. Scope covers the same root in #6403 (a blocked task holds its worker) and #6440 (generator yield is a park/wake, about 20 us). Engineer away the downsides (task/channel/cancellation semantics unchanged on every tier, blocking foreign calls and OS waits offloaded, fairness and deadlines, I9 parity, debuggability), then build. Target: w11 beats every peer on wall, CPU and RSS (bun 9.25 ms CPU; jet 19.5 ms after fixes 1-4).

Main 2026-11-08 04:55 w11 fix 3 landed bee6af85ed (inet_pton for literal hosts, no getaddrinfo): perf task-clock -r30 25.4 -> 21.2 ms CPU, hyperfine user+sys 20.7 -> 17.7 ms, wall unchanged at 87 ms (G1Lead). Fix 2 (persistent epoll registration, 21.2 -> 20.9 ms) is queued in lane-commit; fix 1 (wake after unlock, 20.9 -> 20.3 ms) passed VERIFY and is next. bun stays at 9.25 ms CPU; c2 still fails pending the scheduler redesign.

Main 2026-11-08 04:40 w11 c2 profile (G1Lead, dev at 15e01b1474, perf stat -r30, nice 19, busy box): bun 9.25 ms CPU and 89.2 ms wall against jet-bin 25.8 ms CPU and 87.2 ms wall, so Jet wins wall unpinned and loses CPU 2.8x. Pinned to 12 cores Jet wall is 187 ms (para_map worker cap). Breakdown: 25 para workers spawn and join in 1.6 ms. 100 sequential GETs take 11.1 ms, about 110 us per request against about 40 us for bun, from 22 syscalls per request: 6 futex poller hops, 4 epoll_ctl ADD/DEL on every wait, 4 setsockopt, and a musl getaddrinfo mmap/munmap even for 127.0.0.1. Parallel overhead adds about 9 ms: 1401 of 2090 futex calls hit the HostNetPoller root mutex, which is held while waking ParkSlots and around epoll_ctl. The server delay adds about 4 ms. Approved bounded runtime fixes, to land after the next seed, in this order: Jet-side IP literal parse, register once with MOD re-arm, wake after unlock (prototype 25.8 -> 24.5 ms), then shard the root lock if still hot; estimated 19-21 ms total. The verdict: bounded fixes cannot reach bun 9 ms. The floor of the current model is one OS thread per in-flight request plus a poller hop (2 context switches) per wait. Closing c2 needs the D-PARA-LIMIT1 async-I/O path (waits multiplexed on few threads, epoll on the waiting thread): a scheduler redesign needing owner scope.

Main 2026-11-08 04:15: 7bf10da106 by PortsLead-2 does not meet c2. It resolves IP literals through getaddrinfo AI_NUMERICHOST on the caller thread, adds a word-sized Int division fast path for boxed operands, and reads the clock through vDSO clock_gettime with the replay env parsed once. w11 jet-bin instructions:u 104.4M -> 32.8M, task-clock 45.1 -> 24.7 ms; jet run 164.6M -> 92.4M; clones 126 -> 26, clock_gettime 2909 -> 0. On a loaded machine (15 runs, wall/CPU ms): jet-bin 85.5/19.2, jet-run 99.0/33.2, bun 87.1/8.1, deno 112.8/38.6. Still loses to bun on CPU; the rest is futex/thread-park, about 14 ms of system time, which is a scheduler redesign. A quiet-window measure is queued in proofq as Main-PortsLead-w11-measure.sh.

Spreading receipt for 9177db37e4, same compiler (seed-built from d405d4cb6c). Probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/para/para16.jet: 16 items of a 20M-step LCG kernel; under the old 64-item chunks all 16 ran on one worker. Built with jet build --release: ser wall 0.430 s (cpu 0.44 s); para_map wall 0.042 s (cpu 0.50 s), 10.2x. jet run (O0): ser 1.139 s, par 0.068 s. Every mode prints total 6472. c2 (ScriptBench w11) waits on the ScriptBench rebuild.

dev 9177db37e4 (Main): an unlimited para_map, para_filter or para_partition now passes PARA_EVERY_WORKER (1073741824) instead of -1 (BuildParallel.jet). The runtime caps it at the available parallelism, so chunks are the items spread over the pool, at most 64, and a short list of costly items reaches every worker. para_fold keeps -1 and its 64-item chunks (merge-tree contract). Compile-time code keeps cap 1, so the same value. The Parallel.jet comment and core-library.md core.tasks were updated; 4df47ce6da has the c5 paragraph. Proof is queued for the dev s1 batch: the 16-item probe at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/para/para.jet should show the parallel run well under the serial one, with every result 508760, plus goldens Concurrency/Parallel and ParallelIter.

Finding for c2 (Main 2026-11-07): an unlimited para_map over fewer than 64 items is one chunk, so it runs on the caller thread (Parallel.jet:22-26 keeps 64 items per chunk when limit < 0). 16 items of a 20M-step kernel: built binary par (map+fold) real 0.893 s, user 0.992 s = serial x2. para_fold's 64-item grouping is its contract (BuildParallel.jet:570-573), but para_map, para_filter and para_partition could spread a short list over the pool the way the limited path does (parallel_chunk_size). w11 passes limit: 32, so it already takes the spreading path.

Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 3 criteria from archived #3672: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

c2 remeasured on 2ba0d540c4 (same setup and receipt as #6084: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/w07w11.json; bun 1.3.13). w11 FAILS, so c2 stays open. jet-bin 106.8 ms wall, 21.8 ms cpu; bun 93.4 ms wall, 21.2 ms cpu: jet-bin/bun wall 1.14, cpu 1.03. jet-run/bun wall 1.23, cpu 1.45; jet-run/deno wall 1.03. All other peers are wins. With a 20 ms server delay and 32-way concurrency the ideal is about 4 rounds x 20 ms = 80 ms, so Jet spends about 27 ms of wall outside the server wait against bun's 13 ms: the per-request concurrency path, not CPU, is the gap.

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL vs bun only (wall 1.46, cpu 2.18). Root: parallel_limit (Parallel.jet:11-16) caps limit:32 at the CPU count, giving 20 chunks of 5 blocking GETs; each http.get starts its own thread (121 clones for 100 requests).

ScriptBench w11 on dev bb770de593 (wave-28 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 13:39): still FAIL c2, only against bun. jet-bin 143.6 ms wall / 38.7 ms cpu / 1,860 KiB; jet-run 150.9 ms / 56.0 ms / 15,424 KiB. Loses to bun on wall (1.31x) and cpu (1.75x); beats it on rss; wins against every other peer. The floor for 100 fetches at 32 at a time with a 20 ms answer is 4 rounds (~80 ms), so ~60 ms is scheduling/spawn overhead. Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w05w11.log

ScriptBench w11 on the wave-24 tree (a34ef0affd content, s2), BENCH.md method, measured by Main 08:15 EST while two suites shared the machine: FAIL. jet-bin 231.8 ms wall, 43.5 ms CPU, 2368 KiB RSS; jet run 438.8 ms, 67.9 ms, 13976 KiB. Losses: jet-bin/bun CPU 1.95 (wall 0.95); jet-run/bun wall 1.80, CPU 3.04; jet-run/deno wall 1.11. Every other cell wins, including wall against python, node, deno and ruby. Remaining roots: jet-bin CPU per fetch (0.43 ms vs bun 0.22 ms), and jet run's per-run compile cost (#6087 tier-up and kept-program reuse). Results: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/run/res/w11-r1.json.

Landed on dev at undefined in CardClose-56 (patch row: criterion/count 1): Root removed (tsd: dev 69a987b5a6 + ed139e0622, runtime pack a488a3aa6fb0cd48). jet_rt_native_para_walk sizes chunks at min(ceil(len/limit), 64) for a limited para_map, so limit bounds workers instead of 64-item chunks capping them. Probe: ScriptBench w11 (100 URLs, para_map limit 32) release binary: base 1322 ms, 100 connects from 2 threads; new 92 ms, 100 connects from 25 threads; ok=100 both.

ScriptBench w11 on dev 69a987b5a6 (CardClose-1, sbench/w11-w05.json, w11.strace): LOSS on wall. jet-bin 1395 ms vs bun 15.03x, ruby 7.89x, node 6.33x, python 5.86x, deno 1.18x; CPU and RSS win except bun CPU 2.55x. Root: para_map(limit: 32) keeps only 2 requests in flight, all connects come from 2 threads, so 100 requests take about 50 x 21 ms. The fix is in para_map/pool concurrency for blocking Net calls.

cards.title: `fs.walk` collects and sorts every entry before yielding
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R10 (cells: w02 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `fs.walk` collects every entry, then sorts the whole list by path (`Core/Files/Files.jet:1501-1530`, sort at `:1529`). The program then stats each file again for its size.

Evidence: perf spread over `core_files_walk_impl`, `jet_rt_string_compare`, alloc/free. Timed warm: jet-bin 113.6 ms vs Lua 59.6 ms, Bash 65.6 ms, LuaJIT 65.6 ms.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

412154ebff (G1Lead): fixes the I2 ICE at its root, in JetIR ir_call_row. An argument widened to a union is boxed as the callee parameter's own union, registered by the callee signature, rather than a union respelled in the caller's scope. New case core_path_foundations/core_path_calls_core_files_on_every_tier passes on O0/O1/O2 (9 core.files.path functions plus missing paths); seed a0_038 fails it with 8 ir.build faults. A census of Core union parameters (String|Path 46 sites, [String]|HTTPCorsOrigins 1, Int|ServiceWorkflow 7, LocalDate|DateTime 1) is covered by the same fix. Open structural finding, I8: Core declares Path twice (the Core/Compiler/Lang.jet builtin and core.files.path), so user code `files.exists(path.of("x"))` fails with E0112. Making it one Path is a Core API design call that waits for a ballot. Also seen: CoreSurfaceLedger --check fails under the seed on core.files.__walk_release (seed against tree; it clears with the next seed).

Lander gap closed (Main, 2026-11-08): the precommit census (the lander's census-snap.sh) checked Compiler/JetCli but never Core, unlike Land.jet census selfcheck-core, so a Core spelling no compiler accepts landed in 863e3d6b4e. The census now runs `jet check --threads 12 Core` with keep-going using the compiler it just built, and precommit requires `selfcheck-core rc=0 rows=0`. Probe: dev Core gives rc=0 rows=0; a copy with the old Path.jet:410 spelling gives rc=1 with the same 2 rows (E0047, INCOMPLETE) the a0_039 preflight reported; about 3 s per run.

cd58a15b81 (G1Lead): Core/Files/Path.jet walk unwraps each entry with `entry ?? return Err(err)`. The old `entry?.path` spelling checks under no compiler (E0047 on a0_038 and on dev sema), and it landed because precommit does not gate selfcheck-core; that lander gap is Main's. A Core census under a0_038 and B2 is clean after the fix (0 rows), and the walk cases pass 11/11. Found while fixing it: no case calls core.files.path walk, and every core.files.path function passing path.raw to a `String | Path` parameter ICEs in ir.build ("union String | core.files.path::Path without a definition") on a0_038 and on dev, an I2 violation. Routed to G1Lead ahead of #6082 D: fix the root in lowering, add an O0/O1/O2 case, and census the other Core parameter unions.

Phase 2 landed as 863e3d6b4e (62 files, lane-commit precommit passed). G1Lead reports peak RSS, old vs new, of 13.4/40.2/160.6 MB vs 15.0/15.0/14.4 MB on 20k/80k/323k entries, identical path order, and the Iterable-loop authority fix (E1803/E0740). Main could not re-check this with the a0_038 seed: a probe built inside the dev checkout came out byte-identical to one built outside any checkout and still reported no FS requirement, so the seed does not pick up the checkout Core. c1 is to be measured with a compiler built from 863e3d6b4e or later, in the next batch verification. Scripts: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/walk6086/ab2.sh.

Owner decision 2026-11-08 (to Main): option A, no ballot. walk/walk_files become lazy, with per-entry results: each entry or its own IOError is yielded as the walk goes, break/drop closes the handles, and memory is bounded by depth. One greenfield cutover migrates every caller (G1Lead census: 52 files: Examples using .len()/index, Path.walk() -> [Path], the L0522 lint, docs); collecting is explicit. Engineer the downsides away in the build (error visibility for callers that only want a list, ordering identical to today, the beginner path), then build.

Main 2026-11-08 05:45 c1 is owner-gated (public API). Since e3e314c953 the walk is depth-first and sorts one directory at a time, so the collect-then-sort-everything cause is gone; what remains is the collected result in the public signature: walk/walk_files return [WalkEntry] !IOError (core-library.md). Today a failed directory drops its subtree, the walk continues, and the earliest failure is the Err of the whole walk. A stream cannot keep that contract, because it has yielded entries before the Err exists. Options (G1Lead census, 52 files touched by A: Examples using .len()/index, Path.walk() -> [Path], the L0522 lint, docs): (A) walk/walk_files become a lazy per-entry-fallible stream, and every caller migrates in one cutover; (B) keep the list API and add a streaming twin (new surface, against I8 one mechanism); (C) keep the list: linear time per e3e314c953, peak memory proportional to the tree, and c1 is reworded to time-linear. Needs an owner ballot (with an adversarial review before A/B is built). G1Lead builds whatever is ratified.

MechD-3 stopped (2-agent cap); nothing of this landed. Its proposed design: add fs.walk_iter(root, ignore:) and walk_files_iter, which return an Iterable of Result<WalkEntry, IOError>, walk depth-first keeping only the open directories on the current path, and sort siblings per directory, so the order is by path component (the order __walk_before uses for errors, and walkdir's sort_by_file_name). walk and walk_files keep their signatures and collect over it, which removes the BFS queue and the global string sort. Visible change: 'a/b' now sorts before 'a.txt' and 'a-c'. walk_iter is new public API and the order change is product behavior, so this needs an owner ballot before it is built.

cards.title: Plain `jet run` keeps an unoptimized program, slower than `--release`
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R15 (cells: `jet-run` warm cells that do real work (w03, w05, w06, w14)). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: Plain `jet run` builds with the stock options; only `--release` adds `optimize: full` (`Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:755-757`, `:777`, `:799-801`). So the kept script program is unoptimized, and a warm `jet run` is slower than the `--release` binary of the same file.

Evidence: Timed warm, jet-run / jet-bin: w03 18,572 / 14,790 ms (1.26), w05 2,747 / 1,976 ms (1.39), w06 12,223 / 9,785 ms (1.25), w14 135.7 / 74.1 ms (1.83). (w09 13.8× and w10 2.3× are mostly R12 start-up; w04 0.83 and w13 0.99 are within their ± 34 % / ± 11 % spread.)

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
G8Fix stopped #6087 c2 work at 16:20 (no owner order for G11). Its w03 Regex edits (256M to 219M instructions) are saved unlanded as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G8Fix/unlanded-6087-regex.patch.

Owner instruction 2026-11-10 ~16:10, verbatim: "remember for script performance we are targeting being approximately at hand optimized machine code level (as well as for regular programs). that work should go in the size/speed goal, not script. script goal should not have any speed size work" Applied: #6087 and #6403 now belong to G11 (Speed and size) only, and #5072 c41 (peak RSS) moved to #6639. #6639 gains the machine-ceiling target for scripts. #5072's port bars still measure wall time and peak memory as switch bars (AGENTS.md), but the work that makes Jet faster or smaller is G11's.

t14a landed PerfLead-w14rot and PerfLead-w03stream (53805444ba..01b86931e7). w14 went from 420.0M to 360.0M instructions:u (luajit 360.7M), and w03's peak RSS from 196.7 MB to 1.1 MB. c2 stays open: w03's wall and CPU time still trail bash and php.

t12c landed (4a5c0ec793..aaca1c8db2 (dev 00a2b37a42)): PerfLead-w14, w14v, nonneg (w14 810M -> 420M instructions; LuaJIT 360.7M, still a loss), rxpf, packnames and lazylines (w03 6.517G -> 2.721G instructions, 196 MB -> 1 MB RSS). c2 stays open: w14 still loses to LuaJIT.
G6Lead-completions landed in ecf04d985a..76955986d0: the bash and powershell completion snapshots carry -O0/-O1/-O2. c11 still needs the ScriptBench cells.
G6Lead-runkeepcore2 landed in ecf04d985a. RunKeep's Core-change step passes again (c10 was already met; this keeps it met). c11 still needs the ScriptBench cells (proofq Main-G6Lead-c11-scriptbench).

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Added G11: the card is a run-speed defect (c2, ScriptBench w03 and w14). It keeps G4 for c11 (the D-BUILD-TIER1 run tier) and the c5/c6 output rows. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (later the same day, replacing 'always full'): jet run is O0; jet build defaults to full, with an O1 flag for a faster compile. D-RUN-TIER2 (always full) is withdrawn; RunTier2Review found it NOT CLEAN. The replacing ballot is D-BUILD-TIER1.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (BoardPlanner C-G4-2): jet run always builds the program at full optimization (the Go model), superseding D-RUN-TIER1=B and the O0 rule for jet run in AGENTS.md I9; compile-time code is unchanged. ScriptLead writes the replacing ballot D-RUN-TIER2 (exact behavior: first-run cost, what is kept, jet dev), which gets an adversarial review and is posted before it is built.

Main 2026-11-08 04:05 regression (blocks the a0_037 release): a kept program reused by plain jet run runs as a child of a waiting jet run that does not forward SIGINT, so `kill -INT <jet run pid>` leaves the program running. A fresh compile runs the program in-process, and SIGINT ends it. Lost cases: corelib/core_os_interrupt_delivery_matches_aot_jit_and_interpreter and core_os_interrupt_callback_forms_match_dev_tiers. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/intr/probe2.py. G1Lead is fixing it by making the kept launch take the same in-process path, one mechanism.

Main: c6's tier-trace test and interp/deopt rows have no meaning without an interpreter; c6 now proves native byte-exact runs on every level. c8's 'evaluator' is compile-time code, which runs natively at O0 (I9). CardCleanup Q(c).
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 7 criteria from archived #2862, #2864: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

ScriptBench w15 on dev 69a987b5a6 (CardClose-1): the jet run path costs 16.8 ms CPU and 9.5 MB RSS to launch the kept program, against 1.8 ms and 0.25 MB for the built binary. jet-run cells therefore lose to luajit (CPU 7.01, RSS 3.75), perl (CPU 4.23), php (CPU 2.69) and bash (RSS 1.30), while jet-bin beats every peer. These cells are report-only under D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B. The root is the run-path launch overhead this card and D-RUN-TIER1 cover.

Ballot D-RUN-TIER1 drafted (A: jet run at basic; B: first run at none, a reused script is rebuilt once at full; C: keep, use --release), rec B, at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballot-run-tier1.json. Not posted yet: it needs the cross-family adversarial review pass first.

Ballot input (UiGreen-1, INFERENCE, not measured): (b) costs one kept --release image per script (it replaces the none image, so the net cost is the size difference) and one full-optimize rebuild per script source, about a jet build --release, on the first reuse (2nd run) or in the background after the 1st; the cold run is unchanged. Card warm ms, jet run (none) / jet-bin (release): w03 18572/14790 (1.26x), w05 2747/1976 (1.39x), w06 12223/9785 (1.25x), w14 135.7/74.1 (1.83x).

UiGreen-1 2026-10-31 23:50: owner gate. Plain jet run optimizing none is ratified (Docs/spec spec.md:3815-3816, D-BUILD-DEFAULT1=B, syntax-decisions.md:5713). Fix options for a ballot: (a) jet run stock = basic (cold compile cost; run cases re-key); (b) cold jet run stays none, and the kept script program (ScriptCache) is rebuilt at full once warm (tier-up on reuse, same meaning per I9); (c) keep as is. UiGreen-1 leans (b). Parked until the owner rules; Main is preparing the ballot.

cards.title: No-heap machines: the heap-free proof follows calls into Core with no exemption by name (D-CORE-TARGET1=A)
cards.body:
Finding B10 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md): Core's generic bodies are checked without the selected target's no_os fact, while user bodies are checked with it (sema_scope_environment_no_os in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Scopes.jet tests module_is_core).

D-CORE-TARGET1=A (ratified 2026-11-14) answers the ballot: a chip with no heap means the program promises not to use the heap, the same promise -[!Mem.Alloc]> makes; the compiler runs that proof from the program's start through Core and packages alike, reports a problem inside Core on the program's call, and shows each step of the path.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core uses only mechanisms any package can use.

cards.title: Ballot: does Core ship as a versioned package?
cards.body:
Finding B15 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core comes from the toolchain beside the package graph (JetDriverCompileRequest.core_sources, Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet:180-218), is keyed by `<corelib>/` (Sema/Diagnostics.jet:20-22, Loader.jet:2659), and has a private core.<area>.runtime namespace (E1001, Loader.jet:3616-3625) that packages cannot mirror.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Implement the ballot's answer. Under A, Core resolves through the package graph with a version, and the `<corelib>/` predicates are deleted once F01-F12 land.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c1 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Owner gate: no ballot for Core as a versioned package is on Tower (same state as #6144 in G3). Main drafts it.

criteria.text: Whether Core ships as a versioned package (census finding B15) is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15); under yes, `jet` resolves Core as a package whose version `jet inspect` shows. Proof: `tower decision show <id>` ratified, then `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CorePackage/version_in_inspect`.
The core.<area>.runtime privacy uses the `priv` rule any package can use (D-CORE-HELPERS1=A, D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A), and a user import of it is refused.

cards.title: Core members are declared in Core source; the compiler's twin tables and route tables are deleted
cards.body:
Finding F01 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). The compiler keeps a twin of Core's API. Core members are typed and dispatched by compiler tables (Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet:1-4, CoreCallExtensions.jet; generated Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:10 with 1,998 rows; hand-written Registry/CoreSignatures.jet:88, CorePlatformSignatures.jet:229, CoreHostSignatures.jet:22, CoreValueSignatures.jet). A native row wins over the Core declaration (Sema/Calls/Core.jet:264-270). A package can reach the host only through C FFI.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Add one public declaration for a host-provided function, usable by any package, whose signature, effects, failure and sink facts are read from the declaration. Move every Core member that has a CORE_CALLS row to that declaration in Core source. Delete Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet's member rows, CoreCallExtensions.jet, the generated CoreCallRows table and the hand-written signature tables in one cutover. The spelling of the declaration is ballot A on this card.

log.text: Closed by Main: every criterion is met; each moved to the card that owns its work (#6851 and others), and its blocker #6615 is done.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c14, c15 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

2026-11-14 TowerKeeper-1: split into three streams. This card keeps Core declarations, the twin signature tables, the route tables, CoreReach, core.build and the D-CORE-LOWER1/D-EMBED-TOOLCHAIN1 table work. Core-only privileges (c5, c6, c8, c9, c20, c21, c23, c35, c36) moved to #6851; declaration facts and layout (c18, c29, c30, c32, c33) moved to #6852. c46 restated: D-FLOAT-INT1=A covers scalar conversions, the SIMD bridges stay under D-SIMD1/D-SIMD2.

c18 and c20 depend on #6156/#6157 (G5DevX-1, 2026-11-12). The <corelib>/ key-prefix tests in BuildTypes.jet (about 14 sites, for example lines 33, 399, 547, 561, 598, 3384) and in Sema (about 33) decide runtime-handle layout and Core-only privileges. They can go only once a package-neutral mechanism for both exists, so moving the test into a helper would only dodge the criterion's grep and is refused.

c46 conflicts with ratified D-SIMD1/D-SIMD2 (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4116-4125): [F32#4] bridges through from_array/to_array (E2510/E2511), and Core has 30+ to_array methods in Core/Math (Math.jet:14971..17725). c46 cannot remove them without a newer owner ruling, because by the authority order the ratified decision wins. c46 stays open and unworked until its scope is restated to the to_* conversions outside the ratified SIMD bridge. Source card #6255 no longer exists on the board. c14 (CoreReach names no Core path or helper) needs the demand table derived from Core declarations; it goes to G4Ports-1, which owns CoreReach (c2c, e1384f98cc).

Unlanded work saved from the TLS lane worktree TlsLead-3-6151 (on 73739ba7c3) before it was removed, 2026-11-12 00:15: a Taint rework toward c32 and c33, never submitted. 35 files, +266/-362: Sema/Taint.jet (174 lines), ProveReplay.jet (99), CoreSourceRows.jet (27); it deletes JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Sinks.jet, and touches CoreCalls.jet, CoreRecords.jet, the E0722 docs and about 25 tests/ui/taint goldens. The diff is at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/tls-unlanded/TlsLead-3-6151.patch. It has not been reviewed, built or tested; whoever takes c32 starts from it.

c32 credential sinks: no new marker (that would need a ballot). Sinks are derived from declarations. A credential sink is any call whose declared effect row writes outward (Log, IO, Net or FS writes), plus to_string/to_bytes on an Encode-trait impl. The Taint.jet hand table is deleted. The effect half lands first, then the sink half with a sweep of every Jet source; legitimate releases go through the existing #Secret release path. Taint.jet:315 (core.watcher.process_pid to Exec) goes away with declared destinations.
t18a landed TlsLead-6151c26 (c2cecce162..0a995af312): c26 and c27 met.

t17a landed TlsLead-6151c17 (c17 met), TlsLead-6151c23 (c24 met; c23 stays open: the Calls/Core.jet E0510 host-leaf gates remain until #6615 c5) and TlsLead-6151c52 (e75850d064..c2cecce162). c52 isn't met yet: its ffi and export case lines had red rows. Lander2 traced them to 4 selfhost_terminators jet_lexer cases broken by ScriptAPI-7 (EffectVocabulary's embed_file of toolchain:Compiler/Prelude/Effects.jet gives E0945 when a case copies JetFoundation out of the tree) and a musl race in cffi concurrent-bridges that passes alone. c52 is met when ScriptAPI's fix-forward lands and both lines pass.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). D-FLOAT-INT1 was ratified A on 2026-11-08, so c46 (Type{value} conversions) and c51 are unblocked. Owner gate (2026-11-06): c14, c15, c17, c18, c29, c30, c35, c36 wait for one plain owner question per feature (package-private helpers, layout and lazy lowering, trait-bound format and decode, declaration facts); none is drafted yet.

c46: the conversion question is ballot D-FLOAT-INT1 (what Int{f} means for a Float). Correction to the earlier note: Type{value} is already the ratified scalar conversion (D-DOTCTOR3 amendment, syntax-decisions.md:1214-1239); only Float to Int is open. c46's work (no to_* conversions left in core.math) uses Type{value} or Target.from_source either way.

c46 (conversions), owner note 2026-11-06: owner recalls conversions use the literal constructor form (Int{myFloatVar}). The ratified rule in Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:1122 is D-SHAPE-CONVERT1=A, Target.from_source(value) (Float.from_fraction(f)); no ratified Target{value} conversion form was found. c46 stays open until the owner confirms which form rules; no code changes until then.

Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat, cut questions): "Core plays by package rules" criteria wait. Main designs the public features each needs (package-private helpers, layout and lazy-lowering control, trait-bound format/decode, declaration facts) and asks the owner one plain question per feature; nothing is dropped.

MechB-2 (2026-11-06): c44 and c45 landed in 362a902d3c (12 private to_u8 helpers become the public wrapping(U8{n}); git grep -w to_u8 Core is empty). Not mechanical until #6615 lands: c1, c2 (= #6615 c5), c3, c11, c12 (the D-HOST-LEAF1=E cutover) and c48-c50 (CoreCallRows, Core.jet and signature tables wait for #6615 c4/c5). Waiting on cut rows: c6 (cut c5), c9 (cut c8), c33 (cut c32).

Single-source census F18 (Docs/audits/2026-11-05-single-source-census.md): Builtin method lowering routes. Already owned by #6151 c11, #3325; this is the drift evidence those criteria must clear. One hand-written home: BuiltinMethods.jet rows (plus the runtime export). Fix: gen: put the runtime symbol in the row and derive arity and borrow flags from parameters and access. Drift check: Generator `--check`; `runtime-abi-symbols.mjs` confirms each symbol exists. Drifted on 2026-11-05: Not checked row by row Effort L.
