Merged #6369 "Retire the [Int]-only combinatorics copies of generic list operations (Law 8)" into this card (one Core declaration per API: no twins (Law 8)); its 1 open item(s) are carried as "(was #6369)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

OWNER 2026-10-30 asked what Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet is ('looks nothing like jet ... some weird kind of table or config file'). Facts at dev 216cac590b: 2546 lines in a custom line format, not Jet: 1938 dispatcher_row lines (1791 of them embed literal Rust constructor text, CoreCallRecord::new(...)), 343 ambient_route, 115 module export lists, 113 source_module owner lists, 7 format_row and 4 bootstrap lines. The module, export and owns rows restate what Core/*.jet already declares. It is read by about 10 compiler registry files, Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-core-sources.mjs and Tools/agent checks, and its header still names deleted Rust tables. C2 deletes its member rows; under D-DECL-TYPES1 A (ratified) the remaining runtime-symbol and ambient facts become markers on the Core functions themselves, so the file goes entirely.

Merged #6163 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Build core.build and the fn build host on the public compiler library. Body: Finding F16 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). core.build is implemented inside the compiler: Compiler/JetBuildSession/Source/Session.jet:1-4 (private compiler service linkage), Keys.jet:1-5 (Rust v2 key contract), Declarations.jet:1-2 (Rust runtime_bridge positional contract); Compiler/JetEval/Source/BuildServices.jet:1-3; Build and BuildPlan methods are dispatched by member-name strings in Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BuildAdapter.jet:36-81. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Make core.build ordinary Core source over the public compiler library's typed extension points (#6139). The fn build host calls those functions; delete the string dispatch in BuildAdapter.jet and the private session linkage.

Merged #6162 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core lexes and parses with the same rules as packages (amends #5978). Body: Finding F14 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core is lexed with reserved identifiers allowed (Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/MarkerGroups.jet:222, Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Terminators.jet:558-560) and parsed by its own job with owned members (Loader.jet:3489-3497, 3525). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Give packages the same private `__` name rule #5978 settles for Core, or remove Core's exception; then lex and parse Core with the ordinary job. Fold this into #5978's plan if Main prefers.

Merged #6161 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core calls get effects and sink classes from their declarations. Body: Finding F12 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). A Core call gets its effects and credential-sink class from module-name tables, not its signature: Sema/Taint.jet:240-288 (sema_taint_core_effect) and 290-300 (sema_taint_credential_sink). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Write each Core function's effects in its signature and its sink class with a public marker; read them like a package's. Delete both tables. Coordinate the moved effects with #6137.

Merged #6160 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Copy, resource and typestate facts come from declarations, not Core type names. Body: Finding F11 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Copy, resource and typestate facts come from name lists: Sema/Ownership/Copy.jet:298-307, 597, 697; Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:225; Sema/Typestate.jet:67-68 (Task join and detach). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Declare each fact on the Core type with the public derive, marker or typestate syntax. Delete the name lists and the hard-coded Task transitions.

Merged #6159 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core receives every diagnostic packages receive. Body: Finding F09 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core skips marker vocabulary and site checks (Sema/MarkerModules.jet:439, 447), unbuilt generator and runtime-use checks (Sema/CheckProgram.jet:5005, 5037), typestate validation (CheckProgram.jet:3189-3192, Sema/Typestate.jet:64, 70), budgets (Sema/BudgetSpecs.jet:158-165), a serde pass (Sema/Registration/SerdeItems.jet:1513), and the unbuilt-Core-call refusal (Sema/Calls/Core.jet:218-224). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Remove each exemption. Fix the Core sources the checks then flag, or record each needed exception with the public allowance a package would use.

Merged #6158 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core follows the same #Unsafe and secret rules as packages. Body: Finding F08 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core reads secret bytes without #Unsafe (Sema/Expressions/Places.jet:752-760, any core.* caller skips E0510). Core alone may wrap a generic formal in ExpiringSecret (Sema/FailureLaw.jet:631) and call ExpiringSecret.new with 3 arguments (Sema/Calls/Static.jet:871). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Wrap each Core read of secret bytes in an audited #Unsafe region. Give ExpiringSecret a public bound that admits Core's generic use, or move the use behind the public API. Delete the three exemptions.

Merged #6157 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Remove constructs only Core may write. Body: Finding F07 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Some record literals, annotations, private native types and protected type names are legal only in Core: Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet:402 with Registry/CoreModules.jet:431; Sema/FailureLaw.jet:549-555 (IOOperation, IOContext, owner annotations); Sema/Registration/Items.jet:3509-3510; Sema/Calls/Methods.jet:1345; Sema/TypeRelations.jet:888 (core.email Limits); Sema/Calls/Core.jet:271 (core_private_seam lets Core reach unexported members). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Replace each with ordinary visibility: private fields or constructors, package-private types, and exports. Delete core_record_literal_is_core_only, the owner-annotation suffix list and core_private_seam.

Merged #6156 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Give every package the lazy-lowering and layout rules Core gets. Body: Finding F06 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Unreached Core bodies are not lowered, but other packages' bodies always are (Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:2643-2661, jet_driver_prunable_core_modules). Core types get runtime handle layouts by identity (Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildTypes.jet:347, 494-504, 538). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Apply reachability pruning to every source module, not only Core. Give runtime-handle layouts a public declaration (F01's host declaration carries the handle type), and remove the `<corelib>/` tests in BuildTypes.jet.

Merged #6155 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Bind format, decode, precise math and line loops through public traits. Body: Finding F05 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Language features call named Core helpers by file path: Compiler/JetIR/Source/CoreReach.jet:35-66 (format selectors to Core/Text/Fmt.jet), 68-82 (__decode_* in Core/Encoding/Encoding.jet), 90-104 (Core/Math/Math.jet precise helpers), 117-138 (`loop line in handle.lines()` to read_line / __stdout_next_line). A user type cannot take part. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Express each binding as a public trait (formatting, decoding, precise arithmetic, line source) that Core implements and any package may implement. Lower the language form through the trait. Delete the path and name matching in CoreReach.jet.

Merged #6154 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Lower Core calls through host-leaf declarations, not IR route tables. Body: Finding F04 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). IR lowers Core members straight to runtime symbols: Compiler/JetIR/Source/RouteHandle.jet (1,035 lines), RouteBuiltin.jet (660), RouteBrowser.jet (509); runtime Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/RouteAFont.jet, RouteAGame.jet, RouteBrowser.jet, RouteTerm.jet, RouteWeb.jet. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: After F01, lower a call to a host-leaf declaration the same way for Core and packages. Delete each route table once its members are host-leaf declarations.

Merged #6153 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Move per-domain call checks out of sema into Core declarations. Body: Finding F03 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Sema has a hand-written checker per Core domain: Sema/Calls/Http.jet (920 lines), HttpRouting.jet (1,167), Services.jet (785), TaskGroups.jet (1,116), StreamHandles.jet (571), ProcessHandles.jet (518), TimeHandles.jet (517), UiHandles.jet (515), Hardware.jet (468), Data.jet (1,564), Geometry.jet (308); Static.jet:871 (ExpiringSecret.new with 3 arguments, Core only). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: For each file, state each rule with a public mechanism (typed signatures, traits, typestate, marker rules or a library lint) in the Core module it guards, then delete the file. Work one domain per landing; the checklist is the file list above.

Merged #6152 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Replace compiler gates on Core host leaves with ordinary visibility. Body: Finding F02 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Sema refuses some host leaves unless the caller is one named Core module: Sema/Calls/Core.jet:1143-1147 (core.term __stdio_*), 1149-1154 (core.mem.__loader_new from core.data only), 1155-1160 (__coerce_* from core.encoding.json only), 1161-1166 (CSV leaves), 1170, 1268-1272 (global Shared constructor, E0067 outside Core); Sema/Calls/Data.jet:777. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: After F01, declare each gated leaf private to the module or package that uses it, so ordinary visibility refuses other callers. Delete the module-name gates in Sema/Calls/Core.jet and Sema/Calls/Data.jet.

criteria.text: Every Core member that has a CORE_CALLS row is declared in Core source, and the compiler's twin of Core's API is deleted in one cutover: Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet's member rows and Registry/CoreCalls.jet, CoreCallRows.jet, CoreCallExtensions.jet, CoreSignatures.jet, CorePlatformSignatures.jet, CoreHostSignatures.jet and CoreValueSignatures.jet (census F4, F19). cards.title: Odin-level array programming: element-wise array operators, swizzles on any small array, matrices
cards.body:
Owner 2026-10-29 (direct): Odin's built-in array support (array arithmetic with + - * / that just works, swizzling, strong support for 3D and graphics) must ALL be added to or verified in Jet. This amends D-VECARITH1 (element-wise operators closed to compiler-provided lane and linalg types) and widens D-SWIZZLE1.

Today: swizzles work only on five hard-coded Core type names (F32x4, F64x2, Vec2, Vec3, Vec4; Sema/Expressions/Places.jet:679), with x/y/z/w only and no rgba. Element-wise arithmetic is limited to compiler-provided lane and linalg types. Fixed arrays `[T#N]` (S76/D-FIXARR1) get no element-wise operators or swizzles.

Odin reference set to audit row by row: fixed arrays of numbers with element-wise + - * / % and bit ops between arrays and with a scalar (broadcast), and unary minus; == and !=; swizzles .xyzw and .rgba for N<=4 (read, write and repeat-read); swizzle on the result of an expression; built-in matrix types with * as matrix product, matrix-vector product, transpose and the like; quaternions; #simd vectors; #soa struct-of-arrays layouts; array-to-slice conversion; `len` as a compile-time constant; and compile-time evaluation of all of the above.
cards.plan:
1. Audit: write a table of every Odin array, matrix, quaternion, simd and soa feature (cite the Odin docs/spec) against Jet today, with each row PASS, PARTIAL or MISSING and a probe program. Send the table to Main before implementing; any new spelling needs an owner ballot (I7).
2. Implement every MISSING and PARTIAL row whose spelling is already ratified or needs no new syntax: element-wise operators on [T#N] numeric fixed arrays (array op array, array op scalar), swizzles on [T#N] with N<=4 plus rgba on every swizzleable type, driven by a type fact instead of hard-coded Core names.
3. One runtime meaning on all tiers (I9), with lowering to SIMD where the backend has it.
4. Examples/features/lowlevel goldens; UI snapshots for length mismatch, a non-numeric element and an invalid lane.
5. Pair each new performance-relevant surface with a two-program perf cell against the plain loop (AGENTS.md performance gate).

log.text: Array ballots on Tower: D-ARRAY-CORENAMES1, MATRIX1, KEYED1, LAYOUT1. Drafted by KitSpeed-2; adversarial reader Ballots-4. Ratified conflicts fixed (card #1437 matrix family INDEX1=E, MUL1=F, LIT1=E, BCAST1=E, SOLVE1=B, HOME1=D; D-LANES1=A; D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A; ..= is E0318). Readings for the owner to confirm: MATRIX1 treats Matrix*Vec as the transform product, with BCAST1 limited to repeating operators; LAYOUT1 says push through a window is refused where visible and stops otherwise. Main replaced alias declarations in MATRIX1 with the #6176 form.
Correction to the audit counts (KitSpeed-2): 87 rows, of which 25 PASS, 6 PARTIAL, 55 MISSING and 1 bug.

Audit (KitSpeed-2, 2026-10-29, 78 probes at O0 and full on 25f9dee): 19 PASS, 7 PARTIAL, 49 MISSING, 1 bug. SIMD S1-S11 is ratified but unbuilt (E2104 cites #5984). Swizzle write is broken (lowlevel/swizzle.jet FAILs on all tiers). Rows needing no new syntax are in implementation; B0-B10 go to owner ballots.

cards.title: Portable wasm seed: bootstrap Jet from the repo alone with a C compiler (jet compiler as wasm + tiny C wasm interpreter)
cards.body: Split from #4154 step 3 (owner-approved plan, 2026-10-01; split approved by Main, 2026-10-29). #4154 closes on steps 1–2 (the tagged chain and per-release seed binaries). This card owns the third leg: a portable seed checked into the repo and refreshed occasionally, like Zig's zig1.wasm. It is the Jet compiler built to WebAssembly plus a tiny C wasm interpreter, so any machine with a C compiler can bootstrap from the repo alone, with no downloads and no older Jet binary. Today the self-hosted backend emits only x86-64 (Compiler/JetBackend/Source/X64). The wasm32 target triples exist only as target-machine facts (TargetMachine.jet wasm.browser / wasm.wasi), with no wasm code emitter. So the first prerequisite is a JetIR → wasm32 core-module emitter. The wasm decoder and validator from the plugin engine (#5487, Docs/proposals/plugin-wasm-engine-2026-10-29.md) are reusable for checking the emitted seed. Related: #5455 (bootstrappability from a small seed as the trusting-trust answer).
cards.plan: 1. A JetIR → wasm32 core-module emitter (wasm 1.0 + bulk memory + multi-value), with a minimal WASI-like host import set (args, environ, fd read/write/seek, path open/stat/readdir, clock, exit) that is exactly what jet build needs. 2. Build the compiler (Compiler/ workspace, JetCli) to jet.wasm and check it with the #5487 validator. 3. A small C99 wasm interpreter (one file, no dependencies) that implements that import set over POSIX. 4. A bootstrap script: cc the interpreter, run jet.wasm to build native s1 from the repo, then s2 = s3 fixed point against the released seed. 5. Check the seed in (compressed, with recorded sha256) and document the refresh: who regenerates it, and when.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). c4-c13 need the JetIR to wasm emitter that #5201 (G9, Web target on JetIR) builds, so #5201 blocks this card.
Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (BoardPlanner C-G1-6): this C-compiler bootstrap stays, as an emergency path only; the normal build stays C-free (#6687 c2). Tagged G7 (seed distribution).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 2 criteria from archived #3009: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

Merged #6265 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Wasm seed S3a: wasm32 backend so the compiler builds as jet.wasm. Body: Part of the portable wasm seed card (#4154 step 3 split; q/cards/owner-1029b/wasm-seed.json). Today the self-hosted backend emits only x86-64 (Compiler/JetBackend/Source/X64). This step lowers JetIR to a core wasm module and builds the compiler itself. Estimate 80-120 h. Plan: Reuse Compiler/JetWasm's types, binary encoder and validator. Lower JetIR functions, calls, linear memory, globals, data segments and the function table (indirect calls) to wasm 1.0 + bulk memory + multi-value. Define the stack and heap layout and the C-ABI-like call convention. Add `jet build --target=wasm32-wasi`. Grow coverage from the golden examples up to the Compiler workspace.

criteria.text: On a clean machine with only a C compiler, git and the repo (no network, no earlier jet binary), the documented bootstrap builds a native jet that reaches the s2 == s3 fixed point and matches the release chain. Proof: a committed receipt of the clean-machine run with the s2 and s3 hashes.
The checked-in seed records its sha256 and generating commit, and a Jet test fails when the seed no longer validates or no longer builds the current compiler.
The C wasm interpreter (seed/runner.c) is one C99 source with no third-party dependencies, and `cc -O2 seed/runner.c -o runner` builds without warnings under gcc and clang.
`jet build --target=wasm32-wasi Compiler` produces jet.wasm and the JetWasm validator accepts it.
The wasm32 golden subset matches the native output under the seed runner (a reference runtime may serve only as a test oracle, never in the chain).
jet.wasm runs `jet check` and `jet build` on a small package through the WASI preview1 subset, with output matching native.
Every unsupported leaf on wasm32 (spawn, threads, sockets) returns its typed failure, and nothing traps.

(from #6265 Wasm seed S3a: wasm32 backend so the compiler builds as jet.) (from #6267 Wasm seed S3c: small C wasm interpreter (the seed runner)) `cc -O2 seed/runner.c -o runner` builds warning-free with gcc and clang.

cards.title: Value passing is physically optimal: named-tuple returns in registers, last-use moves are true moves, and large read-only values pass by address
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): multiple returns (Jet named tuples) and value passing must be maximally performant, optimal and efficient. Last-use moves are ratified (D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A, D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A; spec.md ~1103-1150). Calls carry no marks; a take is declared && in the signature (D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A) and an early move is written x.move(), including for fields, values with cleanup, type parameters and lambda captures. Nobody has verified that the generated code actually achieves this. The nbody profile (#3039 C6) already showed hidden heap boxes and copy/drop helpers on hot paths.
cards.plan: Write a small benchmark and inspect corpus (jet inspect code, D-CODE-INSPECT1) at O1/O2: (1) functions returning small named tuples (2-4 scalar fields): the result must come back in registers, with no heap and no stack round-trip beyond the ABI; (2) last-use moves of List/String/struct locals into take parameters and receivers: no copy, no extra retain/release; (3) large read-only struct parameters: passed by address, with no copy; (4) the `^`-required exception cases: confirm each is required for meaning, not for a codegen limitation. Fix every gap in the backend and IR. Add each case as a paired perf cell against the C/Rust equivalent per the performance gate.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c7 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c8 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c9 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A supersedes D-CALLSITE-MARK1=A's ^ exceptions.

Retargeted c4 (owner order 2026-11-02: an invalid criterion is retargeted to a valid one). Old text: Each case has a perf cell at parity or better against C/Rust (Rust <= 1.05) Why: AGENTS.md performance gate: Rust has no parity band (Jet/Rust must be below 1.00 like every peer) and every required cell needs a machine-ceiling reference. The old 'Rust <= 1.05' band is retired.

C4 measured on f75020e91d (IrTypes-2, one build slot, 7 runs pinned to CPU 31, clang-21 -O2 / rustc 1.97 -O3, loaded machine): LOSES. Jet/Rust and Jet/C at O2: multi-return 2.86 / 3.12, recursion-aggregate 2.82 / 2.85, fixed-return-64 1.50 / 2.79, destructure-move 0.82 / 3.02. At O1: 3.15/3.44, 5.16/5.24, 2.40/4.45, 0.66/2.45. cards.title: Research: modularity, scalability and extensibility of every layer of Jet, then one extension-architecture design
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): every level, semantic, syntax, feature and scope of Jet must be analysed through the lens of modularity, scalability and extensibility, so that every domain can grow indefinitely the way D-CORE-BOUNDARY1 makes hardware a library change and D-INFRA1 makes infrastructure typed Jet code. Hardware and FFI are two drops in that ocean. A dedicated research agent (owner-approved) does this.
cards.plan: Write a dated research document in Docs/research that covers every layer: lexical/syntax, the type system, semantics (effects, memory, errors, concurrency, evaluation, comptime), the compiler pipeline, the runtime, tooling, build/packages, every standard-library domain, deployment/targets, and evolution over time. For each layer: what is closed today and where (file:line, measured), the possible extension mechanisms, prior art with citations, costs (performance, tooling, readability, safety, I8 one mechanism, I9 tiers), and what the evidence favours. Then draft one extension-architecture design meeting the ballot rework bar, and specify a 'no closed lists' gate.

cards.title: Native struct layout is physically optimized (reordered and packed) on every type, and C interop works with that optimized layout
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): always keep the compiler's memory-layout optimization, unlike Rust where #[repr(C)] turns field reordering off. C interop and FFI must be confirmed working with the optimizations on. Current state (Main probe on dev bb9c74e522): a default struct reports kind "default", guarantee "physical layout unspecified" and no size fact (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:682-723; `Mixed.$layout.size` is empty). The same 5-field struct {U8, Int, U8, Int, U8} under #Layout(c) is 40 bytes, while the optimal order is 24. Runtime record glue (e.g. JetRuntime/Source/DataPlotFlat.jet:68-92) stores each field in its own 8-byte word in a jet_rt_alloc block. That suggests default records are heap blocks with a word per field, the same cost the nbody profile showed for [T#N] (#3039 C6).
cards.plan: 1. Measure the real native representation of default structs (stack vs heap, word-per-field vs packed) at O0/O1/O2. 2. Make the default layout physical and optimal: fields ordered by alignment then size, small fields packed, niches used for optionals (D-MEM-UNBOX1), inline (not heap) for value structs, and a defined $layout size/offset fact. 3. C interop with optimization on: a Jet type exported to C emits its C declaration in the optimized field order, so C sees the same bytes with zero copies. A type imported from a C header keeps that header's layout because it is a C type. Today's 'wire mirror' copy at the boundary (syntax-decisions D-PLACE1 text) is removed wherever the layouts already coincide. 4. #Layout(c) remains only for matching an externally fixed layout; if its public meaning changes, that part goes to the owner through the ballot bar. 5. Prove it with a C round-trip test: C reads and writes Jet-exported optimized structs, on every tier.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c6 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

OWNER RULING 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'keep field order unchanged' for hand-written #Layout(c) structs that mirror an outside layout. Final rule: every struct defined in Jet source is layout-optimized, including ones exported to C (C gets a generated declaration in Jet's order). #Layout(c) marks a layout owned elsewhere and keeps its written field order, as do C types imported by use from a header or C source.

OWNER DIRECTION 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'if we define the layout in our source, then we should optimize it. If we are pulling it from elsewhere we shouldnt change it.' Applied: every struct defined in Jet source is layout-optimized, including ones exported to C (C gets a generated declaration in Jet's order). Types pulled from elsewhere, such as C structs imported from a header or C source by use (D-FFI-CINPUT1 A), keep the foreign layout unchanged. Open edge sent to the owner: hand-written #Layout(c) structs that mirror an outside layout (Jetpack HeaderParser structs, embedded MMIO register blocks) count as 'defined in our source' by the literal reading, which would reorder them.

Landed bc8aba3913: C1 C2 C3 C5 met. C4 (perf cell vs C/Rust for the packed layout) stays open; the struct-packed cell is ready in IrTypes-2's tree, measurement paused by the owner's overnight priorities.

Main reading of the owner direction (reported for confirmation): every Jet-owned struct gets the optimized layout, including structs exported to C, which get a generated C declaration in offset order (C3). #Layout(c) keeps C declaration order, because it marks layouts the foreign side owns (Jetpack HeaderParser structs and the embedded MMIO register blocks); reordering those would break them. No new marker is added. If the owner wants #Layout(c) reordered as well, the foreign-owned layouts would need a different spelling, which is a ballot.

Correction from IrTypes-2's measurement (e6, jet emit --ir at none/full plus O2 objdump): default user structs are NOT heap. They are one IR Aggregate in a stack slot on every tier, laid out in declaration order with natural C alignment (Mixed {Bool, Float, U8, I32, Float} = 32 B; reordered and packed = 24 B). The word-per-field heap glue is the runtime's 163 hand-written jet_rt_record_new_*/jet_rt_handle_* shims for specific Core types (boxed records at the Core/runtime boundary), not user structs. Read-only by-value params already pass by address. Returns copy from a frame temp into the caller's sret (#6201 C6). The remaining scope of this card is reordering/packing, the  size fact, C export in the optimized order, and whether those boxed runtime records should become plain aggregates.

cards.title: Lambda is an unnamed function: `fn(n: Int) -> Int { n * n }` (ballot D-LAMBDA-FN1)
cards.body: Owner idea (2026-10-29): a lambda is a function without its name, just as `A | B` is an unnamed enum (D-UNIONTYPE1). Today `->` starts the result type in `fn f(x: Int) -> Int {}` and in the type `fn(Int) -> Int`, but starts the body in a lambda `(n: Int) -> n * n`. So `(n: Int) -> Int { n * n }` silently parses `Int{n * n}` as a typed value, and adding a line makes it E0399. Census at d345e35902: 4,768 lambdas in 1,194 files, 59.1% relying on E0801 inference. Ballot D-LAMBDA-FN1 decides the form.
cards.plan: After ratification: parser (fn + `(` in value position parses an unnamed function, reusing the callable signature parser), sema (written result/error types checked against the expected type; the declaration rules apply when there is no expected type), a `jet fix` migration of all lambdas, and updates to the spec, the syntax registry, editor grammars, examples and diagnostics in one cutover.

cards.title: Debug info for optimized builds: DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine entries and location lists for locals at -O1/-O2
cards.body: Found by RustOut7-2 while probing lldb on a native jet build at 236cd9310c for #6221 P1. At the default optimization level, inlined functions (e.g. `area`) leave no inlined_subroutine entries, and most locals have no location, so `--release` binaries can't be debugged meaningfully. #6221 P1 covers aggregate type DWARF and makes `jet debug` build with optimize=none/inline=off. This card covers the optimized tiers, which C compilers support (gcc/clang -O2 -g).
cards.plan: Emit DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine with call-site file/line for every inlined call, and location lists for locals across register allocation. Verify with lldb on a -O2 probe: break in an inlined function, show frames, print locals.

cards.body: Found by BallotDesign (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext). Compiler/Prelude/core/prelude.jet:21-22 declares `fn check(text: String) Error! -[]>` and `fn encode_hole<T: Printable>(value: T) String -[]>`. In user code `String -[]>` is E0003 (only `-[]> String` is accepted), and user traits cannot declare bodiless methods at all (E0081 '`fn name` has no body'). Pillar 5: Core may use no form a package can't write.
cards.plan: Make the Prelude use the user grammar (`-[]> String`). Decide whether user traits may declare required (bodiless) methods; if the ratified trait design allows required methods, lift E0081 for trait declarations. Otherwise the Prelude must use the same form users use. Cutover in one patch.

Sema already has an error-tolerant symbol for an untyped parameter (sema_function_param_scope_symbol). c64 extends that same rule to field and payload types whose name resolves to nothing (E0119), so the declaring module is no longer marked incomplete (sema_check_registration_module_start) and Pipeline.jet:4064 no longer stops every body. The poisoned member type is the existing error type, which suppresses follow-on noise (.size UnknownField, needs Missin but the value is Int), and items whose checks reach it are recorded as skipped. Error recovery inside the collect-all contract is an implementation choice the approved contract already covers. It adds no syntax or user-visible semantics, so it needs no ballot (AGENTS.md Owner gates).

c180 scope ruling (Main, 2026-11-11): the rule counts entries, not the name run. An entry is the load's entry file or any file a package or project declares as an entry or binary: a `run: fn` entry or a script body. Within one load graph, package or project, entries are all script bodies or all `run` entries, and a script-style scope has exactly one script file. Library functions that happen to be named run (Core/Game/Game.jet:23 game.run(scene, …), Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet:230 tasks.run()) only run when called, so they don't count and are not renamed (a public API rename would be owner-gated). A UI case proves importing core.game from a script stays legal.

Clarification of the D-FILE-STATEMENTS1 withdrawal (owner, 2026-11-11: run fn and script style are both allowed, and mutually exclusive within one file). This is the rule as built. On seed-t22, a file with only top-level statements runs (prints 6), a file with only `run: fn` runs (prints 6), and a file with both is refused with E0621 TopLevelStatementsBesideRun ('Move the statements into run: fn, or remove run: fn'). The withdrawal adds no named local functions. A helper that captures the script's locals is an ordinary closure.

From MemDesign #6385 research (2026-10-30): an unknown static method on a builtin number type (for example U8.from_int) reports a misleading E0107 "Nothing named `U8`"; it should report E0311 naming the type and the method. Folded here as part of C22 instead of a new criterion on #6389.

Merged #6183 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A local trait implemented through `impl labels.Tag.Mine` passes coherence, but calling its method gives E0102. Body: Found by IrTypes-2 while working on g10 (#6170/#6171/#6172, 2026-10-29) on jet-u13 / dev 36825b7a15; the repro is in the IrTypes-g10 msg. Not fixed by g10. A local trait implemented with a module-qualified head (`impl labels.Tag.Mine`) is accepted by coherence, but a call to its method is refused with E0102, so the impl can never be used. Plan: Reproduce from the g10 msg. Make method resolution find impls registered under a qualified head, using the same key that coherence uses. Add a case test.

Merged #6181 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `Mat3<Int>(...)` silently ignores its type argument; a missing static method on Mat3 reports E0107 "Nothing named Mat3". Body: Found by KitSpeed-2's #6177 Odin array audit (2026-10-29; probes in kitspeed/w6177/probes, run at O0 and full on 25f9dee, with both tiers agreeing). (1) Writing a type argument on a non-generic Core math type, `Mat3<Int>(...)`, is accepted and the argument is silently discarded, so the program builds a Float matrix. It should be a registered diagnostic. (2) Calling a static method that doesn't exist on Mat3 reports E0107 "Nothing named `Mat3`" instead of E0311 naming the missing method. Plan: Reproduce with the audit probes. In sema, reject type arguments on non-generic types (registered code, UI snapshot), and route missing static methods on an existing type to E0311.

Merged #6285 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `[T]{}` means the empty list in an expression but is E0003 as a field default (`values: [DBValue]{}`). Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/holes_b_default.jet). A field default `values: [DBValue]{}` is E0003 'Expected a value'; only `[DBValue]{[]}` parses. In expressions, `[DBValue]{}` is the empty list. The same text should mean the same thing in both places. Plan: Accept `[T]{}` as the empty-list default in field position (one grammar rule shared with expressions). Migrate any `{[]}` defaults if the ratified spelling is `{}`.

Merged #6284 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A static trait method cannot return `Self`: `-> Self` gives E0108, and `-> Cypher` gives E0913. Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/self_static.jet). In an impl of a trait whose static method returns Self, writing `-> Self` and returning `Cypher{...}` reports E0108 'This needs Self, but the value is Cypher'; writing `-> Cypher` reports E0913 (signature mismatch). Self must be the implementing type inside an impl. Plan: In sema, resolve Self to the impl's target type in static trait methods (signature and body), consistently with instance methods. Add a golden and a ui snapshot for a true mismatch.

Merged #6283 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Two spellings of unit success: `Ok(())` and `Ok()` in the corpus. Body: Found by BallotDesign: Examples/ has 13 lines of `Ok(())` and 12 of `Ok()` (for example web/state_surface.jet:42). Reaching the end of an `E!` body already succeeds. One meaning needs one spelling (I8). Plan: Pick the canonical form from the ratified decisions (or ballot it if none decides), migrate every caller in one cutover, and make the other spelling a diagnostic with a jet fix.

Merged #6282 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Impl methods do not inherit the trait method's declared effect row (E0907 asks to restate `-[]>`). Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/unit_norow.jet). An impl of CheckedText.check without `-[]>` gets E0907 'must be pure. Declare this CheckedText method pure', even when the body is pure. The trait's declared row is not used as the impl's row. Under D-EFFECT-OMIT1 rows are inferred, and an impl should take its row from the trait (a pure body checks; an impure one reports E0907 at the effect). Plan: In sema, an impl method with no written row takes the trait method's declared row as its ceiling and checks the body against it. Update the E0907 snapshot to point at the offending effect.

Merged #6257 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Is Float Comparable? The generic bound `T: Comparable` admits Float, but `#Comparable` on a Float field is E0905 and Solver.jet:258 says Float isn't Comparable. Body: Found by Ballots-4 for #6174 (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/p74/gen2.jet, gen3.jet). TypeRelations.jet:1168 treats Float as a member of the scalar family at generic bounds, so min/max over Float work and NaN propagates. Deriving #Comparable on a struct with a Float field is refused (E0905), and the solver has a Float-specific 'isn't Comparable' fix text. One meaning (I8) needs one answer: either Float is Comparable everywhere, with NaN-propagating comparisons (the generic-bound behaviour min/max now relies on), or nowhere (and min/max over Float need a separate ordering such as total_cmp). Plan: Pick the meaning that matches the ratified Comparable contract (Docs/spec, D-CORE-LAWS1 laws for Comparable). Make the bound, derive and solver diagnostics agree, and add UI tests for each path. If the contract is silent and a choice is needed, it is an owner ballot.

Merged #6252 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `return` inside a braced lambda passed to generic `map` is checked against the enclosing function (E0113) instead of the lambda. Body: Found by Ballots-4 while probing for D-LAMBDA-FN1: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/lamp/p12.jet. A `return` inside a braced lambda body passed to a generic `map` is type-checked against the enclosing fn's result type and reports E0113. The retired Rust test sort_comparator_early_return_is_local_to_lambda expected `return` to be local to the lambda, and spec S47 says return leaves the lambda. Plan: Make lambda bodies a return scope in sema for every call shape, including generic callees whose result is solved from the body. Port the Rust test as a case/golden.

Merged #6199 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A comma between enum cases gives a misleading E0003 ("Expected a name for a variant name", fix "e.g. `main`"). Body: Found by Main (2026-10-29, dev bb9c74e522). `enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }` reports E0003 "Expected a name for a variant name, found `,`". The Why is "Names start with a letter or `_`" and the Fix is "e.g. `main`, `count`, `_tmp`". The real cause is that enum cases are separated by whitespace or newlines, not commas, and every user coming from Rust, Swift, TS or C writes the comma. The diagnostic must name the actual rule and offer a machine fix that drops the commas. If the owner changes the separator rule (enum comma question, 2026-10-29), this card follows that outcome instead. Plan: In the enum case parser, detect a `,` where a case name is expected after a case and report a dedicated registered diagnostic (what/why/fix: enum cases are separated by spaces or newlines; remove the comma) with a structured fix. Add a UI snapshot. Re-check after the owner's separator ruling.

criteria.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (language review): a module-level `name: value` is a guarantee, not a try. It is always evaluated while building; one that fails while building, or that cannot run then because it has effects, is a build error with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot whose fix names the three ways out (move it into `run`, make it lazy explicitly, or use a pinned build input such as embed_file). No code runs before `run`. Today `BAD: 10 / zero()` at module level passes jet check and jet build and stops at first use with E3010 (probe, seed a0_042). Inside a function a plain `name: value` still only tries to fold; in a file of top-level statements the lines are the program and run in order. Cases prove the same meaning on O0, O1 and O2, and every module-level binding in Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and tests is clean under the rule in the same cutover.

criteria.text: Owner order 2026-11-11: a program is EITHER script style OR a single run entry, never mixed, with no workaround at any scope. If a `run: fn` exists anywhere in the program's load graph, its package or its project (any module, nested module, re-export, import rename such as `use { run: other.main }`, or code a marker or template generates), then top-level executable statements anywhere in that scope are refused, and the reverse also holds. A script-style program has exactly one file with top-level statements, its entry, and no `run: fn` anywhere. Today E0621 covers only both in one file and E0620 covers only an imported script body, so an entry script whose imported module or package declares `run: fn` is not refused. One registered diagnostic (what, why and fix, plus a UI snapshot) names both sites. UI cases cover the same file, an imported module, another module of the same package, a renamed import, a re-export and generated code. Before landing, sweep every Jet source in the repository (Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples, tests and fixtures) and migrate every hit in the same batch.

criteria.text: A ?? fallback that returns a value built from err.copy() keeps the left side's type. cards.title: The gc opt-in is built: `#Policy(gc)` collects the cycles of the types under it, and `jet gc report` and `jet audit memory` show every promotion
cards.body:
Destination: D-GC-OPTIN1=A (2026-10-30) is built. `#Policy(gc)` opts in the types declared under it, so their cycles are collected wherever their values go, with collection only at the D-GC-WHEN1 points; E0221 still fires for code without the opt-in; one Jet-owned collector serves every tier; and trace mode, `jet gc report`, `jet audit memory` and `jet fix memory` explain each promotion and how to remove it.

Why: a ratified opt-in that lifts nothing leaves cyclic programs with no escape.

Source: probes q/bd/probe/gc (BallotDesign, dev 94df799429), with archived #658, #659 and #1895. `Mem.Gc` became a declared leaf on dev 84f8b2f7ff (c1).
cards.plan: Make the opted scope lift E0221 for the types under it and route their cycle-capable values to the collector (D-GC-WHEN1 timing); keep E0221 elsewhere; then the trace, report, audit and fix tools.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1: D-GC-OPTIN1 is ratified A, so c2 states the outcome directly. c1 met (dev 84f8b2f7ff), c7 met (Gc<T> retired). Each other criterion names its case; c5 uses `.copy()` because `~` is retired.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Tagged G10: the GC opt-in is memory work. c2 waits for ballot D-GC-OPTIN1, which is not on Tower (to draft). c6 no longer names the Rust emission tier.

Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/GCOptinCycleCollected` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter shared_cycle_without_gc`.

Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter PolicyScope/package_gc_policy_applies_once_across_imported_modules` and `--filter policy_scope/hosted_gc_policy_matches_all_tiers`.

criteria.text: Sema promotes values to traced storage automatically only inside the effective gc scope, and keeps the meaning of an unmarked read, `&` write, `^` take and `.copy()`, and the ownership-only escape refusal. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/gc_promotion_scope_` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter gc_escape_ownership`.

JetIR, native emission and `jet dev` use one Jet-owned collector as the only backend, with the same behavior and no external dependency. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/GC` passes on O0, O1, O2 and under `jet dev`, and git grep finds one collector implementation.

(was #658 c4) Public core.gc/Gc<T> wrappers, aliases, adapters, examples, and docs retire; scoped automatic promotion is the only source mechanism [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today]

Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLISettings/gc_trace_` and `--filter memory_semantics/gc_trace_records_promotions`.

Ledger rows persist across runs at the configured path, and a missing ledger is a registered error with a snapshot beside E2110. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter MemorySemantics/gc_promotions_append_to_the_configured_cross_run_memory_ledger` passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv.

cards.title: Rebuild Tower in Jet: the board's CLI, store, server and web UI become a Jet web application (stress test for Jet as a web domain language)
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-30: 'Rebuilding tower in jet rather than TS/JS will be the goal as a stress test for jet as a web domain language.' Tower today is a Node application under Tools/tower (63 .mjs/.js files: CLI tower.mjs, app/store.mjs, app/server.mjs, the web UI and tests). The rebuild uses Jet's web stack end to end (Core web, HTTP server, routing, live UI, storage), so every gap it finds is a Jet defect or missing capability, recorded as a criterion here or a gap card. The board data in Tools/tower/.tower/ keeps its format unless the owner rules otherwise, so the cutover needs no data migration. The owner runs tower serve; agents use the CLI.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-16: Tower in Jet is paused (frozen) for now.
Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): #6676 c1 (Tower's write path is Jet, no node) is merged into c4; #6676 is closed.
Owner order 2026-11-11: Tower is not to be rebuilt in Jet any time soon. Removed from G9 and given no goal, so no lane works it. Tower stays on node.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Tagged G9: Tower rebuilt as a Jet web application is the web goal's stress test. c9-c54 are Node Tower behaviors folded in; they are the parity list for c2/c3.

#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 46 criteria from archived #519, #667, #773, #1195, #1203, #1375, #2331, #2332, #2338, #2924, #2929, #3513: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

Merged #5962 "Tower hygiene report: cards without epoch or criteria, stale cards, blocked by done cards, near-duplicates" into this card (Tower in Jet); its 3 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5962)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

criteria.text: A gap census: every capability Tower uses (HTTP server and routing, file-backed JSON store with atomic writes and locking, CLI argument parsing, live web UI, markdown rendering, the test suite) is mapped to a Jet Core API that exists or to a named gap, committed under Docs/Research with file:line evidence. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Research/*tower-in-jet*"` names the census.

The Tower CLI is a Jet program with the same commands, flags, output and exit codes; Tools/tower's own test suite, ported to jet test, passes against it, and the board files it writes are byte-identical to the Node version's on the same operations. Proof: `jet test Tools/tower` passes against the Jet CLI and a byte comparison of board files with the Node version is empty.

tower serve is a Jet web application serving the same board UI and live updates; a scripted browser test drives the main flows (cards, criteria, decisions, ballots, questions) on the Jet server. Proof: the scripted browser test of tower serve on the Jet server.

Cutover: Tools/tower holds no .mjs/.js/.ts outside generated browser output (per the #5201 rule); AGENTS.md, skills and docs name the Jet commands; nothing falls back to Node. Proof: `git ls-files "Tools/tower/*.mjs" "Tools/tower/*.js" "Tools/tower/*.ts"` prints only generated browser output.

A Tower workload cell in the perf manifest compares the Jet server with the Node one (request latency and memory) under the performance gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry tower-server`.

One `tower report` command prints counts and card lists for: open cards with no epoch; open cards with no criteria (by phase); open cards with no log entry in 30+ days; open cards whose blockers are all done; near-duplicate open titles; open cards in arrived epochs.

`tower report` on the 2026-10-28 board export, committed as a fixture board, reproduces the tower_health.mjs counts (639, 624, 385, 38, 108 pairs, 144), and this runs in the Tower test suite. Proof: the ported Tower suite's report test passes under `jet test Tools/tower`.
(was #5962) The report runs in the Tower test suite against a fixture board.
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6311 c7: the suite run is c7's proof

cards.title: Type conversions: make explicit conversion clean (owner asks about Int{myFloat}-style constructor casts)
cards.body:
Owner question 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'Type conversions generally need casts, how can we make this clean? Should casting be done by wrapping the value to cast in a type literal constructor? like Int{myFloatVar}?'

Starting facts: D-SHAPE-CONVERT1 A (ratified 2026-07-14, #566) makes conversion destination-owned: Target.from_source(value) (U8.from_int(n) ?? return, UserId.from_int(raw)); checked narrowing is fallible; safe widening is implicit; casts, to_* and convert() are refused. D-JAI-SMALL1 A adds #As member conversion. Type{...} braces already mean typed literals and field defaults (String{""}, ANSI{"..."}), so Int{x} would overlap them.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the owner order that a retired spelling gets no teaching diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule.

Owner 2026-10-30 on float to int: 'for integer, let's do the swift/rust style. we have advanced APIs with variadics and optionals and defaults and named vs positional etc. but dont think we really use them, but this may be a good place for that.' Direction for the ballot: separate exact conversion (fails unless the value is whole and in range, like Swift Int(exactly:) and Rust TryFrom) from the deliberate lossy forms (truncate, round, saturate), and use Jet's named, defaulted and optional parameters for the lossy choices.

OWNER 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'what about casts as a kind of generic trait that can be implemented? then using the Int{myFloatVar} would detect that you are trying to construct an int literal and detect the type of the internal type, then use the implemented conversion trait implicitly? Thoughts'. Main's findings: Type{x} conversion already exists for scalar heads under D-DOTCTOR3 and its 2026-09-28 amendment (#3739; syntax-decisions.md:1187-1229): Float{n}, U8{i}, F32{v}, Int{I64{v}} work, and Int{myFloat} is deliberately E0112. Those rules are compiler-builtin while from_* (about 2821 call sites) is a second mechanism. The #6313 ballot leads with the owner's trait design.

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers the owner's question: the current rule and how it reads in real code (counted call sites in Core, Examples and Compiler), the pain points with evidence, how Int{x} would interact with typed literals, field defaults and checked text, which conversions are lossy (float to int rounding, narrowing, sign) and how each must be spelled, and prior art (Rust as/From/TryFrom, Swift Int(x), Zig @intCast, Odin cast, Go T(x)).
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-type-conversions.md (SurfaceDesign-docs.patch): current rule with file:line (BuiltinStatics.jet:175/212, Checked.jet:389), probes m6313/m6313b/m6313c/m6313p o0=o1=o2; lossy cases (float->int truncation, Float.from_int rounding, narrowing wrap, sign); typed-literal and checked-text interaction; census of from_float/from_int/_rounded/round sites in Core, Examples, Compiler; prior-art table (Rust as/From/TryFrom, Swift, Zig, Go, C, Java, C#, Python, Kotlin, JS)

criteria.text: A ballot-ready Tower decision presents same-program alternatives (keep Target.from_source; Int{x}; Int(x); others the research finds), each with exact spelling for widening, checked narrowing, rounding, saturating and wrapping, and the beginner and expert paths; it states which earlier decisions it amends.
criteria.evidence: D-CONVERT-TRAIT1 added to Tower on card #6313 (ballot-ready: Tower decision add validation passed, readycheck READY, plaincheck PLAIN OK, recommendation losses []).

criteria.text: D-CONVERT-TRAIT1=A is built: From(S) is a Core trait with one method from(value: S) -> Self; impl Celsius.From(Float) makes Celsius{x} and Celsius.from(x) work; To(T) is only a bound (prep S: To(Float) means Float.From(S) exists), and writing impl X.To(Y) is an error whose fix writes impl Y.From(X). Every caller, example, test and doc is migrated in one cutover, the old spelling is not Jet syntax and gets no diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule (owner order 2026-11-06), and the examples pass on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Convert/FromTrait` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Convert/impl_to_refused`.

`impl Celsius -> Float` no longer gives the self-contradicting E0113 naming the internal errconv_Celsius_to_Float; the declaration follows D-CONVERT-TRAIT1=A (`impl Float.From(Celsius)`) and the old form is an ordinary parse error.

D-FLOAT-INT1=A is built: Int{f} converts a whole, finite, in-range Float and otherwise stops with a registered error naming math.trunc, floor, ceil, round and round_even; a literal body is checked at compile time; saturating(Int{f}) truncates, clamps and maps NaN to 0 on every integer head; no from_float or saturating_from method exists. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Convert/int_from_float_` on O0, O1, O2 and web, and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter int_from_float_`.

D-ROUND-EVEN1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). math.trunc, floor, ceil, round and round_even take any number through a Roundable trait and return the same type: Float, F32, Decimal and Fraction give a whole value of their own type, and Int and every sized integer come back unchanged. round ties away from zero, and round_even ties to even. x.rounded(mode) takes a run-time mode, and impl MyFixed.Roundable makes a user number round like the built-in ones. Proof: a golden over every number type and both tie rules on O0, O1 and O2, and a case with a user Roundable type.

D-ROUND-EVEN1=A conversion half (ratified 2026-11-13). Int{} converts a whole Float, F32, Decimal or Fraction exactly, and stops on NaN, an infinity, a fraction part or a value out of range with a registered error naming math.trunc, floor, ceil, round and round_even; checked(Int{...}) gives None instead. This covers Int{Decimal} and Int{Fraction}, which are refused with E0108 today. Every in-repo caller that relied on round returning Int is migrated to Int{math.round(x)} in the same cutover. Proof: cases for each source type and each stop, ui snapshots for the stops, and the golden suite on O0, O1 and O2.

core.math keeps no source-owned scalar conversion that `Type{value}` spells (D-FLOAT-INT1=A): `to_float` is removed and its callers write `Float{x}`. The SIMD `from_array`/`to_array` bridges stay, because D-SIMD1 and D-SIMD2 (ratified) require them. Proof: `git grep -n 'to_float: fn' Core/Math` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Math` passes. (was #6151 c46)

cards.title: Custom allocators and struct-of-arrays: native, complete support and its interactions
cards.body:
Owner questions 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'How can jet support custom allocators? What does this feature intefere with? Does this overlap with anything? Can we just support it natively? what about soa data types? We should support those.'

Starting facts: D-REGION1/D-ALLOC1/D-ALLOC2 (mem.Arena, scope-bound views, E0631/E0632), D-FIXED-BACKING1 (mem.Fixed), D-ALLOCFAIL1 (try_alloc family, AllocError), D-ALLOC-DEFAULT1 A (Jet-written size-class mem.Heap), D-TARGET-ALLOC1, D-SOA1/D-SOA2A-D (#Layout(columnar), whole-struct only, E1107-E1109), D-SOA-SITE1 A and D-SOA-TIER1 A. Core/Mem/Mem.jet declares empty struct Arena {}, Bump {} and Pool<T> {}. #6109 (Arena/Bump .alloc) closed; #6310 is an allocator-view ICE; #5042/#5043 are allocator speed cards.

log.text: Unlanded work, recorded 2026-11-12 (dead-lane sweep, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/REPORT.md). Staged in Main/inbox from the dead G3Ctx lane and not on dev: G3Ctx-5/6 (c3), G3Ctx-9 (c9, the ICE 101 fix), G3Ctx-10..14 (c8), and G3Ctx-16/16r and 17/17b (c3 slices 2a and 2b). G3Ctx-18 (c3 completion: a user mem.Allocator value as a #Context(allocator:) carrier) is only work in progress, saved as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/G3Ctx-t9.patch, with its draft message at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/g3ctx18.msg. Each is rebased on dev and re-proved before landing. Owner: G12Docs-4 (G3), after #5971.

Ballot NEW-D-ALLOC-MIGRATE1 withdrawn 2026-11-11 after an adversarial rewrite (owner order: confusing or parallel ballots are redone, and questions an existing mechanism answers are decided rather than balloted). Decided: Migrate through ordinary recoverable error propagation: infer AllocError, admit it into typed domains unless an explicit nonallocating conversion exists, and retain Never only after proof or explicit handling. It extends: origin/dev:Core/Mem/Mem.jet:16-20 defines AllocError. D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C, read in full, requires ordinary allocation failure, typed admission or conversion, and proof or handling at Never boundaries. origin/dev:Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet carries the ordinary failure solve; no allocation-specific failure system is needed. The full record is $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots-v4/NEW-D-ALLOC-MIGRATE1/verdict.md. Withdrawal decides the direction; it does not mean the build is done.

Amends Main's 2026-11-11 c8 migration-form log, after G3Ctx's measured census ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/c8/census.mjs, a name-based call-graph over-approximation on t4). Of 81,415 function bodies, 58,136 reach a growth call. Under the propagate rule, 21,549 Never! functions would drop Never! (Compiler 9,768, Core 5,495, Jetpack 4,416, Tools 1,607, tests 248), and 8,691 typed-domain functions would widen `E!` to `(E | AllocError)!` across about 300 error types (StoreError 703, IOError 461, SSLError 310), which breaks the field reads in `.Err(e)` arms. D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C says typed domains 'admit or convert' and does not choose between them, and the choice reshapes about 30k signatures and Core's public error types. That is public API at a scale the ballot did not measure, so it goes back to the owner as NEW-D-ALLOC-MIGRATE1 (admit as a union, convert with one impl AllocError -> E per type, or a mix by rule; and the Never! form: drop Never! and propagate, or keep it and handle once per function). D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C stays in force. Meanwhile the work that every outcome needs proceeds: the nonallocating AllocError -> Err (G3Ctx-10), fallible IR and runtime routes for every growth operation (List insert/extend, Map add/add_new/setdefault/update, String push_str), an inline fast path for plain push with a fallible slow path plus a paired perf cell, and the codemod with each outcome as a mode and a --census. The cutover itself waits for the vote.

c8 migration form, decided by Main on 2026-11-11 within D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C (no new ballot). G3Ctx measured the reach on t4: 27,821 growth call sites (Compiler 15,345, Jetpack 5,095, Core 4,147, Tools 3,234) and 22,279 Never! lines. The ratified text fixes the form: "first reduce plumbing through ordinary inference and propagation, then choose stopping once at a boundary"; Never! must prove or handle failure, and no flag silently changes a contract. The cutover is a program SUB (a codemod run on the composed train tree, with a --check mode), not a static patch. Its order: (1) an unannotated function infers AllocError, and nothing is written; (2) a typed-contract function whose domain admits it gains mem.AllocError in its contract, written in the source; (3) a Never! function that allocates loses Never! and propagates, unless it is a real no-failure boundary, which handles it once with `?? panic("no memory")` at its outermost call, never at each growth site; (4) entry points (the jet driver main, tool main and run functions) are the stopping boundaries. A per-call `?? panic` is used only where the codemod cannot find a boundary, and the SUB lists those sites. A paired perf cell (propagating growth against the pre-cutover build on a growth-heavy workload) proves the cost before ratification closes, and the census of the whole repository runs collect-all before the train.
D-SOA-SITE1 A retired the #Layout(columnar) marker in favour of Columns<T>; the criterion named the retired spelling.

criteria.text: D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C is built: a refused allocation is recoverable by default through core.mem.AllocError on the ordinary failure rail, and `?? panic("…")` is the explicit stop; the ballot program (load: fn() -> Int mem.AllocError! pushing three rows) prints 3, and 0 under a refusing test allocator; List, Map and String growth and reserve report AllocError with no second error type; the spec describes the route. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/AllocFailRecoverable` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter alloc_error_unhandled`.

I2 defect found by G3Ctx, 2026-11-11, on seed-t20: passing a raw-pointer dereference as a borrowed place is ICE 101, "ir.build unlowered: write place Deref". The trigger is `bump(pointer.*)` where `bump: fn(c: &Counter) { c.n += 1 }` and `pointer := mem.from_addr<Counter>(mem.address_of(c))` inside #Unsafe. A generic `pointer.*.bump(by)` through a trait `&self` method fails the same way. The repros are $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/probe/derefw.jet and a2fn.jet. IR lowering handles a Deref write place (a borrow of the pointee) on O0/O1/O2, and both repros become cases that print the bumped value.

D-REGION-ALLOC1=F is built (owner ratified 2026-11-11): a value built inside `#Context(allocator: arena)` that escapes the context is placed in its final owner's memory from creation, through the existing Context allocation route (Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildTransact.jet:253-260), with no silent escape copy and no `_in` API family. An escape that can't be resolved is refused with a diagnostic naming the explicit repair. The ballot program prints ada;lin. Owner: the G3 lane. Proof: an example golden on O0, O1 and O2 printing the ballot's intended output, a UI snapshot for every diagnostic the form adds, and every in-repo use migrated in the same batch (greenfield, no old spelling kept).
The caller-backed `Fixed.over` example shows typed allocation, reuse, close and exhaustion inside caller storage with no heap fallback, with the same output on O0, O1, O2 and web.

Columns<T> (D-SOA-SITE1=A, which retires #Layout(columnar)) stores a struct list column by column and supports the full logical-list API, and no #Layout(columnar) use remains. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/ColumnsSoa` on O0, O1 and O2 and `git grep -n 'Layout(columnar)' -- Core Examples Compiler` prints nothing.
All three particle variants still print 599.9999999999977 on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter S5ColumnarWitness/`. (was #2889 c3)

cards.title: Terminal control API: broad, deep core.term so no external terminal library is needed
cards.body:
Owner order 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'I want to ensure it is easy to use Terminal "commands" like "execute(term.clear_buffer, term.enable_raw_mode, term.enable_alternate_screen, term.hide_cursor)" with an excellent, broad and deep API so external libraries would not be needed'.

Starting facts: Core/Term/Term.jet (64 fns) and Core/Tui/Tui.jet (62 fns) exist; D-TUI-ANSI1 A (ANSI{...} checked text plus cursor, clearing, alternate-screen and mouse helpers returning one checked value), D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1 A (one lossless key decoder), D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1 A (is-a-terminal), D-CORE-PROCGROUP1 A. #6147 is an open ballot on whether the terminal UI leaves Core; this card's API must agree with its outcome. cards.title: Binary size: Jet's default build must produce the smallest output of any language, for every program, by design rather than per-program tricks
cards.body: Owner (2026-10-30): 437 KB for hello world is far too big. Measured by Main on this machine (x86-64 Linux, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/hello): Zig 0.15.2 ReleaseSmall 10,720 B (static), Zig ReleaseFast stripped 18,744 B, C gcc -O2 stripped 14,440 B (dynamic glibc), C musl static stripped 17,696 B, Rust 1.97.1 -O stripped 394,032 B (dynamic). Jet with #6106 C1 (per-function sections plus gc): 437,416 B with .text 387,880 B (IrTypes-2 measurement); dev before #6106 C1: 5,210,576 B. A hand-written static ELF hello is a few hundred bytes. The size comes from runtime code that startup and print reach (allocator, task and thread setup, panic and formatting machinery), not from the program.

Owner asked (2026-11-15) whether precompiled Core should serve only jet run, not jet build. Main's answer (operational), recorded here:

cards.title: FFI v3: build the ratified boundary design for calling and being called by almost any language
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-30: a terse but thoroughly engineered, robust proposal for a theoretically perfect FFI that beats every existing one, designed greenfield with no Jet limitations, then judged for adoption into Jet. It must follow the composition principle: a complete primitives layer that can express everything, plus high-quality wrappers for the common cases.

**The proposal:** Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-30.md (commit e99e795e4c). Section 9 maps every idea onto Jet; three owner ballots follow from it: D-FFI-PRIMS1 (public primitives layer), D-FFI-ISOLATE1 (isolation as a placement option) and D-FFI-EXPORT2 (rich exports).

## Plain summary

- **The idea.** Every foreign boundary is described once, as a *boundary
  contract*. That is a typed list of functions and types, plus the facts a C
  header cannot say: who owns memory, how long a view lives, how errors come
  back, which thread may call, and whether a call is async.
- **Readers and writers.** A reader package builds the contract from whatever
  the other side has (a C header, a Rust crate, a `.d.ts`, a WIT file, a JVM
  class, Windows metadata, a GPU shader). A writer package turns the same
  contract into bindings for whoever calls *us*. Both directions share one
  model, so N languages cost N readers plus N writers, not N×N bridges.
- **Two layers.** A small, complete, unsafe *primitives* layer can express
  every boundary: layout, symbols, calls, memory, callbacks, errors, threads,
  async, isolation. Pareto *wrappers* sit on top: `use "png.h" as png`,
  `#Export`, and typed imports for Rust, Python and JS. Every wrapper
  expands into primitives that you can inspect, so the expert path is a ladder,
  not a cliff.
- **Safe by default.** A call is safe when its facts are checked, vouched for
  in a named `#Unsafe("reason")`, or *isolated*. Isolated means the same import
  runs in a wasm sandbox or a separate process, with no source changes.
- **Zero cost.** A crossing whose types already match costs one direct call.
  When the foreign source is visible, the optimizer can inline across the
  boundary.
- **For Jet.** Most of this is already ratified: header import, C source import,
  binder packages, ownership sigils at the border, vouches, both embedding
  artifacts, and the hardened profile. The new pieces are a public primitives
  layer, isolation as a placement option, and rich exports. Each is one ballot.
  Inline C stays, and becomes a thin wrapper over C-source import, which
  removes the "two ways to bring in C" loss that D-FFI-ONE1 recorded.

This builds on, and does not replace, the boundary audit
[`Docs/audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md`](../audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md)
(#2933), which covers project arrangements and workflows. This document is the
mechanism underneath them.

log.text: Split and closed 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. c2 met by decision (D-FFI-PRIMS1, D-FFI-PLACE1, D-FFI-EXPORT3 ratified). The design stays in Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-31.md. New cards: #6945 C ABI shapes, #6946 C boundary types, #6947 callbacks, #6948 foreign facts and C++, #6949 binding-cache resolver, #6950 language binders, #6951 Rust crates. Sandbox rows moved to #6930, WIT export to #6906, the PowerShell binder row to #6942. Known-failing rows that cited #6366 should cite these cards.

G5DevX-1 diagnosis, 2026-11-12 00:2x, b10: the *_bind cases fail with E1002 jet.ReservedRootShadowed on `use x: <lang>.<lib>` (for example lua_bind_runs_embedded_vm_and_recovers_after_hostile_calls: `ops: lua.ops`). The rule is jet_driver_check_reserved_import (Loader.jet:2956), whose .Module root check against JET_DRIVER_FIRST_PARTY_RESERVED exempts only c and cpp (jet_driver_is_foreign_provider_import, Loader.jet:2269). The case needs tool:lua, so it only SKIP-HOSTed until lua reached the devshell PATH. Lifting E1002 alone turns it into E0610, because no resolver maps an active ForeignLanguage import <lang>.<lib> to the generated .jet/bindings/<lang>/<lib>.jet under the importer's root. Planned languages (swift) stay E1002 per c3 and c4. That resolver is the root fix for c3 and c27 and for the KF rows at 72, 73, 103, 104, 292-304, 324 and 325.

cards.title: API design principle: strong composable primitives first, pareto wrappers on top, full use of variadics and named/positional arguments
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-30: wrappers solve some problems but often make everything outside their case harder. Jet's APIs need a very strong primitives layer that can express everything, then pareto-level high-quality wrappers for the common work. Jet's API tools (variadics, named and positional arguments, defaults) are barely used today and should be, to make APIs more powerful and more streamlined. This must become a fundamental design element of the project, with a review that checks the APIs follow it.

cards.title: Attach to a running program: the live inspector, span export and the dev console
cards.body:
Destination: a running Jet program can be attached to. `jet inspect live --attach PID` shows its task tree, channels, deadlines, effects, spans and allocations (D-OBSERVE-LIVE1=A, a viewer over the existing observability rails); spans export and replay with parent links; and the dev console attaches to the app's services, database resources and in-process router with read-only default authority, sandbox transactions and guards.

Why it matters: seeing a live program's state is the fastest way to find a stuck task or a bad request.

The tests/cases/live_inspect and event_observations rows in tests/known-failing.tsv belong to this card.

History: this card first collected every developer tool that did not build on the self-hosted toolchain (found by ToolsJet-2 while fixing #6346). On 2026-11-15 the other tools moved to their own cards: LSP #4917 and #6901-#6904, jet dev #5931, jet debug #6730, SemIndex #6630, flash #6905, embedding #6906, records #6907, Canvas #6618.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

Split 2026-11-15: this card keeps attach (console and live inspector, c1-c4, c125, c128-c131). Moved: flash to #6905, embedding to #6906, records to #6907, c85 to #6887, c86 c114 c118 to #5931, c87 to #6898, c112 c113 to #6630, c117 to #6730, c127 to #6618; c126 merged into #6889 c6.

When this card builds the behavior, it registers the code again with its emitter, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot. cards.title: Build `reject(Diagnostic)` (D-MARKER-DIAG1=A): library compile-time checks raise their own error codes
cards.body: Found by #6385 on dev 59213de00f. D-MARKER-DIAG1=A ratified that a library error is a struct implementing Core's Diagnostic trait (what/why/fix as one-literal methods) and that `reject(err)` raises it while compiling, from a marker's expand or a helper. `reject` is not built: probes/zig/z05_reject.jet reports `E0102 Nothing named 'reject' exists here`. Today a comptime check can only `panic`, which gives E3010 with a message but no code, why, fix or `jet explain` page. This is Jet's version of Zig's @compileError, done better.

cards.title: core.compute port: devices, streams, sparse tensors and transfer receipts need storage in the registered compute vocabulary
cards.body: The R1 port of core.compute to Jet source (Core/Compute/Compute.jet) cannot express on_device and transfer to non-CPU placements, transfer_show, streams, sparse CSR, VJPRun or deserialize receipts. The registered types have no storage for them (core-library.md:4289-4291 makes the registered vocabulary their only owner). ComputeDevice, ComputeStream and SparseTensor are opaque to users today (E0119 on a literal, E0302 on field access), so their storage is added as private core_only field rows. Tensor is a 5-field literal that users can read and assign today (a.requested = "Metal" changes compute.placement), so where its reason and transfer receipts live is the owner ballot D-COMPUTE-TENSOR-STORE1 on this card.
