cards.title: Native code faults (SIGSEGV at 0x0) seeking a handle bound by '&executables[i].file == .Val(input)' in store_reuse_executable_lease_members
cards.body: Repro (Linux, admitted compiler 657d0c5553 and HEAD 83c4c6521b runtime alike): assemble the Engine unit (JETPACK_BOOTSTRAP_AREAS=$(node Jetpack/Bootstrap/areas.mjs closure Engine) JETPACK_BOOTSTRAP_OWN_AREA=Engine node Jetpack/Bootstrap/assemble.mjs aot), then in its project run: jet test src/jetpack.jet "realize verified round trips". The claim 'store broker realize verified round trips through broker and fails closed on auth' (Jetpack/Store/Tests/Broker.jet) FAILs with Fault [SIGSEGV] invalid memory access at address 0x0; backtrace compiler_fs_error <- store_reuse_executable_lease_members (Jetpack/Store/Source, line '&input.seek(0)' after 'if &executables[index].file == .Val(input)') <- store_reuse_build_lease <- store_snapshot_lease_unlocked <- store_snapshot_lease <- store_realize_verified. Safe code must never fault (I1): either the borrowed-pattern binding of an Option field through an indexed borrow lowers a null handle, or the File handle in SnapshotFile is dropped early. The claim is not listed in Tools/testkit/known-failing.tsv. Found by Main while proving #6426.

log.text: QuickLead receipt, 2026-11-08 (seed a0_038, source dev 759775d626): the Engine-unit claim passes on every tier. Steps: Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet areas closure Engine; Assemble.jet aot (560 sources, 559 claims, no E1271); then jet test --optimize=none,basic,full src/jetpack.jet "realize verified round trips" gives 1 passed, 0 failed at each of none, basic and full. The minimal repro is the b75e525782 case borrowed_list_of_optional_handles. Main reruns this exact proof before meeting c1.

b75e525782 repro half: cases --filter borrowed_list_of_optional_handles PASS 1/1 (seed-built d405d4cb6c + 8405a508b0). The Engine-unit claim (store broker realize verified round trips) still waits on a locked jetpack source (E1271).

a0_034: minimal repro of the faulting pattern (a [SnapshotFile] with FileReader? handles passed by value to a loop, then twice through '&executables[i].file == .Val(input)' seek+read) prints names 3 / bytes 12 / again 12 on O0, O1 and O2: no fault, handles stay open. The Engine-unit claim still needs its jetpack env run.

Likely root: #6677. The faulting statement compares '&executables[index].file == .Val(input)': it widens the borrowed FileReader into an Option union, and before 060bbcd0f1 and 8ac163916e the widened value was moved and dropped, which closes the caller's handle (the 'corrupt after' bisect). Re-run the claim with a0_034, the first seed carrying both fixes, before any other work on this card.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Bisect (assembled Engine unit, s1 of 60324f013d, scratch edits to the assembled copy only): the SnapshotFile FileReader is valid (stat ok) before store_reuse_create_exec_wrappers and corrupt after it; the corrupt handle sends seek/stat into compiler_fs_error, which faults at 0x0. The general FS error path works in the same unit (open of a missing path reports NotFound). A probe placed right after 'ready :: store_reuse_keeper_line(&child)' faults, a probe after the spawn hides the fault, and probes at every step hide it (claim passes). --checked-alloc also hides it (passes). So the damage happens in or around the first keeper_line call (loop line in child.stdout.lines() -> return line: early return out of a shared process-lines iterator, IterSources.jet iter_source_node shared clone/release) and is heap-layout dependent. A standalone repro of that pattern (spawn sh, keeper_line twice, stat a FileReader between) runs clean on jet run. Next: build that standalone with --checked-alloc and run to main return (sweep catches write-after-free), then shrink inside keeper_line. Parked for the owner's marker work.

criteria.text: The Engine-unit claim 'store broker realize verified round trips through broker and fails closed on auth' passes on the assembled Engine unit at O0, O1 and O2, and a minimal repro of the faulting pattern passes too. The Jetpack Foundation tests pass with no failures and no SIGSEGV at NetFetchError.jet:179. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Foundation`. (was #3590 c48)

cards.title: Leak freedom is structural: safe Jet cannot leak
cards.body: Owner rule, 2026-11-05: Jet never leaks memory. Leak freedom is part of the memory-safety guarantee (I1); only an expert #Unsafe block may leak, so the language must structurally prevent leaks rather than fix them case by case. On 2026-11-05 three lowering families leaked in safe code (c8a 5037b3ce72: a reassign after a move; c8b 2d712dd94a: a field read off a fresh call result; c8c: a loop over or an index into a fresh List or Map), found only because jet repl grew 6.2 GB over 9 turns. This card makes such a defect impossible to ship: the compiler checks its own output, and the suites fail any program that leaks.
cards.plan: 1. An ownership verifier pass after IR lowering. 2. A leak gate in the golden and cases suites, plus the compiler itself, using the checked allocator. 3. Fix every leak the two find, by lowering family. 4. An audit of every construct that could leak in safe code (shared values and cycles, tasks parked at exit, channels, globals, closures) with a structural rule for each, or an owner ballot where the rule is a language choice. 5. I1 in AGENTS.md states leak freedom.

log.text: Golden leak-gate census, 2026-11-05 on dev 02602250cc (s1 with the checked allocator; runtime process roots tagged; under --checked-alloc the runtime runs the entry's drops instead of the exit shortcut): about 1170 of the golden programs leak (o0 1164, o1 1162, o2 1161 rows; about 100 more rows leak on only some tiers). On o0, 610 rows leak only runtime init roots (jet_rt_*_init, TLS keys), so the runtime frees or tags those at shutdown; 507 have real library or user leaks. Leak-gate rows: 3492 of 4715. Starting point for c2 and c3 when G19 is worked.

c3 progress (invariant fixes), f2ba7d34bf: the fresh-temporary-never-dropped family. loop x in make(), make()[i], make_map()[k], every non-mutating Map/Set builtin on a fresh receiver, and Set.from(make()) (buffer) now end the temporary. Before: 100-520 MB VmRSS per 40,000 rounds per shape on O0 and O2. Three new cases FAIL->PASS, one guard case PASS on both; every shape clean under --checked-alloc on O0 and O2; chain FIXED_POINT; golden A/B 267 = 267; cases A/B over 284 ids. Probe audit of the flat shapes (match, if pattern, struct method, String chains, ?. and ??, slices, tuple fields) is in the guard case.

criteria.text: After IR lowering, a verifier checks that every owned value, temporaries included, is dropped or moved exactly once on every path out of its scope, outside #Unsafe. It runs on every compile at O0, O1 and O2; a violation is an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a user diagnostic. A negative-control case shows it catching each of the 2026-11-05 leak shapes when the matching fix is reverted.

The golden and cases suites run their programs with the checked allocator and fail any row whose program exits with a live owned block allocated outside #Unsafe, at o0, o1 and o2. The compiler itself passes the same check: jet check and jet build over Core and over the compiler's own sources end with zero leaked blocks, and 9 jet repl turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins stay flat. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden` and `--profile cases` with the leak gate on report zero leak rows at O0, O1 and O2, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Repl/repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins` stays flat over 9 turns.

Every leak the verifier or the leak gate finds is fixed at its root, per lowering family, each with a case per shape; the full suites then run with the leak gate on and show zero leak rows. Proof: with the leak gate on, `jet test Compiler --profile golden` and `--profile cases` report zero leak rows, and each fixed family has a `--filter leaks/` case.

An audit, committed under Docs/Audits, lists every construct that can keep memory alive in safe Jet (shared values and reference cycles, tasks or generators parked at exit, channels, globals and caches, closures and captures) and states the structural rule that prevents a leak for each, with a case; any rule that is a language choice goes to an owner ballot. Proof: the audit is committed under Docs/Audits, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Leaks/structural_rule_` has a case per construct.
AGENTS.md I1 states that safe Jet cannot leak memory (only #Unsafe may), and Docs/spec/philosophy.md's memory-safety guarantee says the same.
criteria.evidence: 520bfbfa0f: AGENTS.md I1 says memory safety includes leak freedom: safe Jet cannot leak memory, and only code inside an #Unsafe block or function may. Docs/spec/philosophy.md design priority 1 says safe Jet cannot leak memory: every value it allocates is freed, and only #Unsafe code may leak.

criteria.text: jet repl does not keep every turn's compile in memory (Repl.jet:338-348 held 773 MiB at 1 turn and 5.6 GiB at 9 on 2026-11-04). Memory per turn stays flat: 9 turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins stay under 1 GiB (also #6543).

A run-time leak and double-drop witness proves leak freedom per program. On 2026-11-12, JET_MEMORY_LEDGER recorded only unsafe sentry events, and the counting allocator cap did not trip on String allocations (a 32 MB copy ran under a 48 MB cap, #6677). A safe-Jet program run under the witness reports 0 live allocations at exit and fails on any double drop, on O0, O1 and O2. jet test and jet dev print the same witness (live allocations, unreleased foreign handles and Shared cycles, with their sites), and release builds carry no tracking.

D-EXIT-TASKS1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). When run returns, the runtime cancels every live task, with no OBSERVE_TASK_CAP limit, and drains until none is queued, ready or running, or until 1 s of monotonic time has passed, then exits with run's status. A waiting task unwinds at its wait and runs its cleanup. E3013's exit report is retired (registry row, explainer and the runtime_e3013 ui snapshot, which becomes a case exiting 0), and the leak witness names each abandoned task. spec.md states the rule. Proof: cases for a waiting task that cleans up and a busy loop that is abandoned after 1 s, on O0, O1, O2.

D-RETAIN-BOUND1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). The no-leak promise covers memory nothing can reach; data a live global, cache or task still reaches is the program's own. jet audit retention (also jet inspect audit retention, with --json) lists every store that can grow without a bound: #Memo(bound: none) caches and module Shared globals holding growable data, both exact, and loops that never end by themselves and keep appending, marked "may grow". Each row gives place, kind, name and type. help, man, completions and cli.md list it. Proof: a golden on the ballot program showing exactly its 2 rows, a --json golden, and a program with only bounded stores printing no rows.

cards.title: Close rate: one source of truth per fact, structural checks, criteria sized to close
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-05: cards take too long to close; a well-designed codebase should take a change in one place. Measured on 2026-11-05: a compiler rebuild to fixed point takes about 5 minutes (147 s s1 + 132 s), and a lander batch averages 129 s over 111 batches, so build and landing are not the bottleneck. The causes are copies of one fact that drift (a diagnostic lives in the Prelude row, the generated DiagnosticRows, the coverage baseline, the snapshot, the explain page and spec prose: retiring two codes touched 10 files, and ui --coverage found 137 drift errors), checks that are found serially instead of structurally (three leak families found one at a time; 1170 leaking golden programs), unported Rust behavior that is porting work rather than edits (82 KF-UNPORTED ui rows over about 60 codes, 23 more Rust-only codes, 294 open G15 criteria), and criteria merged from old cards that each hold a whole feature.

cards.title: JSON event reader drains a document about 10x slower than parse
cards.body: Measured by GoldenRoots3 on dev aeeb2c479c (golden serde/json_selective, 1.05 MB document, --release): draining every event from the JSON reader takes 1.37 s against 80-123 ms for parse, and decode<Small> builds the whole Dyn tree before projecting (129 ms, 84 MB peak vs 67 MB for parse). cards.title: Every CLI flag must also be a setting: non-build commands (registry publish --force and others) have no settings home
cards.body: Standing owner order: every CLI flag is also a setting. The only flag↔setting table is JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (build profiles, fn build, pins), which only build, run and dev read. jet registry publish --force (CLICommands.jet:796; it also gates E1218 per #6600) and every other non-build command flag have no setting. First census every registered CLI flag against its setting home. Then ballot where non-build command settings live (e.g. package.jet publish: {…} vs a per-command settings table in jet settings), with same-program alternatives. Then build it, with one flag↔setting mechanism for all commands.

log.text: meet-6606 (seed-b8, dev cc09d22cb9, 29 lines PASS-only) credits c2 only. c1: the cases rows cover four families (keep-going, trace, opt-dump, fmt --check). c1 asks for a row per command family and a census of every registered flag; the full family list and a row for each are needed. c4: rows cover keep-going, trace and opt-dump. Still missing: the disable, verify and SSA-stress hooks, the GC trace, the phase counters and the memory ledger, plus proof that AGENTS.md, the skills and the repository tools use the flag rather than the variable. c6: the text and --json snapshots pass, but the redaction test (Controls.jet "a URL's user and password never show") wasn't among the lines, and the criterion's 'every registered variable that is set' needs a line without --command. Routed to ScriptAPI-2.

Edge the ballot did not cover: a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME. ScriptAPI-50 refused it, which broke roots-sh (parity 0/11 on b8) and cache_cli_status. Decision: jet ignores a relative value and falls back to the default, as the XDG Base Directory specification requires. ScriptAPI-62 makes that fix, with cases.

Criteria c3-c7 added on the owner's order (2026-11-10 ~21:00, G5): environment variables become one registry in code, every behavior control becomes a flag or setting first, transport moves to one channel, one listing command is added, and the D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot gates the public spellings. Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q24 A): one registry. Every CLI command flag row gets a key <command>.<flag>, readable from package.jet settings and the user settings file; precedence flag, then package, then user (the JET_BUILD_OPTIONS mechanism). Destructive flags are marked not persistable and setting one is refused with a registered diagnostic. ScriptLead builds it.

Census (c1 first half), Main 2026-11-07, dev eb47eb7277 on seed a0_034. Method: jet help for all 49 commands and every action of the group commands (117 help pages), parsing each flag a usage line or flag row lists. A flag counts as homed when its long name is a JET_BUILD_OPTIONS row (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet, 7 rows) and its command reads that table (build, run, dev). Result: 429 command-flag rows over 76 commands and actions. 21 are homed: build, run and dev each have 7 (backtrace, bounds, inline, libs, optimize, os, small). The other 408 rows (157 distinct flags) have none. The most common homeless flags are --json x52, --color x44, --quiet x44, --live x8, --verbose x7, --profile x6, --set x6, -p x6, --gate x5, --release x5, --target x5, --threads x5, --trace x5, --dry-run x5 and --allow x4. Rows per command: test 57, build 34, run 32, dev 26, inspect 26, new 17, cc 16, c++ 16, jobs 15, check 12, fmt 11, self 11, budget 9; registry has 7, including publish --force and --no-sign. Flags with a neighbouring but non-flag-keyed home (--allow/--deny to package authority, --target to package targets, --profile to build profiles) count as homeless, because none goes through one flag-to-setting mechanism. The census is regenerated on demand by $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/flags/{collect.sh,census.mjs} (scratch; the porting home is the CLI registry, not a committed table). Next: the ballot on where non-build command settings live, then one shared mechanism.

criteria.text: A census lists every registered CLI flag with its setting (or none); after the ratified ballot, every flag has exactly one setting through one shared flag-to-setting mechanism, with a cases row per command family proving that flag and setting have the same effect Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLISettings/flag_equals_setting_`, one row per command family.

Authority flags (--allow, -A, --gate, --token, --allow-unofficial) have no setting: the census marks them never persisted, and a package.jet or user settings key for one is refused with a registered diagnostic (owner 2026-11-09); a cases row proves the refusal.
criteria.evidence: Lander meet-6606 on seed-b8 at dev cc09d22cb9, each line judged PASS-only with its source printed. Line 8: tests/cases/cli_settings/permission_flags_are_never_settings.case, landed in fe4c65249b (ScriptAPI-66), shows that a package.jet commands block or the user settings file naming --allow, -A, --gate, --token or --allow-unofficial is refused with the registered E2117 before the program starts. Lines 19-20: the CommandSettings.jet census tests "no flag that gives permissions is a setting" and "a remembered destructive flag is refused as its CLI snapshot records" (ScriptAPI-49/50, 5263e2258c) mark them never persisted. D-ENV-SURFACE1 was ratified A on 2026-11-11.

criteria.text: Owner 2026-11-10 ~21:00: "seems like we rely heavily on env vars ... other languages just use build settings and build flags, not a ton of hidden envvars ... yes we need to fix that". Main's census on dev c2cecce162: code reads about 140 JET_/JETPACK_ variables (193 names in all), and Docs/Spec/Reference/environment.md, which calls itself the registry, lists 66 plus 3 wildcard families; 113 read names are on no list. One registry in code holds every environment variable that jet, jetpack, the runtime, Core or a repository tool reads. Each row gives the name, the owning module, its kind (user, automation, maintainer, transport between Jet processes, or test hook), its value type and default, and the flag or setting it overrides. A guard refuses a read of a name that has no row, across Compiler, Core, Jetpack and Tools. environment.md is generated from the registry, with a --check that the lane checks run. Zero unregistered reads. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter env_registry_covers_every_read`, and the environment.md generator's `--check` passes.

Every user, automation or maintainer behavior control is a CLI flag or a settings key first, and its environment variable only overrides that setting, through the shared flag-to-setting mechanism of c1. The controls include keep-going and its report and skip lists, trace file and trace detail, the optimizer dump, disable, verify and SSA-stress hooks, the GC trace, phase counters and the memory ledger. AGENTS.md, the skills and the repository tools use the flag, not the variable. A cases row per family proves the flag, the setting and the variable have the same effect. D-ENV-SURFACE1=A (ratified 2026-11-11): concise descriptive flags and the existing command-qualified setting names.

Transport between Jet-owned processes goes through one channel: argv, or one handoff file or descriptor that the parent passes to the child. It does not go through a separate environment name per value. The JET_FRONT_*, JET_DEVELOPMENT_RECEIPT_*, JET_DEVTOOLS_RELAY_*, JET_PROVE_*, JET_EVIDENCE_*, JET_TEST_SUITE_ROOT, JET_TEST_PLAN, JET_TEST_SETTINGS and JET_READ_SCOPE families are cut over in one greenfield cutover, with no old names kept. A launched user program inherits no Jet transport variable it does not own (a run case proves its environment). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Run/launched_program_inherits_no_jet_transport_vars`, and git grep finds none of the listed families in Compiler, Core or Jetpack.

D-ENV-SURFACE1=A: the env command group gains a pure vars listing, not a new environment manager. It prints every registered variable that is set, with its effective value and where that value came from (environment, setting, flag or default), redacts secret values, and has text and --json forms with UI snapshots, like `go env`.

The D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot is written and validated (Tools/agent/ballots/Validate.jet). It shows same-program alternatives for the c4 flag and setting spellings and for the c6 listing command, with beginner and expert paths, a comparison with Go (go env, go env -w), Cargo (config.toml mirrors CARGO_*), Zig and Python (-X flags), and an adversarial review of the recommended option. The owner ratifies it before c4 and c6 are built.

cards.title: Test suites run in seconds: fix the slow programs, the timeouts and the per-program cost
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-06: suites should finish in seconds or minutes, not take a long time; the golden suite once took about 15 minutes at most.

Measured on vb5 (dev 7f0b3d03ed, s1, 32 cores):
- golden: 4766 rows, about 4 minutes wall, median 0.28 s per row. The 4655 rows under 5 s alone sum to 74 CPU minutes, so per-program cost sets a floor of about 2.3 minutes even with perfect parallelism.
- cases: 4501 rows, about 13.5 minutes wall, median 0.10 s; 284 rows of 5 s or more account for 97 of 131 CPU minutes; 12 rows hit the 60 s wall-clock limit.
- ui: 2412 rows, about 1 minute wall.

Slowest golden programs (all tiers): concurrency/job_queue 248 s, foundations/storage 177 s, foundations/text 161 s, crypto/file_seal_jetc 153 s, game/raylib_indexed 148 s, foundations/realtime 100 s.
Timeouts: cffi/concurrent_bridges_share_one_target_publish_without_racing, cffi/ffi_capability_boundary_is_safe_only_inside_unsafe, ffi_rust/rust_extern_std_round_trip_uses_the_canonical_descriptor, fixtures_crypto_bridge_entropy/jetc_v2_record_boundaries_are_canonical, fmt_project/top_level_jet_fmt_delegates_non_jet_file_to_realized_formatter, jetpack_nix_index/index_backed_nixpkgs_repairs_only_missing_transitive_object, jetpack_nix_index/static_publication_resolves_signed_index_and_nix_objects, jetpack_tool/use_ephemeral_execs_inside_and_outside_project_without_path_projection, repl/repl_tty_prompts_and_reuses_exact_session_tuple, ui_fixes/ownership_ui_fixes_compile_ffi_companions, unsafe_and_runtime/ffi_capability_edge_uses_shared_sentry_prelude, web_dev/embedded_devserver_rejects_hardlinked_source.

For every slow row, first record where the time goes (compile front end, Core/Prelude re-check, code generation per tier, link, the program's own run, or a fixed sleep or timeout in the test), then fix that root. Never raise a limit, drop a tier or move a row out of the default profile to make a number.

log.text: Moved from G1 to G5 by owner ruling 2026-11-07. a0_033 release kit timings (parallel, under load): golden 1479 programs, median 528 ms, 420 at 5 s or more, rows sum 5037 s; cases 4637, median 156 ms, 524 at 5 s or more, sum 8201 s; ui 2252, median 66 ms, 9 at 5 s or more, sum 939 s. c4's shared per-run Core check is compiler work, the same as #6623 and #6647.

c4 progress: MechD-3's 59d955887b (store capacity checks replay a footprint tally instead of scanning every entry) cut golden wall from 1086 s to 118.7 s on fab74a230c s1, all rows passing (4318 PASS, 0 FAIL). The per-program median is 348 ms over 3 tiers, about 0.12 s per tier, against the 0.1 s target. About 90% of each tier is re-checking Core identically for every program; caching checked Core by content key is the remaining c4 lever, and df runs about 6 times per build. c5 still needs a run on the batch machine (118.7 s against the 90 s target).

criteria.text: Each of the six slow golden programs (concurrency/job_queue, foundations/storage, foundations/text, crypto/file_seal_jetc, game/raylib_indexed, foundations/realtime, or their successors after the Examples cutover) runs in under 5 s per tier on the batch machine, with the root cause of its old time recorded on this card. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Each program>` timings in the testkit report.
The 12 cases rows that hit the 60 s wall-clock limit on vb5 are root-caused and each passes, or fails for a recorded unrelated reason, in under 10 s.
criteria.evidence: 85dea10ff4 (TestSystemLead-2). The 12 vb5 60 s rows, rerun at HEAD (release jetpack aaa6331fc067, cargo and bwrap on PATH). Root causes, from reproducing each on 7f0b3d03ed: cffi/concurrent_bridges was a jet check futex deadlock (PASS 3.0 s); ffi_rust/rust_extern_std was an ICE 101 (PASS 2.7 s); fixtures_crypto_bridge_entropy/jetc_v2 was an fsync stall in jbd2 on loaded ext4 scratch (PASS 3.1 s); fmt_project/top_level_jet_fmt was the old jetpack hanging in env -- nixfmt (PASS 0.26 s); jetpack_nix_index static_publication and index_backed_repairs were the old jetpack hanging in env --prep (PASS 4.4 s and 9.5 s); web_dev/embedded_devserver_rejects_hardlinked_source was jet dev watching until the limit (now KNOWN-FAILING #6386, 2.2 s). cffi/ffi_capability_boundary (1.4 s), unsafe_and_runtime/ffi_capability_edge (0.3 s) and ui_fixes/ownership_ui_fixes_compile_ffi_companions (2.6 s) pass; the first two now declare requires tool:cargo/rustc and report SKIP-HOST without cargo. jetpack_tool/use_ephemeral is KNOWN-FAILING #3594 (8.0 s); repl_tty_prompts is KNOWN-FAILING #5949 with its limit lowered to 6 s (6.1 s). Row lists: lanes/TestSystemLead/kf82.txt, kf84.txt, kf85.txt.

criteria.text: Every cases row that took 5 s or more on vb5 (284 rows) runs in under 5 s, or this card records why its work is inherently longer (for example a real network or Nix fetch) and that row moves to a named opt-in profile that the default run does not include. Proof: the testkit report timing table for the cases suite.

Per-program cost: a profile of a typical golden row splits its time into Core and Prelude checking, the program's own front end, code generation per tier, link and run. Any work repeated identically for every program (for example re-checking Core) is done once per suite run and shared, and the median golden row drops to 0.1 s or less. Proof: a committed per-phase profile of a typical golden row and the testkit report median.
On the batch machine the golden suite finishes in under 90 s wall, the cases suite in under 3 minutes and the ui suite in under 30 s, measured on the same commit and recorded with the commit.
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6610 c14: c14 holds the tighter owner budget of 2026-11-04 (about 60 s for all three suites)

criteria.text: The two step timeouts set for #6651 c2 are removed and both rows pass on the default 60 s step limit under full-kit load: Tests/Cases/CompiledWorkloads/compiled_workload_gate_self_check.case (19 s alone; warm 11.6 s splits into contract 2.2 s, synthetic report 2.1 s, 33 check_report calls with about 63 ms of start-up each, then tier, peer, sample and tier-receipt checks) and Tests/Cases/ComptimeSequenceParity/repl_list_and_fixed_list_sequence_methods_are_exact.case (50 REPL turns at about 0.4 s each). Proof: both rows pass in `jet test Compiler --profile cases` with no step timeout in their .case files.

The packages suite on a fresh clone finishes in under 5 minutes wall: the hosted Jetpack engine build overlaps the package runs (2a5ad087af), and the engine unit's claims, which run serially because they share process state, run in under 1 minute. Proof: a timed `jet test Compiler --profile packages` on a fresh clone, committed as a receipt.

Every corpus suite (golden, cases, ui, packages) runs as wide as the machine's cores and memory allow, with no fixed job cap below that. Proof: the job count logged by `jet test Compiler --profile golden` on the batch machine equals its cores-and-memory bound.

Excluding the toolchain fetch, jet test Compiler --profile full on a fresh clone finishes in under 10 minutes on the batch machine. A per-phase timeline is recorded with the commit. Proof: a committed per-phase timeline of the fresh-clone run.
The cold toolchain fetch inside that run (#6592) takes 30 s or less, so the whole fresh-clone run finishes in under 11 minutes. Proof: the fetch phase in the same timeline.

The fresh-clone full profile's startup (building the test runner and assembling before the first suite row; about 4 minutes on 2026-11-07) is measured by phase and cut to under 30 s. Proof: the startup phases in the same timeline.

Mutation testing on by default (#6060): The stock jet test run with mutate: changed and generated rows on stays fast enough to be on by default: a paired cell in the perf manifest compares the default jet test rerun against the matched peers (cargo-mutants plus cargo-fuzz, Go's test cache plus go test -fuzz) under the performance gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry mutation-default` shows no loss.
The closed-list guard (#6206) runs in under 5 s (4.2 s measured for the census). Proof: the timed `jet test Tests/Guards --filter closed_lists`.

Owner 2026-11-04: tests take seconds, a minute at most for a few thousand, and never run out of memory unless something leaks. The full ui, golden and cases suites finish in at most about 60 s of wall time on the dev machine, and no test job is killed for memory (today suite.sh gives each job 3 GiB, allows a 6800 s timeout, and cases runs were OOM-killed on 2026-11-04, while hello costs about 180 ms CPU and 15-19 MB). Proof: a testkit report with a per-test wall-time and peak-RSS table for every suite, and a timed full run that meets the budget, committed with the commit.

Running one test costs about that test's own time: the testkit's fixed startup is listed phase by phase (kit build or load, harness compile, corpus scan, Core load, worker start), and a run filtered to one golden entry at --jobs 1 finishes within 0.5 s of that entry's own compile-and-run time (today about 35 s of fixed overhead). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter One entry> --jobs 1` timed against that entry's own `jet run`, in a committed receipt.

Jet's test runner is the fastest of any language: a peer-matched cell runs the same corpus (a few thousand small unit tests plus whole-program goldens) in Jet, Rust (cargo test and nextest), Go, Zig, TypeScript (Bun test and Vitest) and Python (pytest), measuring cold full run, warm full run and edit-one-test-and-rerun in wall time and peak memory, with Jet/peer below 1.00 for every peer and metric. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry test-runner` shows no in-group loss.

Compiler/JetDriver/Tests checks and its tests run in lane-check (on dev 8219108260 CLISeams.jet, RustForeign.jet and SchemaIngress.jet did not compile), so a driver test cannot rot unseen. Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetDriver` passes and lane-check lists it. (was #6637 c21)

cards.title: Tool symbol paths use `.`, not `::`: inspect, find, semindex, docs and the impact selector
cards.body:
Owner 2026-11-06 chose A: with `::` gone from source (D-DECL-COLON1=A, #6586), tool symbol paths switch from `module::name` to `.`, matching source qualification such as `alias.Type.method`. This changes the public JSON and text output of jet inspect, jet find, the semantic index and jet docs, and the user-typed selector of `jet inspect impact <file> <symbol>`. Greenfield cutover: no `::` reader stays behind.

Sites found by the syntax owner at c92bf872eb:
- User-typed: the jet inspect impact selector (Inspect.jet:1580).
- User-visible JSON or text: semindex identity, summary and call_path keys (SemIndexBuild.jet 149/1481/1526/1530/2151, Sema SemanticIndex.jet:422, InspectOutput.jet:32; the case semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects expects `inferred_effect_signature::announce`); inspect rights keys (InspectRights.jet 142/168/173); inspect shapes (InspectShapes.jet:422); find (Find.jet:308); docs `parent::name` (Docs.jet:279); codemod and try identities (Codemod.jet:1371, Try.jet:242).
- Internal parsing: ArchitectureAdvice.jet:47, Fill.jet:80, SemIndexBuild.jet:1797, and the ComptimeIR.jet:103 and Pipeline.jet:2712 cache keys.
- Real Rust paths in RustForeign.jet:210-232 are foreign syntax and stay.

Module paths contain dots (`core.process`), so a tool must know where the module path ends. The tools have the module graph, so a reader resolves the longest prefix that names a module, and the rest is the member path. Writers emit the same form.

log.text: c3 held (Main, 2026-11-13). x6612 on the gate-p25 jet over dev c01ff2ad91: semindex/ 31/0 + 9 KF, docs 5/0 + 4 KF, codemod 22/0. inspect has 8 FAIL, find 2 FAIL and try 21 FAIL. Most are unrelated rows that the substring filters catch (jetpack_*, pkg, image, env_dev_trust). Two rows that name a symbol still fail, build_entry/inspect_choices_shows_each_inlined_call_and_why and concurrency_boundaries/inspect_choices_shows_storage_form_and_its_lock ("expected storage form, got inlining"), so c3 is not met until they pass or are shown not to be affected. Full list: Lander5 report, 2026-11-13 21:xx.
Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat, second cut questions): c1 stands as written: every `::` in Compiler/ goes, internal keys included (~3,800 sites), not just the tool-visible paths.

criteria.text: Every tool output and selector listed in the body writes and reads symbol paths with `.` (for example `inferred_effect_signature.announce`), with no `::` writer, reader or fallback left except real Rust paths in RustForeign.jet; a repo search for `::` in Compiler/ outside Rust-foreign code and dated docs finds none. Proof: git grep for `::` in Compiler, outside RustForeign.jet and dated docs, finds nothing that writes or reads a symbol path.

Readers split a dotted path at the longest prefix that names a module in the program's module graph; a case proves `jet inspect impact <file> core.process.spawn`-style selectors and an ambiguous or unknown prefix gives a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Inspect/impact_dotted_selector` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter dotted_path_unknown_prefix`.

The affected cases, snapshots and goldens (semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects and every inspect, find, docs, codemod and try row that names a symbol) are updated in the same commit and pass on the default tier; the spec text that documents these outputs shows the `.` form. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects`, and the inspect, find, docs, codemod and try rows pass.
criteria.evidence: p238 batch compiler (dev 5bea729463), full collect-all suite: cases Semindex/semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects PASS; no inspect, find, docs, codemod or try row fails.

criteria.text: A guard case fails on any `::` in UI, golden or case expected output, and in a JetCli or JetSemIndex string literal; only foreign-language subjects such as C++ and Rust FFI snippets are exempt. Semindex definition identities, inspect's callable identity, live value ids and expand's static paths use dotted paths with one kind-prefix scheme.

cards.title: D-HOST-LEAF1=E: the runtime is an ordinary library that Core uses
cards.body: Owner ratified D-HOST-LEAF1 option E on 2026-11-06. jet_runtime becomes an ordinary library: Core and any package write use rt: jet.runtime.time and call rt.sleep_ns(duration.ns). No marker, no symbol string, no hand-written manifest. Internals stay hidden by pub. Amended by the adversarial review (Docs/audits/2026-11-06-d-host-leaf1-option-e-review.md): a declared effect row on a pub runtime function introduces its effects, and the interface is generated from source with the runtime pack. This card builds the runtime side. The #6151 criteria (c4-c41) and #6111 c1/c2 that waited on the host-leaf ballot are unblocked by E and stay on their cards: they remove Core's privileges, which E's ordinary-library model makes possible.

log.text: Closed by Main: every criterion is met with recorded evidence (landed commits and audits), and moved criteria live on their owning cards.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c10 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.
Cleaned: the TLS host reads (c12, c14, c15) moved to #6861; c16-c17 restated as the freestanding execution proofs #2300 left; c18 merged into c17.

Main decisions 2026-11-11 (TlsLead-3's open items): (1) the row_splits rows in RuntimeEffectRows (jet_time_raw_wall_sample via ssl_time, jet_random_os_entropy, jet_files_read_bytes_os, jet_fs_directory_open/close) stay until the owner ballot on whether a protocol root (Net) covers its host reads (Time, Rand, FS.Read); if it does not, the TLS entries declare the full rows in one cutover. (2) The F32 bit pair (core.math.__to_bits_f32/__from_bits_f32) has no runtime carrier: it is an IR-lowered pure intrinsic like sqrt, exempt here, pinned by a signaling-NaN round-trip case at O0/O1/O2. (3) tls.client is one declaration (tcp, server_name, config?, deadline?) -[Net, Time.Wait]> TLSStream NetError!; the host/port form and the sema arity/type dispatch are removed, and callers use tls.connect_host. (4) The 402 E3203 NonCAbiType errors come from seeds that predate the carrier commits (1e02b82ef1, 3bf0e43440, 8ff2c54775). No gate depends on them; the chain's last SUB checks the runtime binding package on the first batch compiler after it lands.

Ballot candidate (owner choice, not built): TLS certificate-validity checks read the wall clock (ssl_time via tls.__host_wall_sample). Today Net covers that read by a deliberate rule (Core/Net/SSL/Defs.jet:1501). Surfacing it as Time would add Time to about 60 SSL functions, the 10 Net callback fn types (Defs.jet:1054-1125), every Tls.jet engine fn and the public tls client/read/write/ready, http client/serve and ws upgrade rows (TlsLead3 cascade census, 2026-11-11). For #6615 the runtime binding declares Net under that rule, as an explicit exception row in RuntimeEffectRows. The open UI case: paint_state through a backend trait method needs Browser on the web backend only (effect-polymorphic trait methods); it keeps its route until decided.

Ballot NEW-D-HOST-CAP1 withdrawn 2026-11-11 after an adversarial rewrite (owner order: confusing or parallel ballots are redone, and questions an existing mechanism answers are decided rather than balloted). Decided: Preserve the existing UI needs contract in the checked runtime interface and propagate it through resolved calls; generate vocabulary from UICapability, not deleted call rows. It extends: origin/dev:Core/Ui/Host.jet:22-30 is the UI capability vocabulary. origin/dev:Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CoreUsage.jet:445-480 checks declared needs; origin/dev:Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Loader.jet:256-260 currently derives valid names from Core call rows. D-HOST-LEAF1=E requires ordinary runtime library declarations and their checked interface. The full record is $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots-v4/NEW-D-HOST-CAP1/verdict.md. Withdrawal decides the direction; it does not mean the build is done.

t22 landed (dev 5dc51a93f5): TlsLead-6615s4be (47d0ff8ba6, the text-cell and ETF-string decode scopes on jet.runtime.encoding) and TlsLead-6615s4bl (b48dfee798, core.log on jet.runtime.log, 15 bound leaves deleted). This is slice S4b of c5. CoreSourceRows and RuntimeEffectRows --check pass (0 differences), with no new case or core failures. c5 stays open for the remaining rows (c5a is staged).

t21 landed on dev 4a9268e62c (83b33f14dc..4a9268e62c): TlsLead-6615s3a/s3afix (jet.runtime.time binds all 13 raw time exports core.time calls, identity-keyed, so a user lookalike stays a C import with E3101/E3203/E1341), s4ar/s4arfix (48 handle-free term/log/encoding/process leaves bound with Option-of-tuple and tuple-of-Option carriers; the unchecked string_byte/bytes_into_text and coerce_now/coerce_emit stay Core-only behind E0510 until S7), s4bp (the dead core.process __signal_* leaves, records, dispatcher rows and IRRoute rows deleted, so jet.runtime.process is the only path) and s4bpfix (the unknown_module snapshot lists the 5 runtime modules). RuntimeEffectRows joins 59/59. Every test line passes after a clean census. c4 and c5 stay open: TlsLead3 census finds most S5-S8 leaves need Result/struct carriers (S11, go) or a Core-only visibility (ballot facts pending if no ordinary mechanism fits).

t19 landed TlsLead-6615c4 (0efcf91a49..97462b6d92), the c4 mechanism. A jet.runtime call lowers to the runtime export its interface row names at O0/O1/O2 and in a built binary, and Tools/agent/RuntimeEffectRows.jet --check (in VerifyFull) joins each interface function to its Core leaf by name with 0 differences. c4 stays open until every runtime function Core calls is bound this way (S3 onward).

Main ruling 2026-11-10 on S3, the time cutover (TlsLead3). Under D1 (the carrier projection ABI), each jet.runtime.<module> member is a body-less binding onto the runtime export that holds its one body. The binding is generated from the runtime export rows (the c3 interface), never hand-written, and lowered through a route derived from its Jet signature, so the hand IRRoute rows go. Sema admits carrier types (Option, tuple, List) only for bindings of the generated interface, keyed on its identity, not on a module name; a user `jet.runtime.*` module gets the ordinary C-law errors. The raw exports stay as each function's one far-side body, so they are not a twin, and c8 deletes the dispatcher rows and the compiler twin, not these exports.

Main rulings on the c3-c5 slice plan (TlsLead3, 16 slices, written up in its lane as 6615-plan.md). D1: a jet.runtime call uses the carrier projection of its Jet signature, computed on both sides from the one signature; no exported internal ABI. D2: `jet.runtime.<module>` is the spelling these criteria already name. `jet` is a compiler-provided namespace beside `core` and holds only `runtime`, with no other members. D3: c5 lands one module at a time (S3-S14). A module moves whole, with no dual path inside it, and its dispatcher rows, CoreCallRows, IRRoute rows and RuntimeStopExports go in the same SUB. c5 is met only when the last module lands and a census shows 0 dispatcher_row lines. Finding: c38-c40 on #6151 (core.build) are compiler comptime, not runtime, so jet.runtime does not unblock them.

t15a landed G6LeadC-11 (01b86931e7..8327f5ae47): c6 clause 2 (an ungated #Import(c) of a runtime export is E3101, UI snapshot runtime_import_needs_unsafe; a gated one works) and c7's interim clause (architecture.md limits the one-runtime claim to O0/O1/O2 and names the web tier's JavaScript runtime functions). c6 stays open for clause 1, and c7 for the web runtime itself.

Defect found by TestSystemLead-2 at 56e30acfcf: an #Import(c) call to the runtime symbol jet_rt_process_exit lowers into jet_rt_unreachable. The program prints 'internal error: entered unreachable code:' and exits 101 whatever code it passed. Repro: a 10-line program that imports raw_exit: fn(code: I64) = "jet_rt_process_exit" and calls it. Sites hit: Compiler Host.jet:1563 jet_cli_defect_exit, the JetTestKit fixture compiler.jet, and Compiler/JetTestKit/Assets/no_nix.jet. It belongs to c6 (reaching a runtime C symbol through #Import(c)): the imported call must exit with its argument and print nothing.

cards.title: Verify batches see self-compile miscompiles before a release does
cards.body: a0_030 (e32b979063) failed its release gate on an I2 regression that only the release's s2/s3 show: an ICE exits 1 instead of 101. Root (CoreCliLead): b4e29635ce made the runtime map a user program's process.exit(101) to status 1 (101 is reserved for ICEs). The compiler exits through the same Core call, so a jet linked with a pack built from post-b4e2 runtime source (s2/s3 link pack1) loses its 101. s1 links the seed's (a0_029) pack and still exits 101. Main's vb batches build and test s1 only, so every runtime change reaches the compiler's own behaviour unseen until the release run (33 minutes here). Fix the batch so a cheap probe runs on every batch: a jet linked with the batch's own runtime pack, on the rows most exposed to runtime changes in the compiler (ICE exit codes, process exit codes). Don't add a full s2 suite to each batch.

log.text: 2026-11-06 a0_030 retry on 2edea7b26a: census-snap preflight passed (rc=0) but the chain's s2 stopped with 19 jet.MissingMoveMarker errors in Core/Http, Core/Net/Tls and Core/Web. The rule came from c78da98b1b (#6611, calls never copy); the preflight and LaneCheck both check with the a0_029 seed, which lacks that rule, so a sema change that tightens Core is invisible until s2. Gap: the preflight needs a candidate pass (build s1, then a keep-going s1 check of Compiler, Core and Jetpack) before a release launches.

criteria.text: `jet Tools/Agent/Land.jet batch` builds an s2 from the batch's s1 (or reuses one at the same commit) and runs the backend_ice cases and a process-exit-code golden against it, failing the batch on any row that differs from s1. Proof: a committed batch receipt shows the s2 probe step and its row counts.

A Land.jet batch on a commit carrying a known self-compile difference (the a0_030 ICE exit at e32b979063) reports a batch failure naming the s1/s2 split. Proof: a committed receipt of `jet Tools/Agent/Land.jet batch` on that commit showing the failure.

cards.title: Canvas runs on the self-hosted toolchain: its scenarios restored, parser spans, the shared Core-call record and one edit-transaction seam
cards.body:
Destination: `jet dev --canvas` (Compiler/JetDevserver/Source/Canvas) runs on the self-hosted toolchain on solid foundations. The 88 browser scenarios deleted in the #6035 c3 cutover are back. Functions and spans come from the parser, Core names come from the shared Core-call record, and every edit crosses one transaction seam. Plain `jet dev` stays terminal-first (D-CANVAS-CMD1=A). State on dev 699e07d4c6 with gate-p141: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter canvas` gives 6 PASS, 6 KNOWN-FAILING and 3 SKIP-HOST. Scenario proof (used here and on the Canvas cards): `jet run --allow=Env,Exec,FS,IO,Net,Time Tools/canvas-test/Run.jet -- scenario --scenario --port

`, run against a running `jet dev --canvas`, prints PASS. The Canvas product moved out of #6418 and #6419 by owner ruling 2026-11-06. It runs inside JetDevserver, so it waits on #5931. Related cards (2026-11-15 split): workspace and session #6908, debugger #6909, graph edits #6910, source truth #6911, projection parity #6912, workbench UX #6913, previews #6914.

This card keeps the foundations: the 88-scenario restore (c66), parser spans (c63-c64), the Core-call record (c43-c44) and the edit-transaction seam (c55-c57).

cards.title: Reactive notebook: `jet notebook` reruns only affected cells, with typed controls, reconnect, attached outputs and diff-friendly .jetnb files
cards.body:
Destination: `jet notebook` runs a reactive kernel. Editing a cell reruns its pure descendants and marks effectful ones for confirmation (D-DX-CELLS1=A). Typed function arguments render as controls. A browser reconnects only with matching identity and authority. Outputs stay attached to their cells. A `.jetnb` file holds only source, so `git diff` shows one cell's change. The notebook runs and builds like a program, and a Jupyter kernel adapter exists.

The notebook rows in tests/known-failing.tsv are on #6418 (unbuilt `jet notebook`, E2104).

Moved out of #6418 by owner ruling 2026-11-06. The notebook app moved to #6922 on 2026-11-15.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).
Cleaned 2026-11-15. The notebook app (c11-c14) went to #6922. c10 (the D-DX-CELLS1 proof stub) merged into c1.

criteria.text: Editing a defining cell reruns only its pure transitive dependents automatically, records the dependency order, and marks effectful dependents for confirmation, labeling skipped work stale (D-DX-CELLS1=A).
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c5, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: A typed function argument renders as a validated control, and changing the control reruns the affected cells, while invalid input keeps an explicit error state.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c6, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Deleting a defining cell scrubs its bindings and invalidates the dependent outputs, and an old cached value is never shown as current.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c7, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Closing and reopening the browser reconnects to the same bounded kernel only when the source and build identity and the authority checks pass, and an unauthorized reconnect is rejected with a registered error.

Proof: a tests/cases notebook row under `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jetnb`.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c10, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

cards.title: `fn build` per-package permissions
cards.body: fn build scope and authority: declared inputs, explicit grants, dependency order and rejection before effects. Moved out of the known-failing card #5454 by owner ruling 2026-11-06.

criteria.text: Each build unit receives only its declared Tier-1 inputs and explicitly named Tier-2 grants, and dependency order, computed package facts, plan, execution, lock and explain output agree.

Unlisted dependency authority, grant escalation, cycles, outside-root paths, read or write failure and stale computed facts are refused before any effect, each with its registered error and UI snapshot.
In a multi-member workspace, grants are not inherited, dependency grants are explicit, order and root-layer boundaries hold, and a failed build rolls back.
The package-default authority floor (#3718) is part of the JetDriver package facts.
`b.include(pkg)` in your `fn build` runs the package's own `fn build` only under that package's authority, and records producer, input and output identity in the Jetpack lock.
Importing a package or using its helpers never runs its build entries or hooks implicitly.
Plan fragments and generated modules from an included build merge transactionally, and a collision or denied effect leaves no partial publication.
Shared preparation can generate the same outputs on non-AOT tiers without misusing `fn build`.
An Examples/ golden of a bindings package used through `b.include` passes on the self-hosted toolchain.

cards.title: core.compute correctness: CPU-oracle parity, checked failures, SIMD kernels and kernel helpers
cards.body: core.compute data integration, tensor meaning, failure checks and CPU-differential proof. Moved out of #5454 by owner ruling 2026-11-06.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: criteria restated with proofs; c4 now names the failing compute_autodiff golden.
Defect recorded here because #3026 is frozen and design card #3218 is archived as done: ratified D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1=A is unbuilt. Report: Docs/audits/2026-11-10-run-where-review.md.

criteria.text: Tensor storage, views, operations, precision, placement, streams, kernels, derivatives and serialization match the CPU oracle: a differential test runs each operation family on every available backend against the CPU result.

Shape, alias, bounds, race, barrier, precision, device-loss, transfer, gradient and unsupported-operation failures are checked at the owning layer and give typed errors, never a fabricated success. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Compute/failure_` with a negative case per failure.
compute_autodiff runs (no internal compiler error) and prints its expected output on O0, O1, O2 and the AOT build.
criteria.evidence: p238 batch compiler (dev 5bea729463), full collect-all suite: golden Compute/ComputeAutodiff PASS on o0, o1 and o2.

criteria.text: The ufunc and kernel set that must lower to SIMD is listed in Core/Compute, and a scalar-versus-SIMD differential test proves byte-equal results for each.
Runtime dispatch picks the AVX2 or SSE2 path through jet_compute_simd_backend, and both paths give the same results.

D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1=A is built: a #Kernel that calls a pure helper (for example a function returning `x * 3`) checks and runs on every applicable tier instead of E1102 at the marker (Sema/Kernel.jet rejects every call edge today), and a rejected helper's diagnostic keeps its span. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Compute/KernelHelper` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter kernel_helper_rejected`.

A handled ComputeError (for example from `compute.eye(-1)`) shows its typed detail through the supported surface, with a golden on O0, O1 and O2; the E0915 suggestion for ComputeError-like types compiles on the next check.

cards.title: Live hot reload keeps state: #Persist values survive edits and restarts, migrate by rule, and every reset names its reason
cards.body:
Destination: under `jet dev`, editing a running program swaps the code and keeps every #Persist value whose type is unchanged. Type changes follow D-HOTSTATE1=A and D-LIVE-PERSIST1=A: defaults, drops, `migration` blocks, or an announced restart that names the blocking field. Restarts keep #Persist values through the session pipe (D-DEV-STATE1=A). Game state and controls live in the same session (D-DX-GAMELOOP1=A).

Until this card lands, JetDevserver's swap paths (NativeSwap, NativeSwap02, WebModuleSwap) refuse with not-available (#5931, Main's log 2026-11-13). Diagnostic E2210 is registered again with its emitter when this card builds the behavior.

Moved out of #5454 by owner ruling 2026-11-06.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: proofs added to every criterion. c4 merged into c10 (D-LIVE-PERSIST1) and c13 (the renamed-binding reset), and c7 into c8.

Note (Main): until this card lands, JetDevserver swap paths (NativeSwap, NativeSwap02, WebModuleSwap) refuse with an explicit not-available result instead of using HotSwapDecision and StateRetentionFact; they are restored against the real types when this card lands (#5931).

Main, 2026-11-11, #4260 c29 cleanup (G5DevX-dead-codes-3): diagnostic code E2210 is removed from the registry because nothing emits it, and its known-failing cases go with it. When this card builds the behavior, it registers the code again with its emitter, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot. The behavior the deleted cases expected: tests/cases/dev_parts_routine/{struct_field,enum_variant,fn_signature}_change_emits_e2210.case: a jet dev edit to a type surface restarts instead of swapping.

criteria.text: On every live edit, each #Persist key's retention comes from its checked type identity, and its payload shape is validated at one Foundation migration boundary. Only unchanged typed values are kept, and changed or unavailable keys record an explicit Fresh or Reset reason, on O0 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DevPartsRoutine/persist_binding_survives_hot_swap_and_resets_on_shape_change` on O0 and O2.

Game hot swap runs through the production WatchSession facts and one shared swap kernel. Asset, script and world changes get typed decisions, the resident dev tools apply them, and each is published as an event.

`jet dev` selects the tier, runs the O0 and O2 source paths, watches by content digest, and keeps #Persist semantics in resident live execution across a long-lived session. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DevPartsRoutine/ul6_native_watch_matrix_budget_and_reconnect` and `--filter dev_parts_routine/persist_example_survives_hot_reload` on O0 and O2.
(was #2504 c2) Published Persist migrations use one shared canonical Shape migration plan; restart and renamed-binding reset policies are implemented (moved from #5454 c69)
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6625 c10: a published #Persist migration through the one Shape migration plan is D-LIVE-PERSIST1=A's step function; the renamed-binding reset is now in c13

criteria.text: A save swaps by default, the explicit session and project restart opt-outs work, existing field values are kept, and each save reports a typed outcome.
Live inspection shows typed pinned #Persist values and their shapes through the ratified live inspect route.
(was #2504 c5) All named live/dev/parity/inspection/diagnostic proof and O0/O2 smoke pass as tests/cases rows on O0 and O2 (#2919, which held them, is gone) (moved from #5454 c72)
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6625 c8: the ported live and dev proofs on O0 and O2 are c8's cases

criteria.text: Under `jet dev`, editing a function body in a running program applies the change and keeps every #Persist value whose type is unchanged, on O0 and O2. The Rust-era tests of #2426 and #765 are ported as cases. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DevPartsRoutine/persist_` on O0 and O2.

D-LIVE-PERSIST1=A: when a persisted value's type changes and the type is #PublishedSchema with a migration that covers the change, the value migrates in place through the same step function decode uses, and the save line says so. Otherwise `jet dev` announces a restart. A value is never silently reinterpreted. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DevPartsRoutine/persist_published_schema_migrates_in_place` and `--filter dev_parts_routine/persist_unpublished_change_announces_restart`.
One declared rule decides which state survives an edit. A failed edit never silently repeats external work, and the displayed active revision agrees with the machine diagnostics.

D-DX-GAMELOOP1=A: game state and controls live in the existing resident `jet dev` session. One session owns source and runtime, Canvas routes stay authoritative, and headless and rendered runs share events.

D-HOTSTATE1=A: on a hot swap, an added field takes its declared default, a removed field is dropped, renames and type changes use `migration` blocks, and a renamed binding resets. When no rule applies, `jet dev` restarts and names the field that blocked the swap. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DevPartsRoutine/hot_state_`, with one case per rule.

D-DEV-STATE1=A: the jet process holds the #Persist store and gives each program child a private pipe through the session. On a stop request, a runtime thread in the child copies every JetPersistCell whole, so #Persist values survive a `jet dev` restart without the store ever being written to disk. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DevPartsRoutine/persist_survives_restart_through_session_pipe` on O0.

cards.title: One receipt kind: test results, goldens, budgets and API snapshots are receipts with one shape, written by shared Prelude code
cards.body:
Destination: every development act (a test run, a golden, a budget or an API snapshot) writes a receipt of one kind: act, locked closure, content-addressed inputs, witness and outcome. Shared Prelude code writes it on every tier.

Decisions: D-ECO-RECEIPT2=A (one connected receipt) and D-FOUND-RECEIPT1=A (typed sections on the one receipt). Start with a design note and an adversarial review of how the existing stores (the #6035 test store, golden files, budget history, API snapshots) map onto the one shape.

Source: #2110, #2112 and #5069, through #6035.

criteria.text: Test results, goldens, budgets and API snapshots are all stored as receipts of one kind.
One receipt record shape exists, with act, locked closure, content-addressed inputs, witness and outcome, and it is the only such shape in the tree.
A development act writes a receipt without the caller asking for one.
A receipt names its inputs by content address, so an identical act over identical inputs is recognisable as the same act.
Shared Prelude code writes the receipt on every tier (I9), with no per-engine re-encoding. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Receipts/` on O0, O1 and O2 gives identical receipts.

criteria.text: (was #3033) [#3032] A direct source without authentication needs interactive approval before the first artifact GET; `-y` and `--trust` cannot grant it. A grant binds source, metadata authority, repo, resolver, selector, asset policy, target, platform, proof floor and ordered HTTPS origins, and excludes mutable version, tag, digest and URL. A later candidate in an unchanged scope needs no new prompt. A new origin stops before the request. Any scope change invalidates the grant. Known pins check identity, grant and origins before the GET and the SHA-256 after it. Same identity with different bytes fails and preserves the working pin and generation. cards.title: Compiler code health after the port: retired teaching, stale comments, stutter names and unwired code
cards.body:
Destination: the compiler source reads as conventional Jet after the port from Rust. No retired Jet spelling is recognized or taught, no comment cites deleted Rust code, no name repeats its package, tool packages run their tests, the docs teach only current forms, and no test claims an interpreter tier.

Why it matters: leftovers from the port mislead every reader and every agent that learns from the source (Pillar 5, Docs/spec/philosophy.md; AGENTS.md Greenfield cutover).

A1 is jet run's kept programs, A2 the jet build executable restore, A3 BuildExecutor action reuse, A4 the C dependency archives, A5 the C provisioning record and A6 the Rust FFI bridge. Two result caches go off too: B1, jet test result reuse (its --fresh flag is removed), and F3, Admit's suite and census caches. Main's ruling: every one is off by default, and its reuse code is unreachable until a ballot ratifies an opt-in spelling. The in-process memos C1/C2 stay on. ScriptAPI-2 measured Jet at about 19-21 MB against bash's 7-12 MB on batch10, integrate10, streamb10 and verify-rows, and the cost is the runtime's baseline, not the twins. The fix goes in the general mechanism (runtime start-up, reserved heap or arena sizing, and eagerly mapped tables), and is proven on a second small program. PortBars shows peak memory PASS on all nine. Part 1 (ScriptAPI-3, image layout locality and the build key; it rides t16) took the warm small-script peak from 15.5 MB to 7.1-7.5 MB, and batch10, integrate10 and streamb10 still lose (11.8 against 10.6 MB, 12.9 against 8.6, 10.6 against 8.6), while verify-rows ties. Name where the uncached 30 ms and 37 MB go (front end, sema, lowering, emission, link, runtime start), fix them in those general mechanisms toward the 30M lines/s compile target, and prove it on hello world and on a repository tool twin. Proof: a committed GNU time receipt for hello and a repository tool twin, with the phase breakdown.

cards.title: Reasoning about code: Jet beats every language on how well readers and tools can reason about a program
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: beat all other languages on the ability to reason about code.

criteria.text: A reasoning benchmark defines task families (predict the output, find every effect of a call, show two values never alias, find every caller, find what a change breaks, find where a failure can come from) over matched programs in Jet, Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, Zig and C++. Proof: `git ls-files "Tools/Gauntlet/reasoning/*"` names the task families and matched programs.

Each task is scored for readers (human or model: accuracy and time) and for tools (what `jet inspect` and the language server answer mechanically versus each peer toolchain). Proof: the committed scored receipt for readers and tools.
End metric: Jet scores best on every task family; every loss names its root on a card. Proof: the same receipt shows Jet best on every family, each loss naming its card.

A seeded repair exercise (a typed CLI error, an invalid external record, a guest failure) records the rejection stage, side effects, edit, check and repair steps and the five quantities against pinned peers. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry repair-exercise`.

Core workflow tasks (imports, errors, lifecycle) are added to the existing runner and measure the five quantities, with no second registry or runner. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry core-workflow`.

For every declared source and ergonomics metric (LOC and tokens included) and every peer in every required gauntlet cell, Jet/peer < 1.00, Rust included; no median, Python-only subset, aggregate, missing or unmeasured row passes. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs` source-metric report shows no loss.

Each of the 36 selected ecosystem and capability cells has a versioned evidence disposition and a specific executable contrast, or a justified non-applicable boundary. Proof: the committed cell table, checked by `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs`.

A scripting comparison audit under Docs/Audits compares Jet with Lua, JavaScript, TypeScript, Bash and Python on speed, source tokens and readability (the #5072 c14 checklist); every cell is measured, not estimated, and each cell Jet loses names the card that owns it. cards.title: Expert performance APIs: every technique the asm-parity ceilings use is expressible in Jet
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: advanced APIs so codegen can produce the equivalent of the best hand-optimized machine code.

log.text: Moved G11 to G13 by Main 2026-11-12 02:25: every open criterion is about expressing and emitting the ceiling techniques, which is the ceiling stage (G13 hill climbing per the owner ruling).

HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c3 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size climb: moved from G13 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11. It stays a horizon card under the 2026-11-08 rule: it blocks no card, milestone, release or gate, and its targets are not pass/fail criteria elsewhere.

criteria.text: Every technique an asm-parity reference uses that Jet code cannot express (SIMD lanes, prefetch, alignment and layout control, branch and cold hints, non-temporal stores, syscall batching and others) is listed with the cells that use it. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Research/*expert-techniques*"` names the committed table.

Each missing technique gets an owner ballot with its plain and expert spellings (expert control by explicit opt-in) and a paired two-program cell; it ratifies only when it strictly beats the plain form. Proof: each row of that table names its decision ID and its paired cell.

End metric: every required cell can be written in Jet with its ceiling's technique, and codegen emits that technique. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` with each required cell written in Jet using its ceiling technique.

Each ratified cache-control surface (D-CACHE-CONTROL1=A: `mem.prefetch`, `mem.stream_store`, the cache-line size fact) has a paired two-program cell against the plain spelling it replaces, recorded in the canonical manifest, and strictly beats it. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry cache-control` shows no loss. (was #6312 c4)

Cache facts distinguish build and exec targets, private and shared caches and unknown values; the acceleration gate uses them without enlarging the scratch budget or worker count; transforms keep output, failure, effect and drop order; the decision ledger reports the facts; and a cache-locality paired entry (nested reuse against a single pass) passes the gate. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetirFacts/cache_facts` and `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry cache-locality`. (was #6312 c13)

cards.title: Transpile Jet to other languages through target libraries that implement one trait (C and Rust first-party, any language by a package)
cards.body:
Owner request 2026-11-07, re-scoped the same day: Jet transpiles a program to another language, and any language can be added as an ordinary Jet library implementing a target trait. Seeding and bootstrapping the compiler are a separate, frozen question on #6683; this card comes first.

Why: interop (Jet code inside C, Rust, Lua or JavaScript projects), reach (platforms with no Jet native writer), and the language-is-a-library priority.

Design: ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1. The recommended shape: one shared pass makes every meaning explicit, and core.compiler exposes a versioned program view. A Target trait has required operation methods, host leaves and optional idiom hooks. Capabilities are checked first, and `jet test --to <target>` checks every executable example against `jet run`.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-16: transpiling moves from G6 to G13 for now.

Ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1 posted and ready. The fresh adversarial review (PortsLead-2, against dev 964e737fcc) broke the first draft's recommendation. Today's IR still leaves exact-Int spill, trap and stop meaning to each writer (X64Select.jet, Web/Select.jet). The runtime's platform layer is 75 #FFI(asm) leaves plus 383 raw x86-64 syscall sites. Comptime and the only native writer are x86-64, so a C seed cannot rebuild itself elsewhere. --target already means a platform. Recommended now: staged A, with a Wasm seed from the existing web writer (C syscall host, evaluator comptime), then a shared pass that makes every check explicit plus jet build --emit c, then third-party emit libraries once the form is declared stable. If ratified, the criteria follow the ruling.

Ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1 drafted (owner request: challenge, refine, improve). Options: A target libraries over the compiler's final lowered form, with C and WebAssembly first and a C seed every release (recommended); B readable source-level transpilers per language; C WebAssembly seed only (Zig's approach); D prebuilt binaries only. It passes Tools/agent/ballots/Validate.jet except the review pass. Tower needs the adversarial review even for a draft, so the fresh review (PortsLead-2) is in progress, and the ballot is posted once its findings are folded in.

criteria.text: An adversarial design review in Docs/audits tests every claimed strength of the ratified D-EXPORT-TARGET1 design (library-defined targets for any language, one meaning across targets, readable output through idiom hooks, interop) against Haxe with Reflaxe, Fable, Kotlin's shared IR, Nim, Gleam and LLVM targets. Every gap it finds is on a card or ballot.
criteria.evidence: 32ee48040b (batch 47): Docs/audits/2026-11-14-d-export-target1-review.md tests all four D-EXPORT-TARGET1 claims against Haxe with Reflaxe, Fable, Kotlin, Nim, Gleam and LLVM, using code facts from dev 9623399213. Each of its nine gaps is on a card: #6151, #3520 c22 and #6675 c7-c15.

criteria.text: A ratified Tower ballot fixes the command's name and flags, the target-library API (what a target receives from the checked program and how it emits text), and the first-party targets, with same-program alternatives and beginner and expert paths.
criteria.evidence: D-EXPORT-TARGET1 ratified A (2026-11-07): one public core.compiler.target Target trait over the explicit program, with required op methods, host leaves and optional idiom hooks; capability errors before output; jet build --to <target>; jet test --to conformance; C and Rust first-party.

criteria.text: A target is an ordinary Jet library any package can write, using only public compiler-library seams: a third-party test target built outside the repository exports a program as well as a first-party one.

Exporting a program to C and building it with a stock C compiler gives the same stdout, stderr and exit code as `jet run` at O0, O1 and O2 for every executable example, with memory safety, fault reports and error behavior unchanged.

One shared IR pass makes exact-Int spills, fixed-width traps and the stop protocol explicit for every writer: the IR has explicit operations for the inline-Int test and the big-integer spill (jet_int_add, jet_int_sub, jet_int_mul, jet_int_compare, jet_rt_int_clone), for fixed-width traps with their stop texts, and for the stop protocol, proved by an IR dump test. X64Select.jet and Web/Select.jet consume those operations and no longer decide them; `! git grep -n ir_x64_ Compiler/JetWeb/Source/Web/Select.jet`, and the golden and web suites pass. c3 and c4 build on it. (gap from the D-EXPORT-TARGET1 adversarial review, Docs/Audits/2026-11-14-d-export-target1-review.md) Proof: the IR dump test `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Jetir/explicit_int_traps_stop`, `! git grep -n ir_x64_ Compiler/JetWeb/Source/Web/Select.jet`, and the golden and web suites pass.

The public program view has a version, and a target library built against another version gets a registered error naming both versions before the target runs (adversarial review, Docs/Audits/2026-11-14-d-export-target1-review.md).

An idiom hook may not hand copying, string encoding, Float text or map iteration order to the host unless conformance covers the hosted form: `jet test --to <target>` runs each target with its hooks and again with only the defaults, and both match `jet run` (adversarial review). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --to c` passes in both modes.

A target implements a closed host-leaf table that replaces the runtime's numbered system calls (168 os_syscall_* sites in 30 runtime files on dev 9623399213); the spec names the table and the code holds it. Builds on #6151 (adversarial review). Proof: `git grep -c os_syscall_ -- Compiler/JetRuntime` reports 0 outside the table's own module, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes.

The program view exposes value ranges the compiler proved (Int ranges, loop bounds, proven-inline operands), so a hook may spell host arithmetic where no spill is possible, and conformance covers it (adversarial review).
A transpile target declares Core/Target MachineFacts, and its capability errors are the existing machine denial rows, with no second capability list (adversarial review).

Transpiled code carries Jet source locations: C output writes #line, other targets write source maps where the language has them, and a fault in transpiled code names the Jet file and line (adversarial review).
A target library runs in the build sandbox and can write only its output directory (ties to #3520's sandbox work; adversarial review).

The interop question the review found (X5) is decided: owner ballot D-EXPORT-INTEROP1, drafted at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Meta/c3/ballot-D-EXPORT-INTEROP1.json, is reviewed, posted and ratified, and its outcome is added here as criteria. Proof: `tower decision show D-EXPORT-INTEROP1` reports ratified.

cards.title: The remaining Tools/ scripts and Tower itself run on Jet
cards.body: Owner ruling 11-07 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md priority 6): Jet fills every role; a capability Core lacks is a Core gap to close, never a reason to use sh, node, Python or C. The 11-07 census found non-Jet scripts that no open card owns. Tools/agent-eval (run-cold-context.mjs, test-cold-context.mjs, the foundations-trust, domain-foundations, ffi-assurance and test-economics drivers), Tools/adoption (validate.py, tests), Tools/cli-census/census.mjs, Tools/foreign-build-hosts/jet-library.sh, Tools/jet-nix-eval/differential-report.mjs and Tools/datetime_accuracy.py are ported to Jet. Tools/compiler-modules (dissolve-collections, drop-file-imports, inventory, migrate-examples, migrate) are finished one-off migrations: delete them. Tower (Tools/tower, a node application with 29 app and 40 test files) is the work ledger: port it to Jet, with its browser UI produced by the web target. Editor packages stay in the format their editor requires (the VS Code extension's JS, tree-sitter's grammar.js).

log.text: G1Lead landed (a) 1893c623ad (JSON reader memory and render) and (b) c884e9421c (Board.jet). Worker figures, old to new peak RSS and wall: card show #6096 162 to 56 MB; archived card show 785 to 117 MB, 1.32 to 1.1 s; card list 198 to 117 MB, 0.56 to 0.39 s; milestone list --archived 785 to 118 MB; lint --docs 784 to 117 MB, 1.6 to 1.18 s; five dumps 1.56 to 0.39 s, byte-identical; Board parity 149/149. w06 decode 507 to 369 MB, encode 1.33 to 0.98 s with identical bytes. Board memory took down the a0_038 retry, 2026-11-08 07:11 (release of c902740d37). The release scope cap is 18 GB (memory.max 18874368 kB). The kernel OOM killer fired with 24 concurrent Board processes at 0.6-0.9 GB RSS each, the largest 223k pages, spawned by the cases suite at --jobs 6 across 4 shards; oom.group killed the whole release. The release was rerun with --jobs 3 as a stopgap. Root: Tools/tower/Board.jet parses all of tower.json and the history shards into Dyn trees (json.parse_with_limits, lines 374 and 427). Fix direction: Board decodes only the fields a projection needs, through typed json.decode<T> on the #6082 D streaming reader, so no document tree is built. It is routed to G1Lead as D's first real consumer, after D's first step lands.

Main 2026-11-08 03:35 defect: Tools/tower/Board.jet uses 22-60x the board file in memory. `card show #6096 --json` peaks at 309 MB RSS (0.95 s) on the 14 MB tower.json, and the projections the gates run reached 670-860 MB anon each. In the a0_037 release cases suite, 14 concurrent Boards (spawned by gate-running cases) plus compiles filled the 18 GB release memcg, and the OOM killed the whole release (rc 137 at 03:24). Root fix: read the board without materializing the whole Dyn tree, or project only what each command needs (the JSON event reader from 5ed4a14dcd fits), so each Board stays near the file size. Meanwhile the release runs admit with --jobs.

3c8544784c: Tools/tower/Board.jet (card show/list, decision show/list, milestone list, all with --json) is the read path. CloseoutGate, CoreSurfaceLedger, DecisionIndex and CompiledWorkloads read the board through it. CloseoutGate's milestone closeout write still goes through node (criterion stays open).
