cards.title: Test results are reused across runs: the full profile and the admit skip rows whose compiler and inputs are unchanged
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; no cached or incremental work now.

Measured: a fresh-clone `jet test Compiler --profile full` took about 2 hours (engine 4 min, cold toolchain fetch 45 min, suites 64 min). The release admit then reruns every suite for the same commit, about 40 more minutes. Corpus rows total 248 CPU minutes (golden 160, cases 79, ui 9).

criteria.text: Test-result reuse is opt-in and off by default: with it on, `jet test Compiler --profile full` and the release admit skip a row only when the compiler identity and every input of that row are unchanged, and each skipped row prints as reused. Not built now (owner direction 2026-11-07: no cached or incremental work now); Main schedules it.

cards.title: The compiler's default thread count is fixed at start from the instantaneous load, so a build started on a busy host runs on one core
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; do not build now.

`jet_cli_default_threads` (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Request.jet) reads procs_running from /proc/stat once at start and drops to one thread when the host is busy. The thread count then never grows. In the full profile, the hosted Jetpack engine build started beside four package runs took about 13 minutes on one core; it took 184 s when it started on a quiet host.

criteria.text: A build's parallel width follows free cores while it runs, instead of being fixed by the load at start.

The hosted Jetpack engine build started beside 8 concurrent package runs finishes within 1.5x of its quiet-host wall time, measured on the batch machine and recorded with the commit. Proof: a committed batch-machine receipt, quiet and loaded.
The quiet-host self-build wall time does not regress (compared on the same machine and commit range as #6527). Proof: the #6527 c1 self-build cell receipt for the same commit range.

cards.title: core.crypto SHA-256 runs at 45-50 MB/s; a scalar native implementation does about 500 MB/s and SHA-NI about 2 GB/s
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; do not build now.

Measured on #6592: pure-Jet core.crypto SHA-256 runs at about 45-50 MB/s at O1 and O2, and a hand-unrolled Jet version gives the same speed. The backend has no SHA-NI path. Toolchain install hashes about 450 MB, so hashing alone costs about 9 s per pass on one thread.

cards.title: Compiler/build.jet declares the whole project: every artifact, generated table, toolchain, chain stage and profile is one build graph
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: make full use of Jet's customizable build function for this project; card it, do not build it now.

Today Compiler/build.jet declares one target, the jet executable. Everything else is assembled outside the build graph, each piece in its own serial step: the self-host chain (Tools/agent/chain/chain.sh), the runtime pack (cc-pack and pack, with musl found through JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB), the Jetpack engine (Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet, then a separate jet build inside the packages suite: 3 min quiet, 13 min under load), the generated registry tables (regenerated by hand and checked at precommit; a stale CoreEnumRows failed a landing on 2026-11-07), and the test and release tools.

The Build API already offers add_executable, add_library, add_test, add_package, add_publish, add_install, add_doc, action, generate, toolchain, probe, signing and embed, the registered build options, and core.build graph receipts with receipt_diff.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

SpeedLead: build.jet cannot list a folder at plan time (b.find returns files only, walks into .jet, and is not recorded as a plan input; #4833 known-failing). So c6 keeps STAGE_FOLDERS and STAGE_FILES as a kernel.tsv row, plus a tests/guards check that every top-level entry of a split stage package (except Generated and dot entries) is listed, so the list cannot go stale silently. The .jet/deps alias hole touches 5 to 6 files in two packages and is now its own criterion; c6 does not depend on it.

c6 layout ruling (Main): the build-graph contract stays. SpeedLead moves the 4 kept generated sources into <pkg>/Generated/ (JetFoundation PreludeMarkers, JetSema PreludeDerives and PreludeUnits, JetLexer KeywordSpans). Stages read those packages top-level entries minus Generated/, derived at plan time, not a hand list, plus the kept files through .reads. The rejected alternative (narrow folders plus about 105 explicit files) would be a stale-prone closed list. Owner Q20 is withdrawn. Validator defect found by SpeedLead: both validators compare spelled folder paths, so a dependency bound at .jet/deps on the same real folder escapes the rule. It is fixed in the same patch by comparing resolved folders, with a #Test.

c6 blocker (SpeedLead): the self-host stages read the 17 Compiler folders whole, and the build-graph rule (Graph.jet:109-121, Jetpack Validation.jet:173-177, spec.md:5050, E3502) refuses step outputs inside them: the runtime step outputs under JetCli/.jet/build, and the c5 kept outputs (Prelude copies, KeywordSpans.jet). Main ruling: an output under a .jet or .git part being outside the folder read is a defect fix (one meaning with the folder snapshot, Cache.jet build_folder_skipped). SpeedLead lands it with a BuildGraphRules #Test. Allowing an output inside a read folder when the reader also reads it changes the spec contract, so it is owner Q20. SpeedLead is costing the keep-the-rule alternative.

c4 landed on dev as 42d3bedfe8 (SpeedLead lane-commit; precommit census on a0_039: check, build, runtime from jet build Compiler, self-check, Core self-check). It is the owner (A) stopgap shape (host cc plus musl), removed under #6687. On master as merge cb5a55054d, the exact tested dev tree. A cherry-pick conflicted in the generated Docs/spec/safety.md and would have given master an unbuilt tree, so the merge also carries 1f8f46177e (#6690) and 775f3b07ae (#6686). Main updated its precommit census for trees where jet build Compiler writes the pack. c5 (generated tables as kept build outputs) is next, and c6 (s2 and s3 as build actions) is approved.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 on commit 4: "A as stopgap but removed when we have 100% jet." So c4 lands in the (A) shape: a fresh clone builds with the dev shell or a host cc plus static musl, and ReuseSeedRuntime.jet is deleted. The host C requirement goes when #6687 (no C dependency) closes; the fresh-clone criterion there proves it. Landing waits for a0_039 to be the current seed, because a0_038 rejects the new build.jet (Build.folder arity). SpeedLead holds the tested patch (LaneCheck CHECK OK on dev c884e9421c).

Commit 4 is held for an owner question (2026-11-08). Under c4, `jet build Compiler` builds the runtime pack, so it needs cc plus a static musl libc.a. A fresh clone with neither stops at the probes, so bootstrap.md "From a fresh clone: no Nix" (seed build plus ReuseSeedRuntime) stops being true. Using the toolchain own jet cc inside build steps needs new public build API: steps run sandboxed (bwrap, cleared env, no net) and see only the builder folder and probe results, not the Hangar cc pack. The pack also lacks nm (RuntimePack symbol gate) and ships compiler-rt instead of libgcc.a/libgcc_eh.a. Options for the owner: (A) the fresh clone uses the dev shell or a host cc plus musl; (B) a ballot for a jet-cc build-step surface; (C) keep ReuseSeedRuntime as an exception. SpeedLead finishes the rest of c4 as a tested patch meanwhile.

Main ruling, commit 4: `.file(b.found(p))` accepts a find_program result too (it already accepts find_folder), within the approved D-BUILD-GRAPH1/D-BUILD-TREES1 surface, so no ballot. The found program gets the same sandbox visibility it gets as a step tool; the action key covers its bytes and its probe fact; the old refusal and its snapshot go; a cc case proves it. The runtime pack logic moves to Compiler/Toolchain/RuntimePack.jet, run as one b.run step. Also fixed: staged inputs lost the exec bit.

Commit 3 landed as 74bbf2a07c (the find_folder probe, with no caller; E3505 with a UI snapshot). Main decided commit 4: flatten jet-runtime/ to fixed paths, with the identity in native.key. It is an internal pack format, one cutover across the CLI lookup, ReuseSeedRuntime, the chain store, the pack cache and publishing, with no fallback reader; the alternative was a new public step.output_folder API (I8). The vendored C is reached through source-less foreign packages at Core/Vendor/Sqlite3 and Core/Vendor/Mbedtls (not a Core/package.jet, which would mark Core as its own project); this needs a side-effect census first. A flake.nix LIBRARY_PATH export is allowed only with a host glibc-link proof.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked via Main): Compiler/build.jet builds jet with Core embedded, the committed generated tables (D-BUILD-ROWS1 = A, kept: true) and the runtime pack (jet-runtime: Core/Vendor C compiled with cc, static musl linked) as one complete toolchain. Tools, the docs site and Jetpack stay out of it. Folder inputs (D-BUILD-TREES1 option A: b.folder / b.dependency(name).folder / find_folder, hashed per file) are approved for the trees this needs (Core/, Core/Vendor, Compiler/JetRuntime). The cc and musl needs end with #6328 c11 and Jet-native db/TLS. Owner: SpeedLead (already owns Compiler/build.jet); top priority, ahead of #6328.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked via Main): D-BUILD-ROWS1 = A. Generated tables stay in git as build outputs (.output(path, kept: true)): jet build Compiler rewrites them when inputs change and refuses hand edits; the precommit freshness check becomes build plus clean tree. D-BUILD-TREES1: owner accepts folder inputs but rejects the scope as drafted: Tools are separate from the compiler build (Compiler/build.jet covers the compiler and Core, not Tools), and questions why the compiler build needs C sources, cc and musl at all. Scope question pending. Blocker (1) is cleared: a0_037 (3a8dd83e79) contains every D-BUILD-GRAPH1 step (4361eec2f4 is an ancestor).

Main 2026-11-08 02:00, BuildLead final handoff (slot ended). Landed: C4 profiles 3af734e9cb; step 1 b.run/b.found/action_timeout ccf9915f44; b.action and b.legacy retired 74942e812c; step 2 b.host/b.jet/one parallel graph c9c3ce97a6; gate fix 8a85d45051 (a b.jet() step gets the running compiler's identity); step 4 receipts, times and jet inspect build --times 64f57f1583; step 5 b.dependency(name).file(path) 509708b651; step 6 b.image(target) a749167d57; step 7 a step never overwrites a file no build made 4361eec2f4; closed-list kernel rows ec519cce83. Criteria per BuildLead: 6 and 7 met in code (Main meets them after the c65 run #3 proof); 1 partly met (the graph and the jet target; other targets need D-BUILD-TREES1); 2 blocked by D-BUILD-ROWS1 (every generator writes committed files a step may not overwrite; CoreSourceRows also writes outside Compiler/); 3 and 4 blocked by D-BUILD-TREES1 (jet embeds all of Core/, PrebuildRuntime.jet is in Tools/, and no probe finds a folder); 5 blocked by #6623. Owner ballots drafted, not yet adversarially reviewed, in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/BuildLead/ballots/. D-BUILD-ROWS1 recommends kept outputs: .output(path, kept: true) rewrites a committed table when its inputs change and refuses hand edits; the alternatives are build-only files or today's hand-run generators. D-BUILD-TREES1 recommends folder inputs (b.dependency(name).folder(path), b.folder(path)) plus a find_folder probe; the alternatives are listing a dependency's files one by one, or keeping the scripts. Both pass Validate.jet apart from draft:true and an empty reviewPasses. No scripts were deleted.

Main 2026-11-07 23:50: BuildLead reports the D-BUILD-GRAPH1 API done locally (steps 1-2 on dev; 4 records, 5 dependency, 6 image and 7 refuse-overwrite landing in order). Three blockers stop migrating Compiler/build.jet. (1) build.jet is compiled by the seed, so it needs a seed with steps 1-7; Main cuts a0_038 after they land. (2) Owner question: refuse-overwrite means the generated row files (CoreCallRows and so on) leave git and come from jet build Compiler, so jet check or jet test on a fresh member fails until a build runs. Choose untracked generated rows or keep the committed rows with their precommit freshness check. (3) Owner question: C2/C3/C5 read trees outside Compiler/ (Core, the runtime C sources, Tools) and need cc and musl. That needs folder inputs or listing a dependency's files, which is new API and needs a ballot. Ballot drafts for (2) and (3) go to $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/BuildLead/ballots/; they have no adversarial review yet.

Main 2026-11-08: the owner ratified D-BUILD-GRAPH1 = A. BuildLead builds it, in this order: b.run with declared inputs and outputs and Duration timeouts; b.host and b.jet; the one-graph executor; times.json; b.dependency().file; b.image and b.found. b.run replaces b.action in all 51 callers, with no alias. Then the repo build scripts move onto it (c1-c3, c5, c6). c4 landed as 3af734e9cb.

Main 2026-11-07: BuildLead drafted D-BUILD-GRAPH1 (a build step can run a program the same build makes; host-built tools; files declared where passed; Duration limits; times.json), the ballot that unblocks c1/c2/c3/c5/c6. Main ran the adversarial pass (same model family) and BuildLead redesigned it; claims with file:line are in the ballot. A cross-family review pass is still owed before ratification, because the owner allowed no further agent slot tonight. c4 (build profiles) is held until the a0_035 release ends; c7 waits on #6623.

cards.title: Portable seed: build a working Jet on a machine that has only a C compiler or a WebAssembly runtime
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: seeding and bootstrapping the compiler is a separate question from transpilation (#6675, D-EXPORT-TARGET1) and is frozen for the future. Transpilation comes first.

Goal: a machine with no Jet binary builds a current Jet from what it already has, so a seed never goes stale and a new platform is never stuck.

Candidate plan from the earlier D-EXPORT-TARGET1 draft, which is not ratified: compile the compiler with the existing WebAssembly writer, then turn that .wasm into C with a committed WebAssembly-to-C translator. A small C host answers the runtime's system calls on POSIX, and compile-time code runs on the IR evaluator instead of an x86-64 child. Every release checks that the seed rebuilds the release's own stage-2 bytes. Once the #6675 C target exists, exporting the compiler to C is the alternative route. Trust limit: a seed built from generated output still trusts the compiler that wrote it; only an independent Jet implementation removes that.

criteria.text: An adversarial design review in Docs/Audits tests the seed's claims (durability, onboarding, trust) against existing bootstrap chains: Zig's WebAssembly seed, Nim's generated C, mrustc, and bootstrappable builds. Every gap it finds is on a card or ballot.
A ratified Tower ballot picks the seed route (WebAssembly translated to C, the #6675 C target, or prebuilt binaries only), with same-program alternatives and the trust limits stated.

Exporting the compiler's own source to C (and to Wasm) gives a compiler that, built with only a C compiler (or a Wasm runtime), compiles the same tree to a byte-identical stage-2 compiler: a portable seed for every release, linked with #6186.
Install docs describe building Jet from the exported seed with a stock C compiler, and a fresh machine with no Jet binary follows them to a working jet.

cards.title: The hosted Jetpack engine takes about 3 minutes to build on a quiet host while the whole compiler self-compiles in about 10 s
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: Pareto speed work for the fresh-clone full profile.

The packages suite builds the hosted Jetpack engine (Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet hosted, then `jet build src/jetpack.jet`, in Compiler/test.jet jetpack_prepare). It took 184 s when it started on a quiet host and about 13 minutes on one core under load. The compiler, a larger codebase, self-compiles in about 10 s (#6527). The ratio points at something specific to the Jetpack build path (the assembled single unit, its optimization level, a pathological function, or a phase that grows superlinearly), not at code size.

log.text: Main 2026-11-07: SpeedLead landed 3412bcf62f (jet build cache entries, locks, leases and touches publish unsynced; reads verify digests, so a lost entry is a miss; the rlib cache, runtime pack, objects and LTO keep their syncs). The store publish tail went from 127.3 s/17.0 s to 8.4 s/5.0 s (fresh store, interleaved), with zero fsync calls during the build (strace). It also landed ef8a3f930d (L0534 copied the 12.5 MB engine module once per block: sema.finalize 149 s -> 5.8 s; sema.bodies 97 s -> 2.7 s; tests/ui_lint/map_group_round_trip.jet still prints L0534 at 10:9). Whole hosted engine build: 168 s -> 33.0 s at load 14 (28.6 s on a rerun); a cache hit takes 16.9 s. Proof by Main is pending (batch).

criteria.text: A per-phase profile of the hosted engine build (front end, sema, lowering, optimization, emission, link) names where the time goes, and it is recorded on this card with the commit.
criteria.evidence: Per-phase traces (jet build --trace; wall s / CPU s; 12 CPUs pinned on the busy 32-CPU host) of jet build src/jetpack.jet in the assembled hosted project (618 sources; one 12.5 MB module). dev eaa085b237: total 156.8-243.9 s wall, of which sema.finalize 98-149 s (sema.bodies 48-97 s wall / 547-928 CPU-s) and the store tail 17-127 s (fsync D-state); the front end 5-7 s, lowering 0.7-1.2 s, ir.opt 2.2-3.5 s, emission 0.7-0.9 s, link 0.15 s. Root cause 1: store fsyncs, fixed by 3412bcf62f (no fsync calls in strace). Root cause 2: the L0534 lint (10ce9aab90) copied the whole module bytes per block, fixed by ef8a3f930d. With both fixes: total 32.95 s wall / 49.7 CPU-s; sema.finalize 5.81 s; store tail 11.8 s under writeback throttling; cache hit 16.9 s. The table and the exact commands are in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/SpeedLead/6684-phases.md.

criteria.text: The root cause is fixed in the compiler or in Jetpack's assembly, and the hosted engine build on a quiet batch host takes at most 30 s, measured and recorded with the commit. Proof: a committed quiet-batch-host receipt of the hosted engine build.
The built engine is byte-for-byte the same program as before the fix, or every packages-suite engine claim still passes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes every engine claim.

cards.title: The Jetpack engine unit's claims all run serially because they share process state
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card the remaining slow phases.

Compiler/test.jet jetpack_engine_rows runs `jet test src/jetpack.jet --serial` over the assembled engine unit (about 559 claims), because the claims share process state. Every claim waits for the one before it.

log.text: Main 2026-11-07, from SpeedLead measurements (hosted engine unit, after #6684 fixes; host busy, load 12-40): `jet test src/jetpack.jet --serial` took 243 s (compile 55 s, claims about 188 s); without --serial 195 s, with the same 807/22/15 and the same 22 known failures. One clean parallel run is evidence that the claims share no state, not proof; dropping the flag means editing jetpack_engine_rows. Compiling the unit alone at load 7 takes 15.7 s. 715 claims take under 0.1 s each; four take 102 of 225 s: StoreIngestLate.jet:42 "store closure readers are serialized with registration and compaction" 57.8 s, StoreIngestLate.jet:31 18.0 s, Lifecycle.jet:302 14.9 s, NixCache.jet:784 11.5 s. strace of the 57.8 s claim shows it is CPU-bound in the store, with no child processes and temp files on tmpfs: every closure-graph load re-verifies every record (producer and metadata decode, receipt rehash, seal checks), and 70 ingest+load pairs make that quadratic. Under 1 minute needs incremental verification in the store (a trust-design change), plus parallel claims. Ruled out: per-test module-scope copies in sema (5.7 s sema.bodies at low load).

criteria.text: The wall time of the engine unit's compile and its serial claim run are measured on the batch host and recorded with the commit. Proof: a committed batch-host receipt.

Claims that share process state are isolated (each owns its state, or the shared state is per-claim), so the unit runs without --serial and every claim still passes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes with the engine unit run without the serial flag in Compiler/test.jet.
The engine unit's claims finish in under 1 minute wall. Proof: the engine-unit wall time in the packages suite receipt.

Every non-JetOS Rust module in crates/jetpack (including src/bin), jetpack-bin, jet-nix-eval, jet-store and the Jetpack-owned parts of jet-env-model and jet-pkg-model has a named Jet home under Jetpack/<Area>/Source/, listed in Jetpack/Bootstrap/sources.list, with its unit and integration tests ported and no second copy of anything Compiler/ owns. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter jetpack_port_coverage` (each Rust module maps to a sources.list entry). (was #3590 c1)

Every slice passes Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet and `jet test Compiler --profile packages` on O0, O1 and O2 (I9), with no `#Unsafe` lacking an audited reason and no new external dependency outside an approved bridge. Proof: `JET=jet jet Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet --deps-from-head` exits 0 and `jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes. (was #3590 c2)

Integrated proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes every Jetpack engine row and Check.jet passes on the integrated tree, with the receipt path and unit SHA recorded here. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages` plus the committed receipt. (was #3590 c13)

Jetpack/Integrations has its areas.list entry with its real dependencies (the CLI CompilerExtensionHost.jet uses it), and the Trust and CLI claims run in `jet test Compiler --profile packages`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Integrations`. (was #3590 c44)
pkg_json_render returns its EncodingError to the caller instead of an invariant panic. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter PackageModel/json_render_encoding_error`. (was #3590 c46)

The Jetpack Services and Store areas check with 0 errors once checking reaches function bodies (599 drift errors at the time of filing), and their claims run in `jet test Compiler --profile packages`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Services` and `--filter Store`. (was #3590 c49)

Jetpack/Store checks clean (no E0107 on IngestRequest), and the 3 Jet tests ported from hangar_store_v2 and receipt_store pass. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Store/hangar_store` and `--filter Store/receipt_store`. (was #3590 c50)

Every Jetpack area passes Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet on dev, and `jet test Jetpack/Publication/Tests/Diff.jet` runs (it reported E0957 on 0d1ea12f79). The 2026-11-04 compiler-slice failure came from check.sh, which 34ef2f2c43 deleted. Jetpack and Tower migrate every audited fixed-shape CLI, typed JSON, URL query, list equality, recursive-directory, ASCII and path, DataTree comparison and named domain-truthiness site to the Core helper; behavior and parity tests pass, and no local helper remains unless its occurrence-scoped manifest reason proves a different contract. `jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes, including the StoreCache.jet, StoreIngest.jet and NixStoreProjection.jet claims that call the Reuse functions (Reuse.rs had no inline tests). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Store`. (was #3590 c190)

cards.title: No C: full libc coverage in Jet (census libc against Core and the runtime, then fill every gap)
cards.body: Owner, 2026-11-08: "We should already have a lot of what libc covers just need to fill the gaps." Track full coverage of what a C libc provides (POSIX and C23: memory, strings, stdio and files, time and locale, process, signals, threads and sync, networking and name resolution, math, environment, users and groups, terminal, dynamic memory), as Jet-native Core or runtime surface. Step one is a census: every libc function family, with the Core or runtime API that already covers it, and the gaps. cards.title: No C: a Jet Linux sandbox replaces the bwrap binary shipped in the C toolchain pack
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-08 (Q8): "B4 BUT that is a longer term card I dont want done now. for the time being, ship bwrap until the sandbox is built PROPERLY in jet, make sure this task is not lost so we dont forget to remove bwrap in the future." Context: #6686 found no bwrap on a NixOS host, so jet cc refused with E1275. The stopgap ships bwrap (a C binary) in the C toolchain pack. This card builds the sandbox in Jet (namespaces plus landlock or seccomp, ratified D-PORTABLE1=A: Jet own sandbox) and removes bwrap. Longer term: not to start before the owner says so. Related: #6687 (Jet depends on no other language), #4268 (authority and sandbox boundaries).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c4 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: Process isolation for `jet cc` and every other sandboxed launch is done by Jet code (user, mount, pid and network namespaces, landlock rules or a seccomp filter) with the same confinement bwrap gave. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/jet_sandbox_refuses_`, one case per refused access.

The bwrap binary is gone from the C toolchain pack and every launch path, with no fallback, and the pack is re-pinned without it. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter no_bwrap` (git grep finds no bwrap in Compiler, Jetpack, Tools or the pack manifest).
On a host without unprivileged user namespaces, a sandboxed launch refuses with a registered error naming the missing kernel feature.

There is one canonical Core sandbox API: Foundation NativeSandbox.jet (tooling: arbitrary source, output and read-only mounts) and Core ProcessSpec.under (cwd-derived repository grants) become one implementation with one policy and no observable differences. The API shape is the ballot D-SANDBOX-API1, on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: git grep finds one sandbox policy implementation, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/sandbox_policy_single_home` passes.
A process spec's `.under(grant)` narrows authority through the shared runtime (`jet_std_process_spec_under` is registered).

Declared filesystem, process, network, environment, device and resource policy is enforced and recorded by the platform backend: a child runs under the native sandbox (Jetpack/Foundation/Source/NativeSandbox.jet, SandboxPolicy.jet) with a declared policy, each denied access fails, and the recorded policy matches. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/native_sandbox_policy_enforced` on Linux.

A launch's plan, transaction, descendants, limits, outputs and receipt share one policy digest and record the authority actually enforced. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter AgentExecutor/policy_digest_shared` on Linux.

Unsupported enforcement, denied access, an escape attempt, limit exhaustion, cancellation and child-process abuse each fail closed, with no leaked handle, secret or process. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter AgentExecutor/fails_closed_`, one case per failure on Linux.

cards.title: Core math completeness: correctly rounded results (CORE-MATH grade) and all of C23 math.h
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-08: "it needs to be portable and accurate. we want people to use jet for EVERYTHING including mathematics, simulations". G1Lead audit (musl 1.2.5 worst cases reproduced against MPFR 4.2.2): under 1 ulp: exp .51, exp2 .51, pow .52, log .52, log2 .55, cbrt .67, log10 .81, sin/cos .83, atan .86, log1p .90, expm1 .91, acos .93, asin .98; over 1 ulp: tan 1.01, erf 1.02, cosh 1.03, hypot 1.03, atan2 1.55, atanh 1.80, sinh 1.87, asinh 1.91, tanh 2.22, acosh 2.24, erfc 3.72, exp10 4.14, tgamma 15.9, lgamma 4.4e15 near its zeros, Bessel j0/j1/y0/y1 1e14-1e15 near zeros. Plan: port CORE-MATH (MIT) binary64 and binary32 per function family into Jet, worst gaps first (lgamma, tgamma, erfc, tanh, acosh, exp10, atan2, then the rest), each replacing its musl port in one cutover; Bessel needs its own accurate design (no correctly rounded binary64 implementation exists). Estimate about 150 agent-hours serial.
cards.checkSteps: per function: a committed MPFR-generated corpus (CORE-MATH .wc hard cases plus random inputs) shows 0 mismatches against correctly rounded bits on O0, O1, O2 and web; jet test never calls MPFR; the census marks each function CR

Harness and commands: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G1Lead-3/HANDOFF-6700.md. Next: find the sinpi memory hold on one chunk, then rerun with -P 4 in the heavy-job slot.

Criteria added from the card body and the slices so far. Landed in b6d: correctly rounded sinpi/cospi/tanpi (d8db0efaec), rsqrt/exp10 and the MPFR-CR harness (f0c28ff1e6). Slices 9-15 are in batch b7. G1Lead-2 owns this card.

criteria.text: binary32: every Core F32 elementary function (exp/log/pow/trig/hyperbolic/inverse, erf/erfc, tgamma/lgamma, cbrt, hypot, the pi variants) is correctly rounded to nearest, proven by an exhaustive scan of all 2^32 inputs against MPFR (f32scan receipts). Proof: the committed f32scan receipts with zero misrounded inputs per function.
binary64: the same functions in F64 are correctly rounded, proven against MPFR on the CORE-MATH worst-case corpus plus at least 10^8 random inputs per function, with 0 misrounded results.
criteria.evidence: dev bcc9c4b023 (CORE-MATH ports, train 1; Core/Math fn bodies identical on 6cea1699f9 except Int abs and Decimal decode, neither scanned): MPFR 4.2.2 scan, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G1Lead-3/f32mpfr ./run64.sh over 40 F64 fns (exp..atan2pi), CORE-MATH src/binary64/<fn>.wc corpus + 10^8 seeded random inputs each -> 0 misrounded finite results. Only diffs are conventions, not roundings: rsqrt(-0) = -inf (IEEE 754-2019, CORE-MATH agree; MPFR +inf) and sNaN operands to pow/hypot give qNaN (IEEE; MPFR has no sNaN). Receipt results64/SUMMARY; handoff HANDOFF-6700.md.

criteria.evidence: 18cd07d573 (on dev): math.rem_quo, math.remainder and math.fmod given two F32 arguments return an F32 through sema_call_try_core_math_f32 (computed in Float on the exactly widened operands and rounded once). rem_quo gives (rem: F32, quo: Int) through the internal Core __rem_quo_f32, and no public name is added. On the gate-p55 jet (dev 9623399213): `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter core_math_f32_exact_and_bit_functions_match_c23_on_every_tier` rc 0, 1/0 (the fmod, remainder and rem_quo corpora cover signed zeros, subnormals, infinities, NaN payloads, halfway and past-2^31 quotients against glibc 2.42 and musl remquof, at O0, O1, O2 and web); `--filter core_math_matches_musl_bit_for_bit_on_every_tier` rc 0, 1/0 (Float arguments keep Float results).

criteria.text: core.math's elementary functions accept F32 and return F32 at the same width: the Float-only source facade (Core/Math/Math.jet, e.g. `sin: fn(n: Float)`) gains the F32 forms the old sema accepted, with no widening.

Every C23 math.h function (float and double forms, frexp, ldexp, modf, remquo, nextafter, erf, tgamma, lgamma, rsqrt, exp10m1, exp2m1, log2p1, log10p1, the pi-trig family, pown, powr, rootn, compoundn and the rest) exists in core.math. Proof: a census #Test in Core/Math lists the C23 names and fails on any missing one (`jet test Core/Math`).

The inputs where musl 1.2.5 differs from the correctly rounded result are listed in Docs, with documented musl bugs named (such as acosh of large negative inputs returning a number instead of NaN). Proof: `git ls-files Docs | grep -i musl` names the list and each entry cites its input and both results.

cards.title: Native windows in pure Jet: a Wayland client that opens a window and presents frames, no external libraries
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-08: "i want jet to be able to draw to screen immediately with native windows using a full jet native framework/system asap no external dependencies. start with wayland support." Today the static native runtime never opens a window (RouteAGame.jet: the old bridge dlopened libraylib) and core.ui native is headless. Plan: a Wayland client written in Jet (wire protocol over the AF_UNIX socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY, wl_registry, wl_compositor, wl_shm with a memfd buffer passed by SCM_RIGHTS, xdg_wm_base/xdg_surface/xdg_toplevel, frame callbacks, wl_seat pointer and keyboard, the compositor keymap parsed in Jet), presenting the existing Jet software rasterizer canvas; then core.game.raylib windows and the core.ui host on top. X11 follows as a separate card.
cards.checkSteps: jet run of an example opens a native Wayland window on a stock compositor (GNOME/KDE/sway), draws animated content from the Jet rasterizer, takes keyboard and pointer input, resizes and closes cleanly; the executable links no external library (symbol census); a headless-compositor case proves it on O0, O1 and O2

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: c3 split into one-implementation, full Wayland and X11 criteria; proofs added.

t15a landed G6LeadC-13 (01b86931e7..8327f5ae47): the Wayland wire part's `net: core.net` broke every web build that imports core.ui (E3304). Fixed at the root: the target socket check judges only the program's own `use`, and ui.open reaches the wire part only under a comptime Linux branch. Proof: cases web_build 31/0, including web_ui_open_answers_no_display.

c1 scope decision (Main, 21:45 EST). The raylib census covers code, examples, tests, tools, registries, specs, guides, env and flake inputs, and gauntlet entries. It excludes Docs/audits, Docs/research and Docs/proposals (evidence and rationale), the decision IDs and ballot history in syntax-decisions.md and Tools/slate/ballots.mjs (decision history, owned by Tower), and Tools/tower/.tower. Within scope: the CLI --renderer help and Bundle.jet become headless|ui; the agent-eval area-games pkg is ported to core.ui or deleted, and its captured run records are deleted; the gauntlet game-frame author becomes the maintaining lane; the dead raylib_window.jet row leaves authority-streamline-sites.tsv; syntax-decisions prose that presents raylib as current is marked superseded by #6701.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (D-UI-BLEND1, ruled directly from the chat summary before a Tower ballot existed: 'use recommendation for one rule'): core.ui composites with ONE rule, sRGB-space source-over on premultiplied bytes, d = s + d*(255-sa)/255, on every surface (canvas, sprites, text, core.ui.font.blend); the linear-light path is removed. Proof: a case that asserts alpha 20 over #0B0B0D gives #1E1E20 on every surface at O0/O1/O2.
Renderer speed is tracked on child #6718 (owner: fastest renderer).

Owner 2026-11-09, after running a dev native-window demo: 'it is extremely choppy and ugly. i dont like the unrasterized text default in the pane, the header bar is way too bulky and should be dark mode by default but adapt to the user theme. those need to be fixed asap. also, I wanted the logo to work for the app that shows up in the taskbar, not in the header bar itself by default.' Measured: a headless 900x600 frame with a full gradient, ~15 shapes and ~7 text lines takes ~140 ms at O0 and ~55 ms at O2, against a 16.7 ms budget. draw_text still uses the 5x7 bitmap font. Dispatched to WaylandLead3 as top priority: rasterizer speed (a few ms per 1080p frame at O0), anti-aliased Atkinson text by default (the 5x7 font deleted), a slim header bar that is dark by default and follows the portal color-scheme and accent, the icon via xdg-toplevel-icon in the taskbar and not in the drawn frame, and a new showcase demo.

cards.title: Prove the runtime OS edge safe: leaf contracts, model checking, fault injection, checked mode
cards.body: Owner direction: find a way to prove the safety of the unsafe runtime layer, holistically. #6701 c4-c6 shrink the trusted base, make misuse unwritable through ownership and range types, and remove Linux hazards by design. This card proves what remains: every runtime syscall leaf against a written contract. Kernel-enforced confinement (a default seccomp allowlist) is a separate owner ballot. A public claim that the edge is proven needs a passing adversarial review per AGENTS.md. Limit: this proves Jet against the kernel documented behaviour, not kernel bugs.
cards.checkSteps: each item has a case or gate that fails when broken

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1: c1, c3 and c5 split into one outcome each (LEAFPROVE, FAULTINJ, WIREFUZZ, EDGEREVIEW); each criterion names its proof.

criteria.text: Every runtime syscall leaf carries a machine-checkable contract: precondition, postcondition, and frame (which bytes and fds it may touch, with no arithmetic overflow).
The syscall number and argument registers emitted for every runtime leaf at O0, O1 and O2 match a committed table derived from the kernel's syscall_64.tbl, and a mismatch fails.

A pure-Jet model of the fd table and mappings runs at least one million random operation sequences against the real kernel with no divergence. Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetRuntime --filter fd_model_differential` with a committed receipt of the run.

`--checked-alloc` keeps a shadow ledger of open fds and mappings and checks every leaf call against it (owned and open, in range, not after close), and the cases and golden suites pass in this mode. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CheckedAlloc/fd_ledger_` and a committed receipt of the cases and golden suites under --checked-alloc.

Drift gates: the unsafe-site ratchet can only fall, every leaf has a contract and a proof record, and `jet audit foreign` stays clean. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter unsafe_site_ratchet` and `jet audit foreign` exits 0.
A symbolic checker written in Jet, with no external solver, proves each runtime syscall leaf's JetIR against its contract, and a leaf without a passing proof record fails the build.
A fault-injection test mode makes every runtime syscall leaf return each documented errno (EINTR, EAGAIN, ENOMEM, EMSGSIZE, truncated control data), and every error path runs.
The Wayland wire and XKB parsers are fuzzed over a fixed seed budget with no hang or panic.

A dated adversarial review in Docs/Audits tries to break the claim that the runtime OS edge is proven, and passes before any public text makes that claim (AGENTS.md). Proof: `git ls-files Docs/Audits` lists the review, and git grep finds no public claim older than it.

cards.title: A range-typed Int(lo..hi) argument is rejected for a plain Int parameter (E0108); no explicit widening exists
cards.body:
Found by WaylandLead (#6701 c5, range-typed OS-edge params). Seed a0_039:
plain: fn(value: Int) -> Int { value * 2 }
ranged: fn(size: Int(1..1073741824)) -> Int { plain(size) }   // E0108
Int{size} and size.raw() are rejected too; only arithmetic (size + 0) widens. A value of a refined range type is always a valid Int, so widening to the unrefined type should be implicit (or have one ratified explicit spelling). Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/WaylandLead/probe/range_widen_repro.jet.
cards.checkSteps: jet run of the repro prints 10 on O0, O1 and O2; a case under tests/cases covers the call, a return and an assignment of a range value to Int

log.text: c2 sweep by G5DevX-1 on dev 16f96f3c7a. Narrow form: git grep -nE "wrapping\([a-z_]+ \+ 0\)" -- Core Compiler Tools tests hits only Core/Sys/Sys.jet (14 sites), all removed by G5DevX-range1b2, so 0 hits on its tree. Broad form: git grep -nE "[A-Za-z_)\]] \+ 0\b"; every other hit is Float arithmetic (+ 0.5 and the like), index symmetry (base + 0, start + 0 in generated lexer rows), Int + 0 on an Int, comments, or awk/shell text, none of them a widening workaround. Meets after range2 (b15) and range1b2 (b16) land and the range-widening cases pass at O0/O1/O2.

Main sweep 2026-11-12: still E0108 on seed-b13 (repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/r6704/main.jet). spec.md says safe widening is implicit, so Int(lo..hi) to Int is implicit with no new spelling; routed to G5DevX-1 as G5DevX-range1.

criteria.text: Passing, returning or assigning an Int(lo..hi) value where Int is expected type-checks and runs with the same value on O0, O1 and O2 (case under tests/cases).

A ranged Int or a narrower fixed-width integer passes where Int is expected at each place, at O0, O1 and O2, and narrowing stays refused. Proof: the tests/cases range-widening case covers every position and its refused case. No `+ 0` widening workaround remains in Core, Compiler, Tools or tests.

cards.title: Wayland window and ui stack: measured best against every alternative
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-08): the native Wayland window is good enough for now (the compositor-paced frame loop ran "buttery smooth" at 240 Hz). Land the deterministic functionality first, then hill-climb this card until it is near perfect. The window and ui stack must beat every strong alternative on the same compositor and display, idle and under a full-machine load. The alternatives are GTK4 (frame clock), Qt 6 (QQuickWindow), SDL3, winit with softbuffer, a Chromium/Electron requestAnimationFrame page, and a hand-written C wl_surface.frame + wp_presentation loop as the machine ceiling. The xkb keymap is measured against libxkbcommon. Peer programs stay outside the tree. Each loss is fixed at its root in the runtime leaves or the loop, never by dropping a feature (AGENTS.md performance gate).
cards.plan: Start after the Wayland functionality (frame loop, CSD, HiDPI and fractional scale, cursors, clipboard, multi-window, keyboard) and X11 have landed. Build the same bouncing-square program and a resize/HiDPI/text scene in each alternative, measure every metric in the criteria, rank the losses in Pareto order and fix them.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c3 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

cards.title: Safe read-only file maps expose bytes another process can change, and fault with SIGBUS when the file shrinks
cards.body: Found by the D-MAP-WRITE1 adversarial review (Docs/audits/2026-11-08-D-MAP-WRITE1-review.md). files.map gives safe code a borrowed byte view of a MAP_PRIVATE read-only mapping. Private mapping is not a snapshot: an external write changed an already borrowed byte from 3 to 9 (probe Current.jet). An external truncate makes the next access of a borrowed byte die with Fault [SIGBUS] and exit 135 (probes Shrink.jet and CFreeLead's MapShrink.jet); the shared flock is advisory and does not prevent it. Safe Jet must not observe a borrowed value changing under it, and an I/O failure in safe code must surface as a typed error or a registered, explained fault, never a raw signal death. This holds whatever D-MAP-WRITE1 decides.
cards.plan: Decide the I1 contract for read-only maps: copy-on-read, or a view the runtime keeps stable (e.g. MAP_PRIVATE plus a seal or lease where the kernel offers one), or an Unsafe-only borrowed view with a safe copying API. Then make the truncation case a typed IOError or a registered fault with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot, with one meaning on every tier. A choice that changes public API or behavior goes to an owner ballot first.

log.text: Finding for c5 (PrecompiledCore-4 measurement, 2026-11-15): on dev 8a24784b9b, core.files Map of a 461 MB file took 192-265 ms and 454-903 MB RSS to read 21.6 MiB of records, because mapped.bytes copies the whole mapped file. c5's zero-copy views must remove that copy; core.bodies uses positioned reads (read_at, 24 ms, +2.1 MB RSS) meanwhile.

c5 split (G10Safe-1, 2026-11-13): Linux lease, copy and tmpfs paths are built and proved on ext4 and tmpfs. Still open: the clone path needs a btrfs or XFS host (none on the dev machine), the Windows deny-write and APFS/ReFS clone paths, and the #Unsafe raw map (S3).

criteria.text: A safe borrowed view of a mapped file never observes a byte change made by another process after the borrow, on every applicable tier.

Another process truncates and rewrites a mapped file during safe access, and the program keeps reading the bytes it mapped (including past the new end) with no SIGBUS or other fault and no change visible through the map, on every applicable tier (D-MMAP-STABLE1=A).

(was #2790 c1) Implementation-only closure: mapped files use the existing read-only view ownership mechanism, return checked view-shaped types through nested Option/Result/Shared carriers, root every borrowed result in the receiver mapping, and route O0, O1, O2 and web where applicable behavior through the same mmap Prelude kernels [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today] (was #4620 c11)
criteria.evidence: dev fbd660ba2f (G9Web-6706c4): Examples Systems/Files/FilesMapViews returns mapped windows through Option, Result, a named pair, a list and a Shared carrier (guard_read gives View<U8>? from SharedGuard<MappedFile>, read by a task through a handle copy), each rooted in the receiver map, through the one mmap Prelude kernel. The web target returns a typed IOError (ENOSYS). Lander ran on seed-b14: golden FilesMapViews PASS 3 (o0, o1, o2), golden FilesMapAdvise PASS 3, ui mapped_window_outlives_its_map PASS 1 (E2305), and DiagnosticRows --check rc 0 after the E2305 page regeneration.

criteria.text: D-MMAP-STABLE1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). files.map gives zero-copy views that another process cannot change: it maps a private file-system clone where the file system can (btrfs, xfs, APFS, ReFS); otherwise it holds the file with a lease on Linux or deny-write sharing on Windows and copies only when a writer arrives; otherwise it copies into an unnamed temp file. Only file systems that cannot be written at all (squashfs, erofs) map directly. mapped.kind() reports Clone, Held or Copy, and an #Unsafe raw map remains for shared live bytes. Proof: c1 and c2's cases on a clone-capable and a non-clone file system, plus a case printing kind() for each path.

cards.title: Generic call to a trait method returning `T? Never!` loses the optional and fails in the backend (ICE)
cards.body: Found by SqliteLead on the b6c compiler (#6695 slice 8). A generic call `fn<H: Host>` to a trait method declared `-[]> T? Never!` loses the optional, and the backend rejects it: `ir.build unlowered: ... binder got of type ?[U8] bound to a value of type [U8]`. The smallest repro is the trait `Src{grab -[]> [U8]? Never!; grab2 -> Int? Never!}`, called generically. It works without `Never!`. That breaks I2 (a backend rejection of checked code must not happen) and the one-mechanism promise for effect rows. A workaround is in core.db: VdbeAux.jet Host.vtab_take_errmsg is declared without `Never!`; remove it once fixed. Criteria: a regression case in tests/cases compiles and runs on O0/O1/O2; the workaround is removed.

criteria.text: A generic call to a trait method declared `-[]> T? Never!` keeps the optional: the trait `Src { grab -[]> [U8]? Never!; grab2 -> Int? Never! }` called through `fn<H: Src>` builds and runs with no backend rejection (I2). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter generic_trait_method_optional_never_keeps_the_optional` on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Release cut in 10 minutes or less: faster golden and cases suites
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-09): the whole seed-cut process (preflight, self-host chain, packs, the golden/ui/cases gates, tag and publish) takes at most 10 minutes of wall-clock time. Today a fresh cut takes about 37 minutes: chain ~3, packs ~2, golden ~10.6, ui ~2, cases ~20 (the suites run one after another with 4 shards x --jobs; the baseline side and the retries add more). Speed it up without weakening the gate. Every row still runs or is soundly reused by content identity; no dropped rows, no easier tier, I9 parity is kept, and timeouts are not hidden as flakes.
cards.plan: 1. Profile one fresh admit: wall time per phase, and per-row cost split by compile, link, run and harness overhead; find the slowest rows and the idle cores. 2. Find the levers: concurrency (shards and jobs sized to cores and memory, the three suites run concurrently), baseline rows reused from the previous seed's recorded evidence instead of rerunning the release side, fine-grained input-hash reuse of candidate rows, compiler start-up and per-row compile cost (cached Core and Prelude artifacts, one compile shared by the O0/O1/O2 rows where the meaning allows), fewer process spawns, and timeout and retry policy. 3. Implement in Tools/release and the testkit, and measure the result on a real admit.

They stay in the inbox for the lane that resumes #6717.
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from no goal to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

OWNER 2026-11-09: take the win now and don't pay for double runs. SuitePerfLead's subset release column is approved (c2 edited). SuitePerfLead builds it as SuitePerfLead-5, with candidate rows started early beside pack, jetpack and engine.

SuitePerfLead-4 landed on dev 3761b75b0c (jet_rt_host_restart, 2a). 2b shared Core: correct on 2427 rows (2 normalized diffs open) but no speedup (fork CoW plus a double fork); told to make the shared heap immortal, use one fork, and make the cold front end 2x faster. The subset-release-column proposal changes c2's lost-row comparison, so it goes to the owner.

Owner 2026-11-09: 'im sure vitest would run it much faster than under 10 minutes'. Asked whether in-run sharing of checked Core per worker is allowed; the owner chose 'Both': share checked Core within one run (nothing kept across runs) AND make the cold front end >=2x faster. Estimate with sharing: about 2.5 min at 24 threads.

Owner 2026-11-09 on L1: a release admit may use 24 threads on cores 8-31; cores 0-7 stay free for the owner. At 24 threads, <=10 min needs the compiler front end ~2x faster (today's estimate is 15.9 min).

SuitePerfLead measurement (cold, s7): one row (NumericMethods jet run) = 640 ms wall, of which Core lex+parse 290 ms (3.18 MB at ~11 MB/s), register 70, comptime 70, sema.finalize 170, backend+link 30; jet invocations are 96-97% of suite CPU and the front end ~85%. Suite CPU 22,900 CPU-s for both sides. Floors: today 31.8 min at 12 threads, 11.9 at 32; front end 2x faster 18.3/6.9; front end at hand-optimized ~50 ms/compile 5.7/2.1. Levers: L1 CPU allotment (owner call: the admit takes the whole machine), L2 front-end throughput (Core parse 23.9%, finalize 25.3%, registration 8.5%, string clone/hash 15.7%), L3 single-thread compiles in a full pool (-15%), L4 suite overlap (-2.5 min, Tools/release, in progress), L5 quadratic long line under an inline package header.

Owner 2026-11-09: 'i do not want caching or incremental builds etc. I WANT THE TESTING SPEED TO BE BASICALLY AS FAST AS HAND OPTIMIZED MACHINE CODE.' Reuse levers dropped; the target is raw cold-path throughput. Probe: a cold jet run -O0 of Examples/Math/NumericMethods.jet takes 673 ms and jet check 1.9 s.

criteria.text: A fresh release admit of a dev commit with no reuse of candidate rows from an earlier admit, on this workstation, runs from the preflight to publish in at most 10 minutes of wall-clock time, with its timestamped log as evidence. Proof: the committed timestamped admit log.

The gate keeps its strength. Nothing is cached or reused between runs and nothing is built incrementally (owner 2026-11-09): every run starts from source. Within ONE run, each test worker may parse and check Core once and share that checked Core in memory across the rows it runs (owner 2026-11-09, the vitest model); each row still compiles and runs its own fresh native program on the candidate. A proof run shows the shared-Core verdicts are byte-identical to per-row cold compiles on every row. OWNER 2026-11-09 (later): the release (previous seed) column runs only on the rows that fail on the candidate, the release's known-failing rows, and rows whose files changed since the baseline commit, with gains and losses judged exactly as before; every candidate row still runs. There are no new skips and no dropped tiers, and the compiler front end itself also gets at least 2x faster cold (owner: both). Proof: the committed diff of shared-Core verdicts against per-row cold compiles is empty, and the admit log shows every candidate row run.

The flaky-timeout rate under the new concurrency is no higher than today's: retried TIMEOUT rows are counted and reported. Proof: the retried TIMEOUT count in the admit log against the prior baseline.

cards.title: core.ui renderer is the fastest 2D renderer: gauntlet cells against Blend2D, Skia raster, tiny-skia and cairo/pixman, with an asm-parity ceiling
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-09: 'we should be the fastest renderer especially since we have top to bottom full control over the whole language stack.' Today a 900x600 frame (a full gradient, ~15 shapes, ~7 text lines) takes ~140 ms at O0 and ~55 ms at O2. Under the AGENTS.md performance gate, core.ui's rasterizer (Core/Ui/Draw.jet and the font rasterizer) gets required cells in the GUI-applications area. For each workload, Jet/peer must be below 1.00 against every matched CPU 2D renderer (Blend2D, Skia's raster backend, tiny-skia, cairo/pixman), and Jet/ceiling at most 1.00 against a hand-written SIMD reference (asm-parity) doing the same work, on every tier (O0 included, since  is what users run) and in both cycles and bytes. The workloads: solid and gradient fills, anti-aliased paths and shapes (rects, rounded rects, circles, polygons), alpha blending (straight and premultiplied), anti-aliased glyph text, image blits and scaling, and full-frame redraw at 1080p and 4K. Use the whole stack: SIMD in the runtime or Core through vetted internals, compiler codegen (bounds-check elimination, vectorizing span loops) and data layout. Fix compiler-side gaps at their root in the compiler, not by hand-unrolled Jet. Semantics and pixels are identical on every tier.
cards.plan: 1. Gauntlet cells plus peer harness: same scenes, same pixels (compared as images), peers built at their best settings. 2. asm-parity ceiling references with the best known technique (AVX2/AVX-512 span fill and blend, analytic coverage rasterization). 3. Profile Jet per workload; split the gap into rasterizer algorithm, codegen and runtime. 4. Close the gap: algorithm first (span and coverage pipelines like Blend2D's), then codegen defects as compiler cards. 5. Gate: every cell passes both stages.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). AA Atkinson text: 7 lines in 344 us at O0. Byte-identical to the per-pixel reference. Remaining: span/coverage pipeline, translucent fill, a [U32] canvas, and gauntlet cells. Compiler defects are on a child card.

Each has an image-equality check against every peer (Blend2D, Skia raster, tiny-skia, cairo/pixman) and a hand-written SIMD ceiling reference. cards.title: Codegen: pixel-loop throughput (fill leaf through a &struct field place, slow U64 arithmetic at O2, O0 indexed stores ~3 ns/element)
cards.body: Found by WaylandLead3 while speeding up the core.ui rasterizer (#6718); the renderer lane's Micro.jet repro is gone, so the proofs are cases and the pixel-loops gauntlet entry. (1) The O2 fill leaf doesn't fire for stores through a &struct field place: 1.15 ns/B vs 0.07 ns/B for a local. (2) U64 arithmetic takes ~10 ns/iteration even at O2, no faster than O0. (3) An O0 indexed store costs ~3 ns/element, so per-pixel Jet code can't redraw 1080p in a few ms at O0 (jet run). Fix each at its root in the compiler (IR/backend), not with library workarounds. The same semantics on every tier (I9).

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from no goal to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

criteria.text: Stores through a &struct field place reach the O2 fill leaf, as stores to a local do. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter fill_leaf_through_a_struct_field_place` shows the fill leaf in the O2 IR of the field-place loop.

U64 arithmetic at O2 compiles to native 64-bit instructions with no per-operation call or check beyond Jet's overflow meaning. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter u64_arithmetic_is_native_at_o2` (the O2 IR of the loop has no runtime call).

An O0 indexed store costs no more than the bounds check plus the store, so per-pixel code can redraw 1080p in a few ms under jet run. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry pixel-loops` reports at most 1 ns per element for the O0 indexed-store row.

cards.title: Games: Jet ships every primitive needed to build a full high-resolution 3D game (no engine)
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-09): Jet is to be the best language for making games, so it must be capable of rendering full high-resolution 3D games. Do not build a 3D rendering engine now, but ship all the tools and primitives needed to make one: GPU device, swapchain and presentation on the native window, buffers, textures, render passes and pipelines, shaders written in Jet (D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1), GPU compute, 3D math (vectors, matrices, quaternions, SIMD), image and mesh asset loading, raw and relative input, audio, frame pacing and GPU timing. Related cards: #c0ce571w (shader stages and pipelines), #c0li0kor (GPU kernels), #c084tcrl (device providers), #c0776o2m (game platform layer), #c0ba141x (linking model: GPU drivers need the platform loader). First step: a gap map against code, then ballots for every public API.

criteria.text: A dated gap map (Docs/Research) lists each primitive a high-resolution 3D game needs and, for each, what Jet has today, proven by code, an example or a probe, and what is missing, the dependencies, the owner gates and the related cards.
Every missing public API or new syntax has a Tower ballot that has passed adversarial review before it reaches the owner.

An executable example draws a lit, textured, depth-tested 3D mesh of at least 100k triangles at 2560x1440 through the GPU in a native window, using only shipped primitives and no engine code in Core, with golden-tested output (headless image hash) on every applicable tier.
Gauntlet cells measure the GPU path (frame time and draw submission cost) against C with Vulkan and Rust with wgpu, with an asm-parity ceiling reference, per the performance gate.

cards.title: core.ui GPU acceleration in native Jet, with the same look native and in the browser
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-09, on the Showcase: 'it would also be excellent if it can be gpu accelerated - again with native jet support, not some additional dsl or sub language, but native jet', and 'we want this to look the same whether it is running in a native app or in a browser'. Standing direction: one unified GPU language built into core Jet (ratified markers: #Shader for graphics, D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1=B; Kernel for compute, D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1), working on any GPU out of the box, with no per-vendor or per-OS DSLs. Conflict: D-GPU-UI1=A keeps desktop defaults on software (a static single file, no driver loading), so a GPU default on desktop needs a new owner ballot that revises it, tied to the linking-model ballot #c0ba141x (GPU drivers need the platform loader). Open technical questions for the ballot: GPU rasterization isn't bit-identical across vendors, so 'same look' must be defined (bit-identical through the software path vs perceptually identical through the GPU), and how a static musl binary reaches the system Vulkan/WebGPU driver.

criteria.text: An adversarially reviewed owner ballot (revising D-GPU-UI1) decides the desktop and web GPU default for core.ui, the fallback, the driver-loading model, and what 'the same look native and in the browser' means, with same-program alternatives. Proof: `timeout 120 node Tools/tower/tower.mjs decision show` for the D-GPU-UI1 revision shows it ratified with its review.

core.ui draws through the GPU from native Jet code only (#Shader/#Kernel), with no shader-language source, per-vendor path or DSL in the repository, on Linux native and in the browser. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter UI/GPUDraw` on Linux native and web, and `git ls-files "*.wgsl" "*.glsl" "*.hlsl" "*.metal"` prints nothing.

The same Showcase program renders the same look native and in the browser, proven by headless checksums or a perceptual-difference bound the ballot fixes, on every applicable tier. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter UI/ShowcaseSameLook` on native and web.

cards.title: I1: branch lowerings carry a move from one path onto the other, so values leak (same class as the ?? fallback leak)
cards.body: ReplMem's audit after fixing ir_or_fallback (ReplMem-1): these lowerings in Compiler/JetIR lower user code inside a branch without saving and joining binding ownership, so a .move() on one path disowns the binding on the other path too and the value is never dropped. ir_short_circuit (&&/|| right side), ir_condition .And, ir_optional_call (x?.f(y.move())), ir_range_switch and ir_mixed_switch (arm fall-through), the require/require_eq message branches and the contract message (BuildContracts.jet), and contract post clauses under present. Fix them all through the shared save/restore plus ir_meet_paths join, as for the valued if and ??. Separate residual: about 12 MB per REPL turn inside jet_eval_native_load (the per-compile native session's image and stub buffers).

criteria.text: I1 use-after-free in safe Jet, found by G1Lead4 on seed-t21, 2026-11-11 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G1Lead-4/out/miscompile-push-break.jet). Inside `loop item in items { path: "dir/{item}"; loop _ in 0..<2 { out.push(path); break } }`, `out` ends up holding freed text (it prints `got  ,got  ,got  ` instead of `dir/c,dir/b,dir/a`): the break path frees `path` after push has moved or shared it into `out`. Same class as c-branch moves, a move on one control path carried onto another. The fix is in the shared lowering of moves and drops across break and continue edges, not in this loop shape. The repro becomes a case printing the right list on O0/O1/O2, plus variants with continue, a labeled outer break, `?? return` and a `match` arm exit, all under the leak and sanitizer checks.

cards.title: I1: values leak: boxed trait values are never dropped, and branch lowerings carry a move from one path onto the other
cards.body: ReplMem (2026-11-09): a trait-value row (Compiler/JetIR BuildTypes.jet:286) is a Pointer row with no drop and no clone, so a boxed trait value has no drop glue and its payload leaks. A strong_count probe leaks one per binding. In the compiler, Pipeline.jet's compiler_queries (a JetEvalCompilerQueryHost trait value) holds a Shared context whose eval_config.native keeps the whole JetEvalNativeSession (about 3.25 MB image plus the child) alive on every compile: the REPL residual of about 12 MB per turn. The fix gives trait values drop glue that dispatches on the payload's implementer, keeping today's observable copy and alias semantics as the spec states them, and handles move-receiver dynamic calls.

log.text: Board cleanup: #6724 (the same leak class) merged here; its open census criterion is c5.

Main sweep 2026-11-12 on seed-b13: c4 still fails. jet repl fed 1 binding turn peaks at 206.8 MB and 30 turns at 251.2 MB (systemd-run Memory peak), about 1.5 MB per turn against the 1 MB bound; 30 turns took 28.0 s. Inputs in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/r6727.

A trait value can hold an instantiation of a generic type that implements the trait, and a dynamic call reaches its implementation on O0, O1 and O2. cards.title: jet debug's contract on the self-hosted toolchain: the DAP wire, honest session states, accepted revisions and one watch parser
cards.body:
Destination: `jet debug` keeps a Jet-level contract on the self-hosted toolchain. `--break` and `--dap` drive one session. Attach, pause, restart and raw frames work over the production DAP wire, or are refused with E2236. Every end state is honest. Breakpoints and values refer to the accepted revision, and inspection never changes the guest. Watches parse with the compiler's parser. DAP has conditional breakpoints, logpoints and evaluate, and its speed is measured against lldb.

The tests/cases/debug/dap_cli_* rows in tests/known-failing.tsv belong to this card.

Related cards (2026-11-15 split): debug info and values #6918, record and replay #6919.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

Decision (Main, within approved scope): jet debug takes a built image as well as a source file (usage debug [<file.jet|image>]). The card's stale-binary and same-image timing criteria already presume debugging a built image. With lldb gone, this gives E2203 its deterministic carrier: a text file passed as the image (tests/cli/debug_image_without_jet_debug_info_e2203.txt); the lldb carrier is deleted. SUB GoalsB-5-native-debugger (c25, c23) is queued for cycle 190.

The G9 slot (GoalsB-5-2) takes it after its returned fixes; G9 is unstaffed until an agent snowballs past G6. Owner: GoalsB-5-2 (Pareto order 6730, 4632, 6918, 6841, 6919).

External tools serve only as comparators (as in #6730 c29) or as optional interop for users who bring them. jet debug owns breakpoints, stepping, locals and values itself; lldb is only the timing comparator in c29.

cards.title: Core range fill: one call fills a span of a list or buffer (owner: no ballot)
cards.body: OWNER RULING 2026-11-09 (chat): no ballot; build it with an idiomatic Jet API design. The UI canvas's full redraw is ~15 ms at 2560x1440 (36 ms at 3440x1362), and 74% of it is per-byte fill stores, about a 5.2 ms floor, because Jet has no range-write primitive. Add a whole-span fill on lists and buffers that the runtime lowers to memset/word stores, with one meaning on every tier (I9). The canvas fill uses it. Target: a full redraw ≤ 6 ms at 2560x1440 O2. It needs a paired perf cell (the plain loop against the fill) per the performance gate, plus an example with golden output.

log.text: Spelling decision (Main, 2026-11-10, within the owner ruling that a public whole-span fill needs no ballot). xs.fill(range, value) is the plain form. xs.fill_repeat(range, pattern) repeats a multi-element pattern across the span, for RGBA pixels and gradient rows. Neither clamps: a range outside 0..len stops with the same bounds fault as range indexing, and an empty pattern stops the same way; a span that is not a whole number of patterns ends with a partial pattern. Both methods share the one fast path that replaces the internal xs.__fill, and every caller moves in one cutover. G6Lead is building it.

Landed in train 2 (dev c057ea659d): 75ae287c5f makes core.ui opaque fills write in place through xs.__fill and deletes the stitch rebuild; a5a8142d89 gives the program one built-in face. WaylandLead3-10cr measured a full 2560x1440 redraw at 4.9-5.2 ms on its compiler (it was 223-240 ms). Still open: __fill is internal, so the public spelling, the perf pair and the example remain; criteria 1-4 track them.

criteria.text: A public, idiomatic whole-span fill on lists and byte buffers (not a double-underscore internal) lowers to memset or word stores, with one meaning on O0, O1, O2 and web (I9).

cards.body: OWNER HARD REQUIREMENT (2026-11-09): acronyms are all caps in types AND file names, Title Case otherwise (Core/Net/TLS.jet, not Core/Net/Tls.jet). S66 and D-ONCE-CASE1 already require this for type names (E0358) and name the lexicon for file names, but nothing enforces file names. A census of dev (lexicon Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Acronyms.jet) finds 156 distinct file and folder names with a word-cased acronym (642 path hits), e.g. Ast.jet, Cbor.jet, Cli/, Db/, Http/, Tls.jet, CanonicalJson.jet. Cutover landed on dev: ba783d11b9 (tree a74ed030aa, parent aa8715dacd), built from scripts only (genmap, rewrite, repair, restore, digests, fixups in the Main titlecase lane). cards.title: Moving a task &&name capture inside the task body is a false E0121 at the capture mark
cards.body: Found by WaylandLead3 on a0_042. owned: Box{..}; child: task &&owned { consume(owned) } with consume(b: &&Box) reports 'owned was consumed by consume, so it can't be used here' at the capture mark, with no later use. The same happens for 'mine: owned' and 'owned :=' inside the body. The capture hands ownership into the task, so a move inside the body is the task's own last use. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT-style scratch file a.jet (copied into the card's case when fixed).

criteria.text: Moving a task `&&name` capture inside the body (a call taking `&&`, a let binding, a `:=` rebinding) checks clean and runs on O0, O1 and O2 with the value dropped exactly once. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/task_capture_move_in_body_`, one case per form, each failing on a0_042.
A real use of the captured name after the body's move still reports E0121 at the later use.

A value taken by a task `&&name` capture runs its Close exactly once when the task drops it, for plain and grouped tasks on O0, O1 and O2, the same as a local or call-taken value (on seed-b14 it never runs: an I1 leak). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/task_capture_close_once_`, one case per form printing the close line.

cards.title: A package's authority.allow takes a scoped grant with the same meaning as jet run --allow
cards.body: `jet run --allow='FS.Read("<path>")'` confines reads to that path (spec.md, reference/cli.md, tests/cases/authority/run_allow_read_path_confines_reads_to_the_granted_paths.case). The package model refuses the same scoped grant in a manifest's `authority.allow` and accepts a scope only in `deny` or on FFI. Its message also wrongly calls the grant "a parameterized memory denial" (Jetpack Blocks/Authority.jet:315). Examples/Modules/Packages/PluginFailure/package.jet and tests/run/Foundations/Capabilities put `FS.Read("<dir>")` in allow, so their manifests fail to parse. One meaning per form (I8): a scoped grant in allow means what the flag means. Found by G6Meta-73's manifest round trip.

log.text: c2 is partly proved (G5DevX-2, gate-p29, dev 72fc3a5f3c): golden PluginFailure 1/0. The Capabilities manifest parses: jet check tests/run/Foundations/Capabilities/run.jet reports only E1257 plugin-interface errors, and its golden row is KNOWN-FAILING for #4599 (no guest build). A refused scope has a registered E1221 message with ui snapshot authority_scope_names_its_argument_as_a_string, and "parameterized memory denial" now applies only to Mem. Still open: the Capabilities run case, which cannot pass until #4599.
G5DevX-2 (2026-11-13): c2 holds except tests/run/Foundations/Capabilities, known-failing under #4599 (no sandbox build target for capability_guest.wasm). c2 is blocked on #4599.

Decision by Main within the card's approved scope (2026-11-11): a scoped path in a manifest's authority.allow is resolved against the directory that holds the manifest, while a scoped path in --allow is resolved against the working directory where it is typed. The grant's meaning (kernel confinement, no escape by .. or symbolic link) is identical. Reason: an author's grant must not change with where the user runs the program; working-directory resolution would turn FS.Read(".") into a grant of the user's current directory. G6Meta-76 implements it, with a two-directory case.

criteria.text: The package model accepts a scoped FS.Read/FS.Write grant in authority.allow, and a run of that package is confined exactly as `--allow` confines it (same E1803 refusal and wording). Proof: a tests/cases/authority case running a package whose manifest grants FS.Read("<dir>") in allow, with a read inside and a read outside the grant.

The rule: a host read whose value can change what the program does or prints is declared under its own effect; a read that is an internal nonce or the process's view of itself, and cannot change observable behavior, is exempt and listed as such in the inventory. Applied: H3 declare Time, Rand and Env on the core.service entry points that read them. H4 drop the timestamp from the JSON coercion audit (it adds a hidden clock read for no user value). H5 declare Env on the TUI terminal reads (TERM, COLUMNS and similar change the output). H6 and H7 exempt the temp-name and atomic-write pid nonces. H8 declare Env on path.home(). H9 exempt the PATH lookup as part of Exec, which resolves a program by name, and the Exec docs say so. H10 exempt /proc/self introspection. cards.title: Peer floor, enforced structurally: Jet is faster and uses less peak memory than every other language
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-11 late. A Jet program must be faster and use less peak memory than the same program in any other language. Only highly optimized hand-written machine code is exempt, and Jet aims as close to it as it can. A loss to any peer on wall time or peak memory is a codegen, runtime or Core failure. It is fixed generally, structurally and robustly in the mechanism every program uses, never per cell, so that the result holds for programs nobody measured. The machine ceiling stays the hill-climbing stage (G13): its ratio is reported, but it holds no cell until the owner opens it.

log.text: Main 2026-11-12, found by G11Speed-4 measuring c3: the gauntlet's run tier reuses each compiled peer's binary-only row (rust, c, zig, go), comparing jet run (a cold compile plus the run) with a prebuilt binary. That is mismatched evidence, and it contradicts the ratified run-cell rule: jet run time-to-answer is gated, after an edit and on a repeat run, against lua, luajit, python3 and node; the hello cell must come within 0.5 ms of a minimal hand-written program; the first run after install is reported only. The manifest's report_contract.peer_measurement ratio_tiers [aot, run], which reuses peer rows for every Jet tier, is the defect. G11Speed-4 is fixing the manifest contract and run.mjs so run-tier ratios use only the interpreted peers and compiled peers gate aot and build time. The c3 census waits for that fix and runs on b12. Sieve smoke on b11: aot beats all 5 peers on wall and peak; jet run is 0.73 s / 271 MB, all front end over Core (load 280 ms, comptime.bodies 210 ms, core_demand 140 ms, finalize 130 ms), which is the #6759 root.

criteria.text: The perf gate encodes the peer floor: on the canonical manifest it fails every required cell where Jet/peer is at or above 1.00 on wall time or on peak memory for any matched peer, names the cell, peer, metric and ratio, and reports the asm-ceiling ratio without failing on it. A unit test plants one time loss and one memory loss and expects both refusals.
criteria.evidence: G11Speed-G40 landed on dev 6ca4d72969 (tool-only: Tools/gauntlet/harness run.mjs, status.mjs, measurement-manifest.test.mjs, matrix.json). Lander5 loop 2026-11-12 02:3x on HEAD 70cfb9499a plus the patch (seed-b10 jet@a0.0.45#c089d4d3), rc 0 on each: node --test --test-name-pattern="the peer floor fails a planted wall-time or peak-memory loss" Tools/gauntlet/harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs (tests 1 pass 1 fail 0); --test-name-pattern="a cell passes on the peer floor; its ceiling ratio is reported only" (1/1, fail 0); --test-name-pattern="the matrix encodes the peer floor and the reported machine ceiling" (1/1, fail 0); node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/status.test.mjs (10/10); node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/integrated-gate.test.mjs (6/6). The gate fails a cell at Jet/peer >= 1.00 on wall or peak memory for any matched peer, names cell/peer/metric/ratio, and reports the ceiling ratio without failing. Out: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lander/loop/out/G11Speed-G40/{1..6}.out.

criteria.text: Every required cell measures peak memory for Jet and every matched peer with the same method. A cell or peer without a memory reading is reported as uncovered and fails the gate.
