Out: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lander/loop/out/G11Speed-G40/{2,4}.out.

criteria.text: A loss census on the current compiler lists every cell, peer and metric where Jet loses. It groups the losses by root (the codegen, runtime or Core mechanism responsible), and each root is on a card with its general fix. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*loss-census*"` names the committed census, each root row naming its card.

Structural coverage beyond the cells: a generated or curated corpus of at least 30 programs that use the language's features in varied ways (the gauntlet programs and their peer twins) is measured against the peers on wall time and peak memory, and its losses join the census, so that a fix that only helps a measured cell is caught. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry coverage-corpus` measures all 30 or more programs against the peers.

The loss census is empty: on the canonical manifest and the coverage corpus, Jet beats every matched peer on wall time and peak memory, each fix proven on a second program that uses the feature differently. Proof: the census rerun on the canonical manifest and the coverage corpus lists no loss.

Peak memory is measured per program, not per harness. The gauntlet's peak_rss readings no longer inherit the timer's own high-water mark across exec: each reading is the measured process's own exact VmHWM, read at its exit, for every peer and Jet alike. Proof: the Jet hello binary reads under 1 MB through both the gauntlet timer and GNU time; coreutils true reads within 5% of its exact /proc VmHWM at exit; the timer's own overhead on wall time is reported for one cell; and the hello cell's rss is re-judged under the fixed timer. (Found 2026-11-12: timer.py's ru_maxrss gave every reading a floor of about 15.3 MB.)

ScriptBench peak memory is measured per program too. Its rss column comes from hyperfine's memory_usage_byte, which reads hyperfine's own high-water floor: Jet hello (exactly 0.19 MB) and coreutils true (exactly 2.47 MB) both read 3.66 MB, so every rss row under about 3.7 MB is the harness floor. Bench.jet reads each run's exact VmHWM at exit through the G51 launcher. Proof: the hello and true rows read within 5% of their /proc VmHWM, and the ScriptBench rss rows are re-judged.

cards.title: Compile-time folding bakes vDSO reads: rt.clock_mono_ns() in a local became one build's constant
cards.body: Found by G4Ports-1, 2026-11-11, root of the run-cold-context parity failure. sema's comptime-local folding treated an initializer as pure when the seccomp filter saw no syscall. vDSO reads such as clock_gettime never trap, so 'now: rt.clock_mono_ns()' in Core/Http/Client.jet __client_until held one build's reading: every 500 ms HTTP send failed at once in a process older than that. The same latent bake sits in the Tls, Db, Server, Web and Wayland deadlines. Fix: G4Ports-clock.

log.text: c2 amended (Main, 2026-11-13). G10Safe-runtime-reads2 gave the live cell IO, and IO then spread into every Db write signature (Core/Db/Db.jet execute and rollback), which broke corelib. An effect row is the wrong tool for a read whose effect is invisible to the caller. Such reads are now run-time-only (RUNTIME_ONLY_READS), which already exists and is consulted by the same never-fold rule, so this adds no second mechanism. Bindings whose effect is real to the caller (watcher poll IO, task_cpu_ns Time) still carry rows. A keep-going sweep over Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and tests found 0 IO and 0 Time violations.

Main ruling 2026-11-12 (c2 scope): the goal is that no ambient read is baked into the image; an effect row is one means. task_identity keeps an empty row (context is an implicit input, D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1=F) but joins a sema run-time-only set (the c3 never-computed-while-compiling rule), avoiding a Context row cascade into Compiler trace functions. os_family may stay reviewed-pure only if a case shows a cross-target fold yields the target family; otherwise it joins the run-time-only set. The census names each reviewed entry with its reason.

criteria.text: Sema folds a local at compile time only when the solved effect row of its initializer is empty. An initializer that reaches Time, Rand or any other effect is never folded, whatever syscall path it takes (vDSO included), and seccomp is only a backstop. Proof: a #Test that fails on the base compiler (two clock reads in one process equal) and passes on the fix, a second test for another vDSO-backed read, and the run-cold-context PortBars parity cases 2, 5, 6 and 7 passing.
criteria.evidence: 32cf234624: jet test Core/Http/Client.jet -> 1 passed 0 failed; jet test Core/Net/Tls.jet -> 6 passed 0 failed (Lander holdsweep $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lander/holds/7-6758-c1.out)

criteria.text: Every runtime binding that reads ambient state is never computed while compiling. It either declares the effect it reads (so the empty-row rule refuses to fold it, as clock_mono_ns does), or it is a run-time-only read (RUNTIME_ONLY_READS) when an effect row would spread into user signatures that never perform that effect. live_load and replace reach every Db write, so they are run-time-only reads. Found by G4Ports-1, 2026-11-12: live_load, task_identity, simd_lanes, os and os_family, clipboard_get and event_pop had empty rows. Proof: a census #Test lists every jet.runtime binding with an empty row and no run-time-only listing, and fails unless that list matches the reviewed pure list. A comptime case shows each read runs at run time on O0, O1 and O2 as a local, and is E0643 as a module value.
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev since 591822c267 (no read of ambient state is computed while building). `jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Tests/Registry/RuntimeInterfacePurity.jet`: 255 passed, 0 failed, including "every jet.runtime binding with no effect row is on the reviewed pure list or run-time only"; `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter runtime_interface/runtime_reads_are_never_computed_while_building` (E0643 per module value, runs at -O0/-O1/-O2 as locals): PASS, on the gate-p136 batch jet.

criteria.text: A computation whose result carries a raw address or a pointer (RawOf, RawAddressOf, PtrFromAddr), or a local value whose body runs #Unsafe code, is never computed while compiling, whatever its effect row says: a compile-time address has no runtime frame. Module values take the raw rule only, because Core has 171 #Unsafe blocks and a refused module value is an E0643 build error. Found 2026-11-12: a1e1b740f6 folded addr: leak(), so the expired-stack sentry reported R0801 instead of R0802. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile cases tests/cases/custom/sentry_fault_kinds_hold_at_every_tier.case (expired-stack R0802, provenance R0801, quarantine R0802, at O0, O1 and O2), and tests/cases/custom/sentry_faults_are_tier_parity.case, both PASS.

criteria.text: A call to a function that reads a mutable global (or any other state a call can change) is never folded at compile time, even when every argument is a constant. Proof: a tests/cases case where such a function's result changes after the global is written, printing the run-time values on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Cold compile of a small script is about 1-4 s, and comptime.bodies is its largest phase
cards.body: Measured by G4Ports-1, 2026-11-11, on seed-b9, from the #5072 port twins (PortBars runs each twin from source, so every case pays a cold compile). jetc-trace, a 148-line file: jet run 1063 ms, against a 3 ms run of the built binary and node's 24 ms. Its phases: comptime.bodies 0.29 s (4 comptime programs built and run), load 0.26, sema.finalize 0.19, register 0.07, ir.build+opt+x64 0.07, link about 0.01. run-cold-context: jet run -- --help takes 4108 ms against node's 40 ms. Its phases: comptime.bodies 1.26 s (31 programs, 381 functions), sema.finalize 0.80, load 0.60, ir.opt 0.40, register 0.23, ir.build 0.08, x64 0.08. The port bar measures exactly what the 30M lines/s cold-compile target is about: the cost is general compile cost, not twin code.

c10 known gap (Speed-3-2, 2026-11-15): core.rt stays in the system layer, not the prelude row D-CORE-LAYERS1=A lists it in. The only allowance is that helpers may sit one layer below their natural home, and Instant is public core.time surface, not a helper. Moving Instant down would change its home module and surface, and returning raw Int ns is a public API change (withdrawn c10-rt). Cost, measured on the p178 seed with jet check, median of 5 runs, shared JET_STORE_DIR: a program that imports only core.rt (tests/cases/corelib/fixtures/rt_next_deadline_without_time_import/main.jet) takes 108 ms at 86 MB peak and loads Core/Time/Time.jet (8.2 ms parse CPU). An empty program takes 38 ms at 55.5 MB. A core.time-only program (time.instant()) takes 100 ms at 83 MB. So core.time accounts for about 60 ms and 28 MB of each core.rt-only check. Only programs that import core.rt without core.time pay it. Closing it needs a ballot that either gives the prelude a monotonic instant type or changes next_deadline's result type.

Reuse is not the fix: the standing order counts cold compile time. Proof: `jet Tools/Gauntlet/PortBars.jet` speed and memory bars for census-snap2 and roots-mjs, cold compile counted. (was #6527 c10)

Peak memory: a small Jet tool's peak RSS is no higher than its original's on every PortBars entry. ScriptAPI-2 measured Jet at about 19-21 MB against bash's 7-12 MB on batch10, integrate10, streamb10 and verify-rows, and the cost is the runtime's baseline, not the twins. The fix goes in the general mechanism (runtime start-up, reserved heap or arena sizing, and eagerly mapped tables), and is proven on a second small program. PortBars shows peak memory PASS on all nine. Part 1 (ScriptAPI-3, image layout locality and the build key; it rides t16) took the warm small-script peak from 15.5 MB to 7.1-7.5 MB, and batch10, integrate10 and streamb10 still lose (11.8 against 10.6 MB, 12.9 against 8.6, 10.6 against 8.6), while verify-rows ties. criteria.evidence: The owner ratified D-COMPTIME-SIZE1=A on 2026-11-13 (fixed storage rule, no switch). Its build criteria are c7 and c8 here.

criteria.text: A build-time constant's payload is mapped read-only: immutable folded data lands in a read-only ELF segment, not a writable one. Found by the D-COMPTIME-SIZE1 review on seed-b13. Proof: readelf of a built binary holding a large folded String shows its bytes in a non-writable PT_LOAD, and a case asserts it.

A consumer that needs only a large constant's length does no run-time scan of it. In the ballot program, `big.len()` of a folded 50 MB String folds to its constant, and the emitted IR holds no Unicode scalar count over it. Proof: jet inspect decisions shows the folded length, and a case checks the IR.

Bytes of a build-time value that no run-time code reads are not emitted. In the D-COMPTIME-SIZE1 program (two 50 MB repeats used only for their lengths), the --optimize=full binary holds neither run and is within 10% of the size of the same program reading its size at run time (136,272 bytes on seed-b13). Proof: a case builds it, asserts the binary size bound and the output 100000000, and readelf shows no 50 MB run.

Build-time evaluation costs no more than running the same code: building the D-COMPTIME-SIZE1 Collatz table at compile time takes at most the time and peak memory of running it plus the compiler's own floor (seed-b13: 12 s and 4.1 GB against 1.24-1.29 s and 596 MB). Proof: a committed receipt measuring `jet build` and `jet run` of the ballot program on one machine.

D-COMPTIME-SIZE1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). One fixed storage rule applies to every emitted value at O0, O1, O2 and web, with no switch. A value of at least 64 KiB whose bytes repeat one pattern of at most 64 bytes is stored as pattern plus length, and an all-zero value as zero-fill. Item reads, length, loops, slices, comparisons, searches and hashing work on the pattern. print and file or socket writes stream from one reused 64 KiB buffer. A use that needs fixed bytes, such as a [U8] parameter or foreign code, fills it once under a guard into reserved read-only pages. jet inspect decisions lists each pattern value. Proof: identical output digests on every tier, binary size never above raw, the ballot program near 50.1 MB, and a racing-threads fill-once case.

D-COMPTIME-SIZE1=A author path: core.archive.zstd compress writes real compressed blocks, not only stored blocks, and round-trips through zstd.decompress. `jet inspect decisions --estimate` prints each large raw value's stored size and its zstd-estimated size, running only when asked. Proof: a golden of --estimate and a round-trip test.

cards.title: Tests fail under machine load: a wall-clock step limit turns slow into failed
cards.body: Owner, 2026-11-12: a test that fails under load, rather than passing more slowly, is a reliability defect. In the a0.0.45 admit of dev 2844b04984 (run beside a train build, landings and probes), about 200 rows across candidate chunks 2-5 and 8 were TIMEOUT or ERROR. 82 golden, 20 ui and 59 cases rows passed only on retry. Five browser_bidi and web_app rows ERRORed with an empty 'free-port probe failed', because the probe's own wall-clock timeout was reported without its reason. The root: JetTestKit gives every step a 60 s wall-clock timeout (Compiler/JetTestKit/Source/Exec.jet KitOptions timeout: 60, process.cmd(...).timeout), so a loaded host's slowness is judged as failure. The admit retry masks it instead of fixing it.

log.text: c5 case half passes: fe131e30c3 on dev, jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_entry/run_steps_stop_a_looping_step_at_its_cpu_limit gives PASS 1 with bwrap on PATH (gate-p66, 2026-11-14). The loaded jet build --profile dev Compiler half and the c3 load sweep are pending: they're Main heavy-slot jobs after the batch compiler.

criteria.text: A test step's limit judges the work, not the host's load: JetTestKit bounds each step by the CPU time of the step's process tree (unaffected by other load). The wall-clock limit stays only as a hang guard, set far enough out that a loaded host can't reach it on a working step. A hit on either limit reports TIMEOUT with the limit kind, the CPU and wall seconds used, and the step. A Core.jet #Test proves a CPU-bound step that exceeds the CPU limit is TIMEOUT (cpu) and that a step sleeping past its wall guard is TIMEOUT (wall).
criteria.evidence: f15ece1132 on dev. 2026-11-14 15:0x, gate-p66 jet on dev 6cd4312a1a: jet test Compiler/JetTestKit/Tests/Core.jet --filter 'past its CPU limit' gives 1 passed, 0 failed

criteria.text: Every helper inside a test step that has its own deadline reports a deadline miss with its reason, never as an ERROR with an empty message. This covers the free-port probe (kit_steps_free_ports, StepsTokens.jet) and any readiness or port wait in the case harness. A case forces the free-port probe past its deadline and checks the TIMEOUT reason.
criteria.evidence: f15ece1132 on dev. jet test Compiler/JetTestKit/Tests/StepsHost.jet --filter 'free-port probe past its deadline' gives 1/0, and --filter 'host-port cases hold' gives 1/0 (gate-p66, 2026-11-14)

criteria.text: Load sweep: the corpus rows that were TIMEOUT, ERROR, or passed only on retry in the a0.0.45 admit are run again while a load generator holds every core busy (for example stress-ng at 2x the core count). Every row passes, and each failure found on the way is fixed at its root: either the harness limit, or a product deadline. A product deadline in Jet's runtime or Core (a BiDi handshake, a service delivery wait, a readiness wait) waits on its event or uses the user's own deadline, never a fixed wall time that load can exhaust. The rows, the generator and the result are recorded. Proof: the recorded load-sweep result under Docs/Audits lists every row as PASS under the named load generator.

The release gate stops masking load sensitivity: a row that fails and then passes on retry is reported in REPORT.md as a flaky row with its two outcomes, and fails the gate unless it carries a disposition that names an owning card.

cards.title: A string or byte literal body after an effect row lexes as a typed head, so escapes and holes are wrong
cards.body: Found by G12Docs-4 (G12Docs-69) on seed-b13: h: fn() -[]> String { "a\nb" } prints a literal backslash-n. Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Payload.jet string_head_modes reads Ident { followed by a string as a typed head (raw text, holes, undecoded escapes), and its only exemption for a return type, returned_type_at, recognizes just ) -> before the type. After an effect arrow -[E]> the body String { ... } becomes the typed head String{...}: \n stays raw, \u{41} becomes \u plus a hole, and interpolation breaks. The [U8] { byte head has the same gap. char literals, return, parenthesized and if bodies are unaffected. It is wrong output with no diagnostic.

log.text: Both criteria met: the literal-body case (c1) and the parser-owned typed-head decision with an unchanged golden corpus (c2, p237 dev ab95db25f2).

criteria.text: A function body that is a string, byte or interpolated literal lexes as a body after every return-type form: -> T, an effect arrow -[E]> T with one or several effects, generic, list, map, optional, fallible and qualified return types. Its escapes decode and its holes interpolate exactly as in the same body after -> T. A case covers each literal kind (escapes, \u{...}, interpolation, byte strings) with and without an effect row, at O0, O1 and O2, and a real typed head written as a body expression still lexes as a typed head.
criteria.evidence: dev 6a10ad7d0c, gate-p64 jet, b53proofs 2026-11-14 (dev 99aa698189): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter language_features/literal_body_reads_as_a_body_after_every_return_type_form -> PASS 1/FAIL 0 (each literal kind with and without an effect row, O0/O1/O2, and a typed head).

criteria.text: The typed-head decision is made in one place from the parser's knowledge of the return-type position, not from a lexer token-pattern guess that each new return-type spelling must extend. The tests/ and Examples corpus show no output change other than the fixed cases, by the golden profile at O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden` on O0, O1 and O2 changes only the fixed cases, and `git grep -n returned_type_at -- Compiler/JetLexer` prints nothing.
criteria.evidence: dev ab95db25f2 (lexer heuristic removed by 5c858f4290): `git grep -n returned_type_at -- Compiler/JetLexer` prints nothing; p237 batch compiler full golden profile PASS 5026, FAIL 0 on o0, o1 and o2, with 0 new failures against p236.

cards.title: A lambda that moves a capture runs the move on every call
cards.body: Found by G9Web-1-2 (#6779 work, dev 46855ae09a, seed-b14). Sema accepts a lambda whose body moves a captured owner, even when the lambda is passed to a per-item callback. `[1,2,3].map(x -> consume(s.move()) + x).sum()` prints 33 and fold prints 27: the same owner is moved three times, a use after move (I1). Probe: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G9Web/probe6779/mapmove/main.jet. The safe fix needs no new syntax: refuse the move. A call-at-most-once parameter mark that would allow it for one-shot callbacks is a language choice and goes to a ballot.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c2 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

c3 is wider than written (CardCloser-3 probe on gate-p131, 2026-11-14): a lambda stored in a struct field (h: Holder{action: fn() { k += 1 }}) or in a list silently loses even a plain k += 1 on a := Int, not only a &self method call. A lambda bound with := or passed as an argument does write through. So the loss follows storing the closure in an aggregate: the capture is copied at the aggregate store instead of referenced. This is a silent miscompile (I1 type/memory-safety class), G10 priority. The fix needs one capture-mode rule in sema (by-reference for mutated := captures, or refuse storing a mutating closure in an aggregate) and its IR lowering.

criteria.text: Sema refuses moving a captured owner inside a lambda body whenever the lambda may run more than once (any lambda that escapes into a call or a binding), with a registered code, what/why/fix text (copy, clone or move the value in as a parameter) and a UI snapshot of the probe. The rule is swept over Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and every tests/ tree first, and every hit is fixed in the same batch.
criteria.evidence: dev 499cb49813: E0121 'moves out of a lambda that can run more than once'; jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter lambda_move_capture_repeated_call: 1 PASS on batch compiler gate-p131 (dev 8d83659ef3), verified by Main on dev 529aba0d26

criteria.text: A one-shot callback may move a capture only through a call-at-most-once parameter mark, which is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15); c1's refusal lands first and does not wait. Proof: after the ruling, `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Closures/one_shot_callback_move`.

A stored closure (in a struct field or a list) that writes a captured `:=` local, by `k += 1` or a `&self` method call, either writes the original or is refused with a registered error; it never silently loses the write (gate-p64 prints 10; CardCloser-3 found the field and list forms on gate-p131). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter stored_closure_capture_write` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Closures/stored_closure_capture_write_` on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Derive the runtime can-stop set from the runtime IR instead of the hand-kept ir_route_can_stop list
cards.body: ir_route_can_stop (JetIR) is a hand-kept list of runtime routes that skip the stop poll after a call. Its generated twin RUNTIME_STOP_EXPORTS has no callers. The poll catches a stop that the callee published, so the sound set is the runtime closure of routes that can publish one, with fatal traps (allocation failure, capacity panic, invalid layout) declared fatal rather than stops. Plan (G11Speed-5, 2026-11-13): build a stops receipt from the runtime IR at library build, as the .threads receipt is built (BuildLibrary → Request → RuntimePack → Host), and prune stop points after the build from it. G11Speed-c29j1 extends the list by hand for now.

criteria.text: ir_route_can_stop answers from a stops receipt built from the runtime IR at library build (the closure of routes that can publish a stop, with allocation failure, capacity panic and invalid layout declared fatal), and the hand-kept list and the uncalled RUNTIME_STOP_EXPORTS are deleted. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter stop_poll_follows_the_runtime_stops_receipt` (a call to a pure scalar runtime route has no stop poll after it in the lowered IR; a call to jet_time_sleep_until has one), and the cancellation and deadline cases pass at O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Data-oriented compiler core: interned u32 ids, flat columns, per-phase arenas, no RC, under 1 GB
cards.body:
Owner order (2026-11-13): "i want one slot working the data oriented core immediately. this should be done carefully, systemically, and cleanly. it should be a fast intelligent cutover." This card is the work home for #5479 plan step 3 (#5479 c7) and the memory half of #5910. #5479 c7 and #5910 stay as the gates and are met from this card's evidence.

What it is: every compiler name, symbol, type and function becomes an interned u32 id, with no String-keyed maps. The AST, types and IR become flat struct-of-arrays columns instead of per-node heap objects. Compiler data lives in per-phase arenas freed in bulk and carries no reference counts. Peak memory falls under 1 GB.

Why: G11Speed-5's 2026-11-13 profile (check RunColdContext on the core-b1 jet) has no symbol above 2.3% self time. The cost is spread across allocation, RC, string keys and copies, which this work removes. From today's numbers (8,510 lines/s on the c1 cell, about 5 of 32 threads busy, so roughly 590 µs CPU per line), the c7 gate of 5 µs per line is about a 100× CPU cut. The parallel pipeline (its own card) needs this card's arenas and ids to scale.

How: one slot (G11Speed-5). Design and census first, then slices in dependency order. Each slice is a whole cutover (greenfield: no parallel representation, no adapter layer, no flag) whose proof is identical output: the self-host chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases. The worker writes code and submits; Lander5 builds, runs the chain and lands. A slice that cannot be cut over whole is split by package boundary, never by keeping two representations.
cards.plan:
Census (G11Speed-5, base c490f18529; commands, census.awk and per-file.tsv in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed-5/6793/). Over the nine pipeline packages:
- 1333 `[String:` maps and sets (Sema 933, Driver 143, IR 103, Foundation 86)
- 393 `Shared<`
- payload node enums: Expr 51, Stmt 35, Item 24, TExprKind 77, NodeKind 99/95, Type 23/17
- peak: jet check of one Sema file is 4414 MB (seed-b14, 28 s), held across sema

Slices, each a whole cutover with no second form, proved by chain fixed point plus identical goldens, ui and cases:
- S0: census guard and ledger, plus Docs/spec/compiler-data.md
- S1: ModuleId
- S2: SymbolId
- S3: Names, String maps to 0 (c2)
- S4: flat AST (c3)
- S5: TypeId and flat checked bodies (c4)
- S6: IR and backend ids, no Shared
- S7: phase arenas, no Shared in sema (c4, c5)

Decisions (Main, 2026-11-13; all as proposed):
- F1: compiler data means the nine pipeline packages (Lexer, Parser, Foundation, Sema, IR, Backend, Driver, Eval, Wasm). Tool packages read it through accessors.
- F2: nominal type names become SymbolIds in S2; structural TypeIds come in S5, after the flat AST, so the Type tree is rewritten once.
- F3: the split is by id space across every package, because Foundation types are shared. A package split is used only for package-private data (S3, S6).
- F4: "no RC" means the only heap blocks are single-owner column buffers whose count word never moves after creation. There is no String, box, Shared or per-node block. Literal zero count words would need a language feature outside this card.
- F5: S1 comes before S2.

log.text: Gap found 2026-11-14 while landing: Docs/spec/compiler-data.md says a parallel phase lends read-only tables to its workers, but the compiler has no mechanism to do that. A task's read capture copies the value (BuildExpr ir_copy_value), a lent parameter is E1102, and every parallel phase in Compiler/ uses Shared in a file whose row already counts it. So a new parallel phase (record take, Core body decode, O2 pass threads) either adds a Shared cell, which the ratchet refuses, or copies the whole input per worker. Withdrawn for this reason: Speed-2 6759-c2-core-record-take-parallel and 6759-c9-core-bodies-decode-parallel-r2. GoalsA-1's o2-*-threads and PrecompiledCore's parallel encode/pack are being reworked against the same constraint. Closing this needs a read-only lend for tasks, which is a language or Core surface and so an owner ballot.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-14), compile speed (build.plan): the build-plan query (RootRun "build", running a package`s build.jet plan) loads only the sibling members the build entry reaches, through the existing jet_driver_namespace_reach scan, plus their imports. Measured by G11Speed-5 on seed-b17: Compiler/test.jet pulls in jet_testkit (164 modules, a 574-function comptime closure) that build.jet never uses; `jet inspect graph Compiler/build.jet` 7.8 s with it and 1.78 s without; `jet check Compiler/build.jet` 4.48 s and 0.61 s. Chosen over moving test.jet into its own package, because that would tailor only the measured package, while every user package with build.jet plus test.jet pays the same cost. `jet check` and `jet test` still check every member, and target compiles still check what they compile; only the build script`s plan run stops loading unreached siblings. Proof: a case where the plan runs while test.jet has a type error that `jet check` and `jet test` both report; the win on a second user package; the cold self-compile row.

S1 boundary decision (G11Speed-5, 2026-11-13). Module identity text is also the prefix of every SymbolID key and is printed in IR names and goldens. So S1 moves module records, rows and lookups to ModuleID and one ModuleTable: the loader interns and the graph takes a copy. Symbol.module_name and key text stay text until S2 and cross at module_find. S2 moves Symbol.module_name to ModuleID together with symbol keys.

criteria.text: Design and census first. The card plan records, for Compiler/ by package: every String-keyed map and set, every heap-allocated node type, every RC-carrying compiler struct, and every phase's data lifetime, each with counts and a reproducible census command. It also records the slice order with each slice's files and its proof. A short durable design note goes in Docs/spec (for example compiler-data.md) with the contract: id spaces, column layout, arena lifetimes, and the rule that compiler data holds no RC.
criteria.evidence: S0 landed as dev baac72385c (G11Speed-6793-s0-r2): compiler-data census guard ratchet in LaneCheck and Land RATCHETS, plus Docs/spec/compiler-data.md. Lander5 on 543f291c8a with seed-b14: CompilerData test 2/0, --check ok, --write with no diff, LaneCheck rc 0, Land check rc 0, AgentDocFlags rc 0, guards 152/0.

criteria.text: Interning: every compiler name, symbol, type and function is a u32 id from one interner per id space. The census command from c1 shows zero String-keyed maps and sets in compiler data. Proof: that census, a self-host chain fixed point, and goldens, ui and cases identical to before.

Flat AST: the parser writes struct-of-arrays node columns into a phase arena, and no AST node is a separate heap allocation. Proof: the census, the chain fixed point and identical goldens, ui and cases.

Flat types and IR: the type table and IR are flat id-indexed columns in per-phase arenas, freed in bulk at phase end. Compiler data carries no reference counts. Proof: the census, the chain fixed point and identical goldens, ui and cases.

Memory: peak RSS of the self-compile is under 1 GB (#5910), and jet check of one Compiler file is under 1 GB (#5910 c62), each measured with GNU time maxrss on the dev tip. Proof: committed GNU time maxrss receipts for both commands on the dev tip.

Speed gate: the #5479 c1 cell (cold, uncached jet build of Compiler plus Core, n=3 median) shows at most 5 µs CPU per line, and #5479 c7's gate is met from this evidence. Each landed slice records its before and after row in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/speed-metrics.tsv and a log on this card. Proof: the #5479 c1 cell receipt.

jet check of one Compiler file stays under 1 GB peak RSS. Today the command jet check Compiler/JetCLI/Source/CLI/InspectBuild.jet peaks at 10.65 GB and takes 30.9 s on plain dev b9687be981 (probe g12d-devck, GNU time maxrss 10,654,668 kB). Proof: the same command on the dev tip reports a maxrss under 1,048,576 kB, with its wall time reported. (was #5910 c62)

cards.title: Parallel compiler pipeline: streaming modules, parallel comptime, wait-free queues, per-thread arenas (24 of 32 threads)
cards.body:
Owner order (2026-11-13): the parallel pipeline is tracked as its own card so it cannot be lost. This card is the work home for #5479 plan step 2 (#5479 c6), which stays as the gate and is met from this card's evidence. It is not staffed today: the data-oriented core (#6793) takes the speed slot, and this card starts once #6793's interning and per-phase arenas have landed. Lock-free per-thread allocation and contention-free scaling depend on them.

What it is: modules stream through the pipeline as soon as their dependencies are checked, with no phase-wide barriers. Comptime runs in parallel. Work queues are wait-free. Each thread allocates from its own arena and takes no global lock.

Projected ceiling (from today's numbers, not measured): about 5 to 24 busy threads, so at most about 5× wall time on its own with CPU per line unchanged. Its 400K lines/s gate needs #6793's CPU cut as well.

criteria.text: Design: a slice plan on the card covering the module dependency scheduler, removal of the phase barriers in the driver, parallel comptime children, the wait-free work queue, and per-thread arenas built on #6793's arenas, each with its proof. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*parallel-pipeline*"` names the design note and its passing review.

Streaming: a module enters sema, lowering and codegen as soon as its dependencies are checked, with no phase-wide barrier in the driver. Comptime evaluation runs in parallel. Output is identical: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Scaling: on the #5479 c1 cell (32 hardware threads, cold, n=3 median), average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) is at least 24, 32 threads beat 16, no global allocator or queue lock shows in a perf profile, and throughput is at least 400K lines/s. #5479 c6 is met from this evidence. Proof: the #5479 c1 cell receipt with a perf profile.

cards.title: Copy-and-patch machine code for the O0 tier (jet run, jet dev, comptime)
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 1 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. At O0, each IR operation is emitted by copying a pre-built machine-code template (stencil) and patching its holes (constants, frame offsets, jump and call targets), with no instruction selection or register allocation at O0. The stencils are built once with the toolchain, like precompiled Core, so they are toolchain, not a cache (D-EXEC2=A holds). Prior art: Xu and Kjolstad, "Copy-and-Patch Compilation", OOPSLA 2021; the CPython 3.13 JIT (PEP 744). O1 and O2 keep the optimizing backend. Sequenced after the data-oriented core (#6793) lands its IR ids (S6), because stencils are keyed by flat IR opcodes. Unstaffed today (speed ranks below goals).

criteria.text: A design note and a passing adversarial review in Docs/Audits (per AGENTS.md "Adversarial design review") cover this card before any build SUB. The review names the strongest existing implementations and checks the claimed gain against a runnable probe. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*copy-and-patch*"` names the design note and its passing review.

O0 code generation emits every IR opcode by copying and patching a toolchain-built stencil, with no instruction selection or register allocation at O0. The stencil set is built by Compiler/build.jet and embedded in the jet binary, with no file I/O per compile.

Output is identical before and after: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases on every tier. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Measured: O0 backend CPU time per function falls at least 10× on the #5479 c1 cell, and a second program (jetc-trace) shows the same gain. Run-time speed of O0 code is reported beside it and stays within 1.5× of the current O0 backend. Proof: the #5479 c1 cell receipt and a jetc-trace receipt.

cards.title: Parallel lexing and parsing inside one file
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 3 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. A SIMD pre-scan finds top-level declaration boundaries in a file, and chunks are lexed and parsed on separate threads, then joined in source order. This matters because the compiler itself is essentially one large module, so module-level parallelism (#6794) cannot split it. It requires that lexing can restart at a top-level boundary. If that needs a language rule (for example, no raw newline inside a string literal), the rule goes on a ballot before the build. Sequenced with #6793 S4 (flat AST) and #6794. Unstaffed today.

criteria.text: A design note and a passing adversarial review in Docs/Audits (per AGENTS.md "Adversarial design review") cover this card before any build SUB. The review names the strongest existing implementations and checks the claimed gain against a runnable probe. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*parallel-lex-parse*"` names the design note and its passing review.

A file is lexed and parsed in parallel chunks split at top-level declaration boundaries found by a SIMD pre-scan, and joined in source order. Any language rule this needs is ratified on a ballot first.

Output is identical before and after: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases on every tier. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Measured: front-end wall time on the largest single module of the #5479 c1 cell scales with threads (16 threads at least 8× faster than 1), and a second large file shows the same scaling. Proof: the #5479 c1 cell front-end receipt at 1 and 16 threads, and the same for a second large file.

Lexer classification on the self-host unit runs at or below 1 ns per byte, using the public vector tools (#Multiversion, Lanes and a core.arch block classifier; SPEED-500K M5). Proof: the per-byte figure in `JET_TRACE_FILE` phase output for `jet check` of the self-host unit, in a committed receipt.

cards.title: Shared generic code at O0: one compiled body per generic function, types passed as a hidden argument
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 4 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. At O0, a generic function is compiled once and takes its type information (size, alignment, trait method tables) as a hidden argument, as Swift does for unspecialized generics and Go does with GC-shape stenciling and dictionaries (Go 1.18). O1 and O2 keep per-type specialization. Meaning is identical on every tier (I9): only the implementation strategy differs, and the proof is identical goldens, ui and cases on o0, o1 and o2. Per-type copies are the main compile-time cost of generics in Rust and C++. Sequenced after #6793 S5 (TypeId). Unstaffed today.

criteria.text: A design note and a passing adversarial review in Docs/Audits (per AGENTS.md "Adversarial design review") cover this card before any build SUB. The review names the strongest existing implementations and checks the claimed gain against a runnable probe. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*shared-generic*"` names the design note and its passing review.
At O0, each generic function is compiled once and receives its type information (size, alignment, trait method tables) as a hidden argument. O1 and O2 keep per-type specialization.

Output is identical before and after: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases on every tier. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Measured: O0 compile time and code bytes for a generic-heavy program (for example Core collections used at 20 element types) against per-type specialization, plus a second program. Run-time cost at O0 is reported beside it. Proof: a committed receipt for both programs.

Per-function code size: no Core or generated function carries code its callers cannot reach or expansion a hand-written version would not. Measured by Main on seed-b13, 2026-11-12, default jet build: core_encoding_json_parse_string 21,323 B, __core_encoding_stream_jcs_number 37,759 B, core_regex_scan 35,189 B, unit_unicode_upper_mapping and lower_mapping 28-29 KB each, and MemorySafetyFuzz_run_memory_safety_fuzz_axis 58,080 B. A dated breakdown names, for each function over 4 KB in the tool-twin binaries, what the bytes are (inlined callees, unrolled loops, tables as code, checks) and the general codegen or Core rule that shrinks it; each fix shows the gain on two programs. Proof: the committed dated per-function breakdown, each fix with its two-program receipt. (was #6328 c29)

cards.title: Cheaper compile-time execution: one warm child per compile, fast O0 code, shared-memory values
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 6 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. Compile-time code runs natively in a child of the compiler (I9). Today that costs process start-up, an O0 compile and value serialization per batch. The plan: start one child per compile and keep it warm for that compile only (nothing survives the compile, so D-EXEC2=A holds); compile compile-time functions with the copy-and-patch O0 path (its own card); and pass values through a shared-memory region instead of serializing them. Related: #6759 c1 (one comptime child per compile) and the re-finalize cost measured 2026-11-13 (1.19 s of the 2.86 s RunColdContext check). Unstaffed today.

criteria.text: A design note and a passing adversarial review in Docs/Audits (per AGENTS.md "Adversarial design review") cover this card before any build SUB. The review names the strongest existing implementations and checks the claimed gain against a runnable probe. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*comptime-child*"` names the design note and its passing review.

One compile-time child runs per compile, stays warm for that compile only, and exits with it. Compile-time functions are compiled on the copy-and-patch O0 path (#6795), and values cross through a shared-memory region with no serialization.

Output is identical before and after: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases on every tier. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Measured: compile-time cost (comptime.bodies plus the re-finalize) of check RunColdContext and jetc-trace before and after, each showing the gain. Proof: a committed before-and-after receipt for both programs.

cards.body: Gap card for #6792 c6/c7 (owner order 2026-11-13: one cohesive package covering everything a web app and a native app need, with styling far better than HTML and CSS). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md. log.text: Owner order 2026-11-16: native-platform cards split; Linux and the web stay in G9, macOS, Windows, iOS and Android move to G13. macOS, Windows, iOS and Android work moved to #6983 (G13).

Ballot D-PUSH-CREDS1 posted (blocks c1): where push keys come from. Rec A: .push(apns: app.apns(...), fcm: app.fcm(...), web: app.web_push(...)) in the server entry, naming the app's env variables. Validator ok; adversarial passes by AnyReview11 and Main (the mail precedent is ratified in D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1, not built).

Route set (Main, 2026-11-16): ratified text settles it with no ballot. Rule 1 (one graph) plus #6445 c6: the server's own evaluated graph is every target's route set. Speed-3-2 builds it on app.App now (option X, about 5 SUBs). c2 also needs, unbuilt: the app.new graph type, ui.Node (#6447), native.push() (#480). Findings: lanes/Speed-3/route-set-check.md (scratch).

Decision (Main): app.notify keeps the proposal's signature fn<V>(to: auth.AccountID, title: String, body: String, open: V) -[Net]> Never!. Sema checks open: against the one route table (c2's jet check failure) and lowers the call to an internal app.__notify carrying the route's wire form, the way enqueue is lowered. The route table gets the state encoder, and Core never sees V. Rejected: a V: Encode bound. It changes the published signature, and it would report E0905 'V isn't Encode' in place of c2's route diagnostic.

c1 decisions (Main, 2026-11-16):
- Device registration is internal transport behind .with(native.push()): a framework-mounted POST /__jet/push/devices for the signed-in caller, rows in __jet_push_devices through a store hook like CallOutbox.
- The HTTP/2 client stays internal to core.http.client.
- Push provider credentials (APNs key, key id, team, topic; FCM service account; VAPID key and subject) are public config surface the proposal doesn't define. Mail's precedent, .mail(app.smtp("SMTP_URL"), from:), has the server entry name the transport. The push equivalent needs an owner ballot (to draft); until then the providers build against an internal priv(package) configuration record, and fixed JET_* environment names are refused.

criteria.text: One server call, app.notify(to:, title:, body:, open:), reaches every browser the account registered with .with(native.push()) through Web Push (RFC 8030 with RFC 8291 encryption). native.notify shows a local notification on the Linux desktop (the freedesktop Notifications service) with no server. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/notify_sends_web_push_payloads` (a local fake push endpoint checks each payload) and `--filter NativeApp/notify_shows_a_local_linux_notification`.
criteria.evidence: p246 batch compiler (dev 8672bcfd81); feature 29b999b5bc + fix 14938c75d6: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter NativeApp/notify_shows_a_local_linux_notification n=1 bad=0 (Linux org.freedesktop.Notifications steps; the web build step refuses a local notify).

criteria.text: A tap opens the open: state through the one route table on every target that registered. An open: value whose type has no route on such a target fails jet check.
criteria.evidence: p238 batch compiler (dev 5bea729463), full collect-all suite: cases NativeApp/push_open_state_without_a_route_is_a_compile_error PASS.

criteria.text: Crewboard's "assigned to you" push is sent only after update_task's transaction commits, and a rolled-back write sends nothing. This uses the after-commit outbox (#6825 c1).

auth.AccountID is the one account identity type, as ratified (D-DB-TABLE1: Member.account: auth.AccountID; app.caller() returns it). Today it doesn't exist and accounts are Strings: Core/App/App.jet:619 Who.Account(String), :640 as_caller(account: String, ...), :651 maybe_caller() -> String?, :660 caller() -> String, Core/Db/Db.jet:954-955 db.Who.Account(String). Proof: a cases row where a #Table struct with an auth.AccountID column round-trips through the store and app.caller() returns it, on O0/O1/O2; git grep shows no Account(String).

criteria.text: The desktop output writes an AppImage and a Flatpak on Linux, signed with the identities named in outputs:. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter BuildEntry/desktop_output_writes_signed_linux_packages` (it checks the structure and the signature of each package).

A client below the server's min_client gets the typed UpdateRequired (section 4.12) and is offered the update.

`jet package` builds a real, deterministic desktop bundle from the checked package plan, with installer metadata, signing hooks, an updater artifact and a byte, digest and mode receipt, with no placeholder archive and no second bundler.

D-INSTALL1 is ratified and the install page documents only the channel it picks. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter install_page_single_channel`. D-INSTALL1 is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). (was #5950 c1)

On a clean Linux x86-64 container with no Nix and no Jet, the documented install command installs `jet`, and `jet new hello && cd hello && jet run` prints the greeting; the release gate runs this on every release. Proof: the release gate's committed install receipt for the release. (was #5950 c2)

`nix run github:<org>/jet -- --version` prints the release version: flake.nix exports `packages.<system>.default` built from the pinned seed release asset (D-SEED-DIST1=A). Proof: `nix flake show` lists `packages.x86_64-linux.default`, and the release receipt records the `--version` output. (was #5950 c3)

A freestanding aarch64 program runs under QEMU in the release gate and prints its expected output. Proof: the release gate's committed receipt of the QEMU run (waits for hosted CI, which returns with a pinned native seed release; owner ruling 2026-11-08). (was #5950 c8)

A missing entry, an ambiguous project, an unsupported host, an install failure, invalid code and offline state each give a registered error with a tested next step; retired entry layouts get no migration (owner order 2026-11-06), so the case's legacy-layout step is removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter OnboardingRecovery/entry_recovery_covers_missing_ambiguous_legacy_and_stale_layouts` with its known-failing row removed. (was #5950 c13)

criteria.text: An app.Upload streams to storage, and a body over the api's max_upload gets 413 before it is read.

criteria.text: Storage names each stored file itself and returns a blob ID. The client's file name is kept only as metadata and never becomes part of a path, so a name such as ../../etc/passwd stores safely. The server checks the media type from the bytes against the declared list, and a body declared image/png that holds HTML gets 415.

criteria.text: Before it reads the body, attach runs the method that #App.UploadCheck(method:) names, as the caller and after the session check; that method applies the project's row policy (D-DBPOLICY1, #3709), so a signed-in caller who is not a member gets 403 and the body is never read.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072; uploads 33b4f0a1d8 + 46177eada7): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/upload_by_a_non_member_is_403_before_it_is_read PASS (in WebApp/upload_ 3/3).

criteria.text: A download of a stored blob runs the read policy of the row that holds its BlobID and is served with Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072; uploads 33b4f0a1d8 + 46177eada7): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/blob_download_runs_row_policy PASS 1/1.

criteria.text: An upload is spooled after its check passes and before the transaction starts; a retried transaction reads the staged body; a blob kept in a transaction that rolls back is deleted. A staged file lives no longer than its request, and one left by a crash is deleted when the server next starts.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072; uploads 33b4f0a1d8 + 46177eada7): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/upload_spools_before_the_transaction_and_rolls_back PASS (in WebApp/upload_ 3/3).

cards.title: HTTP caching for pages and assets: Cache-Control, ETag and immutable hashed assets derived from facts
cards.body: Gap card for #6792 c6/c7 (owner order 2026-11-13: one cohesive package covering everything a web app and a native app need, with styling far better than HTML and CSS). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md. log.text: All criteria met (p222 batch compiler, dev 18bc53b3e6). Closed by Main.

Implementation decision (Main, within the ratified CachePolicy and .cache<V> surface, no new spelling): sema lowers .cache<V>(policy) to __cache(reply_type: "V", policy), as .screen lowers to __screen. Every GET page or #App.Public endpoint whose reply type is V gets public, max-age plus an ETag; a matching If-None-Match gets 304; the server keeps the encoded reply for max_age, so false, 0 and empty text stay hits (c3) and freshness runs through the expiry instant (c4). #App.SignedIn replies always get private, no-store (c1). c5's shared store is pending Main's reading of D-NEST-UPSTREAM1 (is a store in the app's own database file app-owned?). Speed-3-3 builds c2, then c3, c4 and c1.

criteria.text: Signed-in responses carry Cache-Control: private, no-store. .cache<V>(.Public(max_age:)) sends public, max-age with an ETag, and a matching If-None-Match gets 304.
criteria.evidence: p217 batch compiler (census build of dev ec9df40248): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter cache_policy_headers_and_etag_revalidation PASS

criteria.text: Built assets (images, fonts, icons and static files) have content-hashed names and are served with public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Changing an asset changes its name.
criteria.evidence: p220 batch compiler (dev 17c073989d): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebBuild/hashed_assets_are_immutable PASS 1/1

criteria.text: A server response cache keeps false, 0 and empty text as hits, never as misses.
criteria.evidence: p217 batch compiler (census build of dev ec9df40248): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter cache_keeps_falsy_values PASS

criteria.text: Cache lifetimes are Durations, and an entry is fresh up to its expiry instant and stale after it.
criteria.evidence: p222 batch compiler (dev 18bc53b3e6): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/cache_expiry_boundary PASS 1/1 (Speed-3-3-6814-c4c5, c6497febfa)

criteria.text: Two server instances share one cache store: both read a cached false value, a write to the source invalidates it for both, and a cache store failure falls through to the source instead of failing the request.
criteria.evidence: p222 batch compiler (dev 18bc53b3e6): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/shared_cache_two_instances PASS 1/1 (c6497febfa)

Core/App/App.jet:125,139 compare each MAC with crypto.constant_time_equal_bytes.

kit.Form<T> runs the submission lifecycle (editing, submitting, accepted, refused with field errors) and the use-site validation chain of D-VALIDATE1=A, with goldens on O0, O1, O2 and web.

The table and virtual list views are headless typed models: a column access is checked against the row type, local and server data use one state, and a 100,000-row virtual list renders only its visible rows, with goldens on O0, O1, O2 and web.
A kit.Form field name that T does not have is a compile error with a registered diagnostic.

log.text: c6 code landed in dev 136c4759d9 (Store implements Driver: query/query_one need DB.Read and execute needs DB.Write, with no row policy; a policy scope allows select 1). Both proof cases PASS on the p252 batch compiler. c6 is NOT met: its text names the no-policy default as ballot D-SQL-SCRIPT1, which is not posted or ratified. The landed behavior is option A of that ballot, and the owner may keep it or revert 136c4759d9. On Main's morning ballot list.

batch compiler p187 (dev 9860836a00), 2026-11-15: c2's TableMigration golden passes 3/3, and tests/run/CoreDB/TypedTable.jet passes; TableSecretField and TableSecretMigration fail at o0/o1/o2 with E0737, because the derived #Codable branches on a #Secret field. GoalsB-5-2 owns the fix.
c2 split (Main, 2026-11-15): the table half is built (GoalsB-5-6822-c2-table, lands after c1-db on a seed with c1-sema); the service half is its own criterion, waiting on typed service state.

Decision for c1 (Main, 2026-11-15): the #Secret storage codec is a real codec, a new serde handle op (stored encode/decode) through the existing THandleOp/BodyHandleOp path. Default Encode/Decode methods cannot carry it, because .encode() is a handle op and builtins have no impls. Rejected: a sema-supplied per-type secret-field list beside the codec, which would be a second mechanism and a compiler-known name. The wire codec skips #Secret fields in place of today's E2411. Planned as four SUBs from GoalsB-5-2 after #6869: seed a (Prelude rows and the new op), ir lowering, sema and derive bodies, then Db Table and the golden. Landed for c4 and c3: queued in the next batch.

Handoff (CardCloser-3 stopped, agent cap; no code written yet): c1 needs a compiler-derived storage codec and a change to E2411 for #Secret fields; c2 waits on #Table; c3/c4 need db.Table/Store exports in Core.rows (compiler rebuild) plus read-set tracking in app.state. Implementation choices to settle under D-DB-TABLE1=A: whether DBConnection is renamed to Store, and whether DBError becomes an enum.
Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): c1 split; read and write sets are #6822 c3, the DB.Write effect error is #6822 c4. blockedBy D-DB-TABLE1 (open ballot).

Main 2026-11-14: no ratified decision pins db.Table<K, T>: its constructor and binding, key declaration and method signatures exist only in the proposal (D-DBMIGRATE1 and D-DBPOLICY1 cover SQL and policy; D-QUERY-RETAIN1 retired a public Table<T> carrier). GoalsB-4 is drafting ballot D-DB-TABLE1 after #6830 slice 2. #6445 c5 and #6820 c3 wait on it.

criteria.text: D-DATA-EVOLVE1=A, service half: the D-SERVICE-UPGRADE1 migrate function derives from the state type's one migration block. Waits on typed service state: today service state is untyped String records with a hand-written migration class, so no typed handoff exists to drive it. A script can run `db.open("notes.db").query(SQL{"select …"})` with no row policy, joining tables or touching none, with `query` needing DB.Read and `execute` DB.Write so the #5949 prompt shows read-only versus writing, while a row policy stays available through `with_policy`; and a policy scope no longer refuses a query outside its one table such as `select 1`. Today `c.query(...)` is E0102 and a script needs `db.policy`, `with_policy` and `migrate` first (Core/DB/DB.jet:697-727). The default without a policy is the ballot D-SQL-SCRIPT1, on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). cards.body: Gap card N1 from the #6792 r3 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md, section 7.12 interim forms; 3.9). Its language surface needs ballot D-BOUND-METHOD1 (drafted in the r3 gap file; posted with D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1 after review).

log.text: Correction to the previous entry: ... IS Jet syntax, the spread sigil (SIGIL_SPREAD, D-VARIADIC1: name: ...T variadic parameters, f(...xs) call spread, [...a, x] list spread). So option D's crew.tell(..) is one dot from crew.tell(...xs): a typo risk the owner named. The owner ruled the options not good enough; D-BOUND-METHOD1 is being redesigned as v2.

D-BOUND-METHOD1 option D corrected (2026-11-14): its text called crew.tell(..) a free spelling, but .. is the inclusive range operator (OP_RANGE, 1..10), so D gives .. a second meaning (I8 cost). ... is not Jet syntax. The ballot's review missed this; D's detail now states it. The owner's <> question was answered: <> keeps its one pipe meaning.

D-BOUND-METHOD1 is withdrawn in #6792 r4: the closure is the target form for app.live, keyed by its one call. #6824 is no longer a dependency of the proposal and stays a language gap without a ballot.

cards.title: app: server jobs, the after-commit outbox and schedules (#App.Job, #App.Every, app.enqueue)
cards.body: Gap card N2 from the #6792 r3 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md, section 4.14; crewboard/Logic/crew.jet tell_assignee, send_invite, remind_due_today). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

log.text: All criteria met (p222 batch compiler, dev 18bc53b3e6). Closed by Main.

Ballot D-JOB-STORE1 posted (blocks c9): rec A, no public job-store slot; jobs stay in a core.db store's outbox in the call's transaction, and c9 is reworded to that contract. Main added B's best case (Redis or a cloud queue: job load off the DB, independent scaling) and A's cost (job rows share the database).

p209: c2 (9fb22f4c60) hangs every served mux. Server.jet mux_serving relied on list remove(0, .Slot) giving None on an empty list, but .Slot stops on an out-of-range index (E3010), so the serving task dies at its first serve and the client times out. That broke about 100 suite rows (HTTP examples, web_app, http_server_lifecycle, ws, tls, canvas). Speed-3-2 sends the fix first in p210, sweeping every .Slot ?? return|default caller (App.jet:995, Db.jet:2178). c1, c2, c3 and c4 proof rows fail on p209 for this root.

c9 ruling (Main): a queue store adapter can't be written by user code today. The only adapter seam is core.app's priv(package) transactions module with CallOutbox (Core/App/App.jet:775, :836), joined only by core.db (Core/Db/Db.jet:1362). Refusing a service with #App.Job methods that holds no db.Store would contradict the ratified text in core-library.md:5664-5665 (a call that used no store runs the job at once without keeping it), so that reading is rejected. c9 has a subject only once a public adapter surface exists, and adding one is owner-gated public API. c9 is blocked on a ballot for it; Speed-3-2 moved to #6800 c1.
Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): c1 split; the per-send keys are #6825 c10.

criteria.text: app.enqueue inside a #App.SignedIn method stores the job call in that method transaction: a rolled-back write queues nothing, and a committed one runs the job at least once after the commit, retried with backoff up to retries:.

criteria.text: auth.Accounts.verify_email works end to end on the test host: a new account cannot sign in before it confirms its address.
kit.account_flows adds the sign-up, confirmation, reset, passkey and two-factor screens to the one route set on every target.
auth.verified_email returns an address only after it is confirmed; Crewboard's invite and accept_invite pass end to end, and an account with an unconfirmed matching address cannot accept.
app.mail sends through the .mail(transport, from:) of the server entry; a mail queued in a job is retried with the job.

Invitations: accepting an invitation deletes it; an invitation lapses after its expiry and a nightly job deletes it; the members policy refuses a member insert from a lapsed invitation; auth.verified_email returns the lowercased address.
auth.Accounts.reset_password works end to end on the test host: a reset link is single-use and expires in an hour.
auth.Accounts.passkeys works end to end on the test host: a WebAuthn passkey signs in.
auth.Accounts.two_factor works end to end on the test host: once turned on, a TOTP code is required, and recovery codes sign in.
auth.Accounts.limit_sign_in(per_minute:) works end to end on the test host: the sixth failed sign-in in a minute for one address waits.
Membership: set_role, remove_member and leave keep at least one owner (LastOwner); a removed member's open live queries re-run and are refused; jobs that push check membership first.

The `auth` package verifies tokens per D-AUTH-TOKENPOLICY1=A: JWT verification requires a named nonempty audience, exp and a matching aud (the empty-audience bypass is gone), HS256 only with constant-time comparison, and the selected PASETO mode. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Auth/TokenPolicyHostile` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #6448 c13)

Each mail a job sends gets its own Message-ID, made from the run key, the recipient and the send open: or link: value, hashed to fit the header, and app.mail passes it to the transport. A retried run repeats each Message-ID even when its query returns rows in another order, and two different mails from one job never share one. (Moved from #6825 c10; needs c4.)

cards.title: db: full-text search index and relation loading on typed tables
cards.body: Gap card N4 from the #6792 r3 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md, section 4.2; crewboard/Logic/crew.jet search and my_projects). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

criteria.text: store.table(..., search: fn) keeps a full-text index (SQLite FTS5, Postgres tsvector) and Table.search(words) returns rows that match every word, under the table's row policy.

Rows.count_by(group) is one query (GROUP BY), and my_projects runs two queries whatever the number of projects, counting the policies' statements. A policy whose reads are key lookups compiles into the query as a join; other policies run per row, memoized per key in the transaction, and jet inspect choices names them.

A way to load a row's related rows in one query (a join or an IN list) exists and Crewboard's board uses it; the query count of board(), policies included, does not grow with the number of members, and limit counts rows after the policy.

cards.title: ELF object writer: extended section numbering (SHN_XINDEX) for objects over 65280 sections
cards.body: The sweep2 Core object reached 107273 sections, above the ELF limit of 65280 without extended numbering. The stage-A build worked around it by splitting or merging the Core object. The object writer should emit extended section indices: e_shnum 0 with the real count in section 0 sh_size, e_shstrndx SHN_XINDEX with the index in section 0 sh_link, and a .symtab_shndx table for symbols in sections at or above SHN_LORESERVE, so that any program of any size links.

criteria.text: The object writer emits extended section numbering (SHN_XINDEX, .symtab_shndx) when an object has 65280 or more sections, and a generated program whose object has more than 70000 sections links and runs on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter object_writer_extended_section_numbering` (it builds that program and runs it on O0, O1 and O2).

cards.title: A dynamically typed value (any) and explicit Any construction (D-PRIM-ANY1)
cards.body: Split out of #5021 (Jai parity, G6) by owner order 2026-11-13: the dynamically typed value is its own card and belongs to no goal. D-PRIM-ANY1 asks whether hiding an arbitrary concrete type requires explicit Any construction. The owner has paused that ballot; this card waits on it.

criteria.text: D-PRIM-ANY1 is ratified by the owner (the ballot is owner-paused). Proof: `timeout 120 node Tools/tower/tower.mjs decision show D-PRIM-ANY1` shows it ratified.
criteria.evidence: tower decision show D-PRIM-ANY1: status ratified, outcome C.

criteria.text: If adopted: the any value has its registry row, an executable example with golden output on every tier, and a UI snapshot for its misuse diagnostic. If refused: the spec lists it with its reason and the Jet mechanism that covers the use case. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Prim/Any` on every tier and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Prim/any`, or the spec row with its reason.
criteria.evidence: dev 890feb6258: Docs/Spec/spec.md 'Deliberately absent' lists `any` with its reason and the covering mechanism (union or opted-in trait, compile-time type arms, reflect.of); syntax-decisions.md records D-PRIM-ANY1=C (option C keeps the no-top-type wall).

criteria.text: Under D-PRIM-ANY1=C (no Any value; type arms over unions and trait values): member arms accept generic arguments (.Pair<Int, String>(p); today E0003). A value whose type has no arm spelling ([Int], Int?, function types) reaches else. A trait value holding a view of a local, returned from its function, fails with the provenance diagnostic. Proof: cases rows plus a UI snapshot for the escape (found by the 2026-11-15 D-PRIM-ANY1 adversarial review on p201; probe in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/GoalsA-1-4/any-review, g6, q1). The same spelling holds over union and trait-value subjects. It separates two instances of one generic: over Box<Int> | Box<String>, the arms are .Box<Int>(b) and .Box<String>(b) (qualified: .geo.Box<Int>(b)). The bare .Box(b) is E0305 'names more than one member' and offers both arms, and a table of both arms needs no else (review 9 probes f01-f01d). Over a union with one instance of a generic, Int \| Box<Int>, the bare .Box(b) names that instance, whether Box is local or imported when no other member has that leaf; today both are E0305 'doesn't belong' (v05; k04 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes/fm). Over a trait value a generic arm always spells its arguments. In an arm, .Name< opens type arguments; as an expression it would be a direction-changing chain, E0333 (t04).

If D-PRIM-ANY1 adopts E: the extended member test (a .Type(x) arm read over an Any subject) has a registered diagnostic, with what/why/fix and a UI snapshot, for an arm naming a type that cannot be a member (an enum case in case position, an unknown type, or a type the arm spelling cannot name), following the resolution rule in the ballot: on an enum .X is a case (E0305), on a union a member type or named case, on an Any any type in scope. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter any_member_arm.
criteria.evidence: D-PRIM-ANY1 was ratified C, not E; the option-E diagnostic is not built. Option C's arm rule is c5.

criteria.text: If D-PRIM-ANY1 adopts C: a bare arm over a union or a trait value names the type its name names in type position. Over a union only, a name that names no type there names the union's one member with that leaf. Every member has an arm, so a package's own Point is .Point(p) beside geo2.Point. Where Point names a type in scope, .Point(p) names it throughout the file; where it names none, each union's arm names its own member (k01). o7's fallback still works, and v03, whose arm binds geo.Point today, becomes E0305. The E0641 exemption for same-leaf members (Sema/Coverage.jet's same-name skip) is removed, so an else over a later-added member is E0641 (a04b). E0307's fix names each member's arm (f06, with #6839 c52). Proof: cases rows for o7, k01, the package's own member's arm and the generic arms; UI snapshots for v03 (E0305), a04b (E0641) and f05; probes are in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes, lanes/AnyReview10/probes/fm and lanes/AnyBallot/probes/fm. Over boxes.Box<Int> | kit.Box (both imported, no Box in scope) the bare .Box(b) is E0305 naming .boxes.Box<Int>(b) and .kit.Box(b); today it binds kit.Box, and E0641 offers .M_Box_Int_ (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 11, probes fm/m31 and fm/m31b). Proof: a UI snapshot of the E0305.
criteria.evidence: On the p254 batch compiler (acc7351dae, trait-arms-fix.r2 71586a086f): cases union_arms_name_the_type_in_type_position (steps fallback = o7, per_union = k01, own/own_o0/own_o2 = the package's own member's arm, generic/local_generic = generic arms) PASS, trait_value_type_arms PASS, union_arms_spell_type_arguments PASS; ui UnionArmNamesLocalType (v03 E0305), UnionElseOverOwnMember (a04b E0641), UnionQualifiedArmBesideOwnMember (f05), UnionArmNamesGenericAndPlain (m31 boxes.Box<Int>|kit.Box E0305), UnionArmNamesTwoMembers, UnionMissingSameLeafMembers all PASS.

cards.title: Gauntlet peer standings: every entry against Rust, C, Zig, Go, Python, Bun, Node, Vite and the hand-written asm ceiling, for startup, run time and binary size, shown in Tower
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-13: measure each gauntlet entry against Rust, C, Zig, Go, Python, Bun, Node, Vite and hand-optimized asm, comparing startup speed, run-time speed and binary size. The first goal is beating each language (the peer floor); the final goal is meeting or beating hand-optimized asm (the ceiling). A temporary Opus subagent improves the gauntlet harness and Tower; Lander5 runs the full rerun.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-14 ~11:00: post the peer measurements now, on the Tower gauntlet page, as the bars Jet must meet; Jet's rows are added later for the comparison. This supersedes the 2026-11-13 hold that waited for #6328 c22. Started at 10:59: node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --languages rust,c,zig,go,python,node,bun,vite,lua,luajit on dev a8ad13ab06 (the gate-p66 jet only for tool probes), then asm-parity ceilings. criteria.text: Every gauntlet entry has a peer slot for Rust, C, Zig, Go, Python, Bun, Node and Vite, plus its asm-parity ceiling reference. A peer that cannot express the entry is recorded in the manifest with its reason (Vite applies to web entries only); a missing program is an uncovered row, never a dropped one.

criteria.text: Each cell measures three metrics per peer: startup (exec to first output, wall), run time (wall, cycles and peak RSS) and binary size (the deployed artifact in bytes; for interpreted peers, the script plus the runtime it needs, labelled as such). Each gives a Jet/peer ratio judged at below 1.00 for the peer floor and at most 1.00 against the ceiling.

criteria.evidence: Landed on dev in light2 (980e02feb4..6fd8510b1f, Lander5), proved on the batch-15 jet (gate-p20) over the fit tree: 3eae175762 (GauntletTower-harness): one command (node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --jet-bin J) runs collect-all, and the dry-run lists every cell with measure, uncovered, not_applicable or unmeasured and its reason.

criteria.evidence: Landed on dev in light2 (980e02feb4..6fd8510b1f, Lander5), proved on the batch-15 jet (gate-p20) over the fit tree: 9135cddd94 (GauntletTower-tower): the existing Gauntlet page renders standings (entry x peer + asm x metric: ratio, floor pass/fail, ceiling gap) from a fixture results file, plus GET /api/gauntlet/standings and tower gauntlet standings; tower tests 26/26 and 53/53.

cards.title: Sweep regressions: the batch-17 ui sweep, the 2026-11-14 cases sweep and the 2026-11-15 p162 collect-all sweep
cards.body: The full ui profile on the batch-17 jet had 155 FAIL (157 on batch 16). G5DevX-2 and G6Meta-4 triaged every row on 2026-11-13. Rows whose new text was correct are re-blessed in light SUBs that cite the commit that changed the text. The rows below are real regressions, grouped by root. Each criterion names its owner in brackets. Diffs: Lander5 b17proofs/2.out on the gate-p22 jet.

Registering a route charges only what registration runs. Sema folds a lambda`s effects and call edges into the function that writes it (sema_effect_merge_lambda, JetSema Effects/Checks.jet:2605, called at :3370), so App.__route`s call_edges contain __app_page_response, and route() with a pure handler reaches FS.Read, Net and Time.Wait through the spooled body reader (Http.jet:967). Interim (2026-11-14): the send_fn_lowering and app-handler fixtures declare those effects, with a comment, which is sound because serving needs them. Fix: a TEffectFacts field that keeps edges from lambdas filling closed-row slots apart from a Core function`s own calls, charged where the lambda runs (app.serve()), not at registration. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Effects/route_registration_charges_only_registration` (route() with a pure handler reaches nothing; serve() reaches FS.Read, Net and Time.Wait), and the send_fn_lowering and app-handler fixtures drop their interim effect declarations.
