Today the type is accepted, the arm gets E0305 telling the user to name a member (Shown is one), and passing a Point gets E0112 (p206, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 5), probe v04_trait_member_in_union.jet in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview5/probes. Proof: a UI snapshot or cases row.

Val(s) of a read parameter never copies silently: with no from clause it is refused, as a bare return of the same value is (E0120), or it needs a written .copy(), since spec.md:1887 says Jet never hides a clone. Val(p) returned under a from clause (fn(..) -> T? from item) stays legal: it is a lend, not a copy. Today Val(s) compiles and copies with no mark (p206, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 5), probes v08_val_wrap_copy.jet, v08b_val_wrap_alone.jet and n15b_owned_payload_val.jet in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview5/probes. Sweep every enum or optional constructor wrapping a read value. Proof: a UI snapshot of the refusal, a cases row with the written copy, and a cases row of Val(p) under a from clause.

A lent result through dynamic dispatch keeps its loan and is not silently copied. With a trait method point: fn(self) -> Point? from self called on a [Shown] element, moving or mutating the list while the result lives is E0212, as the same loan on a struct method already is (probe w03d). p208 compiled it with no E0212; since p210 (c1fca7426c) w03b, w03c and y01 are E0212 on every tier, so the check half holds. The result is still a hidden copy: it reads 41 after the stored Point was bumped to 141, the IR of Point.point allocates and copies, and jet audit reports no copy (p208, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 6, probes y01_trait_loan_then_mutate.jet (with its .ir.out), y01d and y02 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes; earlier w03b/w03c in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyBallot/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot of the E0212 on the trait-dispatch form, a cases row of the legal use reading through the loan with no copy (jet audit shows none), and a sweep of every dyn-dispatch call site carrying a from-self return.

A union's named case and a qualified member may not share a last name segment: Point(Int) | geo.Point is refused with E0363, as Point(Int) | Point already is (y09b). Today it is accepted, and a bare .Point(n) arm binds the named case, leaving the member with no bare spelling (p208, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 6, probes y09_union_named_case_vs_member_leaf.jet and y09d_named_case_bare_arm_binds.jet in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot of the E0363 and a sweep of every union in the tree that the rule refuses.

Writing to an arm binding over a &Item parameter is refused with a report that blames the binding: the binding is read-only, and item itself is writable. Today it gets E0205 'Cannot edit through item — it has read access only', which names the wrong thing (p208, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 6, probe y08_write_subject_arm.jet in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot.

A from clause naming a && (owned) parameter is refused at the declaration with a registered diagnostic, since an owned argument is consumed and nothing outlives it to lend. Today the declaration is accepted, and the call is then refused with a misleading E0209 pointing at the result as a later use of item (p208, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 6, probe y07b_owned_subject_with_from.jet in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot at the declaration.

A from return is a real loan at run time: a function returning T? or T from a borrowed owner (fn(item: X) -> T? from item with a read parameter, and a method -> T? from self, called directly or through trait dispatch) carries a pointer into the owner's payload, with no new cell, no byte copy and no retain, on O0, O1 and O2. Two cases must stay safe first: (a) an argument converted at the call (a Point passed where a union is expected) lives in a temporary cell that is released right after the call (op 16 in the IR, probe z04), so the loan must keep that temporary alive for the result's life, or the call is refused; (b) a body that returns a fresh value, or a copy of another parameter, on some path under from item (probe z05) has no owner to point into, so that path either stays a copy that jet audit reports or is refused. Today the from form and the same function without from emit identical IR at O0 (a 24-byte optional cell, a byte copy and a retain), and jet audit counts only the one without from (p207-p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 reviews 6 and 7, probes y12_from_val_copy_audit.jet with its .ir.out in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes, z01, z01b, z04 and z05 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview7/probes). Proof: a cases row whose IR or jet audit shows no copy for each form, a case or UI row for (a) and for (b), and a paired size/speed cell against the copy form. Before lowering, two more cases must be checked (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8): a view captured by a lambda (c50) and a view of a Shared field written through any handle (c51); c46 lands only after both. Review 9 found more carriers: c46 lands only after c50, c51, c54 and c56 (struct field, enum payload, list, defer, method value, Shared to task).

The same-named-member E0305 branch treats only member types, never a named case, as a member. Today on Point(Int) | Point it adds a second error after E0363, and its suggested fix Point1(Point(Int)) | … fails with E0003 when applied (p209, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 7, probe z07 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview7/probes, control y09b in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes). Every fix a diagnostic suggests must compile when applied. Proof: a UI snapshot of y09b showing E0363 alone, and a cases row applying the remaining suggestion.

A type already refused by E0363 gets no follow-up E0641 (no-cascade rule): one root, one report. Today z03 reports E0363 and then an E0641 whose suggested fix also leaks the mangled name .M__fn_Int_____Int_ (the name leak is c27) (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 7, probe z03 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview7/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot showing E0363 alone.

I2: a generic function with a union parameter compiles and runs. Today any call of fn<T>(x: String | Int, ...) style signatures ICEs (exit 101, 'ir.build unlowered … argument type String | Int') on O0, O1 and O2 (p209, dev a1c3325a65; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes a07, a07b and a07c in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes). Proof: a cases row calling generic functions with union parameters (and union-typed generic arguments) on O0/O1/O2, plus a sweep of IR argument lowering for union types.

A from view captured by a lambda keeps its loan: moving or writing the owner while the lambda that holds the view lives is E0212, as it is without the lambda (spec.md:2058-2059 (at dev 7f902dd915): captures keep the view fact). Today the lambda form lets the owner move with no error (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probe a01 against a01b in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes). Safe today only because the view is a copy; once #6839 c46 lowers views to pointers this reads freed memory. Proof: a UI snapshot of the refusal and a cases row of the legal capture. Also stored and returned lambdas that capture a view outlive the owner's move today (review 9, probes e02 and e03 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes). Stored lambdas clone their captures, so the capture stays a loan: moving or rewriting the owner while the lambda lives is E0212 (D-PRIM-ANY1 ballot ¶48 at round 10: every holder keeps the owner borrowed).

A from view read out of a Shared field is checked against writes to that field, through the same handle or a second one: the write is refused while the view lives, or the view is not a loan. Today the view survives the write, and in the IR the value it was read from is released right after the call (op 70) (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes a03 and a03b with IR in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes). Safe today only because the view is a copy; c46 must not lower this case to a pointer until it is checked. Proof: a UI snapshot and a cases row for each handle form.

E0305's suggested fix for a same-named pair compiles when applied. Today it spells the file's own type as <filestem>.Point, which fails with E0119 and then an E0108 that contradicts itself (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes a04 and a04c in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes; c47 covers the named-case form). Proof: a UI snapshot of the corrected fix text and a cases row applying it. E0307's fix has the same defect: it spells the package's own member as filestem.Point (review 9, probe f06 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes); fix both.

An arm refused with E0305 still declares its binding (with an error type), so its uses add no cascade E0107: one root, one report. Today each use of the binding adds an E0107 (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes c1, a04, a08 and o8f in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot showing E0305 alone.

A loan keeps its owner through every carrier: a view (a from result or an arm binding) stored in a struct field (e01, against control e01b, which is E0212), an enum payload or nested binding (e07, against e07b), a list built in a loop (e05), a defer (e06), a method value bound to it (e08), or a Shared cell handed to a task (e09, which bypasses E1102) keeps the owner borrowed: moving or rewriting the owner while the carrier lives is E0212. A plain arm binding escapes the same way today (e10), and rewriting the owner leaves the view reading the old value (e11). Safe today only because views are copies; #6839 c46 must not lower views to pointers until this holds (p209, dev a1c3325a65, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 9, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes). Proof: one UI snapshot per carrier, plus a cases row of each legal carrier use. Also a tuple field, pair: (view: got, tag: 1) (h02), and a map value, m["k"] = got (h05): each lets the owner move and reads the old value today (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 10, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes).

Two instances of one generic type in a union (Box<Int> | Box<String>) have defined arms, and no diagnostic suggests or accepts the compiler's internal names. Today the bare .Box(b) arm is E0305 with the wrong text ('doesn't belong') (f01); the else is E0641 (f01b); and E0641's fix suggests .M_Box_Int_ | .M_Box_String_, which compile and bind (f01c, f01d), although the internal identity tag is refused elsewhere (a08). Internal names are never user spellings (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 9, probes f01-f01d in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes). Proof: UI snapshots of the corrected E0305 and E0641 text, and a case showing a mangled-name arm is refused. The same holds with one instance: E0641 over Int | Box<Int> offers .M_Box_Int_ (m33), and .M_Box_Int_(x) binds boxes.Box<Int> beside kit.Box (m31b) (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 11).

A from result or an arm binding chosen by a value-producing if or table keeps its owner borrowed: with got: pick(item), w: if flag -> got else -> None (h06), the call itself in a branch, w: if flag -> pick(item) else -> None (h09), the same view in both branches (h08), a table's value (h10) or an arm binding (h11), moving or rewriting the owner while w lives is E0212, as it is for a second local (h01) or a relay through a from function (h03). Today each compiles, the move prints the old value, and rewriting the owner leaves w reading 41 (h12). spec.md:2057-2058 keeps invalidation through control-flow joins and 2068-2069 unions branch sources (dev 7f902dd915). Safe today only because views are copies; #6839 c46 must not lower views to pointers until this holds (p209 and p210, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 10, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot per form and a cases row of the legal use.

A bare generic name in type position (fn(b: Box) with Box: struct<T>) reports E0104 alone: one root, one report. Today it adds an E0112 at the call, '`show` wants `Box` for argument 1, but this is `Box`<Int>', whose type text puts the type arguments outside the backticks (p209, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 10, probe t03 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot showing E0104 alone.

A user trait implemented for a library trait type (impl lib8.Shown.Back {}) is refused with E0301 at the impl, as impl Shape {} is (spec.md:924-925), since a trait names no type to implement it for; or it works. Today it is accepted and inert: a Shown value has no point() (E0311, m44), and a Shown value at a T: Back bound gets E0904 'No trait named Back is in scope for the bound on T', naming a declared trait (m47) (p210, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 11, probes fm/m44, fm/m44b, fm/m47). Proof: a UI snapshot.

cards.title: Optimization levels are spelled O0, O1 and O2: the -O0/-O1/-O2 flags replace --optimize=none|basic|full
cards.body:
Owner order (2026-11-14): "The flags for o0 o1 o2 should be o0 o1 o2 not optimize=basic."

Today the optimize build option (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet:48) has the values none, basic and full, spelled --optimize=basic on the command line, optimize: basic in a build profile and b.optimize(.Basic) in a build fn, with -O<n> accepted as a second spelling of the same flag. The levels are named O0, O1 and O2 everywhere else (AGENTS.md I9, the specs, traces and reports).

Decision (Main, within the owner order): one spelling of a level everywhere, with no alias (greenfield cutover). The flag is -O0, -O1 or -O2. The option's values are O0, O1 and O2, so a profile writes optimize: O2 and a build fn writes b.optimize(.O2). --optimize=<word> and the words none, basic and full are removed. Every in-repository caller moves in one cutover.

log.text: c1 holds except its jet explain clause: build_entry/optimize_levels_are_flags_and_trace_their_level PASSES on gate-p131 and jet build --help lists -O0/-O1/-O2, but local jet explain fails with E1227 (jetpack a0.0.44 against jet a0.0.45). c1 stays open for the explain proof after the next release admit.

criteria.text: The optimize option's values are O0, O1 and O2 in the BuildOptions registry. `jet build -O0|-O1|-O2`, `jet run`, `jet test` and every command that takes the option accept only these flags. `--optimize=none|basic|full` and `--optimize` with any value fail as ordinary unknown flags, with no teaching error, alias or jet fix rule. A build profile writes `optimize: O1` and a build fn `b.optimize(.O1)`. Help text and `jet explain` name the levels O0, O1 and O2. Proof: a cases row runs `jet build -O0`, `-O1` and `-O2` on one program, checks the level each traces, and shows that `--optimize=basic` is refused.
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev since c85b927fab (with 41f5054d46): the optimize option's registry values are O0/O1/O2, -O0/-O1/-O2 are its flags and --optimize with or without a value is jet.UnknownFlag. `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_entry/optimize_levels_are_flags_and_trace_their_level` on the gate-p136 batch jet: PASS (1 PASS, 0 FAIL).

criteria.text: Every in-repository caller moves in the same cutover: Compiler, Core, Jetpack, Tools (agent, release, ci, perf, gauntlet, tower), tests cases and UI snapshots, Examples, package.jet profiles, Docs/spec and the website source. Proof: `git grep -n -e '--optimize' -e 'optimize: \(none\|basic\|full\)' -e 'optimize(\.\(None\|Basic\|Full\))' -- Compiler Core Jetpack Tools tests Examples Docs/spec` prints nothing, and the touched cases and goldens pass on the batch jet.
criteria.evidence: The criterion's git grep over Compiler Core Jetpack Tools tests Examples Docs/spec finds no caller: its only hits are the board's own records quoting this criterion (Tools/tower/.tower/tower.json 67, history.json 37) and tests/cases/build_entry/optimize_levels_are_flags_and_trace_their_level.case (7), the proof that --optimize is refused as UnknownFlag, which passes; zero hits in Compiler, Core, Jetpack, Examples, Docs/spec or any other Tools or tests file on batch compiler gate-p131 (dev 8d83659ef3), verified by Main on dev 529aba0d26

cards.title: Exceptional built-in debugging and profiling, built on Jet's reflection and metaprogramming (Jai-style)
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-14), high priority, on G5: Jet ships exceptional built-in debugging and profiling, done early so the team dogfoods it to fix Jet itself. As in Jai, much of it should come cheaply from the reflection and metaprogramming Jet already has: type facts drive value display and watch expressions, and compile-time code that sees every function can insert profiling spans or checks without a separate tool. Today: jet perf (run, test, attach, view, compare, export; source sampling, memory counters, .jettrace) works; jet debug (lldb and DAP) is weak on the self-hosted toolchain (#6730 has 24 open criteria, and Compiler/JetDebug no longer checks); no metaprogram instrumentation exists; whole-program compiler events are still being planned (#5009). Depends on #6730 and #5009.

log.text: OWNER ORDER 2026-11-15 ~13:10: one goal agent slot does Jet's native debugger, profiler and perf (G5: #6730 jet debug, #4632 jet perf, #6918 debug info, #6841, #6919), native only with no lldb, gdb or Linux perf dependency. The G9 slot (GoalsB-5-2) takes it after its returned fixes; G9 is unstaffed until an agent snowballs past G6. Owner: GoalsB-5-2 (Pareto order 6730, 4632, 6918, 6841, 6919).

Owner direction (2026-11-15, chat): debugging and profiling are native Jet. jet debug and jet perf do the work themselves and depend on no external tool such as lldb, gdb or Linux perf. External tools serve only as comparators (as in #6730 c29) or as optional interop for users who bring them. This card is the native core of that direction.

criteria.text: A dated adversarial review in Docs/audits compares Jet's debugging and profiling, built and planned, with the best existing tools: Jai's metaprogram instrumentation (the compiler message loop and its profiling modules), Tracy, Superluminal, RemedyBG and the RAD Debugger, rr and Pernosco, Go's pprof, and the perf and Instruments tooling. Every claimed strength is attacked and every gap is put on this card or a ballot. Proof: the audit file and its verdict lines.
criteria.evidence: a98caf9890 on dev: Docs/audits/2026-11-14-debugging-profiling-review.md

criteria.text: Every new user surface this needs (an instrumentation hook, a #Profile-style marker, compiler-event APIs, debugger commands) is on a ratified Tower ballot before it is built. Proof: `tower decision show <ID>` reports ratified for each ballot ID listed on this card.

A user-written compile-time program instruments every function of a package with profiling spans through reflection and compiler events, with no change to the profiled source. It produces a jet perf view, and the instrumented program prints the same output on O0, O1 and O2. The instrumentation also sends meta.events call timings to a sink (merged from #4632 c7). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Tooling/Performance/InstrumentEveryFunction` passes on O0, O1 and O2.

Debugger display and watch expressions come from the compiler's type facts (reflection), so every Jet type shows as its Jet value in jet debug and over DAP, with no hand-written per-type formatter. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/type_facts_display_every_kind` on the native tier (with #6730 c2/c3 met).

jet perf and jet debug work on the self-hosted toolchain end to end: the Examples/Tooling/Debugging and Performance examples pass their goldens on O0, O1 and O2 (the Compiler/JetDebug package check is #6730 c25).

Instrumentation costs nothing when it is off and stays within a measured budget when it is on, so a profiled build keeps Jet's performance gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry profile-overhead` reports the instrumented and plain pair from the canonical perf manifest.

A join's wait interval in the trace names the awaited task and its spawn source location, and the timeline links them without manual alignment. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Perf/join_wait_names_awaited_task`. (was #4632 c1)

Inclusive and exclusive time are both reported per source location, and a recursive fib reports inclusive time without double counting. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Perf/recursive_inclusive_time`. (was #4632 c2)
The perf receipt names the build profile and capture settings used. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Perf/receipt_names_profile_and_capture`. (was #4632 c5)

Frame profiling and draw-event tracing run through typed game events, a bounded relay, strict identity and truncation checks, and `jet perf` run and attach, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Perf/game_frame_events` on each tier. (was #4632 c6)

`jet perf --pprof` writes the protobuf that `go tool pprof` opens, and an OTLP export exists; each is proved by opening the file in the peer tool (Docs/Audits/2026-11-14-debugging-profiling-review.md). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Perf/pprof_and_otlp_open_in_peer_tools`, SKIP-HOST without the tools. (was #4632 c8)

jet perf, natively, attributes each sample to the Jet function and source line that ran, matching what Linux perf reports on the same -O2 image (perf serves only as the comparator): a probe with fib under main shows fib's share. (was #4727 c9; Docs/Audits/2026-11-14-debugging-profiling-review.md) (was #4632 c9)

The ratified cache visualization ships: a jet command or report shows, per function and source line, cache misses by level and the points where the program falls to RAM or to disk (page faults), with an example whose golden output is checked on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Perf/CacheVisualization`. (was #6312 c3)

`jet perf run` with the memory method reports L1D, LLC and dTLB misses and page faults per source line on Linux x86-64. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter PerfRun/memory_counters_per_line`. (was #6312 c6)
A strided array walk reports more L1D misses per element than a sequential walk. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Perf/StridedVsSequentialL1D`. (was #6312 c7)
Hosts without counters report unavailable with a reason, never zero counts. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter PerfRun/no_counters_reports_unavailable`. (was #6312 c8)

`jet perf run` on ScriptBench w04 (wordfreq) writes a sampling profile with self and inclusive time per Jet source line plus allocation counts per line. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter PerfRun/sampling_profile_per_line`. (was #6312 c9)

`jet inspect live --attach PID` on a process started with observe enabled prints the task tree, channel depths, deadlines and effect counts (D-OBSERVE-LIVE1=A); on the decision's example it shows the blocked transform task with its full channel. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LiveInspect/`. (was #6386 c2)

The live view also shows open spans and allocation counts per task. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LiveInspect/live_inspector_reads_running_tasks_channels_and_resources_without_payloads`. (was #6386 c3)

Attaching to a process not started with observe enabled, or owned by another user, fails with a named error and changes nothing in the target. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter inspect_live_attach_refused`. (was #6386 c4)
jet perf is built. Proof: every Tests/known-failing.tsv row on #6418 that reports E2104 for `jet perf` passes on the default tier, and the rows are removed. (was #6418 c6)

The time to the first stop and the time per step are measured against lldb on the same image (Docs/Audits/2026-11-14-debugging-profiling-review.md). Proof: a committed measurement under Docs/Audits naming the image hash, the commands and both timings. (was #6730 c29)

cards.title: One audited memory chokepoint: every raw memory action goes through one small, heavily audited module
cards.body:
Owner direction, 2026-11-14: memory actions go through a single inspectable place that is heavily audited, so any memory-safety risk is found by looking in one spot, and memory bugs are prevented structurally rather than reviewed site by site.

Today raw memory actions sit in about 1528 #Unsafe regions spread across Compiler (about 791), the runtime and Core (Docs/spec/safety.md, Tools/agent/UnsafeRatchet.jet). The ratchet counts them but does not concentrate them.

Shape (to be attacked by the adversarial review before anything is built): one memory kernel module owns a small set of typed primitives (allocate, free, resize, raw read and write, pointer offset, copy and move of bytes, atomics, OS mapping, foreign-pointer crossing), each with stated preconditions and its own tests. The chokepoint is enforced in source by sema, not paid for at run time: sema refuses a raw memory operation anywhere outside the kernel, and the primitives inline at O1/O2, so the chokepoint costs nothing. Accesses that sema already proves safe (checked indexing, owned fields) stay ordinary loads and stores; the kernel covers what sema cannot prove. Centralizing the operation does not by itself centralize the reasoning about why a call site meets a precondition, so the primitives should carry typed capabilities (handles a caller cannot forge) to make most preconditions type-enforced rather than reviewed.

log.text: Closed 2026-11-15 by Main. All 12 remaining criteria are met with exercised evidence (c1-c5 and c7-c10, c12-c14). The two performance criteria (c6 zero cost, c11 ceiling) moved to #6975 (G11) under the owner order of 2026-11-15. #Unsafe count over the kernel cutover, lines with a #Unsafe(...) region, dev e1ef911ec1 (2026-11-14 16:55) against 604cc6eb7a (2026-11-15 06:15): runtime 643 to 488 (-155), Core/Crypto -5, Core/Encoding -2, Core/Testing -1, Core/Mem +4 (the kernel itself), JetBackend +13 and JetFoundation +3 (non-kernel work tonight), tests and UI fixtures +56, Examples/Memory +3, Tools/perf +6. Whole repository 1426 to 1348. Shipped code (runtime, Core, Compiler) net -143.

c12 route decision (Main): with the runtime-identity scope removed, a sema probe finds 109 E3114 hits in the kernel files (Alloc 64, RawWords 25, Sync 9, Fault 5, Secret 3, Thread 3; 87 functions). The ratified address rule exempts package-private (priv) and #Unsafe functions, so the kernel helpers whose every Jet caller is inside the runtime package become priv. That uses the ratified rule, with no scope. A runtime function that another package calls by Jet name stays public and gets a typed owner or view signature. C ABI exports keep their symbols. The scope is deleted, and a guard keeps any later public raw-address runtime function under E3114. What is not done: c12's text also describes moving about 13,400 runtime-internal call sites of rt_text_word and sync_load to typed owners and views. Those sites raise no E3114 once the helpers are package-private, and the ratified rule does not require that migration, so it is not part of meeting c12. A typed internal API would be a separate design choice. Owner: CardCloser-3, in slices per file group.

c14 boundary decision (Main): two direct kernel-call sites stay as the boundary of 'no direct mmap', each with a stated reason at the site: the loader's emitted OS_SYS_MUNMAP executor rows, which run before the runtime and its sentry exist, and Assets/FaultReport/report.S, a relocation-free dying-path blob that cannot call Jet. The allocator's large-block mremap goes through the kernel primitive family (an untracked heap remap beside os_map and os_unmap), not a raw syscall. SUB CardCloser-3-kernel-maps-untracked-form is queued; the remap follow-up is stacked on it.

c14 decision (Main, within approved scope): the sentry tracks live storage precisely. (1) The allocator's own slab, large-object and page-map mappings are the heap; per-block MemStorage registration covers them, and registering whole slabs would make freed blocks look live. They still go through the kernel map primitive, in its untracked form, not a raw mmap. (2) Mappings on paths that must not allocate (Fault, auxv and Secret pages) and the ProductionReceipt scratch also use the untracked kernel form, each with a stated reason. The comptime reply mapping named in c14 stays tracked; only a separate refused-frame scratch on the dying path may be untracked. (3) Done means: a grep of Compiler/ and JetRuntime for raw mmap/munmap finds only the kernel primitive, and the c14 R0801 case passes on every tier. Owner: CardCloser-3.

Its runtime-mappings-sentry change (3852240eb4) is in the runtime, which a compiler links from its seed, so it shows one batch later; recheck on p165 before c7. Separately, single-use-holders (df9300826a) broke 6 context_allocator cases (E0140/E0142 on a counter allocator); CardCloser-3 owns the fix and the sweep of every source the rule reaches.

All but atomics are still over 1.00.

c11 allocfree root (CardCloser-3, p157 release build, disassembly and perf): both fast paths are hit (alloc_try's thread-cache path; free's cache push; 0 samples in refill, slab, validate and lock). Per operation: 361 instructions and 108 cycles; cycles: run loop 47%, alloc 42%, free 11%. Roots: (1) the Core wrapper adds a 16 B header on top of the runtime's 24 B, so a 1-byte request takes 41 B and lands in the 64 B class; (2) the alloc fast path is about 75 instructions (a class ladder, 5 callee-saved pushes, two header stores), and free recomputes the class from the size; (3) the loop carries a stop poll after every call and int_clone tests on Int. Order: (1), (2), then the Result out slot (mapping), then (3) in codegen.

c11 mapping (CardCloser-3 profile on p152; 400 cycles and 1080 instructions per pass): ~35% is the boxed Result<Region> return (a 40-byte heap box plus a store-forward stall), ~17% the two lock cmpxchg on the window stack, ~10% the region record's heap alloc/free, and the rest page-map work plus madvise. Ruling (Main, under the AGENTS.md performance-gate rule that the reference includes the smallest hand-written implementation of each feature the Jet program delivers): the mapping asm reference registers the region in a minimal page map. Work order: window stack without locked cmpxchg; region record from a per-thread free list; reference update; then general Result lowering (a two-word payload returns in registers) split into items of an hour or less.

On p144: 32 B (3.20x) / 1.50x. The pointer-step-fold second program (CardCloser-3-pointer-step-fold/second/measure.sh, 11 pinned runs of run 20000): 166 B / 694.2M cycles on p144, 114 B / 254.9M on p146, output sum 81920000 unchanged. The fold (9a82866572) cuts the general pointer step's code 31% and its cycles 63% on a program unlike the cell. rawword cycles stay over at 1.28x; the gap is open.

c11 decisions (Main, 2026-11-14 23:35). (1) Each remaining primitive cell (mapping, compare, alloc/free, resize) lands as an honest measurement even while it fails the ceiling. (2) No easier substitute: Region.claim is an extra cell, never alloc/free's replacement. The alloc/free and resize references implement the same features at minimum size: a slab with size classes, the page map, and cross-thread free. (3) Compare adds no primitive (I8): the cell measures existing [U8] equality against a memcmp-class SIMD reference; a byte-loop loss is fixed in the general equality lowering. (4) Mapping: the runtime fix carves page-map units from one aligned VA reservation (no trim munmaps) and keeps the global lock off the fast path, general for every Region.reserve.

c11 rawword (CardCloser-3, 2026-11-14 23:25). The Int-to-word conversion for a raw pointer offset is already inline: an add/jo tag test, about 12 B per access, with the call only on the cold big-Int path. OptRange deletes it when it proves the Int inline. rawword paid it because its Op table held Int fields while ref.S holds 4-byte fields; the cell moves to U32 fields so both sides do the same work on the same data. Known general cost: a raw access indexed by an Int that OptRange can't prove inline pays the 12 B tag test.

OWNER ORDER 2026-11-14 ~21:00, standing overnight and superseding earlier orderings. Agents work ONLY this list, in this order, closing it out: (1) precompiled Core, #6328 c22/c37 and #6759; (2) speed plan steps 1-5 of #5479 exactly as its plan defines them (step 2 = #5479 c6 + #6328 c23; step 3 = #5479 c7 + #5910; step 4 = #5479 c8; step 5 = #5910 c6 + #5479 c2), with no other speed or size work until G11; (3) the memory kernel #6842, including c11; (4) G6; (5) G9; (6) G3; (7) G5; (8) G10; (9) G7. No other cards and no side work. Finished, ready work is never pulled: it lands. The only exceptions are fixes for failures that block the list's own work and owner-requested ballots, and Main decides them. TowerKeeper-1 (temporary, owner-approved) rebuilds the board: frozen cards untouched, nothing obsoleted without a ratified authority, no work lost.

Owner order 2026-11-14 ~21:15 (standing; supersedes earlier allocation and goal orders). Five agent slots: (1) FINISH precompiled Core ASAP (#6328 c22/c37 and #6759: a measured win over no precompiled Core), then help finish speed steps 1-5 (#5479). (2) Finish speed steps 1-5 (#5479) ASAP. (3) Finish the memory kernel (#6842, D-MEM-CHOKEPOINT1=A) ASAP. (4) and (5) Finish G6 and G9 ASAP. When slots 1-3 are done, they help on G6 and G9. After G6 and G9: G3, then G5, then G10; then G7, then G11, then G13. Pareto wins land first (a hard requirement). Main self-evaluates every 30 minutes against these goals and the overnight timeline and corrects course; the order is recorded durably (Tower, plus Main's handoff file) so compaction cannot lose it.

Main 2026-11-14 (operational, within ratified D-MEM-CHOKEPOINT1=A): c3's 'one memory kernel module' reads as the ratified form. Each package names its kernel files in policy memory: .Kernel([...]). A file goes in only if it implements a primitive (allocation, free, region, mapping, atomic word, device register, copy or fill) or an owner type that hands out views. Files that only use raw memory migrate to call those primitives. After Core's kernel, 483 regions remain: the runtime 387 across 80 files, OS/Linux.jet 57, and the image Loader and SessionHost 39. CardCloser-3 migrates the small-site files by area, then the JetRuntime and JetBackend kernel policies, which need a batch compiler carrying r3.

Main 2026-11-14: c6's zero-cost bar against the direct spelling stays, now proved by exact codegen-catalog equality with a zero_cost_pairs timed pair beside it; the new ceiling criterion adds the machine-code maximum on top. Owners: CardCloser-3 (kernel policy, sema, View, c8 and c10); GoalsA-1-3 (c2 inventory, the kernel public-fn rule, the c4 cutover); PrecompiledCore-4 (c6, c7 and the ceiling cells, with the primitives' lowering).

Main, 2026-11-14: c1 met; ballot D-MEM-CHOKEPOINT1 is open (recommended A: kernel files hand out close owners plus owner-tied views, checked by the existing E0212/E2305/E0211). c3-c7 wait on the ballot. The review found I1 holes that hold in today's code regardless of the ballot, so they are fixed now under this card: (1) .copy() of a #SingleUse handle compiles, and so does copying a struct that holds one; releasing both frees twice and release builds exit 0 with no #Unsafe in user code; Core mem.Block copies the same way. (2) a mem.Window handed out by a handle reads after the handle is released. (3) a view stored in a field of a returned record escapes its owner. (4) values bound by a pattern skip close duties (owners are not closed; handles skip the drop error E0140). Probes are in the review's tests (inbox MemKernel-2-review/tests/adv).
Created by Main from the owner direction of 2026-11-14 (a single inspectable memory chokepoint). Built only after criterion 1's adversarial review passes.

criteria.text: Adversarial review first: a dated audit in Docs/audits attacks each claimed strength of the one-chokepoint design (structural prevention, single audit spot, zero run-time cost) against the strongest existing practice, with sources: Rust's unsafe concentrated in std and audited crates (and its unsafe-code guidelines), seL4's verified kernel boundary, CHERI capabilities, Zig's explicit allocator interface, Go's runtime-only unsafe and Swift's UnsafePointer surface. It checks each claim with a runnable probe or measurement, and ends with a verdict per claim. Nothing below is built until the verdict holds or every gap is redesigned and reviewed again.

criteria.text: Each primitive has a test per stated precondition, plus a fuzz run over allocate, resize and free sequences, and O0, O1, O2 and web agree on every kernel test (I9). Today that scope keeps E3114 at its state before the cutover, while E3113 holds everywhere. Proof: the scope is deleted, and jet check of Compiler/JetRuntime and its fixtures reports E3114=0.

cards.title: Known-failing ledger: the remaining failing cases and their three open criteria
cards.body:
Successor of #5454, which closed with 90 of 93 criteria met because it had grown too large to read. This card owns every row in tests/known-failing.tsv that names it (163 rows moved from #5454), and the three criteria #5454 left open, copied unchanged with their history.

State on gate-p131 (dev 8d83659ef3), 2026-11-14: pure has 2 rows needing the unbuilt `jet profile` command; comptime_core_pure_parity has 9 rows (Tally<enum> refused as not hashable, ID<String> without ==, weekday off by one at comptime, Measurement +); authority has about 20 rows needing the unbuilt core.process.workspace/run surface; taskgroup_params has 1 row (E1110 missing its second count).

criteria.text: Compile-time values match run time in the pure suite: store record generations and nested pretty rendering of compile-time values print the same as at run time.

The authority testkit cases that still fail (grants and providers, E0119, non-hosted verbs, core.process.run, fixtures, jet query, fix status on stderr) each pass or have their known-failing row re-pointed at the card that owns the unbuilt feature. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/` shows no FAIL and no KNOWN-FAILING row naming #6843.

cards.title: Reflection reads typed facts: callables, declarations, fields, markers and run-time views
cards.body:
Destination: every reflection read in Jet returns a typed record from one checked fact path, so a library can read a function's parameters, a type's fields, a marker's arguments or a run-time value without parsing strings. This is the reading half of the metaprogramming ladder (D-META-LADDER1=A) and what markers, derives and fn build all stand on.

Governing decisions: D-META-REFLECT2=A (the TypeInfo, FieldInfo, FunctionInfo records; TypeId identity; PreparedValue), D-PREP-SURFACE2=A, D-MARKER-REFLECT1=A (a marker reads as the typed record its declaration describes), D-REFLECT-FIELDTYPE1=A (field.type is a TypeId). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.

Decisions already taken for this work (Main, 2026-11-11): PreparedValue is a public enum mirroring the compiler's compile-time value cases (Int, Float, Bool, Char, String, Enum, List, Struct, Unit); TypeId is the TypeInfo identity; SourceSpan gains its file; SettingOrigin adds Build beside Declaration, Profile and CommandLine because fn build writes settings. A guard refuses a String-typed reflection field wherever a typed value exists. Fact reads are compile-time only since 4328d5ff94, so run-time examples read them through #run.

Carried from #3520 (closed 2026-11-14) and #6039 (closed 2026-11-14).

cards.title: Generated code: the Compiler value, Meta effects, generation rounds and rollback
cards.body:
Destination: a program that generates or rewrites code does it through one passed, root-created `Compiler` value whose actions are Meta effects checked like any effect, and generation is deterministic, provenanced and all-or-nothing. Why: generated code must be as trustworthy and debuggable as hand-written code, and nothing above marker expansion may happen by import alone.

Governing decisions: D-META-LADDER1=A (Meta effects follow the rule of every effect; compiler control is one passed value; macros stay out), D-META-OPTIN2=A (a checked package opt-in suffices for above-level-five operations), D-HOOK-STAGES1=A, D-ADDSTRUCT-TYPE1=A (meta.add_struct names a field's type with a TypeId). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.

Carried decisions: the org policy file accepts the same `authority: { deny: [...] }` record as package.jet (D-EFFBUDGET1), applied as an outer rung that only narrows (Main 2026-11-11). `#build`, `#program`, `#package` and `#phase` are spelled with `#` and cannot be shadowed (D-META-HASH2=A, landed 00a2b37a42..53805444ba). Sizing (owner 2026-11-11): each Compiler-value slice is at most one hour of code and one hour of tests. Background: the Compiler value needs a build session alive through application checking and closures called on each checked-function event; see the G6Decl notes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Decl/BLOCKED.md.

Carried from #3526, #3520 and #4276 (closed 2026-11-14).

criteria.text: A metaprogram action above marker expansion (adding declarations outside a marker, rewriting a body, making a type from text) needs a `Compiler` value, and each action checks its Meta cases (`Generate`, `Include`, `Rewrite`, `Types`, `Raw`) like any effect: denied by written code, otherwise allowed; without a `Compiler` value it is refused with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot.

Standard mode allows complete read-only reflection and explicit checked generation and refuses operations above level 5 unless the package opts in (D-META-OPTIN2=A); `#run` runs at every tier, fn build runs only for artifacts, and a built artifact never re-runs `#run`; a pure cache hit keeps every observable effect (print count and order).

`meta.add_struct` takes each field's type as a TypeId (D-ADDSTRUCT-TYPE1=A, ratified 2026-11-13); the String form of CompilerField.type is gone in one cutover, and a computed name is still refused with its registered code.

Each generated declaration and rewrite carries a stable identity and its full producer and Compiler-handoff chain in `jet inspect`, `jet explain`, the editor and the CLI; diagnostics name the caller, handler, output or missing producer separately.
criteria.evidence: Landed on dev in c6d9e746f2 (the editor names what made a generated module, from .jet/build/receipt.json; its message records that inspect, explain and the CLI already carried the producer and handoff chain). Checked 2026-11-14 on dev 72a8142651 with the gate-p136 jet: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter meta_ladder_missing_producer` PASS 1.

criteria.text: Each generation round, source identity, collision check, dependency edge, lock fact and rollback result is deterministic and source-provenanced: two runs, and runs with permuted, cold, warm and parallel schedules, give byte-identical output and provenance.

Shadowing, duplicate output, self and multi-node cycles, round exhaustion, outside-root paths and materialization failure each leave no partial module and report their registered code with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot; each test fails if the code, span, message or cleanup path is bypassed.

`generate {}` helper values and inline `b.generate` are one mechanism with byte-identical output and source maps; handwritten code uses the generated items; a collision reports at the helper's line; opt-in in-tree materialization fails on drift; raw source strings are refused.
Generation follows a dependency-aware schedule (declared inputs, rounds, typed barriers, promised outputs); cycles and duplicate outputs are detected with registered codes.
When a promised generated output is missing, the error names its producer and its consumer, and an unrelated unknown name is not reported as a generation promise.
Cancelling generation midway, or exhausting memory or steps during it, leaves no partly published declaration and no stale checked fact; the next run starts clean.

The Compiler value's method list is generated from Core declarations: Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerValueMethods.jet no longer lists records and fields by hand, so a new field on `CompilerChecked` appears with no evaluator edit.

Each number family has one generic definition that compile-time code expands to the needed widths (D-CORE-NUMFAMILY1=A), replacing one hand-written type per size. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/` on O0, O1 and O2, and `git grep` shows one family definition per number kind in Core. The frozen #4570 holds the original item.

Modules a package's build: fn adds load the same way under jet run, jet check and jet build (I9): today only jet build loads them (found 2026-11-15 by GoalsA-1-4 on the EntityBuckets example, whose sidecar case runs jet build then the built program as a workaround). Proof: a case that adds a module from build: fn and runs it with jet run, jet check and jet build, with one output.

cards.title: Compile-time evaluation: #run values match run time, fall back cleanly and run once
cards.body:
Destination: compile-time evaluation (`#run`, `#if`, `#loop`, `NAME: #run value`, and automatic folding of immutable bindings) means exactly what the same code means at run time, reports every failure at its source with a registered code, and never runs twice. Why: compile-time code is ordinary Jet; any drift between the two meanings is a silent wrong answer.

Governing decisions: D-META-SPELL1=A (`#run`, `#if`, `#loop` replace `comptime`; shipped, cases ratified_p12/d_meta_spell1_forms), D-COMPTIME-WORD1=A, D-PREP-BRANCH1=A, D-PREP-FN1=A, D-MODULE-BUILD1=A (a module-level value that fails or has effects is a build error, E0643), D-EXEC2=A (tiers are O0, O1 and O2; no interpreter). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md; the 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-10 entries of Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md.

Carried from #4276 (closed 2026-11-14).

cards.title: One fact registry: typed rows, one query, uniform flow joins and one gate ledger
cards.body:
Destination: every compiler fact a user can see (marker rules, knowledge planes, rights, build facts, gates, send-safety, failure attribution) lives in one registry of typed rows, read through one public query, so tools and libraries see the same facts the compiler uses. Why: today facts live in several tables with several readers, so tools drift from the compiler.

Governing decisions: D-META-REG1=A (one registry substrate, told apart by attachment), D-META-REG2=A (one public `compiler.query`, ratified 2026-11-11), D-LEDGER1=D (three lifetime-separated stores behind one typed query), D-FACT-FLOW1=A, D-FACT-GATE1=A, D-FACT-HOME1=A, D-FACT-OWN1=A. How a fact is declared is D-DECL-TYPES1=A (field-less structs implementing Fact), built on the declarations card. Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.

Carried from #4276 (closed 2026-11-14).

criteria.text: `core.compiler` has one public typed query, `compiler.query(store, kind: FactKind) -> [FactRow] MetadataError!`, over the schema, package and plugin fact stores (D-META-REG2=A); `jet inspect facts --store=… --kind=… [--json]` renders the same call with the same rows, identities and errors, and no second registry reader remains; a golden counts marker rows both ways and gets equal counts on O0, O1 and O2, and a missing store reports its MetadataError with a UI snapshot.
Marker rules, knowledge planes, rights and build facts register in one registry substrate, told apart by attachment (D-META-REG1=A); no second registration table remains in Compiler/.

One flow-fact store on the checker holds every per-binding fact; each plane supplies only its join rule, and the walker applies joins the same way at every if, loop and arm table for ownership, effects, state and taint (D-FACT-FLOW1=A).

Every gate lands in one ledger: unsafe regions, impure marks, grants, trust and .Force, taint scrubs, duty drops and precision demotions; `jet inspect gates` prints counts per kind with security kinds first and a filter selects one kind (D-FACT-GATE1=A).

Facts with user-visible meaning are typed registry rows readable through the fact query: send-safety, failure attribution, #Track, view and unit-scale provenance, and maturity; prover internals such as uninitialized tracking and exhaustiveness stay inside the engine (D-FACT-HOME1=A).
The borrow checker stays a prover, never a fact plane: the registry has no ownership plane row, and the ownership sigil surface stays as ratified (D-FACT-OWN1=A).

One current version and fact-shape reference links its history, and `compiler-proof checking` reads the version from emitted output, not from a hard-coded number. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter fact_shape_version_from_output`. (was #3186 c11)

One interned, checked derivation relation records how each fact was produced across facts, execution and optimization; producers are authoritative, persistence is lossless, and the CLI and LSP read it. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Explain/derivation_relation_`. (was #3186 c15)

cards.title: Markers, effects, facts, derives and tags are ordinary declared types (D-DECL-TYPES1)
cards.body:
Destination: Jet has no special declaration words for markers, effects, facts, derives or tags. Each is an ordinary struct, enum or impl of a Core trait (Marker, Effect, Fact, Trait.Derive), so one mechanism, one reader and one set of tools serves all of them, and libraries declare their own on equal terms with Core.

Governing decisions: D-DECL-TYPES1=A (2026-10-30), D-TAG-MARKER1=A, D-FACT-MARKER1=A, D-DERIVE-PROVIDER1=A, D-MARKER-INBODY1=A (built by #6562), D-MARKER-MODULE1=A, D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1=A, D-MARKER-LAW1=A, D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1=A, D-DECL-COLON1=A. Owner orders: retired declarations get no teaching diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule (2026-11-06); Jet's own diagnostic types live under the `jet.` prefix (2026-10-30).

Decided without ballot (Main 2026-11-11): wrap is typed with the existing Code value and lowered through root-authorized Compiler events and Meta.Rewrite; library combine is as already ratified (no package marker sets resolution). Package settings take ordinary markers on the package settings record (a header in package.jet, the same marker on an inline package record); no inner-marker sigil. Marker struct form: `struct X { fields; impl Marker { settings; fn expand(self, target: Target) { template } } }`; a trailing list field without a default is variadic.

Carried from #6039, #4276, #4284 and #3662 (closed 2026-11-14).

The criterion requires the word gone and the 46 Prelude effects converted.

cards.title: jet fmt --simplify: guard clauses, single-use temporaries and one corpus migration
cards.body:
Destination: `jet fmt --simplify` rewrites code to the ratified simplest forms, the repository is migrated once with it, and style points are rewritten, never reported. Plain `jet fmt` keeps its one default style. Why: style should cost nobody attention; Jet has no warnings (owner, 2026-11-09 language review), so anything a tool can fix it fixes.

Governing decisions: D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1=A (plain jet fmt unchanged; the rewriter runs only with `--simplify`; teams canonicalize a repo in one deliberate run). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/cli.md (jet fmt), Docs/spec/spec.md (formatter).

Carried from #4276 and #6637 (2026-11-14).

criteria.text: The in-repo corpus is migrated once with `jet fmt --simplify`, in one mechanical commit, and stays migrated: `jet fmt --simplify --check Compiler Core Jetpack Tools Examples tests` exits 0, and a plain `jet fmt` run leaves code it did not format unchanged. Proof: `jet fmt --simplify --check Compiler Core Jetpack Tools Examples tests`

`jet fmt --simplify` rewrites a nested if/else into guard clauses (early return) without changing behavior and never reports it; it is applied across Compiler/, Core and Jetpack in one mechanical change, `jet fmt --check Compiler Core Jetpack` passes, and the self-host chain reaches its fixed point.

`jet fmt --simplify` inlines a needless temporary (an immutable binding used once, on the next line) only when evaluation order is unchanged, and never reports it; a fmt case pins an order-sensitive negative that is left alone.
`jet fmt` rewrites the old arm-table shapes (adds an explicit `else` arm, removes redundant returns and fallback tails), keeping comments, bindings, order, effects and spans, and reports nothing.

Tests/Cases/Fmt has one AST-equality and second-pass stability case for every enabled simplify rewrite, and fmt_project/simplify_mode_is_stable_across_a_project exists. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Fmt/fmt_simplify_` and `--filter fmt_project/` pass.

cards.title: Core gets no privilege a package lacks: host-leaf gates, per-domain call checks, Core-only constructs, #Unsafe and lexing
cards.body:
Destination: Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use (Docs/spec/philosophy.md, pillar 5). Today sema lets Core do things a package cannot: it gates host leaves on the caller's module name, keeps a hand-written checker per Core domain, accepts constructs only in Core files, exempts Core from the #Unsafe secret rules, and lexes and parses Core with its own rules.

Why it matters: a third-party library must be able to do what Core does, and every privilege is a second rule that tools copy and drift on.

Sources: findings F02, F03, F07, F08 and F14 of Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md (line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Split from #6151, which keeps the Core-declaration and twin-table work. D-HOST-LEAF1=E (runtime is an ordinary library, #6615). Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4).

Ballot: package-private `__` helpers (the lexing criteria) are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

log.text: c3 needs an owner ballot: Http Body's static constructors (text/json/form/reader) share names with its reading methods; options are a rename, static and instance members with the same name, or free constructors. GoalsA-1-4 drafts it; the card moves on to #6847. c11, c13 and c14 depend on MemKernel-6's __-helper codemod.

c13 ruling (Main, 2026-11-15, under ratified D-CORE-BUILTINS1=A and D-CORE-ROLE1=A): of the 324 compiler-known Core names, the 14 types and traits plus the 13 dispatcher-row functions move into jet_builtins; the about 291 bodied Core helpers the compiler lowers to by name stay in their own modules (bodies, private dependencies and ring unchanged), drop the __ prefix and carry #builtin.Role(.X), and the compiler finds them through a role table instead of by name. Synthesized calls bind the role-resolved symbol, so E1013 needs no exception. Done by codemod in large slices; owner MemKernel-6.

Finding (MemKernel-6 sweep, 2026-11-15; list at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemKernel-6/byte-slice-hits.md): about 120 compiler sites slice byte offsets with the character-counting String.slice. Family A (about 70) quotes span text: sema KeyBy, CLI expand/explain/copy-marker, LSP completion/rename/formatting/folding, Canvas/devserver. Family B (about 50) cuts names, keys and paths at find/rfind or byte-scan offsets. LSP lsp_uri_to_path also panics on a non-ASCII file: URI. Compiler fix: one JetFoundation byte-slice helper replaces the ad-hoc copies, landed by package group. Root in Core needing an owner ballot: Core String mixes units (find/rfind/count_bytes count bytes; slice/len/index_of count characters), and Core carries at least 8 private slice_bytes copies (Text, Fmt, Files, Net, Url, Term, Auth, Data/Sketch). One unit, or a public byte-range slice, is public API. Ballot to draft: D-STRING-UNITS1.
c1 on dev 5cc6567e75: one hit remains, Calls/Methods.jet:1906 (protected: ... type_name_value.starts_with("<corelib>/")). Sent to MemKernel-6.

Finding (MemKernel-6, 2026-11-15): jet inspect codemod cannot index or edit Core sources. It compiles every root as a user unit, so a Core file fails with E0067 on its own __ helpers and the plan stops before renaming. A symbol_rename also cannot add priv, and it refuses a destination name that resolves anywhere in the unit (locals included). The D-CORE-HELPERS1 renames of the large Core files (Math, Web, Server, Tls, Image, Db, Client; about 3000 sites) therefore use a throwaway lexer-token rename script, reviewed by diff and jet check Core. A Core-unit mode for codemod belongs on the codemod card when one is opened.

cards.title: Copy, resource, typestate, effect, sink and layout facts come from declarations, not Core names
cards.body:
Destination: the checker reads copy, resource, typestate, effect and sink facts, and IR reads runtime-handle layout, from the declaration of a type or function. No compiler file keeps a list of Core type or module names to decide them.

Why it matters: a package type declared the same way as a Core type must get the same facts, and every name list drifts from Core (census F1 found Core/Jobs/Jobs.jet `queue() -[DB, Env, FS, Time]>` reduced to Effect.DB).

Sources: findings F06, F11 and F12 of Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md (line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f); D-CORE-LOWER1=A (lowering). Split from #6151.

Starting point for the taint criteria: an unlanded, unreviewed rework saved from lane TlsLead-3-6151 (on 73739ba7c3) at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/tls-unlanded/TlsLead-3-6151.patch (35 files: Sema/Taint.jet, ProveReplay.jet, CoreSourceRows.jet; deletes JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Sinks.jet).

Ballots: the declaration-facts criteria and the layout criterion are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

log.text: c7/c10 spellings needed (DeclTypes): (1) RouteBuiltin String/Bytes/List/iter rows need a way for Core to declare methods on the built-in String, [T] and Bytes types; (2) RouteHandle event rows need Core declarations for the generic Event/Hook handle types plus host leaves that take closures; (3) c10 needs a declared host-leaf spelling for compile-time compiler services (only #Import(c) exists) so Build/BuildPlan methods bind by declared symbol. The c7 precise-math slice is being submitted. The FileReader/FileWriter intercept removal is feasible, moves no baseline row, and is kept as a pending c7 slice.

c8 waits on ballots: format selectors and decode are ballot-gated by c8's own text, and the line loop needs a fallible-iteration trait (Iterator.next is Never!) that no decision gives. The precise-math part can land as a slice once those ballots are decided; alone it cannot empty CoreReach.jet. DeclTypes moved to c7.

c5 slice 1 (BuildTypes prefix tests via module_is_core, Pin matched by declaration, 14 -> 6 corelib sites) is in p253. Slice 2 waits on the runtime-handle-layout ballot already on c5 (Main's ballot list): Core handle types (HTTPRequest, Point2, TaskStatus) are plain structs/enums found only through IR_RUNTIME_HANDLES keyed by Core identity, so a package type needs a declared 'carried by runtime handle X' spelling. The key-row cutover patch is parked unlanded at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes-6-1/c5slice2/patch.

c11 design decided (Main): source-owned Core calls carry no effect set of their own; sema and jet inspect read the effects from the Core declaration, which is already the checked row (E0740 names them). This is one mechanism, so nothing can drift, and the build does not embed and scan the 5.4 MB of Core sources. Adapter rows (no Jet declaration yet) replace effect_kind/effect_leaf with an effects set from the hand list until c7 gives them host-leaf declarations; at that point the hand list is deleted. The c11 proof shows jobs.queue's full effect set through jet inspect and E0740.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c1, c2, c5, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

cards.title: Open vocabularies: the compiler reads Core members as trait impls, never by name (D-EXTEND-ARCH1)
cards.body:
Destination: every compiler list that holds a Core member becomes a Core trait that any package implements with `impl Member.Trait` and trait constants (for example `impl TOML.Format { name: "TOML" }`). Core impls are pre-generated (D-OPENTABLE1); package impls are read once per build, only when imported. No compiler file recognizes a Core member by name.

Why it matters: a third-party database head, file format, unit or protocol must get the same powers as Core's without a compiler release.

Decision: D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A. Design: Docs/research/2026-10-29-extensibility-every-layer.md sections 6.1-6.3 (rules, the per-layer table, the checked-text worked example) and section 8 (the closed-list guard, landed as tests/guards/closed_lists.jet in 912fae1170). Each vocabulary that moves shrinks tests/guards/closed_lists/baseline.tsv.

Done so far: Core's SQL, HTML, Sh, URL, DateTime and Path are CheckedText impls and TypedHeadKind is gone (549b47e704); CheckedText keeps holes as typed values with Hole and build (9afa7da76b, D-TEXTHEAD-HOLES1).

Ballot: growing public enums (a marker requiring an `else` arm) are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Split from #6202 (the research card).

log.text: c9 parked unlanded by owner priority (#6733/#6734 first): network handle types declared in Core with impl blocks; patch at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes-6-1/c9park/patch (base 6c4b88d8f1, applies), notes in c9park/STATUS. Needs its runtime leaves in a seed before the Core caller (two-cycle split).

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c7, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

String format selectors get their meaning from a trait: StrFormat (AST/Expressions.jet) and its TStrFormat mirror are gone, and a package selector formats a hole with no compiler change. Proof: `git grep -n 'StrFormat' Compiler` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Packages/FormatSelector` passes.

Byte and budget suffixes are Core unit families: one `#UnitFamily` declaration per suffix family replaces the lexer and budget suffix lists, and a package family (for example `hop`) works the same way. Proof: the suffix lists leave Tests/Guards/closed_lists/baseline.tsv and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Units` passes.

Core protocol traits are declared in the Prelude and the compiler's table is generated from them (OWNED_TRAITS via Tools/Agent/OwnedTraitRows.jet): no compiler file spells a protocol trait name outside the generated table. criteria.text: Growing public enums: adding a member to an enum carrying the growth marker breaks no caller, because a match on it from outside its package needs an `else` arm. The growth marker is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Library types take on language meaning (what `+` calls, what indexing calls) through declared roles (D-CORE-ROLE1=A, PascalCase markers), never by compiler name lookup. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter core_role_operator_dispatch`. The frozen #4570 holds the original item.

The network handle types (TCPListener, TCPStream, UDPSocket, UnixListener, UnixStream, WsConn, WsMessage) are declared in Core with their methods (impl blocks in Core/Net and Core/Web/Ws), and the compiler's handle-op row table (from #3147 c8) shrinks to the runtime leaves those bodies call. cards.title: Taint kinds, effect roots, devices and schedulers come from declared rows and providers
cards.body:
Destination: policy, taint, accelerator devices and schedulers read declared rows and providers, so a package adds a taint kind, an effect root, a device or a scheduler with no compiler or policy-code edit.

Why it matters: these four vocabularies are closed lists in the compiler today (TaintKind in Core/Compiler/Lang.jet with three copies of the taint tags; the policy key and gate lists in Policy/; the device names in Registry/CoreValueSignatures.jet; the scheduler choice). The four built-in tags themselves become Prelude structs on #6849 c6.

Decisions: D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A, D-HOST-CAPS1 (package hardware kinds), D-ACCEL-LIB1 (device interface), D-CORE-PROVIDER1 (provider traits). Design: Docs/research/2026-10-29-extensibility-every-layer.md sections 4.9, 4.28, 4.31 and 6.2.

Split from #6202.

log.text: All five criteria met; c4 closed by the p251 batch compiler: a package-declared target profile selects its Scheduler provider through link-time run-queue hooks (no per-spawn cost), cases target_selects_package_scheduler and program_run_queue_hooks_take_every_spawn PASS.

c4 plan (Main): no new card (owner order: gaps are criteria on the owning card). IfHole builds c4 as SUBs of an hour or less, in order: (1) a package-declared target profile that resolves TargetProfileIdentity.Named, the minimal slice of #758 c11 that c4 needs; (2) a Scheduler provider trait in Core; (3) binding the runtime's jet_rt_native_task_spawn/park/wake to the selected provider at link time, with no per-call cost; (4) the target_selects_package_scheduler case checking the spawn IR is unchanged.

cards.title: Packages extend the editor, formatter, debugger and law tests through declared hooks
cards.body:
Destination: a package that adds a block marker, a container type or an open trait also teaches the tools about it through declared hooks: editor stages, a formatter stage for block bodies, a Core DebugView trait and law tests that `jet test` runs.

Why it matters: without hooks, every package feature needs a change to the LSP, the formatter or the debugger.

Decisions: D-HOOK-STAGES1=A (the compiler and tool moments packages may hook), D-HOOK-ONE1 (an unattached hook emits nothing), D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A rule 3 (laws travel with the interface), D-CORE-LAWS1. Design: Docs/research/2026-10-29-extensibility-every-layer.md sections 4.17-4.20 and 6.2.

Split from #6202.

cards.title: Build tools, package sources and JetOS options are package providers
cards.body:
Destination: a foreign build tool, a package registry or service preset, and a JetOS module option are each one package implementing a provider trait or declaring rows, not an edit to the build session, Jetpack or JetOS.

Why it matters: today Session.jet:664 names cmake, make, gradle, npm and cargo; Jetpack's ServicePresetKind has 43 presets and its provider list sits in four places that disagree (#6217); JetOS options render from a closed table (OptionsRendering.jet:117).

Decisions: D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A, D-CORE-PROVIDER1, D-INFRA1. Design: Docs/research/2026-10-29-extensibility-every-layer.md sections 4.24, 4.25, 4.29 and 6.2 (`b.toolchain`, `b.action`, a Jetpack provider trait). Frozen cards #470 (JetOS option merge law) and #323 (JetOS option schema) cover nearby ground and are not touched.

Split from #6202.

criteria.text: A Meson provider package implements `b.toolchain` and builds a Meson project from `fn build` with no build-session change; Session.jet names no foreign build tool.

Jetpack reads package sources and service presets through one provider trait: a new registry or preset is one package, and the four provider lists (RefSpec.jet, ProviderFamily.jet, Syntax.jet, ProviderFacts.jet) become one declared home.
JetOS module options are package declarations with a stated merge law: two packages set one option and the result follows the law.
Provider leaves are written in Jet source using the ratified F4/F5 facilities.

Each supported ProviderKind uses one adapter module for trust checks, cache expectations, download planning, approval facts and realization, with one source classification and one adapter lookup. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Provider/adapter_single_home` and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter provider_adapter_lookup_single`.

Core, Nix, CRAN, LuaRocks and script-registry providers keep their cache identity, offline rules, authority checks, progress facts, error codes and unsupported-provider error, proven by planning and realization through Core, Nix and one script-registry adapter, including trusted cache reuse and offline refusal. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackEngine/typed_env_build_hook_approval_binds_declared_dependency_refs` and `--filter jetpack_acquisition/non_tty_download_without_yes_fails_before_realization`.
Provider, network, shell and realization work stays inside Jetpack, with no new dependency or compiler back-edge.

cards.title: Language-review cutovers: arrow-first signatures, brace records, brace layout and one program entry form
cards.body:
Destination: the owner's 2026-11-09/11 language-review rulings are the only spellings in the repository. Signatures put the arrow first (D-SIG-ARROW1), records use braces and paren tuples retire (D-RECORD-BRACE1), commas separate data members but not bodied methods (D-BRACE-LAYOUT1), and a program is either script style or one `run: fn` entry, never mixed (owner order 2026-11-11).

cards.title: Jet has no warnings: jet fmt rewrites style, tidy errors never stop run or dev (D-NO-WARNINGS1)
cards.body:
Destination: Jet prints no warnings. A style point `jet fmt` can rewrite is rewritten and never reported; everything else that matters is an error. Tidiness errors (an unused binding, an unused import, unreachable code) never stop `jet run` or `jet dev` and are not printed there; `jet check` and `jet build` list every one and exit non-zero, so the list works as a todo list.

Why it matters: the final-return and positional-Bool lints print thousands of lines when Jet's own runtime compiles, which hides real errors.

Decision: D-NO-WARNINGS1=A (ratified 2026-11-10). Related: #4624 (member liveness findings follow the same rule) and #6326 c4 (state-machine lints L0529, L0302, gated on that design).

Source: #6281 c129 (split here 2026-11-14).

log.text: p216 (efb3da4f6c): tidy_errors_run_vs_check, failure_arm_cannot_arrive and Guards pass, but c2 is held. Builds now fail on tidy errors, which broke golden Examples/Apps/UI/Surface.jet and Tests/Run/Net/ConsumingMethodDropsSelf.jet on o1/o2 (UnusedLocalBinding) and about 8 cases. Sent to IfHole-6-1.

p208 landed the tidy error tier (MemKernel-6-tidy-errors-c2-r3 bc60c2fa1d, c24-l0304-tidy-r3 bac11a8e4a); the p208 suites lost 773 rows (553 ui snapshots print tidy findings beside the real error, 163 cases and 53 run rows meet unswept tidy sites in tests/ and Examples, 242 golden lines), and L0101 has two false positives (a read inside an already-refused expression; a binding kept alive for its drop). Main reverted both on dev. The r4 stack fixes both false positives, sweeps every tree the rule reaches to 0 hits, and keeps check output stable or regenerates every snapshot in the same SUB.

p207 (dev 0e93e25032): MemKernel-6-2's assembled-unit-imports a3436a9533 (CoreImports.jet removed; each assembled Jetpack file imports what it uses), unit-tidy-sites 401a2b9016 and tidy-cleanup-2 8d40093b4c landed. The c2 tier (tidy-errors-c2-r3) and c24 (L0304 tidy) are stacked in p208; c2's closing proof is the nested tidy census on p208's compiler showing 0 hits. golden Tooling/StructureLiveness passes on O0/O1/O2; ui lint shows only its 3 known-failing rows.

criteria.text: The final-return and positional-Bool style points are `jet fmt` rewrites, not reports: compiling Jet's own runtime prints neither.
A tidiness error (unused binding, unused import, unreachable code) never stops `jet run` or `jet dev` and is not printed there; `jet check` and `jet build` list every one and exit non-zero.
criteria.evidence: p218 batch compiler (census build of dev 7300cf5099): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter tidy_errors_run_vs_check PASS. The p216 o1/o2 UnusedLocalBinding regressions are fixed: golden profile 5008 pass, 0 fail

criteria.text: No L code remains active: each is a `jet fmt` rewrite or a registered tidy error with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot. Proof: no active row in Compiler/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet has an `L` code, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter diagnostics_coverage` passes.
The whole repository is clean under `jet check`. Proof: `jet check` over Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools and Examples exits 0.

A marker application counts as a use of its import, so it raises no false unused-import error, while a genuinely unused import is still reported as the registered tidy error (listed by jet check, never stopping jet run). An unknown or qualified marker gives one E0927 per site whose Why and Fix match D-META-USER1 and name the declaring import. A parse error in an imported file renders with that file's path, line and text. Proof: UI snapshots for all three under `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter marker_import`. (was #3720 c50)

A namespace needed by a used dotted, grouped or forward-alias member import is never reported unused, and no safe fix removes it, while a genuinely unused namespace still gets the unused-import tidy error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter unused_import_`. (was #3720 c51)

cards.title: Module variables belong to the main task; a task that touches one is refused (D-MODULE-VAR1)
cards.body:
Destination: a plain module variable is owned by the main task. Each function type carries its touch set (the module variables it reads or writes) as a deny-only fact; a task spawn requires an empty touch set; functions may write module variables (the E0111 function-write ban goes); borrow exclusivity holds across calls that touch the same variable.

Why it matters: module state is easy for beginners and stays race-free without locks or annotations.

Decision: D-MODULE-VAR1=A (ratified 2026-11-10). Each refusal is a registered error with what/why/fix and a UI snapshot; the example runs the same at O0, O1 and O2.

Source: #6281 c158 (split here 2026-11-14).

criteria.text: A function type carries its touch set (the module variables it reads or writes, transitively) as a deny-only fact, and `jet inspect` shows it.
A task spawn whose function touches a module variable is refused with a registered error naming the variable and the touching call.
A function may write a module variable: the E0111 function-write ban is removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/ModuleVariables` passes on o0, o1 and o2.
Borrow exclusivity holds across calls: a call that writes a module variable while a borrow of it is live is refused.

cards.title: Library promise changes show in jet check, and publish computes the minimum version (D-API-SURFACE1)
cards.body:
Destination: a package records its public promises (signatures and effects) in package.api. `jet check` reports a changed promise and tells the author to accept it; `jet registry publish` computes the minimum semantic version from the promise diff, and the author may raise it but never lower it.

Why it matters: users can trust a minor release, and a new required effect on a released function is never shipped as a patch.

Decision: D-API-SURFACE1=A (ratified 2026-11-11). Related: #5459 (capability diff on dependency update).

Source: #6281 c179 (split here 2026-11-14).

criteria.text: `jet check` compares a package's public promises with its recorded package.api and reports a changed promise with a registered diagnostic (what, why, fix) that tells the author to accept it.
`jet check --accept-api` rewrites package.api to the current promises.

`jet registry publish` computes the minimum version from the promise diff: an unchanged API is a patch, an added function a minor, and a released function newly needing Time a major; an author raise is kept and a lower version is refused. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter publish_minimum_semver` covers the four cases.

package.api records each public function's failure set: infallible to fallible, or a new member in a closed set, is a major change that `jet registry publish` refuses below a major version without acknowledgment (D-FAIL-PUBSIG1=A).

`jet registry publish` has a Jet public-API producer (PublicAPIItem from the checked package, structs included): `#CLI struct Config { port: Int{3000}; required: Int }` freezes as `struct Config { port: Int; required: Int [positional 0] }`, so a typed default is not frozen as positional.

Every deleted pkg.rs public-API test has a Jet Publication #Test over the public-API producer: v2_snapshot_upgrade_matches_duplicate_inline_leaves, public_effect_metadata_preserves_symbolic_rows, public_trait_effect_contract_drift_is_breaking, soft_public_names_are_not_semver_promises and inferred_public_effect_drift_is_breaking.

Physical-unit APIs freeze with canonical dimensions: physical_unit_api_freeze_and_semver_share_one_canonical_signature and physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions pass as Publication #Tests.

cards.title: TLS host reads are effects: clock, entropy and CA bundle reads show in the effect row and obey denials (D-NET-HOSTREADS1)
cards.body:
Destination: every host read TLS makes (wall clock, OS entropy, CA bundle files and directories, and the other ingress leaves the review lists) is an ordinary inferred effect on the TLS and HTTP calls that reach it. A denial of FS, Rand, Env or one CA file refuses the program with the registered effect diagnostic, and a denied override never falls back to another bundle.

Why it matters: an effect row that hides host reads is a false promise; a sandboxed HTTPS client must be able to deny entropy or its CA file and know it holds.

Decision: D-NET-HOSTREADS1=A (ratified 2026-11-12), with its adversarial review (sol-reviewer, 2026-11-11). Probes: the seed-b5 probes (a local HTTPS client denying FS, Rand and Env; a scoped denial of its CA file; a server denying Rand).

Source: #6615 c12, c14, c15 (split here 2026-11-15). Related: #3418 (one effect-policy model).

criteria.text: Each TLS host-ingress leaf (wall clock, OS entropy, CA bundle files and directories, and the rest the review lists) is an inferred effect on every TLS and HTTP call that reaches it, carried through TLS and HTTP errors, callbacks and tasks, with the caller, registry and docs cutover in one change (D-NET-HOSTREADS1=A).

A local HTTPS client denying FS, Rand and Env, a scoped denial of its CA file, and a server denying Rand are each refused with the registered effect diagnostic, and a denied CA override never falls back to another bundle. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter tls_host_reads` (the seed-b5 probes as cases).
A dependency's TLS use under a dependency sandbox that denies one of its host reads is refused at the dependency boundary (sandbox intersection).

On a target with no clock, no entropy source or no filesystem, a TLS call that needs it is refused at check time with a registered error, and the host-read cases pass on O0, O1, O2 and web where applicable.

An embedded or file-free CA configuration never removes the conservative effects by itself: file-free sandboxed TLS uses separate precise entry paths or a complete provider API with a lifetime design.

cards.title: Typed data loaders: deterministic snapshots, exact invalidation, no leaked credentials
cards.body:
Destination: a typed data loader (`file<T>(path, format, limits)` and the archive, parameter and provider forms) yields one canonical snapshot with provenance and schema identity, is invalidated by exactly its inputs, and never exposes credential-sensitive metadata.

Why it matters: notebooks, apps and data scripts all read data through loaders; a loader that caches wrongly or leaks a credential into public state breaks every one of them.
