Decisions: D-DATA-READER1=A (Arrow reader behind the format boundary), D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1. Spec: Docs/spec/core-library.md (data loaders). Related: #5968 (dataframes), #6619 (notebook).

Source: #5985 c9-c12 (archived #2448 c1-c4, re-added by the 2026-11 precut audit as unproven).

criteria.text: Loading the same input twice gives the same canonical snapshot content, provenance and schema identity, and the result is marshalled into the declared type T, on O0, O1 and O2.
A change to the loader's input file, archive member, parameter or authority invalidates its cached result, and a change to anything else does not.
Credential-sensitive loader metadata never appears in public loader state or output, and a provider payload the loader's authority does not cover is refused with a registered error.
Loader preview, status and cleanup read and remove only the state of their own invocation; an app or notebook using a loader goes through the same loader, not a second copy.

cards.title: jet new adds services, routes, jobs and migrations to an app, with preview and undo
cards.body:
Destination: inside an app package, `jet new` generates a service, a route, a job or a migration from explicit inputs, shows a preview first, and can undo what it generated from its receipt. Generated code uses the ratified app APIs (D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A: #App.Job, app.enqueue) and the migration CLI (D-DX-MIGRATE1=A), and compiles as written.

Why it matters: generators are how most people start a backend feature; generated code that does not compile or cannot be undone teaches the wrong shape.

Source: #5985 c16-c19 (archived #2458 c1-c4, re-added by the 2026-11 precut audit as unproven). Related: #6825 (jobs), #6552 (web framework).

log.text: All 3 criteria met on p230/p232 (dev 823706b2d9).

criteria.text: `jet new service|route|job|migration <name>` in an app package writes the generated files from explicit inputs, and `--preview` prints the exact files and contents without writing.
criteria.evidence: p230 batch compiler (dev 47086f2eb3), commit 1579aacf8c: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_new_app_generators PASS 1/1; Compiler/JetCLI/Tests/CommandModel.jet PASS; CLIPartsRuntime/help_all PASS.

criteria.text: Every generated service, route, job and migration compiles unchanged and uses the ratified app APIs (#App.Job, app.enqueue, the migration form of D-DX-MIGRATE1=A), with deterministic file and declaration names.
criteria.evidence: p230 batch compiler (dev 47086f2eb3), commits 1579aacf8c (page files under a .routes(from:) folder keep page file-private) + 7902872cd8 + f14557e1e4: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_new_app_generated_code_compiles PASS 1/1, generating a service, a job, a migration and 1, 2 and 3 routes into one app package and checking the app and each file after each.

criteria.text: Undo removes exactly the files its receipt lists, refuses when one was edited since (integrity check), and a regenerated migration reuses its version number.
criteria.evidence: p232 batch compiler (dev 823706b2d9), commits 2912e85f8e + d1dc9b6b36: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_new_app_generator_undo PASS 1/1.

cards.title: Typed routes: checked paths and search params, loader boundaries and route data freshness
cards.body:
Destination: a route declares typed path and search parameters, a loader and its navigation contract; a wrong route or parameter is a compile error; a loader's pending, error and not-found states render; and route data stays fresh by the compiler's read sets.

Why it matters: routing and data loading are the spine of every web app; untyped routes are the most common source of broken links and stale pages.

Decisions: D-ROUTE-ONE1=A (one route table on web.app()), D-ROUTE-FILES2=A (page file words become the address), D-INVALIDATE1=A (the compiler decides what a write makes stale), D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A.

Source: #6552 c8, c10, c11, c12 (from archived #2472). Parent: #6552.

log.text: All 5 criteria met; the last, c4 (capability boundary E2823/E2824), passed on p229 (dev 8c9859caba).

c2 SUB Speed-3-3-6864-c2-app-navigation (queued p226) builds client navigation on web.app()'s one route table: App gains navigate, settle, abort, navigating and shown; core.web.router gets no second public API (D-ROUTE-ONE1=A).

c2 design (Main): route loader boundaries go on web.app()'s one route table (D-ROUTE-ONE1=A: only page rows join client navigation), on the screen routes c1 defines; a loader/settle/show API on core.web.router would be a second route mechanism (I8). Speed-3-3's router-level SUB was returned for that reason.

criteria.text: A screen's route is its state struct (typed `:field` path parameters and `#App.Query` search parameters), its view is the loader, and url_of, go and current are its navigation; a link or navigation to an unknown route or with a wrong parameter type is a compile error with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: p223 batch compiler (dev a8b53c68d8): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter web_route_ PASS 4/4 (2ee79b3cf2)

criteria.text: A route loader's pending, error and not-found boundaries render, and an aborted navigation cancels its preload, on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072), commit 5e327e8133: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/RouteLoaderBoundaries PASS 6/6 (Native o0/o1/o2 and Web); navigation lives on web.app()'s one route table.

criteria.text: Route data is keyed by its route and arguments, turns stale when a write meets its read set (D-INVALIDATE1=A), refetches, and is dropped after its last screen leaves.
criteria.evidence: p225 batch compiler (dev 1b2c2d0a54), commit e05ccf100e: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/route_data_lifecycle PASS 1/1 (O0, O1, O2 and web in the case).

criteria.text: Browser code that uses a server-only capability, or server code that uses a browser-only one, is refused at the app boundary with a registered diagnostic, one UI snapshot per rejection kind.
criteria.evidence: p229 batch compiler (dev 8c9859caba), commits 46a7723059 + e3a2ca03a5: jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter web_capability_boundary_ PASS 2/2 (E2823 browser_reaches_database, E2824 server_uses_browser); the check reads each body's own uses over call edges, so cases WebApp/enqueue_takes_one_job_call and WebApp/live_takes_one_remote_call PASS (no false positive); Tests/Guards/diagnostic_registry_ratchet.jet PASS (p227); full suite p229 has no new failures from it.

criteria.text: Conflicting routes give a deterministic two-span error (E2804); Mux, router and App pick the same handler; HEAD and typed path failures are recorded. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_route_ambiguous_overlap` and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter net/route_overlap`.
criteria.evidence: dev 0b58edf739, gate-p176 jet: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/RouteOverlap gives 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2). The golden tests/run/Net/RouteOverlap.jet records HEAD running the GET handler, a typed path mismatch as 400, and 405 with its Allow list; Router, App routes and marked mounts share one HTTPMux and pick the same handler. jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_route_ambiguous_overlap gives 1 PASS (E2804, two spans). The card's original golden filter net/route_overlap named no row; the golden's path is tests/run/Net/RouteOverlap.jet.

cards.title: Endpoints: one checked contract drives dispatch, the typed client, schema, form and OpenAPI
cards.body:
Destination: an endpoint is declared once (a marked method or route) and its contract derives dispatch, the typed client, the JSON schema, the form and the OpenAPI document; all of them agree with an independent HTTP client.

Why it matters: hand-kept clients and schemas drift from the server; one derived contract removes that whole class of bug.

Decisions: D-ENDPOINT-SHAPE1=A (contracts derived from typed handlers), D-ROUTE-ONE1=A, D-HTTP-ROUTE-EXPOSE1=A (route markers on struct methods, added with one call), D-FOUND-COREAPI1, D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A.

Source: #6552 c20, c28, c29, c34 (from archived #2962, #3304, #2852). Parent: #6552.

criteria.text: A typed endpoint is admitted, lowered to one descriptor, invoked, and encoded through the native and web codecs, with goldens on O0, O1, O2 and web.

Renaming a public input changes the derived client, schema and form in one place, and an independent client (curl) sees the same typed errors, auth requirements and HTTP statuses as the typed client. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter endpoint_contract_replay` on O0, O1 and O2.

Malformed path, query or body input is refused before the handler, private result fields never cross the public boundary, and optional, nested, enum, list and recursive schema references appear only where the endpoint declares them.

web.openapi(app) derives one deterministic OpenAPI document from the route table (D-ROUTE-ONE1=A): stable operation IDs, typed input, success, failure, auth and status, and no internal or visual routes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/AppOpenapi` on O0, O1 and O2.

Route markers on struct methods are added to the app with one call (D-HTTP-ROUTE-EXPOSE1=A): a jokes API with GET and POST routes serves identically on O0, O1 and O2, `web.openapi` renders both routes, and a bad path parameter is a compile error with a UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: p150 (dev cb824d0276; JokesAPI landed 0fec89bfa1, renamed a147a156e6): jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/JokesAPI: PASS 3 FAIL 0. The criterion's filter Web/JokesApi predates the rename and matches nothing; the example's name is JokesAPI.

criteria.text: An action's security policy runs before any mutation: malformed, oversized, CSRF, unauthenticated and forbidden requests never mutate, authenticated-but-forbidden differs from unauthenticated, the duplicate JSON member policy is explicit, and no secret appears in a response. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/WebApp` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/action_security_policy_runs_before_mutation`.

A request body read under ?? (request.json<T>() ?? return ...) stays in the route contract and web.openapi. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter openapi_request_body_survives_a_decode_fallback.
criteria.evidence: p149 (batch compiler from dev 413cddeab5, 2026-11-15 00:20; GoalsB-5-15 landed c979f70f49): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter openapi_: PASS 3 FAIL 0, including openapi_request_body_survives_a_decode_fallback; --filter auto_derived_http_inputs: PASS 1 FAIL 0.

criteria.text: A failed route, context or operation check names its source construct and causal dependency, and the machine facts match the human error, with no new graph store or debug endpoint. Emit, check and repair fidelity is measured. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/WebApp` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter route_check_names_cause`. (was #3186 c9)

`json.schema<T>()` emits JSON Schema draft 2020-12 from Codable metadata (required, optional and default fields, renames, variants, recursion), represents custom codecs honestly, and its dialect is explicit and reused at app boundaries. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONSchema`. (was #3236 c13)

Published-schema add, remove, change and rename migrations work with examples, and computed-text typed JSON dispatch is integrated. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/SchemaMigration` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c29)

A method call on a Remote held in a field (client.notes.publish(doc)) checks exactly as the same call on a plain variable (notes.publish(doc)); today the seed refuses the field form with a misleading E0204 'already shared in this call'. Proof: a cases entry calling one Remote both ways, passing on O0, O1, O2 and web, plus the E0204 UI snapshot unchanged for a real double share.

cards.title: Browser tests in jet test: scaffold, UI mode, retry traces and cross-browser runs
cards.body:
Destination: `jet test` drives real browsers for an app: a scaffold sets up the browser test project, a UI mode shows one run in full, a retry records a trace you can open locally, and runs across browsers are deterministic and keep Jet's diagnostics and source positions.

Why it matters: end-to-end browser tests are where web apps break; parity with the best browser test runner (Playwright) is part of the web framework's parity bar.

Source: #6552 c15-c18 (from archived #2498 c2-c5). Parent: #6552.

log.text: All 5 criteria met on p234/p235 (dev 1c5b311279).

criteria.text: The browser test scaffold creates an isolated browser test project with its configured browsers and a reusable `jet dev` web server, then runs a first passing test.
criteria.evidence: p234 batch compiler (dev 77460a182a), commits bf95abc3de + 31080f2e3d (case fix): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter browser_test_scaffold PASS in the p234 full cases suite and alone (with JETPACK_BIN set, as the suite runs it).

criteria.text: UI mode shows the test tree, filters, timeline, DOM snapshots, source, logs, errors, console, network, attachments and watch updates from one test run.
criteria.evidence: p235 batch compiler (dev 1c5b311279), commit 1c5b311279: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter browser_test_ui_mode PASS 1/1.

criteria.text: A retried test records a bounded trace that opens in the local viewer with action snapshots, source, DOM, logs and network details, and page payloads are left out unless asked for.
criteria.evidence: p235 batch compiler (dev 1c5b311279), commit 1c5b311279: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter browser_test_retry_trace PASS 1/1.

criteria.text: Runs across browsers are deterministic in contexts, retries, reporters and failure exit status, and failures keep Jet's diagnostic and source positions.
criteria.evidence: p235 batch compiler (dev 1c5b311279), commits 22b864b785 + 13f7b77421: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter browser_test_cross_browser PASS 1/1 on Chromium 152 and Firefox 155.

criteria.text: page.storage_get works on Firefox the same as on Chromium; today it fails with 'browser protocol failed' on Firefox 155. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter browser_test_cross_browser reads storage on both browsers.
criteria.evidence: p235 batch compiler (dev 1c5b311279), commit 13f7b77421 (the Firefox profile directory lives as long as the engine): browser_test_cross_browser reads storage on both browsers, PASS 1/1.

cards.title: Offline write queue: request keys, row versions, shared tabs, session expiry and refused-write notices
cards.body:
Destination: an app's writes made offline are queued, replayed exactly once, never conflict with the device's own earlier edits, survive tabs and session expiry, and a refused write is never lost silently.

Why it matters: local-first apps (Linear, Convex) win on writes that just work offline; a queue that double-applies, conflicts with itself or drops a refusal loses user data.

Decisions: D-SYNC2=A (typed local collections that work offline and sync), D-SYNC1=A (CRDT values), D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (shape: Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md). Gaps K1 come from the #6792 review round 2.

Source: #3709 c6, c11, c14-c17, c23, c26. Parent: #3709.

log.text: p222 (dev 961427a575): c10's native leg landed; WebApp/device_store_keeps_queue_and_notices_across_restart PASS on O0/O1/O2. c10 stays open for the web leg (waits on #6445 c9 and #6866).

c10 split (Main): the native leg ships now (B1: data_dir on Linux/macOS/Windows; B3: jet_rt_device_load/replace, temp+fsync+rename under data_dir()/<package>/; the entry package name is an image fact the runtime exposes, not a sema rewrite of one call). c10 stays open for the web leg, which needs #6445 c9 (the web Remote network leg) and a jet test browser harness with IndexedDB across a reload (#6866). B2 dropped: #package.name already gives the entry name at compile time, and server: meets no criterion here.

Plan (Main, from DeclTypes): SUB A = server: field (JET_APP_SERVER under jet run), the Unit-write queue with drop-plus-notice rollback, app.pending(), drain on reconnect and before the next call, c1 case sync_two_clients on o0/O1/O2; queue and notices in process cells. B1 = Core/Sys data_dir made correct on Linux/macOS/Windows through one runtime symbol, which the device cell reuses (no second helper). B2 = the driver embeds the entry package name and server: as a compile-time fact of the image. B3 = jet.runtime.device load/replace (atomic; a truncated file loads empty) under both cells, plus the c7 restart case.

Decision (Main): the device store is a runtime-owned cell (jet.runtime.device load/replace), effect-free in Core like the World store and NOTICE_CELL, so remote calls keep -[Net, Time]>. core.db is unusable here (it imports app) and a core.files store would add FS and Env to every remote write. Native is keyed by package name under the platform data dir, written through atomically. Web IndexedDB persistence is a criterion on this card.

Decision (Main, within approved scope): the offline write queue is built to the approved contract for writes whose result is Unit; each such write is queued and returns () at once. c1 rollback of a Unit write drops it and posts the notice; c7 rebases queued Unit writes. Value-returning writes keep the current offline behaviour (.Unreachable, as on the web) until #6555 c2 (prediction, gated on D-PREDICT-JOB1 and D-PREDICT-PIN1) lands; they get no separate path. c1, c3 and c7 proofs use Unit-result writes; queueing of value-returning writes is completed under #6555 c2.

c1, c3 and c7 need the client graph (new #6445 criterion: app.new/.api/.screen/.offline), app.Notice with its list (#6445 c7) and prediction (D-OPTIMISTIC1, #6555 c1 review then c2/c7). DeclTypes-6-1 builds them in that order. No stopgap web.App.offline: it would be a second, unratified mechanism (I8).

Rulings (Main, 2026-11-16 06:00). The offline queue surface is the proposal's .offline(.Queue) on the client graph; no app.offline_queue(path) free function (a second spelling, I8). c4-c7's client half waits on the graph and its card (Speed-3-2 to name it). c5 waits on #6818: the queue sends no session until #6818's native session design exists. Marking an ID type (Core app.ID with a bare UUIDv7 codec, or a marker on a distinct String) is new public API: an owner ballot that Main files, with neither spelling built meanwhile. Built now without a ruling: c6's server half (app.new_id() UUIDv7; Table.add answers Exists only when the caller may read the taken row, otherwise Denied). Queued for p215: c2 request keys (Speed-3-request-keys) and the server-side signed-in caller (Speed-3-signed-in-caller, a dependency of c5-c7).

State on dev 78f4541780 (Speed-3-2 survey): c9's grep matches Docs/research/2026-11-15-sync-partial-bootstrap-and-local-only.md, but the note is a fifth draft whose own status needs a fifth adversarial review before anything is built, and review 4, which it cites, is not in Docs/audits; c9 stays open. c1 and c3-c7 are blocked by no ballot but need unbuilt parts: the offline client queue (.offline(.Queue)); a signed-in caller over HTTP (#App.SignedIn endpoints answer 401 today); a browser runtime with IndexedDB and Web Locks; and the frame's notice list. c2 (request keys) is in progress (Speed-3-2).

criteria.text: Two clients: one edits offline, reconnects, the server refuses one of its writes and that client rolls it back, on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: p220 batch compiler (census build of dev 17c073989d): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter sync_two_clients PASS

criteria.text: Every queued or retried remote write carries a request key; the server keeps (account, key) -> result for 24 hours and answers a replay with the stored result. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/replayed_write_returns_stored_result` (the first response is dropped).
A second queued edit to one row carries the version the first edit predicts, so a device never conflicts with itself.
Browser tabs of one origin share one queue (IndexedDB plus a Web Lock), and the queue replays once.
When the session expires offline the queue is held, never sent under another account, and resumes after sign-in as the same account.

A client-made UUIDv7 ID lets an offline create open its row at once. An ID type's decoder accepts only UUIDv7 text (422 otherwise; a test sends "t1"). Table.add meeting a taken key answers DBError.Exists when the caller can read that row and Denied when it cannot, and the queue reports it.

A refused queued write whose screen is gone, or which is refused after a restart, adds a notice to the app notice list, kept until dismissed. Edits rebased on it replay with the row version each was made against, so one whose row changed since answers Conflict; each is judged on its own checks with its own notice.
criteria.evidence: p227 batch compiler (dev eab1677096), commit d87ae00329: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/refused_queued_write_without_a_screen_becomes_a_kept_notice PASS 1/1.

criteria.text: Network partitions, concurrent merges, duplicated or reordered operations and reconnects keep every replica convergent: a seeded property test of random schedules over two and three replicas ends with equal state.
criteria.evidence: Already holds on dev 78f4541780 (found by Speed-3-2, rerun by Main on the p213 batch compiler): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter sync_crdt/partitions_converge -> PASS tests/cases/sync_crdt/partitions_converge.case, 1 passed, 0 failed.

criteria.text: The sync design covers partial bootstrap for large workspaces and a local-only mode with sync switched off (the parts Docs/Proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md does not cover; it already covers the client cache, rollback, socket fan-out and the offline queue), as a reviewed design note. Proof: `git grep -n -i -E 'partial bootstrap|local-only' -- Docs/Proposals`. (was #3709 c1)

The device store that keeps queued writes and the notice list across restarts has one meaning on every tier: native writes through atomically to the platform data directory keyed by the app's package name, and the web target persists the same cell in IndexedDB through the same runtime load/replace symbols; a reload in the browser keeps the queue and notices exactly as a native restart does. Proof: a golden app case that queues a Unit write, restarts (native) or reloads (web), and prints the same queue and notice list on o0, O1, O2 and web.

cards.title: Live queries scale: shared results, per-server caps, cross-server invalidation and SQL-narrowed read sets
cards.body:
Destination: live queries (D-LIVEQUERY1=A, app.live) stay correct and cheap as subscribers and servers grow: results are shared when they can be, capped and coalesced when they burst, invalidated across servers, and narrowed to the rows they read.

Why it matters: a live query that re-runs for every subscriber on every write does not survive real traffic; one shared wrongly leaks data between callers.

Decisions: D-LIVEQUERY1=A, D-INVALIDATE1=A, D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A. Gaps K3 come from the #6792 review round 2.

Source: #3709 c13, c18-c21, c24, c25. Parent: #3709.

log.text: Every remaining criterion is met; c12 (warm coverage per screen) moved to #6981, the D-WARM-SET1 ballot it waited on.

c12 waits on the owner ballot D-WARM-SET1 (card #6981): how an app names the reads a device keeps warm. Recommendation A, a warm function in .offline(.Queue, warm: fn ...) checked at compile time against each offline screen's live reads.

c4: Speed-3-3 SUB c4-live-invalidation-across-servers (per-file version map plus a 1 s poll in core.db, two processes, no broker) is queued in p215. The Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-up remains: Core has no Postgres client and the test host has no Postgres, so that half waits on a Core Postgres client stream.
c12 waits on the warm-set ballot (sync note §5.1, ballot B1: proposed, not built, never filed). The orchestrator files it; Speed-3-3 moved to c4.

Blockers (GoalsB-5-2 audit, 2026-11-15): c6 waits on app.caller (#6445 c4, now being built by GoalsB-5-2 on the ambient task caller from #6869 c3); c4 needs a Postgres broker and Core has no Postgres client; c5 needs the SQL-filter Query of D-DB-TABLE1, which is not built; c7 needs app.presence, which does not exist.

Status (GoalsB-5-2, 2026-11-15). c3 submitted: a server-wide re-run cap of 1000 per second, with holds that tell watchers after_ms; 1024 bindings; writes between reads coalesce into one re-run. Design ruling (Main): coalescing between reads plus a cap hold replaces the proposal's fixed 50 ms window, because a fixed window adds up to 50 ms to every live update and changes existing event output. Blocked: c4 (Core has no Postgres client for LISTEN/NOTIFY); c6 and c7 (app.caller() and app.presence() arrive with the #App.SignedIn screens, as #3709 c27/c28 do; the row-policy half of c6 already works per user in db_policy); c5 waits for D-DB-TABLE1 typed table queries (#6822), which GoalsB-5-2 now builds.

Decision (Main, operational, within D-LIVEQUERY1): app.state was E1123 on wasm because Live.run is a rowless fn() -> T E!, so state's solved row was unbounded. Live.run and the bind/poll runs are bounded to -[DB.Read, Net, Time]>, which keeps D-LIVEQUERY1's named sources (DB reads, Net fetch, time polling) and lets web build; a live source with any other effect is refused with E0740, whose fix text names the accepted sources.

Parked 2026-11-15 01:55 by owner order (finish Precompiled Core, the speed plan and the memory kernel before goal work). GoalsB-5 moves to #6759. Landing: GoalsB-5-22r2 (c10) and -23r2 (c2), finished, in census181. Open and unworked until the three are done: c11's livelock bound landed as GoalsB-5-24 (in census180, proof on p155); the rest of the card.

c8 is not met yet, though db_scope_live_marks_writes_stale_only_after_commit passes on p152: the second sync review (2026-11-15) reads App.jet state (L404-416) then live_store (L566-584), which clears dirty unconditionally, so a re-run that read before a commit and stores after its invalidation keeps the old value as current. GoalsB-5 adds a per-binding generation counter and a case forcing that interleaving.

criteria.text: A live query over a tracked source updates from real deltas, a no-op write leaves the cached result untouched, a write publishes only after its transaction commits, and cancelling the subscription ends its re-runs, on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: 68be2c34f4 and 7141a40239: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_lifecycle passes (2 of 2) on batch compiler p182 (dev 9003020128).

criteria.text: A live query that reads no caller-dependent input shares one result among all subscribers with the same arguments.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-23r2 landed b0acab4afa (proof case: a live query that reads no caller-dependent input shares one result). on batch compiler p156 (dev aa5f5f1bba), 2026-11-15 02:03: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_shared_result PASS 1 (it failed on p155, which lacked 22r2).

criteria.text: Each server caps live subscriptions and re-runs per second and coalesces bursts of writes into one re-run. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_caps_and_coalescing` (a load case).
criteria.evidence: 96f6bd2767: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_caps_and_coalescing passes (1 of 1) on batch compiler p182 (dev 9003020128).

criteria.text: Invalidations reach subscribers on other servers: a write on one server invalidates the matching live reads on every other server that shares the store, on O0, debug and release.
criteria.evidence: p221 batch compiler (dev 88dc8f59b9): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/live_query_cross_server_invalidation PASS 1/1 (O0, debug, release); still passes in the p222 suite

criteria.text: Predicates the compiler can turn into SQL narrow the read set; any other predicate falls back to table-level invalidation, and `jet inspect` shows which.
criteria.evidence: p219 batch compiler (census build of dev 1123bf884d, Speed-3-3-p215-G-live-filter-comptime landed as 1f51921bea): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/live_query_read_set_narrowing PASS (it failed on p218; the comptime prefetch of a live: local now keeps its SQL filter)

criteria.text: A caller-dependent live query (one that reads app.caller() or runs under a row policy) is not shared between callers; the cost, one re-run per subscriber per write that meets the read set, is measured under the per-server caps.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p187 (dev 9860836a00), 2026-11-15: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/caller_dependent_live_query_is_not_shared 1/1 PASS (landed 7439dda142)

criteria.text: app.presence counts only accounts whose last read of that screen passed its policies: a refused reader is not counted.
criteria.evidence: p221 batch compiler (dev 88dc8f59b9): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/presence_counts_only_admitted_readers PASS 1/1

criteria.text: A write inside a database transaction marks the live bindings over its table stale at the commit or rollback, never at the statement. A binding re-run on another connection while the transaction is open keeps no pre-commit result as current after the commit, and a write outside a transaction marks them at once.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-19 landed 5fa1fd1c85 (marks at commit) and GoalsB-5-21 landed 2ded9a1ded (per-binding generation: a re-run an invalidation overtakes stays stale, review G36). on batch compiler p154 (dev 31ee594ec7), 2026-11-15 01:30: --profile cases --filter live_rerun_overtaken PASS 1; --filter db_scope_live PASS 3; --filter sync_crdt/ PASS 3; golden --filter AppLive PASS 3. The livelock bound is c11.

criteria.text: The WebSocket live hub sends an invalidation only to connections holding a subscription it affects, whose caller passed that source's policy. No event, live or replayed on join, carries another caller's encoded key, and a WebSocket route that reads no live query receives no live event. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_hub_events_reach_only_admitted_subscribers` (a two-account case plus an unrelated route).
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-20r2a landed fad05cd5f6 and GoalsB-5-20r2b landed 1e0820d052 (live events reach only connections watching that binding). on batch compiler p155 (dev 49836bd978), 2026-11-15 01:45: --profile cases --filter live_hub_events PASS 1; db_scope_live PASS 3; RuntimeGenerators --check exit 0.

criteria.text: A read-only parameter passed to app.live or app.invalidate is copied or borrowed by the lowering, not moved. Today (p153) the repro (a live source fn count(project: String), with bind and refresh taking project: String) reports E0120 ReadOnlyValueNotOwned at both call sites, and its fix names the compiler temporary __jet_live_N_0, a name the user never wrote. Proof: a case where jet check passes and jet run prints loaded 3; the case live_rerun_overtaken drops its project.copy() workaround.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-22r2 landed dcf8af1eb2 (app.live, subscribe, push and invalidate take a read-only parameter as an argument with no E0120; Live.jet back to 19 copies). on batch compiler p156 (dev aa5f5f1bba), 2026-11-15 02:03: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter live_calls_read_a_read_only_argument PASS 1; the copy ledger ceiling holds (guards 171/0).

criteria.text: Overtaken re-runs are bounded (sync review 3, G86): under sustained writes to a table a live binding reads, the generation rule (2ded9a1ded) does not re-run the source on every read forever. After a stated bound, the binding settles: it serves a value marked stale, or stores one as current with its generation. Proof: a case with a writer loop that invalidates continuously and a reader that reads N times, where the source runs a bounded number of times and the reader gets a value each time.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-24 landed 8630ccf4dd (from the second overtaken run in a row, a binding serves its stale result for a hold of max(run time, 100 ms), then re-runs). on batch compiler p155 (dev 49836bd978), 2026-11-15 01:45: --profile cases --filter live_binding_under_sustained_writes_settles PASS 1; live_rerun_overtaken PASS 1; golden AppLive PASS 3.

criteria.text: Test-host network abilities (sync review gap G64): the app test host can disconnect a client from the server and restore it mid-test, deterministically, so offline, catch-up and replay cases run without real network faults. Proof: a case that disconnects, writes on both sides, restores, and checks the merged state. (was #3709 c28)
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072), commits b9fbc7793e and 2fe268264c: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter disconnected_client_merges_after_reconnect PASS 1/1 (the app test host disconnects a client mid-test, both sides write, the client reconnects and the merged state is checked).

criteria.text: Closing a live connection ends that account's presence on the screens it held: the runtime hub hands a leave signal back to Core (ws_hub_leave), so app.presence never counts a closed session. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/presence_ends_when_the_connection_closes`, on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: p216 batch compiler (census build of dev efb3da4f6c): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/presence_ends_when_the_connection_closes PASS

cards.title: Row policies: a typed Table.guard judges every read and write, and no path bypasses it
cards.body:
Destination: a table's typed row policy (Table.guard(fn(db.Op, db.Who, db.Store) -> Bool)) is applied to every read and write from live queries, endpoints, jobs and webhooks, and no call path, malformed policy or unauthorized row gets around it.

Why it matters: row policies are the app's access control; one path that skips the guard leaks every row behind it.

Decisions: D-DBPOLICY1=A (typed row-level access policies), D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A. Example app: Crewboard in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

Source: #3709 c10-c12, c22. Parent: #3709.

log.text: Decision for c3 (Main, 2026-11-15): guarded tables judge an ambient, task-keyed caller in core.app, set by the request layer and by as_caller(who, fn); a live binding keeps the caller that created it. With no caller the policy sees Who.Anonymous (fail-closed), never System; System comes only from an explicit job or system run. No per-table acting(who) override, so the ambient caller is the one mechanism and no path can bypass it. c2 uses the same API. Owner: GoalsB-5-2.

criteria.text: Table.guard(fn(db.Op, db.Who, db.Store) -> Bool) judges a read on the stored row, an insert on the new row, a delete on the stored row and an update on both; the policy's reads see the transaction's earlier writes but not the write being judged, and a row the caller may not read is never returned.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p184 (dev 61b4ee98a7), 2026-11-15: cases --filter db/row_policy_judges_each_operation 1/1 PASS (landed e0ea647fe1)

criteria.text: Crewboard's policies hold: a Member's update of its own member row to Owner is refused; the creator rule admits an Owner member insert only for a project whose row names the caller as created_by and has no members, so create_project makes the caller its owner and nothing else can; an outsider's search and my_projects return nothing.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p185 (dev b6b255de57), 2026-11-15: cases --filter web_app/crewboard_row_policies 1/1 PASS (landed 054383bbe1)

criteria.text: The guard runs on every path that reads or writes a guarded table: live queries, endpoints, jobs and webhooks; a seeded test tries each path with an unauthorized caller and every attempt is refused.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p185 (dev b6b255de57), 2026-11-15: cases --filter db/row_policy_no_bypass 1/1 PASS (landed f1a25b1980)

criteria.text: A policy that does not type-check, or that reads a table it may not, is a compile error with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p184 (dev 61b4ee98a7), 2026-11-15: ui --filter row_policy_invalid_ 2/2 PASS (landed 66248e8f83)

cards.title: Lists edited in place: retain, drain, extract_if, splice and fixed-array init
cards.body:
Destination: Core List edits in place with exact ownership: retain keeps only some items without a new list, drain, extract_if and splice own their ranges even when dropped early, a live drain excludes other access, and fixed arrays initialize slot by slot.

Why it matters: ports of Vec::retain, drain and splice otherwise allocate a second list or do quadratic removes, and an early-dropped drain that leaves the list half-edited is a silent data bug.

Decisions: D-LIST-RETAIN1=A, D-ARRAY-INIT1=A. Spec: Docs/spec/core-library.md (List). The frozen #4412 holds the original retain and dedup items.

Source: #5976 c1, c83-c88 (archived #3371).

criteria.text: `[T#N].filled(value)` and `[T#N].from_fn(make)` write slots directly (D-ARRAY-INIT1=A): `filled` with a value that is not Copy is refused with a registered error, and a `make` that fails part-way cleans up exactly the slots already written, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ArrayInit` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter array_filled_refuses_non_copy`.

`List.retain(keep)` removes in place, keeps order and allocates no new list (D-LIST-RETAIN1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ListRetain` and its allocation count in the measurement manifest.

`drain(range)` owns its removal range: `drain(1..<3)` on [1,2,3,4] yields [2,3] and leaves [1,4] even when dropped after one read. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/DestructiveIter` on O0, O1 and O2.
`extract_if(pred)` removes only the visited values its predicate selects: stopped after the first odd it leaves 2,3,4; a predicate failure stops there and leaves the unvisited values in place.
`splice(range, replacements)` states when replacements are consumed: finishing gives [1,8,9,4] and cancelling leaves [1,4].

A live drain excludes any other access or resize of its list, and an unfinished splice guard is a registered error; no clone stands in for the intended mutation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter drain_live_loan` and `--filter splice_unfinished_guard`.

cards.title: Borrowed views over collections: [View<T>] results, chunks and windows, loans that cannot escape
cards.body:
Destination: selections and iteration over a collection (top-k, filters, groups, chunks, windows, text splits) can work through views that read or mutate the live storage without copying it, keep the source's provenance, and cannot outlive or survive an invalidating change to their source.

Why it matters: copying move-only records to rank or walk them is wrong (they cannot be copied) and slow; a view that outlives its source is a memory-safety hole.

Decisions: D-MEM-COPYSEM1 (semantic copy for default read views), D-ITER-BORROW1=A, D-ITER-SLICEPRODUCERS1=A, D-ITER-MAPOWN1=A, D-ITER-VIEWCOLLECT1=A. Related: #3317 (iterator capabilities).

Source: #5976 c69, c70, c72 (archived #3041 c2-c5; option A of its ballot); #3317 c25-c35 (archived #3318, #3340, #3359, #3391, #3393).

criteria.text: An input-preserving top-k returns [View<T>] results that read the actual move-only records with no payload copy (`selected[2][0].score` reads the record), leave the source unchanged, and carry the receiver's provenance through keyed and fallible producers; counts of zero or below are checked before any read. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/TopkViews` on O0, O1 and O2.

A view result that escapes its local owner, or is used after a change that invalidates its source, is refused with a registered error; an allowed write does not re-rank existing results. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter topk_view_escape` and `--filter topk_view_invalidated`.

Owned, shared-borrowed and exclusive-borrowed iteration have distinct observable contracts: mutating a yielded element through ViewMut updates the original collection, replaced slots drop exactly once, and illegal overlap is refused before execution (D-ITER-BORROW1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/BorrowedIteration` on O0, O1 and O2.

Chunks and windows state width-zero, remainder, direction, overlap and mutability: non-overlapping mutable chunks update the source, and overlapping mutable windows are never built from ordinary references (D-ITER-SLICEPRODUCERS1=A).

Borrowed windows and chunks, and text split and lines views, allocate nothing per output where the source storage permits a view, and print their text, not handles. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/BorrowedIteration` with its allocation count on O0, O1 and O2.

A loan cannot escape its owner: an escaping loan, overlapping mutable windows and a resize during iteration are refused before execution, mutable-view escapes stay refused, and default read-view stores keep D-MEM-COPYSEM1 semantic copies (explicit borrowed aggregates are F083).

A mapper over owned items moves each move-only item exactly once; a shared view cannot move its items; exclusive-view mutation reaches the original storage; escaping callbacks respect their loans (D-ITER-MAPOWN1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/MapOwnedItems` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter map_move_from_shared_view`.

No `.view()` special case remains in the formatter (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Formatter/Expressions.jet:2595) or sema (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet:2255 on dev 168e1e9e92); `values[range]`, `&values[range]` and `~values[range]` keep their contracts, and `.view()` is an ordinary unknown-method error. Proof: `git grep -n '"view"' -- Compiler/JetParser Compiler/JetSema` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter view_method_unknown` passes.

An explicit `[View<T>]` collect is rooted in live storage with no payload copy; temporaries cannot escape, invalidating mutation is refused, and default `to_list` keeps D-MEM-COPYSEM1 copies (D-ITER-VIEWCOLLECT1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/BorrowedCollect` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter view_collect_`.

`s.chars()` lowers as a stream without building a list only when a paired measurement cell (list against stream: wall time and allocations) shows the win (D-CHAR-SCALAR1=A). Proof: the paired cell row in the measurement manifest, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3262 c33)

peek never pulls twice and its first side effects are documented; a rejected conditional consume keeps the pending item (or the rejection branch's replacement); an accepted consume advances once with no copy; peeked mutation targets the buffered item, and a loan cannot outlive or overlap a cursor mutation (D-ITER-LOOKAHEAD1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Peekable` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter peek_loan_across_next`. (was #3317 c10)

Fixed-width group reads keep every value of a short final group (typed partial result, or returned to the cursor), tell too few from too many without overconsuming, and state width zero, move-only values and remainder lifetime (D-ITER-EXACTGROUP1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ReadExact`. (was #3317 c14)

The unread remainder reflects mixed front and back advancement without copying; a mutable projection is exclusive; `into_remainder` keeps the source lifetime; UTF-8 byte units are kept; opaque and filter sources expose no contiguous remainder (D-ITER-REMAINDER1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterRemaining` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter iter_remaining_`. (was #3317 c16)

A copied borrowed slice iterator starts at the same position, advances independently and keeps its loan; one-shot and exclusive cursors are not copyable; shared external state stays shared; assigning from an explicit copy has clone_from meaning (D-ITER-COPY1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterCopy` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter iter_copy_one_shot`. (was #3317 c17)

cards.title: Map upsert in one hash lookup, with one spelling
cards.body:
Destination: Map has one method that inserts or updates a value in one hash lookup (the counter idiom `counts[k] += 1` without a second lookup), chosen by ballot.

Why it matters: today Map.update takes an entries argument (a merge), so an upsert costs two lookups and every port writes it differently.

Source: #5976 c63, c64, c66 (archived #1886).

criteria.text: A ballot presents 2-3 worked one-lookup upsert spellings with peer-language evidence and a one-mechanism argument (I8), ready for the owner. Proof: `timeout 120 node Tools/tower/tower.mjs decision list` shows the upsert ballot with its worked spellings.

After ratification, the chosen method does one hash lookup, runs on O0, O1 and O2 from one Core body, has cases under Tests/Cases/CoreLib/ and a teaching example of the counter idiom, and core-library.md documents it; no second upsert spelling exists.

cards.title: core.time: one now, one sleep, one format-pattern meaning, and time zone data
cards.body:
Destination: Core time has one Instant identity for now(), one sleep that takes a Duration, one meaning for date and time format patterns, and time zone and calendar data with exact DST behavior.

Why it matters: two sleeps (one unit-less) and two pattern meanings are the classic source of off-by-1000 and wrong-hour bugs.

Decisions: D-TIME-FORMAT-CANONICAL1=A, D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A.

Source: #5976 c48, c49, c50.

criteria.text: `unix_ms(now())` equals the epoch milliseconds of the same instant: now and Instant share one identity.

Date and time format patterns have one meaning in formatting and parsing (D-TIME-FORMAT-CANONICAL1=A), driven by one pattern table. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Time/FormatPatterns` on O0, O1 and O2.

One sleep: `tasks.sleep(ms: Int)` (Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet:270, unit-less, clamps negatives) is deleted, every caller uses `time.sleep(Duration)` (D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A), and a negative Duration behaves as core-library.md states. Proof: `git grep -n -E '^sleep: fn' -- Core` prints only Core/Time/Time.jet, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CoreLib/sleep_negative_duration` passes.
Time zone and calendar data: a lookup resolves a zone, a DST gap and an overlap resolve as core-library.md states, and a missing zone database is a typed error, not a crash.

UTC leap-second parsing, formatting and ordering live in Core time (23:59:60 is accepted and labelled), and checked Civil and Period methods route through one core.time method identity on O0, O1, O2 and web. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Time/LeapSeconds` and its UI snapshots.

cards.title: Mail and MIME parsing in Core: placement ballot, then hostile-input parsing
cards.body:
Destination: Core (or a first-party package, by ballot) parses and formats mail and MIME data: headers, encodings and attachments, separate from sending and authentication, safe on hostile input.

Why it matters: mail parsing is a frequent attack surface; it must have no network or credential side effects and must bound its work.

Related: #6826 (outgoing mail), #3280 (the MIME quoted-string scanner).

Source: #5976 c51, c52 (archived #3285, re-homed by the #6563 audit).

criteria.text: A research note under Docs/Research and a ballot settle the library, API and placement for mail and MIME parsing; parsing and formatting stay separate from sending and authentication. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Research/*mime*"` names the note, and the decision list shows the placement ballot.
Mail and MIME parsing handles hostile headers, encodings, size limits and attachment streaming, with no credential or network side effect.

One canonical quoted-string scanner parses MIME parameters: quoted `;`, escaped quotes, duplicate parameters, unterminated quotes and unknown extensions have explicit outcomes, and HTTP and web use the canonical type.

cards.title: core.io.progress: lazy, truthful progress over lists and iterators (D-PROGRESS-COUNTS1)
cards.body:
Destination: one progress adapter wraps a List or an iterator, stays lazy, counts the items actually pulled through every adapter, renders correctly on a TTY and off one, and gives the same output on every tier.

Why it matters: a progress bar that counts what it was told instead of what was read lies exactly when it matters (early break, filters, errors).

Decisions: D-PROGRESS-COUNTS1=A (truthful progress with automatic completion), D-COREIO1=A.

Source: #5976 c54-c58 (archived #1402), #3549 c13-c14.

criteria.text: `progress` accepts List<T> and Iter<T>, stays lazy until consumed, and reports count and percent when the total is known, with no caller bookkeeping. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter IO/Progress` on O0, O1 and O2.

Counts follow actual source pulls through map, filter, step, dedup, chunk, window, flatten, intersperse, zip, take_while, skip_while, filter_map and try_collect, including natural end, early break, unknown total and a ParseError mid-stream.
On a TTY progress redraws one line; off a TTY it prints one line per update; NO_COLOR strips ANSI from custom formats; description and format are explicit options rendered by the shared renderer.
progress_each, progress_bytes (a failed buffer is not counted) and a scoped progress_task with child tasks and unknown totals share one ProgressTask model and renderer.

core-library.md and the D-COREIO1 syntax record describe the shipped adapter, with no manual-bookkeeping claim left. Proof: `git grep -n -i 'progress' -- Docs/Spec/core-library.md` shows the adapter, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes.

Every Jet-owned human status line (CLI, compiler, runtime) goes through the one output adapter: TTY capability, TERM, NO_COLOR and `--color` select ANSI or plain, and `--json` writes only the machine schema.

cards.title: core.db crash consistency: every write and sync boundary crashed, whole-or-absent transactions
cards.body:
Destination: a deterministic crash harness crashes the real DB bridge at every reachable write and sync boundary (including dropped and reordered unsynced writes), and every reopen shows each transaction whole or absent; metamorphic SQL tests catch wrong queries.

Why it matters: a database that can come back with half a transaction loses data silently; only exhaustive crash schedules show it does not.

Related: #6448 (the SQL engine leaves Core for the `sql` package).

Source: #5976 c99-c105 (archived #3000, #3001).

criteria.text: A Jet test db_crash_reopen crashes every reachable write and sync boundary of a two-transaction workload on the real emitted DB bridge under the stated storage model (including dropped and reordered unsynced writes); each reopen shows whole-or-absent transactions with `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok, and the smallest failing schedule replays from its seed and reduces.
A timeout, an invalid oracle, unsupported storage or an incomplete schedule never counts as a pass, and network filesystems get no untested atomicity promise.

Metamorphic SQL pairs over generated data compare equal under core.testing.compare; a planted wrong query yields the first difference and a reduced replay; malformed DB or SQL input reports typed failures.

cards.title: One DataTree: duplicate keys, exact numbers, strict decode, readers and limits (D-DATATREE-RULES1)
cards.body:
Destination: every text and binary format parses into the one DataTree with the ratified rules: duplicate keys are errors unless asked for, numbers keep their exact text, decoding is strict, binary byte strings are Bytes; readers and limits have one shape; the duplicate encoding carriers are gone.

Why it matters: a second carrier or a lenient default gives the same input two meanings.

Decisions: D-DATATREE-RULES1=A (owner rulings 2026-10-05), D-ONE-CODECS1=A. The frozen #4602 holds the original per-format duplicate-key item.

Source: #5976 c2, c3, c6, c7, c93.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c4 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: JSON, YAML and TOML each report a duplicate object key as a parse error naming the key and both positions, and the explicit allow-duplicates option keeps the later value. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Encoding/duplicate_keys_`, one case per format.

Numbers keep their exact text (1.50 re-renders as 1.50; 1e400 and integers beyond Int survive), JSON "42" into an Int field is a decode error, and CBOR byte strings decode to the Bytes variant. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/DatatreeRules` on O0, O1 and O2.

`json.parse_allow_duplicates` accepts custom limits the way `json.reader_allow_duplicates` does (a `limits:` parameter defaulting to EncodingLimits.safe()). Proof: a #Test in Core/Encoding/JSON.jet; `jet test Core/Encoding/JSON.jet` passes.

`json.JSONReader` and `jsonl.JSONLReader` have one `next()` shape for text and file sources (today DataEvent for text and DataEvent? for files), as the ballot D-JSON-READER1 (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)) decides.
Lenient untyped JSON decode, declared pure, neither reads the wall clock nor writes to stderr: it runs with Time and IO denied.

The canonical DataTree and generated format and error source replace the duplicate encoding carriers, including the web ambient JSON, with byte and diagnostic parity. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/` on O0, O1 and O2.

Typed JSON decode allocates no DataTree, and its failure values and messages are byte-identical to the DataTree path on every fixture. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/TypedJSONDecode` and its allocation count in the measurement manifest.

Adjacent enum tagging (tag field plus a separate content field) encodes and decodes exactly: unit omission, shape, a wrong tag and missing content, and a content name that collides with a field is a compile error. Its spelling under D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1 is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EnumAdjacent` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter enum_adjacent_content_collides`. (was #3236 c8)

An opt-in retained-unknown enum case keeps the parsed tree of an unknown variant; known-case malformed payloads still fail and the strict default is unchanged; an untagged enum, two unknown cases, a wrong payload and direct construction are compile errors. Its spelling is on the same ballot (Main's ballot list, 2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EnumUnknown` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter enum_unknown_`. (was #3236 c9)

Decode aliases read old variant names and write only the canonical name; an alias collision is a compile error before codegen. Its spelling is on the same ballot (Main's ballot list, 2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EnumDecodeAliases` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter enum_decode_alias_collision`. (was #3236 c10)

Field metadata in the D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1=A forms: `#Codable(unknown: .Deny)`, `#Codable(.Flatten)`, custom Decode precedence and required, default and optional fields; missing, null and wrong-type values are distinct; unknown fields are rejected or retained in order. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/FieldMetadata` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c12)

Explicit-ID graphs round-trip, alias duplication is handled, input-selected types are rejected, and CBOR tags 28 and 29 are refused. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/GraphIdentity`. (was #3236 c15)

Docs/Spec defines the boundary crossing grid (time, schema, checker, evolution and fact columns), records the ratified literal, manifest, dependency, link, wire, validation, migration, fact, trust and error rules as grid cells with no second mechanism, and every new boundary feature names one cell. Proof: the grid table in Docs/Spec and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter spec_links`. (was #3236 c17)
A boundary planned on the grid behaves the same on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/FiveProjectionShape` on every tier. (was #3236 c19)

Per-projection rename metadata reaches text formats, Env, Args, DB and Layout inspection; migration stays scoped to published schemas. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/FiveProjectionShape` (one Shape fixture over JSON, Env, Args, DB and Layout) on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c31)

Derived codecs work across modules: a derived encode has the visibility of its type (no E0605 from another module), a field whose type is declared in another file derives, and the None policy is one documented rule (omit or null) with a typed option for the other. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/DerivedCodecCrossModule` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c32)

D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1=A is built: #Codable alone means both directions; type options .Encode or .Decode, unknown: .Deny, tag: .External (default), .Field("kind") or .None, from: .Base and published; field forms #Codable(.Skip) and #Codable(.Flatten). #Encode, #Decode, #DenyUnknownFields, #Discriminant, #Untagged, #CodableAsBase, #PublishedSchema, #Skip and #Flatten are gone from the Prelude, the syntax registry and every caller with no teaching diagnostic (on dev 168e1e9e92, `#PublishedSchema` still appears in 24 .jet files). Combinations keep their results and E2407-E2415, E0905 and E0910 stay. Proof: `git grep -l -E '#(Encode|Decode|DenyUnknownFields|Discriminant|Untagged|CodableAsBase|PublishedSchema|Skip|Flatten)\b' -- '*.jet'` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/` passes on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c33)

A field default that calls a fallible function uses its success type under the selected propagation or refusal, and generated locals stay bound (no unbound jet_serde_ok_value). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter codable_fallible_field_default`. (was #3236 c34)

unknown: .Deny composes with a .Flatten field: consumed keys are tracked across flattened fields and residual unknown keys are rejected. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/CodableDenyFlatten`. (was #3236 c35)
Synthesized encode and decode never collide with a type's own encode and decode methods. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter codable_own_encode_method`. (was #3236 c36)

core.data.jmespath (D-CORE-JMESPATH1=A): compile and search pass the pinned official compliance corpus including all 26 built-ins; work is bounded, there is no I/O, and compiled expressions are reusable; invalid function, type and arity, zero-step slices, mixed numbers and duplicate names are exercised. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Data/jmespath_compliance`. (was #3280 c9)

json merge patch passes the RFC 7386 appendix A cases (null deletes, arrays replace); the original is unchanged on failure; limits are enforced; typed re-entry goes through Decode. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONMergePatch`. (was #3280 c10)

`patch(before, diff(before, after)) == after` for every fixture; ordering and array policy are stated; nonfinite input is rejected; time and memory are bounded. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONDiff`. (was #3280 c11)

A merge diff whose null update cannot be represented returns Unsupported with a path, and representable pairs verify a round trip. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONMergeDiff`. (was #3280 c12)

Runtime field selection works at top level and nested, with empty, duplicate, overlapping and unknown paths; rename, skip and custom codecs are honoured; hidden fields are never emitted; array-element projection is refused; the json_selected_vs_dto pair is measured. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONSelect` and the paired cell in the measurement manifest. (was #3280 c13)

`json.update<T>` is atomic; missing, null, default and unknown fields have defined behaviour; validation and custom Decode precedence are kept. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONUpdate`. (was #3280 c14)

Top-level exclusions serialize all fields except the named ones: empty, duplicate, unknown and all-field exclusions are handled, order is preserved, newly added ordinary fields are emitted and Encode-omitted fields stay absent. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONExclude` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3280 c54)

Exclusion keeps exact numbers and custom or renamed field meaning without a JSON round trip, and its allocations are measured against an equivalent application projection. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONExclude` and the paired cell in the measurement manifest. (was #3280 c56)

json.parse and json.decode take an optional `limits:` label defaulting to `EncodingLimits.safe()`, and a bare call behaves as today; the sibling `parse_with_limits` (Core/Encoding/JSON.jet) is deleted and its callers move (D-CORE-JSONLIMIT1=A, D-API-COMPOSE1=A). Proof: `git grep -n parse_with_limits -- Core Jetpack Examples` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Data/JSON/JSONParseLimits` passes on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3280 c59)

sign_extend takes `bits: Int(1..64)` and stays infallible (D-BINARY-SIGNEXT1=A; Core/Encoding/Binary.jet takes a plain Int today), and every caller migrates in the same change with no teaching diagnostic or jet fix rule (owner 2026-11-06). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter sign_extend_bits_out_of_range` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Encoding/sign_extend`. (was #4472 c1)

Scoped requested-capacity accounting enforces the encoding max_bytes limit exactly on every tier, including the error and Int-growth paths. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Encoding/max_bytes_exact_`. (was #4472 c7)

cards.title: Byte streams and the HTTP server: read_into, WebSocket routes and wss upgrade (D-NET-READINTO1, D-WS-ROUTE1)
cards.body:
Destination: every byte stream reads into a caller-owned buffer, the HTTP server, client and TLS reader use it, and the HTTP mux has a WebSocket route kind that authenticates, validates and upgrades over TCP and TLS.

Why it matters: a fresh limit-sized buffer per read is the main allocation cost of a steady server, and WebSocket handlers returning a fake response after the socket is gone is a design defect.

Decisions: D-NET-READINTO1=A (2026-11-10), D-WS-ROUTE1=A (2026-11-10). Depends on the concurrent serve loop (#4635).

Source: #5976 c42, c43, c110, c112, c113.

criteria.text: `read_into(buffer, limit)` appends up to `limit` bytes to the caller's [U8] and returns the count, as an inherent method on TCPStream, UnixStream, TLSStream and file readers, with a deadline form; it returns 0 at end of stream and a limit below 1 is invalid input; the Reader trait is unchanged (D-NET-READINTO1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Net/read_into_` on O0, O1 and O2.

The HTTP server, the HTTP client and the TLS record reader use read_into, and a paired cell (a read(4096) loop against read_into: wall time, allocations per read, peak memory) is in the measurement manifest with read_into strictly winning. Proof: the manifest row and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/` on O0, O1 and O2.

`mux.websocket(pattern, handler)` and `#Server.WebSocket(path)` (D-WS-ROUTE1=A): the server runs authentication and Origin policy, then validates and upgrades, and the handler returns nothing; one adapter and handshake serve TCP and TLS; the route owns GET (an equal GET registration is refused, HEAD gets 405, OPTIONS lists GET); upgraded tasks stay inside server limits and shutdown; close codes are kept and 1011 is sent only before the transport closes; OpenAPI describes the handshake only. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/WebSocketRoute` on O0, O1 and O2.
The HTTP server upgrades a TLS connection to WebSocket (Core/HTTP's upgrade path no longer needs a raw fd >= 0).
WebSocket lifetime: two connection contexts stay isolated, a disconnect cleans up, MessageTooLarge is an explicit bound, an acknowledgement means queued only, and raw WebSocket is not Socket.IO.

HTTP/1 server framing, session policy and PEM/X.509 parsing are in Jet, with a real TLS server stream on every applicable tier (today Core TLS is client-only: #6317 refuses the core-tls-server cases). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPServerTLS` and `--filter core_net_tls`, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/TLSPeerIdentity`.

Server policy order: CORS never authorizes, security headers survive errors, untrusted forwarded identity cannot bypass rate or auth limits, and malformed or oversized input is rejected before any handler mutation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/HTTPPolicyOrder` on O0, O1 and O2.

http-service run and dev tiers pass every probe with the same responses as AOT: a Jet case runs GET /health, PUT /kv and GET /kv against O0, O1 and O2 with byte-identical responses and no probe timeout. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPService/probes_identical_on_every_tier`. (was #2873 c4)

One documented retry rule (today Core/HTTP/Client.jet retries PUT and DELETE while the old runtime retried only safe methods), and every route calls the one Jet meaning: golden net/http_client shows a PUT retry and a POST non-retry with identical output on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/HTTPClient`. (was #3665 c2)

Pool reuse and decoding: pooled_h1_reuses_only_after_drain_and_decodes_gzip_natively, h1_skips_early_hints_reuses_final_response_and_rejects_upgrade, gzip_decoding_streams_before_the_response_finishes, custom_client_clones_share_pool_cookie_jar_and_transport_facts and public_client_policy_exposes_pool_cookie_timeouts_and_facts pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/` on those rows. (was #3665 c4)

HeaderName and HeaderValue are checked text types (D-HTTP-HEADER-BAD1=A): every header setter and builder takes them, dynamic parse returns HTTPError.InvalidHeader with no second runtime validation, an invalid written character is a compile error with a fix, session_retries bounds fail, and there is no silent unchanged-header fallback. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_header_` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/`. (was #3665 c9)

`http.Client.new()` and every builder method in core-library.md are Jet functions in Core/HTTP/Client.jet, and every semantic item from the old runtime HTTP policy has its Core home with only socket, TLS and gzip provider leaves left. Proof: `git grep -n 'HTTPClientNew\|jet_http_client_new_impl' -- Compiler Core` prints nothing (on dev 168e1e9e92 it matches 16 lines in 10 Compiler files). (was #3665 c11)

The http_client_law fixtures that call Client.new() typecheck and run: public_client_allow_http_downgrade_method_typechecks and public_client_retries_method_typechecks pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv (both name #6843). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/public_client_`. (was #3665 c12)

Incoming request and received response text projections use the one body lifecycle and the one-MiB default cap: default, explicit-limit, over-limit, consumed-body, error-identity, binary and streaming cases pass, and hostile streamed overruns report InvalidFraming. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPI9/` (http_text_projections_preserve_default_limits_and_body_lifecycle_on_all_supported_tiers and hostile_http_response_sinks_reject_streamed_overruns_on_both_dev_tiers leave Tests/known-failing.tsv). (was #3665 c16)

The request builder's json(value) takes a Codable value, uses the typed encoder, sets JSON framing and does not conflict with decode-side inference; the hand-escaped request example is replaced by malformed and error tests. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter http_request_json_body`. (was #3665 c17)

A one-shot HTTP response's second body().text returns Err(.BodyConsumed) and never yields the body again. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPI9/` (the BodyConsumed row passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv). (was #3665 c23)

An HTTP JSON body keeps malformed JSON, a wrong field type and a real framing failure distinct; the FieldError path survives with no second decode; body limits are unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter http_json_decode_errors_stay_typed`. (was #3665 c25)

The configured client's cookie jar is in Core: http_client_law cases cookie_jar_rejects_domain_attributes_on_ip_hosts, cookie_jar_uses_schemeful_registrable_sites_and_rejects_public_suffixes and cookie_jar_enforces_per_domain_and_global_count_bounds pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/cookie_jar_`. (was #3665 c27)

Redirect policy is in Core: follow_same_origin_credentials_strips_authorization_on_redirect, cross_origin_redirect_strips_request_credentials_and_rejects_proxy_auth and unreplayable_307_closes_redirect_body pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/` on those rows. (was #3665 c28)

Proxy selection is in Core: public_client_proxy_none_ignores_environment_proxy and public_client_proxy_url_sends_absolute_form pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/public_client_proxy_`. (was #3665 c29)

The h2 client and HPACK are in Core: explicit_h2c_negotiates_hpack_and_reuses_one_session and the http_client_law/h2_ rows (queued frames, idle stream flood, invalid HPACK names and padding, 64 MiB body overrun) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/h2_` and `--filter explicit_h2c`. (was #3665 c30)

Client TLS policy is in Core: public_client_tls_custom_only_trust and public_client_tls_identity_and_version_bounds pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/public_client_tls_`. (was #3665 c31)

Request bodies stream: `.body(...)` takes a byte source, and upload_streams_before_the_body_source_finishes, unknown_length_upload_uses_h1_chunked_transfer_encoding, h2_upload_streams_data_frames_before_body_eof and post_307_replays_streamed_body_under_redirect_tee_cap pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/` on those rows. (was #3665 c32)

Client deadlines: request_first_byte_timeout_overrides_client_phase_budget and ambient_context_deadline_upper_bounds_client_total_timeout pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/` on those rows. (was #3665 c33)

The four corelib/core_http_client_ fixtures (binary body once, multipart boundary, pre-response errors, invalid redirect limits) are written in current Jet and pass, leaving Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CoreLib/core_http_client_`. (was #3665 c34)

core.http uses HTTPS by default: an HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect is refused unless `allow_http_downgrade` is set, and HTTPS negotiates h2 with an explicit root. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/https_to_http_redirect_denied_unless_allow_http_downgrade` and `--filter http_client_law/https_negotiates_h2_with_an_explicit_root`. (was #3665 c35)

cards.title: Core API shape: results come back as returns, no API that can never succeed, spec matches Core
cards.body:
Destination: public Core APIs return their results instead of filling out-parameters, none of them is a stub that can never succeed, core-library.md matches the declared signatures, and module identity does not depend on file paths.

Why it matters: out-parameters and never-succeeding stubs are the API smells the owner ruled out; a spec that drifts from Core teaches the wrong surface.

Decisions: D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A (the frozen #4561 holds the original item). Related: #6367 (API design principle), #6848 c5 (maturity as a typed fact).

Source: #5976 c25, c29, c30, c35.

criteria.text: No public API in Core, Jetpack, Compiler or Tools has an output-only `&` parameter: each returns a value, tuple or struct, with every caller and teaching doc migrated in one cutover (D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A); real edits, buffer reuse, streams and foreign boundaries keep `&`. Proof: a guard that lists output-only `&` parameters reports none: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter output_returns`.

No public Core function can never succeed: one that fails with Unsupported on every target is implemented or removed. Proof: a guard over Core's public functions reports none: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_never_succeeds`.

core-library.md documents each public Core function with the signature Core declares (the drift found by the 2026-10-05 API comparisons is fixed). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes.
A Core module's identity is its module path, never its file path: moving a Core file without changing its module declaration changes no symbol, cache key or diagnostic name.

cards.title: Core names, modules and prelude follow the ratified contracts: one name, one owner, one prelude
cards.body:
Destination: Core spells each operation once, each job has one owning module under the ratified module map, the prelude is one short readable module with the ratified contents, and foreign spellings are taught by fixes, never aliased.

Why it matters: duplicate names and plural/singular module twins make every port and every doc guess; the decisions are ratified and only the cutovers remain.

Decisions: D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A, D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1=A, D-CORE-SPELLING1=A, D-LISTREMOVE1=F, D-ONCE-VERB1=A, D-ONCE-PRINT1=A, D-VERDICT-1321-1, D-CORE-PRELUDE1=A, D-CORE-PRELUDE2=B, D-NAME-ALIAS1=A, D-LANGNS-NAME1=A, D-RULEARG-TYPES1=A. Greenfield: each cutover migrates every caller in one change with no alias or teaching row for the retired name.

Source: #3548 c45, c47-c49, c51; #4022 c2, c4 (ballots ratified) and c21; #5976 c37.

criteria.text: One Jet name per Core operation (D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A): each family's kept name is listed in core-library.md and every duplicate (such as loads/load) is deleted with its callers migrated. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` exits 0 and reports no alias pair.

The 20 most common Python collection and string spellings in the ScriptBench Python programs (`sorted`, `list(range(...))`, `Counter`, `join`, `split`, `strip`, `startswith` and so on) each map to one Jet name or get an E0311 whose `fix_edits` names it; `xs.sorted()` and `(0..<8).to_list()` no longer fail without a fix (today E0311 for both).

The module renames of D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1=A are done: collections to collection, files to file, jobs to job, tasks to task, units to unit, testing to test, args to cli, sync to replica, and tui nests as term.ui (Core/ still has the old directories on dev 168e1e9e92). Proof: `git ls-files Core | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u` shows none of the old names, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden` passes on O0, O1 and O2.

Each job has one owning module (D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1=A): process owns the working directory, environment, pid, arguments and exit; Session lives in auth; app folds away; and a guard lists any export carried by two modules. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_module_owners` reports none.
Core names use one English (American) spelling (D-CORE-SPELLING1=A). Proof: a guard over Core's public names reports no British spelling: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_spelling`.

`remove(x)` deletes the first item equal to x, `remove(i, .Slot)` deletes a slot and `remove(x, .Val)` states the default (D-LISTREMOVE1=F). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ListRemove` on O0, O1 and O2.

One verb per collection job (D-ONCE-VERB1=A): pop removes and returns on every collection, replace keeps only the List swap meaning, bare `.from()` is the conversion constructor, and retired verbs are gone.

One print family (D-ONCE-PRINT1=A, D-VERDICT-1321-1): ambient print ends the line and prints each argument on its own line, io.print is its #NoPrelude twin, and io.println, io.sprint and io.repr are gone with callers migrated. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'io\.(println|sprint|repr)\(' -- '*.jet'` prints nothing, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/` passes.

The prelude is one short readable Core module (D-NAME-ALIAS1=A, D-CORE-PRELUDE1=A): ambient basics are declared there, the rest are `pub use` aliases into the Core tree, the compiler opens it for every file, a user declaration replaces a prelude alias, and #NoPrelude opts a file out.

read_file, write_file and file_exists are ambient prelude names with their file effects visible in signatures; random stays in core.math.random (D-CORE-PRELUDE2=B). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/PreludeFiles` on O0, O1 and O2.

Language declarations live in core.lang (D-LANGNS-NAME1=A) and marker argument types are the 14 generated prelude enums (D-RULEARG-TYPES1=A). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes and `git grep` shows the enums in the generated prelude.

reactive.unsubscribe, reactive.is_active and the text.combinators module are admitted by canonical export generation, with import and call goldens. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Reactive/` and `--filter text/combinators` on O0, O1 and O2.

Every row in the one authored operation row set states receiver and result ownership, eager or lazy timing, callback count and order, stop-item consumption, failure channel, empty result and required buffering. Proof: a #Test in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet fails on a row missing any field (`jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`). (was #3325 c7)

Examples cover empty all and any, zero, first failure, strict, short and padded zip, and remainder continuation, and no source error prints as a success. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/OperationContract` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3325 c8)

Generated docs mark each operation as shipped or source-only; LAST ties stay as #2298 pinned and eager defaults stay D-CORE-EAGER1=A and D-CORE-EAGER2=A. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/` passes and the generated operation docs show the marker. (was #3325 c9)

The four method tables in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet are replaced by one authored row set; JetSema, JetCodegen and the generated docs, completion and explain views all read it, with no second registry, and `jet check Compiler` is clean.
