Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/` passes and `git grep -n -i 'not built' -- Docs/Spec` lists each unbuilt feature with a card.
Unsupported public claims are removed or narrowed, and every evidence link in the README and Docs/Spec resolves to a committed golden, case, conformance or suite artifact.
The first-hour journey runs end to end with no skipped step and is registered in the cases suite (it fails today because `jet add` is not built, #4944).

Generated documentation catalogs and their producers are removed, while the executable registry and proof checks keep their input coverage. Proof: `git ls-files Docs | grep -i -E 'generated|catalog'` prints none and `jet test Tests/Guards` passes.

Per-tier adoption playbooks and case studies link only to measured evidence (benchmarks, receipts or cases in the repo). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter docs_links_resolve` over the adoption docs. (was #2199 c26)

jet inspect structure --core --json is the one spelling of the Core catalog and prints it from any directory with no package: a positional core would collide with a target named core. The five Core tools (LaneCheck's Core row, LibcCensus, CoreModuleCheck, CoreSurfaceLedger, RuntimeEffectRows), cli.md and the code comments use it, and no positional structure core form remains. On dev 4b334eae76 the tools call the positional form, which fails with E2105, while --core needs a package (E2104). Proof: a ui case for jet inspect structure --core --json at the repo root and in an empty directory, plus LibcCensus --check and CoreSurfaceLedger --check passing on the built compiler. (moved from #5072 c62) (was #6418 c150)

No .jet comment cites deleted Rust code (crates/…/src paths or .rs:N lines; 134 files on dev 72a8142651). Proof: `git grep -l -E 'crates/[a-z_-]+/src|\.rs:[0-9]' -- '*.jet'` prints nothing. (was #6637 c14)

AGENTS.md and Docs/Spec/Reference teach only current failure forms (no `x?` propagation, no `T ! E`). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter syntax_reconciliation` passes and `git grep -n -E '[a-z)]\?$| ! [A-Z]' -- AGENTS.md Docs/Spec/Reference` prints nothing. (was #6637 c17)

No test prose, case name or closure template claims an interpreter comparison (there is no interpreter tier, D-EXEC2=A; 291 test files mention 'interpreter' on dev 72a8142651), cut over with the case renames in one change. Proof: `git grep -l -i interpreter -- tests` prints nothing. (was #6637 c20)

The HTML report checker (.agents/skills/html/scripts/check.mjs, check "no external resources") accepts citation hyperlinks: an `<a href="https://...">` link passes, while loaded dependencies (script, link stylesheet, @import, img, font and other src= URLs) are still refused. Proof: a checker fixture with a citation link passes and one with an external script or stylesheet fails.

The HTML report checker's prose-wall rule (check.mjs proseRun) counts only three adjacent sibling paragraphs: two separate pairs of long paragraphs in different containers, as in `

`, pass, because no regex capture may span a closing

. Three long sibling paragraphs in a row still fail. Proof: both fixtures in a checker test.

cards.title: Guides: a design guide, architecture rows for every Core namespace, embedded systems, and API maturity
cards.body:
Destination: Docs/spec/guides/design.md teaches a method for hard problems, SOLID translated for Jet and the escape-hatch ladder, linking every cited decision; Docs/spec/architecture.md classifies every Core namespace; and the docs cover embedded systems and API maturity.

Why it matters: these are the pages a programmer reads before writing a large Jet program.

Source: Map card #5982 c1, c2, c15 (from #4728, #4800, #155).

criteria.text: Docs/Spec/Guides/design.md exists with a method for hard problems, SOLID translated for Jet and the escape-hatch ladder, and links every decision it cites. Proof: `git ls-files Docs/Spec/Guides/design.md` and each D- id in it resolves in `tower decision show`.

Docs/Spec/architecture.md has a classification row for every Core namespace (60 were missing). Proof: a guard compares the namespaces under Core/ with the architecture rows (`jet test Tests/Guards --filter architecture_rows`).

The docs have a page for embedded systems (targets, no-OS machines, boards) and one for API maturity tags, each linked from the guide index. Proof: `git ls-files Docs/Spec/Guides | grep -i -E 'embedded|maturity'` names both.

cards.title: LSP references and rename follow checked identity across files, versions and Unicode
cards.body:
Destination: definition, references, prepareRename, rename and document symbols in `jet self lsp` resolve by checked semantic identity, not by name text: they pick exactly the declaration meant across aliases, shadowing, same-name modules and qualified calls; return real absolute URIs and exact identifier spans; apply edits at the checked overlay positions of unsaved documents; refuse when the target or document version is not current; and handle UTF-8 and UTF-16 boundaries.

Why it matters: a rename that touches the wrong `letter` or edits stale positions breaks code silently.

The proofs are tests/cases/lsp/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename and lsp_document_symbol_returns_symbols_for_imported_package_module (known-failing on dev 6f82527b17, rows naming #6386).

Source: #4917 c11, c37, c39-c46 (from #3183, #3184, #2370, #6164).

criteria.text: References and rename on BIG-P02 select exactly scoring.letter's declaration and call, and leave the unrelated util.letter and its call untouched.
Returned document URIs name the actual absolute files and ranges cover the exact nonempty identifier spans, with no `file://run.jet` host-like URI or 0:0 insertion.

Definition, references, prepareRename, rename and semantic-op metadata agree on identity and location for aliases, shadowing, same-name modules and qualified calls. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_definition_imported_identity_collisions_are_exact` and `--filter lsp/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename`.

An unresolved or incomplete rename target gets an explicit refusal or a coverage-limited result, never a claimed-safe rename. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename` (refusal step).

A sibling document with unsaved inserted lines receives edits at the checked overlay positions, not disk positions. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename` (overlay step).

A document version change between check and apply blocks automatic application and asks for a new check, exercised through the real LSP response and version contract, not a range helper. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename` (version step).

Saved, dirty and UTF-8/UTF-16 boundary cases keep the selected declaration and change no unrelated text, and a Unicode identifier hovers and renames correctly. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename` (Unicode steps).
textDocument/documentSymbol returns the declarations of an opened imported package module with zero diagnostics.
Through the real LSP on the self-hosted index, renaming an enum variant crosses sibling modules (leading-dot and bare patterns) and leaves same-spelled cases and `#Rename` wire names alone.

Hover on a local, a parameter and a Core call shows its type; go-to-definition reaches a declaration in the same file, in another module and in Core. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_hover_returns_signature` and `--filter lsp/lsp_definition_` pass (lsp_definition_returns_location and lsp_hover_returns_signature PASS on dev 6f82527b17; the imported and generated definition cases are known-failing). (was #4917 c3)

Framing, positions, edits, progress, errors, cancellation and shutdown meet the LSP standard through the real stdio transport. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_json_transcripts` and `--filter lsp/lsp_incremental_sync_rejects_stale_and_malformed_edits`. (was #4917 c63)

cards.title: Editor assists from checked facts: completion with foreign-word rows, semantic tokens and inlay hints
cards.body:
Destination: completion, semantic tokens and inlay hints in `jet self lsp` read lexer tokens and checked facts. Completion maps foreign method words (append, length, size, push_back) to the Jet name through the same registered rows E0311 uses; semantic tokens follow current syntax; inlay hints show call marks (D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A), automatically passed-up failures and scattered-method breadcrumbs.

Why it matters: these are what an editor shows on every keystroke; a private scanner or a second table drifts from the compiler.

Source: #4917 c10, c24-c27, c31, c49-c52 (from #6164, #4625, #662, #6014, #88).

criteria.text: Hover, references and completion find identifiers from lexer tokens, with no private text scanner in Compiler/JetLSP. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_hover_` and `--filter lsp/lsp_references_finds_all_uses` pass, and JetLSP has no character-class identifier scanner (`git grep -n -E 'is_ident_(start|char)' -- Compiler/JetLSP` prints nothing).
Typing `nums.app` on `nums: [Int]` returns an item labelled `push` whose filter text is `append` and whose edit inserts `push`; the same for `.length` and `.size` to `len` and `push_back` to `push`.

Accepting a foreign-word completion never writes the foreign word, and the result compiles with no diagnostic. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_completion_foreign_words` (apply step).
Completion reads the same registered rows as E0311, and a test fails if a row exists in one view and not the other.

Ordinary prefix completion is unchanged when no foreign row matches. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_completion_returns_items` and `--filter lsp/lsp_completion_returns_snippets_and_auto_imports` pass.
Semantic tokens give retired local `view`/`.view` spellings no identifier or method token, while View<T> and ViewMut<T> stay type tokens.

The token classifier follows current syntax and handles comments, strings, incremental edits and qualified names without skip heuristics. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_semantic_tokens_` passes, delta fallback included.
Inlay hints show breadcrumbs for scattered methods.
Inlay hints show `&` and `&&` at calls (D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A) and the server underlines a changed argument.
The server sends an inlay hint at every call whose failure passes up automatically: a fixture with 4 such calls receives exactly 4 hints.

For each #Todo, the checker lists a bounded, ranked set of in-scope locals, parameters and imported functions that fit the goal type, and the LSP shows the same candidates. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter todo_candidates` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_todo_candidates`. (was #3720 c13)

cards.title: The LSP stays current: cancellation, fresh verdicts, embedded Jet regions, workspaces and the VS Code, Zed and Neovim matrix
cards.body:
Destination: `jet self lsp` never publishes a stale or cancelled result: cancelled work returns -32800, the latest edit gets the fresh verdict, Jet regions inside host documents map edits and diagnostics through incremental edits, workspaces with inline metadata and multiple roots behave honestly, and VS Code, Zed and Neovim run the real server with correct visible results.

Why it matters: an editor that shows yesterday's error, or applies an edit to the wrong version, is worse than no editor support.

Decisions: D-LSP1=C (editor engine architecture). No new scheduling policy, worker count or public cancellation semantics is chosen silently.

Source: #4917 c57-c60, c67-c70 (from #3196, #3410-#3413, #3003).

criteria.text: Cancelled work returns the -32800 response and never later publishes a result as current.

The latest request receives the correct fresh verdict, diagnostics already published for unrelated modules stay correct, and nothing is reused across server restarts (no compile cache); no new scheduling policy, worker count or cancellation semantics is selected outside D-LSP1. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_overlapping_edits_latest_checked_revision_wins` and `--filter lsp/lsp_sibling_import_edit_never_publishes_stale_verdict` pass (both PASS on dev 6f82527b17 with gate-p141), plus a restart step.

The edit-stream latency run prints p50 and p95 cancel-to-release and edit-to-current-verdict latencies, peak in-flight checks and the binary and input identity, attached to the card. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_repeated_edit_stream_latency` (opt-in).

A host document with two Jet regions (including the UTF-8 25..46 / UTF-16 23..44 case) checks through the JetDriver SourceDocument query; diagnostics and edits map to host byte ranges after an incremental edit; cancellation, stale versions, Unicode and partial syntax never return a false current result.

Every applicable semantic feature and Jet construct cell has a witness test or a reasoned N/A: navigation, references, rename, completion and hierarchy follow checked identity across files, generics, shadowing and generated origins and stay version-correct during broken edits.

Workspace and document operations work for inline single-file metadata and multi-root projects; formatting uses the canonical formatter; unsaved, read-only, generated, Unicode, symlink and dependency-change cases behave honestly. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_workspace_symbols_follow_all_roots_and_folder_changes` and `--filter lsp/lsp_workspace_honest_cases`.

VS Code, Zed and Neovim each run the real server against the client matrix with correct visible results, with limitations evidenced and bound to versions. Proof: a scripted client-matrix run per editor under Tools/Editors, its report committed under Docs/audits.

Opening a file with a type error publishes the same diagnostics (code, range, message) as `jet check` on that file. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_checked_imported_diagnostics_and_repairs`. (was #4917 c2)

The editor extension in Tools/Editors starts `jet self lsp` with no extra settings; a scripted smoke test opens a file and receives its diagnostics. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/editor_extension_starts_lsp`. (was #4917 c4)

JetSemIndex and JetImpact compile against the current driver and sema API (no Rust-shim calls, no missing SemaCompilerModuleSource fields), and the Tests/Cases/LSP rows run instead of REFUSED. Proof: `jet check Compiler/JetSemIndex` and `jet check Compiler/JetImpact` exit 0, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/` reports no REFUSED row. (was #4917 c8)

The LSP publishes the same report meaning and recovery data as `jet check` for the same program on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_checked_imported_diagnostics_and_repairs`. (was #4917 c30)

The initialize response and registrations advertise only complete handlers and respect negotiated client capabilities. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_initialize_capabilities_have_named_test_coverage`. (was #4917 c62)

A Jet LSP conformance test runs every case of an LSP 3.18 inventory checked in beside the LSP tests. Each applicable row names a witness test that exercises it through the real stdio transport, each N/A row carries a concrete reason, and the test fails on any row that is unknown, has no witness, or is marked N/A because it is unimplemented. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter lsp_conformance` passes. (was #4917 c66)

cards.title: Editor refactors on checked facts: callable summary, signature-change preview, extract and inline, and marker moves
cards.body:
Destination: the editor offers refactors that are proven safe from checked facts: an opt-in callable summary (D-READ-LOCAL1=A), a signature-change preview with explicit caller values (D-BIG-SIGNATURE1=A), extract and inline transforms that keep evaluation order, capture, control flow, ownership and effects, and the D-MARKER-MOVE1=A code actions.

Why it matters: refactors that cannot prove safety should refuse, not guess.

Source: #4917 c29, c53-c55 (from #3191, #3168, #3187, #3198).

criteria.text: D-MARKER-MOVE1=A, editor half (the CLI half landed in 37eae4f5d6): code actions on a struct and on a function offer 'Write the markers above the declaration' and 'Write the markers inside the declaration's body', and each edit gives the same text as `jet fix --markers above|inside`.

An opt-in callable summary anchored by semantic identity shows failure type and source, write-access parameters, the effect row and checked links, and labels missing facts unavailable (D-READ-LOCAL1=A); fixtures cover normal, typed-failure, write-access, impure, invalid and stale cases.

The signature-change preview (D-BIG-SIGNATURE1=A) needs an explicit caller value, names the declaration, document versions and exact checked callers, blocks on unresolved uses, and re-checks after a document change.
Every advertised extract and inline transform has a before/after or refusal receipt that keeps evaluation order, capture, control flow, ownership and effects, using the checked index.

Import fixes resolve same-leaf symbols, aliases, private targets, already-imported names and generated declarations to the selected accessible identity, and organize-imports keeps every required import. A missing action is listed as a follow-on, never silently skipped. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_import_fix_selects_accessible_identity` and `--filter lsp/lsp_organize_imports_keeps_required`.

Hover and inspect label foreign and generated origins and unknown analysis boundaries, so a reader never has to inspect compiler special cases. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_hover_marks_foreign_and_generated_origins`. (was #3186 c4)

Hover, signature help and the checked call record for ambient `print` and `core.term.print` report the same one-or-more-argument Printable contract and declaration identity, through real CLI and editor requests (spans, codes, fixes, URIs and invalidation included). Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetLSP --filter print_hover_signature_call_record_agree` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_print_contract_matches_cli`. (was #3186 c8)

Every `fix_edits` entry in a diagnostic is offered as an LSP code action, and hover on a call shows the callee's effect row (fixture test). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_fix_edits_are_code_actions` and `--filter lsp/lsp_hover_shows_effect_row`. (was #4917 c7)

JetLSP reads declaration visibility from Sema facts, never from source text: the import quick-fix fires for a public function in another module, and signature preview reports external callers for public functions and not for functions inside a priv module. Proof: JetLSP tests whose fixtures contain no `pub` keyword (`jet test Compiler/JetLSP`). (was #4917 c71)

cards.title: jet flash: watch, rebuild and flash a board, show flash and RAM budgets, and fail by name with no probe
cards.body:
Destination: for a supported board, `jet flash --watch` rebuilds on save, flashes and streams the board log; `jet build` for a board target prints flash and RAM use per section against the board budget; the programmer comes from canonical TargetMachine facts and every flash writes one typed receipt binding the image digest and the programmer invocation; a missing board or probe is a named error.

Why it matters: the embedded edit loop should be one command, and a budget overrun should fail the build, not the device.

Decisions: D-HW-DECLARE1=A (boards are typed values), D-TARGET-SURFACE1.

Source: #6386 c10-c12, c115 (from #6022, #2856).

criteria.text: For a supported board, `jet flash --watch` rebuilds on save, flashes and streams the board log until stopped. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Flash/watch_edit_cycle_qemu` runs one edit cycle against an emulated board.
`jet build` for a board target prints flash and RAM use per section against the board budget and fails with a named error when a budget is exceeded.
With no board or probe attached, `jet flash` fails with a named error listing what it looked for.

`jet flash` takes its programmer from canonical TargetMachine facts, binds the image digest and programmer invocation into one typed receipt, and reports an unavailable or failed programming through the registered command error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Flash/receipt_binds_image_and_programmer` against an emulated board.

cards.title: Jet embeds in a C host and as a wasm component from one export surface, with authority checked at load (D-EMBED1=E, D-EMBED2=C)
cards.body:
Destination: one typed export surface lowers to a native C-ABI libjet and a WASM component (D-EMBED1=E) from one capability contract (D-EMBED2=C): a C host links libjet, loads a Jet module, calls a function and gets its result; the component runs the same module in wasmtime with the same output; the embedding header is generated with a runnable C example; and the host passes an Authority value so a guest lacking a grant is refused at load, before any guest code runs.

Why it matters: embedding Jet in an existing C or C++ program is how many teams would first adopt it; load-time authority beats Lua's run-time global removal.

Source: #6386 c16-c18, c20 (from #6023, the acceptance checks of #1915).

criteria.text: A C host links libjet, loads a Jet module, calls a function and gets its result with the self-hosted `jet`.
The wasm component runs the same module in wasmtime with the same output.
The embedding header is generated, and its doc page carries a runnable C example checked by a test.
The host passes an Authority value: a guest module that calls files.read without an FS.Read grant is refused at load time with a named error before any guest code runs.

D-WIT-EXPORT2=A: a Jet component exports against a pinned WIT world, with type pairing and canonical-ABI errors. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter wit_export`, with a UI snapshot for each canonical-ABI error.

Embedded runtime size and call speed (#6386): The runtime a host links for a guest that uses only core.text and core.math is smaller than the Lua 5.4.7 interpreter (329,248 bytes), and 10M host-to-guest calls of a small function finish faster than `lua_pcall` on the equivalent Lua function (Jet/Lua < 1.00). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry embed-runtime` shows no loss.

`jet build --lib` produces the archive and .jet/build/<name>.h. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LibraryOutputs/guest_import_library_calls_native_c_and_cpp_hosts` on every applicable tier, with the `jet build --lib` known-failing rows removed. (was #6418 c35)

A C test compiled against the generated header reads and writes an exported default struct, with no hand-written declaration, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LibraryOutputs/` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #6418 c37)

cards.title: One record index: canonical identity, build verify, safe capture by default in dev, and indexed replay (D-RECORD1=B)
cards.body:
Destination: D-RECORD1=B on the self-hosted toolchain. One index under .jet/records lists every ratified record artifact with one identity key (target inputSha256, tool, engine) and cross-links a proof to the replay it consumed and the receipt it produced; build verify resolves indexed inputs and compares rebuilt output; jet dev captures the safe replay (clock only) on every run within a retention budget; replay resolves indexed IDs and paths.

Why it matters: a failure seen once should be replayable by ID, and a build should be verifiable from its record.

Source: #6386 c121-c124 (from #2506).

criteria.text: The records index and receipt and proof sources use canonical target identity and consumed/produced links, with authenticated admission of sensitive records.
Build verify resolves indexed inputs and compares rebuilt output, with explicit mismatch and error outcomes and native byte identity.
jet dev captures the safe clock replay by default with bounded retention, explicit opt-outs and recorded skipped-capture reasons, measured on a corpus.
Replay resolves indexed IDs and paths, runs saved claims first, handles stale saves and deduplicates, with no backward-stepping implementation added here.

cards.title: Canvas opens any project as one workspace: one resident session, a separate app listener, one project tree and last-good state
cards.body:
Destination: `jet dev --canvas` opens any project, not only a web target, as one workbench. It builds one project graph from package and workspace files, sources and .jet/lock (D-CANVAS-WORKSPACE1=B) and shows it as one semantic project tree (D-CANVAS-WORKSPACE-NAV1=A). Multi-file edits are previewed, checked source transactions (D-CANVAS-WORKSPACE-AUTH1=A). The app server and the Canvas control host have separate listeners but share one resident session (D-CANVAS-SESSION1=A). The control host is Jet-owned, loopback-only, on an OS-chosen port (D-CANVAS-TARGET1=A). Panels receive typed, authorized #DevPanel feeds (D-DX-PLUGIN1=D). A failed rebuild or a disconnect keeps the last good state. Why it matters: Canvas is meant to be the IDE for every kind of Jet project, and it must never take over the app's routes. Scenario proof: `jet run --allow=Env,Exec,FS,IO,Net,Time Tools/canvas-test/Run.jet -- scenario --scenario --port

`, run against a running `jet dev --canvas`, prints PASS. Source: #6618 c15, c45-c50, c52-c54, c69 (from #352, #2169, #2170, #4265).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c10 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: Canvas opens a project graph built from package.jet, workspace files, sources and .jet/lock as one tree of packages, targets, modules, symbols and function graphs (D-CANVAS-WORKSPACE1=B, D-CANVAS-WORKSPACE-NAV1=A). A multi-file edit is one previewed, checked source transaction (D-CANVAS-WORKSPACE-AUTH1=A). With no package, single-file mode is the fallback. Proof: scenario `workspace_project_tree_and_multifile_edit`.
Canvas opens command-line, service, web, native UI, game, library and build projects without `--target=web`. Proof: scenario `opens_every_project_kind`.
Canvas opens the full project IDE before any output is chosen, and project and run selection stay in its normal workspace. Proof: scenario `ide_before_output_choice`.
A project with several valid outputs lists them in the IDE's output launcher, never in a terminal or prelaunch chooser. Proof: scenario `multiple_outputs_in_launcher`.
Canvas, code, graph, designer, preview, terminal, debugger, tests and custom servers all report one session identity and the same accepted source revision. Proof: scenario `one_session_identity`.

A custom app server keeps its own host, port, routes, middleware and reload policy on a listener separate from the Canvas transport. Canvas reserves no application route or middleware namespace (D-CANVAS-SESSION1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebDev/jet_dev_web_status_does_not_expose_canvas_session_data` and scenario `custom_server_separate_listener`.
A failed rebuild keeps the last good preview, graph, debugger state and runtime while the IDE shows diagnostics for the current source. Proof: scenario `failed_rebuild_keeps_last_good`.
A disconnect and reconnect keep the accepted edits, the selected project, the run configuration, the debugger state and the last good program. Proof: scenario `reconnect_preserves_session`.

`jet dev --canvas` runs one resident session with separate listeners and a Jet-owned loopback control host on an OS-chosen port (`--canvas-port` overrides it), and feeds panels typed, authorized #DevPanel events (D-CANVAS-CMD1=A, D-CANVAS-SESSION1=A, D-CANVAS-TARGET1=A, D-DX-PLUGIN1=D). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CanvasCLILifecycle/` and `--filter web_dev/jet_dev_web_exposes_canvas_panel_and_graph`.

The owner's visual review (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)) accepts the workbench as one Unreal-like IDE: project, output, preview, graph, code, diagnostics and run state. Proof: the owner's acceptance is logged on this card against screenshots from scenario `workbench_tour`.

cards.title: Canvas debugs the running program: breakpoints, live values, paused locals and replay on the tier that is actually running
cards.body:
Destination: the Canvas debug overlay works through one seam whose backend is whatever is actually executing (D-CANVAS-DEBUG-UX1=D). Compiled runs use the native jet debug session; under jet dev, the O0 session is used (the old JIT and interpreter tiers are gone). Breakpoints and watches are local and anchored by file hash and source span, and stale anchors become invalid (D-CANVAS-DEBUGSTATE1=A). The overlay shows real values on pins and wires, the active node, the traversed wire, the call stack and the paused locals, and it never presents a cached value as live.

Why it matters: a visual debugger that shows stale or simulated values is worse than none.

Scenario proof: as on #6618.

Source: #6618 c2, c5, c8-c11, c68 (from #273, #983, #984, #6573).

criteria.text: The Canvas debug overlay offers a session selector, breakpoints and watches anchored by file hash and source span, values on pins and wires, an active node and wire pulse, step, resume and stop, a call stack and an execution trace. It is driven by the native session for compiled runs and by the O0 session under jet dev (D-CANVAS-DEBUG-UX1=D, D-CANVAS-DEBUGSTATE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebDev/jet_dev_web_live_canvas_debug_session_round_trip` and `--filter debug/canvas_debug_`.

Setting and clearing a breakpoint on a node, continuing and stepping each work through the production protocol, and the test fails if the gesture path is bypassed. Proof: scenario `breakpoint_gestures`.
At a breakpoint the debugger shows real values, stack frames, the active node and the traversed wire path from the live runtime session. Proof: scenario `debug_values_at_breakpoint`.
The paused frame's locals render with their types and current values through the production protocol. Proof: scenario `debug_paused_locals`.

After source edits move code, breakpoint and value anchors report themselves stale instead of pointing at wrong spans. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/canvas_debug_stop_requires_matching_source_revision_and_tier` and scenario `debug_anchors_go_stale`.
Disconnecting the runtime makes the UI show a disconnected state and present no cached value as live; the test fails if the disconnect path is removed. Proof: scenario `debug_disconnect_not_live`.

A recorded Canvas debug session (run_session_recorded) replays exactly (run_session_replay) through the native O0 image, and the call sites removed from JetDevserver at #6576 c2 are restored against the real functions.

A rejected unsupported continuation leaves the live session and paused state unchanged, and the next valid continuation keeps the same session ID; source-revision and tier mismatches are still refused. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/canvas_debug_stop_requires_matching_source_revision_and_tier` and `--filter debug/canvas_debug_session_replays_one_source_bound_session`. (was #6730 c20)

cards.title: Canvas graph edits write ordinary Jet source: wiring, typed pins, conversions, collapse and extract, and exec-wire reorder
cards.body:
Destination: every Canvas gesture that changes the program writes ordinary Jet source through the one edit-transaction pipeline, with undo, formatter round-trip and reprojection without drift. There is no hidden semantic sidecar or graph asset. Gestures covered: wiring, palette insert, rename, inline edit, promote to binding, control rails, drag-off-pin menus filtered by expected type, visible conversion calls (D-CANVAS-CONVERT1=A), collapse as a view over a source span with extract-to-function (D-CANVAS-COLLAPSE1=A, D-CANVAS-MULTIEXEC1=E), exec-wire reorder and the Details editors.

Why it matters: Canvas is only trustworthy if every edit is plain Jet that a text user can read and diff.

Scenario proof: as on #6618.

Source: #6618 c17, c19, c21, c33, c38-c40 (from #272, #277, #280, #374, #867).

criteria.text: Each of these is one source transaction with undo, a formatter round-trip and reprojection without drift: dragging a wire between compatible pins, inserting a node from the palette or search, breaking or moving a link, renaming a binding, editing an inline expression, promoting a pin to a binding, and creating branch, switch, loop and failure rails. Proof: scenario `structural_write_`.

Dragging off a pin opens a menu filtered by the checker's expected type. An incompatible wire is refused with a Jet error. A compatible but different type inserts a visible conversion call into the source (D-CANVAS-CONVERT1=A). Proof: scenario `typed_pin_authoring`.

Collapsing a selection gives a node that is a view over its source span. Reusable collapse extracts an ordinary helper function whose tunnel pins are its parameters, returns and captures. Inlining runs only where the checker proves it safe and otherwise gives a Jet error. A second exec drop opens the extract preview (D-CANVAS-COLLAPSE1=A, D-CANVAS-MULTIEXEC1=E). Proof: scenario `collapse_extract_inline`.
Dragging an exec-wire endpoint reorders statements behind a diff preview; undo restores the order, and the formatter output is stable. Proof: scenario `exec_wire_reorder`.
Collection and nested-value editors validate input before writing: invalid text is refused with a visible reason and changes zero source bytes. Proof: scenario `details_editor_refuses_invalid`.
Every refusal path (validation error, stale revision, Escape, blur) writes nothing, and undo after a successful apply is exact. Proof: scenario `details_refusal_paths`.
Every rendered Details control has a live apply operation or is absent, and a structural test fails if a dead control is added. Proof: scenario `details_no_dead_controls`.

cards.title: Canvas and the source never disagree: lossless round trips, atomic refusals, one transaction history and converging clients
cards.body:
Destination: source text is the single truth. The graph, edits, undo, diagnostics and saved text stay lossless and mutually consistent through repeated visual and text edits, stale revisions, conflicts and disconnects. Every surface shares one source transaction history (D-CANVAS-SCM1=A stale-edit guard), and two clients editing one file converge.

Why it matters: a projection that silently drifts from the source corrupts programs.

Scenario proof: as on #6618.

Source: #6618 c6, c7, c32, c34-c37, c41, c42, c51, c67 (from #373, #489, #867-#878, #872, #983, #984, #1053-#1057, #2170, #4171).

criteria.text: About 20 core-loop scenarios pass: open, read, insert each category, wire data and exec, edit values, rename, a 20-deep mixed undo, run and output. A random fuzz of 30 operations checks after every step that the projection equals the source. Proof: scenario `core_loop_` and scenario `random_op_fuzz --seed 373`.
Selection, connection compatibility, edits, formatting, undo and redo, and source spans stay stable through repeated visual and text edits. Proof: scenario `mixed_visual_text_edits_stable`.
Ambiguous targets, incompatible wires, stale selections, invalid drops and concurrent source changes are each refused atomically with a recoverable explanation. Proof: scenario `atomic_refusals`.

For every construct, create, inspect, edit, format, undo and reload keep its types, scopes, provenance and canonical Jet spelling. The source, graph, edits, undo, diagnostics and saved text stay lossless and consistent. Proof: scenario `construct_round_trip_` over every projected construct.

Incomplete, ill-typed, ambiguous or stale edits stay recoverable and never emit plausible but different source. Parse errors, conflicting edits, invalid graph operations and failed saves keep the source and undo history with no hidden shadow model. Proof: scenario `bad_edits_recoverable`.
Files, search results, diffs, diagnostics, breakpoints, values and execution state all refer to the same current source revision. Proof: scenario `one_revision_everywhere`.
Stale indexes, moved code, runtime disconnects, large result sets and failed edits stay bounded, report staleness and keep the user's work. Proof: scenario `bounded_and_stale_disclosed`.

All editor surfaces share one source transaction history, with conflict checks, undo, stale-revision refusal and accepted-revision receipts (D-CANVAS-SCM1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CanvasCLILifecycle/jet_dev_canvas_applies_and_refuses_source_transactions` and scenario `one_transaction_history`.
Two clients editing one file at once (text and Canvas) converge to the same source, and node identity survives a rename. Proof: scenario `two_clients_converge`.

Canvas/SchemaApi.jet imports no individual edit operation and matches no edit-operation name; after source selection it crosses one private edit-transaction function. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'EditActions|op_name' -- Compiler/JetDevServer/Source/Canvas/SchemaAPI.jet` prints only the one transaction call. (was #6618 c55)

The edit-transaction module owns request decoding, validation, projection, rewrite, format, compiler check, stale-revision check and atomic commit, and imports no transaction facts from the schema API. Proof: `git grep -n 'SchemaApi' -- Compiler/JetDevServer/Source/Canvas/ProjectTransactions.jet` prints nothing. (was #6618 c56)

Every existing Canvas edit protocol name, schema version, JSON field, error and source result is unchanged through `apply_transaction_json`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CanvasCLILifecycle/jet_dev_canvas_applies_and_refuses_source_transactions`. (was #6618 c57)

Canvas and the dev server find functions and spans from parser nodes, never by scanning source lines. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'split\("\\n"\)|\.lines\(' -- Compiler/JetDevServer/Source/Canvas` prints nothing. (was #6618 c63)
A function whose `fn` keyword follows a marker or comment on the same line appears as a Canvas graph. Proof: scenario `fn_after_marker_on_same_line`. (was #6618 c64)

cards.title: Canvas projects every Jet form: a generated parity table that fails closed, rails, events, traits and tasks
cards.body:
Destination: every Jet language form has a Canvas projection status, generated from the AST forms; a new form without a status fails the test (D-CANVAS-PARITY1=C). Supported forms project to specific nodes with source spans, unsupported ones show a Canvas error with the reason. Rails show control, data, failure, task, effect and unsafe flow; events, traits and tasks project as views over ordinary Jet source. Core calls come from the typed Core action catalog (D-CANVAS-CORECATALOG1=C).

Why it matters: the Blueprint-class editor goal (owner directive 2026-07-02, #182) needs no 'drop to code' cliff.

The repo-wide syntax census on #6898 covers fmt, LSP and Canvas together; this card owns the Canvas rows.

Source: #6618 c16, c18, c20, c23, c25, c26, c28, c29 (from #182, #274, #278, #285, #311, #316, #319, #364).

criteria.text: A parity table generated from the AST item, statement, expression and type forms gives every form a projection, edit and support status (D-CANVAS-PARITY1=C). A new form without a status fails the test, and an unsupported form shows a Canvas error with its reason.

Every supported construct projects to a specific node with a source span on every node and pin, as deterministic JSON with no opaque fallback: methods, structs and enums, bindings, calls, loops, match, failure flow, tasks, effects, modules, unsafe regions, comments and collapsed regions.
Rails render control, data, failure, task, effect, unsafe and debug flow for calls, branches, loops, error propagation, tasks, effects, unsafe regions and tests, as projections that add no semantics.

Event<T> and Hook<T,R> project as emit nodes with payload pins and subscriptions as event-graph entry views. Subscription lifetime is visible, and a delivered/queued/dropped overlay sits on the debug rails; every edit is an ordinary source transaction over core.event (D-CANVAS-EVENT1=D).

A type's graph view shows the traits it implements. Creating an impl writes member stubs. Trait and impl jump to each other. A missing member shows the real Jet error. Trait methods appear in the palette on typed pins.

Spawn, join, channel create, send and receive, and deadline blocks from core.tasks project as palette actions and nodes, and rails show task boundaries and blocking waits, all over ordinary source with no scheduler nodes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Canvas/tasks_projection` on a producer/consumer example.

cards.title: Canvas workbench UX: navigation, a versioned protocol, search and refactor, extension actions, docs on hover and persistent errors
cards.body:
Destination: the Canvas workbench feels like Blueprint. It has full keyboard and pointer navigation and a versioned graph and edit protocol. Search and refactor go through the LSP and SemIndex query engine. Packages can add extension actions that only return edits (D-CANVAS-EXT1=B, D-CANVAS-EXT2=B). The code lens is read-only until an explicit Edit Source mode (D-CANVAS-CODELENS1=C). Actions are intent cards with an expert drawer (D-CANVAS-ACTIONAUTH1=C). Doc comments show as tooltips, errors stay visible, and the Code Map view (D-CODEMAP-VIEW1=A) lives here. Browser tests use the dev-shell Chromium and its CDP driver (D-CANVASTEST1=A).

Why it matters: the visual editor is the product surface beginners meet first.

Scenario proof: as on #6618.

Source: #6618 c1, c3, c4, c22, c24, c27, c30, c31, c70 (from #271, #276, #282, #284, #287, #318, #365, #372, #3868).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c9 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: The workbench supports pan, zoom and zoom-to-fit, a graph picker, breadcrumbs, a minimap, marquee, shift and ctrl selection, dragging nodes and groups, arrow nudge, context menus, a command palette, an inspector, source jump, keyboard focus and accessibility. Desktop and mobile screenshots are nonblank with no layout shift. Proof: scenario `workbench_interactions_`.

The graph and edit JSON protocol is versioned and documented. A no-op edit round-trips, a stale edit is refused, and unknown fields are forward compatible, all checked by snapshot tests. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CanvasCLILifecycle/jet_dev_canvas_serves_status_page_session_graph_and_source` and `--filter canvas/protocol_`.

Find in graph, project search, find references, rename, source-to-graph and graph-to-source jump, and refactor preview all use the LSP and SemIndex query engine, with stale-transaction handling. Proof: scenario `search_refactor_nav`.

A package declares ordinary Jet action functions with `canvas.action` authority (D-CANVAS-EXT1=B, D-CANVAS-EXT2=B). Canvas runs them through the checked compile path, and an action returns a CanvasEdit, source diff or error and cannot write files itself.

The code lens is read-only by default, and an explicit Edit Source mode uses the same transaction pipeline (D-CANVAS-CODELENS1=C). Pin and signature controls, context menus filtered by pin type, built-in and action search, and nested function editing all work. Proof: scenario `blueprint_ux_`.
Doc comments from the source render as node and pin tooltips, pin types link to their docs, and a dismissible first-run tour keeps only local state. Proof: scenario `node_doc_hover`.
Run, Check and Build show as intent cards whose expert drawer gives the exact command, grants, touched files and outputs (D-CANVAS-ACTIONAUTH1=C). Proof: scenario `action_intent_cards`.

A failed transaction shows the full Jet error (what, why, fix) in a persistent panel until dismissed. Check runs into a results panel with jump-to-node, and nodes with errors carry hoverable error bubbles. Proof: scenario `error_surfacing_`.

The Code Map view in Canvas (D-CODEMAP-VIEW1=A) draws a treemap of the code-map rows with every metric plus Blend, all four border choices, click-to-source and zoom. Rectangles update live in the dev loop, and a saved --json snapshot opens in the same view. First-render and hover latency on Compiler/ are logged. A test proves that sizes, colours and hover values come unchanged from the --json rows. The owner's acceptance of the visual design is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Canvas edit actions read fallibility, defaults and submodule membership from the shared Core-call record (the typed Core action catalog, D-CANVAS-CORECATALOG1=C). Proof: scenario `core_action_catalog_facts`. (was #6618 c43)

The 88 canvas scenarios deleted with Tools/CanvasTest/scenario.mjs in the #6035 c3 cutover (last commit logged on this card) are restored, each keeping its assertions and messages, as the original driver or as Tools/CanvasTest/Harness.jet scenarios. Proof: every scenario passes on the running canvas (`jet run Tools/CanvasTest/Run.jet -- scenario --scenario N` for each ported N, or the restored driver for the rest). (was #6618 c66)

cards.title: Named previews in Canvas from ordinary core.ui values (D-DX-PREVIEW1=A)
cards.body:
Destination: a source file registers named preview scenarios through ordinary core.ui values and functions, with no new syntax (D-DX-PREVIEW1=A). Canvas renders each variant's normal UiNode tree, runs shared fixtures once, isolates variants, and keeps the last good preview when one breaks; a playground path runs the same checked source through Canvas and `jet dev`.

Why it matters: previewing UI states side by side is how UI work gets fast.

Source: #6618 c58-c62 (from #2464).

criteria.text: Named previews register through ordinary core.ui values and functions with no new syntax, and D-DX-PREVIEW1=A's declaration, variant and shared-context rules hold.
A source file renders two named variants in Canvas, and switching variants neither restarts the app nor changes another variant's output.
Expensive fixture setup runs once for several variants, and changing one preview leaks no mutable state into another.
A malformed preview reports source errors while the last good preview stays visible.
A playground path runs the same checked source through Canvas and `jet dev`, with output and console errors tied to the source revision.

No private list of Core members remains in Compiler/JetDevServer/Source/Canvas: every Core name comes from the shared Core-call record. Proof: review of `git grep -n -E '"(push|len|insert|remove|get)"' -- Compiler/JetDevServer/Source/Canvas` finds no member table. (was #6618 c44)

cards.title: Stops show where they happened: compile-time stop trails, panic traces on every tier, and one division-by-zero and list-position stop
cards.body:
Destination: every stop names where it happened and how execution got there.
- A compile-time stop points at its `panic` and lists every compile-time call, innermost first, in the same Trail format runtime failures print. In a derive or marker body it names both the body line and the use site.
- A runtime panic prints its frames innermost first on O0, O1 and O2, as `backtrace: full|brief|off` selects.
- A zero divisor for `/`, `/%` and `%` gives one shared E3010 stop.
- Every list-position stop goes through one message owner.

Why it matters: learnability probes t04 and t06 found stops that point at the wrong place or print no path.

State: tests/cases/runtime_stops/every_division_by_zero_stops_at_its_line passes on dev 104ee83c5a with gate-p141. It pins the shared stop and its line on all three tiers, and it asserts that no source line is quoted.

Source: #3720 c31-c35, c41, c44 (from #6398, #6399, #4627).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c6, c8 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: t04_comptime_panic.jet gets one E3010 whose primary location is the `panic` call at line 4, with a second label on the `check_size(400)` call at line 10.
A compile-time stop three calls deep lists every compile-time call, innermost first, in the same Trail format runtime failures print.
A compile-time stop inside a derive or marker body names the line inside that body and the use site that ran it.

t06_panic_trace.jet prints the panic, then `inner` (line 4), `middle` (line 9), `outer` (line 13) and `run` (line 17), each with its file and line and innermost first. This holds under `jet run` and under `jet build` with the stock `backtrace: full`, on O0, O1 and O2.
`backtrace: brief` prints only the panicking frame and `backtrace: off` prints none, and a failed `assert` and `assert_eq` follow the same rule.

`/`, `/%` and `%` with a zero divisor at run time all give the same E3010 'divided by zero' stop with the division's file, line and column and a caret under the divisor, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter RuntimeStops/every_division_by_zero_stops_at_its_line`. On dev 104ee83c5a it passes for the shared stop and the line; the column and caret are owed; whether a stop quotes the line with a caret is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Every list-position stop site calls one shared message owner. Proof: `git grep -n 'is out of range (length ' -- Compiler` lists only that owner (on dev 104ee83c5a it finds two sites, Dyn.jet:599 and :877).
An E3001 panic report shows the 1-based column, and it quotes the source excerpt if the c6 ballot (Main's ballot list, 2026-11-15) keeps quoting.

A stop raised inside Core names the caller's file and line, not a Core location, and a failed #Pre reports as its own contract stop, not as E3001. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter RuntimeStops/core_stop_names_caller` and `--filter runtime_stops/pre_failure_is_a_contract_stop`.

A #Test whose body stops (a failed check, a panic, a cancelled task) reports that stop as its own failure on O0, O1 and O2, never a lost edge or a pass. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TestRunner/stop_is_test_failure_`, one case per stop kind. (was #3239 c63)

cards.title: A handled Core error prints and names its type: ParseError is declared, and {err}, {err:Debug}, err.message and the E0915 and E0112 fixes all work
cards.body:
Destination: inside a `??` handler, a Core error value such as Int.parse's ParseError has a declaration a program can name. It prints with `{err}` and `{err:Debug}`, and `err.message` works, on O0, O1 and O2. The fixes E0915 and E0112 suggest for such values compile.

Why it matters: G5DevX-2 found on 2026-11-13 that `{err}` gives E0915, `{err:Debug}` gives E0112 and `err.message` gives E0302, so a learner cannot even print the error they caught.

Source: #3720 c47, c49, c84 (from #3703).

criteria.text: Int.parse's error type, ParseError, has a declaration in Core, so a `??` handler can name it. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Errors/parse_error_named_in_handler` on O0, O1 and O2.
Inside a `??` handler, `{err}`, `{err:Debug}` and `err.message` all render a Core error value on O0, O1 and O2.

The fixes suggested by E0915 and E0112 never propose a spelling that fails for the same value, and each suggested fix compiles. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0915_fix_compiles` and `--filter E0112_fix_compiles`.

cards.title: Progress and errors never tear: one bottom status region on a terminal, plain sequential output elsewhere
cards.body:
Destination: realization progress (jetpack env, jet build) renders in one bottom-anchored status region, and errors print atomically above it through one writer. Non-TTY, NO_COLOR and CI output is plain and sequential, with no cursor movement.

Why it matters: torn progress lines mid-error were seen in a real session. The Rust-era fix (#2215) went with the Rust code and is unproven on the self-hosted toolchain.

Source: #3720 c68, c69 (from #2215).

criteria.text: Realization progress renders in a single bottom-anchored status region, and errors print atomically above it with no interleaved or torn lines. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIOutput/progress_region_no_torn_lines` (pty).
Non-TTY, NO_COLOR and CI runs use the plain sequential fallback, and a test asserts no ANSI cursor movement in that mode.

cards.title: Debug info tells the truth: lldb, gdb and perf show Jet names, real values and inlined frames, and no local before its binding
cards.body:
Destination: the DWARF and symbol tables the native backend emits let any debugger show what the Jet program holds:
- Jet function names.
- Bignum Int, String, struct, list and Decimal locals by value.
- No local before its binding runs: each location range starts at the binding.
- Inlined frames and live locals in O2 builds.
- O2 split debug files found through the debug link.

Why it matters: release a0_041's `jet debug Examples/Tooling/Debugging/Debug.jet` printed `a = 4262344   s = <unavailable>` at its first stop, which is uninitialized memory shown as a Jet value.

G5DevX-2 found on 2026-11-13, with lldb on PATH: debug/ 13 PASS, 11 KF, 6 FAIL; the debugger stops, but locals read `<Unavailable>`.

Source: #6730 c1, c2, c5, c6, c8, c9, c26, c27 (from #6738, #6739, #6742, #6745, #6271, Docs/audits/2026-11-14-debugging-profiling-review.md).

log.text: OWNER ORDER 2026-11-15 ~13:10: one goal agent slot does Jet's native debugger, profiler and perf (G5: #6730 jet debug, #4632 jet perf, #6918 debug info, #6841, #6919), native only with no lldb, gdb or Linux perf dependency. The G9 slot (GoalsB-5-2) takes it after its returned fixes; G9 is unstaffed until an agent snowballs past G6. Owner: GoalsB-5-2 (Pareto order 6730, 4632, 6918, 6841, 6919).

Owner direction (2026-11-15, chat): debugging and profiling are native Jet. jet debug and jet perf do the work themselves and depend on no external tool such as lldb, gdb or Linux perf. External tools serve only as comparators (as in #6730 c29) or as optional interop for users who bring them. Each value this card wants lldb to show (bignum, String, struct, list, Decimal locals, binding ranges, inlined frames, Jet names) must first show truthfully in jet debug and jet perf, from Jet's own debug facts. The lldb/gdb/perf proofs here are interop checks only, and must not be the only proof of a criterion. When this card is worked, the criteria get a native jet debug proof beside or in place of the lldb one.

criteria.text: A bignum Int local shows its value, not its tagged pointer word. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/bignum_local_shows_value` with lldb on PATH.

String, struct, list and Decimal locals render their values, because the DWARF types them as what they are, not Opaque, Aggregate or void*. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/locals_render_string_struct_list_decimal` with lldb on PATH.
lldb finds an O2 build's split debug file under .jet/symbols through the binary's debug link.
Bounds stops (E3010) name the faulting function and show its locals, like every other stop report.

No local is shown before its binding runs: each local's DWARF range starts at its binding, not at function entry. The stale 'generated Rust' comments in Examples/Tooling/Debugging (Debug.jet, DebugNative.jet, PanicReport.jet) are corrected. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/local_not_shown_before_binding`, and `git grep -n -i 'generated Rust' -- Examples/Tooling/Debugging` prints nothing.

lldb on an -O2 jet build shows inlined frames and prints at least the live locals of a probe. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/o2_inlined_frames_and_live_locals` (SKIP-HOST without lldb).

The case gate runs with the dev shell's lldb on PATH, so debug/ rows are not SKIP-HOST, and break_then_continue_stops_at_breakpoint, native_breakpoint_reads_a_jet_local, next_line_takes_a_breakpoint and loop_next_edges_are_line_mapped pass. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/` with lldb on PATH has no FAIL outside named known-failing rows.
The symbol table carries Jet names for functions, so lldb, perf and gdb show Jet names.

Breakpoints, frames and values refer to the accepted revision. Inspection never changes the guest or grants authority, and the script and library_loadable guest matrix runs with lldb present, without skip. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/` with lldb on PATH. (was #6730 c21)

cards.title: jet debug steps backward: record and replay, watch-aware reverse navigation and checked fix-and-continue (D-TIMETRAVEL2)
cards.body:
Destination: `jet debug --record=r1 prog.jet` and then `jet debug --replay=r1` step backward and answer 'where was this value last set' (D-TIMETRAVEL2). Recorded histories keep per-sequence write transitions; replay navigates indexed retained events without re-executing; and a transactional fix checks its inputs, candidate and checkpoint before installation. Every route (native and DAP) refuses unsupported, stale, empty-history and invalid-watch requests with a source error.

Why it matters: pdb and the Node inspector cannot step back. Reverse debugging is a headline Jet tool.

Related: the record index is #6907.

Source: #6730 c15-c19, c24 (from #2463, #4720 c10).

log.text: OWNER ORDER 2026-11-15 ~13:10: one goal agent slot does Jet's native debugger, profiler and perf (G5: #6730 jet debug, #4632 jet perf, #6918 debug info, #6841, #6919), native only with no lldb, gdb or Linux perf dependency. The G9 slot (GoalsB-5-2) takes it after its returned fixes; G9 is unstaffed until an agent snowballs past G6. Owner: GoalsB-5-2 (Pareto order 6730, 4632, 6918, 6841, 6919).

criteria.text: `jet debug --record=r1 prog.jet` and then `jet debug --replay=r1` step backward and answer 'where was this value last set' with file:line (D-TIMETRAVEL2).

The debugger offers forward and reverse navigation, bounded Jet-path watches and explicit fix commands through the live, native and replay routes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/navigation_watches_fix_` on the native and DAP routes.
Recorded histories keep per-sequence write transitions and watch-aware forward and reverse navigation, and a live watch change refreshes its baseline.
Replay navigation uses indexed retained events and never re-executes the program.
A transactional fix checks unchanged inputs, a checked candidate bundle, and the checkpoint's type, layout and authority before it installs.
Unsupported, stale, empty-history and invalid-watch requests each get an explicit source error on the native and DAP routes.

Watch expressions are parsed by the compiler's parser, and no second watch-expression parser remains in Compiler/JetDebug. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/watch_expression_uses_compiler_parser`. (was #6730 c10)

Breakpoints, stepping, frames, variables, async tasks, optimized code, errors and source locations keep their Jet-level meaning across the platform matrix through the production DAP wire. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/dap_cli_` (known-failing on #6730 today). (was #6730 c13)

Stale binaries, optimized-away values, process exit, attach denial, signal or exception storms and disconnect each end cleanly with an honest state, including attach, pause, restart and raw-frame refusal over DAP (E2236). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/dap_cli_`. (was #6730 c14)

`jet debug prog.jet --break file:line` stops there, prints locals with their types, and steps over and into, and `jet debug --dap` drives the same session from VS Code. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/break_then_continue_stops_at_breakpoint` and `--filter debug/dap_cli_`. (was #6730 c23)

Compiler/JetDebug checks clean as a package and its DAP tests run, which unblocks #6187 C1 (E2231-E2239 rows with runner-produced snapshots). Proof: `jet check Compiler/JetDebug` exits 0 with no problems, and `jet test Compiler/JetDebug` runs its DAP tests. On 2026-11-14 the check gave 0 errors with gate-p66 at 7700a065ff; the DAP tests have not run yet. (was #6730 c25)

jet debug's DAP supports conditional breakpoints, logpoints and evaluate (Docs/Audits/2026-11-14-debugging-profiling-review.md). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/dap_conditional_breakpoints_logpoints_evaluate`. (was #6730 c28)

The debugger event-observation behaviours the deleted Rust tests covered have Jet cases: only executed, redacted sync and hook facts; pressure drop, failure, close and single terminals; exact async registration and once-removal; a bounded runtime event sequence the debugger preserves exactly. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter EventObservations/`. (was #6730 c30)

cards.title: The Rust-era lint checks exist again under D-NO-WARNINGS1: each is a tidy error, a jet fmt rewrite or a jet lint report, with exact spans
cards.body:
Destination: every lint check that the Rust checker had and the Jet checker lacks exists again in the form D-NO-WARNINGS1=A gives it:
- a tidy error (listed by jet check and jet build, never stopping jet run, jet dev or jet test);
- a `jet fmt` rewrite; or
- a `jet lint` report.

Each comes with paired positive and negative fixtures and reports its construct's own span.

Why it matters: these checks caught real bugs, and their ui fixtures still expect them.

Related: #6858 (no L code stays active as a warning; it owns the form each code takes) and #6895 (new likely-bug checks).

Source: #6425 c15-c23 (from #3919, #4111, #3920-#3922, #3716, #3734, #3554, #4207).

criteria.text: L0501-L0506 and L0508-L0510 (L0507 is #3681's) each exist as a tidy error, a `jet fmt` rewrite or a `jet lint` report (D-NO-WARNINGS1=A), with paired positive and negative fixtures. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter UILint/L050` and `--filter ui_lint/L0510`.

L0511-L0520 each exist as a tidy error, a `jet fmt` rewrite or a `jet lint` report, with paired positive and negative fixtures. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter UILint/L051` and `--filter ui_lint/L0520`.

L0521-L0531 and L2510 each exist as a tidy error, a `jet fmt` rewrite or a `jet lint` report, with paired positive and negative fixtures. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter UILint/L052`, `--filter ui_lint/L053` and `--filter ui_lint/L2510`.

The unused-name checks (L0103, L0104, L0105) are package-aware, and alias use from an impl head counts as a use. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter unused_import_package_aware` and `--filter unused_alias_in_impl_head`.
L0301 exists as a tidy error with fixtures, and L0302 follows the state-machine design gate on #6326 c4.

L0202, L0206, L0207, L1101 and L1141 each exist as a tidy error, a `jet fmt` rewrite or a `jet lint` report, with fixtures. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter UILint/L020` and `--filter ui_lint/L11`.

An `else` arm after exhaustive arms (L0303) gets a safe delete edit, and open-set and non-exhaustive matches stay quiet. The E0307 fix names the missing arms, and pattern_matching.jet and the other triggers are migrated. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter else_after_exhaustive` and `--filter E0307`.
Each lint reports its construct's own span: L0507 on comment, lambda and end-of-file shapes; L0530 on a non-return final call; L0528 never on loop reassignment; no lint located in Core sources.
one_shot_mut_adjacent is reported once as a registered tidy error with no machine edit, and read-between, capture, later-write and loop cases stay quiet.
A write to a local after an escaping lambda copied it is a registered tidy error, and read-only captures are quiet.

L0514 skips bodies a derive generates: a #CLI program with three or more options checks with no L0514 on `__r`, `__n` or `__command`, while a user-written function of the same three-guard shape in that file still gets exactly one L0514. The skip keys on the derive origin the compiler records on the function, not on the binding name.
JetSema reports the #Test scope and test-runner rules the Rust checker had (#3899). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter test_scope_`. (was #6425 c9)

`assert_eq(x, None)` gets its registered error, and L0528 does not fire on generated bodies (#3903). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter assert_eq_none` and `--filter L0528_generated`. (was #6425 c11)

The paired fixtures of six written ports pass: #3887 E0433, #3896 Display and Debug interpolation checks, #3910 module-graph errors, #3957 test, fuzz and coverage harness artifacts, #3979 Shared owner methods, and #3981 core.encoding and edition binding. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0433` and the named fixtures of each port, run with gate-p141 or newer. (was #6425 c12)
The remaining effect-system codes for package purity, determinism and policy are reported on the fixture matrix. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter effect_policy_`. (was #6425 c13)
JetSema reports the task detach and freeze rules the Rust checker had (#3900). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter task_detach_` and `--filter task_freeze_`. (was #6425 c24)
JetSema reports doctest E2901 (#3905). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E2901`. (was #6425 c25)
Pattern coverage checks nested patterns beyond single-slot payloads, as #3904 required. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter nested_pattern_coverage`. (was #6425 c26)
JetSema reports the serde errors E2408, E2414 and E2415 (#3907). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E2408`, `--filter E2414` and `--filter E2415`. (was #6425 c27)

cards.title: Impact and hierarchy views agree with the checked graph: body-only versus signature edits, identity, scope and provenance
cards.body:
Destination: the impact, navigation and hierarchy views in the CLI and the LSP derive from the checked graph and agree with it. A body-only edit and a public signature change give separately checkable checker-work and dependency results. Definition identity, snapshot, build identity, target scope and provenance agree across views. Imported, generated and external nodes keep their origins. Unsupported modes say so instead of returning complete-looking empty results.

Why it matters: the retired Rust tests structure_fact_plane::three_module_projections_match_checked_facts and lsp::impact_and_hierarchy_match_checked_graph pinned this. Their Jet replacements do not exist yet.

Source: #6630 c9-c16 (from #3191).

criteria.text: On a three-module fixture, a representation-only body change and a public signature change produce separately checkable checker-work and semantic-dependency results, and neither is labelled complete runtime reachability.
Definition identity, source snapshot, build identity, target scope and static-versus-observed provenance agree across the CLI and LSP views.

Type and implementation navigation and the call and type hierarchy views keep the same declaration relationships as the checked graph, before and after the body-only and signature edits, and no passive label contradicts them. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_type_hierarchy_trait_impls` and `--filter semindex/hierarchy_matches_checked_graph`.
Static, live and replay results each keep their own observation scope, and an unsupported mode returns an explicit status, never an empty complete-looking result.
Imported, generated and external nodes keep their origins and exclusions, and an unknown scope is explicit.
Impact reports record the exact command, binary and input hashes and payloads they came from.
The typed build-graph query agrees with the CLI build graph on nodes, dependencies and provenance.

A type dossier query returns its status envelope in JSON and text forms, with members sorted as semindex_sort_members did (old SemIndex/Queries.jet:138, Facts.jet:114, Codec/Dossier.jet:9-141, Queries.jet:196-206), and JetLSP's Tests/Integration/SemindexTests.jet dossier tests (lines 79, 157 and 564-599) pass. Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetLSP --filter Semindex`. (was #6630 c1)

A structural audit lists added, removed and changed declarations between two indexes (old Queries.jet:172 structural_audit, :217 semindex_structural_signature). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/structural_audit`. (was #6630 c2)

package_facts_for_entry, E1215, the overlay policy and the E1202 stale-lock check work (old Queries.jet:76,83, Open.jet:58-128), and SemIndexJSON.jet stops writing null for package facts. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/package_facts_and_stale_lock`. (was #6630 c3)
An index opens over unsaved editor overlays (old Entry.jet:23-96, Open.jet:146-185). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/open_over_overlays`. (was #6630 c4)

The query API offers derivation windows, invalidate_derivations, references_to, call_sites, effect_of, lookup and lookup_identity (old Queries.jet:54-134). Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetSemIndex --filter query_api`. (was #6630 c5)

The LSP symbol database and hover come back: build_symbol_db, propagation hints, state-graph hovers, the inferred hover tail and breadcrumb hints (old Finalize.jet:64-299, Structure.jet:427). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_hover_projects_typestate_graph_facts` and `--filter semindex/state_symbols_keep_their_struct_owner`. (was #6630 c6)

Semantic blame (old Receipts/SemanticOps.jet:265,281) is reachable from a jet command. Dropping it instead needs a ratified decision first. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/semantic_blame`. (was #6630 c7)

The doc graph takes native paths (as the old Docs/Graph.jet:21 DocSource with OsPath did) instead of String paths. Proof: `git grep -n 'path: String' -- Compiler/JetSemIndex/Source/Docs` prints nothing, and `jet test Compiler/JetSemIndex --filter doc_graph` passes. (was #6630 c8)
A search by effect returns the functions that hold that authority. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/search_by_effect`. (was #6630 c17)
A search by input/output example returns candidates and shows why each matched. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Semindex/search_by_example`. (was #6630 c18)

cards.title: A notebook becomes a local app: `jet notebook --app` serves cells and controls from the running kernel, with isolated tabs and live edits
cards.body:
Destination: `jet notebook --app` starts a loopback server. It renders the notebook's cell outputs, layouts and controls from the running notebook kernel, with no second evaluator. Each browser tab has its own typed session state. Edits under `jet dev` update the running app and keep the state whose type did not change. A machine-readable receipt names the bind address, sharing, data reads and trust grants.

Why it matters: marimo and Streamlit users turn notebooks into apps. Jet does it from the same checked kernel.

Depends on the notebook kernel, #6619.

Source: #6619 c11-c14 (split 2026-11-15).

criteria.text: `jet notebook --app` starts a loopback server that renders the notebook's cell outputs, layouts and controls from the running notebook kernel, with no second evaluator.
Two browser tabs on one notebook app get separate typed session state, run callbacks in a fixed order, and reset or reconnect independently; one tab cannot read or change the other's state.
Editing the notebook or one of its typed functions under `jet dev` updates the running app, keeps state whose type did not change, and names the reason when it resets state or shows a stale output.
The notebook app binds to loopback only unless sharing is asked for, and prints a machine-readable receipt of its bind address, sharing, data it reads and trust grants.

Editing a defining cell reruns only its pure transitive dependents automatically, records the dependency order, and marks effectful dependents for confirmation, labeling skipped work stale (D-DX-CELLS1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/shared_session_identical_stale_rules_across_clients`. (was #6619 c1)

A typed function argument renders as a validated control, and changing the control reruns the affected cells, while invalid input keeps an explicit error state. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/notebook_typed_argument_control`. (was #6619 c2)

Deleting a defining cell scrubs its bindings and invalidates the dependent outputs, and an old cached value is never shown as current. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/notebook_declarations_are_file_wide_but_state_cells_stay_ordered`. (was #6619 c3)

Closing and reopening the browser reconnects to the same bounded kernel only when the source and build identity and the authority checks pass, and an unauthorized reconnect is rejected with a registered error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/headless_protocol_interrupt_stdin_debug_perf_and_clients`. (was #6619 c4)

Text, HTML, SVG and table results stay attached to their cell, imported output stays quarantined, and exports report any semantics they drop. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/jetnb_cache_merge_ipynb_and_jet_export_never_hide_loss`. (was #6619 c5)

A `.jetnb` file holds only source and cell markers; outputs are recomputed when the notebook runs and are not stored between runs, and editing one cell changes only that cell's lines in `git diff`. Proof: a Tests/Cases notebook row under `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jetnb`. (was #6619 c6)

A Jupyter kernel adapter runs Jet cells: a scripted `jupyter nbconvert --execute` of a three-cell notebook passes where Jupyter is installed and is SKIP-HOST with a reason elsewhere. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/jupyter_kernel_runs_three_cells`. (was #6619 c7)

`jet run nb.jetnb` and `jet build nb.jetnb` print the same output as running every cell in order, and a corpus of 20 notebooks reruns from a clean state with identical output 20 of 20 times. For comparison, 4% of Jupyter notebooks reproduce, and marimo cannot build a native binary. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/run_and_build_match_cell_order` and `--filter notebook/corpus_reruns_identically`. (was #6619 c8)

Editing one cell of a 10-cell notebook reruns only its dependents and shows the new output sooner than marimo does on the equivalent notebook (Jet time over marimo time below 1.00). Proof: a committed measurement under Docs/Audits with both timings and the commands. (was #6619 c9)

cards.title: Moves never copy: field, parameter, pattern, destructure and task-capture moves lower to moves in JetIR
cards.body:
Destination: every move the checker decides (a last use, a written `x.move()`, a destructure of an owned temporary, a pattern payload binding, a task argument or capture) lowers to a move in JetIR on O0, O1 and O2, and no copy appears without a sema decision.

Why: a hidden copy costs time and memory, and it breaks D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (the compiler chooses moves when unmarked; `x.copy()` is the only way to ask for a copy). Returning several results must cost no more than output parameters (D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A). The copy ledger and the zero-unjustified-copy guard live on #3836; this card fixes the lowering that makes copies the checker never asked for.

Source: map #5989 (board consolidation 2026-10-28), carrying folded cards #4562 (task moves, SP13), #4564 (stage-2 copy gaps), #4567 (frozen; destructure copies), #4569 (linear copy residues), #4916 (field moves), #5821 (task capture lifetime), #5031 (pattern payload copies) and #5041 (no implicit copies).

criteria.text: `s.f.move()` and moves out of struct fields and parameters lower to a move in JetIR, with no clone, and the clone-gate copies the old FieldMove lowering added are removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/field_and_param_move_no_clone` on O0, O1 and O2.

Destructuring an owned temporary (`(program, values) := returned_tuple()`, or a returned struct) moves every field on every tier, with no clone of the fields (D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A; frozen #4567 holds the original report). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/destructure_returned_tuple_moves_fields` and a paired cell against output parameters.
Pattern payload bindings of owned locals and parameters move at the last use or alias under a stable root, never deep-copy the payload.

Task arguments are moved or borrowed exactly as the sema decision says, and typed lists of tasks lower to the right types. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Tasks/` passes, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/task_args_follow_sema_decision` shows no clone without a decision.

When a task body moves a captured value out or drops it, the closure environment no longer keeps it alive. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/task_capture_moved_out_frees`, where a task moves out a large captured value and then allocates as much again, and peak RSS stays below twice the value's size.

The three linear copy residues in Compiler/ (the L1 payload copy, element leftovers and the ref-binding move) use the sema copy decisions, so no copy appears without one. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/linear_copy_residues` and a lower copy count from `jet inspect choices` over the self-hosted compiler.
The about 64 remaining dead parameter copies at O1 are gone. Proof: the entry-clone count from `jet inspect choices` over the self-hosted compiler is 0 (receipt with command and count).

A `#Static` fixed array is one shared addressable constant, so a hot loop over it (the SHA-256 K table) emits no array copy. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/static_array_loop_no_copy` on O1 and O2.
The stage-2 copy-work repros for E0204, E0320 and the false L0102 are each accepted or rejected as the Jet spec says, each with its own UI snapshot.

D-RESOURCE-REASSIGN1=A: once a replacement value is ready, the displaced owner is released before the next statement, the next statement observes the released owner, and a surviving alias keeps its provider alive until its final owner ends; the ratified sample prints false, true, true, true. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/d_resource_reassign1_contract` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #5989 c21)

cards.title: Plain data is freed in one step: root regions and no exit teardown
cards.body:
Destination: dropping plain data (no Close, consume or scrub duty) is O(1) at its last use. Trees and lists of plain data are allocated from a region owned by their root or phase, so releasing the root frees the region in one step. At process exit, plain memory is not torn down; only values with duties (files, locks, connections, flush and commit protocols) still close.
