`jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes the PackageModel claims of #3611–#3615 (FFI and C binders, language binders). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter PackageModel`. (was #3590 c25)

cards.title: User Rust crates in native programs: offline cargo, builds inside packages, foreign panics as stops, and undo hooks
cards.body:
Destination: a native Jet program uses a user Rust crate (D-FFI-RUST1=A, D-FFI-RUSTIMPORT1=A): cargo metadata forwards only CARGO_NET_OFFLINE, extern rust builds inside a package, a foreign panic stops as E3014 with one Jet source frame, and #Undo inverses of extern rust calls run with distinct identities across modules.

Source: #6366 c6 and c15, plus its known-failing rows for transact_ffi_with_undo and cross_module_foreign_undo_bindings. E3014 must be registered again with its emitter (2026-11-12 log on #6366).

criteria.text: Native user-Rust FFI: cargo metadata forwards only CARGO_NET_OFFLINE (the hosted path forwards all ambient CARGO_*).
extern rust builds inside a package (base64 prints aGk=).

A foreign panic stops with exit 70 as Stop [E3014] --> ffi.jet:7, and E3014 is registered with its emitter and a UI snapshot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DiagnosticsCoverage/ffi_runtime_stop_keeps_one_jet_source_frame` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E3014`.

The #Undo inverse of an extern rust call runs on rollback (prints `undo 3`), and two modules' undo bindings keep distinct identities. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Effects/transact_ffi_with_undo_registers_rollback_hook` and `--filter effects/cross_module_foreign_undo_bindings_keep_distinct_identities`.

cards.title: `jet generate` runs a checked #Job generator explicitly, previews and applies writes atomically, and records a reproducible receipt
cards.body:
Destination: D-DX-GENERATE1=A is built. A #Job with `generates:` and `inputs:` metadata is a source generator; `jet generate <Job>` previews and `--apply` writes every declared output atomically after an authority check; build and test never run generation; an unchanged plan gives an identical receipt.

Why: generated source must be reviewable and reproducible, never a hidden build side effect.

Source: #3693 c14-c18 (carried from #2442). Decision: D-DX-GENERATE1=A (reuse #Job for generators).

criteria.text: `jet generate --help` describes the explicit invocation, preview mode, authority requirements and receipt output.

An explicit `jet generate <Job> --apply` writes the declared outputs in deterministic order and records generator identity, source location, inputs, outputs, package authority and toolchain provenance.
Repeated generation with unchanged inputs is reproducible and rewrites no equivalent output, while changed inputs give a receipt naming the affected outputs.
Build and test never invoke source generation, and a missing or stale generated input is reported as an actionable source-local error rather than silently repaired.
A generator failure leaves no partial outputs, and the audit trail records the failed command, authority decision and source context without exposing unauthorized environment data.
Every jetpack_tasks case passes and its known-failing rows are removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/`. (was #3693 c4)

A built binary dispatches the same jobs with the same output as `jet jobs`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/jet_build_job_dispatch_matches_default_and_interpreter`. (was #3693 c5)

The built binary runs `after:` predecessors in order, stops on a failing predecessor, refuses a bad root argument with E1331 (exit 2) before any predecessor runs, and prints byte-identical output to `jet jobs` and `jet run`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/jet_jobs_after_runs_predecessors_and_scalar_args`. (was #3693 c6)

`jet jobs web --port 3000` forwards `--port` to the job while global flags stay with jet and `--` forwards, typed job arguments parse from argv, and reserved job names fail with E0928. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/jet_top_jobs_forward_flags_after_name`, `--filter jetpack_tasks/jet_run_job_typed_cli_args` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0928`. (was #3693 c7)

Job graphs, authority context, working directories and arguments are validated before any job effect runs, with a failure-path case per check. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/validates_before_effects_`. (was #3693 c11)

Declared input and output freshness, dependency invalidation, per-job working directories and affected-subgraph watch work together. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/freshness_and_watch_`. (was #3693 c12)

Job dependency, status, inspection and the canonical lifecycle events use the one process and job identity model, with no second model. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/inspection_and_events_`. (was #3693 c13)

`jet <job>` runs a project job by name before retired words, paths and path plugins are considered, and an unknown name suggests the project's jobs. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/top_level_jobs_precede_retired_words_paths_and_path_plugins` and `--filter jetpack_tasks/jet_top_job_runs_by_name_and_unknown_suggests_jobs`. (was #3693 c20)

An executable example sets STAGE=prod through ProcessSpec.env on launched commands, with golden output on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter ProcessSpecEnv`. (was #3693 c21)

Every generator is listed in one generator registry with a `--check` mode and one implementation, and the lander runs every check as a gate, so a generated file cannot drift (architecture review Repo1; census F20, F21). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter generators_fresh` runs each registered generator's `--check` and passes. (was #5073 c2)

Every generated registry table (CoreEnumRows, CoreStructureRows and the rest) comes from `b.generate` over its source registry, so it cannot be stale, and the precommit generator checks for those tables are deleted. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter generated_tables_from_build` and no precommit generator check for those tables remains. (was #6682 c2)

cards.title: The gauntlet scores every cell by one peer law: in-group Jet/peer below 1.00 per metric, AOT against systems peers, run and dev against Python and JS, tiers as context only
cards.body:
Destination: the gauntlet harness, its status projection, the integrated gate and the Tower view apply one comparison law. AOT builds are scored against Rust, C, Zig and Go; `jet run` and `jet dev` are scored separately against Python and JavaScript; Node, Bun and Vite stay required web-development comparisons against `jet dev`; the main chart has one JS column and no Node or expert columns; the four peer tiers (scripting, managed, systems, ceiling) are reporting context only.

Why: a speed claim is only as honest as its comparator. A missing, mismatched or averaged result must never pass, and an out-of-group comparison must never block.

Decisions and rulings: AGENTS.md performance gate (Jet/peer < 1.00 with no Rust band, then Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 against Tools/perf/asm-parity); owner directions 2026-09-14 (group split, one JS column, hide expert columns) and 2026-11-08 (four tiers); D-PERF-RUNCELL2=A (the `jet run` wait is gated against Lua, LuaJIT, Python and Node), which supersedes D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B. Historical receipts are immutable.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; carries the merged #3404 harness-split criteria.

log.text: Owner instruction 2026-09-03: criteria that only need a measurement, census, suite or review run live on a testing card, not on the feature card. #2858 held them as one card; on 2026-11-15 TowerKeeper-1 split it into focused measurement cards #6953-#6960, keeping that rule: feature cards still close on implementation evidence, and each cell names its feature card.

criteria.text: Every required in-group cell and metric records Jet/peer < 1.00 for every peer, Rust included (no parity band), and reports Jet/ceiling in cycles and bytes against the cell's Tools/Perf/AsmParity reference. Missing, wrong, unavailable, mismatched or inconclusive required evidence fails; no average, median or peer subset passes; an out-of-group loss is visible but never fails. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs` over all entries with `--ceiling-results` from `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs` exits 0 with no in-group loss.

AOT results are scored against Rust, C, Zig and Go, and `jet run` and `jet dev` results separately against Python and JavaScript, for execution, first-result and edit-to-result; compiled-rival compile-plus-run comparisons are shown as non-blocking, and AOT build-speed gates are unchanged (owner 2026-09-14). Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.test.mjs` group-assignment cases.

The main chart has exactly one JS language column and no Node language column or expert columns; JS runtime and tool versions are measurement metadata; entry metadata, source metrics, counts and comparisons share one identity with no lost workload or double count. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/standings.test.mjs`.

Node, Bun and Vite are separately measured, required web-development comparisons against `jet dev` on the live_reload axis, and each result names its command, runtime, watcher (nodemon for Node) and versions. Proof: the receipt of `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/live-reload.mjs` lists each comparison with those fields.

Runtime, startup, first-result and edit-to-result measurements use matched lifecycle boundaries, with cold, warm and steady-state rows kept distinct. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.test.mjs` lifecycle cases.

Wrong output fails correctness in every applicable execution mode even when its performance comparison is non-blocking, no correctness or I9 defect is recorded as a performance exclusion, and no tier exclusion is introduced. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.test.mjs` with a planted wrong-output fixture.

`jet run` and `jet dev` each have their own measured, gated dynamic-peer result; an AOT result, run result or trace never stands in for a missing dev measurement. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/status.test.mjs`.

Report generation, status projection and merge, the integrated gate and the Tower view agree on grouping and verdicts, proven by consumer checks and real O0, O1, O2 and Node, Bun and Vite evidence; historical receipts stay unchanged and cannot silently pass the current law. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/status.test.mjs` and `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/standings.test.mjs`.

Every peer in the gauntlet and ScriptBench manifests carries one tier: scripting (python, node, bun, deno, perl, ruby, lua, luajit, php), managed (Go, Java, C#), systems (idiomatic C, C++, Rust, Zig with the same features: bounds checks, error reporting, same output) or ceiling (the asm-parity reference). Reports show the best Jet/peer ratio per tier for each cell and metric, for the binary and for `jet run`, never a combined score, and tiers never close a cell (owner 2026-11-08). Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/standings.test.mjs` tier cases.

Under D-PERF-RUNCELL2=A the wait from `jet run` to its answer is gated on real scripts against Lua, LuaJIT, Python and Node, a tiny hello is gated against the process-start floor, and after-edit, repeat and install cache states are recorded as separate rows. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.test.mjs` run-cell cases.

Each cell runs a matched standalone or package workflow for every peer, with no Jet-only preparation or hidden warming; setup, cold and warm build, execution and source-to-result are separate and reproducible; and the manifest, runner, receipts and Tower agree. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs`.
`jet perf run` records cycles, instructions, cache misses and branch misses in the existing trace format, and writes an honest `unavailable` record when a counter cannot be read.

The pinned report reproduces every current Jet loss with the frozen task, hostile input, selected peer, toolchain, sample policy, tolerance, and source boundary unchanged. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/standings.test.mjs` reproduction cases.

Every applicable native, cross-target, O0, O1, O2, normal and hostile execution row still produces the frozen observable result with separate artifact and output receipts. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.test.mjs`.

The release gate passes with zero unowned losses; any remaining loss names a live narrower Tower card and keeps the release claim false. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/status.test.mjs` unowned-loss cases.

A frozen workload manifest covers systems, service, CLI, library, compute, embedded and cross-platform tasks against the best compiled peer, with the same inputs, versions and source boundary. Reports cover the ten metrics plus the unsafe/audit burden. Proof runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, native and cross where applicable. Removal canaries make false greens fail. The release gate cannot pass with an unowned loss, and a fresh reviewer verifies fairness. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs` and the Linux, macOS and Windows receipts.

The ratified surface/plain performance contract, paired-program manifest and strict loss/missing-evidence gate are implemented, with a test that fails on a missing or losing pair. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.test.mjs` paired-program cases.

The paired O2 cells for logreport, text-script, datasummary and taskfile-cli record Jet against the plain implementation and every required peer, with Jet/peer < 1.00 for every peer and metric, Rust included, and Jet/ceiling at most 1.00. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry logreport` (and text-script, datasummary, taskfile-cli) shows no in-group loss. (was #2865 c1)

http-service median, p99, startup and RSS each pass against every required peer in its group (Rust, Go, Node, Python), with no aggregate hiding a losing cell. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry http-service` shows no in-group loss. (was #2873 c1)

concurrency-service passes every required peer and metric in its group on O0, O1 and O2, p50 and startup below Node included, with JavaScript appearing once and its Node runtime named in the metadata. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry concurrency-service` shows no in-group loss. (was #2873 c2)
http-client at O2 has wall time below Rust (Jet/Rust < 1.00). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry http-client`. (was #2873 c3)

After correctness, a matched authenticated create-and-list service protocol (#3173) against Nest and Fastify reports cold startup, p50, p95 and p99, overload, CPU, memory and errors separately, keeping losses. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry service-protocol`. (was #2873 c9)

Jet one-liners (#6067): on a 1M-line input, each of the 10 one-liners runs faster than `perl` and than `gawk` on the second (cached) run (hyperfine -N; Jet/perl and Jet/gawk below 1.00 for every row). Proof: the committed hyperfine receipt, numbers logged on this card. (was #5949 c24)

On every ScriptBench cell (Tools/Perf/Scriptbench), `jet run` of the script, compile included, has a lower wall time than every measured peer's run (Python, Bash, Node, Perl, awk and the rest), on a first run with nothing kept and on a warm run, measured with the manifest method on one quiet machine (owner ruling 2026-11-09, C-G4-1). Proof: the ScriptBench receipt for every cell, cold and warm. (was #5949 c25)

A matched script cell family (hello, a 50-line text-processing script, a JSON transform, a directory walk, a subprocess pipeline) runs `jet run` against Lua 5.4, LuaJIT, Python 3, Node, Bun, Deno and Perl, measuring exec-to-exit wall time, cycles and peak RSS, Jet compile included, cold and warm reported separately. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry script-cells` records every peer and metric. (was #6639 c1)

End metric: Jet wins every cell and metric against every peer (Jet/peer below 1.00), cold and warm; every loss names its root on a card. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry script-cells` shows no loss. (was #6639 c2)

Every applicable gauntlet corpus entry on default `jet run` and on `jet dev` independently beats CPython and JavaScript under matched harness conditions, with the JS runtime named and no second language column. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs` run and dev groups show no loss. (was #6639 c9)

Every gauntlet corpus program runs native code with no fallback path, and typed scalars and direct calls stay unboxed where sema facts allow. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLICompilerSpeed/no_fallback_unboxed`. (was #6639 c10)

With no kept program, cache or incremental state, `jet run hello.jet` (a fresh process, nothing reused from an earlier run) shows a lower mean than `luajit hello.lua` under `hyperfine -N --warmup 3 --runs 30` on the same host (Jet/LuaJIT < 1.00); the final target is at or below one exec plus a compile of the user code only (the hand-written ELF hello is 0.155 ms on the reference host). Baselines 2026-11-08 (a0_037): cold 17.8 ms, luajit 0.58 ms, lua 0.75 ms, Jet AOT binary 0.175 ms. Proof: a committed hyperfine receipt. (was #6639 c11)
Peak RSS of `jet run hello.jet` with no kept program or cache (GNU time %M, median of 10) is below `lua hello.lua` on the same host. Proof: a committed GNU time receipt. (was #6639 c12)

After a one-line edit to a 30-line script that uses core.files and core.regex, `jet run` prints its first output sooner than `python3` runs the equivalent script (hyperfine with a prepare step that applies the edit; Jet/Python < 1.00), with no kept program, cache or incremental state: an edited run costs what any run costs. Proof: a committed hyperfine receipt with the prepare step. (was #6639 c13)

Script startup beats Lua: on one host, the same-run median of `jet run hello.jet` and of `jet run` after an edit are each below lua 5.4 hello.lua, by design rather than by reusing a kept program or incremental state (owner 2026-11-08: do not rely on incremental compilation or caching to win; the final target is the hand-written machine-code ceiling). Baselines in the #6328 log, 2026-11-08. Proof: a committed same-run receipt. (was #6639 c14)

binparse at O2 has Jet/Rust, Jet/C, Jet/Zig and Jet/Go each below 1.00 on wall time and peak memory, with its Jet/ceiling ratio against the binparse asm-parity reference reported. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry binparse` shows no in-group loss. (was #6954 c1)

sieve and wordfreq at O2 pass every required in-group peer and metric, Rust and Zig included, and the O2 synthesis counts only after every required metric passes, never a primary-metric-only or historical weaker result. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry sieve` and `--entry wordfreq` show no in-group loss. (was #6954 c2)

regex-logscan passes at O2 against its compiled peers and on run and dev against Python and JS. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry regex-logscan` shows no in-group loss. (was #6954 c4)
The memory-safety-fuzz entry's Zig rail is measured. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry memory-safety-fuzz` reports a Zig result. (was #6954 c9)
The parallel-grep Jet entry builds and is measured. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry parallel-grep` reports a Jet result. (was #6954 c10)

cards.title: The named gauntlet workloads beat every in-group peer: binparse, sieve, wordfreq, regex-logscan, nbody, taskfile-cli, memory-safety-fuzz, parallel-grep and dispatch loops

cards.title: Every conformance, corpus and witness program gives the same answer on O0, O1 and O2, and routing canaries catch a silent tier change
cards.body:
Destination: the Core conformance census and the gauntlet corpus run byte-identical on O0, O1 and O2; every public Core item maps to a value-consuming conformance row or an owner-ratified exclusion; a clean `jet check` followed by `jet run` and `jet build` never fails in the compiler on the witness corpus; and canaries fail when a command silently changes its tier or falls back.

Why: I9 (one meaning on every tier) is the precondition for every speed number; a faster wrong answer is not a result.

Decisions: I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; rows came from #2286, #2334, #2389, #2270 and the merged #2859 (#1027, #1028).

criteria.text: Every conformance program and every changed gauntlet corpus entry is byte-identical across O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Conformance` on O0, O1 and O2.
A tagged public-surface denominator maps every public Core item, on every applicable tier, to a value-consuming conformance row or an owner-ratified counted exclusion.

A clean `jet check` followed at once by `jet run` (O0) and `jet build` (O1, O2) produces no new compiler-side failure across the witness corpus; tier proofs come from side-effect-free validators, and a coverage miss is never reported clean.

The profile-routing canary runs `jet run`, `jet dev`, `jet build` and `jet build --release` on a canonical source and records the expected O0, O1 or O2 level, output, diagnostics and phase identity, failing if the default level silently changes, bypasses its route or changes meaning.

The O1 route canary in the cli_compiler_speed rows records the selected backend and any explicit fallback and checks output and diagnostics against O0, O1 and O2, failing if O1 is silently bypassed or falls back without a receipt.

cards.title: Thirty frozen puzzles, both parts, measured against every peer on every tier
cards.body:
Destination: thirty puzzle IDs, both parts, are frozen with a stated selection rationale before any Jet measurement; each comparison language has a complete, natural solution; an independent oracle and owned fixtures establish both answers; and all sixty part cells are measured against every applicable peer under the peer law.

Why: a broad set of small, varied programs catches losses that a few showcase workloads hide.

Decisions: the peer law and groups live on #6953. Neither official puzzle prose nor personal inputs are redistributed.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; rows came from #3407 and #3408.

criteria.text: Exactly thirty puzzle IDs and both parts are frozen before any Jet measurement, with a diverse, declared selection rationale. Proof: the committed puzzle manifest and its rationale, dated before the first Jet receipt.

Every applicable comparison language has a complete, correct, natural solution, and differing algorithms and optimization opportunities are disclosed. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry puzzles --check` verifies every solution's answers.
An independent oracle and owned fixtures establish both answers, and no official puzzle prose or personal input is in the repository.
Every applicable Jet tier preserves both answers, and a wrong, missing, unsupported or inconclusive cell cannot pass. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Puzzles` on O0, O1 and O2.

The existing gauntlet consumers discover all sixty part cells without replacing real-workload requirements or changing historical receipts. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs`.

All thirty puzzles, both parts, have matched measurements against every applicable peer and rail, with correctness, setup, build, execution, source-to-result and source metrics shown separately under the peer law. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry puzzles` shows no in-group loss.

cards.title: Core library speed claims each have a paired cell that passes the performance gate: iterators, collections, allocators, codecs, dataframes, byte loops, gathers and FFT
cards.body:
Destination: every Core surface that claims to be fast or zero-cost has a paired cell in the canonical performance manifest against the plain spelling or a matched peer, and passes the performance gate before the claim is published.

Why: a zero-cost or speed claim without a matched measurement is a guess (owner direction: diagnose before discarding, retest when the precondition lands).

Decisions: AGENTS.md performance gate; owner order 2026-11-11 holds small optimizations until the language is mostly stable, so these cells measure and record, and a loss names its root on #6756. D-LANES-GATHER1 stays a draft ballot until its cell wins.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; each criterion names the feature card it measures.

criteria.text: Iterator capability facts (#3317): a matched workload measures allocations, peak memory and time before any zero-cost or speed claim for size_hint, fuse, by_ref and peek adaptation is published. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry iter-capabilities` records the three metrics.

core.collections Counter, OrderedMap, Chain and the heap helpers no longer copy on every operation: a paired cell shows linear, not quadratic, growth. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry collections-growth` at 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5 elements.

Matched owned-value, borrowed-view and finite owning-Iter cells include candidate keys, payload materialization, View headers, result storage and iterator construction; same-job semantics precede performance qualification; C keeps its sort-before-count behavior; no redundant-copy-only win or public adoption is claimed until prototype/plain < 1.00 and Jet/peer < 1.00 for every cell and metric. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry core-views` shows no in-group loss.

Custom allocators and struct-of-arrays (#6314): each allocator and SoA surface has a paired two-program cell against the plain spelling (default heap, array of structs) and strictly beats it. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry allocators-soa`.

State machines (#6326): the built state machine surface has a paired cell against a hand-written enum-and-match machine and passes the gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry state-machine`.
core.compute SIMD dispatch (#6624): the AVX2 path's measured speedup over the scalar path is asserted and recorded. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry compute-simd-dispatch`.

Typed codec forms (#3236): encoded bytes, allocations and encode and decode medians, plus malformed-input behavior, are recorded per form with the jet and serde adapters. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry enum-codec-bench`.

Dataframe over Arrow batches (#5968): filter, group-by sum, join and sort over a 10M-row CSV run faster than Polars and pandas on the same host (Jet/Polars < 1.00, Jet/pandas < 1.00). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry dataframe-10m`.
Byte loops of the Core/crypto expert-loop class reach matched-peer speed, with paired cells. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry byte-loops` shows no in-group loss.

Checked lane gather (#6177, draft D-LANES-GATHER1): two programs do the same Doom-style two-stage byte lookup (texture byte, then light-table byte) over the same tables with the same output and bounds-checked safety, one with a checked `Lanes<U8, N>` gather and one with checked scalar reads; the cell records target, commit, optimization level, cycles and bytes. The ballot is posted only after the gather strictly wins; a loss stays logged. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry lanes-gather`.

core.compute FFT (#6408): the repro's time meets its target on the release tier, and every timing receipt binds length, precision, tier, transfer policy, warmup, samples and exact-result identity; an unmatched external library timing is not evidence. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry fft-4096`.

Paired cells for a 30-state tokenizer and a bytecode VM compare plain Jet with C (switch and computed goto) and Zig (labeled switch), and the emitted dispatch is inspected before any syntax proposal. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry dispatch-loops` plus the committed disassembly note. (was #6954 c11)

cards.title: Safety checks and runtime hooks cost nothing measurable: pause checks, diagnostic chains, unused context hooks, drop glue, exit teardown, checked pointer reads and the hardened profile
cards.body:
Destination: each always-on safety mechanism and runtime hook has a measured cost within the gate's rules: loop-turn pause checks, the diagnostic chain, unused context hooks, boxed trait drop glue, the exit flag in inlined refcount release, checked raw-pointer reads, the checking-mode test run and the hardened profile.

Why: safety that costs measurable speed gets turned off; Jet's promise is that safe code is also fast code.

Decisions: D-TASK-SLICE1 (busy-task loop-turn checks), D-HOOK-RUNTIME1=A (hooks cost nothing when unused); AGENTS.md performance gate.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; each criterion names the feature card it measures. The c140 root analysis (2026-11-12, G11Speed-4) is in the #2858 log.

criteria.text: Strong pause .CheckLoops (#4636): the default-mode cost on the hot-loop kernels is within noise under the performance gate and recorded in the canonical manifest. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry pause-checkloops`.

Busy-task loop-turn checks (D-TASK-SLICE1): a new default turns on only after the hot-loop kernels show no measurable slowdown; until then the wait-point rule stays. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry task-slice-turns`.

The diagnostic chain (#3720) is read only when a stop is reported: a benchmark loop of 10^7 calls stays within 1% of its time without the chain. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry diagnostic-chain-cost`.

Unused context hooks (#5025, D-HOOK-RUNTIME1=A): when no code reads `context.trace`, a loop of 10^7 calls stays within 1% of the same loop built from the commit before `.trace` landed. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry context-hooks-unused`.

Boxed trait value drop glue (#6727): a paired cell with dynamic dispatch in a hot loop shows the drop glue's cost against the base, within the gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry trait-drop-glue`.

The inlined x64 refcount release honors the process-exit flag, so drop walks do not run at exit: an A/B on two exit-heavy programs shows the walk skipped and exit time reduced, with identical output on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry exit-teardown` A/B.

The checked raw-pointer read finds its allocation in constant or logarithmic time without a global lock on the read path, keeping every check; the raw-read kernel is within 1.5x of the list kernel at O2, and out-of-bounds and use-after-free reports are byte-identical. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry checked-raw-read` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter raw_read_reports`.
The nightly checking-mode `#Test` run's slowdown against normal O0 (#6011) is measured and logged. Proof: the committed nightly receipt with both timings.
Safe-Jet-only programs show no measurable overhead under `--profile=hardened` against the normal profile. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry hardened-profile`.

Inside a proven-pure call (`-[]>`), values that existed before the call skip generation checks, alias checks and count updates, while values created inside keep them. `jet inspect choices` lists every skipped check, removing the purity restores them, and a paired cell with and without `-[]>` is recorded. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetirFacts/purity_skips_checks`. (was #3039 c11)

cards.title: Web features prove their speed: first result beats JS and Rust, and each automatic web form beats the hand-written code it replaces
cards.body:
Destination: Jet web's first result beats JS and Rust; every performance-relevant framework element has a gauntlet cell against the best framework for it; each automatic form (secret fencing, wire-skew checks, reactive plain data, compiler-decided invalidation, optimistic updates, resumable pages) passes a paired cell against the hand-written form it replaces; and the jet dev study timings are rerun with the gauntlet method.

Why: automatic web features are only worth having if they are at least as fast as the code a careful developer writes by hand.

Decisions: D-SECRETEDGE1, D-WIRESKEW1, D-REACT-REF1, D-INVALIDATE1, D-OPTIMISTIC1, D-RESUME1, D-WEB-IMAGE1=A; AGENTS.md performance gate.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; each criterion names the feature card it measures.

criteria.text: Web first result (#5201): on one matched run of the web-app and web-widget entries, Jet/JS and Jet/Rust first_result_s are both below 1.00, and every Examples/features/web golden still passes on every applicable tier. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-app` and `--entry web-widget`.

Jet web framework elements (#6552): every performance-relevant element has a gauntlet cell and ceiling reference that passes the gate against the best framework for it. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-framework-elements`.

Secrets never reach browser code (#6557, D-SECRETEDGE1): a paired cell compares the automatic form with the hand-written form it replaces and passes the gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-secret-edge`.

Old clients keep working after a deploy (#6558, D-WIRESKEW1): a paired cell compares the automatic form with the hand-written form and passes the gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-wire-skew`.
Jet web images (#4695, D-WEB-IMAGE1=A): the image build step's time is measured and recorded. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-image-build`.

Plain data that updates the screen (#6553, D-REACT-REF1): a paired cell compares the automatic form with the hand-written form and passes the gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-react-ref`.

Compiler-decided stale cached reads (#6554, D-INVALIDATE1): a paired cell compares the automatic form with the hand-written form and passes the gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry web-invalidate`.

The timing cells of the 2026-11-04 jet dev study (Docs/Research/2026-11-04-jet-dev-vs-incumbents.md) are rerun with the gauntlet method against Vite, Bun, Next.js, Deno, Astro, Rsbuild and Parcel, and every loss is on a card with its root cause. cards.title: Tool latency is measured against the best peer: edit-to-verdict, Core activation, LSP, package lowering, install and memory profiling
cards.body:
Destination: the developer-facing tools have measured latency and cost against their best peers: cancellation and edit-to-verdict under a repeated-edit stream, Core battery activation cost, LSP hover and diagnostics against tsserver, build time with lazy package lowering, install-to-hello against Deno and Bun, and `jet perf` sampling overhead against py-spy.

Why: developer experience is mostly waiting; each of these waits is a number Jet can lose on.

Decisions: AGENTS.md performance gate; no zero-cost claim from dead-code elimination alone.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; each criterion names the feature card it measures.

criteria.text: Cancellation-to-release and edit-to-current-verdict latency, plus retained work, are measured under a bounded repeated-edit stream with exact binary, input and protocol receipts. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry edit-stream-latency`.

After import closure, with a frozen compiler and control, import and use arms, each Core battery's target-specific reachable dependencies, startup, linked sections, initialization and per-call allocation are measured, with unavoidable compile cost reported separately and no zero-cost claim from dead-code elimination alone. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry core-activation`.

Jet LSP (#4917): on a 2,000-line file that uses Core, p95 latency of hover and of diagnostics after an edit is below tsserver on an equivalent TypeScript file (Jet/tsserver < 1.00). Proof: the scripted LSP harness receipt `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry lsp-latency`.

Package lazy lowering (#6151): building the examples is not slower once a package's unreached functions are no longer lowered. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry compile-throughput` A/B.

Install (#5950): on a clean Linux x86-64 container, one-line install to the first `hello` output is faster than the Deno and Bun installers (median of 5, Jet/peer < 1.00), and the downloaded archive is smaller than both. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry install-to-hello`.

`jet perf` memory method (#4727): the w04 sampling profile's overhead on the run is below py-spy's overhead on the Python version (Jet/py-spy < 1.00). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry perf-measure`.

cards.title: Number-crunching kernels beat Rust: Decimal parse, add and format, fixed-width byte loops, and integer mod and div
cards.body:
Destination: the arithmetic kernels behind csvtransform, embedded-data and embedded-sensor-ring are faster than Rust at O2: Decimal parse, add and format; the fixed-width take_pattern and byte checksum loops; and integer mod and div. Output stays byte-identical and the Decimal, bigint-promotion and checked-arithmetic tests are unchanged.

Why: these kernels sit under every data and embedded workload; a slow kernel loses every cell built on it.

Decisions: AGENTS.md performance gate. Owner order 2026-11-11 holds small optimizations until the language is mostly stable, so a fix goes in the general mechanism, never a per-entry trim.

Source: split from #2865 (text pipelines) on 2026-11-15; the rows came from #2866, #2871 and #2872.

criteria.text: csvtransform at O2 has Jet/{Rust, Go, Zig, Python, Node} < 1.00, and the Decimal parse, add and format micro witness is at least 5x faster than today with byte-identical output and unchanged Decimal goldens. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry csvtransform` and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Decimal`.

embedded-data at O2 has Jet/{Rust, C, Zig, Python, Node} < 1.00, and the fixed-width take_pattern loop and the byte checksum loop micro witnesses are each faster than Rust (the binparse cell is #6954 c1). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry embedded-data`.

embedded-sensor-ring at O2 has Jet/{Rust, C, Zig} < 1.00, the integer mod and div micro witness is faster than Rust, and the bigint-promotion and checked-arithmetic tests are unchanged. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry embedded-sensor-ring` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter checked_arith`.

cards.title: Values move without hidden copies: no list clone in elementwise loops, a field read clones one field, and moving a large struct is not a bulk copy
cards.body:
Destination: an elementwise `c[i] = a[i] + b[i]` loop over 20M elements runs in under 0.1 s with no list clone; a stored-field read such as `self.width` clones only that field; returning a large struct and moving it into a list does no bulk copy; and each gauntlet cell reports its bulk-copy count.

Why: hidden copies are the main way a safe language loses to C on memory and time; Jet promises value semantics without paying for them.

Decisions: copying is explicit `.copy()` (the retired `~`); AGENTS.md performance gate. Ownership, alias, order, bounds, cleanup and error-location semantics must not change.

Source: split from #2865 (text pipelines) on 2026-11-15; the rows came from #2890, #3735 and #4178.

criteria.text: The elementwise `c[i] = a[i] + b[i]` loop over N=20M on an AOT release build has a median under 0.1 s, RSS under 500 MiB and no list clone in the loop; N=20k runs in under 2 s and N=200k in under 20 s on O0; L2510 no longer fires on that shape, or its fix names a user edit; and bare, shared, write, copy, nested, out-of-range and non-place cases keep their ownership, alias, order, bounds, cleanup and error-location semantics. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Copies/elementwise_loop_no_clone` and `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry elementwise-20m`.

A stored-field read (`self.width`) clones only that field, and the bmp_enhanced 4000x4000 sprite has peak RSS within 1.5x of C, with struct, pinned, shared-guard, file-owner and computed-field goldens unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Copies/field_read_clones_field` and `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry bmp-enhanced`.

Each gauntlet cell reports its bulk-copy count, and returning a large struct and moving it into a list performs no bulk copy. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Copies/large_struct_move_no_bulk_copy` and the bulk_copies column in `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs` output.

The emitted code for a line-parsing witness has no per-line String allocation for literals, no double clone of split results, and no stack-frame call on infallible functions in the default profile. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TextPipeline/line_parse_witness_codegen`. (was #2865 c2)

Every changed text-pipeline shape keeps byte-identical output on O0, O1 and O2, with existing goldens unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TextPipeline` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #2865 c3)

Debug and hardened profiles keep their stack sentry, failure carrier, panic text and diagnostics, and the default profile removes a frame only when checked infallibility proves it safe. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TextPipeline/frame_elision_profiles`. (was #2865 c4)

A dead `String.from_bytes(token)` binding followed by a map increment uses the borrowed-byte map-update helper, keeping UTF-8 validation, ordering and fallback (the wordfreq cell is #6954 c2). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Optimizer/borrowed_byte_map_update`. (was #2865 c10)

cards.title: A recursive list builder of a million elements is stack-safe on every tier
cards.body:
Destination: a recursive function that builds a list element by element (cons-style) runs for 1,000,000 elements without exhausting the stack on O0, O1 and O2, with stack depth and time measured first; if it is not already stack-safe, one shared JetIR tail-recursion-modulo-cons transform makes it so.

Why: recursion is the natural way to write many list builders; a stack overflow at scale pushes users to rewrite correct code.

Decisions: I9 (one meaning on every tier); one shared JetIR transform, no per-backend fix.

Source: split from #2865 (text pipelines) on 2026-11-15.

criteria.text: Stack depth and time are measured for a recursive list builder; if it is not already stack-safe, one shared JetIR tail-recursion-modulo-cons transform makes a 1,000,000-element builder stack-safe. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Trmc` on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Nested joins never hang: a join on a child that has not started runs it, whatever the task count
cards.body:
Destination: with more running tasks than about (cores+8)/2, nested joins finish instead of hanging. A join on a child that has not started yet runs that child on the joining thread, or an equivalent that never deadlocks.

Why: today every thread waits in futex_wait on a task that never gets a worker, because the scheduler adds at most 8 workers to cover blocked waits (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Scheduler.jet). It was found by TestSpeedLead on 2026-11-05: a testkit pool whose entries each join a child and its resident watcher task hangs on the AOT and run tiers, and JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=256 is the workaround.

Decisions: I9 (one meaning on every tier).

Source: split from #5910 c59 on 2026-11-15.

criteria.text: A cases fixture nests joins inside a task group whose limit is at least the core count and finishes on O0, O1 and O2, with a join on a not-yet-started child running that child on the joining thread.
The testkit's default pool no longer sets JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS as a deadlock workaround. Proof: `git grep -n JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS -- Compiler/JetTestKit Tools/testkit` prints nothing.

cards.title: Measurement helpers are proven: `keep(x)` holds benchmarked work on every tier and `compare` records replayable differences
cards.body:
Destination: `keep(x)` (D-BENCH-KEEP1=A, an always-available Prelude identity sink) stops the optimizer from deleting measured work on O0, O1 and O2, and Core Testing's `compare(cases, reference, candidate, relation)` (D-TEST-COMPARE1=A) returns a comparison record whose differences replay. Both exist on dev (Compiler/Prelude/Core.rows keep row; Core/Testing/Testing.jet compare) but no test proves either behavior.

Why: every performance cell relies on the work it times not being optimized away, and A-against-B claims rely on a comparison that can be replayed.

Decisions: D-BENCH-KEEP1=A, D-TEST-COMPARE1=A, D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A (shipped in #2082; its retired-spelling teaching rows go with #6637 c11).

Source: split from #5910 c40 on 2026-11-15; D-MEGAPROJ1 went to #6311.

criteria.text: A measured loop whose result passes only through `keep(x)` is kept at O2: the loop body is present in the release binary and its timing scales with N, on O0, O1 and O2.

`compare(cases, reference, candidate, relation)` on two implementations that differ on one case returns a comparison naming that case, and replaying the recorded difference reproduces it; equal implementations pass `assert_equal`.

jet budget is built, including the BenchMeasurement provider (runs #Test(.measure) 20 times) and the RelativeTo baseline history (pooled_samples, history.report_ids). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsCore/budget_bench_measurement_bootstraps_then_consumes_compatible_history`, with its known-failing row removed. (was #6418 c3)

cards.title: Caches are off by default: every run and build compiles live, and the retired cache stores are gone
cards.body:
Destination: `jet file.jet`, `jet run` and `jet build` compile live every time by default; no kept program, result cache, build store or incremental state serves a run unless the user opts in through an existing switch; and the retired cache stores and their environment switches are deleted.

Why: owner order 2026-11-11, caches off. Cold compile time is what users feel, and a cache hides it from every measurement.

Decisions: owner order 2026-11-11 (caches off; any new public opt-in spelling goes to a ballot and nothing else changes until it is ratified). The kept-program cache removal itself is #6328 c24.

Source: #6527 c9 and c12 and #6639 c6, gathered 2026-11-15.

criteria.text: Build reuse and the jet build binary store are off by default, per the standing caches-off order. Found by G11Speed on 2026-11-11: Executor.jet:324 restores any reusable step unconditionally, BuildExecute.jet:188 always opens the store when a build has steps, and Cli/BuildCache.jet:29 keeps the binary store on by default, with no switch (cli.md:504 documents made-or-reused). Fix (G11Speed-7c): a default build opens no store and puts nothing; opting in uses only an existing switch, or the executor API for tests if none exists, and any new public opt-in spelling goes to a ballot. cli.md and the BuildExecutor action-reuse test are updated in the same cutover. Proof: a test shows a default build opens no store; the opted-in reuse test passes; and cold and warm jet build Compiler are measured n=3 before and after.

No BuildCache, RuntimeCache, RunCache, ReceiptStore, BuildPlanReplay or JET_TIMING, JET_RUN_TRACE, JET_RECEIPT_BYPASS, JET_CACHE_DIR or JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR remains, and architecture.md, compiler-speed.md and the syntax-decisions ledger describe the graph, store, units and levels as shipped. Proof: `git grep -n -E "BuildCache|RuntimeCache|RunCache|ReceiptStore|BuildPlanReplay|JET_TIMING|JET_RUN_TRACE|JET_RECEIPT_BYPASS|JET_CACHE_DIR|JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR" -- Compiler Core Tools Docs/Spec` prints nothing.

Owner order 2026-11-11: the script cache is off by default. `jet file.jet` and `jet run` compile live every time, and no kept program, result cache or incremental state serves a run unless the user opts in. ScriptCache.jet's default flips. The opt-in spelling goes on a ballot (a flag or an environment variable) and nothing else changes until it is ratified. CLI #Tests prove a second run of unchanged sources compiles again by default (no read or write under the scripts dir). Every in-repository caller, doc and test that assumed a cache hit is migrated in the same patch.

Seed-seam step (b) for the embedded jet`s mode: the Jetpack executor publishes every run-step output 0600 (Store/Build build_publish_sandbox_outputs -> build_atomic_restore_file), so the c22 embed (s3) can only start the embedded jet on seed-b17 through a temporary step (a), either the BuildExecute executable-output route or a chmod on RuntimePack`s --jet input. G12Docs-c22-s3x fixes the executor (an output its action left owner-executable is published 0755, and the cache record keeps an x flag). After the first admitted seed that carries s3x, the step-(a) chmod is removed, if one was used. Proof: the s3 gate passes on that seed with no chmod, and `git grep` finds no mode workaround in RuntimePack.jet. (was #6328 c36)

A cold artifact store opens without per-directory fsync stalls, and the open is traced. Found by G11Speed on 2026-11-11 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/b30/hang-finding.md): Jetpack/Store/Source/ArtifactStore/Store.jet (~964-971) creates the layout directories cas, ac, lto, locks, leases, quarantine, build-records and records through store_artifact_ensure_dir (Codec.jet:277), which fsyncs the parent after each mkdir. On a busy ext4 that cost 22.55 s across 8 fsyncs in one bench30k build (63 s total), all in an untraced gap between sema.finalize and ir.build; at 4G, 8 of 8 builds stalled. Fix: layout directories are recreated by any later run, so they aren't synced (per Codec.jet's own rule); durable records keep their sync; and a store.open trace span covers the work. Proof: a cold-store jet build of bench30k on the scratch disk ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT), n=3, shows store.open under 0.5 s in the trace and no untraced gap above 1 s, and the store crash-safety tests still pass. (was #6527 c8)

cards.title: The build graph runs deterministically and shows its work: ordered scheduling, the ratified pools, alias-safe step outputs and the build board
cards.body:
Destination: `jet build` schedules a graph deterministically (longest remaining path, then key; only the ratified pools cpu, memory, linker, console and gpu; a failure cancels only its dependents), refuses a step output reached through an aliased read folder, and shows its work on a TTY board of at most 8 lines with one final receipt line, plus `--json` NDJSON and `--trace` Chrome trace output.

Why: a build users can trust gives the same order and diagnostics every run and shows progress without flooding the terminal.

Decisions: D-BUILD-UI1=A (what jet build shows while it works). The owner's acceptance of the board look is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Source: #6682 c8, c9 and c10 (from #2514 c10 and c11, #2526 and #2527), moved 2026-11-15 because they are build-executor behavior, not the project build function.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c3, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: The step-output-in-read-folder rule (Graph.jet and Jetpack Validation.jet, spec.md:5050, E3502) compares resolved real folders, not spelled paths. A dependency bound at .jet/deps (or any other alias) that resolves to a folder holding a step output is refused. The project root and each dependency root are threaded into both validators and resolved through the host.

Scheduling is deterministic: identical start logs across runs of a 40-node graph, and stable diagnostics under randomized delays. Only the ratified pools exist (cpu, memory, linker, console, gpu), with a RAM-derived cpu cap. Ready nodes are ordered by longest remaining path, then by key. A failure cancels only its dependents, and keep-going continues the rest.

A TTY board of at most 8 lines redraws in place, with one final receipt line. UI snapshots cover building, success, no-change, failure, notes, piped and NO_COLOR. `--json` emits schema-valid NDJSON and `--trace` emits Chrome trace JSON. SIGTSTP/SIGCONT and resize restore the terminal, and TERM=dumb falls back. Old BuildProgress strings are deleted. The owner's acceptance of the look is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Determinism under scheduling chaos: 64 schedule seeds times workers {1, 8, 64} give identical diagnostic bytes, TIR hash and binary SHA (the SPEED-500K section 10 scheduling-chaos knob). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ParallelCompile/schedule_chaos_identical_output`. (was #4310 c9)

Parallel check over N workers is deterministic: the canonical state dump equals the single-worker dump. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ParallelCompile/check_state_dump_matches_single_worker`. (was #4310 c11)

jet explain is built for build facts, the syntax dictionary, build settings and the web graph. Proof: every Tests/known-failing.tsv row on #6418 that reports E2104 for `jet explain` passes on the default tier, and the rows are removed. (was #6418 c5)

Sealed check-input reads and their read audit (CheckReads, JET_CHECK_READS_AUDIT and JET_CHECK_READS_INJECT) have a Jet implementation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter BuildEntry/check_inputs_are_all_declared`. (was #6418 c134)

Each compiler package (JetFoundation, JetLexer, JetParser, JetSema, JetIR, JetBackend, JetCli and the rest) is its own library target, and independent packages compile in parallel within one cold build. Depends on #6623. Proof: the `jet build Compiler` graph receipt shows the package targets overlapping in time. (was #6682 c5)

Build profiles give a fast `dev` profile for targeted testing and a `ship` profile for release stages. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CompilerBuild/dev_and_ship_profiles`. (was #6682 c6)

Every build records a core.build graph receipt with per-target wall time; receipt_diff between two commits shows the per-target time change, and the per-phase timeline for #6610 is read from it. Proof: `jet build Compiler` writes the receipt and receipt_diff of two commits' receipts lists every target with both times. (was #6682 c7)

cards.title: Compiler and runtime stacks hold: valid programs never overflow the compiler stack, thread stacks are sized by measurement, and the hosted CLI links glibc dynamically
cards.body:
Destination: small valid programs never overflow the compiler stack under `jet run`; native jet compiles deep programs at the default 8 MiB `ulimit -s`; runtime threads reserve a stack sized by measurement instead of a fixed 192 MiB; and the Jet linker produces the dynamically linked glibc image the hosted CLI needs (D-OS-FLOOR1).

Why: a compiler crash on a valid program, or a thread reservation far above need, costs users more than any speed win; the glibc link is the last piece of the hosted CLI path.

Decisions: D-OS-FLOOR1 (glibc floor for the hosted CLI); I9 (one meaning on every tier).

Source: split from #6328 (binary size) on 2026-11-15 with Main approval; c7, c9 and c10 there came from #4919 (#4689, #4964, #5467) and c8 from #4768. No linker card owns the dynamic glibc link, so it rides here.

criteria.text: The fuzz-found small valid programs that made `jet run` abort with 'jet-compiler has overflowed its stack' (while `jet check` and emit passed) compile and run on O0, O1 and O2.
The Jet linker links dynamically for the D-OS-FLOOR1 glibc path (PT_INTERP and DT_NEEDED plus bundled glibc stubs) for the hosted CLI.
Native jet runs the compiler on a stack sized for deep recursion, so deep programs compile without raising `ulimit -s` above the 8 MiB default.

The default stack reservation of runtime threads is set from measurement (the deepest stack in the corpus plus a recorded margin) instead of a fixed 192 MiB, and a deep-recursion program still reports a clean stack overflow on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Data costs what it should: packed list strides, non-atomic unshared reference counts, unboxed scalar options and allocation-free aggregate captures
cards.body:
Destination: `[Bool]` and `[U8]` lists store one byte per element and `[I32]` four; reference counts are atomic only for values shared across tasks; an Option of a scalar is never heap-boxed; and capturing an aggregate in a closure allocates a flat count.

Why: representation overheads multiply through every program; a hand-written version pays none of them.

Decisions: AGENTS.md performance gate; owner hold 2026-11-11 (architecture and regression fixes first, no small tuning during language churn), so each fix goes in the general representation, proven on a second program.

Source: split from #6414 (run time against hand-written assembly) on 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. The rows came from #5925 (#5471, #5475), #5469 and #5919.

criteria.text: `[Bool]` and `[U8]` lists store 1 byte per element and `[I32]` 4 bytes (today 8), with identical output on O0, O1 and O2.

Reference counts are non-atomic unless the value is shared across tasks (today rc_add is always atomic), with task-sharing goldens unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Rc/nonatomic_unless_shared` and `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate --cells allocfree`.
An Option of a scalar is not heap-boxed: pop, get, first and last on a list of scalars allocate nothing.
Capturing an aggregate in a closure allocates a flat count as the aggregate grows, with goldens unchanged and the self-compile fixed point held.

cards.title: Hot loops emit what a hand-writer would: tag compares, no entry uniqueness test, range-only slices, cheap appends, two-instruction stop polls and no frame traffic
cards.body:
Destination: the hot code `jet build` emits for common shapes matches a hand-written version: fieldless enum compare is a tag compare; a borrowed list parameter does no uniqueness test on entry; slicing touches only its range; interpolated append is cheaper than Rust; a loop stop poll costs at most 2 hot instructions; and loops with at most 9 live general values touch no stack frame.

Why: these shapes sit inside nearly every hot loop; each extra instruction is paid on every iteration.

Decisions: AGENTS.md performance gate; owner hold 2026-11-11 (no small tuning during language churn), so each fix is general and proven on a second program.

Source: split from #6414 (run time against hand-written assembly) on 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. The rows came from #5925 (#5473), #6362, #6363, #6472 and #6478.

criteria.text: Equality and compare on a fieldless enum lower to a tag compare (today a 3852-instruction derived compare chain), on O1 and O2.

A & list parameter passed an exclusively owned list does no uniqueness test or copy on entry at o2 (emitted code shows none), copy-on-write meaning unchanged, and k6343/axpy.jet within the gate's band against C. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Codegen/borrowed_list_param_no_uniqueness_test` and the k6343 axpy cell.

Slicing touches only the requested range and does not copy the whole text; k6342/slice_loop.jet is faster than Rust (Jet/Rust < 1.00, no parity band) and meets its asm-parity ceiling, output unchanged on o0, o1 and o2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Codegen/slice_touches_range` and `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` for the k6342 slice_loop cell.

Building a string by repeated interpolated append (`s += "{i % 10}"`, 10k times) costs less than the Rust equivalent at o2 (Jet/Rust < 1.00) (today about 470 cycles and 2,800 instructions per append, 5.27M cycles in total against Rust 6.39M for the whole slice_loop program). Proof: the k6342 slice_loop cell in the same run as Rust.
Default build: a loop's stop poll costs at most 2 hot instructions per iteration, with the poll call out of line (objdump of the asm-parity hot loops).

Default build: the crc16 fast loop, the regex DFA step loop and find_paired have zero [rbp-*] (frame) accesses inside the loop body when at most 9 general values are live (objdump of the asm-parity images).

For every corpus program, `jet build` (default flags) runs within 1.10x of its assembly reference in cycles, with identical output; any program over that bound has a named codegen root on a card. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` shows every program at or under 1.10x cycles. (was #6414 c2)

The perf gate fails any corpus program over the bound, and a plan document (Docs/Proposals) names the codegen and runtime design changes, with modelled gains, that close the gap without per-program tricks. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` exits non-zero on a program over the bound, and `git ls-files "Docs/Proposals/*asm-ceiling*"` names the plan. (was #6414 c3)

Work backwards from hand-optimized machine code (owner direction 2026-11-11). A kernel catalog covers each common code shape: counted and iterator loops, list sum and map, text scan and compare, struct copy and move, enum match, option and error return, hash lookup, bounds-checked index, call and return, allocation and drop. Each kernel has a small Jet program and a hand-written, maximally optimized x86-64 reference that does the same work with the same safety checks. For each kernel, a checker compares the hot code that `jet build` emits with the reference: instruction count, spills, loads and stores, checks, and calls. Every extra instruction is named with its root (bounds check not hoisted, value spilled, copy not elided, loop not vectorized, call not inlined, or atomic reference count). Each root is fixed once, in the general lowering, never per kernel, and is proved on a second program that uses the feature differently. Each kernel then gets a machine-code golden that pins the emitted hot loop at O1 and O2, so a regression fails the gate. The gate fails any kernel whose emitted hot code is over its reference in instructions or cycles. Every new codegen feature adds its kernel and reference before it lands. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` over the catalog cells and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CodegenKernels` (machine-code goldens at O1 and O2), with instructions per element recorded before and after each step. (was #6414 c15)

cards.title: One verified optimizer pipeline: O0 is the reference, passes are canonical and deterministic, stale facts fail closed, and adaptive rebuild is opt-in
cards.body:
Destination: one target-neutral, ordered IR optimization pipeline produces deterministic canonical bytes and stores its facts once; every pass is checked against O0 as reference semantics; stale or malformed facts fail closed; and adaptive rebuild from a run record (D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1=B) exists as an opt-in.

Why: optimization is only worth having if it never changes meaning; a single canonical pipeline is also what makes speed work repeatable.

Decisions: D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1=B (opt-in, owner ruling); I9.

Source: split from #6414 (run time against hand-written assembly) on 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. The rows came from #5925 (#5064), #2886, #2912, #2951, #3038 and #4571 (frozen #4571 holds the same adaptive work).

criteria.text: Every IR optimization pass is checked against O0 as reference semantics: a differential harness runs each pass corpus at O0 and with the pass on, and fails on any difference.

One post-lowering IR optimization pass canonicalizes literal and immutable Boolean loops plus proven literal integer ranges before every execution tier, preserves source markers and carries counted-loop vector proof metadata, with tier goldens, shape tests and a performance cell. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Optimizer/LoopCanonicalize` on every tier.

One target-neutral ordered IR legality and optimization pipeline produces deterministic canonical bytes and stores bounds, fusion, loop, copy-cost, failure-edge and data-plan facts once; every execution adapter rejects non-canonical input instead of deriving tier-local optimization policy.

All five bounded optimization experiment families have paired executable source, falsifying controls, exact machine, premise and observation contracts, and a real checker, inspect, run and Gauntlet collection driver, without adopting unproved transforms.
An eligible-to-ineligible transition caused by a supported IR rewrite or reduction rejection no longer leaves stale positive eligibility; a regression fails before the repair and passes afterward.
Fresh optimization, unchanged re-optimization and changed-input validation agree on facts and canonical identity; no-op optimization is stable and malformed/stale evidence fails closed

The affected source program keeps its values, effects, first error, cleanup and reduction bits on O0, O1, O2 and web; unsupported optimization takes the safe path. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Optimizer/SafePath` on O0, O1, O2 and web.
D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1=B is built as an opt-in: a run record feeds a rebuild that specializes hot paths, with output identical to the plain build (frozen #4571 holds the same work).

Sema facts (types, integer bounds, exclusivity, purity and comptime values) reach JetIR through one typed fact channel, with no second side table. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jetir_facts` has one case per fact class that fails when the fact is dropped. (was #3039 c9)

At least one existing optimization consumes each sema fact class without re-deriving sema policy in codegen, and absent facts keep the current conservative behavior. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetirFacts/consumer_per_fact_class`. (was #3039 c10)

cards.title: Automatic acceleration keeps its fallback: column copies and auto-parallel loops consume checked facts and keep the serial meaning on every tier
cards.body:
Destination: transient column copies are bounded by checked nested-reuse and single-pass facts, release lowering schedules automatic parallel work through the existing bounded pool from typed acceleration facts, and both keep the original scalar or serial fallback with the same meaning on O0, O1 and O2.

Why: automatic speedups are only safe if the plain meaning is always there to fall back to and to compare against.

Decisions: I9; AGENTS.md performance gate.

Source: split from #6414 (run time against hand-written assembly) on 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. The rows came from #2893 and #2894.

criteria.text: Transient column-copy source is limited by checked nested-reuse/single-pass facts and fixed cache-block storage; the shared measured gate and retained-sample paths consume the first chunk exactly once
The original scalar fallback and shared canonical kernel semantics stay available on O0, O1 and O2, with gravity timing and transform-on/off output goldens.

The source release lowering consumes typed acceleration facts and the shared sampled gate, schedules through the existing bounded pool, preserves sampled work, and publishes actual decisions to typed inspect receipts

Automatic parallel code keeps the original serial fallback and the canonical independent kernel meaning on O0, O1 and O2, with output goldens and a performance cell. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Accel/AutoParallelSerialFallback` and `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry auto-parallel`.

cards.title: Classic benchmark kernels beat C and Rust: the benchmarks-game set, tensor-map, enum dispatch, gradients and sprites, and the Doom renderer
cards.body:
Destination: nbody, spectral-norm, mandelbrot, fannkuch, binary-trees and a text workload beat C; tensor-map and the enum-union bridge beat every peer; the gradient and sprite cells beat Rust; and the Doom renderer kernels reach gcc and clang -O2.

Why: these are the programs readers use to judge a language speed claim; each loss is a codegen or runtime root.

Decisions: AGENTS.md performance gate (Jet/peer below 1.00, Rust included); scoring per #6953.

Source: split from #6414 (run time against hand-written assembly) on 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. The rows came from #6205, #2414 (#3135, #2778), #3736 and the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c4 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: nbody, spectral-norm, mandelbrot, fannkuch, binary-trees and a string or text workload each beat C (Jet/C < 1.00) with identical output. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry <each>` shows Jet/C below 1.00.

`node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry enum-union-bridge --runs 11` gives equal checksums for every cell and peer. It records tags, copies, spills, ownership transfers, allocation/copy counts and medians for direct named-enum, structural-union and explicit-conversion dispatch. Proof: that run receipt.

The 256² and 512² tensor-map repros finish within the resource cap on a fresh release binary, and 4K does not regress into a timeout. The paired tensor-map cell gives Jet/peer < 1.00 for every peer, Rust included. A golden shows identical results on every level. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry tensor-map` and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TensorMap`.

The gradient and sprite cells (#3736) are committed with harness, baselines and a manifest entry, and Jet/Rust < 1.00 on both gradient cells and the sprite cell, measured in the same run with byte-identical outputs. Whether they are required cells is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry gradient` and `--entry sprite`.

On the Doom renderer kernels (R_DrawColumn, R_DrawSpan, FixedMul/FixedDiv, recursive BSP walk) with matching checksums, jet build --release is measurably faster than --optimize=none and reaches the peer floor against gcc -O2 and clang -O2. Measured on 2026-11-05: Jet O2 is 8.6x, 7.1x, 8.3x and 2.5x slower than gcc -O2; O0 and O2 run at nearly the same speed; #Inline(Always) and wrapping arithmetic make no measurable difference; --bounds=off only halves the column kernel. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (dev 0ccdff27ea). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry doom-kernels` against gcc -O2 and clang -O2.

nbody at O2 has Jet/{C, Zig, Rust} < 1.00 in the default profile and jet-expert below c-expert and rust-expert, with byte-identical output, matched expert implementations, the same SIMD policy, and vectorized f64 lanes in the default profile with output identical to `#Scalar`. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry nbody` shows no in-group loss. (was #6954 c5)

cards.title: A runtime stop names the same source site on every tier: web images carry the location table native images use
cards.body: Since ae7fe7adaf, a stop raised inside Core names the user's call that reached Core, read from the image's location table (.debug_jetline). A web image has no such table, so it prints the Core site instead; the spec allows that fallback for an image with no location table. That makes one program report different stop sites on native and web, which breaks I9's one meaning across tiers. Found by SweepFix-162 (web-no-exec, 2026-11-15): the web host had also answered mprotect(PROT_EXEC) with success, so the frame walk trapped. That trap is fixed, and the e1003 web case now pins the two sites separately instead of comparing bytes.

log.text: Met on p237: web stop reports match native user-line reports byte for byte.

criteria.text: A stop raised inside Core reports the user's call site (file and line) on web exactly as on native: the web image carries the location table (or its equivalent), and the stop report reads it. Proof: the e1003 case and the golden stops IntPowNegativeStop, FloatBitsRangeStop and TypedAbsI64Min compare their web output byte for byte with native's user-line report.
criteria.evidence: p237 batch compiler (dev ab95db25f2; case landed in ba783d11b9 lineage): cases FailureTierParity/core_stops_name_the_users_call_on_web_as_on_native PASS (jet build --target web of IntPowNegativeStop, FloatBitsRangeStop and TypedAbsI64Min, compared byte for byte with the native goldens .out/.err.out) and runtime_e1003_web_uses_the_same_stop_metadata_and_exit_70 PASS; the three goldens PASS on o0, o1 and o2.

cards.title: Memory kernel performance: zero cost against the plain spelling, and the machine-code ceiling for every kernel primitive
cards.body: The memory kernel (#6842, D-MEM-CHOKEPOINT1=A) is built: one audited chokepoint for every raw memory action, with the address rule, single-use values, windows, sentry-tracked mappings and the runtime cutover proven there. Its two performance criteria move here under the owner's 2026-11-15 order that speed and size work belongs to G11 and does not block other goals. Work in flight: the inline-under-auto SUBs (kernel owner methods and from_addr inline under the default policy, constant divisors no longer stop inlining, the E0917 false positive for same-named calls) and the zero-cost paired cell (Tools/perf/ZeroCostPair.jet, 64 losses on p171). Ceiling cells measured on p160r (Jet/ceiling cycles): mapping 4.73x, allocfree 2.77x, compare 3.19x, resize 1.88x, rawword 1.35x, atomics 1.00x. Planned roots: an inlined call's Result boxes kept in the frame (landed 6595a58009), the allocator header cut from 24 B to 8 B, finer size classes.

criteria.text: (was #6842 c6, moved to G11 by owner order 2026-11-15: speed and size work moves to G11 so it does not block) Zero cost: kernel primitives inline at O1/O2. A paired two-program cell (kernel primitives against the direct spelling) and the cold self-compile show no wall or peak-memory regression on the reference machine; any loss is fixed before ratification. Proof: a committed receipt of the paired cell and the cold self-compile on the reference machine.

(was #6842 c11, moved to G11 by owner order 2026-11-15: speed and size work moves to G11 so it does not block) Owner order 2026-11-14: the kernel is safe and at the theoretical maximum performance for machine code, so the ceiling stage is open for it now. Each kernel primitive (allocate, free, resize, raw read and write, pointer offset, byte copy, move, fill and compare, atomics, mapping) has an asm-parity ceiling cell in Tools/Perf/asm-parity. Each cell uses the best known technique for its workload: SIMD copy, fill and compare chosen by size class and CPU features, branch-light fast paths for allocation and free, no redundant checks on paths sema has proved. Jet/ceiling is at most 1.00 in both cycles and code bytes at O2, measured live. Any safety check the kernel keeps appears in the reference at its smallest hand-written cost, and no check is removed to meet the ceiling. Any loss is fixed in the general lowering, not per cell. Proof: asm-parity `--gate` reports ok for every kernel primitive cell (as logged for rawword on p146).

cards.title: Shrink #Unsafe beyond memory: one typed syscall table, safe once-only runtime state, and no per-call regions for host leaves
cards.body: After the memory kernel (#6842) the inventory (jet Tools/agent/UnsafeRatchet.jet --inventory, p175) shows 842 #Unsafe regions in Compiler, the runtime, Core and Jetpack, and 0 outside the kernel files perform a raw memory action. 506 are not memory actions. By a first sort: about 160 runtime call sites each spell a raw Linux syscall (os_syscall_i64) inside their own region; about 52 write process-wide runtime state during start-up ('runs before any other thread exists'); about 48 are Core calls to private runtime host leaves; about 37 manage Secret zeroizing owners; 26 call crypto expert primitives; about 200 are unclassified. About 336 are raw memory actions inside the kernel files themselves. This card cuts the non-memory regions at their roots, so each unsafe fact is stated once in an audited home instead of at every call site.

criteria.text: The inventory's 'other' class is split into named classes (syscall, start-up state, host leaf, secret owner, crypto expert, and any further class the code shows), so no region is unclassified. Proof: jet Tools/Agent/UnsafeRatchet.jet --inventory prints 0 under other, and its test pins one region per class.

Syscalls: the OS layer has one typed wrapper per Linux syscall the runtime uses, each holding the only #Unsafe region for that syscall with its contract stated once. Runtime call sites call the wrappers and hold no region of their own. Proof: git grep -n os_syscall_i64 -- Compiler/JetRuntime outside the OS-layer wrapper file is empty, the inventory's syscall count equals the number of distinct syscalls, and the runtime fragment cases pass on O0, O1 and O2.

Start-up state: runtime state written once before other threads exist goes through one audited once-only primitive, so its writers hold no region. Proof: the inventory's start-up-state count is 1, and the runtime fragment cases pass on O0, O1 and O2.

Host leaves: Core calls runtime host leaves through the D-HOST-LEAF1=E ordinary-library route (#6615), so a Core call site holds no #Unsafe region for a host leaf. Proof: the inventory's host-leaf count under Core is 0.

Every remaining #Unsafe region names an irreducible reason (a raw action inside the kernel, a foreign crossing, or a ballot-approved expert boundary), and the ratchet's total falls with each step. Whether crypto expert primitives keep requiring #Unsafe is an owner choice on its own ballot. Proof: the ratchet baseline in Docs/Spec/safety.md falls in each landing commit, and the ballot is ratified.

Each core.os fact is computed once, in Core, not inside the runtime host, and reports the same value on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter OS/Facts` on O0, O1 and O2, with the core.os examples passing. (was #3549 c19)

Every runtime function Core calls is a pub function of jet_runtime with a Jet name, Jet types (Int, not I64; typed handles) and a declared effect row. A generated comparison over every bound function proves each declared row equals the effect_kind and effect_leaf the compiler row held before the cutover, with zero differences. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Runtime/declared_rows_match` shows zero differences. (was #6615 c4)

A safe package that names a runtime function that isn't pub fails with the ordinary visibility diagnostic, and reaching a runtime C symbol needs #Import(c) inside #Unsafe. Proof: a UI snapshot for each. (was #6615 c6)

The runtime is an ordinary library (D-HOST-LEAF1=E) and the IR route tables (IR_RUNTIME_ROUTES, the route.export rows and the generated handle helpers) are deleted, so Core's runtime calls take the ordinary call path.
