decisions.title: Read complete enum values as compile-time metadata
decisions.gist: Should a payload-free enum expose its complete values as compile-time metadata?
decisions.lesson: A payload is data stored inside a case. A payload-free case is already a complete value. Jet has typed compile-time facts; this proposal derives values from the same enum declaration. A reads metadata, C creates an iterator, and B keeps manual lists. None invents payloads, integer conversions, or a second case registry.
decisions.story: Mina builds a complete direction selector and derives its count before the program runs. Adding East must update both from one declaration. She still uses an explicit list when she wants a subset or a different display order. The owner asked whether this should be an @ metadata reader instead of a generated method. A now makes that distinction explicit.
decisions.inWild:
enum Direction: CaseIterable { case north, south }
print(Direction.allCases.count) // 2; adding east makes 3.
decisions.detail:
## Answer to the owner question

Yes. Recommended A now uses T.@values through the existing typed compile-time fact reader. It replaces the proposed T.cases() operation rather than adding an alias beside it. B still means manual lists. C makes the original iterator design an explicit alternative. No option has been selected.

## Exact contract

For an eligible nominal enum T with N checked leaf cases, T.@values returns an ordinary immutable fixed array [T#N]. Each item is a real T value. The result is compile-time data, not CaseInfo, an erased Value, or a stored mutable iterator. It can feed normal collection operations or an explicit ordinary iterator conversion. Each iteration has ordinary independent cursor state.

The reader uses the existing @ grammar and registered fact mechanism. Register this reader and its typed result in the existing declaration/fact registry, not a parser special case or a second enum registry. No new token, keyword, nominal collection type, package, or dependency is proposed. A grammar change would require a full ballot before implementation.

Generate the value expressions from the same checked enum leaf rows used by matching, construction and D-ENUM-CASEMETA1. Do not cast discriminants to enum values or rediscover names through runtime reflection. N is the array's ordinary constant length; this does not let arbitrary metadata values mint types.

T.reflect().cases remains the D-ENUM-CASEMETA1 catalog of descriptions, including payload shapes. T.@values is the typed inhabited-value projection for the strictly payload-free subset. These are different questions over one declaration owner, not interchangeable names or independently maintained tables. This ballot does not change CaseInfo, Value.case(), or reflection capture authority.

All flattened leaf cases must have unit payloads. A single Bool payload still has multiple possible values. A zero-size payload type still requires a payload. Reject a payload-bearing or non-enum receiver in Jet; do not omit ineligible cases or synthesize defaults. Respect the existing enum validity rules, including whether an empty enum is legal. A legal empty domain produces an empty array; a singleton produces one value.

Emit every declared leaf once in declaration order. Groups contribute paths, not extra values. Sparse explicit discriminants do not create gaps or define indices. The array preserves T's nominal identity. Its order is not a wire ordinal, and its length is not an ABI or future-version promise. Existing non-exhaustive and visibility rules remain law.

A complete query uses ordinary source access checks. If the caller cannot access a required case, reject the complete query rather than returning a filtered domain. Publishing a lawfully obtained collection is ordinary intentional publication. This does not grant a foreign generator new access rights.

The @ reader is compiler-owned under the existing fact namespace. Do not shadow user members, silently replace a declaration, or reserve an unmarked values/cases method under A. Use the registered diagnostic machinery for invalid reads. Explicit application lists remain available for subsets and custom ordering.

Keep the array at compile time when it only supplies counts or generated code. Runtime use follows normal fixed-array ownership and lowering, without a mandatory Vec conversion or heap allocation. This is not a zero-copy or measured-speed claim. It introduces no performance-only surface waiver.

## Other complete designs

B adds neither a fact nor a method. The application owns completeness, subset and presentation order. Existing reflection law still applies, but B adds no automatic typed value enumeration.

C generates T.cases() returning a fresh ordinary Iter<T>. It follows the same eligibility, completeness, order, visibility and nominal-type rules as A. It uses the existing iterator protocol, with no required intermediate heap collection. A conflicting cases member receives the ordinary duplicate-member diagnostic. C adds no @values reader. No design ships both A and C as aliases.

## Proof after owner ratification

Exercise the same Direction program before and after East. Check actual typed items, declaration order, flattened groups, sparse codes, empty/singleton behavior where legal, two independent iterations, and source refusals. Prove compile-time use and runtime collection use across applicable I9 execution modes. Check generated artifacts for the chosen ordinary representation. Do not claim runtime parity or a speed win from this proposal.

## Evidence and retained law

The captured source/witness home remains docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f03-finite-case-values. Source owners are crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:964-1008 and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:773-833,6905-6920. These prove existing fact routing and compile-time reflection, not the proposed @values implementation.

D-FACT-READ1=A as respelled by D-ONCE-AT1=D, D-META-CONST1=A, D-ENUM-CASEMETA1=A, D-UNIONTYPE1=A, D-TAG1, D-MAP-KEY1 and I1-I9 remain binding. This revision changes an unanswered proposal only.

decisions.title: Checked local obligations in existing tooling
decisions.gist: Should compiler tools show checked local obligations at a selected source point?
decisions.lesson: A local obligation is a checked duty at one source point, such as whether a name is being read before a write. A read window is the period in which that read still matters. A exposes the checker’s bounded record; B keeps today’s public facts. Neither turns missing data into permission.
decisions.story: Mina reads values in a loop and then calls values.push(3). At the point before push, she wants to know which binding owns values and whether a read is still active. A shows the checked write requirement and active views. B leaves her to reconstruct that answer from source and diagnostics.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

### mechanism

One additive typed payload within the existing SemIndex/canonical derivation projection; the existing checked compiler result carries that index. There is no core.compiler.index function, new command family, mutable compiler API or runtime core.compiler capability.

### fact boundary

Source content identity and exact before/after point; semantic binding identity, not spelling alone.

Reuse existing public type/mutability, target references and interface provenance.

Publish only checker-established access/move/view/invalidation/reachability/cleanup relations. Do not promise runtime values, exact alias sets or cleanup execution.

Retain current/unknown/unavailable/unsupported/stale/truncated distinctions and the static_derivation method.

No second analysis or independent fact store; selected facts come from existing check/projection producers.

Retain clean-check publication law. Invalid editor input has unavailable current data or an explicitly stale last-good record; no new privilege to publish recovered partial state as fresh valid facts.

### proof

READ-F10 requires actual selected-point outputs for shadowing, joins, moves, read-view last use, Fixed backing close, invalid input and stale edits. Coordinate BIG-F17 facade parity and READ-F16 nested schema authority.

### independent choice

READ-F01/D-READ-LOCAL1 may summarize current callable facts without this addition. Adding local fact records is independently decidable.

### distribution

Existing build/comptime-only core.compiler facade and developer tools. No new library or dependency; D-FOUND-COREAPI1’s eleven additions do not grant blanket future API approval.

### worked record

ballot-example-data.json binds the full source bytes, point and concrete JSON. Record is the proposed payload, not a complete current SemIndex document. Concrete definition/source IDs are fixture values; implementation reuses compiler-issued identities, not a new ID algorithm. Checked empty active views, unsupported cleanup, current/stale freshness and truncation remain distinct. Invalid input cannot publish this as current valid output.

### finite scope

READ-F10 enumerates all captured local fact planes in an availability matrix, including initialization, freezing, sendability, narrowing, typestate and compile-time string/path constraints. Reuse existing public facts; export only checker-established constraints. Unprojected/nonapplicable/unknown categories stay explicit and never mean no obligation. Raw runtime values are out of scope.

## corelib change

### library

core.compiler

### addition

checked local-obligation records through the existing checked-result semantic-index projection

### placement

existing immutable build/comptime-only facade and existing tooling

### dependency

none

### gate

D-READ-STATE1

## design away record

Reuse existing compiler-owned facts, identities, APIs and protocols; no second index, analyzer or dependency.

Keep ordinary source calls unchanged; request or expand detail only when needed.

Represent stale, redacted, unsupported and unavailable facts explicitly rather than invent values.

Retain source/build and captured-versus-executed limits; comparative usefulness and cost still require scoped proof.

## Recommendation reasoning

A gives Mina a bounded answer at the point before push while preserving unknown and unsupported states. B keeps the smallest API but leaves the local duty implicit.

Option B: B keeps existing facts but does not state the selected-point obligation. A exposes it without granting permission when data is missing.

decisions.title: Locate public compiler diagnostics in their source snapshot
decisions.gist: Should each compiler diagnostic identify the checked source snapshot for its byte span?
decisions.lesson: A byte span says which bytes were involved, but not which source file or text supplied them. A source snapshot is that exact checked input. Jet’s diagnostic has code, message, cause, fix and span, while imported diagnostics can lose their source identity. A stores optional origin data with the row; B keeps source context beside it. Neither changes program validity or the read-only facade.
decisions.story: Mira combines diagnostics from generated source. E0107 points to bytes 55–63, but a detached span does not say which input those bytes came from. A pairs the row with the known source digest and a null path for raw text. B leaves Mira to carry the path and digest in a sidecar. Both describe the same E0107.
decisions.detail:
Add optional origin to the existing read-only CompilerDiagnostic value, mirrored by the Rust DiagnosticView and existing compiler CLI JSON projection.

The proposed facade API/data version is2.

The origin is an optional structural record: path is optional text and source_digest is a lowercase64-character SHA256 of the exact UTF8 source bytes.

No new public type export, Core module, optional package, dependency or runtime compiler service is adopted.

A known raw source has a digest but may have path=null; never infer a physical path from a span.

Equal byte strings can have equal digests in different files/invocations, so this field is content provenance rather than universal declaration/request identity.

Reuse internal immutable source identity; do not recompute or copy the full source per diagnostic.

Keep build/comptime/E0956 restrictions.

Distinguish the compiler-facade API version from nested semantic-index/package schema versions.

Existing CLI/LSP source-origin repair is BIG-F08 regardless of this vote.

Exact proposed JSON value contract for CompilerDiagnostic.origin (a structural record, not invented Jet declaration syntax):
```json

  "type": [
    "object",
    "null"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "source_digest": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path",
    "source_digest"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```


decisions.title: How should a typed F32 list become a Tensor?
decisions.gist: Should a typed F32 list use from_list or a separately named F32 constructor?
decisions.lesson: F32 is a 32-bit floating-point value. A Tensor owns an array of such values. The current ordinary constructor follows Float/F64 source behavior. A preserves the input type through from_list; B adds from_list_f32. Both promise typed F32 storage and readback for the same one-value job, but neither has physical-storage proof yet.
decisions.story: Mira starts with the typed list [F32]{42.0}. A sends it through compute.from_list; B sends it through compute.from_list_f32. Both proposed jobs should return the typed list [42] from the Tensor. A uses the input type once; B repeats F32 in the operation name. Physical 4-byte storage remains a proof requirement, not a label.
decisions.inWild:
# CuPy adaptation; dtype is explicit; not run here.
import cupy as cp
x = cp.array([42.0], dtype=cp.float32)
assert x.dtype == cp.float32
assert x.nbytes == 4
print(cp.asnumpy(x))  # Intended:[42.].
decisions.detail:
A adds the typed F32 admission to the existing operation: `from_list(values:[F32]) Tensor<F32> !ComputeError`. B adds `from_list_f32(values:[F32]) Tensor<F32> !ComputeError` and leaves the old from_list route unchanged. Both use ordinary Core calls; neither adds parser syntax or a new tensor owner. The shown `show(values:[F32])` function makes the intended result element type explicit.

Both borrow the input for construction and return an owned rank-one tensor with the same F32 values and input length. The result cannot expose future mutation of the borrowed list as a hidden tensor mutation. Physical numeric storage remains32-bit across construction, device transfer and typed readback. There is no F64 staging, numeric narrowing or profile-only retagging. Existing allocation, size, finite-value and shape errors remain typed ComputeError results.

Empty typed input has shape[0], not an unknown dtype.

Existing ordinary Float input keeps its Float/F64 behavior. The current captured from_list takes Vec<f64> and builds Arc<Vec<f64>>. That source does not establish this new physical F32 path. The older constructor packet has current-line equality evidence but no historical file digest; the newer Core API packet records its captured source hashes. Neither is execution proof.

The source-facing choice is narrow: infer F32 from a typed list or also spell F32 in the function name. It does not admit authored U32 kernels, choose an atomic-cell constructor, alter the ratified launch, or approve a device compiler dependency. The separate U32 and Atomic drafts show their own exact admissions. Both F32 options must integrate with the same Tensor/View owner and target metadata.

The CuPy comparison establishes an explicit float32 constructor and physical byte-width check as a peer mechanism. Its script is an unexecuted adaptation, not a benchmark. In Jet, prove the returned [F32] consumer boundary, four-byte physical elements, shape and value preservation. Test non-finite rejection, actual allocation refusal, empty input, mixed typing and transfer/readback without assuming a profile string proves storage width.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-COMPUTE-TYPE1 remains the one Tensor/View owner law. D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1 is unchanged. Every new spelling is a proposal. Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

Existing ordinary Float input keeps its Float/F64 behavior. The current captured from_list takes Vec<f64> and builds Arc<Vec<f64>>. That source does not establish this new physical F32 path. The older constructor packet has current-line equality evidence but no historical file digest; the newer Core API packet records its captured source hashes. Neither is execution proof.

The source-facing choice is narrow: infer F32 from a typed list or also spell F32 in the function name. It does not admit authored U32 kernels, choose an atomic-cell constructor, alter the ratified launch, or approve a device compiler dependency. The separate U32 and Atomic drafts show their own exact admissions. Both F32 options must integrate with the same Tensor/View owner and target metadata.

The CuPy comparison establishes an explicit float32 constructor and physical byte-width check as a peer mechanism. Its script is an unexecuted adaptation, not a benchmark. In Jet, prove the returned [F32] consumer boundary, four-byte physical elements, shape and value preservation. Test non-finite rejection, actual allocation refusal, empty input, mixed typing and transfer/readback without assuming a profile string proves storage width.

Storage, ownership, errors and results are otherwise identical.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-COMPUTE-TYPE1 remains the one Tensor/View owner law. D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1 is unchanged. Every new spelling is a proposal. Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

decisions.title: Observe remaining bounds with one runtime query
decisions.gist: Should remaining size use one runtime query rather than compile-time metadata?
decisions.lesson: A cursor changes as it yields items. Compile-time metadata cannot describe a live cursor’s changing remainder. A adds one non-consuming query returning lower and optional upper bounds. Equal bounds mean an exact count. B keeps consuming count only. Both retain existing compile-time facts and ordinary evaluation rules.
decisions.story: Ravi reads one record and then reserves space for the remainder. The size answer must fall from three to two without reading the next record. The owner asked whether this belongs in @ metadata. The answer separates stable compile-time facts from changing runtime state, while removing the previously proposed extra trait and exact-size method.
decisions.detail:
## Answer to the owner question

A changing remaining count is not an @ metadata field. @ reads compiler-known facts or demands evaluation of known inputs. It cannot inspect a live file, channel, predicate result or partially consumed runtime cursor before that state exists. A runtime property named with @ would give the mark a second meaning.

Stable declaration facts may still use the existing metadata mechanism. The ordinary evaluator may compute a size expression when all needed inputs and operations are available at compile time. Neither case requires a duplicate public @remaining API. This proposal does not widen compile-time effects or promise that every iterator runs in the evaluator.

## One public query, ordinary types

Recommended A adds size_hint() to the existing Iterator/Iter capability contract. It is a non-consuming observation returning the ordinary pair (lower: Int, upper: ?Int). Default knowledge is (0, None). Both numbers, when present, are nonnegative. A supplied upper must be at least lower. Equal bounds state an exact remaining yielded-item count; unequal or absent bounds do not.

Remove the earlier proposal's separate ExactRemaining capability and remaining_len() method. Consumers needing exactness inspect the same pair and handle absence normally. There is no new size wrapper, capability hierarchy, precision flag, or second public query. Ordinary len/count operations keep their existing consuming meanings.

The query must not call next, poll a live source, invoke mapping/filtering callbacks, or change cursor position. It reports knowledge about that source's current state, not its original input length. Source protocols preserve their existing ownership, effects and borrowing rules. A later advancing operation invalidates any application assumption that an earlier pair describes the new remainder.

An absent upper means unknown or not representable by the declared bound representation; it does not prove infinity. Bounds count yielded items, not bytes, memory usage, cost, or future success. A separate end-of-stream or cancellation contract is not encoded in this pair. A temporarily empty poll is not a permanently exhausted source.

A source may return conservative bounds. Safe user-provided hints never authorize unchecked indexing, uninitialized elements, or unchecked allocation arithmetic. Consumers remain memory-safe if an implementation gives a false hint. Internal proven facts may support optimization only under their existing proof rules.

## Propagation and boundaries

Map preserves cardinality when its existing contract yields one output per input. Filter and filter_map generally lower the guaranteed count to zero while retaining a lawful upper. Chain combines bounds with checked representability; overflow never wraps into a false exact count. Zip uses lawful minimum bounds. Take caps them. Exactness is the result of these ordinary rules, not a separate trait claim.

Mixed front/back advancement updates the same remaining range once that independently gated operation is implemented. No item may be duplicated. A permanently exhausted wrapper remains exhausted. Do not label a resumable source fused from an empty poll. Dynamic failures, stop and cancel retain their ratified distinct meanings.

The same internal cardinality knowledge should serve queries, adapter propagation and compiler analysis. Do not add a second public type hierarchy or require dynamic allocation to carry it. Reuse current copy/view provenance, callback ownership and Stream/task rules. Do not change extrema or top-k tie laws while implementing size propagation.

## Alternative B

B adds no non-consuming query. Existing metadata facts remain available, but they cannot answer live remaining state. Existing len/count consumes the source, invokes its normal effects, and may not terminate on an unbounded source. Explicit application tracking remains possible without acquiring a new core capability.

## Proof and scope

After ratification, run the same three-item cursor before and after next(). Check exact, filtered, unknown/live, empty, unbounded and checked-overflow cases. Ensure the query does not invoke callbacks or advance input. Check dishonest safe hints cannot compromise memory safety. Exercise mixed-direction behavior with its own approved dependency, rather than claiming that draft feature now works.

No new dependency, module, grammar or I1-I9 exception is proposed. AOT, default run and applicable interpreter/web paths must share meaning. This is a state-observation feature, not a measured speed claim. Comparing consuming and non-consuming programs cannot establish a matched performance win. Existing performance-gated drafts remain gated.

## Evidence

crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:1137-1188 defines the current private JetIter wrapper and consuming len. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:773-833 places static reflection and fact reads before code generation. crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:125-133,964-1008 defines the current @ mark and fact dispatch. These are source observations, not runtime receipts.

Retain ITER-F005 and ITER-F022 evidence in docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md. D-FACT-READ1=A as respelled by D-ONCE-AT1=D, D-META-EFFECT1=A, D-ITER-HOOK, D-ITER-RESUME1=A, D-MEM-COPYSEM1 and I1-I9 govern implementation. This revision changes an unanswered proposal only.

decisions.lesson: A backward iterator can take the next item from the remaining back as well as the front. Example: The capable source is [1, 2, 3]. Read from the front, then from the back, without crossing the cursor. Expected output: The reads are 1 then 3, leaving [2]; a one-way source cannot do the back read. Authored NOT RUN.
decisions.story: Same job: The capable source is [1, 2, 3]. Read from the front, then from the back, without crossing the cursor. Expected output: The reads are 1 then 3, leaving [2]; a one-way source cannot do the back read. Authored illustration; NOT RUN.

let out: Vec<_> = [1,2,3].into_iter().rev().collect();

A backward iterator can take the next item from the remaining back as well as the front.

Same job (authored illustration; NOT RUN):

Input: The capable source is [1, 2, 3].

Expected output: The reads are 1 then 3, leaving [2]; a one-way source cannot do the back read.

Both options use this same job. Only the choice named by each option changes.

decisions.title: Make permanent exhaustion explicit
decisions.gist: Should a source declare or request permanent exhaustion?
decisions.lesson: A fused iterator stays finished after its first end result. Example: A source returns 1, then no item, then would otherwise return 2. decisions.title: Borrow a source without copying its items
decisions.gist: Should one iterator loan support borrowed items and resumable adapters?
decisions.lesson: A borrowed view reads the same source storage without taking ownership of it. Example: The source storage is [10, 20, 30]; read two items through a borrowed adapter. A keeps a checked loan and then resumes the owner; B collects owned adapter input first. Expected output: The borrowed prefix is [10,20] and the owner can continue at 30 after the loan ends. Authored NOT RUN.

decisions.title: One GPU calculation: return one answer or place several?
decisions.gist: May one GPU calculation place several answers?
decisions.lesson: A kernel is a function repeated on a graphics processor. Each run gets a position, starting at zero. A view reads an existing array; a writable view also changes it. F32 is a 32-bit fractional number. Both examples turn [3,5] into [9,25,-9,-25].
decisions.explainer:
Beginner path: ordinary one-answer functions keep the approved launch call; no output array needs to be created. Expert path: both options add indexed reading of existing arrays. A also permits one writable destination whose positions the compiler proves safe. The host call still returns the completed result.

Reading key: #Kernel(.parallel) marks independent repeated calculations. Invocation supplies linear, this run's position, and extent, the number of runs. View<F32> reads numbers without taking their owner; ViewMut<F32> writes them. :: binds a name, xs[i] selects position i, % gives the remainder, and -> F32 names the return type. A runs twice and writes two positions each time. B runs four times and returns one number each time.

Shared work: add indexed input reading and position facts to the existing checked launch. Preserve its real-GPU default, explicit CPU reference choice, completion, error, ownership, and numeric rules. This vote does not approve a separate checker or execution engine.
decisions.story: Maya squares two signal values and needs both signs of each square. She wants all four answers in one array.
decisions.detail:
Decision audit: D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1=A approves compute.launch(kernel, inputs: tuple). It returns one value per input position, with expert output/grid/device/stream controls. D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1=A and D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1=A are ratified, despite the old draft calling them pending. Neither they nor the later group/atomic/ranked/helper rulings decides this amendment.

D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A requires public APIs to return new answers. It preserves real reusable storage and private machine destinations. Host launch returns a Tensor in both options. A's terminal write-view callback needs explicit owner acceptance if classified as an output-only callback. That approval would not permit output-only public APIs elsewhere.

Current source: Core/compute/compute.jet:41-46 declares Tensor with shape, [Float] data, device and numeric_profile. A targeted search finds no launch, Invocation, resources or ViewMut in that file. Neither proposed indexed program is established as working. No program or GPU timing was run. Historical frozen executable evidence is not a receipt for current source.

Common proposal: compute.Invocation is the explicit first kernel parameter. Only launch/reference execution creates it. Read-only linear:Int is in [0,extent); extent:Int counts logical runs. resources:(xs,) supplies corresponding read-only View<F32> parameters from compatible Tensor owners or views. Inputs remain borrowed through completion. A resource-only call requires grid:[N]. With scalar inputs, the existing common shape supplies the domain.

Resource lengths may differ only when source proof and runtime lengths permit it. No implicit copy repairs incompatible layout. Read views and independent output are rank-one F32, including valid strides. Ranked contracts remain separate. Size, offset, stride, byte-range and index overflow fail before submission.

Shared setup: use core.compute as compute. Inside fn run(), create xs :: compute.from_list([F32]{3,5}) ?? panic("{err}"). A also creates buffer :: compute.from_list([F32]{0,0,0,0}) ?? panic("{err}"). A calls out :: compute.launch(pair, resources: (xs,), grid: [2], output: ^buffer) ?? panic("{err}").

B calls out :: compute.launch(pair, resources: (xs,), grid: [4]) ?? panic("{err}"). Both finish with print(compute.to_list(out)), intending [9,25,-9,-25]. These proposed call contexts were not executed. ^ moves ownership; ?? panic shows the actual error and stops.

Default launch requires a compatible real GPU, never an implicit CPU substitute. device:compute.device_cpu() explicitly selects the reference. Unavailable or unsupported providers error. F32Strict preserves 32-bit operations and rounding; Reproducible preserves declared order. No hidden F64 staging, contraction, reassociation or reduced precision is allowed. The shared compiler checks sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers and control. Providers consume checked facts rather than redo language checking.

Successful launch returns completed storage, never a pending token. Inputs live through completion. A moved output is consumed even on runtime validation or execution error. No partial output or restored owner is returned. Retry requires valid new output storage; device loss may also require recreated inputs. Only audited provider adapters may use the existing unsafe boundary.

Performance blocker: A is a new performance-motivated surface. Its registered complete candidate/plain pair and strict measured win are missing. Source evaluation counts do not establish speed: B might be optimized. AGENTS.md:165-168 requires a strict win, not parity. Compare identical inputs, all four outputs, F32 meaning, setup, submission, transfers, completion and generated work on every required cell and metric. B does not authorize A or waive this gate.

options.name: Let the function place both answers

Ordinary one-answer kernels stay available. Beginner calls remain unchanged; experts supply output storage when one run writes several positions.
options.technical:
A kernel either returns one F32 per run or returns Unit with one final ViewMut<F32> parameter. It cannot combine the forms. Launch supplies the final parameter, never resources. Fresh output defaults to N positions. output:^buffer may supply another rank-one length when complete coverage is proved. The example runs twice against four output positions.

One operation-wide exclusive output loan must prove in-range stores and no input/output byte overlap. It rejects output reads before initialization, duplicate writes, holes and escaped writable references. Helpers contribute complete checked access facts; opaque helpers cannot bypass proof. Prove ranges [0,N) and [N,2N) generally, not by recognizing this program.

A repeated second write to out[at.linear] rejects with an overlap/missing-position diagnostic. Restoring +at.extent repairs it. A too-short buffer returns the existing compute error before submission. Empty grid plus empty output returns an empty Tensor. An empty grid cannot initialize nonempty output. Explicitly approve this narrow terminal kernel callback under D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1, not a general output-parameter exemption. The performance gate remains a pre-ratification blocker.

Each run returns one F32; launch writes it at that run's position. For N=4, indices modulo 2 read positions 0,1,0,1; the branch chooses positive, positive, negative, negative. Input length must satisfy the checked read precondition before submission. Empty work returns empty output. All shared validation, completion, provider and precision rules remain. decisions.title: One enum case reflection model
decisions.gist: Should the existing reflection model expose enum cases and active payload fields?
decisions.lesson: An enum selects a case and payload—the attached value. A/C generate complete catalogs or reject inaccessible nested details. A returns a handle holding an independent ordinary value copy. It refuses shared mutable data and unproved field access. Passing a lawful handle exports its captured fields. B writes catalogs and matches. C generates catalogs but keeps runtime matching.
decisions.story: Mina writes a documentation generator and a reusable enum inspector. The generator should include new cases automatically. The inspector should handle different payload types without new case arms. She must not accidentally expose private nested data or retain live shared state.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

A and C add case descriptions to the existing compiler-owned Core reflection module. A also adds runtime case inspection. B adds neither. The new projections are TypeInfo.cases and Value.case(); this proposal adds no enum-only module, runtime type registry, permission token, capture flag, freezing operation, or new ownership trait.

### One checked row model

TypeInfo.cases: [CaseInfo] uses the existing registered declaration rows. CaseInfo contains name:String, path:String, payload:CasePayload, discriminant:?Int, markers:[MarkerInfo], and span:SourceSpan. CasePayload is Unit, Single(Type), or Named([FieldInfo]). Type, FieldInfo, MarkerInfo, and SourceSpan are existing reflection descriptions. FieldInfo.ty is the payload field's Type handle. No sample payload value is constructed to describe its type.

A adds Value.case(): ?Case. Case.name(), path(), and fields() describe the active alternative and return existing typed Field handles. Field.name() names a field; Field.value() returns a typed Value, not a String. Value.display() is the existing operation that produces text. There is no new get, read, cast, write-by-name, or constructor operation.

A unit case has no fields. A single unnamed payload has one synthetic field named value. Named payloads preserve their declared field names and order. A non-sum type has an empty cases catalog; a non-sum Value.case() returns None. That shape result is separate from source refusal for inaccessible or unsnapshotable data. The generic inspector below explicitly panics on an unintended non-sum input; it does not use a runtime permission failure.

Named enums expose declaration-ordered flattened leaf cases. Groups contribute to paths but are not values or separate rows. Structural sums use their existing canonical member order and canonical member type names; written order does not invent new identities. Canonical option/result rows use their registered case order. Generic rows describe instantiated payload types. None of these rules reopen D-TAG1, D-UNIONTYPE1, or the independent payload-free value iterator in D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1.

Let P be the existing canonical path of Message. Text(String) has name Text, path P + ".Text", payload Single(String's Type handle), and no explicit discriminant. A group Action containing Text yields P + ".Action.Text". For enum Mode { Read = 1 Write = 4 }, Write's discriminant is Val(4), not its row index or a JSON name. Markers remain checked source/expanded facts. Custom codec output is not guessed from a declaration row.

### The visibility rule is complete-or-refuse

A and C check a cases query in the ordinary source context that checks that expression. They reuse existing private, pub(package), and pub visibility. A type being public does not make all of its stored payload details public. A generator receiving a Type argument gains no extra authority from the type's owner.

Before returning any case catalog, checking must establish permission for all the declaration information reachable through its rows and payload type/field descriptions. This includes nested structs and sums, instantiated type arguments, and the markers/spans attached to those exposed rows. An inaccessible reachable detail makes the entire query a source error. There is no filtered list, placeholder row, partial schema, or silent omission. The catalog is therefore complete when it is returned, or unavailable to that caller.

This is a finite check over the existing registered type graph, not recursive construction of values. Revisiting a recursive type closes the graph edge; it does not omit that type's other fields or leaves. Built-in String and container implementation internals are not new reflected rows. The check follows the compiler's existing exposed row model and relevant instantiated element types, not private allocation machinery.

| Catalog query location | A/C outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Defining source context can read every reachable detail. | Return the full catalog. |
| Same package can read all required pub(package) details. | Return the full catalog. |
| Another package cannot read one nested private or package-visible detail. | Reject the whole query before any CaseInfo is returned. |
| All relevant types, fields, and case details are public. | A foreign generator may return the complete catalog. |
| A generic query has not resolved enough type information to check access. | Reject the unresolved query; do not emit incomplete runtime metadata. |

An owner may deliberately publish a catalog or generated String obtained by a lawful query, just as it may publish other ordinary data. That is intentional publication, not a foreign generator receiving the owner's privileges. Further independent reflection queries still use the normal context that checks them. A/C do not silently rewrite existing visibility rules.

### Runtime authority closes over every derived Value

A's capture is checked before reflect.of erases the source type. The original capture site must be allowed to read the entire transitive graph that runtime field/case projections can expose. Follow each stored field, every possible sum payload, nested struct/sum, and relevant instantiated element type. Apply the same rule again to the type of every Value that Field.value() could return. Recursive type edges are checked through the finite registered graph. Checking only the outer case or the currently selected leaf is insufficient.

Consequently, outer.case().fields()[i].value().case() cannot discover a new permission question. Either the original proof already covers that nested case and every further derived Value, or no root capture is created. There is no later receiver-package check, newly invented permission object, truncated nested view, or private-field fallback. The same closure applies when an existing struct Value can lead to a nested case; starting from a struct is not a bypass.

The root reflect.of call retains the existing Display eligibility rule. Display permits ordinary text output, not arbitrary field access. Nested Field.value() handles use the existing typed field/display operations; this does not introduce a separate Display requirement or new string-only field model. A custom Display implementation cannot override the transitive access or ordinary value-copy checks.

A lawful Value, Case, or Field can be passed to a generic inspector in another package. It intentionally conveys read access to its captured data, including nested private fields that the original provider was permitted to capture. Recipients gain no construction or mutation operation and no access to uncaptured state. Export sanitized text instead when a complete captured handle would disclose too much.

### Snapshot means ordinary value-copy semantics, not freezing

A must take an owned ordinary Jet value copy at capture. For every reachable payload, the normal language value-copy rules must guarantee that later edits through the original value cannot change the captured value. Native strings, records, sums, and value-semantic collections use those existing rules. Physical sharing for copy-on-write storage is allowed only because ordinary mutation already isolates the copies. This ballot adds no deep-freeze operation, locking rule, reference registry, or bespoke graph copier.

A type graph containing observable shared mutable state, borrowed/live handles, or resource state without ordinary snapshot-preserving value-copy semantics is refused at source checking. Shared<T> anywhere in that graph is refused, even under a custom Display implementation or an inactive enum leaf. A user-defined Clone operation is not proof of an independent snapshot. If the ordinary checker cannot prove the required value-copy property, it refuses capture rather than retaining a live alias or replacing the semantic value with display text.

A captured nested value therefore shows its old contents after a permitted original-value mutation. A fresh capture shows the later contents. Derived Value/Case/Field handles refer to that same captured value, and remain valid after the original local ends. The copy strategy, physical allocation count, and speed remain unmeasured; the old-versus-later result does not. B and C add no snapshot mechanism and may keep ordinary live application processing.

### Read the notation before the examples

A compiler checks source before the program runs. @catalog asks it to compute the catalog then; {@catalog} puts that computed text into the program's print call. case_text<T> has a type parameter T. case_text<Message>() supplies the concrete Message type before the reflection query is checked.

A :: binding keeps one value. A := binding permits later assignment with =. [String] means a list of strings. loop visits each item; the generated catalog and runtime inspector both visit all of their returned items. In a match, .Text(s) binds the attached value to s. Value is an erased reflection handle: the inspector knows the operations it supports, not the original Message type.

?Case means Val(case) or None. The inspector's ?? panic("expected sum") makes a mistaken non-sum input explicit. It is not a runtime permission check: inaccessible or noncopyable captures never produce a usable handle.

### The complete shared workload

The documentation job lists every declared case and its payload shape. The inspector job handles Text("hello"), Count(7), and Quit. All current/A/B/C programs below have these Expected observations; all are source-composed and NOT RUN:

```text
Cases
Quit
Text(String)
Count(Int)
Text
value:String=hello
Count
value:Int=7
Quit
```

B writes the catalog text and a Message-specific visitor. C computes the catalog, then uses that same explicit visitor. A computes the catalog and passes each lawful erased Value to inspect. inspect never names Message, Text, Count, or a payload type, and never indexes field 0. It iterates all active fields, including an empty unit field list. The fixed Display text Message only permits root capture; the printed payload comes from Field.value().display().

### The generic compile-time generator

case_text<T> below is an ordinary generic helper, not a new Core operation. The @catalog binding evaluates its Message instance during compilation. Its loop visits every returned row, and its Named arm visits every field. The generated program retains the resulting String, not Type handles, markers, source spans, or TypeInfo tables. @ interpolation prints that generated String.

```jet
fn case_text<T>() String -> {
    text := "Cases"
    loop row in T.reflect().cases -> {
        if row.payload == {
            .Unit -> text = "{text}\n{row.name}",
            .Single(t) -> text = "{text}\n{row.name}({t.name})",
            .Named(fields) -> {
                text = "{text}\n{row.name}"
                loop field in fields -> text = "{text}\n  {field.name}:{field.ty.name}"
            }
        }
    }
    return text
}
```

A and C include this entire helper in their full option code. The surface calls it by name and identifies it as this helper, not a builtin. Generic checking uses the existing concrete instantiation and source context. A resolved instance with sufficient access succeeds; an unresolved or inaccessible instance fails. No new Reflectable bound or permission parameter is introduced.

A runtime inspector is generic in a different way: inspect(v: Value) receives an already lawful erased value. It does not need the original source type because capture already proved the complete authority and value-copy graph. It must not perform a fresh unproved capture after erasure.

### Make the change that distinguishes the options

Add Flag(Bool) to Message and append Message.Flag(true) to the input list.

Under A, neither case_text nor inspect changes. Expected: the catalog adds Flag(Bool), and inspection adds Flag followed by value:Bool=true. The concrete capture remains eligible if the new leaf satisfies the same existing access/value-copy rules. Adding a leaf that fails those rules produces a source refusal, not a partial inspector.

Under C, case_text still includes Flag(Bool), but the explicit describe match must add .Flag(b) -> "Flag\nvalue:Bool={b}" before the program is complete. Under B, the same visitor edit is needed, and the literal catalog must also add Flag(Bool). Omitting B's catalog edit can leave stale documentation even after its visitor is fixed. These are Expected source consequences, NOT RUN, not invented diagnostic wording.

### Nested private data: reject at the first capture/query

This two-package source composition fixes the exact nested disclosure question. The default-private Payload.text is readable in provider/messages.jet, but not in app. The public Outer and Inner declarations do not make that field public.

```jet
// provider/package.jet
name: "provider"
version: "0.1.0"
// app/package.jet
name: "app"
version: "0.1.0"
deps: { provider: ../provider }
// provider/messages.jet
use core.reflect as reflect
pub struct Payload { text: String }
pub enum Inner { Data(Payload) }
pub enum Outer { Item(Inner) impl Display { fn display(self) String -> "Outer" } }
pub fn make() Outer -> Outer.Item(Inner.Data(Payload{ text: "secret" }))
pub fn exported_snapshot() Value -> reflect.of(make())
// app/run.jet
use provider
use core.reflect as reflect
fn rejected_capture() { value :: reflect.of(provider.make()) }
@rejected_catalog :: provider.Outer.reflect().cases
```

Expected under A: rejected_capture is a source refusal before any Value is produced. Under A/C: rejected_catalog is a source refusal before any CaseInfo is produced. Both refusals arise from the same nested Payload.text visibility fact. Do not run this combined file as a successful fixture; it deliberately contains two failing declarations. Exact diagnostics are not claimed.

Remove those two deliberately rejected declarations and use this separate client body to demonstrate intentional provider disclosure:

```jet
use provider
fn run() {
    outer :: provider.exported_snapshot()
    inner :: (outer.case() ?? panic("expected Outer")).fields()[0].value()
    payload :: (inner.case() ?? panic("expected Inner")).fields()[0].value()
    print(payload.fields()[0].value().display())
}
```

Expected under A: secret. NOT RUN. The provider's exported_snapshot query/capture is lawful in its defining context; passing that handle intentionally exports the nested readable value. The indexes in this small nesting witness refer to the fixed Item/Data/text shape only. The reusable inspector above does not rely on indexes. Calling case() or fields() on a derived handle cannot expand its authority beyond the already proved captured graph.

### Mutate a nested ordinary value after capture

This uses the same Value/Field model beneath a case projection. A struct root is included deliberately: an existing struct handle must not bypass the rule when its fields later lead to a case.

```jet
use core.reflect as reflect
struct Inner { texts: [String] }
struct State { inner: Inner impl Display { fn display(self) String -> "State" } }
fn run() {
    state := State{ inner: Inner{ texts: ["old"] } }
    saved :: reflect.of(state)
    state.inner.texts[0] = "new"
    texts :: saved.fields()[0].value().fields()[0].value()
    print(texts.display() == reflect.of(["old"]).display())
    print(texts.display() == reflect.of(["new"]).display())
    print(state.inner.texts[0])
}
```

Expected under A: true, then false, then new. NOT RUN. The saved nested list still has old, while the original nested list has new. Comparing with the ordinary display of each one-element list avoids inventing punctuation for list formatting. This is a requirement on semantic value-copy behavior, not permission to store only those display strings. A physical copy-on-write list is acceptable only if its existing mutation semantics yield this result.

The corresponding active-case replacement is also explicit:

```jet
use core.reflect as reflect
enum Message { Text(String) impl Display { fn display(self) String -> "Message" } }
fn run() {
    message := Message.Text("old")
    saved :: reflect.of(message)
    message = Message.Text("new")
    old_case :: saved.case() ?? panic("expected sum")
    new_case :: reflect.of(message).case() ?? panic("expected sum")
    print(old_case.fields()[0].value().display())
    print(new_case.fields()[0].value().display())
}
```

Expected under A: old, then new. NOT RUN. saved still describes the captured Text("old"), even though the original variable now holds Text("new").

### Shared mutable data is refused, not secretly frozen

```jet
use core.reflect as reflect
struct Item { text: String }
enum AliasMessage {
    Empty
    Data(Shared<Item>)
    impl Display { fn display(self) String -> "AliasMessage" }
}
fn refused(message: AliasMessage) {
    saved :: reflect.of(message)
}
```

Expected under A: refuse the reflect.of call during source checking. No saved handle exists, so there is no later-mutation ambiguity to defer to runtime. The custom Display implementation does not help. The static AliasMessage graph contains Shared<Item>; even an Empty input does not authorize a special-case capture. NOT RUN. A/C may still describe this type in a context with lawful catalog visibility, because a description does not copy a live Shared value. B/C ordinary visitors remain available for processing its live data under existing language rules.

### Generic code does not gain the type owner's privileges

Use the provider package above and the already defined case_text helper:

```jet
use provider
use core.reflect as reflect
fn capture<T>(value: T) Value -> reflect.of(value)
@foreign_catalog :: case_text<provider.Outer>()
fn rejected() { saved :: capture(provider.make()) }
```

Expected: reject foreign_catalog under A/C and reject the capture instance in rejected under A. NOT RUN. The concrete type is known, but app still cannot read provider.Payload.text. A known type is necessary for checking, not a substitute for permission. The same helpers instantiated with a fully accessible ordinary Message succeed under the proposed contract. A caller that only has an unresolved type or an erased value must not cause a hidden runtime access check; it supplies a previously lawful Value to inspect instead.

### Read the Zig comparison without inventing parity

Zig’s @typeInfo obtains the union descriptions.

inline for visits every field during compilation; @typeName prints its native type spelling.

The ordinary for and switch process the same three runtime values, binding each active payload.

std.debug.print writes these Expected observations to stderr.

void denotes a unit payload; []const u8 and i64 are Zig's spellings in this example.

Jet's worked labels are String and Int.

Native type spellings differ; no cross-language type identity is asserted.

The peer comparison is a source-composed illustration, NOT RUN, and does not demonstrate Jet's capture authority or snapshot behavior.

Sources: https://ziglang.org/documentation/0.15.2/#typeInfo, https://ziglang.org/documentation/0.15.2/#typeName, and https://ziglang.org/documentation/0.15.2/#tagName. The current peer capture establishes the reflection model; the worked program remains unexecuted.

### Evidence and authority, not implementation proof

Existing capture reader-reflection-primitives.md supplies the current Value/Field method signatures and source paths. reader-package-phase-primitives.md supplies the package/phase teaching context. adversarial-reflection-access.md (SHA-256 62fbb98d01fc98b74ac4fb88407f4b8810b9a4aa27ea0d0c04edd7f7e6976345) records the root Display gate, registered rows, erased runtime visibility, and transferable handle representation. It does not establish a reflection-specific cross-package rule or exact Tower status for D-METAREFLECT1.

The captured D-METAREFLECT1 spec text requires one registered row model and semantic typed field values, not pre-stringified copies. The captured source bodies do not by themselves prove that requirement across execution routes. The creation-time transitive access rule, complete-or-refuse catalog rule, and ordinary-copy snapshot eligibility above are explicit proposed terms of A/C, not inferred current conformance. Main must reconcile them with the owning reflection law and prove the selected behavior before any implementation claim.

No source, compiler, runtime, test, probe, build, lint, formatter, or new capture was run for this final author repair. The Expected labels define proposed observable outcomes. Quantitative copy cost, storage layout, route parity, and exact diagnostic wording remain unmeasured. These author repairs are not execution evidence; the separately bound reader receipts determine their review status.


### Read the names, indexes and noncopyable boundary

`T.reflect()` asks for T's compile-time type description.

Under A/C, the proposed `.cases` projection adds its complete case rows.

A row's `.name` is its declared case name.

A payload `Type` descriptor's `.name` is its displayed type label: the worked types here are exactly String, Int and Bool.

`Value.type_name()` returns that captured value's type label as a String; `Value.display()` returns its displayed value.

Thus a String payload holding hello contributes `value:String=hello`; 7 contributes `value:Int=7`; Flag(true) contributes `value:Bool=true`.

Names are display labels, not a substitute for checking type identity.

This explains the operations already used by these workloads, not a second type-name API.

Indexes start at zero: `[0]` selects the first item.

In the private-data witness, Outer's Item case has one field containing Inner.

Its first projection gives `inner`.

Inner's Data case has one field containing Payload; its first projection gives `payload`.

Payload's first struct field is `text`, whose saved value displays secret.

In the mutation witness, State's first field is `inner`; Inner's first field is `texts`.

The two `.fields()[0].value()` steps therefore reach the saved list.

`state.inner.texts[0]` addresses the first element of the original list, not that saved list.

The last witness's first Text field is the saved or newly captured string.

These fixed-shape examples do not replace the generic inspector's loops.

A callback supplies a concrete noncopyable part, separate from Shared's aliasing issue:

```jet
use core.reflect as reflect
enum CallbackMessage {
    Idle
    Work(fn(Int) Int)
    impl Display { fn display(self) String -> "CallbackMessage" }
}
fn visit(message: ^CallbackMessage) Int -> if message == {
    .Idle -> 0
    .Work(callback) -> callback(7)
}
fn refused(message: CallbackMessage) {
    saved :: reflect.of(message)
}
fn run() {
    for_visit :: CallbackMessage.Work((n: Int) -> (n + 1))
    print(visit(^for_visit))
    for_capture :: CallbackMessage.Work((n: Int) -> (n + 1))
    refused(for_capture)
}
```

Expected under A: source checking refuses `reflect.of(message)`; the complete program runs nothing.

NOT RUN.

The root has Display, but Work contains a function value.

Ordinary copying requires duplicable parts, and a function value is not duplicable.

Even Idle cannot bypass this static type-graph check.

The move marker ^ gives the visitor ownership; if message == inspects that owned case and binds its callback without copying it.

The caller must not reuse for_visit.

A separate for_capture value isolates the refused capture.

Remove refused and its call to run only the ordinary visitor; its intended result is 8 under every option.

Replacing Work's callback with an ordinary Int, and adjusting construction and the visitor to that Int, removes this noncopyable part.

A user-defined Clone that invents a replacement callback would not prove an ordinary value copy of the captured callback; the same static eligibility check still applies.

Source grounding, not a new execution: `tests/ui/copy_verb_not_cloneable.jet` uses the same `(n: Int) -> (n + 1)` callback and refuses `~f`; its retained E0211 snapshot explains duplicable parts. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Reflect.rs` defines Value.type_name and Value.display. The proposed case projection and capture rules still require implementation proof.


## ratified constraints

D-METAREFLECT1

D-UNIONTYPE1=A

D-TAG1

options.name: Extend existing reflection
options.detail:
A adds the complete TypeInfo.cases catalog and active Value.case() projection to existing Core reflection.

Both creation-time access and ordinary value-copy eligibility close transitively over all derived Values.

Catalogs and captures are complete or source-refused, never filtered.

Ordinary value copies preserve old nested contents; shared mutable or noncopyable graphs are refused.

The full program generates every catalog row and passes Text, Count, and Quit through one erased-Value inspector without field indexes or named-case branches.

A lawful exported handle intentionally discloses its complete captured graph.

decisions.title: Use project policy automatically and trust one launch explicitly
decisions.gist: How should project policy and trusted launches approve effects?
decisions.lesson: Effects are actions such as waiting or reading files. Metadata is project information in package {} or package.jet. Its policy lists allowed and denied effects. Apply that policy automatically. --trust and -T trust only this launch. Trust once means the same. Explicit denies and language safety still win.
decisions.story: Mira wrote a local script and wants it to run without repeated questions. Her team still needs checked project policy and an audit trail.
decisions.inWild:
deno run --allow-read=./data main.ts
deno run --allow-all main.ts
# Jet does not copy the safety bypass.
# Deno has scoped grants and an allow-all escape. Jet keeps explicit denies binding. Source: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/security/
decisions.detail:
Owner-selected amendment to D-RIGHTS-CLI1 and application prompting, not an I1 safety exception. Current evidence: Source/main.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs:1264-1290, crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs. Keep the exact owner clarification on the linked card. No provider safety checks are autoapproved by this design. Formal Tower ratification remains open.

Beginner review prompted the worked policy edit, explicit alias, separate trusted/untrusted timelines, cancellation outcome, and safety glossary. The owner’s metadata-free prompt requirement wins: named --allow alone is not an exemption. Source examples use the existing package authority form and core.time sleep syntax.

Fresh review findings were retained. The author resolved each through the contract and linked card criteria. Review metadata describes that sequence; it does not claim an independent rerun or runtime proof.

options.name: Automatic policy, explicit invocation trust
options.detail:
Use --trust or its exact short alias -T with run, dev, and test. Trust once means exactly the same thing. All three approve otherwise approvable effects for this invocation, including new effects after dev edits. They never write policy.

Apply existing project grants and denies automatically. Metadata presence does not approve unlisted rights. A metadata-free effectful launch asks before execution unless trusted; an effect-free program, such as fn run() {}, does not ask. Named --allow alone does not bypass this metadata-free prompt rule.
options.technical:
The owner selected --trust AND -T, replacing earlier candidate names. Before --, these flags belong to Jet; after --, they are application arguments. Trust once and both flags approve the whole invocation, not only the first displayed gap. No invocation trust is persisted or reused by a later independent launch.

Apply declared project policy without a confirmation to use it. A missing right is not an explicit deny: an untrusted gap can be approved, but an explicit project/CLI deny is refused. Keep the existing named --allow/--deny conflict and root/leaf precedence rules. Without metadata, --allow does not replace --trust/-T or Trust once. It does not skip approval. Explicit denies refuse before any prompt. With metadata, named grants retain their existing right-resolution meaning.

For an untrusted gap, show exactly these choices: [1] Trust once, [2] Update project policy, [3] Exit (default), and [m] Arrow menu. The menu selects the same three actions. Exit, Enter on the default, Escape, EOF, unavailable consent, and unrecognized input cancel before execution with the existing non-success refusal status. They write neither a grant nor a deny.

Metadata means the program’s package facts. Inline facts live in package {} in the source. Separate facts live in the selected canonical package.jet. They are alternative existing forms, not two policies to merge. Editing permission changes authority.holds.allow in that selected source, preserving existing denies and other facts.

Worked source before approval, in app.jet:

```jet
package {
    name: "wait-demo"
    version: "0.1.0"
    authority: { holds: { allow: [Mem.Alloc] } }
}
use core.time as time
fn run() { time.sleep(1ms) }
```

For its uncovered Time.Wait effect, choosing Update shows app.jet and this exact proposed field change:

```text
before: authority: { holds: { allow: [Mem.Alloc] } }
after:  authority: { holds: { allow: [Mem.Alloc, Time.Wait] } }
```

Only accepting that displayed edit writes it. The next covered launch uses it without a prompt. If app.jet has no package metadata, offer the minimal inline block and its complete diff before writing. If package.jet already owns the policy, edit that file instead. Do not create a competing manifest or overwrite an explicit deny.

Read-only, virtual, malformed, changed-since-check, or unsafe paths disable the update with a cause-specific action. A transactional snapshot check must protect the exact approved file and bytes. Persist the approved edit and mandatory authority record before using its grant. Do not ask again after the exact edit has already been approved.

Required authority records identify checked source, policy identity, decision origin, effect scope, and actual outcome through the existing typed audit path. The trigger matrix below distinguishes grants from refusals. Once/flags record invocation trust; they do not pretend a project edit occurred. Required audit persistence failure refuses execution. Its protected storage is not disposable history.

Language memory/type checks and user-written Unsafe regions remain enforced. OS, sandbox, enterprise, delegation, and dependency restrictions still bind. Sensitive recording can contain secrets, so its separate consent remains required. Trust never approves unsigned artifacts, package trust changes, unrelated confirmations, or provider safety checks.

Existing --trust appears in environment/toolchain forwarding. Separate that trust domain from application effects during the cutover. Do not forward an application trust bit as permission for unsigned packages or unrelated operations. Noninteractive --trust/-T works; an untrusted uncovered gap without interactive consent fails with actionable policy/flag guidance.

After the policy diff, show [1] Apply displayed edit and [2] Exit (default). Only 1, or Enter on an explicitly selected Apply row, accepts. Bare Enter, Escape, EOF, unavailable consent, and unknown input cancel without writing or launching. No third confirmation follows successful explicit acceptance.

For missing metadata, insert inline facts only into the unique checked source selected by canonical entry identity. Never select an imported helper arbitrarily. A multi-target test/package invocation without one unique policy-owning source disables Update. Explain the ambiguity: select one source or author canonical package policy explicitly.

Before each checked revision’s first effect, automatic project grants, applicable named grants, flags, and Once require a durable authorization-use record. Record actual source/policy identity, right scope, invocation identity, and decision origin. Existing required delegation records remain required. A pure revision needs no authorization-use receipt.

Explicit deny, cancellation, invalid input, and noninteractive missing consent execute no effect and return the refusal status. They produce the typed diagnostic, not a new mandatory persistent event. Honor an enclosing audit policy that already requires recording refusals. Logging failure never changes refusal into approval.

A trusted dev edit does not prompt again for approvable effects. Before its new checked revision performs effects, persist a new authorization-use record linked to the original invocation decision. Record new source/policy hashes and effective rights. A previous revision’s receipt cannot authorize new source. Required write failure refuses the revision’s effects.

Policy edits use the existing authority transaction with explicit phases. Persist an approved-but-not-applied record containing old/new policy hashes and the accepted edit. Atomically replace the checked source, then persist a committed marker. No effect uses the edit before both policy and marker are durable.

A missing commit marker means attempted or uncertain, never completed approval. Every partial transaction refuses execution. Recovery checks old/new hashes under the same lock, then completes or rejects without overwriting unrelated edits. If storage prevents a failure marker, the durable uncommitted record remains uncertain. Never claim rollback or successful persistence without evidence.

Environment preparation has a separate explicit workflow:

```sh
jet env
# Review environment-only approval in its existing interface.
# Inside the prepared project shell:
jet run -T app.jet
```

Application trust is never forwarded as environment trust. An unprepared noninteractive run refuses with the registered environment diagnostic. Its correction points to jet env and then retrying. Explicitly invoked environment/package trust commands keep their own domains. No new generic trust flag is invented. The -T alias is application-only.

Existing persistent service trust remains explicit, for example jet trust grant "acme/web@github:postgres.service" --scope repo. It is separate from the one-session workflow above. Never create that persistent grant automatically, broaden its subject, or waive signature checks.

The prompt trigger is not merely a nonempty uncovered set. Without metadata, any effectful untrusted revision asks even when --allow covers its rights. Show the checked requested effects honestly, not an empty gap. With metadata, show only uncovered approvable effects. A project edit grants only the exact displayed rights, never the universal scope of Once.
